title: M3.7: Sony lossless-compressed ARW tiles (2×2 CFA cells per LJ92 sample)
author: leipsfur
body:
## Problem

Lossless-compressed ARW files (Compression 7, here from an ILCE-7M4 / A7 IV, firmware 5.01) render as vertical bands with scrambled content and a strong purple cast, in the loupe, the thumbnails and `lightcraft-cli render`.

## Cause

The raw IFD is tiled, 512×512, and each tile is an LJ92 frame of **256×256 with four components** (from the files' own SOF3 headers: `P 14, Y 256, X 256, Nf 4`). Each four-component sample is one 2×2 CFA cell: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right.

ARW with Compression 7 went through the generic TIFF path. That path reads a frame as a row-major sample stream, which is DNG's convention. So frame row `fy` (1024 samples) became tile rows `2fy` and `2fy+1`. The result was each tile's left and right halves interleaved row by row, stretched 2× horizontally, with the CFA order broken.

## Fix

- `crates/raw/src/vendor/arw.rs`: `is_quad_tiled` looks at the first tile's frame header (4 components, half the tile size in each direction). If it matches, `read_quad_tiles` decodes the tiles in parallel and puts each cell in its place. The error handling is the same as the generic path: a corrupt tile is skipped, and decoding fails only if no tile decodes. `Mode::Header` only runs `check_image`. Other lossless-JPEG layouts, and DNG, still use the generic path unchanged.
- `crates/engine/src/media.rs`: `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 3 → 4, so cached thumbnails and views of affected files are rendered again.

## Verification

- New unit test `quad_tiles_place_cfa_cells`: a 14×12 mosaic in 8×8 tiles, where the right and bottom tiles extend past the image. The tiles are stored column by column in the file, as Sony does, while `TileOffsets` stays in raster order. The test checks that decoding reproduces the mosaic exactly.
- Real ILCE-7M4 file (7168×5120, 140 tiles): `lightcraft-cli render` gives a clean 7008×4672 image with no tile seams, in ~3.3 s. The app's thumbnail and loupe are correct too.
- Green order (top-right vs. bottom-left) was…

title: Import: scan folders in the background (fixes Add Folder on network shares)
author: GlemNL
body:
## Problem

Reported bug: adding a folder located on a network share (NAS, CIFS mount) through **File → Add Folder…** does not load, and the folder ends up disappearing. The report is that it happens even for folders with only a few photos.

Root cause found: `library.importPreview` (`import::scan`) ran synchronously on the UI thread and read every file in full (probe + content hash) before the review dialog could open. Over a network share this blocks the window for as long as the folder takes to read. On a folder with tens of thousands of files the window froze and the app was gone shortly after.

Note on reproduction: I reproduced the freeze and the app disappearing with a very large folder on a network share. A 22-file folder on the same share opened the review correctly in my test, so I could not reproduce the small-folder case; the fix addresses the blocking scan itself, which is the only cause I found.

## Fix

- `import::scan` is split into `ScanInput` (snapshot of what the scan needs from the session) and `scan_with`, which has no `Session` dependency and reports progress / honours cancellation through `ScanProgress`. `scan` keeps its signature and is a thin wrapper, so the `library.importPreview` command, CLI and MCP behave as before.
- The UI runs `scan_with` on a worker thread (`ScanTask`), shows a progress window ("Reading photos… N of M") with a **Cancel** button, and opens the review when the scan finishes. On wasm it runs inline.
- `file.addFolder`, `file.addPhotos` and `file.addFromDevice` now return `{"scanning": true}` immediately instead of the candidate counts; the dialog opens on completion.

title: Library: an album source serializes (library.state no longer panics)
author: storybored379
body:
`LibrarySource` is an internally tagged enum (`tag = "kind"`) whose `Album` variant holds an `AlbumId`. serde can't serialize an integer newtype in an internally tagged enum (`cannot serialize tagged newtype variant LibrarySource::Album containing an integer`). With an album open:

- **`library.state` panics** at `cmd/query.rs:84`. Over the control channel (`lightcraft-cli run --connect` / MCP) this **closes the desktop app**. It happened right after `library.import` with `albumName`, which opens the new album.
- **`view.json` is written empty** (`to_vec_pretty(...).unwrap_or_default()`), so the last source, filter, sort and selection are lost on the next launch.

Adjacent tagging (`content = "id"`) keeps the unit variants as `{"kind": "all"}` and writes the album as `{"kind": "album", "id": 8}`. That's the shape `library.source` already takes, so a reported source can be passed straight back. Existing `view.json` files read unchanged.

### How it was found and tested
- Reproduced on Windows with the desktop app: import into a new album, then `library.state` over `--connect`. The app exits with the panic above every time.
- New test `tests_organize::album_source_reports_in_library_state_and_persists_the_view`:
  - `library.state` reports the album.
  - The reported source round-trips through `library.source`.
  - The view (album + sort) is restored after reopening the library.
- It **fails without the change** (same panic) **and passes with it**. `cargo test -p lightcraft-engine` passes; `rustfmt --check` is clean on the touched files.
- Clean-room: no third-party source consulted.

Found and fixed with Claude Code (AI-assisted).

title: Export dialog no longer widens every frame (fixes #8)
author: echelon
body:
## Problem
Opening Export, the dialog kept growing horizontally on its own (#8, Linux).

## Cause
Rows with a trailing button (**Folder / Choose…**, watermark **Graphic / Choose…**, **Save preset / Save**) sized their text field as "available width − a guessed button width" (76 / 60 px). The dialog window sizes itself to its content; when the real button was wider than the guess (font metrics differ per platform, and the Choose… buttons only appear when a native picker is available, as on desktop Linux), the content overflowed by a few pixels, the window grew to fit, and the next frame did the same again.

## Fix
These rows now lay out right to left (`trailing_button_row` in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/dialogs.rs`): the button is placed first and the text field takes exactly the width that's left. No guessed widths remain in auto-sized dialogs. The dialog window's rect is registered as `dialog:window` so tests and agents can measure it.

## Testing
- New headless test `export_dialog_keeps_its_width` (folder + file pickers present, watermark graphic row shown): **failed before** (the dialog grew from 492 → 693 px in 60 frames), passes now.
- Full CI (fmt, parity, clippy, workspace tests, layers, wasm) green. Three known load-sensitive UI tests timed out under heavy machine load and pass when rerun alone.
- Looked at a headless snapshot of the dialog: rows aligned, Save button at the right edge.

Fixes #8

title: Grid and filmstrip keep your scroll position; mouse wheel scrolls the filmstrip (fixes #11)
author: echelon
body:
## Problem (#11)
- The mouse wheel didn't scroll the filmstrip.
- After scrolling the filmstrip or the photo grid (scroll bar or wheel), the view jumped back to the selected photo a moment later, making large collections hard to browse.

## Cause
Both views remembered the last active photo in egui's per-frame memory, but wrote it as `Option<PhotoId>` and read it back as `PhotoId`. The read always came back empty, so "the active photo changed" was true on every frame and `scroll_to_rect` ran every frame, animating back over any scroll the user made.

## Fix
- `grid::follow_active` (shared by the grid and the filmstrip) stores the active photo and the frame it was drawn on, and scrolls only when the **active photo changes** (arrow keys, click, command) or the **view comes back on screen**. Time passing, finished renders, edits and releasing the scroll bar never move the view.
- Filmstrip: a vertical mouse wheel scrolls it sideways (`always_scroll_the_only_direction`; trackpad horizontal scrolling still works). A newly active photo is centred only if it's (partly) off screen, so clicking a visible thumbnail doesn't move the strip.
- `ui.inspect` reports `scroll: {grid, filmstrip}` (docs/control-protocol.md) for agents and tests; parity rows updated.

## Testing
- New `tests_scroll.rs`: `grid_keeps_the_users_scroll_position` (wheel and scroll-bar drag, 120+ frames, an edit, then → scrolls to the new photo) and `filmstrip_wheel_scrolls_and_keeps_its_position`. Both **fail without the fix**.
- Full CI green on the branch; rebased on current main: clippy clean, all 81 `lightcraft-ui-egui` tests pass.
- Headless snapshots checked: the filmstrip and grid stay where they were scrolled.

Fixes #11

title: Import Luminar looks (.lmp, .mplumpack) (fixes #9)
author: echelon
body:
## What (#9)
`.mplumpack` is a Luminar Looks collection: a ZIP of `.lmp` looks plus a `PresetsInfo.plist` with the pack's name. `.lmp` files are XML property lists of adjustment layers → effects → named slider values (Luminar 1 flat layers, Luminar 4 nested develop sublayers, and Luminar 4 bundle folders `Name.lmp/Contents/preset.lmp`). The format was worked out black-box from two freely distributed packs (none of their content is in the repo; tests use synthetic files).

## How
- New `crates/engine/src/preset_luminar.rs`: a small XML plist reader (binary plists refused; nesting bounded so a hostile file can't overflow the stack), `read_lmp`, `read_mplumpack`; looks are converted to `crs:` fields and reuse the existing Lightroom preset mapping.
- Hooked into `preset.import`, folder/zip import and drag & drop (`.mplumpack`, `.lmp`, bundle folders). Packs are grouped by their `GroupName`; disabled layers are ignored; layer opacity scales the sliders.
- Mapped: Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks, Temperature/Tint, Saturation, Vibrance, Clarity (+ Structure/AI Structure), Dehaze, HSL (8 bands), RGB/R/G/B curves, Vignette, Grain. Everything else (AI tools, Orton, glow, LUT layers, masks, blend modes…) is listed in the import report's `unmapped`, so looks are **best-effort approximations**.
- Docs: `docs/xmp-interop.md` (mapping table), `docs/parity.md`, `docs/whats-new.md`.

## Testing
- Engine tests on synthetic looks and packs (both schema generations, bundles, grouping, unmapped reporting, `preset.import` end-to-end, drag & drop detection, hostile nesting).
- Dry-run import of the two real packs: 18 looks, 0 failures.
- Full CI green (stacked with #10 and the curve PR on current main).

Fixes #9

title: Mark raws shown from their embedded preview as "preview only" (refs #10)
author: echelon
body:
## Problem (#10)
A Nikon D3200 NEF showed the camera's B&W picture style. The D3200 writes Nikon's Huffman-compressed NEF, which LightCraft can't decode yet, so it silently fell back to the camera's **embedded JPEG preview**: the user was editing that JPEG, with the camera's look baked in, and nothing said so.

## Fix (honest UI; the decoder itself is not part of this PR)
- The decoder's "unsupported" reason is carried from probe/import into the catalog: `Photo.preview_only: Option<String>` (`serde(default)`; old catalogs load). Reload and Relink re-check it, and undo restores it.
- Exposed to agents: `previewOnly` in `library.importPreview` and `catalog.query`, `preview_only` in `photo.inspect`.
- UI: a **Preview** pill on grid thumbnails; a pill at the top of the loupe ("Preview only: editing the camera's embedded JPEG (Nikon Huffman-compressed NEF)") with the full explanation on hover; the same notice in the Edit and Info panels. Drawn in code with theme tokens (no assets).
- Bug fixed on the way: `source_info` treated such photos as raw (filmic scene-referred tone map and Kelvin white balance on an already rendered JPEG, which shifted the look even with no edits). It now uses `Photo::develops_raw()`, so they develop like JPEGs.

## Testing
- Catalog, engine (synthetic preview-only raw: import, reopen, reload/relink, undo) and headless UI tests (badge and notices shown; none on a normal photo); each fails without the change.
- Checked in the running app with a compressed D5100 NEF (same NEF family as the D3200).
- Full CI green (stacked with #39 and the curve PR on current main).

Decoding compressed NEF (and the other unsupported variants) remains open.

Refs #10

title: Tone curve: drag points, reset curves, point-curve presets (fixes #12, #13, #14)
author: echelon
body:
Three commits, one per issue.

## #12: drag curve points
The editor already had drag code, but it saved the dragged point's index as `Option<usize>` and read it back as `usize`, so the drag was lost after the first frame and dragging only added new points. Fixed: points drag in **X and Y**, X stays between the neighbours, the point is picked where you press, with a grab cursor, a highlighted point and an input/output readout (0–255). One undo step per drag.

## #13: reset the whole curve
- New command `curve.reset {channel?: all|point|parametric|master|red|green|blue}` (default `all`, incl. Refine Saturation).
- Double-click a channel selector resets that channel; a **Reset** button under the graph resets every curve; right-click the graph for "Reset <channel> Channel" / "Reset All Curves".

## #14: curve presets
- Built-ins (our own values): **Linear**, **Medium Contrast**, **Strong Contrast**. User presets are saved in the library's prefs.
- A **Point Curve** dropdown shows the matching preset (or Custom), lists built-in and user presets, **Save Point Curve…**, **Import Presets…**, **Export Presets…** (`.lccurve` JSON); right-click a user preset to delete it.
- Commands for agents/CLI/MCP: `curve.presets`, `curve.applyPreset`, `curve.savePreset`, `curve.deletePreset`, `curve.importPresets`, `curve.exportPresets`.

## Testing
- Headless UI tests (`tests_curve.rs`): drag in both axes with one undo step, clamping past a neighbour, channel reset, Reset all, the preset dropdown (apply, save via the name prompt, re-apply). The drag tests fail on the old code.
- Engine tests for `curve.reset` and the preset commands (incl. persistence across reopening the library, export/import, name clashes, junk files).
- Headless snapshot checked. Full CI green (stacked with #39 and #40 on current main).

Fixes #12

title: MCP: crop returns an error when given no rect, angle or reset instead of a silent no-op
author: storybored379
body:
The `crop` tool fell through to `crop.set` with an empty object when none of its parameters were
given, so a call with a guessed parameter (for example `aspect: "1:1"`) or `reset: false` answered
"ok" and left the photo unchanged. A client had no way to tell its crop was ignored.

It now returns an error naming the parameters it needs (`rect`, `angle` or `reset: true`), the

- Reproduced through the headless MCP server (`lightcraft-cli mcp`): `crop {id, aspect: "1:1"}` returned "ok" with no change.

title: Local: browse a folder in the background with progress
author: GlemNL
body:
## Problem
Local → Browse Folder… listed, probed and imported the whole folder on the UI thread. On a network share the window froze for a long time with no progress feedback (#23). The earlier background-scan fix only covered the Add Photos / Add Folder dialog, not this path.

Related symptoms: a folder picked with Browse Folder… was listed in the sidebar only while it was the active view (it vanished once another source was opened), and the sidebar's Missing count stat()ed every catalog photo on the UI thread, which froze the window for seconds once browsed network photos were in the catalog (#34).

## Fix
- `library.browse` from the UI now switches the view at once, then lists and reads the folder on a worker thread, with the existing progress window (and Cancel). The photos join the view in small batches (2 per frame) afterwards. Clicking the folder already being read keeps the running read and its progress; clicking another folder replaces it; an import-review scan is not interrupted.
- `import_with` reuses probes from a preceding scan instead of reading the files again (the doc comment already described this intent; it was not implemented). This removes the second slow read on a share.
- `library.import` accepts `local: bool` (browse semantics: photos stay out of the library).
- The sidebar's Missing count is computed on a worker thread and shows the last finished count (refreshed at most every 5 s).
- Folders picked with Browse Folder… are remembered in the Local list (saved with the UI settings).
- When a filter hides every photo, the grid and filmstrip now say so ("No matching photos" / "No photos match the filters") instead of "No photos in this folder" / a blank strip.

title: Local: Remove from Local hides a sidebar location, with a way to restore
author: GlemNL
body:
Closes #24.

## Problem
Every Local sidebar location (Pictures, Desktop, Downloads, Home, the folder being browsed) is always listed. The folder context menu only had disk operations (Rename / Move / Show in Finder), so there was no way to drop a location you never use.

## Fix
- Right-clicking a top-level Local location now offers **Remove from Local**. It hides the shortcut only: the folder, its photos and catalog membership are untouched.
- The hidden list is saved with the UI state (`hiddenLocations`), so it survives restarts.
- While anything is hidden, a **"Show N hidden locations"** row under Browse Folder… restores them. Choosing a hidden folder with Browse Folder… also puts that one back.
- Both actions are commands (`local.hide {path}`, `local.restoreHidden {path?}`), so the control channel and MCP can use them. `docs/parity.md` (LR-IMP-LOCAL) is updated.
- Subfolders under a location's triangle do not get the option; only top-level entries do.

## Scope note
On `main` the only non-built-in entry is the folder currently being browsed. Persistent saved roots (#21) are part of #43; its roots are drawn by the same code, so they get Remove from Local as well. This PR does not depend on #43, but it touches the same function (`local_section` in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/left.rs`) and `UiState`, so whichever merges second needs a small conflict resolution.

## Verification
- New test `local_location_can_be_hidden_and_restored` (hide, list, restore, folder still on disk). `lightcraft-ui-egui`: 88 passed, 0 failed (1 ignored).

title: Smart Previews: choose the folder per library
author: GlemNL
body:
Closes #26.

## Problem
Smart previews (the editable proxies used while originals are offline, about 1 MB per photo) were always written to `<library>/Smart Previews`. A large set filled the library's drive, and the only way to move them was to move the whole library.

## Fix
The folder is now a per-library setting (saved in the library's `prefs.json`); the default is unchanged.
- **`library.smartPreviewsLocation`** (new command): without arguments it reports the effective folder (`path`, `default`, `custom`, `available`, `count`, `bytes`); with `path` it switches to that folder; with `reset` it returns to the library's own folder.
- **Explicit choice for existing previews:** when the old folder holds previews, `existing` must be `move`, `leave` (build again later) or `discard`; without it the command refuses and changes nothing. Moves fall back to copy + delete across drives; only `.lcsp` files are touched.
- **No silent fallback to the system drive:** the new folder must accept a test write before anything moves; a folder whose parent is missing (an unplugged drive) is an error and is never created on the current drive. Building also refuses while a chosen folder is unavailable. A full or read-only drive fails the write test with its own message.
- **Used everywhere:** building, discarding, status (`photo.smartPreview`, Info panel) and offline rendering all read the same folder, so the offline-editing behaviour is unchanged.
- **UI:** Settings → Performance → Smart previews shows the effective path before building (red with an explanation when unavailable), count and size, a Move / Leave / Delete choice for existing previews, **Choose Folder…** and **Use Library Folder**.
- `docs/parity.md` (LR-CLOUD-SMARTPREVIEW) updated.

## Not included
- The regular thumbnail cache stays in the library (the issue calls it related but distinct).
- No free-space readout: the standard library cannot report it without a new dependency, so a full drive is detected when the write te…

title: UI: more spacing between in-window menu headings

The in-window File / Edit / View / Photo / Window / Help headings sit too close together, which makes them harder to read and select.

title: LRC-LIB-METADATA: Copyright Status, Rights Usage Terms and Copyright Info URL
author: storybored379
body:
Lightroom's Copyright metadata has four fields: Copyright, Copyright Status (Unknown / Copyrighted / Public Domain), Rights Usage Terms and Copyright Info URL. Working photographers put all four in a metadata preset applied on import, and stock agencies and newsrooms read them from delivered files. LightCraft had only the notice (`dc:rights`). The tracker row said "no copyright status field".

### What changed
- **Catalog**: `Meta` gets `copyright_status` (`CopyrightStatus`: unknown / copyrighted / publicDomain), `usage_terms` and `copyright_url`. They are left out of the JSON when unset, so existing libraries and snapshots read and write unchanged.
- **XMP** (`lightcraft-meta`), following the XMP Rights Management schema, which is also what IPTC Core maps these fields to:
  - `xmpRights:Marked` (Boolean: `True` = copyrighted, `False` = public domain, absent = unknown);
  - `xmpRights:UsageTerms` (Lang Alt);
  - `xmpRights:WebStatement` (URI).
  The namespace was already declared. Values other than True/False read as unknown.
- **Where the fields flow**:
  - Read on import (from the file's XMP) and from sidecars, where the sidecar wins as for every other field.
  - Written to sidecars (Save Metadata to File / auto-write) and embedded in exports. **"Copyright only" exports keep all of them**, since that's the copyright info.
- **Commands**:
  - `photo.setMeta` takes `copyrightStatus`, `usageTerms`, `copyrightUrl` (one undo step, as before).
  - `photo.copyMetadata` / `pasteMetadata` include them.
  - Metadata presets can hold them; Save Metadata Preset from the active photo includes them by default with the other copyright fields.
- **Smart albums**: a "Copyright Status" rule (is / isn't).
- **Info panel**: a Copyright Status picker plus the two text fields under Copyright (same `meta_field` pattern; automation ids `field:copyrightStatus`, `field:usageTerms`, `field:copyrightUrl`).

- **AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md** (identical copies): a "Never crash (outranks feature work)" section ahead of the
  non-negotiables. It covers the rule and why, the bans (`unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`/`unreachable!`/`todo!`/`unimplemented!`/`unsafe`),

title: Never crash: last-resort guard around command execution
author: echelon
body:
Never-crash rollout: the last-resort guard (standard: `craftrules/standards/never-crash.md`; steering in #52).

## Before
Nothing caught a panic in a command: `Session::execute` runs commands on the UI thread (desktop), the control
channel and MCP, so one escaped panic closed the app and lost unsaved state. (Background export and merge workers run
on threads; a panicking worker doesn't take the app down.)

## What
- New `lightcraft_engine::guard`: `catch(what, f)` turns a panic into `Err("<what> failed unexpectedly: <message>")`;
  `install_hook(path)` chains the default hook (stderr report) and appends `time [thread] panic at file:line: message`
  to a log file, best effort.

  `guard::catch`. An escaped panic becomes that command's `EngineError::Other`, which every frontend already shows
  like any failed command, and the session (catalog, library, undo history, journal persistence) stays usable.
- The desktop app installs the hook with `<temp dir>/lightcraft-panics.log`. A Windows release build has no console,

title: LRC-MAP-TRACKLOG: Auto-Tag from Tracklog (GPS from a GPX file by capture time)
author: storybored379
body:
Most cameras don't record GPS, so photographers carry a phone app or a GPS logger and geotag afterwards: load the day's track log, and every photo gets the position the logger had when it was taken. Lightroom Classic does this in the Map module (Tracklog ▸ Load Tracklog / Auto-Tag Photos / Set Time Zone Offset). The tracker row `LRC-MAP-TRACKLOG` was ⬜; this adds it without needing the Map module.

### What it does
- **Photo ▸ Auto-Tag from Tracklog…** (`photo.tagFromTracklog`): pick a `.gpx` file, confirm the camera's time zone, and the selected photos get GPS positions. One undo step; a toast says how many were tagged, how many fell outside the log and how many already had a location.
- **Engine command `photo.autoTagTracklog`** (so CLI, control channel and MCP get it as well): `{path | gpx, ids?, offset?, maxGap?, replace?, dryRun?}` → `{tagged, interpolated, nearest, skipped: {noTime, outside, hasGps}, assumedUtc, points, start, end, photos: [{id, gps, match}]}`.

### Design
- **GPX reader** (`lightcraft-meta`, `gpx.rs`, quick-xml like the XMP reader): GPX 1.0 and 1.1, prefixed or default namespace. It reads the timed `<trkpt>`s of every `<trk>`/`<trkseg>` (lat, lon, optional `<ele>`, `<time>`). Untimed points are counted and left out. Waypoints and routes have no timeline, so they're ignored. It has depth and point limits like the XMP reader.
- **Matching** (`Tracklog::locate`): GPX times are UTC (`xsd:dateTime`; a time without a zone is read as UTC, per the schema).
  - Between two points of the **same track segment** that are at most `maxGap` apart (default 10 min), the position is interpolated linearly in time, taking the short way across ±180°.
  - Otherwise the nearest point counts if it's within `maxGap`.
  - The schema defines a segment as one continuous span of logging, so we **never interpolate across a segment break**: that's where reception was lost or the logger was off.
- **Time zones**: capture times are the camera's local clock.

title: Issue #37: Catalog: compact the log on a background thread with ordered journal boundaries
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #37.


At the 2,000-record threshold the UI thread serialised and fsynced the whole catalog (1-2 s
at 85k photos after streaming). Now `persist()` starts `Journal::snapshot_in_background`:

- the worker writes `catalog.snap` for op N from a clone of the catalog (photos are Arc-shared,
  so the clone is cheap) through `Store::background_writer` (a second FsStore handle; MemStore
  opt-in; none on wasm/web, which stays synchronous);
- appends go on as before (fsynced before every command returns) and are also kept in memory
  as the "tail" (records > N);
- `Journal::poll` (from `persist` and the per-frame `persist_if_dirty`) sees the worker done and
  atomically replaces the log with exactly the tail.

Crash points: before the snapshot rename -> old snapshot + whole log; between the rename and the
log rewrite -> new snapshot + whole log (records <= N skipped as stale, existing rule); after ->
new snapshot + tail. A failed snapshot keeps the log whole and retries after another
max_records records (no retry storm). At most one snapshot in flight; a synchronous snapshot
(close, Optimize Library), reopening a library and dropping the Journal first wait for it, so an
older snapshot can never replace a newer one. On-disk format unchanged.

Tests (crates/catalog/src/tests_background.rs, a gated store holds the worker mid-flight and
"crashes" by copying the files): edits during a background snapshot survive crashes at each
point and the trimmed log holds exactly seq N+1.. in order; failure loses nothing and backs
off; sync snapshot waits (no regression); drop waits; real FsStore with a leftover partial
temp file; a proptest over interleavings of edits / start / land / finish / sync snapshot /
crash. Mutations checked: trimming the log to empty, or not waiting in `snapshot`, fail them.
Engine: `threshold_compaction_runs_in_the_background` (crash copy mid-run, reopen without close).
`library.info` -> persistence gains snapshotRunning, failedSnapshots, maxBlockingMs and
la…

title: Issue #29: Import: Move mode with rename and template folders
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #29.


library.import mode `move` (UI: Transfer ▸ Move, MCP import tool): reuses
Copy's destination, folder organisation (incl. custom templates) and rename
template. Each photo and its XMP sidecars (both namings) are placed without
touching the source (hard link on the same volume, else a new file that is
copied, synced and compared byte for byte; taken names get -1, -2…, never
overwritten). Sources are removed only after the catalog records are
committed and saved, and only when the destination is still intact; failed,
duplicate, unchecked and in-library files keep their sources; sources that
can't be removed are kept and reported (`kept`). Undo removes the catalog
records and leaves the moved files at the destination.

**Safety:** a source is removed only after its destination is written (hard link, or a synced copy verified byte for byte) and the batch's catalog records are committed and saved; failed, cancelled, unchecked, duplicate or symlinked sources are never removed; nothing is overwritten. Undo removes the catalog records and leaves the moved files at the destination.

author: echelon

**Draft: needs a Windows build and test pass before merging** (it can't be built on macOS; the WiX was written against the v5.0.2 sources and docs, `xmllint` and the packaging-lint PowerShell parse check pass locally).

## What changes
- `packaging/windows/lightcraft.wxs`: a small WiX UI set (WixUI_Minimal without the licence page): Welcome → Ready to install → progress → **Completed** ("LightCraft has been installed…", Finish, and a **Launch LightCraft** checkbox, ticked by default). - No licence-acceptance page: LightCraft is MIT OR Apache-2.0, which require nothing from someone who installs and runs it.
- Launch on Finish uses the Util extension's `WixUnelevatedShellExec`, which starts the app through Explorer as the signed-in user, without admin rights, even when the installer UI is elevated. It is UI-only (`/qn` and `/passive` never launch), and `Return="ignore"` means a failed launch never fails an install.

No assets are committed.

- `-culture en-us` together with the extensions' localisation strings

title: Local: forget untouched browse records of folders not browsed for 30 days
author: echelon
body:
Local browse records can be most of a large catalog (85k photos, 90 %
Local: 313.5 MB snapshot). Untouched Local records of folders whose last
browse is older than library.preferences forgetLocalDays (default 30,
0 = never) are now removed from the catalog when the library opens (and by
library.forgetLocal {dryRun?, days?}), as journaled, non-undoable ops, then
compacted in the background. Files and XMP sidecars are never touched;
browsing the folder again catalogues them afresh.

Untouched = a Local file record, not deleted, not a virtual copy, whose
state still hashes to the fingerprint taken when the browse catalogued it
(any change keeps it); records from before fingerprints need every
user-editable field empty/default. Kept too: records in albums (or as
cover), stacks, sources of virtual copies, visible/selected/edited ones,
ones referenced by undo/redo, ones with a smart preview.

Per-folder last-browsed times live in the catalog (Op::SetBrowsed,
normalised with folder_key; re-stamped at most hourly). Old catalogs load
unchanged; folders without a time are stamped now, so nothing is forgotten
on the first open after the upgrade.

persist_bench (85k photos, 76.5k Local, every 7th folder recent, 1 in 50
rated): 63.8k forgotten, plan 162 ms, snapshot 313.5 MB -> 94.9 MB.
Settings -> Performance -> Local folders.

title: Issue #78: GPU export: respect device limits, fall back to CPU on GPU errors
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #78.


A GPU render no longer hands back an image it cannot vouch for:
- set the wgpu device-lost callback (wgpu never reports a lost device as an
  error, so a driver reset went unnoticed); readback waits with a timeout and
  checks the poll result and map callback instead of blocking forever
- each render runs in OutOfMemory/Validation/Internal error scopes; errors
  fail that render (OOM and limit failures for that render only, device
  errors for the process) and it is redone on the CPU
- every buffer is checked against the device limit when created (no
  validation error, no process-wide disable); LIGHTCRAFT_GPU_LIMITS=webgpu|<MiB>
  creates the device with lower limits to reproduce small adapters
- the output buffer is cleared and the per-pixel kernel writes alpha 255:
  any unwritten pixel (work silently dropped, the issue's all-black export)
  fails the render; an all-black result is re-rendered on the CPU
- renders submit per stage and every 16 M invocations, the per-pixel stage
  runs in ~4 MP bands: no long submission for a slow iGPU's watchdog to reset
- ui.inspect perf.gpuReason / perf.gpuFallback, app.gpu reason/lastFallback,
  System Info and Settings say why the GPU is off (e.g. llvmpipe skipped) and
  why the last render fell back

Tests: crates/gpu/tests/fallback.rs (limit, mid-render limit, validation
error, dropped work, black photo), engine export falls back to the CPU image,
banded 3000x2000 GPU/CPU equivalence.

60D, 550D, 600D, 1200D, 1300D, 5D Mark II, 1D Mark IV; RGGB on the 40D,
5D Mark III, 6D, 5DS R and others). Read it from raw IFD tag 0xc5e0
(CR2CFAPattern: 1 RGGB, 2 BGGR, 3 GBRG, 4 GRBG), anchored at the full
decoded sensor; fall back to RGGB when the tag is missing. No model table.

Checked on 35 decoded CC0 raw.pixls.us CR2s (35 models): the tag agrees
with the mosaic's green-diagonal statistic on every file; the SensorInfo
border parity does not predict the layout. Corpus manifest gains the
reporter's samples; a corpus test asserts each layout.

**Evidence:** 35 CC0 CR2 samples (one per model) decoded; tag `0xc5e0` (ExifTool's documented CR2CFAPattern) matched the mosaic's measured green diagonal on every file, including the reporter's 7D / 550D / 5D Mark II (GBRG) and 40D / 5D Mark III / 6D / 5DS R (RGGB). The sensor-border-parity hypothesis was tested and rejected. No per-model table; prose documentation only.

**Test plan:** unit test for tag values, synthetic CR2 round trip, corpus test checking the pattern and the green-diagonal agreement per sample; `cargo xtask ci` green apart from the known load-sensitive headless UI tests, which pass alone.

title: Draft: guarded ARW preview-derived colour estimation (WB fidelity still unresolved)
author: arata-1972
body:
Sony ARW files without camera matrices render visibly dark and muted with the generic camera-RGB≈sRGB fallback. This estimates a bounded 3×3 correction from each file’s own embedded JPEG, following the first calibration step described in the roadmap. All output pixels still come from RAW decoding/demosaicing; the JPEG supplies colour correspondences only.

The fit uses a fixed sensor proxy across thumbnail/full-export sizes, excludes clipped/nonfinite/near-black pixels, requires sufficient colour diversity and bounded covariance conditioning, uses an exposure-biased ridge, bounds coefficients and validates on held-out pixels. Poor fits retain the fallback. DNG matrices, other RAW formats and JPEG processing are unchanged. Cache version 5 prevents stale thumbnails/views.

Local comparison: five private Sony ILCE-6700 RAWs and same-capture JPEGs reproduce the issue. The estimate was accepted on all five and improved brightness/yellow colour, but skin still differs. All five JPEG exports remained pixel-identical before/after. Exposure, saturation and contrast change the original RAW output; a slider no-op was not reproduced in this sample. The original muted rendering has a weaker saturation response.

This is deliberately a DRAFT, not a complete RAW fix or measured camera calibration. Absolute RAW WB remains problematic: an as-shot estimate around 6829 K / −127 tint produces a strong pink cast when temperature alone is changed to 9000 K. The preview fit does not establish the physical illuminant. Same-aspect crops/warps, camera tone curves and styles need broader validation. Maintainer colour-science feedback is needed before enabling this as a general solution.

Validation: synthetic known-matrix recovery and rejection tests (monochrome/nonfinite/singular/unrelated/mismatched references); local UI renders and edits visually checked; 400-px/full-size exports select the same fitted matrix; complete cargo xtask ci passed on the original base and the combined localizatio…

title: Issue #92: XMP: merge into an existing sidecar instead of replacing it
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #92.

Issue #92: XMP: merge into an existing sidecar instead of replacing it

Saving (Cmd+S or auto-write) now merges LightCraft's properties into an

title: Issue #101: catalog.log: cut a partial append back before retrying
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #101.

Issue #101: catalog.log: cut a partial append back before retrying

A failed append (disk full, dropped share) could leave part of its batch in
catalog.log; the retry (same seqs) then shared a line with the fragment and
the next load treated it as mid-log damage, setting later edits aside.

- Journal::append cuts the log back to the last whole record on error (or,
  if that fails too, before the next append).
- FsStore drops a failed append handle so the next attempt reopens the file;
  truncate of a never-created file is a no-op.
- The loader recognises a CRC-valid record glued after a fragment (logs
  written by older builds) and skips only the fragment.
- log_bytes now counts the newline added to an unterminated last record.
- close_library writes the closing snapshot even when appending fails; the
  snapshot absorbs the queued ops (Journal::snapshot_with_unlogged).

title: Issue #102: Catalog format version 2; refuse newer libraries untouched
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #102.

**Compatibility note:** the first time this build opens an existing library it rewrites it as catalog format v2; LightCraft v0.2.0 and older then refuse that library with a clear "written by a newer version" message rather than misreading it (no downgrade after updating).

Issue #102: Catalog format version 2; refuse newer libraries untouched

main added Op::SetBrowsed, Catalog.browsed and Photo.local_baseline while
the snapshot still said version 1, so v0.2.0 read such a library in part
(unknown ops as log damage, unknown fields dropped on its next snapshot).

- journal::VERSION = 2 (now public), with a format table and rules in the
  journal docs; a test with an exhaustive match over Op makes adding a
  variant fail until it is assigned a version.
- Journal::open reads the snapshot header first and refuses a newer
  version with CatalogError::Newer ("written by a newer version of
  LightCraft"), even when its catalog wouldn't parse.
- A log record whose CRC matches but whose op doesn't parse is "newer",
  not damage or a torn tail: refused before any file is modified.
- Opening an older (or snapshot-less) library writes a snapshot in this
  format before anything is appended (LoadReport::upgraded_from); a new
  library gets one at once, so v0.2.0 refuses it instead of reading a bare
  log.

title: Issue #99: Library: exclusive lock so two processes can't open one library
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #99.

Issue #99: Library: exclusive lock so two processes can't open one library

Two processes on one library each kept their own catalog and seq counter;
the last snapshot silently dropped the other's edits.

- lightcraft_catalog::lock: LibraryLock holds an exclusive OS lock
  (std File::try_lock: flock / LockFileEx) on <library>/catalog.lock for
  the session; who holds it goes to catalog.lock.owner (separate file: a
  Windows lock also blocks reads). Released on drop and by the OS when the
  process dies, so leftover files from a crash never lock anyone out. File
  systems without lock support open unprotected with a warning.
- Session::open_library takes the lock before reading anything and fails
  with EngineError::LibraryInUse ("this library is already open in
  LightCraft 0.x (process N on host)"); reopening the session's own
  library hands its lock over.
- lightcraft-cli (mcp/run/snapshot --library) adds how to drive the
  running app instead (--control + mcp --connect).
- Tests: in-process, leftover files, a killed child process, two engine
  sessions, CLI e2e (mcp --library holds it, run --library is refused).
  Existing tests that reopened a library while it was open now drop the
  first session.
- docs: parity row LRC-LIB-CATALOG-LOCK, mcp.md, web.md (no guard across
  browser tabs yet), whats-new.

title: Calibrate Sony ARW starting colour on macOS and preserve RAW editing
author: arata-1972
body:
Sony ARWs can open with inconsistent colour and tone when calibrated linear pixels are interpreted through a scene-fitted display curve, or when a rejected display fit discards successful camera calibration.

Supported Sony ARWs on macOS now keep calibrated scene-linear pixels, capture WB and highlight headroom separately from a directly sampled global RGB display response. A bounded synthetic RGB chart is passed through the installed Core Image decoder's documented linearSpaceFilter API on a separate measurement decoder. The response preserves cross-channel tone/gamut behaviour without fitting the photographed scene or matching JPEG pixels. Neutral rendering applies this response once, after scene-linear edits; explicit display controls remain editable. CPU/GPU interpolation and offline smart previews use the same interpretation. Invalid or unavailable measurements retain the calibrated-source fallback. Unavailable native decoding retains the portable path.

Render-cache version 9 invalidates older rendered results. Explicit smart-preview rebuilds refresh older source versions while preserving existing offline proxies until rebuilt. Existing custom edits and import presets are preserved. The earlier relative WB, Japanese UI integration, calibration-preserving fallback and editable camera-detail defaults remain included. This follow-up does not add a blanket exposure/saturation adjustment or additional noise reduction.

Validation: cargo xtask ci covers format, clippy, workspace tests, parity, layers, assets and WASM. Synthetic regressions cover cross-channel response, one-time neutral application, preserved source pixels, invalid-table rejection, CPU/GPU equivalence and offline response storage. The opt-in native fixture test checks black/white endpoints, stable response/proxies at different decode sizes, and preserved linear highlight headroom.

title: Windows on ARM64: release builds, tested on ARM64 hardware (#135)
author: echelon
body:
Closes #135.

**Release:**
- `release.yml` builds, signs and packages a **Windows ARM64** MSI and portable zip alongside x64 and x86: `lightcraft-<version>-windows-arm64.msi` and `…-arm64-portable.zip` (picked up by the release job's `release-*` artifact pattern).
- It's cross-compiled (`aarch64-pc-windows-msvc`) on the x64 Windows runner, so signing (certificate or Azure Trusted Signing) and WiX run exactly as they do for x64.
- `package.ps1` takes `-Arch arm64` (WiX `-arch arm64`). Before packaging it now checks each binary's **PE Machine** and **subsystem**, so an x64 build can never ship labelled ARM64, `lightcraft.exe` stays a GUI app and `lightcraft-cli.exe` stays a console app. The `--version` smoke run is skipped when the host can't run the build.
- `lightcraft.wxs` needs no change: it installs into `ProgramFiles6432Folder` (→ `C:\Program Files` for arm64) and has no custom-action binaries.

**Validation** (new `windows-arm64.yml`; runs on PRs touching Cargo or packaging files, on `main`, and weekly):
1. **package**: builds the ARM64 MSI exactly as the release does (unsigned here) and keeps it as an artifact for 7 days, so anyone with ARM hardware can try it.
2. **install and run on ARM64**: on GitHub's Windows 11 ARM64 runner, installs the MSI silently and checks that both installed binaries are ARM64. With the **installed** `lightcraft-cli` it then lists commands/controls, writes synthetic bracketed DNGs, decodes and develops one (`render --set …`), merges them to an HDR DNG, imports + edits + exports that, runs auto-tone + export on the demo library, and renders the full UI headlessly (`snapshot --demo`); every output's format is checked. title: Issue #136: Windows: use DX12 by default, honour WGPU_BACKEND, never let GPU init block startup
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #136.


wgpu loads the driver of every backend in an instance's set while it
enumerates adapters. The compute device (crates/gpu) hard-coded
Backends::PRIMARY (Vulkan + DX12 + Metal) and ignored WGPU_BACKEND, and
was created from LightcraftApp::new on a background thread at launch, so
a crashing Vulkan driver (Intel UHD 630, igvk64.dll) killed the process
before the window appeared; the window (egui-wgpu) also listed Vulkan.

- lightcraft_gpu::backend: DX12 only on Windows (Metal on macOS, as before
  on Linux) for both the compute device and the window;
  LIGHTCRAFT_GPU_BACKEND=dx12|vulkan|metal|gl|auto|off, else WGPU_BACKEND;
  backends missing from the build fall back to the default.
- The device is created only when GPU rendering is enabled, after the
  first frame; the preference is applied before the window opens.
- Crash sentinel: gpu-init.marker in the settings folder around device
  creation; if left behind, the next launch starts with GPU rendering off
  and a notice saying how to turn it back on.
- Tests: backend parsing/selection, sentinel, window defaults, headless
  snapshot with LIGHTCRAFT_GPU=0 / LIGHTCRAFT_GPU_BACKEND=off.
- Docs: gpu-pipeline.md (backends, env vars, troubleshooting), whats-new,
  parity LR-BEHAV-GPU.

title: Issue #138: DNG: apply the file's own camera-profile look (HueSatMap, LookTable, ToneCurve)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #138.


Lightroom-converted DNGs carry their camera profile's ProfileHueSatMapData1/2
and ProfileLookTableData (and sometimes ProfileToneCurve). We used only the
colour matrices, so such DNGs rendered flat and muted.

- raw: new `profile` module reads the tags (DNG spec ch. 6: value-major,
  hue-middle, saturation-minor tables, wrap-around hue, tri-linear lookups,
  sRGB value encoding) from the raw IFD or IFD 0; malformed tags are ignored.
- engine: the raw loader applies the hue/sat map (interpolated by the same
  illuminant weight as the matrices) before BaselineExposure and the look
  table after it, in linear ProPhoto; a ProfileToneCurve becomes the source's
  camera tone. Without one the standard base tone is kept.
- dngwrite keeps the look with the data (conversions, smart previews, merges).
- Render cache version 7.

title: Issue #148: Raw: read white balance, black level and crop of pre-2017 Sony ARWs
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #148.


Sony bodies from before ~2017 (RX100–RX100M5, RX10, NEX, SLT, ILCE-6000,
A7/A7II/A7RII, ...) write no plain 0x7313/0x7310/0x74c7 tags in the raw IFD,
so the decoder used unit WB multipliers (strong green cast, e.g. the CC0
DSC-RX100M3 sample), black 512 (800 on 1-inch sensors), and kept padding
columns at the right edge.

- White balance: WB_RGBLevels from the maker note's enciphered Tag2010
  block (layouts per ExifTool's Tag2010a..i tables; byte substitution
  p^3 mod 249 checked black-box on 15 CC0 files: SonyISO matches Exif ISO,
  ILCE-7M3 levels match its plain 0x7313).
- Black level: recovered from the encrypted SR2SubIFD by known-plaintext
  analysis (constant key in every file; RX100M6/ILCE-7M3 plain 0x7310 as
  plaintext; 8 keystream bytes at offset 2510, plausibility-checked).
- Crop: DNG DefaultCrop or the maker note's FullImageSize.
- "12-bit uncompressed" ARWs hold 14-bit-scale data: black/white follow it.
- Render cache version bumped; corpus manifest + corpus test, unit tests.

title: M12: SAM 3 Object and Describe masks (pure Rust, Metal)
author: GuintherKovalski
body:
## AI masks with SAM 3: Object (clicks) and Describe (text)

Closes part of **LR-MASK-OBJECTS** (M12) and the "AI masks" gap in `docs/parity.md`: real segmentation for the Masking panel, from Meta's **SAM 3** (Segment Anything with Concepts), run **in LightCraft itself, in pure Rust**. On macOS it runs on the GPU through Metal; elsewhere on the CPU for now.

### What users get
- **Object** tile: click the thing to select it; each click refines it, **⌥-click** leaves a part out (green / red dots on the photo).
- **Describe** tile: type what to select — `sky`, `the red car`, or `car, road` — every instance the model finds joins the mask.
- **+ / −** right under the selected mask (and the Add / Subtract / Intersect menus) combine selections, e.g. Describe `car` → + → Describe `road`; − → Describe `people`.
- **Detail pass**: about a second after the last click (or after a description), the area around the selection is segmented again, zoomed in, from a sharper source — in the background — for 5–10× finer edges on small objects.
- **Edge** slider per selection: −100 crisper … +100 feathered (resolution independent).
- **Hover a mask** in the Masks list to see it in red on the photo. The always-on overlay is now off by default (O / the eye still turn it on).

### How it's built

title: Issue #150: Raw: NEF colour from the camera JPEG; 12-bit NEF black level
author: treyreynolds
body:
Fixes #150.

LightCraft has no colour matrix for Nikon cameras. Because of this, NEF files showed colours that were too gray and
too green. This change also corrects a black-level error in 12-bit NEF files. That error made some 12-bit files
almost black.

**Changes**

- **Colour.** LightCraft now calculates a colour matrix and a tone curve from the JPEG preview in each NEF file.
  Sony ARW files already use this procedure (`docs/camera-preview-colour.md`). The same quality checks apply. If the
  fit is not good, LightCraft keeps the neutral colour.
- **White balance.** For NEF files, white balance is relative to the as-shot look, as for ARW files. Photos with
  "As Shot" white balance in old catalogs do not change. A render test showed this.
- **One rule for both.** The function `camera_preview::file_local_look` selects the formats for the fit and for the
  relative white balance. `Photo::relative_wb` in the catalog uses the same formats.
- **12-bit black level.** Nikon stores the black level (maker note `0x003d`) in 14-bit units, also in 12-bit files.
  The decoder read it as a 12-bit value. Now the decoder divides it by 4 for 12-bit files. We checked the D750,
  D780, D850, D7500 and Z 50. Older bodies (D5100, D7000) do not have this tag. They do not change.
- **Corpus and cache.** The corpus gets the D7500 12-bit and 14-bit lossless samples (CC0, raw.pixls.us). The render
  cache version increases to 9. Because of this, LightCraft makes the old NEF thumbnails again.

**Results**

We rendered each file at 1200 px and compared it with the JPEG in the same file. The value is the mean colour
difference (CIE76 ΔE, at 200 px). A smaller value is better.

| File | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| D750, 12-bit lossless | 24.2 | 5.3 |
| D750, 14-bit lossless | 13.2 | 5.4 |
| D780, 12-bit lossless | 44.6 | 4.4 |
| D850, 12-bit lossless | 26.4 | 2.9 |
| D850, 14-bit lossless | 14.3 | 2.9 |
| D7500, 12-bit lossy | 34.3 | 4.6 |
| D7500, 12-bit lossless | 33.9 | 4.6 |

title: Faces: one-click model download, a person's page, and a scan that follows what you are doing
author: voshart
body:
Fifth of six; stacked on #174.

> **Draft, stacked.** A PR from a fork can only target `main`, so this diff also contains the PRs below it (#170, #172, #173, #174). **New here: the last 5 commits** — [see only this PR's changes](https://github.com/voshart/lightcraft/compare/pr/faces-4-recognition...pr/faces-5-download-person). A hang found on the way (scan jobs waiting at the memory gate on a rayon worker, one run in three losing photos) is fixed and explained in `faces_worker.rs`.

title: CR3: full-size preview and metadata from the container
author: cruzer45
body:
## Problem
CR3 files (every Canon body since about 2018) imported as preview-only with the small 1620×1080 `PRVW` JPEG and no metadata: no camera, capture time, exposure, lens or GPS. Nothing read the ISO-BMFF container.

## Changes
- **`crates/meta/src/cr3.rs`:** a bounds-checked CR3 box parser. It reads:
  - the Canon `uuid` box: `CMT1`–`CMT4` and `THMB`;
  - each track's sample entry (JPEG or raw), the raw `CMP1` coding header, and where the track's data sits in the file;
  - the XMP `uuid` box.

  Every size and offset is checked against the buffer, and nesting depth and box count are capped.
- **Metadata:** `CMT1` (IFD0), `CMT2` (Exif) and `CMT4` (GPS) are merged into one TIFF Exif block, so `extract`/`from_tiff` read a CR3 like any TIFF-based raw. XMP comes from its `uuid` box. The maker note (`CMT3`) is left out because its offsets are relative to its own block.
- **Preview:** the full-size JPEG track is used first (6960×4640 on an EOS R6 Mark III), with `PRVW`/`THMB` as the fallback. Imports now report the full image size.
- Docs: parity row (LR-IMP-FORMATS), ROADMAP, what's new.

Raw (CRX) data is still not decoded, so CR3 photos remain preview-only. Layout facts come from the public CR3 format description (Laurent Clévy's notes) and were verified black-box on EOS R6 Mark III files. No third-party code was used.

## Tests
- Synthetic CR3 covering boxes, tracks and merged Exif; a truncation and corruption sweep (never panics); JPEG track preferred over `PRVW`, with the fallback when the track points outside the file.
- Checked by hand on nine EOS R6 Mark III CR3s (full-frame and crop mode). Each imports at full size with capture time and time zone, camera, lens, ISO, aperture, shutter and focal length, in about 0.1 s.
- Locally: fmt, clippy and parity pass, and the meta, raw and engine tests pass.

title: LR-BEHAV-LOCALIZE: a language table, Simplified Chinese, and per-script font fallback
author: lzjtugjc
body:
## What this does

LightCraft's localization was hardcoded to English + Japanese: a two-variant enum, an `is_japanese()` gate compiled into the format macro, one catalog pair, and a font stack that only knew Japanese faces. Adding a language meant touching the menus, the settings row, the checkmark logic, the format macro and the font fallback — five unrelated places.

This turns a language into **data** and adds Simplified Chinese as the second translation.

### A language is now one table entry

```rust
language_table! {
    En, "en";
    ZhHans, "zh-hans", "简体中文", "Hans", include_str!("../locales/zh-hans.json");
    Ja, "ja", "日本語", "Jpan", include_str!("../locales/ja.json");
}
```

BCP-47 code, endonym (written in the language itself), ISO 15924 script, catalog. The Language menu, the Settings row, the keyboard-shortcut sheet and the control channel's command list are all built from that table, and `build.rs` picks up `locales/<code>-formats.json` by name. **Another language is one table entry plus two catalogs** — see the new `docs/localization.md`. The language ids stay conventional: `app.language.english` / `app.language.zh-hans` / `app.language.japanese`.

Settings now persist the BCP-47 code rather than the Rust variant name, so a language can be renamed in code without invalidating saved preferences; old `ui.json` files still load. `LIGHTCRAFT_LANGUAGE` accepts system-style tags (`zh_CN`, `ja_JP.UTF-8`, `en-US`).

### Simplified Chinese

- `locales/zh-hans.json` — 1019 entries, key set identical to `ja.json`.
- `locales/zh-hans-formats.json` — 102 entries for messages with runtime values.
- Glyphs come from the Noto Sans CJK SC faces craft-fonts already carries (`scripts: Hans`). Measured: BIZ UDPGothic has no glyph for characters like 简 (cmap 11 741 codepoints) while Noto Sans CJK SC covers the whole catalog (44 810).

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: camera-look hue table, chroma curve and per-model camera profiles
author: haraldh
body:
## Problem

Raws without a camera colour matrix (Sony ARW, and Nikon NEF since #150) get their look fitted to their own embedded JPEG. On ILCE-7M4 photos that fit got two things visibly wrong:

- **Saturated yellow-greens turned olive.** A lime shirt rendered 16° yellower than the camera JPEG. One 3×3 matrix can't follow the camera's hue-dependent rendering: the few saturated pixels carry little weight, and a matrix fitted to them alone breaks everything else.
- **Sunlit scenes looked yellow.** The camera JPEG bleaches colours toward white in highlights and saturates shadows (a per-channel curve). Our luminance-only curve kept full colour up to white, so bright rock came out cream (+4 b* in the brightest fifth of the picture).

## Changes

1. **Hue/saturation/value table** (5 × 72 × 5, DNG `ProfileHueSatMap` layout, linear ProPhoto) fitted to the residuals after the matrix. It is kernel-smoothed, shrinks to identity where samples are sparse, leaves neutrals untouched and keeps luminance. The value axis is needed: dark yellows turn toward orange, bright yellow-greens toward green.
2. **Chroma curve**: `CameraTone` gains 8 nodes of chroma scale by display luminance, fitted per photo (including highlights) and applied after the tone map on CPU and GPU. Old smart-preview headers load with an identity curve.
3. **Selection**: the matrix-only and matrix + table looks are completed and compared in gamma-encoded values (in linear values a slightly missed bright rock outweighed a clearly wrong dark shirt). The acceptance gates are unchanged.
4. **Camera profiles pooled per model.** A small object gives one photo too few samples. `lightcraft-cli calibrate [--max N] [--out DIR] FOLDERS…` pools the colour pairs of many photos per model and fits one matrix (from white-balanced camera RGB) and one table. It writes `<config>/camera-profiles/<model>.json` (or `$LIGHTCRAFT_CAMERA_PROFILES`). Photos of a profiled model take that colour and fit only their own tone and chroma curves. F…

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: built-in ILCE-7M4 camera profile
author: haraldh
body:
Builds on #201 (merged), which added camera profiles and `lightcraft-cli calibrate`.

## What

A built-in colour profile for the **Sony ILCE-7M4** (`assets/camera-profiles/ILCE-7M4.json`, 118 KB).

- Profiles in `assets/camera-profiles/` are compiled in through `camera_profiles::BUNDLED`, so the app, CLI and web build all have them.
- A local profile (`<config>/camera-profiles/<model>.json` or `$LIGHTCRAFT_CAMERA_PROFILES`) replaces the built-in one.
- Built-in profiles are part of the render cache keys.

## Provenance

#201 tested a profile built the same way from 300 Feb–Aug photos on 29 held-out September photos. Mean ΔE against the camera JPEG went from 3.54 to 3.10, and a lime shirt's hue from 68° to 82° (JPEG 81.5°). title: Tests: pass on Windows (path separators, temp folder inside home, one GPU edge pixel)
author: voshart
body:
﻿Nine tests fail on Windows on `main` today, plus the GPU equivalence test on some adapters. None is a product bug; they are assumptions in the tests. With this change `cargo test --workspace` passes on Windows (and still on Linux/macOS, where nothing changes):

- **Paths built with a hard-coded `/`** (`Path::join("a/b")`, hand-written JSON path strings) compare unequal to the platform-separator paths the code returns. They are now joined by component or JSON-encoded (CLI devices test, find-missing, folder move, import review).
- **The rename tests' model volume** spells paths with `/` while the planner joins with the host separator; the fake file system now treats both as one.
- **The Local-folder UI tests** assume the temp folder is outside the home folder. On Windows it is inside, so the sidebar lists the test folder inside Home's tree rather than as its own location. The tests now hide Home for the test where needed, and wait for the folder listing (read on a worker thread) instead of three frames, which also made them flaky under load.
- **GPU equivalence, embedded lens + perspective:** one pixel on the bottom edge differs between the CPU and the card (they fall on different sides of the sampling boundary; 0.0003 % of channels). The test now tolerates up to two edge pixels and still requires the interior to match within the existing limit.

No product code changes.

title: Codecs: a CFA pattern in any IFD marks a TIFF as a raw (Sony A7 IV lossless-M ARW)
author: voshart
body:
﻿A Sony A7 IV "lossless, medium" ARW (from the public raw.pixls.us samples) was detected as a plain TIFF, so it never reached the raw decoder. Its raw SubIFD has compression 7 (lossless JPEG) and a YCbCr photometric interpretation, which none of the markers in `tiff_is_raw` flags.

Its SubIFD does carry the TIFF/EP `CFAPattern` tag (0x828E), which only sensor data has whatever the compression, so `CFARepeatPatternDim` / `CFAPattern` in any walked IFD now marks the file as raw. A synthetic test builds that SubIFD (and the same file without the tag, which stays an ordinary TIFF). `corpus_raw_is_routed` over the full sample set passes; it was the one that found it.

Whether the raw decoder can then decode that particular variant is a separate question; this only stops it being mistaken for a TIFF.

title: Library: Random sort with a stable seed and Reshuffle
author: nledford
body:
## Summary
- Adds `SortKey::Random` and `Sort.seed`. Photos are ordered by a splitmix64 rank of `(seed, photo id)`: the same seed always gives the same order, and photos added or edited later never reshuffle the others. Descending is the exact reverse.
- `library.sort` accepts `key: "random"` and an optional `seed` (0..2^53-1, so JSON-double clients read it back exactly; bad seeds are errors and leave the sort unchanged). Switching to Random from another key picks a fresh seed; re-choosing it or changing only the direction keeps the shuffle.
- New `library.shuffle` command picks a new seed (or takes one). It is derived from the previous seed and the session clock, so no RNG or `rand` dependency is needed and tests stay deterministic.
- Sort menu (View → Sort and the bottom bar) gains Random and Reshuffle; Ascending/Descending are disabled and show no check while Random is active. Ja/zh-Hans/zh-Hant strings added; README and `docs/parity.md` updated.
- Sort is one global setting, so this applies to the library, albums and folders alike. The shuffle is saved with the view state.

title: Build: resolve a relative CRAFT_FONTS_DIR against the workspace root
author: Ndsanes
body:
## Problem

A build script's cwd is its **package** root, so the documented `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=../craft-fonts` resolves to `crates/craft-fonts` and finds nothing:

```
warning: building without craft-fonts: CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=../craft-fonts:
         ../craft-fonts/fonts/manifest.txt: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

That is the spelling the README and craft-fonts' `integration.md` both give, written relative to the workspace root. Anyone following it gets a build with no CJK fonts, and the only symptom is one warning line buried in the compile log.

The resulting build is hard to diagnose from the UI: it starts, the language menu lists all four languages, and selecting 简体中文 or日本語 renders every label as empty boxes — indistinguishable from a broken translation.

## Change

- `resolve()` a relative `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` against both plausible roots (workspace root, then package root) and use whichever is a directory.
- Count what was embedded and warn when nothing was — previously only a *wrong* `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` warned, while omitting it entirely was silent.

Absolute paths and `wasm32`'s font subsetting are untouched.

## Verification

- `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=../craft-fonts cargo build --release -p lightcraft-cli` now embeds all six faces with no warning; previously it embedded none.
- `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=../craft-fonts cargo test -p lightcraft-ui-egui i18n::tests` — 17 passed, including the CJK glyph-coverage tests.
- Settings → General → Language renders English / 简体中文 / 繁體中文（台灣）/ 日本語, and clicking 简体中文 switches the whole UI.
- `cargo test --workspace` — no failures. `cargo xtask fmt`, `layers`, `parity`, `assets` all pass.

Note: `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` fails on `xtask/src/layers.rs:186` (`collapsible_match`), which is present on `main` independently of this branch.

title: Library: switching libraries no longer shows the old library's sidebar
author: nledford
body:
## Problem
After creating or opening another library (File → Open Library…), the sidebar kept the previous library's data (All Photos / Picks counts, the By Date tree, keywords) while the grid correctly said "0 photos".

## Cause
The sidebar counts, keyword tree, date groups and the grid's photo list are cached by `catalog.revision` alone. A catalog loaded from disk counts revisions from 0 (`crates/catalog/src/journal.rs`), and so does a brand-new empty one. Opening an empty library after one that had not been edited in the session gave the same revision, so every cache was a hit. A demo library does not show it because it has edits applied in the session.

## Fix
`Session::open_stores` gives each catalog loaded in the process its own revision range (`counter << 32`), so no revision-keyed cache can mistake one library for another. This covers all such caches, not just the sidebar.

## Test plan
- [x] `opening_another_library_drops_the_old_librarys_cached_panels` (new, `crates/ui-egui/src/tests_switch_library.rs`): reopens a seeded library from disk, then opens an empty one; failed before the fix (cached All Photos count 24, expected 0), passes after. Checks counts, keyword tree, date groups and the grid list.
- [x] `cargo xtask ci` green (fmt, clippy, test, parity, layers, assets, wasm)
- [ ] Not re-run by hand in the desktop app

Independent of #217 (random sort); this branch is based on `main`.

title: Issue #212: Raw: keep vendor white balance when writing DNG
author: Gremiger
body:
Refs #212

## Summary

Issue #212 reports NEF files (Nikon D3300) developing very dark and green, both when imported directly and when copied as DNG. I hit the same issue with a Nikon D3400 on 0.2.1.

- **Direct NEF import** is already fixed on `main` by 22c6aa6 (#165, "NEF colour from the camera JPEG; 12-bit NEF black level"), which is not in a release yet. I checked this with the reporter's `DSC_9077.NEF` and with my own D3400 files: v0.2.1 renders them dark and green and `main` renders them correctly.
- **Convert to DNG / Copy as DNG** was still broken on `main`. This PR fixes it.

## Root cause

NEF (and other vendor raws without a colour matrix) store the as-shot white balance as vendor multipliers in `RawImage::wb_multipliers`, not as a DNG `AsShotNeutral`. `write_dng` only wrote `AsShotNeutral` / `AsShotWhiteXY` from `raw.color`, so a DNG converted from a NEF had no white balance. It decoded with WB `[1, 1, 1]`, which renders raw camera RGB: dark and green.

## Fix

When the source has no DNG white of its own, `write_dng` writes the reciprocal of the vendor multipliers as `AsShotNeutral`. The decoded DNG then gets the same white-balance multipliers as the original NEF.

## Tests

- New regression test `vendor_white_balance_survives_dng_conversion` (`crates/raw/tests/dng.rs`): it fails without the fix and passes with it.
- `cargo xtask ci` is green locally (fmt, clippy, test, parity, layers, assets, wasm).
- Manual check: I converted a real D3400 NEF to DNG and developed it. Before the fix it was dark and green; after the fix it is neutral. (Checked in MacOS 27)

## Known follow-up (not in this PR)

A converted DNG now has the correct white balance, but it renders flatter and darker than its NEF. The NEF's starting look (tone curve and colour) is fitted to its embedded camera JPEG (`camera_preview::file_local_look`). The DNG doesn't get that look: `file_local_look` excludes DNG, and the writer doesn't carry over the embedded preview or the fitted look.

title: Export: clear error when there's no export folder (instead of "Access is denied")
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #237

### Problem
On Windows, exporting without choosing a folder failed with:

> Exported 0 of 1 photo · 1 failed: green_test.png: Access is denied. (os error 5)

`default_export_dir()` built `~/Pictures/LightCraft Exports` from `HOME`, which Windows usually doesn't set, so the folder resolved to `""`. The photo was then written by bare filename into the process's working directory (often not writable). Clearing the dialog's Folder field took the same path on every OS.

### Changes
- **Windows default folder:** `default_export_dir()` now uses `%USERPROFILE%\Pictures\LightCraft Exports` on Windows. That matches `default_library_dir()` in `engine/src/library.rs`, so Export works out of the box there, the same as Lightroom defaulting to a real folder.
- **Clear error:** if the Export dialog's Folder is blank, or no folder can be worked out at all, `app.export` fails with **"You need to specify an export location!"** before writing anything. An exact `path` (single-file export) still needs no folder.
- **Error is visible:**
  - The Export dialog stays open and shows the error, as Import already does, so the user can pick a folder without re-entering their settings.
  - The Export with Preset menu and the Export with Previous shortcut show the error too, where before a failure did nothing.

### Tests
- Extended `menubar::tests::export_with_preset_submenu`: a blank `dir` returns `NO_EXPORT_FOLDER` and writes nothing.
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-ui-egui`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean. `headless::keyword_list_filters_renames_and_suggests` and `tests_masking::local_folder_tree_expands_and_browses` can time out under the full parallel run, but they pass when run on their own, both on `main` and with this branch.

title: M11.3: Olympus compressed ORF decoding
author: marek-hubar
body:
Adds decoding of the 12-bit compressed ORF that Olympus / OM System bodies write, so these raws stop opening as embedded previews only (`LR-IMP-FORMATS`).

## Provenance — please read before merging

**This decoder is not clean-room in the sense of `nefc.rs`.** It was written by an AI model (Claude). No public prose description of the bit stream exists, and the model did not derive the format independently: the first coder it tried already reproduced the reference image exactly, so the structure was recalled from training data, most likely the open-source decoders of the dcraw family, and only confirmed by measurement.

- No decoder source was opened, searched for or fetched while writing it, so nothing was transcribed from a file at hand.
- The author cannot rule out that the code resembles the implementations the format was learned from.
- Reference pixels came from LibRaw's `unprocessed_raw` binary (0.21.4), run as a black box on CC0 samples. Its output was used for comparison only and is not in the repository.

The header of `crates/raw/src/vendor/orfc.rs` records this, along with the measurements. Whether that is acceptable under the project's clean-room rule is the maintainers' call; `ROADMAP.md` and `docs/parity.md` point to the note rather than presenting this as clean-room work.

title: GPU: faster warp coverage mask, warp formulas written once (depends on #243)
author: radialmonster
body:
**Depends on #243.** This branch is built on it. Until #243 merges, GitHub shows its commits here too; review only the last two:

- `2b2ebfc` Geom: write the warp formulas once over a Real scalar (f64 or Interval)
- `1237e19` GPU: build the warp coverage mask per block with interval bounds

#243 fixes a GPU/CPU edge mismatch by building a coverage mask with the CPU's f64 framing decision, one pixel at a time. This PR makes that mask 3.5–24× faster without changing a single bit of it, and without a second copy of the warp math.

**How**
- The warp formulas are written once, generic over a small `Real` trait (`crates/geom/src/real.rs`) implemented for `f64` and an outward-rounded `Interval`. The formulas are `Affine`/`Homography::apply`, `to_corrected`, `corrected_to_source` and `embedded_warp`. The existing f64 functions are thin wrappers, so callers are unchanged.
- One shared `Warp::framing` chain serves the per-pixel check (`covers`), the block check and the CPU reference renderer (`sample_warped`). The image edges are defined once.
- The mask decides 32×16 blocks from interval bounds. A block that can't be decided falls back to the per-pixel check: one with a divisor that could be zero, a non-finite bound, or a bound straddling the edge. About 2.7% of blocks fall back at full size and 6–8% at preview size.

**Correctness**
- **f64 path bit-identical:** the rewrite only commutes operands; there is no reassociation and no fma.
  - A test hashes the output bits of every formula for 2,000 random warps × 40 points, plus the ±1e-300 clamp and zero/subnormal cases. The expected hash was computed on the unmodified pre-change formulas.
  - Reassociating one expression changes the hash.
- **Masks identical:** every block decision is sound. Each interval op takes the same f64 operands in the same order, rounding to nearest is monotonic, and bounds round outward. So the bounds contain every pixel's rounded result. No extra margin is needed.
  - New tests compare every pixel …

title: Web: time raw preview decodes with web_time so wasm doesn't panic
author: andrewyao
body:
## Problem
`load_bytes_now` (`crates/engine/src/files.rs`) timed the binned demosaic with `std::time::Instant::now()`. On `wasm32-unknown-unknown` that panics ("time not implemented on this platform"), so opening a raw file in the web build aborted the decode.

## Fix
Use `web_time::Instant`. `library.rs` already does this, and `web-time` is already a dependency of the engine. Native builds behave the same, because `web_time` re-exports `std::time` there.

## Verification
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-engine --all-targets -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo check -p lightcraft-engine --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`: builds. Its one `unused_mut` warning in `devices.rs` is already on `main`.
- Manual: with this change, the web build loaded a folder of 20 raws and rendered the grid and loupe. Before it, the decode panicked.

Other `std::time` calls in the engine (`availability.rs`, `devices.rs`, `import.rs`, `guard.rs`, `export.rs`) aren't touched here. Some may run on wasm too and deserve the same treatment.

title: CI: pick build jobs from available RAM, not installed RAM
author: radialmonster
body:
#243 (merged) made `cargo xtask ci` choose build jobs from **installed** RAM (one per 2 GB). On a busy machine that overcommits. On a 32 GB desktop with browsers, a VM and editors open, about 7 GB was free and the rule chose 16 jobs. A fresh build then pushed free RAM below 1 GB in 13 seconds.

**Change:** one build job per 1.5 GB of RAM **available when CI starts**, capped at the CPU count. With line-table debuginfo, 4 jobs measured about 3 GB in use, so roughly half the available RAM stays spare.

- **How available RAM is read:**

  | OS | Source |
  |---|---|
  | Linux | `MemAvailable` |
  | Windows | `Win32_PerfFormattedData_PerfOS_Memory.AvailableMBytes` |
  | macOS | `vm_stat` free + inactive + speculative pages |

- **Fallbacks:** if available RAM can't be read, half the installed RAM is assumed; if neither can, 4 jobs.
- **Test threads** still follow, capped at 4.
- **Overrides:** explicit `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` / `RUST_TEST_THREADS` still win.

**Test plan:**
- `cargo xtask ci`, all 7 steps green, fresh build using the new rule: about 9.4 GB available at start → 6 jobs; peak commit 6.6 GB; free RAM never below 6.1 GB; 636 s.
- The `ci_jobs` unit test covers 4 GB and 8 GB machines, a busy 32 GB machine with 7 GB free (4 jobs, not 16), the CPU cap, the minimum of 1, and unknown RAM.
- Not run on macOS or Linux; the `vm_stat` / `MemAvailable` parsing is untested there.

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: RW2 format 8: decode each 2×2 cell column by column
author: radialmonster
body: Fixes #254 (follow-up to #215). Raw format 8 (GH6, GH7, G9 II, S5 II / IIX, S9, S1R II, S1 II) codes each 2×2 cell column by column: top-left, bottom-left, top-right, bottom-right. `decode_strip` placed the values in row order, which puts the two green samples of every RGGB cell on each other's sites. Flat areas are unaffected, so colour and the camera-look fit were fine. Every sharp edge got a one-pixel teal/orange zipper. *Panasonic DC-G9M2. 1: camera JPEG. 2: main. 3: this PR. 100% crop shown at 2×. More crops and the measurements are in #254.* ## Changes (`crates/raw/src/vendor/rw2.rs`) - `decode_strip`: value `k` of a cell goes to row `k % 2`, column `k / 2`. Before, it was row `k / 2`, column `k % 2`. - `encode_strip` (test helper): the same order, so `format8_strips_round_trip` still round-trips. It passed with either order, which is why it didn't catch this. - New `format8_cell_is_coded_column_by_column`: hand-codes one cell with the values 1, 2, 3, 4, independent of `encode_strip`, and checks where they land.
