title: Fix Nikon NEF CropArea and embedded preview colour space
author: Hanmo123
body:
Nikon NEFs currently ignore maker-note CropArea, and embedded JPEG previews without ICC/EXIF metadata default to sRGB even when Nikon records Adobe RGB. This can produce incorrect framing and preview colour.

This is the first isolated change requested in #216, based on current upstream `main` (`8734e95`), including #215 and #213.

### Changes
- Read and bounds-check Nikon CropArea (0x0045), preserving the active area and CFA origin. Apply the default crop after demosaicing and report the cropped metadata dimensions.
- Read Nikon ColorSpace (0x001e) and use it as a fallback only for JPEG previews without ICC/EXIF metadata, before transfer decoding and resizing. Existing JPEG metadata takes precedence.
- Share the preview decoder across quick previews, preview-only RAW and the existing camera-look reference decode. The three-line change in `camera_preview.rs` only routes decoding through this helper; it does not change the fitting algorithm.
- Bump the render cache version to invalidate older previews.

### Scope
No Tint sign change, Kelvin control, camera-temperature metadata, tone/chroma fitting changes, training/validation changes, or highlight reconstruction changes are included.

### Validation
Synthetic regressions cover valid/invalid crop rectangles, CFA-origin preservation, Nikon colour-space tags, fallback colour decoding before resizing, and JPEG metadata precedence. A private Z 8 sample crops from an 8280 × 5520 sensor to 8256 × 5504. Private images/screenshots are not included.

`cargo xtask ci`: all seven steps passed; 1071 tests passed, 10 ignored. The actual Z 8 file was reopened in the headless app: 8256 × 5504, existing relative WB controls retained, no GPU fallback.

title: Correct global Tint direction (compatibility review)
author: Hanmo123
body:
Global Tint currently renders opposite to its green-to-magenta slider: negative values add magenta and positive values add green. This isolated PR fixes the sign convention for review, as requested in #216.

### Change and reasoning
Tint expresses the correction applied to the image. Positive Tint should add magenta; its source illuminant must therefore be greener, because Bradford adaptation removes the source cast. Use `Duv = +tint / TINT_SCALE` and update the inverse conversion consistently. CPU and GPU share this matrix; auto WB and the picker use the inverse conversion. Invalidate cached renders.

### Compatibility — requires review before merging
This changes the interpretation of existing nonzero global Tint values, including saved edits, presets, and imported XMP. It is not a NEF-only fix. This PR does not silently rewrite or migrate those values.

- As Shot remains an identity adjustment.
- For rendered/uncalibrated RAW with a zero As Shot tint, negating an old custom Tint restores its previous appearance.
- Calibrated RAW may carry a nonzero As Shot tint in catalog/source metadata. A general migration requires separate consideration; negating only the custom value is not a universal migration.
- Local mask tint and calibration shadow tint already use the correction convention and are unchanged.

This PR is ready for review and compatibility testing. Please agree on the compatibility/migration policy before merging. This branch is independent of the NEF metadata PR; if another render change lands first, its cache-version bump must be rebased before merging.

### Scope
No NEF crop/preview colour-space changes, camera-look fitting changes, or Kelvin controls are included.

### Evidence
- The existing `Track::Tint` is documented and painted green → magenta, while local mask tint already reduces green for positive values.
- The synthetic neutral-patch regression fails before this fix: Tint −50 renders sRGB `[129, 113, 128]`, visibly magenta. It checks both dire…

title: Fetch: opt-in bearer token, validated file specs, borrowed FileSpec, download_url
author: voshart
body:
﻿Follow-up to #210 (which moved the downloader into this crate unchanged). Two small things, both so the crate can serve downloads whose names, sizes and addresses come from somewhere less trusted than a table in the source:

## What changes
- **A bearer token is only sent when the caller asks for one.** Until now `fetch_file` read `LIGHTCRAFT_SAM3_TOKEN` for every download, so any other caller's request to the same host would have carried SAM 3's token. `Options` gains `token_env: Option<&'static str>` (default `None`); the SAM 3 downloader names its variable. The token is still sent only over https, only to the host the download began at, never to a host a redirect leads to (`bearer()` is a small pure function with a test for each case).
- **Caller-supplied specs are validated before the disk is touched.** A file name must be an ordinary, unique one: no separators, drive or stream syntax (`:`), control characters, leading or trailing dots, trailing spaces, Windows device names (`CON`, `NUL`, `COM1`…) or `.part` suffix. The size must be non-zero and within the caller's bound, the SHA-256 well formed (64 lower-case hex digits), and the number of files, mirrors and attempts bounded. URLs are capped at 16 KiB and error messages no longer echo the whole URL (it can carry a signature).
- `FileSpec` borrows its strings (`FileSpec<'a>`), so a name read from a file needs no `Box::leak`; callers with `&'static str` are unchanged.
- `download_url` fetches one file from an exact address, query string included, for signed links; the local file name never comes from the URL, redirects or response headers.

## Checks
`cargo xtask ci` passes. New tests cover the token cases, hostile names, sizes and hashes, URL limits and `download_url`, all against local synthetic servers (no internet).

The change is in the crate's own files plus one line each in the SAM 3 callers that now name their token variable.

title: macOS menu: single-key shortcuts reach egui (E, C, ⇧P, ratings…)
author: xak47d
body:
## Problem

On macOS (0.2.1 and current `main`), shortcuts shown in the menu bar without ⌘ do nothing: E, C, H, M, ⇧P, ⇧V, I, K, D, Y, J, O, ratings 0–5, labels 6–9, P / U, and so on. Keys that aren't in any menu (Space, G, X, ⌫) and ⌘ shortcuts work.

## Cause

`NativeMenu::publish_shortcuts` puts every shortcut that has a menu accelerator into `LightcraftApp::native_shortcuts`, and `shortcuts::handle` skips those keys, assuming the menu bar runs them. But AppKit only offers a key press to the menu bar when it carries ⌘ or ⌃, or is a function key. A plain key, or one with only ⇧ / ⌥, goes to the window's winit view, which takes it. So no menu item fires and egui ignores the key.

The tests drive keys through the control channel (`ui.key`), which feeds egui directly and never goes through the native menu, so they couldn't catch this.

## Fix

`publish_shortcuts` now lists only the shortcuts the menu bar actually receives (`menu_delivers`: ⌘, ⌃ or a function key). The rest keep their accelerator on the menu item, so the menu still shows the key, and egui runs them. The text-focus handling is unchanged.

## Testing

- `cargo test --release -p lightcraft`: 14 passed. The new `native_menu::tests::single_key_shortcuts_stay_with_egui` fails with the previous behaviour ("E must be left to egui").
- `cargo clippy --release -p lightcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `rustfmt --check`: clean.
- Release build with OS-level key events, not the control channel (macOS, Latin American layout), `--demo` with `LIGHTCRAFT_NO_PREFS=1`:
  - C opens Crop & Rotate, E goes back to Edit, ⇧P opens Presets, 3 / 0 set and clear the rating.
  - ⌘⇧H toggles the histogram once per press, so ⌘ shortcuts don't fire twice.
  - Typing "c" in the search field types the letter and leaves Crop closed.
  - The same build without this change ignored C, ⇧P and 3. The installed 0.2.1 release ignored C and ⇧P too, while ⌘⇧H, Space and F2 worked there.

title: RW2/RWL: apply the distortion correction Panasonic and Leica cameras record in the file
author: radialmonster
body:
Closes #256.

## What it does

Panasonic and Leica cameras record their lens distortion correction in every RW2/RWL (PanasonicRaw tag `0x0119`, ExifTool name DistortionInfo) and apply it to their own JPEG. LightCraft now reads it and applies it under **Lens Corrections ▸ Enable Profile Corrections**, which import turns on for photos that carry a correction. Renders now have the same geometry and framing as the camera JPEG. Files shot with the correction off (e.g. the DMC-GH1 corpus file) are unchanged.

## Which existing mechanism it extends

No new warp code. The RW2 reader expresses the camera's correction as the DNG opcode it is equivalent to: a `WarpRectilinear` in the raw's `OpcodeList3`. From there, everything that already handles DNG-embedded lens data takes over unchanged:

- `embedded_lens()` (`crates/engine/src/files.rs`) turns it into the central `EmbeddedLens` / `EmbeddedWarp` model (`crates/develop/src/settings.rs`).
- The model is applied by the single geometry resample in `crates/pipeline/src/optics.rs`, so CPU, GPU, preview and export all match.
- The "Profile distortion" amount slider, Constrain Crop and orientation handling all apply to it.
- Convert/Copy as DNG keeps the correction, since the opcode is written into the DNG.

The camera's crop after correcting is the warp's `kr0` term. That is the same way a DNG's `WarpRectilinear` scales, so the output framing matches the camera JPEG without a separate crop step.

Two small supporting changes:
- `Opcode::is_lens_correction()` replaces two copies of the same `matches!` (engine loader, merge).
- The loader now removes lens opcodes *before* fitting the RW2 camera look. The look's binned sensor proxy needs an empty `OpcodeList3`, and `corpus_rw2_with_an_in_camera_crop_gets_a_camera_look` fails without the reordering. `camera_profiles::Pool::add` removes them too.

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: fit the camera look away from edges when a lens-corrected JPEG misaligns (#232)
author: radialmonster
body:
Fixes #232.

## Problem

Sony ARW, Nikon NEF and Panasonic RW2 get their starting look from a fit to the camera JPEG embedded in the raw (`crates/engine/src/camera_preview.rs`). When the fit fails its acceptance gates (held-out per-channel RMS ≤ 0.10 and ≥ 30 % better than the fallback), the photo opens with the neutral fallback: grey, flat, too dark.

The A7R II's camera JPEG is distortion-corrected by default ("Distortion Comp.: Auto"), and the raw is not. On the public CC0 ILCE-7RM2 samples (raw.pixls.us; one façade shot in seven variants, FE 24-70 mm at 51 mm) the JPEG is up to 15 px out of 1440 off the render, about one pixel of the 96 px fit proxy. Pixel pairs on the window frames then match unrelated colours. The fit is right, but the misaligned edges alone push its held-out RMS to 0.108–0.115, so it is rejected. The same shot with distortion correction off is fitted at 0.059.

## Change

`fit_pairs_with` keeps the fit on all pixels. When that fit fails the gates, it tries once more, with the same gates, on pairs away from edges: pixels whose 3×3 neighbourhood in either proxy spans a luminance ratio above 3 (`EDGE_CONTRAST`) are left out. There a slight geometric mismatch doesn't change the colour pair. Fits that pass on all pixels are untouched, so no accepted file changes. Camera-profile pooling (`profile_pairs`) is unchanged. `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 11 → 12.

## Results

ΔE76 against each file's camera JPEG after registering the JPEG's geometry to the render (radial fit, `tools/a7rm2-232/registered_de.py`), renders at 1440 px:

| file | held-out RMS, all pixels | away from edges | ΔE median before → after | mean ΔL* before → after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ILCE-7RM2 12-bit compressed | 0.114 rejected | 0.049 accepted | 16.89 → 3.67 | −13.4 → +0.3 |

body:
Closes #245

The browser accepted and persisted `library.preferences {cacheMb}`, but the stored thumbnails stayed over that limit: the worker index pruned with the native default (`DISK_CACHE_BYTES`) instead of the session's budget, so the setting only reached the desktop cache.

- The worker group carries the session's `cache_bytes()` and prunes the index to it when a thumbnail is stored.
- The app refreshes the budget every frame, so changing `cacheMb` applies to the next stored thumbnail without a reload.
- Desktop behaviour is unchanged: its disk cache already attaches with `cache_bytes()`.

Verified with `cargo fmt` and `cargo check -p lightcraft-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`; the existing `thumb_index_prunes_lru` test covers the pruning order the repro exercises.

title: Issue #180: ICC profiles carry a fixed header date, so exports are byte-identical
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #180.

## Cause

`moxcms` stamps the ICC header's creation date/time (ICC.1 §7.2.8, bytes 24–35) with the wall clock on every `ColorProfile::encode()` — `writer.rs` builds the header with `creation_date_time: ColorDateTime::now()`, ignoring the `creation_date_time` field on the profile. Every profile lightcraft embeds goes through `write_matrix_trc` in `crates/codecs/src/icc.rs`, so two exports of one photo with identical settings produced identical pixels and a different embedded profile: the files' hashes never matched, and snapshot/regression comparisons on exported JPEGs could not be byte-exact.

## Fix

- `icc.rs`: `write_matrix_trc` passes the encoded bytes through `fixed_date`, which zeros bytes 24..36 before the existing `align_tags` pass. A profile's bytes now depend only on its colour space and curve. Zero is the conventional "unspecified" value other deterministic profile writers use; readers do not interpret the field. (Setting `ColorProfile::creation_date_time` instead does nothing with moxcms 0.9.1, which is why the fix is on the encoded bytes.)
- No change to the colorants, curves, `chad` or any other tag — only the 12 date bytes.
- Test `written_profiles_are_deterministic`: for every `NamedSpace` (and a linear ProPhoto matrix/TRC profile), two writes are byte-identical, the header date bytes are zero, and the profile ID (bytes 84–99) is still "not computed" rather than a hash that would reintroduce a timestamp.

## Tested

- `cargo test -p lightcraft-codecs icc` — the new test fails on `upstream/main` (the header date bytes carry the current time) and passes here
- `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-codecs --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: Issue #182: library.select and id queries reject a photo id that is not in the library
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #182.

## Cause

`library.select` (the engine command behind MCP `select_photos`) copied the given ids straight into the selection without checking that they are photos of the library. `select_photos {"ids": [9999]}` therefore answered `{"selected": 1}`, and the session's active photo became an id nothing can resolve: the next `render_photo` failed with `no such photo` and `get_develop` with `no photo`, with nothing in the `select_photos` response to say the selection had been invalid. `photo_arg` (the `id?` parameter of `develop.get`, `photo.inspect`, `photo.allMetadata`, `history.list`) accepted an unknown explicit `id` the same way.

## Fix

- `crates/engine/src/cmd/library.rs`: `library.select` checks every id — and `active` — against the catalog **before** touching the selection and fails with `no such photo 9999`. The previous selection and active photo stay in place, so a client's typo does not strand the session. All four modes (`replace`, `add`, `toggle`, `range`) go through the check; the parameter doc says so.
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/query.rs`: `photo_arg` returns `no such photo N` for an explicit id that is not in the library, instead of handing the id on to fail later with a less specific message.
- `docs/mcp.md`: the `select_photos` row documents the error and that the selection is left as it was.
- Tests: engine tests cover an unknown id in each select mode (error, selection unchanged) and `develop.get` with an unknown id; MCP tests cover `select_photos` with an unknown id returning a tool error and the active photo surviving.

The UI's own callers (`import.rs` selecting the first imported photo, the grid, menus, detail panel) only pass ids they just read from the catalog or the import result, so none of them hit the new error.

## Tested

- `cargo test -p lightcraft-engine -p lightcraft-mcp` — the new tests fail on `upstream/main` (`selected: 1`) and pass here
- `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-engine -p lightcraft-mcp --all-targets -- -D warnings`…

title: Camera local tone mapping (ProfileGainTableMap) as a per-photo opt-in
author: BuonBreda
body:
Renders a raw's DNG `ProfileGainTableMap` (Apple ProRAW's local tone mapping) when the photo's Profile option **Camera local tone mapping** is on. The option is per photo and **off by default**. Lightroom Classic renders ProRAW without the map, so off is the parity default.

Built on #427's `GainTableMap` parser. This replaces the first version of this PR, which applied the map at decode time.

## What changes
- **`raw/gaintable`**: `GainTableMap::gain` / `evaluator()` (`GainEval`) per DNG 1.7.1. Tables are interpolated bilinearly with edges replicated. The input is `clamp(weights · (R, G, B, min, max))^gamma` in linear ProPhoto after the baseline exposure, and the index is `input × MapPointsN`, clamped to the last point. Cell math saturates, and maps whose sizes don't match their gains are refused. `SourcePlacement` says where a developed source sits in the active area.
- **`pipeline/local_tone`**: the gain is evaluated per output pixel in the scene-linear stage, before the white balance. Output pixels map back to the active area through the frame (crop, user orientation, lens/perspective warp) and the EXIF orientation. When the option is on, `lin_needs_cpu` routes the stage to the CPU, so CPU and GPU match. `lin_key` includes the option.
- **`develop`**: `Profile::camera_local_tone`. It's omitted from the JSON when off, so existing settings and their hashes are unchanged. Presets and Copy Settings carry it.
- **UI**: a Profile checkbox, shown only when the source carries a map. Translations included.
- `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 16 → 17. Docs: parity row and What's New describe it as an opt-in.

## Verification
- Off renders pixel-identical to `main` on two iPhone 15 Pro ProRAWs (12 MP and 48 MP).
- On adds ~60–75 ms to the scene-linear stage at 1536 × 2048 on a 2-core VM. The cost is the same for both files, because it follows output pixels.
- Tests: `gaintable` unit tests (index and clamping, weights and gamma, interpolation, the overflow cases, `SourcePlacement`) a…

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: ORF colour-filter layout from the file's Exif CFAPattern
author: marek-hubar
body:
Split out of #240 as requested there. **No compressed-ORF decoder**: `orfc.rs` and everything that depended on it are not in this branch, which starts from current `main`. Compressed ORF stays preview-only.

## What changes

All in `crates/raw/src/vendor/orf.rs`:

- **Layout from the file.** The colour-filter layout is read from Exif `CFAPattern` (`0xa302`, Exif 2.3; repeat counts accepted in either byte order) when it describes a 2×2 Bayer cell. BGGR and GBRG were not reachable before.
- **Fallback.** Files without a usable tag still get the green diagonal from the samples, now from totals of 32×32 blocks instead of single-pixel differences, so fine texture no longer outweighs a small red/blue difference. The old version indexed the samples directly; this one uses `get()` and checked arithmetic.
- **Header-only probe.** `probe_info` no longer unpacks 12-bit packed ORFs that state their layout (XZ-2: under 0.1 ms; it ran the same unpack as a decode before, about 11 ms). 16-bit files still read their samples, because their bit depth is measured from them.

## What this does not do

- The E-M1 and E-620 state BGGR in their files, and this reads it correctly, but both write compressed ORF, which still returns `Unsupported`. So **there is no user-visible change for those bodies yet**. For the three uncompressed corpus samples (E-1, E-400, XZ-2) the old guess already gave the right layout. This is groundwork plus a sturdier fallback and a faster probe.
- The header-only probe in #240 mostly skipped decompression. Without a decoder only the packed-12-bit part is left.
- The 11 extra Olympus corpus samples from #240 are not added: they are all compressed bodies.

## Provenance

`CFAPattern` is from the public Exif specification. The fallback and the probe change are our own. Nothing here comes from the decoder in #240. One caveat: the claim that the stated layout matches the picture on the compressed bodies was checked in #240 using that decoder; in this branch it is check…

title: M11.1: add CR3 decoding and measured Canon lens correction
author: wrgdbtry
body:
Supported Canon CR3 files now develop the Bayer sensor image instead of relying on an embedded JPEG. Matched Canon mirrorless lens profiles automatically correct distortion and frame the wider RAW field of view.

- Add clean-room, portable Rust decoding for lossless CRX and version `0x100`/`0x200` C-RAW, with file-derived sensor geometry, as-shot white balance, black/white levels and crop. Select the primary sensor track without substituting Dual Pixel, reduced RAW or HEVC preview tracks.
- Apply measured Canon distortion data consistently on CPU and GPU, with exact camera/lens/focal/crop matching and embedded file corrections taking precedence. Include the pinned Lensfun XML data, attribution and CC-BY-SA licence in Unix and Windows packages; no Lensfun library or external RAW decoder is used.
- Extend guarded per-file camera-JPEG colour fitting to CR3, including independent framing registration. Preserve RAW sensor pixels and use the existing neutral matrix fallback when the fit is unavailable or rejected.
- Migrate the catalog lens field, invalidate earlier rendered caches and document coding, calibration and profile limits in `docs/cr3.md`.

Validation:

- `cargo xtask ci`: all seven stages passed, including WebAssembly checks.
- Six full-sensor references: RAW and C-RAW from Canon M50, R100 and R8 match every sample before cropping or colour processing.
- Real macOS app import, rendering and export; CPU/Metal equivalence within `1/255`, including rotation, partial profile strength and embedded-warp precedence.
- Windows and Linux desktop/CLI compile checks. Runtime validation was performed on macOS.

Unverified CRX configurations return explicit errors and use an embedded JPEG only when available. HEVC previews remain unsupported. JPEG-derived colour is an estimate rather than measured camera calibration. Database profiles provide distortion only; unmeasured lenses, vignetting and TCA are not inferred.

title: Issue #166: `snapshot --script` exits non-zero when a scripted request fails
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #166

## Root cause

`fn snapshot` in `apps/lightcraft-cli/src/main.rs` writes each scripted reply to stdout but never inspects `reply["ok"]`. Only the *implicit* final screenshot (taken when the script took none) was checked, which is why the issue's step 5 exited 1 while the scripted equivalent in step 6 exited 0. `run` already has the opposite contract ("Exit status is non-zero when a command fails").

## Fix

- Count replies with `"ok": false` in the script loop. The run **keeps going** — the failed reply is still printed, later lines still execute and the final `-o` screenshot is still written (continue-and-report, the same shape as `run --keep-going`) — and after the loop (and the background-export wait) `snapshot` returns `Err("{n} scripted request(s) failed")`, which `main` prints as `lightcraft-cli: 1 scripted request(s) failed` and exits 1.
- Usage text for `snapshot --script` and `docs/control-protocol.md` → *Headless rendering* now state the contract.

Continue-and-report rather than stop-at-first was chosen because the existing behaviour of writing every reply and the final screenshot is what a `tour.jsonl` run is for; a CI job still gets the artefacts to look at, and now also the right exit status. No in-repo caller (CI, xtask, docs scripts) depends on a 0 exit with a failing script.

## Tests

- New `snapshot_script_failure_exits_non_zero` in `apps/lightcraft-cli/tests/cli.rs`: a script with `{"method":"ui.set","params":{"view":"grid"}}` followed by a valid `ui.set`; asserts non-zero exit, the `1 scripted request(s) failed` message, both replies still on stdout (first `ok:false` naming `grid`, second `ok:true`), and the final PNG still written at the requested size.
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-cli` (12 passed), `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` all green.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: Issue #157: colour-range mask tolerance narrowed so a sample stops at its own colour
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #157

## Root cause

The CPU evaluator (`crates/pipeline/src/masks.rs`) and the GPU path (`crates/gpu/src/render.rs` → `mask.wgsl` kind 3) agree with each other, but both used `tol = 0.04 + 0.16·refine/100`, with full selection below `tol/2` and a fade to zero at `tol`. At the default Refine 50 that is full selection within **0.06** of the sample in the mask's OkLab metric (a, b at full weight, L at ¼ weight in the squared sum).

The metric is applied after `tonemap_for_select` (`v/(1+v)`), which compresses the two patches from the report hard:

| patch (sRGB) | linear Rec.2020 → tonemapped | OkLab |
|---|---|---|
| 120,150,155 (sampled) | ≈ 0.16, 0.23, 0.25 | L 0.601, a −0.021, b −0.013 (matches the reported sample) |
| 200,198,195 | ≈ 0.37, 0.36, 0.35 | L ≈ 0.715, a/b ≈ 0 |

Distance = √(0.021² + 0.017² + 0.25·0.114²) ≈ **0.063** — just past the 0.06 full-selection edge, so the grey patch was ~99 % selected at Refine 50, ~90 % at 85 and still mostly in at 100. A JND is ~0.01 on this scale, so the old default treated anything within ~6 JND as *the same colour*.

## Fix

`tol = 0.015 + 0.06·refine/100`, computed once in `lightcraft_pipeline::masks::color_range_tolerance(refine)` and used by both the CPU branch and the GPU parameter packing (the gpu crate already depends on pipeline), so the two cannot drift apart again. The WGSL is unchanged — it only receives the scalar.

| Refine | full selection ≤ | gone ≥ | grey patch above |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.0075 | 0.015 | 0 % |
| 50 (default) | 0.0225 | 0.045 | 0 % |
| 85 | 0.033 | 0.066 | ~2 % |
| 100 | 0.0375 | 0.075 | ~24 % |

The slope was chosen so every value the reporter tried (50, 85, 100) keeps a surface ~6 JND away out of the mask, while Refine 100 still spans a usable hue neighbourhood (0.075 in OkLab a/b is e.g. orange → red-orange).

## Tests

- New `masks::tests::color_range_keeps_to_the_sampled_colour` in `crates/pipeline`: builds the report's two patches from their sRGB values (`SRGB.to_space(&RE…

title: Desktop: write log records to a rotating log file as well as standard error
author: switch87
body:
## Why

LightCraft already has a small logger (`StderrLog` in `main.rs`, level from `LIGHTCRAFT_LOG`), but it only writes to standard error, and panics go to `/tmp/lightcraft-panics.log`, which a reboot clears. A launch from a desktop menu or the Dock has no terminal, so an ordinary user has nothing to attach to an issue.

We ran into this in the sister project PhotoCraft (storytold/photocraft#1143): a window that stayed empty on Linux took an hour of `WAYLAND_DEBUG` and `gdb` to understand, while the app had already logged the relevant decision to nowhere. The same logger is now merged in VectorCraft (#465) and PdfCraft (#239).

## What

`apps/lightcraft/src/logging.rs` replaces `StderrLog` (no second logger, no new dependency):

- **Two sinks:** standard error and `logs/lightcraft.log` in the settings directory next to `ui.json` (Linux `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/lightcraft/logs`, default `~/.config/lightcraft/logs`), never in the photo library. `LIGHTCRAFT_NO_PREFS` runs log to standard error only.
- **Rotation:** each launch moves the previous log to `lightcraft.1.log` (and that one to `.2`), so the log of a run that crashed survives the next start.
- **Bounded:** the file stops at 16 MiB with one note; records logged before the file is attached are buffered (max 512).
- **Levels:** `LIGHTCRAFT_LOG` keeps exactly its meaning (`info`/`debug` for `lightcraft*`, anything else warn; a test compares it with the old `enabled()` logic) and takes precedence. Without it, `RUST_LOG` replaces the default with env_logger-style directives; without either the default is `warn,lightcraft*=info`.
- **Panic hook:** registered after the engine guard's hook; it adds an `ERROR` line to the log file (standard error already got the report), using `try_lock` so it can't deadlock. `/tmp/lightcraft-panics.log` is unchanged.
- **Never crash:** no `unwrap`/`expect`/indexing, no `eprintln!` on these paths (the review lesson from vectorcraft#465: it panics on a broken stderr pipe); an unusable direct…

title: Issues #181, #183: `app.export` refuses unknown params and bad values; watermark keys documented and range-checked
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #181
Fixes #183

One PR for both: they are the same code path (`ExportOptions::from_json` and its watermark branch), and the fix for #181 — a strict parser — is where the watermark schema check for #183 has to live.

## Root cause

`ExportOptions::from_json` (`crates/engine/src/export.rs`) reads the keys it recognises and defaults everything else: `p.get(k).and_then(as_u64)` for numbers, `serde_json::from_value(..).ok()` for enums and the `Watermark` object (no `deny_unknown_fields`), with clamps instead of errors. So `longEdgee=400` exported at the 3000 px default, `longEdge=banana` at full size, `qualty=5` at quality 90, `watermark=5` and `{"text":"x","bogus":1}` returned `ok:true`, and `watermark.size: 3` was clamped to 0.5 in the renderer. Nothing told the caller, and the param string listed the object only as `watermark?`.

## Fix

- `from_json` stays **lenient** — it also reads stored prefs (`last_export`) and prefills the Export dialog, where an older key must not break the dialog.
- New `ExportOptions::validate(cmd, params)` and `from_params(params)` (strict): every key must be in `OPTION_PARAMS` or `TARGET_PARAMS` (`id`, `ids`, `path`, `dir`, `preset`, `background`); an unknown key names the nearest known one (`unknown parameter \`longEdgee\` (did you mean \`longEdge\`?)`); every value is checked for kind and range (`quality` integer 1..100, `bitDepth` 8|10|16|32, size keys numbers ≥ 0, enums by their variants, `resize` object keys, `ids` an array of ids, …). A `watermark` must be text or an object of `WATERMARK_PARAMS` with `size` 0.005..0.5 and `inset` 0..0.4 (fraction of the short edge), `imageWidth` 0.01..1 (of the width), `opacity` 0..1, `color` `[r,g,b]` 0..255 — the ranges the renderer draws without clamping, and wider than the Export dialog's own sliders (1–15 % size, 5–100 % opacity, 2–100 % width), which a test pins. Errors go through `bad(cmd, …)` → `invalid parameters for \`app.export\`: …`, the same shape as `photo.rate`. `null` means "no…

title: Issues #164, #169: `--memory` sessions write nothing — no `ui.json`, no settings folder
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #164
Fixes #169

## Root cause

`--help`, the module doc of `apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs` and the README all promise that a `--memory` session "writes nothing", and two code paths ignored the flag:

- **#164** — `PrefsWriter::save` skipped writing only for `keep_file` and `LIGHTCRAFT_NO_PREFS`. `--memory` was passed to `open_session` alone, so the writer saved `ui.json` every few seconds once any UI state changed, replacing the user's saved `thumbSize`, layout or language with the throwaway session's (the README showcase script's `ui.set` calls included).
- **#169** — `gpu_crash_check()` armed the #136 crash sentinel in every session except `LIGHTCRAFT_NO_PREFS`. `with_init_marker` runs `create_dir_all` on the marker's parent, writes `gpu-init.marker`, and removes only the file, so a `--memory` run on a fresh home left an empty `Library/Application Support/LightCraft` (resp. `%APPDATA%\LightCraft`, `~/.config/lightcraft`) behind.

## Fix

- `PrefsWriter` now carries the file it writes (`path: Option<PathBuf>`); `main` passes `None` for `--memory` (and `prefs_path()` is `None` under `LIGHTCRAFT_NO_PREFS` or without a home folder), so nothing is written and no folder created. It also writes nothing while `app.library_problem` is set — the question window and the Continue Without Saving session, which `docs/control-protocol.md` already describes as writing nothing — and resumes once `app.openLibrary` clears it, so the newly opened library is saved as before.
- `gpu_crash_check(in_memory)`: a `--memory` session neither arms the sentinel nor removes a marker it finds. It still *reads* one (new `lightcraft_gpu::backend::read_init_marker`), so after a GPU crash the session starts with GPU rendering off and shows the notice, and the marker stays for the next ordinary launch to report and clear — the discriminating control in #169 (normal launches still write the marker during device creation, and the next launch still reports it) is unchanged.

title: Issue #266: filmstrip labels cut file names on characters, not bytes
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #266

## Root cause
The detail view's filmstrip shortened a long file name with `&name[..13]` (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/detail.rs`), a **byte** slice. For a name with multi-byte characters byte 13 can fall inside a character — for `202407層三限定訂閱圖(4).jpg` it lands inside `限` (bytes 12..15) — so the slice panicked the UI thread as soon as that photo appeared in the strip, and the app quit (exit 101, message on stderr only).

It is the only byte-indexed slice of a user-provided string in `ui-egui` (grepped for `[..n]` / `[n..]` slicing and other truncation helpers).

## Fix
A small `film_label` helper counts **characters**: a name longer than 14 characters is cut to 13 and an ellipsis — the same rule as before for ASCII names, without slicing bytes.

## Tests
- `panels::detail::tests::film_labels_cut_on_characters_not_bytes` — the name from the issue, exactly 14 CJK characters (kept whole), an ASCII name over the limit, a short one, and an empty one.
- `tests_filmstrip::filmstrip_shows_a_cjk_file_name` — headless: renames a demo photo to the name from the issue via `Op::SetFile`, opens the detail view and checks its filmstrip cell is drawn.

Both panicked before the fix with the reported message (`end byte index 13 is not a char boundary; it is inside '限' (bytes 12..15 of string)`); with it, `cargo test -p lightcraft-ui-egui` passes (161 passed, 1 ignored), `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean. Run on a Linux (WSL) build host without a GPU adapter, so GPU-only tests skip.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: Issue #187: the filmstrip highlights every selected photo, not only the active one
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #187

## Root cause
`filmstrip()` in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/detail.rs` painted selection chrome only for the **active** photo (`let sel = Some(*id) == active`). After Edit ▸ Select All, or a ⌘/Shift-click multi-selection, the other selected photos looked unselected even though `session.selection` was right — exactly as the issue describes.

## Fix
Paint it as the grid (`grid.rs`) does:
- every selected photo gets the selected cell fill (`cell_selected`);
- the active one keeps its white frame, the other selected ones get the grid's grey frame (`from_gray(170)`);
- hover tint only for unselected cells, as before.

The `LR-VIEW-FILMSTRIP` row in `docs/parity.md` mentions it; `cargo xtask parity` passes.

## Tests
`tests_scroll::filmstrip_shows_every_selected_photo` (headless, software-painted) samples a filmstrip cell's background next to its thumbnail:
- with one photo selected, the second cell is not filled like the active one;
- after `library.selectAll` the second cell is filled like the active one, and the first stays active;
- after selecting only the first again it is unfilled, and after `library.select` with `mode: toggle` (what a ⌘-click on a filmstrip cell runs) it is filled again.

Before the fix it failed at Select All (`#1C1C1C` canvas instead of `#2D2D2D` selected fill). With it, `cargo test -p lightcraft-ui-egui` passes (160 passed, 1 ignored); `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean. Run on a Linux (WSL) build host without a GPU adapter, so GPU-only tests skip.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: TIFF: invert WhiteIsZero once, and decode 1-, 2- and 4-bit samples
author: Issuenate
body:
Two TIFF decoding bugs in `crates/codecs/src/tiff_codec.rs`, one commit each.

## 1. WhiteIsZero gray TIFFs open as negatives (`cc425d0`)

At every bit depth. The `tiff` crate (0.11) already inverts WhiteIsZero samples as it reads them — `invert_colors` on every chunk read path in `decoder/image.rs`, for 1/2/4/8/16/32/64-bit integer and 32/64-bit float gray — and refuses the WhiteIsZero layouts it can't invert. `tiff_codec.rs` then inverted them a second time. WhiteIsZero is common in scanner and fax output, and CCITT fax uses it by definition.

**Fix:** the second inversion is removed.

## 2. 1-, 2- and 4-bit TIFFs don't open (`88c1e76`)

Bilevel scans, CCITT fax and low-depth gray failed with `sample buffer too short`. The crate returns these samples packed (MSB first, each row padded to a byte); the converter expects one byte per sample.

**Fix:** a small `unpack` spreads them out one per byte, scaled to 0–255 (×255, ×85, ×17 — exact), before conversion, so the rest of the pipeline is unchanged. 3/5/6/7-bit samples and planar multi-sample sub-byte images are refused with an `Unsupported` error rather than guessed at. All arithmetic is checked and the strip length is validated before slicing (never-crash rules).

## Tests

Both tests build their TIFFs byte by byte in code (no media committed), and each fails without its commit:

- `tiff_white_is_zero_is_inverted_once` — 8- and 16-bit, both photometric conventions. Without the fix, the lowest WhiteIsZero sample comes out black instead of white.
- `tiff_samples_narrower_than_a_byte` — 1-bit in both conventions with an odd width and the row padding bits set (to prove they're ignored), 2-bit, 4-bit, and a truncated strip that must return an error, not panic. Without the fix it fails with the original `sample buffer too short`.

Manually: a 600×400 bilevel image, uncompressed and CCITT G4 (generated with PIL, not committed), now decodes to the same pixels PIL reads (white fraction 0.4963 for both).

title: Crop: stop at image edge, lock aspect on every handle, visible lock + custom ratio (#295)
author: nledford
body:
Fixes #295.

## Root cause
The crop drag handed a raw rectangle to `CropGeometry::constrained`, which was written to repair a crop after straightening. Past the image edge it slid the whole frame toward the centre (moving the anchored corner), and the aspect lock was a separate UI-only rule that ignored edge handles.

## Changes
- `lightcraft_geom::drag_crop` (new, `crates/geom/src/crop_drag.rs`): the drag is a domain operation. Opposite edges stay anchored, a locked ratio holds on all eight handles, the frame stops at the image edge and slides along it, minimum size, hostile numbers return the start crop. Given/When/Then scenarios plus property tests.
- `crop.drag` command so UI, CLI, control channel and MCP share it. `crop.aspect` now rejects degenerate custom ratios (non-finite, non-positive, beyond 20:1, non-numeric arrays).
- Crop panel: visible Lock toggle, custom W × H entry, dropdown chevron, button label names the active ratio ("Original", a preset, or `1.37 : 1`) instead of pixel sizes.
- `docs/parity.md` rows LR-CROP-RECT / LR-CROP-ASPECT updated. No separate "As Shot" (Original is the photo's own shape).

## Verification
clippy, layers, assets, parity, and `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` pass. An independent adversarial review found and I fixed: empty crop from tiny custom ratios, locked edge drags unable to grow along a blocked side, extreme-ratio and huge-value handling, 1e-6 overshoot at bounds, loose parsing. Checked visually in a headless snapshot; real mouse drags were not exercised.

Unrelated crash found along the way (`photo.setCaptureTime` overflow in `crates/catalog/src/dates.rs`) is handled in a separate task.

author: hemna
body:
## What

iPhone / Mac **HEIC / HEIF photos open**. This closes the HEIC half of `LR-IMP-FORMATS` (AVIF decode stays open; it needs an AV1 decoder).

- **New crate `crates/heif` (`lightcraft-heif`)** — a thin, panic-guarded wrapper around [`heic-rs`](https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs) (pure Rust, no `unsafe`, MIT OR Apache-2.0, pinned `=0.1.1`): single pictures and grid-tiled photos, 8- and 10-bit (10-bit → 16-bit), alpha auxiliary images, the container's `irot`/`imir`/`clap` transforms, ICC, EXIF and XMP. Without the feature HEIC files are still *recognised* and opening one is a clear "HEIC/HEIF support isn't included in this build" error, never a panic.

- `probe()` reads size/depth/alpha from the container **before any pixel is decoded**, so `max_pixels` refuses a decompression bomb at the header (and `cargo xtask layers` now knows the crate: `heif` is L0, `codecs → heif`).

- Every call into heic-rs runs under `catch_unwind`: PhotoCraft's fuzzing found two out-of-range slices in heic-rs 0.1.1 on malformed files (`boxes.rs:130`, `hevc/decode/recon.rs:70`). **Both are inline-byte regression tests here** (`a_heic_rs_panic_is_a_malformed_error`, `a_heic_rs_panic_is_a_malformed_error` in codecs) — no media committed.

title: Issue #188: Tint follows the DNG / Lightroom sign: + is magenta, − is green
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #188.

## Problem
Dragging Tint towards magenta turned the photo green, and dragging it towards green turned it magenta. `crates/color/src/cct.rs` read a positive tint as a magenta illuminant (below the Planckian locus, `Duv = −tint/3000`). That is the opposite of the DNG specification and Lightroom, where a positive tint is a greener illuminant, which white balance then corrects towards magenta.

LightCraft's own numbers were already on the DNG side. The Daylight, Cloudy and Shade presets carry **+10**, because daylight sits about Duv +0.003 above the locus, and Fluorescent carries **+21**, because fluorescent light is greener. With the old sign those presets pushed the illuminant towards magenta. The DNG SDK defines `kTintScale = −3000` and offsets along an isotherm whose v falls as u rises (for example `t = −0.70471` at 150 mired), so a positive tint raises v ([dng_temperature.cpp](https://lxr.kde.org/source/graphics/digikam/core/libs/dngwriter/extra/dng_sdk/dng_temperature.cpp)).

## Fix
`temp_tint_to_xy` and `xy_to_temp_tint` now use `Duv = +tint/3000`. Both directions flip together, so as-shot tints read from raw files keep rendering the as-shot look. Tints from XMP imports and presets now mean what they mean in Lightroom, and the slider moves the image towards the end of its track that it shows.

## Tests
- New `cct::tests::daylight_has_a_positive_tint`: D65 reads as a tint between +5 and +15, like Lightroom's Daylight preset. `warmer_is_redder` now expects a positive tint to raise v.
- New `pipeline::tests::positive_tint_renders_magenta_and_negative_green`: +50 tint renders a grey magenta and −50 green, for both rendered files (relative scale) and raws (Kelvin).
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-color -p lightcraft-pipeline -p lightcraft-raw` passes, as does `cargo test -p lightcraft-engine -p lightcraft-catalog --lib` (267 + 73 passed).
- Clippy and rustfmt are clean.

title: Issue #168: the desktop app and CLI log warnings to stderr; RUST_LOG works
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #168.

## Problem
`lightcraft-cli` never installed a `log` backend. Every `log::warn!` / `log::info!` record was therefore dropped: the GPU-to-CPU fallback, an unknown `LIGHTCRAFT_GPU_BACKEND`, the adapter chosen. `RUST_LOG=warn`, which `docs/gpu-pipeline.md` documents for the fallback warning, did nothing. The desktop app had its own `StderrLog`, but it read only `LIGHTCRAFT_LOG`.

## Fix
- A new `lightcraft_engine::logging` module, beside `guard`, holds the stderr logger the app already had. Both the app and the CLI install it.
- Warnings and errors are shown by default. `LIGHTCRAFT_LOG` or `RUST_LOG` picks another level (`off`, `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `trace`), and `LIGHTCRAFT_LOG` wins when both are set.
- `RUST_LOG` per-target directives work as people type them: `lightcraft=debug,wgpu=warn` sets LightCraft's level.
- Below warnings, only `lightcraft*` targets are shown, as the app's logger already did, so `info` isn't drowned out by wgpu and winit.
- The app's `--help` lists the variable. Its `log` dependency is dropped because the app no longer uses the crate directly.

This also makes the lock warning from #171 visible on stderr. Surfacing it in the UI is still open.

title: Issue #337: the Import Photos dialog is bigger and resizable; the photo grid fills it
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #337.

The Import Photos dialog was a fixed-size window, and its photo grid stopped at 330 points. You saw about 6 x 2.5 small thumbnails and could not make the window bigger.

What changed:
- The dialog opens at 960 x 720 and can be resized by its edges and corner.
- The photo grid takes the height that the options and buttons below it leave, so making the window bigger shows more photos.
- If the options below the grid get taller (for example, when you switch to Copy), the grid makes room. The window does not grow; if there is not enough room, the content scrolls.

title: Sharp zoomed Detail view: render at the drawn size and render the visible window at the zoom scale (#323)
author: nledford
body:
Fixes #323.

## Problem
The Detail view rendered the whole frame into one texture capped at the "Preview size" setting (default 2560 px) and stretched it over the screen rect, so 1:1 and Retina fit views of larger photos looked soft or pixelated. Zoom above 1:1 was always stretched.

## Root cause
Zoom changed only the on-screen rect, never the render. A whole-frame texture can't be as large as a 1:1–8:1 view of a big photo, and the pipeline had no way to render part of the frame, so a hidden cap was the only guard on memory.

## Changes
- **Preview size is a limit** (`previewLimit`, default *Automatic*): the loupe renders at the size it is drawn, up to the photo's own pixels and an 8192 px ceiling. 1600–5120 px still cap it. The saved key changes from `previewEdge`, so installs that had the old 2560 default move to Automatic. Prefetch and Hover/Before stand-ins stay at the preview source level so they don't evict the open photo's full-resolution source; render sizes move in 64 px steps.
- **Window rendering** (`RenderRequest::window`, `PixelWindow`): render one window of the virtual full-size output. The crop rect narrows to the window, so sampling, masks and the lens warp are unchanged. Post-crop vignette, dehaze airlight, noise-reduction scale and mask edge refinement keep the whole frame's geometry. Spots and Auto Mask strokes grow the window to hold what they read, and the result is cut back.
- **Loupe**: when the whole-frame render is smaller than the zoomed view, the visible window plus a margin is also rendered at the zoom scale (`Slot::Region`) and drawn over it. Not during slider drags, while comparing, hovering a look, soft-proofing or showing an overlay. `ui.inspect` → `loupe.region` reports it.
- **GPU** renders windows (equivalence-tested against the CPU on a real GPU, within the existing 1 LSB); the **browser build** carries windows over the worker wire (capped at 3072 px a side).
- **100 % zoom** is measured against the cropped and rotated size, and …

title: Fix #322: type an exact value into a slider

author: bflatastic
body:

title: LR-IMP-CAMERA-COVERAGE: read Canon ColorData stored as bytes, so PowerShot and EOS M CR2s get their as-shot white balance
author: radialmonster
body:
Fixes #355. Related: #85 (CR2 layout read from the file's own tag), #148 (ARW white balance), #160.

## Problem

25 of the 134 CR2 files in the raw.pixls.us CC0 archive (PowerShot S95 to SX60 HS, EOS M, M3, M5, M6, M10, M100) open with a green cast: neutral areas have a* about -13, b* about +10 against the camera JPEG. Their white balance is 1, 1, 1 and the white point is `d65Default`.

Their maker-note `ColorData` (`0x4001`, ColorDataVersion -3 or -4) is one `undef[5120]` value; on the other CR2s it is `int16u[...]`. `cr2.rs` read it with `Ifd::u64s`, which gives one number per byte for an UNDEFINED value, so the as-shot probe never found a plausible `R G G B` quadruple.

## Change

`crates/raw/src/vendor/cr2.rs`: a small `words()` reads the `ColorData` array by its stored type. Byte and undefined data is paired into 16-bit words in the maker note's byte order (`MakerNote::order`); other types go through `to_u64_vec` as before. `wb_from_color_balance` is unchanged: it already probes word 71, where these files keep the as-shot levels. No per-model table.

It extends the existing CR2 `ColorBalance` probe and the maker-note reader (`lightcraft_tiff::makernote`); it adds no parallel mechanism. `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 11 to 12 (the decoded white balance changes, so renders of these files change).

## How the rule was established

Only from the files and public tag names. ExifTool tag names (`ColorData`, `ColorDataVersion`, `WB_RGGBLevelsAsShot`) are used as names only. No other converter's code or data was used, and nothing from Adobe.

1. A walk of every CR2's TIFF structure (our own script) records type and count of `0x4001`: 104 files SHORT (counts 582 to 1602), 25 files UNDEFINED with count 5120 and first word -3 (19 files) or -4 (6 files), and 5 files without it (G9, SX40 HS, SX150 IS, A480 and a CHDK DNG named .CR2).
2. For the 25, a scan of every word offset for a quadruple `R G G B` with equal greens and plausible R and B finds offsets 1, 5, 9, 71, 111, 151 ... i…

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: NEF lossy type 2 curve of version `0x44 0x40` spans a quarter of the sample range
author: radialmonster
body: Fixes the D780, D6, Z 5, Z 6, Z 7 and Z 7_2 lossy NEFs opening nearly black. Fixes #357. Maker note `0x0096` versions `0x44 0x20` and `0x44 0x40` both store 257 curve points, but the points of a `0x40` table are a quarter as far apart in code space: the first interval rises by `2^bits / 1024` where the `0x20` tables rise by `2^bits / 256`. The curve is the identity in the dark part and spans `2^bits / 4` codes. `parse_table` spaced the points `2^bits / 256` codes apart for both, so the `0x40` files decoded to a sixteenth of their values, below the black level. *Nikon D780, 12-bit lossy compressed. 1: camera JPEG. 2: main. 3: this PR. Whole frame. The other bodies and the numbers are in the issue.* ## Changes - `crates/raw/src/vendor/nefc.rs`, `parse_table`: the span of a type 2 curve comes from the table version, `0x20` all `2^bits` codes (as before), `0x40` `2^bits / 4`. The module docs state the rule and how the files show it. - New `lossy_type2_version_0x40_spans_a_quarter_of_the_range`: table bytes and two bit strings (12 and 14 bit) written out by hand, independent of the test encoder and of `parse_table`'s span rule. It checks curve values (`curve[5] == 5`, `curve[1024] == 4095` and so on), decodes a four-pixel row to known values, and checks that a `0x20` table with the same points still spans all codes. It fails without the change. - `crates/engine/src/media.rs`: `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 11 → 12, since the decoder output changes. - `docs/parity.md`: one sentence in LR-IMP-FORMATS. This extends the existing curve parser in `nefc.rs`. No new table, no per-camera or per-model rule. ## Evidence - **Archive scan:** the maker note tables of all 281 NEF/NRW files in the raw.pixls.us archive (ExifTool tag names, then the bytes): `0x44 0x10` 12 files, `0x44 0x20` 76, `0x44 0x40` 14 (D780, D6, Z 5, Z 6…

title: feat: run SAM3 masks on a remote Metal worker
author: joshuaswarren
body:
Keep LightCraft's native editor on a laptop while a separate Mac runs SAM3 masks. RAW files, the catalog, edits, and exports stay on the client.

## How it works

Set `LIGHTCRAFT_SAM3_REMOTE=127.0.0.1:8793` on the client. Run `lightcraft-sam3-worker` on a Mac with Metal through an SSH tunnel. Leave the variable unset to use the existing local path.

Object clicks, Describe prompts, and detail crops use the worker. It caches the base image, and detail crops do not replace that cache. Only small RGB images and prompts cross the link, not RAW files. Saved masks still work when the worker is offline.

Both ends require loopback addresses. SSH handles auth and encryption. The worker has no auth of its own, so local users must be trusted. It checks frame sizes, image sizes, prompts, and clicks. If the link fails, it reports an error. It does not switch to CPU inference.

The worker serves one client at a time. This adds no new dependencies. It does not add CUDA, RAW denoise, upscaling, or remote RAW edits. Model weights stay separate under the existing SAM license.

## Checks

- Full release workspace suite, offline after fetching dependencies: 1,068 passed, 0 failed, 10 ignored.
- Built the Linux editor and CLI, plus the Mac Metal worker.
- Used a public Sony ILCE-6000 RAW file on Linux with the Mac worker. Checked Describe, detail crops, positive and negative Object clicks, and JPEG export.
- Created remote masks with no local model weights. With the link down, saved masks still exported to a 16-bit TIFF with an ICC profile. A new mask failed without changing the saved mask count.
- Viewed the mask overlays and a headless editor render. I did not test the full flow through the live GUI.

The patch includes setup steps and release notes.

title: LR-IMP-ADD-DIALOG: file dialogs match extensions in any letter case on Linux (#342)
author: radialmonster
body:
Fixes #342.

## Problem

On Linux the Add Photos dialog hides files such as `DSC_1234.NEF`. `apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs` passes lower-case extensions to `rfd::FileDialog::add_filter`. rfd 0.17 turns each one into a `*.nef` glob (GTK backend: `gtk_file_filter_add_pattern`, `dialog_ffi.rs`; portal backend: `FileFilter` globs, `xdg_desktop_portal.rs`), and GTK matches globs case-sensitively. Windows and macOS ignore case, so only Linux is affected. The folder scan already compares extensions without case, which is why Import from Folder worked.

Every other dialog had the same shape (presets `.lcpreset` / `.xmp` / `.cube`, GPX, point-curve presets), so `.XMP`, `.GPX` and so on were hidden too.

## Change

New `apps/lightcraft/src/dialog_filter.rs`:

- `dialog_extensions(exts)` builds the list handed to rfd. Windows and macOS: lower case, de-duplicated (as before). Linux: for each extension the lower-case form, the UPPER-case form and a bracket form such as `[nN][eE][fF]`. rfd formats every entry as `*.{entry}` and passes it through verbatim on both Linux backends, so the bracket form is a glob that matches every mix (`.Nef`, `.nEf`). The plain forms stay as a fallback for a portal backend that does not do `[...]` classes.
- `FileDialogExt::add_filter_nocase` is the only way the app adds a filter. All seven filters in `main.rs` use it.

The Add Photos filter now uses `lightcraft_engine::import::EXTENSIONS`, the list the folder scan and drag-and-drop already use, instead of its own copy. The two differed by `heic` and `avif`, which the dialog did not show although importing a folder or dropping them accepts them. They now show in the dialog as well. This extends the existing import list; no new list.

- Unit tests for the helper: de-duplication and case folding, Linux forms, digits, existing glob syntax left alone, every extension in `import::EXTENSIONS` matched in lower and UPPER case, mixed case matched, near misses (`nex`, `nefs`) not matched.

title: AI masks: the worker stops counting a job as pending before it replies
author: bflatastic
body:
This fixes a race found by CI on the integration stack: `tests_segment::waiting_requests_with_a_damaged_model_are_errors` failed once on `assert!(!s.segmenter.busy())` under a loaded `cargo test --workspace`. It passes when run alone.

**Root cause:** the SAM 3 worker decremented its pending counter in the job guard's `Drop`, at the end of the loop iteration. That ran *after* `job.reply.send(…)`. A waiting caller (CLI / MCP `mask.add`) woken by the reply could therefore still see the segmenter as busy with the job it had just got an answer for.

**Fix:** the guard is dropped explicitly just before each reply, on both the superseded path and the normal path. This is a behaviour fix in the product, not only in the test: `busy()` is what the UI and agents read to decide whether a mask job is still running.

`cargo xtask ci` passes on the integration stack with this branch.

title: Issue #272: Show in Explorer selects photos whose path has a space
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Follow-up to #324 (issue #272).

#324 fixed forward slashes and the menu labels, but on current main "Show in Explorer" still opens Documents for any photo whose path contains a space. This is common: `C:\Users\Me\My Photos\...`, OneDrive folders, `Pictures\Summer 2026\...`.

### Why it still fails
Explorer reads its own command line, and `/select,` only works when the path after the comma is quoted: `/select,"C:\My Photos\a.jpg"`. Main builds `format!("/select,{win_path}")` and passes it with `Command::arg`. When an argument contains a space, Rust's standard library wraps the whole argument in quotes, so Explorer gets `"/select,C:\My Photos\a.jpg"`. Explorer does not recognise that as a switch and opens the default folder.

Main also passes verbatim paths (`\\?\D:\...`, `\\?\UNC\server\share\...`, the form `canonicalize` returns) through unchanged, and Explorer does not accept them either. The reveal path has no test.

One menu still says "Show in Finder" on Windows and Linux: the context menu of the library folder tree (`folder_menu_for_library` in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/left.rs`). That menu came from a separate change made at the same time as #324, so #324 never touched it. #324 changed the other folder menu (`folder_tree`), which uses `reveal_label()`.

### What changed
- `apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs`: `explorer_select_arg` builds `/select,"<path>"`. It turns `/` into `\` and strips the `\\?\` prefix (`\\?\UNC\server\share` becomes `\\server\share`). Windows file names can't contain `"`, so the quotes are always safe. `explorer_select_command` passes that string with `CommandExt::raw_arg` on Windows, so std quoting no longer touches it. Other platforms use `.arg`, so the function compiles everywhere, and it is only called in the existing `cfg!(target_os = "windows")` branch.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/left.rs`: the library folder tree's context menu uses `crate::menus::reveal_label()`, like the other folder menu.

title: Fix #171: a library that can't be locked opens with a warning the user sees
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #171. Thanks to @coygeek for the thorough report and reproduction script.

When `catalog.lock` can't be locked (a file system without locks, such as some network shares), the library opens without the one-program-at-a-time lock. That is the documented trade-off: refusing would lock the user out. But the promised warning went only to a `log::warn!` record, so neither app, CLI nor MCP users learned that a second program could open the library and lose their edits.

**Change:** the warning is now the first of the library's warnings, the same channel damaged settings files already use (#103):
- `library.info` → `settingsWarnings` lists it;
- the app shows it once in its notices;
- `lightcraft-cli run` and `lightcraft-cli mcp` print the library's warnings on **stderr**, so stdout stays results and protocol messages only (`docs/mcp.md`).

A normally locked library shows no warning, and a second opener of a normal library is still refused.

**Tests:**
- `an_unlockable_library_opens_with_a_warning` uses the issue's stand-in (`catalog.lock` replaced by a directory). The library opens with the warning in `library.info` and handed out once; with a lockable `catalog.lock`, there's no warning.
- Checked by hand with `lightcraft-cli run --library <lib> library.info`: the warning appears on stderr.

title: Fix #372: masking tile labels and long mask names stay inside their boxes
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes storytold/lightcraft#372.

## Problem
Create New Mask painted its tile labels with an unconstrained `Painter::text` into tiles capped at 52 pt, so "Background" and "Luminance" ran past their tiles, and longer translations more so. Mask names had no width limit and ran under the eye button. The Describe field reserved a fixed 64 pt for a Select button whose translated width varies.

A tile can grow past 52 pt for a long label. Only in a panel too narrow even for that is a label cut short with an ellipsis, with the full text on hover.
- **Mask rows:** a long name is cut short with an ellipsis before the eye button; the full name shows on hover.
- **Describe:** the translated Select button is laid out first, and the text field gets the rest of the width. Status lines wrap explicitly.
- New helper `widgets::one_line`: a single-line galley truncated at a width.

## Tests

- `masking_contents_fit_the_right_panel_at_any_width` now also checks the painted text, not only the widgets. The label and name rects are registered as `maskNewLabel:*` and `maskName:*`. At four panel widths it checks that the labels sit inside their tiles, that a long mask name stays clear of the eye, and that a long Describe prompt keeps the field and Select button inside the panel.

title: AI RAW denoise with opt-in models and pure-Rust CPU/GPU inference
author: voshart
body:
Adds non-destructive AI Bayer RAW denoise with LightCraft's bounded pure-Rust ONNX CPU/GPU interpreter, cached results and an Amount control. No trained weights are bundled or downloaded at startup.

Rebased on upstream `b188323` (batch #424). Main now contains the accepted PSD and font fixes (#414/#411); the duplicate #404/#418 patches are removed. [#426](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/pull/426) separately fixes the new web-worker window test using the documented CPU/GPU rounding bound. That earlier correction is retained with its original authorship; the duplicate #428 is closed. The separate GPU equivalence tests are unchanged.

The reviewed update makes the offered-model catalog empty by default and adds install-from-file in Settings. The RawNIND offer is a separate disabled-by-default feature awaiting maintainer policy; its conditional GPL terms are disclosed. Installation, extraction, hashing, parsing and self-tests run in a background worker; the frame pump only reports progress. Models/cache metadata live in a lightweight core crate, inference dependencies are optional, work allocations use the memory gate, tile concurrency is bounded, pictures are capped and WASM clocks use web_time. User-visible strings use the translation helpers, with English catalog fallbacks ready for maintainer translation.

Validation on `59ab9b6e9b7199ec04fa8574b24f69fe0bcd7578`: all seven cargo xtask ci gates pass with the exact hosted font input, including WASM. Synthetic regressions cover background installation, pending-photo resume and invalid replacement preservation. Recorded native model/timing/export checks in docs/denoise.md are historical measurements from the reviewed runtime, which is unchanged by the base refresh. Normal CI/release packaging does not download weights or run the ignored real-model suites. Replacing the existing faer backend remains a separate measured follow-up.

title: LRC-LIB-LIBFOLDERS: a chosen folder that follows a move keeps its names' case and the platform's separators
author: radialmonster
body:
Found running `cargo xtask ci` on Windows: `a_moved_folder_keeps_a_chosen_subfolder_chosen` failed on main.

## Problem

When a folder is moved or renamed, a library folder chosen at or below it follows (`follow_library_folder` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/browse.rs`). It compared by `folder_key`, then built the new path from the key's remainder. Two things were wrong on Windows:

- The key is lower-cased on Windows, so the remainder was too: choosing `D:\Photos\Trip\Day1` and moving `Trip` left `D:\Archive\Trip\day1` shown.
- The remainder was joined with `/` onto a `to` written with `\`, giving `D:\Archive\Trip/day1`. This is what the test saw (`...\archive\trip/day1` against an expectation built the same mixed way).

Matching still worked (the key reads both separators), so the effect is the wrong spelling in the filter, the sidebar and the saved state, not a lost choice. Linux and macOS are not affected, except by the new helper's tidier code.

## Change

- `lightcraft_catalog::query::folder_rest(path, root)`: compares with `folder_key` like everything else and returns the names below `root` as spelled (built on the existing `split_path`).
- `follow_library_folder` joins those names onto `to` with `PathBuf`, so the result is spelled like `to`.
- Tests that only mean "the same folder" compare by `folder_key`; a new test (`following_a_folder_keeps_the_case_of_the_subfolder_names`) fails on Windows without the change.

Extends the existing folder identity (`folder_key`, `split_path`) in the catalog; no new matching rule.

## Checks

`cargo xtask ci` with the CC0 corpus, on Windows. The rest of the workspace is green once the two other Windows test failures are fixed (separate PRs: #386, #387).

title: M11.4: the X-T20 corpus RAF is fitted since the away-from-edges retry

## Cause

Two PRs merged the same day. #282 added the test and expected this file to keep the neutral fallback: on all pixels its fit has held-out RMS 0.114, over the 0.10 gate. #263 (issue #232) added a second attempt away from edges, which fits it at 0.056 (uncorrected 0.185), so the look is now accepted, at both decode sizes. Neither PR saw the other. It is not platform- or GPU-dependent, and the corpus file is the one in `docs/raf-corpus.sha256`.

Users are not affected: the photo now gets a camera look instead of the grey fallback, by the gate #263 introduced for lens-corrected JPEGs. Only the test (and a sentence in `docs/camera-preview-colour.md` that still said the file is rejected) was out of date.

The test expects the file to be fitted, with a comment on why; the doc sentence says the same. No code change. CI does not download the corpus, so this only shows with `LIGHTCRAFT_CORPUS` set.

title: POC: Android tablet port
author: Sagigamil
body:
## Proof of concept: Android tablet port

This PR is an explicitly marked **POC** for bringing LightCraft to Android tablets while reusing the shared Rust engine and egui UI.

It adds:

- A NativeActivity Android host with ARM64 packaging and SAF folder/file access.
- Non-destructive import, catalog persistence, export/save-as, sharing, lifecycle handling, and touch/stylus gesture plumbing.
- Tablet toolbar/insets handling, scrollable menus, Android launcher branding, history navigation fixes, and an Android fallback for Object masking when SAM 3 is unavailable.
- Architecture, parity, and SAM-enabled testing plans under `docs/`.

Validation completed:

- Android source/import/export/gesture tests pass.
- Masking tests pass (21 passed, 1 ignored).
- History restore regression test passes.
- ARM64 release APK builds successfully.
- Emulator validation covered startup, toolbar hit targets, status-bar insets, and Android folder picker launch.

POC limitations:

- Full desktop feature parity is not complete.
- The distributed Android APK does not include the optional SAM 3 runtime or its approximately 3.4 GB model; Object masking uses a local fallback in this build.
- Physical tablet validation is still required for stylus pressure, rotation/insets, SAF providers, large RAW performance, GPU differences, and thermal behavior.

See `docs/android-parity.md` and `docs/android-plan.md` for the current status and follow-up plan.

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: TIFF raws with a thumbnail-only IFD0 import as preview only, not as a tiny image
author: radialmonster
body:
Fixes #390.

Extends `probe()` / `RawFormat::OtherTiff` in `crates/raw/src/lib.rs` and the existing preview-only fallback in `crates/engine/src/files.rs` (`40`). No new mechanism.

## The rule

`thumbnail_shell()`: a TIFF whose IFD0 is at least 4x smaller than a declared picture in both directions, where the picture is declared by either
- a `SubIFDs` child of IFD0 (Kodak DCS 3), or
- Exif `PixelXDimension` / `PixelYDimension`, and the file has enough bytes outside every IFD's strips and tiles to carry that many pixels at one bit each (strips shared by IFD0 and its thumbnail IFD count once). This keeps a downsized TIFF that kept its old Exif size an ordinary image.

No maker, model or extension is named. It is checked after the CFA / raw-compression test, so nothing recognised today changes class. A multi-page TIFF (pages in the IFD chain) and a pyramid whose IFD0 is the full image are not caught.

`decode()` returns `Unsupported("4490x3364 raw image in a private block, not decoded yet (the file's first image is a 296x220 reduced copy)")`, which becomes the preview-only reason.

## Preview

None of these files has an embedded JPEG; IFD0 is the only preview. `stand_in_image()` in `files.rs` uses the JPEG when there is one, otherwise (only for a TIFF-based raw we can't decode) the file's own first image through the TIFF reader. Decodable raws never use it. If you prefer a "not supported" error for files without a JPEG, drop that second step; the rest stands.

`RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 13 to 14: these 50 files render differently (preview path instead of a plain TIFF), and old cached thumbnails would survive.

## Evidence (main `48cd9c5` vs this branch `0b8c7a2`)

- Whole archive, `probe()` before and after: 50 files change, all Phase One / Leaf IIQ or the three Canon / Kodak TIFFs above, `None` to `OtherTiff`. No other file changes class (1820).
- Survey of the 50 files: all `raw` (silently a thumbnail) on main, all `preview-only` with the reason here; rendered size uncha…

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: raws we cannot decode import as preview only when any usable JPEG is embedded
author: radialmonster
body:
Fixes #392. Builds on #391 (its commit is the parent of this one, so this PR also shows it until #391 merges).

Extends the existing mechanisms: `probe()` / `RawFormat` and `embedded_preview()` in `crates/raw`, and the preview-only fallback in `probe_bytes` and `load_bytes_now` in `crates/engine/src/files.rs` (`40`).

## Changes

- `RawFormat::{Crw, Mrw, X3f}`, recognised by magic (`II....HEAPCCDR`, `\0MRM`, `FOVb`). Not decoded; `embedded_preview` finds the JPEG.
- KDC: an IFD0 with no `ImageWidth` / `ImageLength` but a JPEG pointer or `SubIFDs` is `OtherTiff` (`is_preview_container`). TIFF compression 99 counts as a raw compression (Leaf MOS).
- `scan_for_jpeg`: for a recognised raw we can't decode, when no tag points to a preview, the largest complete three-component DCT JPEG in the file (marker walk with entropy-data scan, so a stray byte pair or a thumbnail inside an APP segment doesn't count). A preview whose first byte was overwritten is restored. One-component JPEGs are skipped (PowerShot CRW mosaic). Used only for formats that are not `is_supported()`, so decodable raws and DNG tiles are never scanned.
- Import lists: `iiq`, `crw`, `mrw`, `x3f`, `kdc`, `mos`, `erf` are added to `import::EXTENSIONS` and to the headless `PHOTO_EXTENSIONS` (`crates/mcp/src/headless.rs`), so folder import, drag and drop and MCP folder expansion pick these files up (before, only an explicitly named file reached the probe). Only containers that now become preview-only are added: 3FR, FFF, DCR, STI stay out because they still fail. The desktop file dialog has its own list in `apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs`; it is not touched here.
- `preview_reason()` (already there for unsupported variants and CR3 errors) now also returns the reason for any other decode error of a recognised raw (corrupt, limit, TIFF structure), so its preview is shown; only `NotRaw` is still an error. CR3 keeps its own wording. A file with no JPEG still fails with "without an embedded preview".

title: Integrate part of #374 (bounded folder walks, launch imports off the UI thread) and #385, #386, #387
author: bflatastic
body:
## Included

title: LR-BEHAV-HEADLESS: keep snapshots on the CPU and bound viewport dimensions
author: sanyamsingh001
body:
`lightcraft-cli snapshot` now disables GPU photo compute before import, scripted queries and its first UI frame. `LIGHTCRAFT_GPU=1` keeps this CPU session policy. With `--library`, saved desktop `ui.json` preferences remain untouched.

Finite viewport bounds are checked before allocation. UI zoom preserves the requested screenshot pixel dimensions, and resize validates the converted native dimensions so accepted requests take effect. Regressions cover a 1-point width after zooming out and fractional native-scale rounding. Main's headless window commands and texture limits are retained. Locale edits have been dropped as requested; main contains #411's glyph correction.

Validation: fresh `cargo xtask ci` passed all seven stages on current main. Linux CLI tests compare saved GPU-enabled preference bytes after child exit, both without a GPU environment override and with `LIGHTCRAFT_GPU=1`. Seven real CLI snapshot cases passed CPU/no-adapter checks before and after screenshots, settlement, pointer interaction, integer/fractional scales, zoom and resize. Images were inspected; boundary outputs include 1×60 and 122×122 pixels. Normal grid and resized views retain the existing UI. These checks cover Linux CPU snapshots.

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: CR3 C-RAW samples that overshoot the bit depth are clamped, not rejected
author: radialmonster
body:
Fixes #396. Follow-up to #279.

Extends the existing CRX decoder (`crates/raw/src/vendor/crx.rs`, `decode`), where each decoded plane value becomes a sensor sample. It adds no new mechanism.

## Changes

- `sensor_sample()`: a wavelet (C-RAW, `CMP1` levels > 0) sample outside `0..2^bits − 1` is clamped to that range. A lossless (levels 0) sample outside it is still `Corrupt("Canon CRX: decoded sample outside its bit depth")`, as before. The bit depth and the level count both come from the file's own `CMP1` header.
- `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 13 → 14: the 17 files below now render from the raw data instead of their embedded preview. If the preview-fallback PR that also bumps it to 14 lands first, this becomes 15.
- `docs/cr3.md`: one paragraph on the clamp.

## How the rule was established

All evidence comes from the 110 CR3 files in the raw.pixls.us CC0 archive, measured with LightCraft's own decoder: every tile and plane was decoded and the range of `value + midpoint` was recorded before the check. No other converter was consulted.

- **Lossless files never leave the range.** All 59 lossless files (levels 0) stay within 0..16383. 27 of them clip at exactly 16383, including the lossless files of the bodies affected here (SX70 HS 3276–3279, G5 X Mark II 3509/3510, M6 Mark II 3719, EOS R 4515/4643, RP 4673/4674, M200 8469, R5 Mark II 7883, R6 Mark II 6402/6405, R8 6588, R6 Mark III 8961). So the sensor's range really is 0..2^bits − 1, and the strict check stays for lossless data.
- **Every failing file is C-RAW with clipped highlights.** All 17 have 3 wavelet levels, and their headers match working C-RAW files of the same version (quantisation values, tiles, flags). Every out-of-range sample is above the maximum, by 1 to 36 codes, and none is below 0. They sit in bright areas (the median of the 5×5 plane neighbours averages 4414 to 16383 per plane, for small specular points up to large clipped areas). title: Header-only import probes (part of #367), PSD RLE allocation bounds, and #397 (CR3 C-RAW clipped highlights)
author: bflatastic
body:
## Included
- **Part of storytold/lightcraft#367: probes read image headers instead of decoding the pixels.** Probing a non-raw file decoded the whole image just to learn its size, which was ~95% of an import's CPU. A new `lightcraft_codecs::read_header` reads the size and EXIF orientation from JPEG, PNG, TIFF, WebP and PSD headers; GIF, BMP and JPEG XL keep the small decode.
  - **Speed:** JPEG 72.7 → 2.1 ms per file (3.6 MB, 12 MP); PNG 236–265 → 9–10 ms (31 MB). Release build, bytes already in memory.
  - **Behaviour:**
    - Truncated files are still refused at scan, by a cheap structural check.
    - Files the old decode accepted are never refused: tested at every cut point and with ~3,000 random mutations.
    - Damage *inside* complete compressed data now shows at render time instead of at scan.
    - Truncated JPEGs under 128 px, which the old lenient decode imported, are now refused.
    - A TIFF cut off inside its last strip isn't detected at scan.
- **PSD decoding bounds its allocations by the input.** `psd::decode` could abort on out-of-memory with a tiny hostile file in two ways:
  - it reserved the RLE row byte-count table from header-declared dimensions; the old code aborted on a 481 GB allocation in the regression test;
  - zero-padded or repeat-run rows could expand without bound.

  The table is now read in place after a size check. Each row must declare enough encoded bytes for its width (PackBits expands at most 64×), and the data must be present before planes are allocated. Overrunning runs are errors, and buffers use `try_reserve`.
- **storytold/lightcraft#397** by @radialmonster (fixes storytold/lightcraft#396): CR3 C-RAW samples that overshoot the bit depth at clipped highlights are clamped instead of failing the whole file (17 of the 110 CR3s on raw.pixls.us). Lossless planes keep the strict check. `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` goes to 14.
