title: Fix #189: in-window menus and submenus stay below the menu bar
author: ragtux
body:
Fixes #189.

**Problem.** egui keeps a popup inside the window. On Linux/Wayland (and any host with the in-window bar) a menu taller than the room under the menu bar, such as Photo on a short window, was slid up over the bar: the Photo, Window and Help titles vanished under it, the bottom rows were cut off, and the pointer that had rested on the title now rested on the first row and opened its "Add to Album" submenu by itself. Reproduced on `main` (c395789) on KDE Wayland at 2×; same bug and same fix as PhotoCraft's storytold/photocraft#319 / #337.

**Fix** (`crates/ui-egui/src/menu_level.rs`, used by `menubar.rs`): every level of a menu gets only the room it has below the bar and scrolls inside it.

- A top-level menu hangs from the top bar; its rows scroll in the room down to the window's bottom edge.
- A submenu gets whichever is larger: from its row down, or from the bar down to its row (egui opens it upward when that fits). It scrolls inside that room instead of being slid over the bar. The row it hangs from is remembered from the previous frame (`set_anchor`), since a submenu is drawn while its row is.
- Scrolling: wheel, dragging the rows, and ▲ / ▼ strips that scroll while the pointer rests on them, like native menus on a small display.
- Menu levels (`menu-level:<depth>`) and submenu rows (`menusub:<label>`) are registered for the control channel and tests.

**Tests**

- `tests_menubar::no_menu_or_submenu_covers_the_menu_bar` (headless): at 1280 × 703 (the reporter's display less the title bar) and 1160 × 560, opens Photo, File and View, then hovers every submenu row in view; each level must start below the titles, end inside the window, and intersect no title. On `main` it fails with `menu-level:1 [[284.0 7.0] - [523.3 1009.0]] starts above the bar's bottom 31.5` (a 703 pt window).

title: Part of #260: Help ▸ Open Log Folder shows the log file in the file manager
author: ragtux
body:
Part of #260 (idea 4 in the maintainer's list: Help ▸ Open Log Folder).

The desktop app keeps `logs/lightcraft.log` in its settings folder (#286) and a failed start names it (#370), but a user attaching it to a report still had to find the settings folder by hand.

**Change**

- `Services.log_file` (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`): the host's current log file. The desktop app fills it from the path the logger opened (`apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs`); the web app leaves it `None`.
- `app.openLogFolder`, **Help ▸ Open Log Folder**, after System Info… It reveals the file through the existing `reveal` service, so Finder and Explorer select the file and Linux opens the folder. The command returns `{"path": …}` for the control channel and MCP.
- Enabled only with both a log file and a file manager: off on the web, in `--memory` and `LIGHTCRAFT_NO_PREFS` sessions (no log is kept), and the command then says why.
- Label translated in de, es, ja, pt-br, ru, zh-hans and zh-hant. Parity row `MENU-HELP-LOGFOLDER` (an extra, like the keymap editor; summary refreshed with `cargo xtask parity --write`), a What's New line, and the README's Logs paragraph mentions the item.

**Test:** `menubar::tests::open_log_folder_reveals_the_hosts_log_file`: the item is listed in Help and off without a log; a file manager alone doesn't enable it; with a log file it is enabled, the command returns the path and the file manager is asked to show exactly that file; a file manager failure is the command's error.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-ui-egui -p lightcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask parity` and `cargo xtask wasm` pass; the 35 menubar and i18n tests pass.

**Checked in the desktop app** (Linux/Wayland, settings in a scratch `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`): the item appears in Help, and `engine.execute {"command":"app.openLogFolder"}` returned `{"path": ".../lightcraft/logs/lightcraft.log"}` and opened that folder in the file manager.

title: Fix PSD constant chunk iteration for strict Clippy
author: voshart
body:
Main's new PSD decoder fails `cargo xtask ci` with `clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` on the constant 3-byte palette, 2-byte sample and 4-byte sample loops. Use array chunks for those three calls, preserving iteration order, ignored remainders and decoded values. This keeps the cleanup independent of the Olympus and AI denoise contributions.

Validation: `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, strict Clippy, workspace tests, parity, layers, assets and WASM). Existing palette, 16/32-bit PSD, malformed-input and header tests cover the affected paths; no new test fixtures or release steps are introduced.

title: Fix #191: commands' file dialogs run off the UI thread
author: ragtux
body:
Fixes #191.

**Cause.** The desktop app showed `rfd`'s synchronous dialogs on the UI thread (the `pick_*` service closures in `apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs`, called from the command handlers). The dialog blocks the thread until it closes, so the winit loop stopped answering the compositor: GNOME marked LightCraft "not responding" after a few seconds, the File menu stayed drawn in the last frame, and the control channel went quiet. Reproduced on `main` (c395789) on KDE Wayland: while the dialog was up, `ui.inspect` got no answer in 8 s and the `file.addPhotos` request timed out at 60 s. PhotoCraft's storytold/photocraft#574 is the same report with the same diagnosis; `rfd` here is the XDG-portal backend (zbus, no GTK), so the dialog can run on any thread.

**Change** (`crates/ui-egui/src/pick.rs`, new):

- `Services.picker`: the host starts a dialog without blocking and answers through a channel. The desktop implements it with the dialog on its own thread (`apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs`); the web leaves it `None` (its browser pickers are asynchronous already).
- A command that needs a path the caller didn't give calls `pick::ask` and returns at once; `pick::poll` runs each frame and, when a dialog closes with something chosen, runs the command again with the answer under the missing parameter (`paths` / `path` / `folder`). Cancel runs nothing; a dialog already up for a command is not opened twice.
- Converted: File ▸ Import Photos…, Import from Folder…, Open Library…, Import Lightroom Catalog…, Find Missing Photos…, Import Profiles & Presets…, Export Presets…, Import / Export Point Curve Presets…, Photo ▸ Auto-Tag from Tracklog…, Locate Missing File…. Each keeps its old behaviour on hosts without a `picker` (the synchronous services), so the web and headless sessions are unchanged.
- `ui.inspect` → `fileDialogs` lists the commands waiting on a dialog (`docs/control-protocol.md`).

Not in this PR: the "Choose…" buttons inside the Import and Settings dialogs still call t…

title: Top bar: drag to move and double-click to zoom the window (macOS)
author: nledford
body:
## What
On macOS the native title bar is hidden (fullsize content view), so double-clicking the top of the window did nothing and the window could not be dragged by it. The egui top bar now acts as the title bar:

- dragging its empty space (including the traffic-light margin) moves the window (`StartDrag`);
- double-clicking it zooms the window, and again restores it (`Maximized(!current)`);
- a press that starts on a button or the search field is theirs and never moves the window;
- ignored in full screen; not registered when the native title bar is present (Windows/Linux).

## How
- `titlebar.rs`: pure policy, gesture + window state -> viewport command.
- `panels/topbar.rs`: `window_handle` registered before the bar's widgets so they win hit tests.
- `headless.rs`: records window commands and reports the zoomed state back, so the behaviour is testable.
- `tests_titlebar.rs`: BDD-style scenarios (zoom/restore, drag, single click, button, search field, no integrated title bar, drag from a button).
- `docs/parity.md`: new row `LR-BEHAV-TITLEBAR` (🟡).

## Known gap
egui-winit reads the zoomed state only at start-up and after our own `Maximized` command. A window zoomed another way (green button, Window > Zoom, snapping) makes the first double-click a no-op. Zoom is winit's, so it does not follow System Settings > "Double-click a window's title bar to". Noted in the parity row.

## Testing
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-ui-egui`: 245 passed; clippy clean for the crate.
- `cargo xtask parity`, `layers`, `assets` pass.
- Checked by hand on a real macOS window (drag, zoom, restore).
- Full `cargo xtask ci` currently stops at clippy on `crates/codecs/src/psd.rs` (new `chunks_exact` lints), which is already on `main` and untouched here.

title: Fix #374: troubleshooting for the NVIDIA shader-cache startup hang
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes storytold/lightcraft#374 (docs).

On Windows with NVIDIA, the window can stay black and "not responding" for minutes. The cause:
- With **Shader Cache Size: Disabled** in NVIDIA Control Panel, the driver walks the whole system drive inside `D3D12CreateDevice`, before the window's first frame.
- The reporter traced it to `nvwgf2umx.dll` → `NvMemMapStoragex.dll!TotalDiskUsage`.
- The Vulkan driver shares the same code, so switching backend doesn't help.
- Setting the cache back to **Driver Default** fixes it, which the reporter confirmed for both LightCraft and PhotoCraft.

This adds the case to `docs/gpu-pipeline.md` → troubleshooting. The launch-argument walk found during the investigation was fixed separately in storytold/lightcraft#394.

Docs only.

title: M16: use paintable separators in localized UI text
author: midasdf
body:

title: M16: keep grapheme clusters intact in vertical watermarks
author: midasdf
body:
A decomposed voiced kana such as `か\u{3099}` currently gets two vertical watermark cells, separating its dakuten from its base. Upright Latin combining accents also lose marks when shaping produces multiple glyphs, because the old helper retained just one glyph.

Use extended grapheme clusters for vertical cells and retain every shaped glyph and offset. Japanese clusters keep top-to-bottom shaping/vertical origins; upright Latin clusters use horizontal shaping inside their existing cell. A newline starts the next column to the left, and CRLF is one column break. An unavailable cluster uses the existing first-character placeholder in one cell.

Horizontal rendering, export command IDs/options, old preset defaults and stored text are unchanged; no normalization, fonts or assets are added. This does not implement ruby, kinsoku, tate-chu-yoko, Latin run rotation, or emoji/IVS font support. `docs/vertical-watermarks.md` ties the behavior and limits to UAX #29 §3, OpenType `vert`, JLReq and Lightroom's public watermark manual. Lightroom does not document a vertical-text mode; this fixes LightCraft's existing extension rather than claiming undocumented parity.

Validation against main `32cedb3`, Rust 1.99:
- Engine: **374 passed / 2 ignored → 376 passed / 2 ignored**, with optional craft-fonts; **376 passed / 2 ignored** without it. Every original engine status is retained. New regressions compare coverage for composed/decomposed dakuten, handakuten and Latin marks, missing-font sequences and CRLF, and verify a separate combining glyph's offset.
- Built the current CLI and exported `がぱ。\néñ` and its decomposed spelling through the ordinary PNG export path: outputs are byte-identical (SHA-256 `db0f85283a39d274ccc25d972fe5050f34d84727b87e2f8af8d90d85e1131791`) and visually inspected.
- Formatting, diff checks, layers, assets and parity pass. All-target engine Clippy passes allowing only the unchanged PSD decoder's `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` lint, already covered by #404.

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: no overflow deciding whether to scale a full-size JPEG decode
author: Exalted5373
body:
## Summary

A full-size load asks the decoder for the largest box: `SourceLevel::Full` is `usize::MAX`, and `files.rs` cast it `as u32` to `u32::MAX`. `jpeg::decode` then decided on DCT scaling with `m.width >= 2 * mw`, which overflows.

```diff
 jpeg::decode
-  scale if width >= 2 * mw || height >= 2 * mh                      # debug: overflow panic, caught -> "decoder panicked"
+  scale if width >= mw.saturating_mul(2) || height >= mh.saturating_mul(2)
 files.rs (3 call sites)
-  DecodeOptions::fit(max_edge as u32, max_edge as u32)               # truncates edges past u32::MAX
+  fit_box(max_edge)  ->  u32::try_from(max_edge).unwrap_or(u32::MAX)
```

In release builds the overflow wraps and happens to give the right answer; in debug builds every full-size JPEG load failed with "malformed Jpeg data: decoder panicked". Found while rendering camera JPEGs (extracted from CC0 raw.pixls.us files) at full size.

## Evidence

- New test `jpeg::tests::unbounded_fit_box_decodes_at_full_size` (decodes a 32×24 JPEG with `DecodeOptions::fit(u32::MAX, u32::MAX)`).
  **Before:** panics at jpeg.rs (`attempt to multiply with overflow`); `decode` returns `Malformed(Jpeg, "decoder panicked")`.
  **After:** passes, full size, no scaling.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes all 7 steps (combined with the psd.rs clippy fix PR).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way.

**Blast Radius:** JPEG decode at the largest fit box only; release builds already behaved the same.

Split out of #327's review.

title: MENU-BAR: pointing at another menu title switches the open menu
author: radialmonster
body:
Fixes #421.

## Problem

In the in-window menu bar (Windows, Linux, web), with one top-level menu open, moving the pointer over another title did nothing; native menu bars close the open menu and open the hovered one. Not a regression: each title has been an independent popup since the menu bar was added. Context: #28 / #49 set the title spacing, #189 the menu placement. Both are unchanged.

## Change

`menubar::show_in_window` now lays out all titles first, then their popups. `switch_open_title` uses egui's public popup state (`Popup::is_id_open`, `open_id`, `toggle_id`, `default_response_id`) to:

- open the hovered title's menu when a different title's menu is open (egui allows one open popup, so the old one closes in the same frame, with no frame showing none or two) and request a repaint;
- toggle a title by click as before, but not close the menu a hover just opened when the click that follows lands on it.

Nothing happens on hover when no menu is open. Escape, click outside, submenus (`menu_level`) and the `menu:<title>` widget ids are untouched. The narrow-window "Menu" button, which already switches submenus on hover, is not changed.

It extends the existing egui popup mechanism and the in-window menu bar; no new menu state of our own beyond one remembered id (the menu a hover opened) for the confirming click.

## Tests

`tests_menubar.rs` (headless, driven through the control channel):

- `hovering_another_title_switches_the_open_menu`: no menu opens on hover alone; with File open, hovering each other title opens that one and only that one (fails without the change).
- `clicking_another_title_opens_it_in_one_click`: click Edit, click View, View is open; clicking the open title closes it.
- `click_outside_and_escape_close_the_open_menu`.

title: Web: the window wire test allows the CPU/GPU difference
author: Exalted5373
body:
## Summary

`wire::tests::a_window_job_crosses_the_wire_and_renders_the_same_window` (#323) compares the web worker's render with the engine job's render bit for bit. The worker renders on the CPU; the engine job renders on the GPU when the machine has one. So on a machine with a GPU the test fails on `main` by 1 LSB. CI has no GPU, so both sides run on the CPU there and it passes.

```diff
 assert_eq!((a.image.width, a.image.height), (160, 120));
-assert_eq!(a.image.data, b.image.data);

+max channel difference <= 3   # docs/gpu-pipeline.md's CPU/GPU bound
```

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: 12-bit raws packed in 32-bit little-endian words (Coolpix NRW, FinePix S1 / X-A10 / SL1000) and the NRW black level
author: radialmonster
body:
Fixes #417 (likely a COOLPIX P950; see my comment there).

Extends the existing sample unpacking (`crates/raw/src/unpack.rs`, `Packing` in `tiffraw.rs`) and the NEF and RAF readers. The 32-bit-word layout was already decoded for RAF 14-bit files and for ORF 12-bit files, each with a private copy of the word swap; this adds one shared `unpack_words32_msb` and a `Packing::Words32Msb`, and the black level goes into the existing `BlackLevel` of `RawImage`. No new mechanism.

## Changes

Two commits, because the packing and the black level are independent.

1. Packing.
   - RAF (`raf.rs`): the raw IFD flag `0xf006` = 1 means the samples are MSB-first in little-endian 32-bit words, at any depth. A 12-bit file with the flag set used to be read as an LSB-first stream. Files with the flag clear behave as before.
   - NEF/NRW (`nef.rs`): an uncompressed 12-bit strip of exactly 1.5 bytes per pixel (whole 32-bit words per row) in a file whose maker note has an NRW data block (tag `0x0014`, starts with `NRW `) uses the same layout, in file byte order. Without the block it stays an MSB-first byte stream.
   - `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 15 → 16. Another branch may also bump it; whichever lands second takes the next number.
2. NRW black level: when the maker note has no `0x003d`, the black level is the 32-bit value at byte `0x20` of the NRW data block (version `0104`), if it is below a quarter of the sample range.

`orf.rs` keeps its own copy of the word swap because #360 changes that file; it can use `unpack_words32_msb` once #360 has landed. Textual overlap to expect: #270 (WIP: `nef.rs`, `media.rs`).

Tests (hand-made bytes, each fails without the change): `unpack::tests::words32_are_read_as_numbers_then_msb_first`, `raf::tests::flag_selects_word_packed_12_bit`, `nef::tests::nrw_block_selects_32_bit_word_packing` (commit 1) and the same test extended with the black level (commit 2: `nrw_block_selects_32_bit_word_packing_and_supplies_the_black_level`).

body:

Reused Local photos are promoted into My Photos through the normal undoable catalog operation. Restoring only the missing production promotion makes the same CLI test fail with “Local result was not promoted”; repaired code passes the CLI journey & all 9 merge tests (0 failed, 0 ignored). title: fix(macos): prevent SIGILL crash on exit by replacing viewport close …
author: onemannoplan
body:
…with clean process exit

### Summary
When selecting "Quit LightCraft" from the native macOS menu bar, the application occasionally crashes with an `EXC_BAD_INSTRUCTION` (SIGILL) error report during shutdown.

### Root Cause
1. The native menu action triggered `ctx.send_viewport_cmd(egui::ViewportCommand::Close)`.
2. Forcing an explicit viewport close via the command queue while macOS and AppKit are initiating their own termination sequence creates a race condition with `winit`.
3. This conflict during native window, view, and observer teardown leads to an illegal instruction fault.

### Solution
- Replaced the manual `ViewportCommand::Close` trigger on `QUIT` with a clean `std::process::exit(0)`.
- This bypasses the problematic `winit`/AppKit teardown race condition on macOS, allowing the application to shut down instantly and cleanly without generating crash reports.

title: CI: restore green FreeBSD builds
author: echelon
body:
## Root cause

The FreeBSD job was not hanging. It was too slow, and the slowdown traces back to #323.

- Each time a demo photo's source loaded, the procedural scene was evaluated from scratch. That costs a few nanoseconds per pixel times every noise octave, so one **6000×4000 demo original takes about 200 CPU-seconds**. I timed scene 1 (AlpineLake, the photo the Detail tests open) single-threaded at 208 s.
- #323 (1:1 loupe windows) added about 30 `tests_preview_limit::in_the_loupe` tests. Each one opens that photo at 1:1, so each loads the 24 MP original. With Before/After on, the Before window and the After window load it separately, so it is generated twice, in parallel.
- On the 4-vCPU FreeBSD VM, the ui-egui lib run went from **1198 s with 260 tests (before #323) to 3046 s with 338 tests (after)**. All scene generation shares the global rayon pool, so the other tests' small renders queue behind these 24 MP generations. That is why tests unrelated to #323 also hit their 120 s / 300 s waits:
  - `tests_labels`: "fixture thumbnails must be ready"

- I checked and ruled out the other hypotheses:
  - The memory budget on FreeBSD is read from `hw.physmem` and is fine.

## Fix

`lightcraft_engine::demo::scene_pixels` now generates demo-scene pixels **once per (scene, size) per process** and shares them:

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: read plain packed 12-bit PEF strips tagged as PackBits (older Pentax and Samsung GX-1L)
author: radialmonster
body:
**TL;DR:** Six 6 MP Pentax-family files (\*ist DS, \*ist DL, K100D, K100D Super, K110D and the Samsung GX-1L) tag their raw strip as compression 32773 (PackBits), but the strip holds plain packed 12-bit samples; its byte count is exactly width x height x 1.5. The PEF reader now accepts 32773 only when every strip has exactly the packed size, and reads it as uncompressed MSB-first samples. The six files open as raws instead of preview-only, and the Exif colour-filter pattern is now read as the file states it (from the first sample of the stored array), which also corrects the \*ist D, whose red and blue were exchanged on main. Other files I checked render pixel-identically.

Fixes #452.

## Change

- `crates/raw/src/vendor/pef.rs`: a `32773` arm next to `1` and `65535`. `is_exactly_packed` requires one sample per pixel, chunky data, 1 to 16 bits, one byte count per strip, and every strip of exactly `ceil(width x bits / 8) x rows` bytes (TIFF 6.0 section 7 packing). Then the strip is read through `read_image_in` as compression 1 with `Packing::Msb`. Any other 32773 size still returns `Unsupported("PEF compression 32773")`.
- CFA: for the uncompressed variants (compression 1 and this one) the PEF reader now uses the Exif `CFAPattern` as stored, read from the first sample of the stored array (not shifted by the maker note's `ImageAreaOffset`), else BGGR as before. For the six 32773 files the area origin is even, so shifted or not gives the same layout; the \*ist D (odd origin 19, 11) is where it matters, and it changes from BGGR to its stated, measured RGGB. `cfa_from_exif` moves from `orf.rs` to `vendor/mod.rs` and is shared; the Huffman-compressed bodies keep their layout in this PR (see step 4 below).
- `crates/raw/src/lib.rs` `probe`: a `SAMSUNG` make whose Exif maker note starts with the Pentax signature (`AOC\0` or `PENTAX \0`) is `RawFormat::Pef`; other Samsung files stay `Srw`.

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: decode Samsung SRW files with uncompressed raw data
author: radialmonster
body:
**TL;DR:** Samsung NX5, NX10, NX11, NX20, NX200, NX210, NX1000, NX1100, EX1 and WB2000 raw files now open as real raws (developed from the sensor data) instead of showing the camera's embedded JPEG. The newer, compressed SRW files (NX1, NX30, NX300, NX500, NX2000, NX3000, NX3300, NX mini) still open from their JPEG, and now say why. Nothing else changes: 14 other-format files render byte for byte as before.

Part of #220 (the compressed codings are not done).

## Problem

Every SRW file imported as preview-only ("Srw files are not decoded yet"), so no Samsung file could be developed, exported at full resolution or edited with raw headroom. Ten of the twelve bodies in the public corpus store the samples uncompressed, which needs no new coding.

## Change

New reader `crates/raw/src/vendor/srw.rs` (the format was already recognised by its `SAMSUNG` make, `RawFormat::Srw`), wired into `decode_with` and `is_supported`.

- The raw image is the IFD with a private `Compression` value (32769..=32773). It is uncompressed when the strip has exactly `w*h*2` bytes (value 32769: 16-bit little-endian words; EX1, WB2000) or exactly `w*h*12/8` bytes (value 32770: 12-bit samples, two in three bytes). Anything else is a compressed coding and returns `Unsupported` with the value and the stored bits per sample (so the preview-only reason is readable).
- 12-bit files come in two bit orders (NX5, NX10, NX11 MSB-first; NX20, NX200, NX210, NX1000, NX1100 LSB-first). The file does not say which; the decoder unpacks 64 rows both ways and keeps the order whose same-colour neighbours differ least (the ORF reader decides its layouts the same way).
- CFA layout: the raw IFD's `CFAPattern`.
- Maker note (`0x927c`, a plain IFD whose offsets count from the note start): framing (`SensorAreas`, second rectangle = the camera JPEG's size), as-shot white balance (`0xa021`), black (`0xa028`), saturation (`0xa048`). Several vectors are stored offset by `EncryptionKey` (`0xa020`, 11 integers).

title: M11.1: decode EOS R7 C-RAW (odd-height CRX QP map)
author: cookingwithsimon
body:
Before: Canon EOS R7 C-RAW files fail with unsupported raw variant: Canon CRX adaptive QP map with an odd height, so they open from the embedded JPEG only. R7 lossless RAW and every R6 Mark II file already decode.

After: R7 C-RAW develops from the sensor data.

The R7's 4732 sensor rows give a 1183-row adaptive QP map. The map itself decodes to the exact end of its entropy stream once the odd-height rejection is removed. The only open question is the second-level high-frequency bands (4–6), which average QP rows in pairs: their last row has no partner. That row's QP is now used on its own (the second row index is clamped to the last map row).

How:

crates/raw/src/vendor/crx.rs: removes the two odd-height rejections (in header validation and in qp_map) and clamps the paired row in adaptive_step. Adds the unit test odd_height_qp_map_uses_its_last_row_alone.
docs/cr3.md and docs/whats-new.md: document the rule and how it was verified.

Verification and limits:

Even-height maps never reach the clamp, so the six verified M50/R100/R8 fixtures are unaffected.
Checked against paired real R7 captures of the same scene, RAW (lossless) and C-RAW, at ISO 100 and 6400 (owner's files, not CC0, not committed):
all six R7 C-RAW files decode;
at ISO 6400, the C-RAW and RAW sensor means agree within 0.1% (3429.0 vs 3429.9);
developed renders match the RAW visually, including the bottom rows of the frame where the clamp applies.
Not yet checked against a black-box reference decoder sample for sample. It should get that check (as with the existing fixtures) before this leaves draft. A CC0 R7 C-RAW from raw.pixls.us would let it join cr3_corpus.
Clean-room: no third-party decoder source was consulted. The rule was derived from the existing code and observed behaviour only.

title: Issue #441: keep the grid's scroll position when deleting photos
author: chikity
body:
## What
Fixes #441 

Deleting a photo (or several) no longer jumps the grid/filmstrip back to the top. The
selection moves to the next surviving photo, which sits where the deleted one was, so
`follow_active` doesn't re-scroll the view.


## Why

`photo.delete` reset the selection to `visible.first()` after committing, so the active
photo changed to the top of the list and the grid scrolled there — losing the user's place
if they had scrolled down.

## How

`crates/engine/src/cmd/library.rs`
- New `select_after_delete(s, anchor)`: selects the surviving photo now at the deleted
  photo's former index (clamped), or leaves the selection empty when nothing remains.
- `photo.delete` records the target's index in the pre-delete visible list before the
  commit, then selects the photo now at that index.
- `photo.deletePermanently` and `library.emptyRecentlyDeleted` use the same helper.

The grid and filmstrip need no changes: they already keep the user's scroll unless the
active photo changes, and the new active photo is already in view.

## Tests

- `lightcraft-engine`: `delete_selects_the_next_photo` — middle photo, contiguous range,
  and last photo (regression test that fails against the old `vis.first()`).
- `lightcraft-ui-egui`: `grid_keeps_its_position_after_delete` — scroll down, delete, assert
  the next photo becomes active and the grid's scroll offset stays put (not 0).

## Notes

- No user-visible UI/command changes besides the selection target.
- `docs/parity.md` (`LR-LIB-DELETE`) updated to describe the behaviour.
- `cargo xtask ci` green (fmt, clippy, heif, test, parity, layers, assets, wasm). CI has no
  GPU, so the GPU-only `lightcraft-gpu` `nn::tests` are skipped there; unrelated local GPU
  failures on macOS are pre-existing and tracked separately.

title: catalog: group photos without capture date under Unknown Date (#437)
author: peiyan0
body:
Fixes #437

### Summary
When photos do not have a capture date metadata (captured == None), they previously fell back to their import date via p.date(). This caused undated photos to be grouped under the date they were imported (e.g. today's date) in the grid and counted in the sidebar's 'By Date' calendar tree.

### Changes
- In Catalog::date_runs, use p.captured.as_deref() for SortKey::CaptureDate. Photos without a capture date now group under the 'Unknown Date' heading (which already has localized labels in i18n).
- In Catalog::query, sort undated photos together under SortKey::CaptureDate, breaking ties by imported date. In descending sort (newest first), undated photos sort to the end; in ascending sort, to the beginning.
- In Catalog::date_groups, skip photos without a capture date so they are not counted under import date in the 'By Date' calendar hierarchy.
- In Filter::matches_in and token search, match date, date_from, and date_to against p.captured rather than falling back to p.imported.
- Added unit tests in crates/catalog/src/tests.rs and updated crates/catalog/src/dates.rs.

title: Fix #226: a refused Web Locks request no longer leaves the web app loading
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #226.

**What the user saw:** with a persistent store (`?store=idb`), if `navigator.locks.request` throws or returns a rejected promise, the page stays on "Loading LightCraft…" forever and shows no error.

**Cause:** `acquire_tab_lock` in `apps/lightcraft-web/src/safety.rs` waits on a promise that only the lock callback resolves. Its `reject` handle was never used. When `request` threw, the code only logged a warning. When `request` returned a promise, the code dropped it. So a refused request left that promise pending forever, and startup in `web.rs` waited on it.

**What changed:**
- If `request` throws, the error rejects the promise.
- If `request` returns a promise, its `.catch` is connected to `reject`.
- A rejection logs a warning and returns `None`. This is the same result as in a browser with no Web Locks, so startup goes on without the one-tab guard. A busy lock (`Some(false)`) still shows the "already open in another tab" screen.
- `docs/web.md`: browsers that refuse the lock request are not protected either.

I chose the same fallback as for a missing Web Locks API, not a blocking error screen. A refused lock request does not mean another tab is open, so blocking the user would make the app unusable for no reason.

**Tests:** none added. This code builds only for wasm32 and runs only in a browser, and the repo has no wasm or browser test harness. Steps to check by hand (from the issue): replace `navigator.locks` with a `request()` that throws, then with one that returns `Promise.reject(...)`, and load `?store=idb`. The editor should start in both cases, with a "Web Locks request failed" warning in the console. Without injection, a second tab should still show the "already open" screen.

title: Web restore: reject originals that don't match their content hash (#227)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #227.

**What the user saw:** in the web app, a backup zip where an `originals/<content hash>/…` entry held different bytes (with a valid zip CRC) restored without complaint. Exporting the restored photo then gave the replacement image, not the one the catalog describes. A restore that failed later on could also leave that wrong original in storage, and a retry with a good backup reused it.

**Cause:** `safety::restore` checked each entry only against its zip CRC. Originals are stored by content hash, so bytes under the wrong hash became that photo's original.

**What changed:**
- `backup::verify_original` (next to `verify`) checks that `store::content_hash(data)` matches the hash in the storage key. `restore` calls it for `originals/` keys before `backend.write`. A mismatch stops the restore with an error that names the entry, before anything is written for that entry and before `active-library` switches. So a failed restore can no longer leave a wrong original behind.
- Originals that are already in storage are still skipped without being read, as before. Export then uses the stored copy, which is correct.
- `docs/web.md` and the `backup.rs` module docs say that restored originals are checked.

**Tests:** `backup::tests::originals_must_match_their_content_hash` builds a zip whose entry has a valid CRC but other bytes under a photo's hash. `verify` accepts it, and `verify_original` rejects it and names the entry. The matching bytes pass.

title: Fix TIFF detection for camera-authored files (#281)
author: peiyan0
body:
Closes #281

### Problem
When browsing folders that contain TIFF files preserving camera EXIF tags (e.g. `Make: SONY`, `Make: NIKON CORPORATION`, `Make: PENTAX`, `Make: RICOH`, `Make: SAMSUNG`), `lightcraft_raw::probe()` previously checked only `make.starts_with(...)` without verifying that the file actually contained raw mosaic / CFA structures.
As a result:
- `lightcraft_raw::probe()` misclassified ordinary TIFF files as camera RAWs (ARW, NEF, NRW, PEF, SRW).
- `probe_info` or `decode` failed because ordinary TIFFs do not contain CFA mosaic data.
- The files carried no embedded RAW preview, causing `probe_bytes` to fail with `"unsupported raw without an embedded preview"`.
- The import/browse scanner marked them as errors and filtered them out, so the photos never appeared in the browser grid.

### Solution
1. In `crates/raw/src/lib.rs`:
   - Require `has_cfa` in `probe()` for vendor raws (Nikon, Sony, Pentax/Ricoh, Samsung).
   - In `has_raw_ifd()`, include Pentax compression 65535, Sony tone curve (`0x7010`), and CFA pattern tags (`0x828e`, `0x828d`).
2. In `crates/engine/src/files.rs`:
   - If a raw file fails `probe_info` or `decode` and has no embedded preview, allow it to fall through to standard image decoders if `lightcraft_codecs` can decode it (as is the case with ordinary TIFFs).
3. Added regression tests in `crates/raw` and `crates/engine` verifying that TIFFs with camera `Make` tags are recognized and loaded as ordinary images rather than raw files.

title: Advance selection to next photo after deleting (#441)
author: peiyan0
body:
Closes #441

### Problem
Previously, \`photo.delete\` unconditionally reset the selection to the first visible photo in the grid:
\`\`\`rust
let vis = s.visible_cloned();
s.selection = vis.first().map(|f| Selection::single(*f)).unwrap_or_default();
\`\`\`
As a result, whenever the user scrolled down and deleted a photo (or multiple photos), the selection jumped all the way back to the top of the grid (index 0), triggering grid/filmstrip scroll follow-active and causing the user to lose their scroll position.

### Solution
1. Added helper \`select_after_delete\` in \`crates/engine/src/cmd/library.rs\`:
   - Determines the anchor index of the deleted photo(s) in the pre-deletion visible list.
   - Advances selection to the next still-visible photo immediately following the deleted photos.
   - If the deleted photo was the last photo in the list, selects the previous still-visible photo.
   - If all photos in the view are deleted, selection is cleared.
2. Updated both \`photo.delete\` and \`photo.deletePermanently\` to use \`select_after_delete\`.
3. Added unit test \`delete_advances_selection_to_next_photo\` in \`crates/engine/src/tests.rs\` testing middle deletion, multi-photo deletion, last-photo deletion, and deleting all photos.

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: report Sony A200/A230/A350 packed ARW as unsupported (preview fallback)
author: radialmonster
body:
**TL;DR:** The Sony DSLR-A200, A230 and A350 sample files develop as pure colour noise today. This PR makes them report "unsupported" (like the A100/A290/A380/A390/A900 already do), so they open from the embedded preview instead. It does not decode them. Part of #461.

## Change

- `crates/raw/src/vendor/arw.rs`: the one-byte-per-pixel Sony ARW layout (Compression 32767, one strip) was accepted whenever the strip was between 1.00x and 1.25x of width x height bytes. It is now accepted only when the strip is exactly width x height bytes. Anything else returns `Unsupported("Sony ARW version 1 / packed compressed variant ...")`, the same message the A290/A380 already produce.
- `crates/engine/src/media.rs`: `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 16 -> 19. Main is at 16; open PRs #433, #447, #448, #453 and #459 set 17 and #470 sets 18, so 19 is the next free number. Renders of these three files change (noise -> preview). If one of those PRs lands first, this number should just be rebased to the next free one.

## How the rule was established

Only from LightCraft's own code and values measured in the files. For every Sony ARW in the test archive I read the raw IFD (Compression, BitsPerSample, width, height, StripByteCounts) and compared the strip size with width x height:

| Body | Strip / (width x height) | Today |
|---|---|---|
| A200 | 1.060 | noise |
| A230 | 1.232 | noise |
| A350 | 1.041 | noise |
| A290, A390 | 0.969, 0.929 | already unsupported (strip too small) |
| A380, A900 | 1.322, 1.500 | already unsupported (strip too large) |
| 108 other Compression 32767 files (A450, A500, A560, A700, SLT, NEX, ILCE, DSC, ILCA, ILME, ZV, UMC, ...) | exactly 1.000 | decode correctly |

The existing code already used "strip size is about width x height" as its test; the 1.25 upper bound was just too generous. title: LR-BEHAV-GPU: compile DX12 shaders with FXC, never a stray dxcompiler.dll (issue #471)
author: HarrisXiu
body:
Fixes #471.

## Root cause
The issue blames a `dxil.dll` missing from the MSI, but LightCraft ships no `dxcompiler.dll` either. wgpu 30's default DX12 compiler, `Dx12Compiler::Auto`, loads **whichever `dxcompiler.dll` the DLL search path finds first**, which is always another program's copy (a Windows SDK, an Edge/WebView folder, anything on `PATH`). Older copies (e.g. DXC 1.7.2308) without `dxil.dll` beside them print `warning: DXIL signing library (dxil.dll,libdxil.so) not found`. wgpu-hal treats any non-empty DXC error blob as a compile error, so its indirect-validation compute pipelines fail. The device is then lost and `eframe::run_native` returns `Parent device is lost` (exit code 1).

Shipping `dxil.dll` in the MSI would not fix this: the stray `dxcompiler.dll` would still be the one loaded. It would also add a native binary to the product.

## Fix
- New `lightcraft_gpu::backend::backend_options()`: wgpu's env-derived `BackendOptions`, with the DX12 compiler pinned to **FXC** (`d3dcompiler_47.dll`, part of Windows) unless `WGPU_DX12_COMPILER` names another (`dxc`, `auto`…; unknown values warn and fall back to FXC).
- All three wgpu instances use it: the window (`window_wgpu_options`), the render compute device (`ctx.rs`) and the denoise device (`nn.rs`).
- Docs: `docs/gpu-pipeline.md` (backends section) and `docs/whats-new.md` (Reliability).

The startup-failure dialog from #260 is already on `main` (0.4.0 predates it), so a failure like this one is no longer silent.

## Reproduction and verification (Windows 11, RTX 4080 Laptop, DX12)
| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| lone `dxcompiler.dll` 1.7.2308 (from WinSxS) first on `PATH` | **exit 1** with the issue's exact errors (`DXC compile error: warning: DXIL signing library … not found`, `Parent device is lost`) | window opens; log shows `Using FXC for shader compilation` for the window and compute instances, no errors |
| lone `dxcompiler.dll` 1.8.2502 (Windows SDK) first on `PATH` | opens (this version sign…

title: LRC-LIB-CATALOG-IMPORT: import crops from catalog develop settings (#483)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Part of #483.

**What the user saw:** `library.importLightroom` imported every cropped or straightened photo uncropped. The import report listed `CropLeft`, `CropRight`, `CropTop`, `CropBottom` and `CropAngle` as unmapped.

**Cause:** a Lightroom Classic catalog's develop settings store the crop edges and angle, but no `HasCrop` key. XMP has `crs:HasCrop`. The shared mapper in `crs.rs` maps a crop only when `crs:HasCrop` is `True`, so catalog crops were skipped.

**What changed:** `mapped_settings` in `crates/engine/src/lightroom_catalog.rs` (the catalog path only) adds `HasCrop = True` when any crop field is present and `HasCrop` is not. The XMP mapper is unchanged, because in XMP `HasCrop="False"` next to crop fields means the crop is off. This is the fix the reporter suggested and tested on their catalog: after it, all 543 plain crops on unrotated photos match Lightroom's exports. `docs/lightroom-catalog-import.md` now says this, and also lists what still does not work.

**Not fixed here (the rest of #483):**
- Crops on rotated (portrait) photos. Adobe's crop edges are relative to the unrotated image, but LightCraft's crop rectangle is in the oriented frame. To convert them, the import needs each photo's orientation. The importer does not read `Adobe_images.orientation` yet and does not carry over Lightroom's user rotation, and the XMP sidecar path has the same gap. That needs its own change, checked against real rotated photos.
- Crops with a straighten angle. The reporter thinks that with a non-zero angle Lightroom's edges are opposite corners of the rotated rectangle, not an axis-aligned box. That still has to be confirmed before LightCraft's crop model is changed.

On those photos the crop is now applied but can come out the wrong shape. Before this change it was dropped entirely. Either way the crop can still be edited.

title: LRC-LIB-CATALOG-IMPORT: import catalog crops that have no HasCrop
author: rock-meister
body:
Refs #483 (fixes the first of its three causes)

## What

Lightroom Classic catalogs store crop edges and straighten angle in their develop settings (`CropLeft`, `CropTop`, `CropRight`, `CropBottom`, `CropAngle`) but never a `HasCrop` flag; only XMP has `crs:HasCrop`. The shared `crs` mapper applies a crop only when `crs:HasCrop` is `True`, so `library.importLightroom` dropped every crop and reported the fields as unmapped.

`mapped_settings` in `lightroom_catalog.rs` now infers `HasCrop = True` when any crop field is present and the settings don't already say otherwise. The XMP path is unchanged, because there `HasCrop="False"` together with crop fields means the crop is switched off.

## Results on a real catalog

1918 photos, 987 of them cropped or straightened. After import and relink, I rendered every cropped photo and compared the frame's aspect ratio (1% tolerance) with the JPEGs Lightroom exported from the same catalog:

- before: no crops applied
- after: **543 / 543** unrotated photos with a plain crop come out the right shape
- only `CropConstrainAspectRatio` (the UI aspect lock) is still unmapped

Not in this PR (both described in #483):
- crops on photos with a 90°/270° orientation: `crs` crop edges are in the unrotated frame, `CropGeometry` is in the oriented frame
- crops with a straighten angle: probably a different rectangle model

## Tests

- New `catalog_crops_without_has_crop_are_imported`: fails before the fix, passes after. It covers partial edges (defaults for missing `CropTop`/`CropBottom`), angle-only, and settings with no crop.
- `cargo test --workspace`: 1878 passed, 0 failed. I skipped `tests_face_recognize` because five of its tests ran over 30 minutes in a debug build here; they don't touch this code.

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: decode Canon sRAW and mRAW CR2 from their data instead of the preview
author: radialmonster
body:
**TL;DR:** Canon sRAW and mRAW files (the reduced-size raw modes on EOS 5D II and later) used to open from the small embedded JPEG with a "preview only" warning. They now decode from the raw data and get the normal develop pipeline. All 31 sRAW/mRAW CC0 samples (16 camera models) decode; 12 other raw files (Canon CR2 and CR3, Sony ARW including a downsized one, Nikon, DNG) render pixel-identical to main. CR3 sRAW/mRAW is not covered (no sample exists).

Related: #214 (closed for CR3; the remaining request there was Canon mRAW/sRAW), #85 (sRAW noted as the open follow-up), #213 (the YCbCr path this reuses).


## Problem

Canon sRAW and mRAW store the picture as subsampled YCbCr (luma at full size, chroma at half width, plus half height for mRAW) in a lossless-JPEG frame, not as a Bayer mosaic. `cr2.rs` rejected raw type 4, so every one of them rendered from the embedded JPEG. Two users asked (#214, and the 80D sample in #85).

## Change

- `ljpeg.rs`: `decode_subsampled` (added in #213 for Sony M/S ARW) takes a `Prediction`. `Geometric` is Sony's, unchanged. `Sequential` is Canon's: each component is a one-dimensional chain in decoding order, and each frame row starts from the first sample of the previous row. `frame_info_subsampled` also returns the chroma subsampling.
- `vendor/cr2/sraw.rs` (new): reads the `cr2_slice` layout (widths counted in samples, whole MCUs), re-chops the decoded stream into image planes, converts to linear RGB (`cpp` 3, white balance already baked in, so multipliers 1 as for Sony's linear YCbCr), takes the active area from the maker note `SensorInfo` as for CFA files, and sets the white level.
- `cr2.rs`: raw type 4 goes to the new module; other types are still unsupported.
- `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 16 to 21: these files render differently (cached thumbnails of the preview would be stale). Open PRs already use 17 to 20, so this takes the next free number; if the order of merging differs, it just needs whatever number is free then.

title: LRC-LIB-CATALOG-IMPORT: carry catalog crops through the photo orientation
author: rock-meister
body:
Refs #483 (cause 2: crops on rotated photos). **Builds on #489:** the first two commits are #489's, and only the last commit (2ec2b5b) is new. Once #489 merges, this PR shows just that commit.

## What

`crs` crop edges are normalized to the stored (unrotated) image, but `CropGeometry` is in the oriented frame (`pipeline/src/geometry.rs`). Catalog import used the edges unchanged, so crops on portrait photos (EXIF 6/8) landed along the wrong axes.

The import now reads Lightroom's per-image orientation code (`Adobe_images.orientation`) and maps the rectangle with the existing `Orientation::map_norm_rect`; a mirrored orientation also mirrors the straighten angle. The code comes from the catalog, so this works while the originals are still missing at import, which is the usual case when a catalog moves to another machine.

`lightroom_orientation` derives each code from `Orientation::map` (where the stored top-left and top-right corners land, with displayed corners A–D clockwise from the top left) instead of a hand-written table. On a real catalog, all 1918 photos matched their files' EXIF orientation: `AB` = 1 (1220 photos), `BC` = 6 (537), `DA` = 8 (161). The mirrored codes follow the same rule; I have no real files that use them.

## Results on a real catalog

987 cropped photos, rendered after import and relink and compared with the JPEGs Lightroom exported. "Frame right" means the aspect ratio is within 1%; ΔE is CIE76 at 200 px.

| Photos | #489 only | with this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Unrotated, plain crop | 543 / 543 | 543 / 543 |
| 90° CW (`BC`), plain crop | 62 / 137 (median ΔE 26.1) | **137 / 137** (ΔE 10.8) |
| 270° CW (`DA`), plain crop | 14 / 84 (ΔE 30.6) | **84 / 84** (ΔE 10.7) |
| Crops with `CropAngle`, any orientation | 29 / 223 | 32 / 223 |

The angled crops are cause 3 in #483 and aren't addressed here.

title: LRC-LIB-CATALOG-IMPORT: import straightened catalog crops as Lightroom shows them
author: rock-meister
body:
Refs #483 (cause 3: straightened crops). **Builds on #493, which builds on #489:** only the last commit (369c56a) is new here.

## What

With a `CropAngle`, Lightroom's `CropLeft/CropTop` and `CropRight/CropBottom` are the **top-left and bottom-right corners of the tilted crop** on the stored image, not an axis-aligned rectangle. Lightroom's angle also **turns the other way** from LightCraft's `CropGeometry::angle`. The catalog import treated the edges as a rectangle in the rotated frame and kept the angle's sign, so straightened crops came out the wrong shape and size.

`catalog_crop` (replacing #493's `orient_crop`) now:
1. takes the two corners in pixels of the stored image, using `fileWidth / fileHeight` from `Adobe_images`, because the rectangle's aspect matters once it turns;
2. maps them through the photo's orientation (#493);
3. applies LightCraft's own image → rotated-frame transform, `Affine::rotate_about(angle)` about the centre, with `angle = −CropAngle` (a mirrored orientation flips it back);
4. stores the resulting axis-aligned rectangle, normalized to the oriented image.

With `CropAngle = 0` this is exactly #493's mapping.

## How the model was established

There was no spec to work from, so I fitted the model to Lightroom's own output: the 223 straightened crops in a real catalog, compared with the JPEGs Lightroom exported from them (all exported after their last edit).

| Reading of the four edges | Export frame aspect within 1% |
|---|---|
| Axis-aligned box in the rotated frame (current) | 35 / 223 |
| Corners of the tilted crop, rotated by −`CropAngle` | **223 / 223** (median error 0.01%) |
| Corners, rotated by +`CropAngle` | 13 / 223 |

## Results after rendering

All 987 cropped photos in the catalog, after import, relink and render, compared with Lightroom's exports:

| Straightened crops | #493 | with this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Unrotated (`AB`) | 17 / 109 frames right, median ΔE 14.9 | **109 / 109**, ΔE 10.9 |
| 90° CW (`BC`) | 12 / 108, ΔE …

title: LR-EDIT-OPTICS-PROFILE: apply embedded A7R IVA distortion corrections
author: QuirkyTurtle94
body:
Sony A7R IVA RAWs can contain per-image lens distortion data while LightCraft reports no embedded correction. Decode the signed 16-sample raw-IFD table (`0x7037`) into the existing `WarpRectilinear` path. The existing Optics control can disable or adjust the correction, and DNG export preserves it.

The merged implementation is restricted to exact **ILCE-7RM4A Bayer ARWs**, independently checked with the FE 24–105mm F4 G OSS and FE 200–600mm F5.6–6.3 G OSS. Other Sony models remain uncorrected. Preserve main's image crop order: Sony crop tags → DefaultCrop → recorded image size. The warp independently uses DefaultCrop for its centre/normalization.

This PR merged at `7962c78` through #692. It includes the original 11-file model-boundary test and synthetic geometry/header/full/DNG checks. Distortion only; vignetting, lateral CA, other table layouts and unvalidated bodies remain outside scope. No private photos or reference exports are committed.

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: fit the starting tone curve by quantile matching (no flat steps), old fit as fallback
author: radialmonster
body:
**TL;DR:** for raw files without a camera colour matrix, LightCraft fits a starting tone curve to the camera's embedded JPEG. That fit could produce flat steps (many scene tones squeezed into one output tone), which render as posterised patches with hard edges. This PR fits the curve by matching the two images' overall tone distributions instead, which cannot produce steps, and keeps the old fit as a fallback so no photo loses its fitted look. Across a public archive of 1,870 raw files, fitted curves with flat steps go from 384 of 1,023 to 6, no file loses or gains a look, and 765 files render byte-for-byte as before. The 6 files that still have steps are the ones that only pass the acceptance gates with the old curve; see "Results".

Part of #475. Related: #211 and #454 (see "What this does not change").

## Change

`fit_tone` in `crates/engine/src/camera_preview.rs` builds the per-photo tone curve (32 knots) that the starting look uses for raws without a camera matrix (ARW, NEF/NRW, RW2, RAF, CR2/CR3, PEF).

- Before: pair the photo's scene luminance with the camera JPEG's luminance pixel by pixel, bin by scene luminance, take the JPEG's median per bin, then pool neighbouring bins that go the wrong way (isotonic pooling). Camera JPEGs are lens-corrected and sharpened, so on a detailed scene the two images do not line up and neighbouring bins disagree by more than the gap between them. Pooling then turns the disagreement into flat segments: 13 of the 31 segments on a Z 6II forest sample. Every flat segment maps a whole range of scene tones to one display tone.
- After: sort the scene luminances and the JPEG luminances separately and pair the median of each 1/32 slice (quantile matching). A tone curve is increasing, so it must map each quantile of the scene to the same quantile of the JPEG. That needs no pixel-exact alignment and is increasing by construction, so there is nothing to pool.
- Fallback: the quantile fit is a slightly worse least-squares fit than the ol…

title: LR-EDIT-DETAIL-DENOISE: fix shared-memory races in GPU denoising
author: QuirkyTurtle94
body:
Fixes #479.

GPU denoise convolution let different invocations write individual lanes of the same workgroup `vec4`. WGSL permits a component write to access the whole vector, so these writes conflict before the following barrier. On Apple M1 / Metal this made CPU/reference comparisons fail with huge or non-finite values.

Store the shared input tile as independently written scalars and assemble local vectors after the existing barrier. This preserves the shared-memory byte count, vectorized input loads, work distribution and accumulation order. Shared weight vectors already have one writer and retain their existing layout. Neither tolerances nor GPU execution are disabled.

Add repeated partial-tile coverage and make the comparison helper explicitly reject non-finite outputs. Update the denoise documentation and parity row.

Validation on Apple M1 / Metal, macOS 27.0.1, official Rust 1.97.1:
- Unmodified upstream reproduces both failures. A shader-only diagnostic makes both pass; restoring the original shader brings both failures back.
- New repeated-input regression fails with the original writes (`1.2e35` relative error) and passes with the fix.
- Focused GPU suite: five active tests pass, including concurrent runner use; two existing tests remain ignored. Maximum relative error in the existing size/depth cases is about `1.1e-6`, below the unchanged `2e-4` limit.

Full `cargo xtask ci` passes all eight gates: fmt, Clippy, HEIF, workspace tests, parity, layering, assets and all 25 wasm crates. Run with `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=1` and the official Rust 1.97.1 toolchain on PATH.

No real-model weights were downloaded or tested. DX12/Vulkan and M5 confirmation, and real-model throughput measurement, remain unverified. This PR is independent of the Sony lens correction PR #498 and contains no private images or model assets.

title: LR-BEHAV-BG-TASKS: render export batches side by side (issue #496)
author: HarrisXiu
body:
Fixes #496.

## Problem

Each photo's render is already parallel inside (row-parallel pipeline, parallel demosaic and JPEG encoder, GPU when available), but `run_batch` exported a batch strictly one photo after another. The serial parts of each photo — decode, PNG/TIFF/WebP encoding, waiting on a GPU render — left most cores idle. Measured on 32 cores with 24 MP JPEGs: the CPU path averaged ~9.5 busy cores, and with the GPU on the CPU mostly sat at 1–2 cores.

Per-stage wall time of one 24 MP export (1 thread → 32 threads): decode 165 → 85 ms (~2×), CPU render 3800 → 275 ms (14×), JPEG encode 660 → 110 ms (6×), PNG/TIFF/WebP encode ~1–1.5×; GPU render ~150 ms with the CPU idle.

## Change

- **`run_batch` keeps several photos in flight**: `export_parallelism()` = cores / 4, clamped to 1..=4 (1 on wasm32), on scoped `std` lane threads plus the calling thread. Not rayon tasks: a pool thread waiting in a nested call could stack a second GPU render on itself.
- **Batch order is unchanged**: path choice, conflict policy (Unique numbering), original protection, writes, results and `progress`/cancel all run in batch order in a `Placer`, so the files are identical to one at a time. A panic in a lane (`guard::catch`) becomes that photo's error.
- **Memory**: new `memory::export_gate()` (twice the memory budget), separate from the decode `work_gate` it nests over (one gate held across the other's acquire could deadlock). Each `PreparedExport` carries an estimated working-memory weight: source px × 12 B + output px × 36 B — ~1.1 GB for a full-size 24 MP export (measured peak ~1.2 GB), ~145 MB for 2048 px from the preview (measured ~150 MB). With the default budget, full-size 24 MP exports run two at a time.
- Lanes take at most `lanes` photos past the last one placed, which also bounds finished files waiting in memory for their turn (e.g. 144 MB 16-bit TIFFs).
- `render_bench`'s `ONLY=batch` scenario now goes through `export_batch`.
- Docs: `docs/parity.md` (LR-BEHAV-BG-TASKS)…

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: name GoPro GPR (VC-5 DNG) in the unsupported-raw error instead of 'TIFF compression 9'
author: radialmonster
body:
**TL;DR:** GoPro `.GPR` files (DNGs with VC-5 compressed raw data) now fail with `unsupported raw (DNG compression 9 (GoPro VC-5) is not decoded yet) without an embedded preview` instead of `unsupported raw (TIFF compression 9) ...`. Nothing else changes: these files have no embedded preview, so there is still no picture, and import behaves exactly as before.

Fixes #507.

## Change

- `crates/tiff`: a named constant `compression::VC5` (9).
- `crates/raw/src/dng.rs`: when the raw IFD of a DNG says `Compression` 9, the full decode returns `Unsupported("DNG compression 9 (GoPro VC-5) is not decoded yet")` before the chunk decoder gets to produce the bare "TIFF compression 9".
- The header probe is deliberately left alone, so the file still imports (as today) and the clear message is what the user sees when it is opened or exported. Making the probe fail too would refuse the import, and because the file has no preview the import report would only say "not readable".
- No change to any file that decodes today, so `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` stays as it is. Nothing is cached for a failed render.

## How it was established

- Read the tags of all 17 CC0 GoPro files on raw.pixls.us (ids 936, 1634, 2556, 2557, 2558, 2786, 2846, 2908, 5766, 3949, 5767, 4483, 4883, 4894, 7319, 7370, 7371): one IFD each, no SubIFDs, no thumbnail or JPEG pointer, `Compression` 9, `PhotometricInterpretation` 32803. So there is no preview to use, and the "use the embedded preview" path cannot help these files.

  - after: import adds 1 photo (unchanged), render exits 1 with `unsupported raw (DNG compression 9 (GoPro VC-5) is not decoded yet) without an embedded preview`.

title: Fix DNG 1.7 row/column-interleaved rasters (JPEG XL DNGs decoded as a purple 2×2 grid)
author: AER00
body:
**What**

DNG 1.7 can store the CFA mosaic interleaved: RowInterleaveFactor (0xC71F) and ColumnInterleaveFactor (0xCD43) permute the stored raster without changing its dimensions or sample count. LightCraft read the samples straight through, so an interleaved file decoded as n × m half-scale copies of the scene — one per quadrant, in scrambled Bayer colours. Reported as "4 images in a purple grid" on real JPEG XL DNGs written by Adobe's converter.

**Fix**

deinterleave() in crates/raw/src/dng.rs undoes the permutation after decode when either factor is > 1, driven by the two new tag constants in crates/tiff/src/tags.rs. Stored row r belongs to group r / (h / rows) at position r % (h / rows) within it,
and that position holds image row group + rows * position; columns likewise.

Guardrails: factors outside 1..=16 are refused as unsupported; a factor that does not divide the image is refused as corrupt; the permutation is a destination-indexed copy, since it is not its own inverse.

**Verification**

- 4 real ILCE-6400 JPEG XL DNGs now render bit-identical to their non-interleaved twins (max |diff| 0.000/255).
- Unit tests cover a forward/inverse writer simulation, the decode path, and a no-op/refusal case. The decode test uses factors 3×3 deliberately — a 2×2 interleave is self-inverse and would pass with the permutation applied backwards, so 3×3 is what actually pins the direction.

**Notes**

No behavioural change for files without these tags.

title: Match the default raw tone curve to Lightroom's
author: AER00
body:
# Match the default raw rendering to Lightroom (tone and colour)

The default raw look was tuned by eye. These commits measure it against Lightroom Adobe
Standard instead: the tone curve first, then the colourfulness that curve was throwing away.
References are Lightroom output on raws we own, kept locally and never committed.

## Tone

The curve was about a stop dark, had a lifted toe and clipped highlights. It now uses a logistic
shoulder, with `BASE_SLOPE = 1.56` / `BASE_WHITE_EV = 1.30` fitted to **0.045 stops RMS** by
exposure ladder — a pixel's percentile rank is invariant down a ladder, which reconstructs each
engine's scene→display curve on one absolute axis without assuming anything about either.
Whites split into `WHITES_UP` / `WHITES_DOWN`: one symmetric coefficient made it 2.4× too
strong downward, and that slider's mean error drops 19.6 → 8.5 per 255. ARW renders come back
bit-identical, since they take tone from a per-photo fit rather than this curve.

## Color

With tone matched, the render was still **~19 % under the reference in chroma** over saturated
pixels, worse the darker the pixel. It is not the camera profile: the embedded
`ProfileHueSatMap` and `ProfileLookTable` are applied faithfully (perturbing either table *in
the file* moves both engines by the same factor), neutralising both leaves the deficit
unchanged, and the data is md5-identical to Adobe's own DCP.

`ToneMap::new` mapped *luminance* and rescaled the colour with it, which preserves saturation
exactly, where the reference's baseline curve acts on the channels. `DEFAULT_CHROMA` multiplies
the colour back about the mapped luminance — the mechanism `CameraTone::chroma` already had for
file-local looks, which the default curve passed as `NO_CHROMA`. Derived by measurement, and it
avoids a per-channel curve's hue shifts and clipping.

## Results

The 5 DNGs embedding a single Adobe Standard profile (the rest are off-target by construction),
mean over the frame: **ΔE 6.30 → 3.49, chroma 0…

title: Issue #399: Windows MSI: choose the install folder, finish dialog with Launch LightCraft
author: HarrisXiu
body:
Fixes #399. Fixes #18. Supersedes #79: its commit is included unchanged, with authorship kept.

## Why
The MSI had no UI at all. It installed straight into `C:\Program Files\LightCraft` and closed without a word, so a successful install looked like nothing had happened: in #399 Phantomx2 thought the installer had failed. Users also had no way to choose where LightCraft goes.

## What
The interactive installer now walks **Welcome → Destination Folder → Ready → progress → Completed**:
- **Completed page** (from #79, Brandon Thomas): "LightCraft has been installed", plus a ticked **Launch LightCraft** box. The launch goes through `WixUnelevatedShellExec`, so the app runs as the signed-in user, never elevated. Failure and cancellation end on WiX's FatalError / UserExit pages instead.
- **Destination Folder** (new): WiX's `InstallDirDlg`. It defaults to `Program Files\LightCraft\`, **Change...** browses, and `WixUIValidatePath` refuses a folder that can't be used (`InvalidDirDlg`). Patches skip it.
- **Upgrades keep the chosen folder.** `LightcraftApp` writes `HKLM\Software\LightCraft\InstallFolder`. A `RegistrySearch` reads it back into `PREVIOUSINSTALLFOLDER`, and a `SetProperty` after `AppSearch` copies it to `INSTALLFOLDER` unless `INSTALLFOLDER=` was given on the command line. Without this, a major upgrade would move a `D:\Apps\LightCraft` install back to Program Files.
- **Silent / passive installs** (`/qn`, `/passive`) show no dialogs, launch nothing, and accept `INSTALLFOLDER=...`.
- **CI guard:** `packaging-lint` fails if `lightcraft.wxs` loses the UI, the folder page, the remembered folder or the launch action.
- **Docs:** README → Downloads → Windows; `docs/whats-new.md`.

#79's `package.ps1` / `release.yml` changes (UI + Util extensions 5.0.2, generated plain bitmaps, no third-party artwork) cherry-picked cleanly onto current `main`.

## Testing (Windows 11, WiX 5.0.2)

title: Fix brush subtraction and new brush mask creation
author: QuirkyTurtle94
body:
Fixes #516.

`Subtract > Brush` switched to Erase, which only removed paint inside a brush component. On a Sky mask it erased an empty Add component, leaving the sky selected. `Create New Mask > Brush` also reused the current mask and could retain Erase mode, making a new brush appear ineffective.

- Create a brush component with the requested Add/Subtract operation and paint into it. Erase/Alt continues to remove coverage within that component.
- Create a separate brush mask from the New Mask tile; explicit new/add/subtract brush operations start in paint mode and show the overlay.
- Keep subsequent strokes in the latest brush component even after it is renamed, rather than silently creating an Add component.
- Route creation through `tool.brush` for UI/control-channel consistency; document its parameters and update the masking parity rows.

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: fit the camera look without clipped sensor pixels
author: radialmonster
body: **TL;DR:** when a raw has no colour matrix, LightCraft fits its starting look to the camera's embedded JPEG. Pixels where the sensor was clipped (a bright sky, a lamp, a white wall in sun) were used in that fit, although their raw colour is wrong: a white overcast sky with one clipped channel comes out magenta or blue in the raw while the JPEG shows it white. The fit then dulled every colour and removed colour at the sky's brightness. This PR leaves clipped pixels out of the fit. Foliage, skin and painted surfaces get their colour back on many Nikon Z, Sony, Panasonic and Fujifilm files; no file loses its fitted look. Stacked on #499 (review that first; this branch contains its commits). Part of #211 and #244. *CC0 samples from raw.pixls.us. Left: camera JPEG; middle: with #499 only; right: this PR.* ## Change - The small sensor and JPEG images used for the fit now come with a clip mask: a pixel counts as clipped when any raw sample it covers is at 99% of white or more, the same level the render's highlight reconstruction uses. For CR3 the mask is turned and moved with the same framing as the sensor image. - The search for a look runs as before on all pixels and decides, as before, whether the photo gets a look and which attempt gives it (tone fit, camera profile or the photo's own colour, all pixels or only those away from edges). Only that attempt is then fitted again without the clipped pixels. If the new fit misses the acceptance gates, the earlier look is kept unchanged. A photo that had no look gets one when the search without clipped pixels finds one. - Camera profiles built with `lightcraft-cli calibrate` leave clipped pixels out too. - No change to the gates, no per-camera tables. Render cache version 23 (#499 has 22; whichever lands later takes the next free number). ## How it…

title: LR-PRE-AMOUNT: presets with the Grain group apply at any amount
author: AlexChambers
body:
A preset that includes the Grain group did nothing when applied at any amount other than 100%. Presets made with the default copy groups include it.

**Cause.** `scale_patch` interpolates every JSON number as a float, including `grain.seed`, which is a `u32`. At 50%, a seed of 12345 becomes 6172.5, which doesn't deserialize as `u32`. `merged()` then fails, and `apply_partial` falls back to the photo's unchanged settings. The whole preset is dropped silently, not only the grain.

**Fix.** Two numbers interpolate only when at least one of them is a float. Integer fields such as the grain seed and ids are discrete, so they are handled like strings and booleans already are: the preset's value from 50% up, the photo's below. Float settings serialize as JSON floats, so they keep interpolating. Integer literals in preset files, like `"contrast": 40` in the existing test, also keep interpolating against the photo's float value.

**Test.** `amount_keeps_integer_fields_whole` builds a preset from the default copy groups with exposure, grain amount and a grain seed set, applies it at 30%, 50%, 150% and 200%, and checks exposure and grain amount scale while the seed stays whole. Without the fix it fails at 30% with exposure 0, because the preset was dropped.


`cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, heif, parity, layers, assets and wasm pass. The workspace tests pass except `nn::tests::the_gpu_gives_what_the_reference_gives` and `a_runner_serves_many_tiles_from_many_threads` in `crates/gpu`. Those fail the same way on unmodified `main` on an M3 Max (#479, #500).

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: calibrate rejected every ILCE-7RM4 file (camera JPEG proxy a pixel short)
author: rock-meister
body:
## What

`lightcraft-cli calibrate` rejected **every** ILCE-7RM4 (A7R IV) ARW with "skipped (no usable camera JPEG or colour)", so no profile could be written for this camera.

`proxies()` fitted the decoded camera JPEG *into* the sensor proxy's box. Fitting keeps the JPEG's own aspect, which can round a pixel short: this camera's 1616×1080 preview, decoded at 384×257 for the 192 px profile proxy, fits a 192×128 sensor proxy as **191×128**. `collect_pairs` then refused the mismatched sizes for every file.

The fix resizes the JPEG to exactly the sensor proxy's size (new `reference_at`). `proxies()` has already rejected references whose aspect differs by more than 2%, so the stretch is at most a pixel.

## Effect

- **No change to working renders.** `fit` is `resize` at a rounded size, so whenever fitting already landed on the proxy's size the output is identical. On 34 real ILCE-7RM4 ARWs, default renders are bit-identical before and after. The single-photo fit uses the 96 px proxy, where this camera's preview rounds to the exact size anyway.
- **Calibrate works on this camera.** On 923 ILCE-7RM4 ARWs from one trip: before, 0 accepted and no profile written; after, 843 accepted and `ILCE-7RM4.json` written (80 still skipped by the existing gates, e.g. near-colourless frames).
- **The profile fixes the muted fallback.** Across 1852 ARWs from the same body, 58 (3%) rendered far from their own camera JPEG (CIE76 ΔE > 8 on 48 px downscales). Those are files whose single-photo fit is rejected, mostly dull, low-colour scenes, and they get the documented flat fallback. With the profile from this fix, 52 of the 58 match the camera JPEG (ΔE ~1), and the median over all 1852 is unchanged (3.5). This is the "colour way off" symptom in #515.
- Other bodies whose preview rounds a pixel short at 192 px are presumably affected the same way. I only had ILCE-7RM4 files to verify with.

title: LRC-DEV-PROCESS: process versions, so a look change can ship without changing existing edits (#146)
author: AlexChambers
body:
## Why

Issue #146 proposes retuning the default raw tone curve, and notes that this "changes the look of every existing raw edit, so it needs a maintainer decision (e.g. versioned process defaults so existing edits keep their look)". #196 (stronger Highlights / Shadows / Whites / Blacks) has the same problem. LightCraft had no way to tell which rendering a photo was edited under.

#514 (retuning the default raw curve against Lightroom) is the first change that would need it.

This PR adds that mechanism, modelled on Lightroom's process version. It does not change any rendering: there is one process, V1, which is today's pipeline. A tone retune can then land as V2 without touching existing edits.

## What it does

- `DevelopSettings::process: ProcessVersion` (a `u32` newtype) records the rendering process. `Process` is an enum of the processes this build implements (only `V1`), so `match`es on it are exhaustive and adding V2 makes the compiler point at every stage that depends on it.
- **One seam in the pipeline:** `lightcraft_pipeline::finish::base_tone` picks the base tone map by process (`Process::V1 =>` the existing camera / raw / display tone maps, unchanged). CPU and GPU both get it through `FinishParams::new`.
- **New command** `develop.updateProcess`, "Update to Current Process", in the Photo menu after Reset Edits. It moves the target photos that are on an older process to the latest as one undo step (history entry on each photo), keeps slider values, and never moves a photo to an older process. The menu item is enabled only while a selected photo is on an older process, so today it is always disabled (with the reason "already on the current process (version 1)"). A call that names its photos (`ids` / `id`) acts on them whatever is selected: each must exist and one must be on an older process, otherwise it returns an error.
- **Explicit targets:** `Session::execute` checks a command's enablement before the handler sees `ids`, so a selection-based predicate …

title: LRC-LIB-CATALOG-IMPORT: read Lightroom's Custom white balance by its as-shot shift on relative-WB raws (#510)
author: jbasseti
body:
Fixes #510.

A Custom white balance from a Lightroom catalog or XMP sidecar was taken as absolute Kelvin for every raw. Raws LightCraft develops relative to their as-shot look (ARW, NEF, RW2, RAF, CR3, CR2, PEF, where 6500 K / 0 means *as shot*) then read a small tweak as a large blue shift: ΔE 22 against Lightroom's own export on the photos in the issue.

## Change

- The `crs` mapper takes a `Target` (preset, rendered, raw with a measured illuminant, relative-WB raw) instead of a `raw: Option<bool>`. Import, sidecar read and catalog import derive it the same way through a new `lightcraft_catalog::relative_wb_format`, which `Photo::relative_wb` now uses too. A raw shown from its embedded preview counts as rendered.
- **Convert when an as-shot reference exists.** On a relative-WB raw (and a rendered file that has only `Temperature`), a Kelvin value becomes the same mired shift from the packet's `crs:AsShotTemperature` / `crs:AsShotTint`, which XMP sidecars carry. The issue's example, 3650 → 3578 K, lands at ~6275 K on our scale, as the issue predicted.
- **Fall back honestly otherwise.** Lightroom catalogs keep no as-shot white for Custom photos. The photo then stays As Shot (ΔE 12 on the issue's photos instead of 22) and the import report lists `Temperature, Tint (custom white balance without AsShotTemperature: kept As Shot)`.
- Raws with a measured illuminant (DNG), presets and rendered files with `Incremental*` fields are read exactly as before.

Not in scope: estimating an absolute as-shot illuminant from the camera's WB multipliers (the issue's approach 3).

## Tests

- `crs::custom_kelvin_on_relative_wb_raws_shifts_from_the_as_shot_white`: shift, tint difference, same result for rendered, Kelvin kept for absolute raws and presets, as-shot fields not reported.

title: LR-IMP-CAMERA-COVERAGE: Sony black levels: SR2 layouts and lossless M/S pedestal
author: AlexChambers
body:
Part of #535 (items 2 and 3).

## What was wrong

**SR2 black level (item 2).** Sony bodies that don't write the plain black-level tag (`0x7310`) keep it in the encrypted `SR2SubIFD`. The decoder deciphered a fixed position (byte 2510). That position is right for three of the directory layouts but holds other data in two more:

- DSLR-A450, A500 and A550 (27152-byte layout) read 354–365.
- DSLR-A700 (62112-byte layout) read 975.

ExifTool says 512 in all four, and so does the data: the darkest 0.1 % of each channel sits at 528–588. The A700 rendered crushed and dark even with an accepted camera look: ΔE 20.1, ΔL\* −9.8.

**Lossless M/S pedestal (item 3).** Downsized lossless ARWs (M and S sizes, linear YCbCr) are stored 1024 above zero, but the decoder subtracted the 512 the raw IFD records. That left a pedestal of about 3 % of white, i.e. lifted, hazy shadows. An accepted fit partly hides it, and it shows clearly with a camera profile.

## How it was established (black box only)

- **SR2 layouts.** The plaintext came from two places: the plain `0x7310` that newer bodies also write, and the decrypted directory that `exiftool -v3` prints (ExifTool used as a tool, never its source). With it, I surveyed 115 ARWs from 97 bodies on raw.pixls.us, covering 15 SR2 layouts:
  - The keystream depends only on the position in the block. Its first 16 bytes are identical in all 115 files.
  - The directory's first entry is always the black level (`0x7310`, SHORT, count 4). Its value sits at a layout-dependent position, between 1638 and 2786.
  - At each position the keystream is the same in every file that stores its black there: 4 files at 1638, 10 at 2166, 8 at 2418 and 55 at 2510.
- **YCbCr pedestal.** Each of 12 M/S files from four bodies was compared with a full-size coding of the same scene shot seconds apart. On pixels where both camera JPEGs agree, M/S = k · (full-size − 512) · WB + b, with:
  - b = 1015–1052 on 11 of the 12 pairs (the ILCE-7M4 S pair fits 941–965);
  - g…

title: #538: breadcrumbs open their folder as spelled; fix browse test on Windows
author: HarrisXiu
body:
Fixes #538.

## Problem
`headless::tests::browse_a_local_folder` failed on Windows. It compared the browsed folder with `\` replaced by `/`, but `library.browse` stores the path with the platform's separators (`std::path::absolute`), so the strings never matched. The app opened the right folder; only the comparison was wrong.

While looking at it, two real Windows bugs showed up in how a breadcrumb rebuilt the path it opens. The old code joined the names with `/` and kept only a leading `/`:
- **UNC paths:** `\server\share\photos` became `server/share`, so the breadcrumb lost the share.
- **Drive crumb:** clicking `C:` opened `C:`, which on Windows means the *current folder* on drive C, not its root.

## Fix
- `crumbs(path)` in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/grid.rs` lists each breadcrumb's name together with the path it opens. That path is cut from the original string, so it keeps the original separators, a leading `/`, and a UNC `\`. A bare drive gets its separator back (`C:\`). The slicing uses `get`, so it never panics on odd input.
- The test now compares paths (`Path` equality), not strings.

## Tests
- New `breadcrumbs_open_their_folder_as_spelled` covers Unix, a Windows drive (with `\` and with `/`), UNC, relative paths, a trailing separator, non-ASCII names, and empty and root-only paths. It fails on the old join (UNC and drive cases).
- `browse_a_local_folder` passes on Windows.
- `cargo xtask ci` green on Windows.

## Not changed
`library.browse` (like the other folder keys in the catalog) trims trailing separators, so browsing a drive root still stores `C:`, and `/` becomes an empty string. Changing that touches how folders are matched in `catalog/src/query.rs`, so it is left for a separate change.
