title: LR-CROP-ROTATE-DRAG: draw a rotate pointer outside the crop box (issue #534)
author: HarrisXiu
body:
Fixes #534.

## Problem
In Crop & Rotate, dragging outside the crop box rotates the crop, but nothing showed it. The pointer there was egui's `CursorIcon::Alias`, a stand-in because there is no system rotate cursor. winit maps `Alias` to a plain arrow on Windows (`_ => IDC_ARROW`) and to the drag-link cursor on macOS, so on Windows the cursor didn't change at all.

## Fix
- Outside the box the system pointer is hidden, and a curved double arrow is drawn in its place. It is white on a dark outline and bends around the photo's centre, so it reads the same on every platform and on any photo. It is original vector art drawn in code (`rotate_cursor_shape`), recorded in `assets/ATTRIBUTION.md`.
- While rotating, the current angle (e.g. `13.91°`) is shown next to the pointer.
- The drawn arrow replaces the system cursor on every platform: macOS (was the drag-link cursor), Linux (the theme's `alias` cursor) and the web build (`cursor: none`) now look the same as Windows. Rotating by dragging works as before.

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: decode Hasselblad lossless JPEG with selection value 8 (FFF, H3D/H4D/CFV-50c 3FR)
author: radialmonster
body:
**TL;DR:** LightCraft now decodes the Hasselblad raws that store their sensor data in Hasselblad's own
variant of lossless JPEG: every FFF file and the H3D, H4D and CFV-50c 3FR files (the other 14 of the 20 CC0
Hasselblad samples on raw.pixls.us, so all 20 now decode). The coding rule was first recalled by the AI model that wrote this change,
then tested against 17,279 alternatives per file with a tool built for the purpose, and confirmed by
measurements on the files. The measurements corrected the recalled rule in one respect (byte order).

Follows #448 (uncompressed 3FR, now on `main`); together they cover all 20 CC0 Hasselblad samples. Part of #420.

## Change

- `crates/raw/src/ljpeg.rs`: a lossless-JPEG scan whose SOS header gives predictor selection value 8 (which the
  JPEG standard, T.81, does not define) is decoded with Hasselblad's rule (`decode_hasselblad`):
  - the coded data are 32-bit little-endian words, each read from its most significant bit, with no byte stuffing
    (FF bytes are ordinary data);
  - each row is coded in pairs of samples: the two Huffman categories come first, then the two differences;
  - categories 1 to 15 work as in T.81; category 16 is followed by 16 bits that are ignored, and means -32768;
  - each sample is the previous sample of the same column parity in its row plus the difference, modulo 2^16;
    both start at 32768 at the beginning of every row.
- Only the layout that every measured file has is accepted: one component, 16 bits, no point transform, no
  restart markers, even width. Anything else with selection value 8, and any selection value above 8, stays an
  "unsupported" error and the file stays preview-only, as before.
- The Huffman decoder now works over any bit source (a small `Bits` trait), so the existing T.81 path is
  unchanged.
- `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 22 to 23 (these files now render from the raw data).
- `docs/parity.md`: the LR-IMP-FORMATS row lists the newly supported files.

title: LR-BEHAV-BG-TASKS: demo scenes: a rayon worker renders a scene alone, never in parallel (deadlock)
author: AlexChambers
body:
## Symptom

Requests for a demo photo's pixels can hang forever. Seen as two `tests_face_recognize` tests (`indexing_embeds_each_face_once_and_reports_progress`, `suggestions_come_from_the_named_faces_and_are_never_applied`) stuck for 30 minutes in `std::sync::Once::wait`. The same can hang the app: new libraries start with the demo photos, and the faces scan loads them on rayon worker pools.

## Cause

`demo::scene_pixels` generated each scene inside `OnceLock::get_or_init` on the caller's thread, and the render (`Scene::render_fit`) runs on rayon (`par_chunks_mut`). A rayon worker that waits for rows another worker took runs queued jobs on top of itself. In the sampled hang, a faces pool thread was inside `get_or_init` rendering the scene, waited in `join` for stolen rows, picked up the next queued faces job, and that job asked for the same scene: `get_or_init` on the same cell, on the same thread, waits for the generation further down its own stack. Every other request for that scene then waits behind it. A worker that blocks on the cell while holding rows of the generation deadlocks the same way.

## Fix

Each (scene, size) slot has one generation at a time. The first caller renders, with no lock held; later callers wait on a condvar for that generation's outcome. The rule that makes waiting safe: **a generation never needs a thread that waits for one.**

- **A rayon worker** (the faces scan, merges) renders on its own thread alone, without rayon (`Scene::render_fit_serial`, which gives the same pixels as the parallel render). It never runs other jobs mid-render, so it can't re-enter, and the work stays within its pool and that pool's limits: under the scan's light pace or `LIGHTCRAFT_FACE_THREADS=1`, a scene is rendered by that one scan thread.

  **The cost is latency for the scan.** Before, a scene's first render spread over the scan pool's threads. Scan renders (2048 px output) load the 2560 px preview source. Measured in release on an M3 Max (best of 3):

 …

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: Sony ARWs shot with DRO no longer start with the camera JPEG's lifted shadows (#244)
author: AlexChambers
body:
## Problem

In #244, Sony users report that ILCE-7M3 raws "come in with the brightness raised" compared with Photomator, Affinity and darktable. For raws without a colour matrix, LightCraft fits each photo's starting look to its embedded camera JPEG. Sony cameras apply DRO (Dynamic Range Optimizer), a local tone operator that brightens darker regions, to the JPEG only. Its factory default is DRO Auto. The tone fit therefore carried DRO's lifted shadows into the raw's starting look. Lightroom and the other raw developers develop the raw without it.

## Evidence

The data are 24 ILCE-7CR photos (Standard creative style) with Lightroom 9.5.1 default exports. Figures are mean L\* and CIE76 ΔE at 200 px, on current main (88ea1a8):

| | DRO Off (16) | DRO Lv3/Auto (8) |
|---|---|---|
| Lightroom minus camera JPEG, ΔL\* | +0.15 (-1.4 to +1.1) | -5.7 (-10.7 to -2.4) |
| LightCraft minus Lightroom, ΔL\* | -0.2 (-2.7 to +1.5) | +6.4 (+4.4 to +10.5) |
| LightCraft vs Lightroom, median ΔE | 3.6 | 7.5 |

With DRO off, Lightroom renders like the camera JPEG and LightCraft matches both. With DRO on, Lightroom ignores the JPEG's DRO and LightCraft follows it.

The per-photo tone curves fitted to all 131 of the owner's ILCE-7CR photos (71 Off, 58 Lv3, 2 Auto) show where DRO acts. At scene luminance 0.01, 0.02, 0.05 and 0.1, the median DRO-on curve is 8, 10, 9 and 6 L\* above the DRO-off one. From 0.3 up, the two agree. DRO is common: 79 of the 116 CC0 Sony files in the #535 sweep (68 of 100 bodies) were shot with DRO on, 71 of them with Auto.

## Fix

- **Reading the setting.** `lightcraft_raw::embedded_preview_dynamic_range_optimized(bytes)` reads Sony maker-note tag `0xb025`, the tag ExifTool's Sony documentation lists as `DynamicRangeOptimizer`. 0 means off. The documented on values are 1-3 (Standard, Advanced Auto, Auto), 8-12 (Advanced Lv1-5) and 16-23 (Lv1-8). Any other value counts as unknown. It follows the pattern of `embedded_preview_color_space` (the Nikon preview colour …

title: Cmd+= / Cmd+- / Cmd+0 zoom the photo, not egui's interface scale (#566)
author: bitshiftza
body:
Fixes #566.

**Problem.** On Windows and Linux, Ctrl+= / Ctrl+- (View ▸ Zoom In / Zoom Out) scaled the whole interface instead of zooming the photo, and Ctrl+0 (Zoom to Fit) reset the interface scale. egui's `Options::zoom_with_keyboard` was left at its default, so at the end of every frame egui consumed Cmd/Ctrl+Plus, +Equals, +Minus and +0 for its browser-style interface zoom. The app's `view.zoomIn` / `view.zoomOut` / `view.zoomFit` bindings fired as well, but the interface scaling is what the user saw. macOS was unaffected because the native menu bar takes those keys before egui.

**Fix.** `theme::apply` (the app's egui context setup, used by the desktop app, headless snapshots and tests) turns `zoom_with_keyboard` off. The three headless tests that used Cmd+Plus / Cmd+Minus to exercise the interface zoom's viewport handling now set the zoom factor directly, and the CLI snapshot test that did the same is dropped (the unit tests cover the mechanism); that machinery is unchanged.

**Ctrl+wheel in the Edit view.** This landed on main after the v0.4.0 tag (912f56c, LR-VIEW-ZOOM); the new test covers it so it stays fixed.

- `zoom_shortcuts_zoom_the_photo_and_leave_the_interface_scale_alone`: Cmd+=, Cmd+Plus, Cmd+- and Cmd+0 step the photo zoom (Fit → 50 % → 25 % → Fit) while `zoom_factor` stays put; failed before the fix with the interface scale going 1.0 → 1.1.
- `ctrl_wheel_over_the_photo_zooms_it_in_the_edit_view`: Ctrl+wheel over the photo with the Edit panel open zooms it; a plain wheel does not.

title: LR-EDIT-OPTICS-PROFILE: Reload from Disk reads a file's lens data and turns the correction on for untouched photos
author: radialmonster
body:
**TL;DR:** "Reload from Disk" now reads the lens data from a photo's file and, for photos you have not edited, switches the lens correction on, as import does. Before this, RW2 photos imported before the distortion correction existed stayed uncorrected. Part of #314.

## Change

Since #256 the distortion correction Panasonic and Leica record in RW2/RWL files is read and applied by default, but only while a file is being imported. A library imported earlier has no lens data stored for those photos and the correction switch off, and "Reload from Disk" did not change that.

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: decode packed 12-bit Sony ARW (DSLR-A900) from its exact 1.5 bytes per pixel strip
author: radialmonster
body:
**TL;DR:** Sony DSLR-A900 raw files are plain packed 12-bit data (two pixels per three bytes), not a compressed format. This PR decodes them instead of showing the embedded preview. Item 6 of #535. The A850 is not covered by any measurement: there is no A850 sample in the test archive.

## Change

- `crates/raw/src/vendor/arw.rs`: a Sony ARW with Compression 32767, BitsPerSample 12, one strip and an even width is read as packed 12-bit data when the strip is **exactly** width x height x 1.5 bytes. Two pixels are stored in three bytes, least-significant-bit first: `b0 | (b1 & 0xf) << 8` and `b1 >> 4 | b2 << 4`. Any other strip size still returns the existing `Unsupported("... packed compressed variant ...")`, so the A200/A230/A290/A350/A380/A390 behave as before.
- Placement and colour for this layout: CFA pattern from the file's own tag (RGGB, also measured), black 128 (the 14-bit 512 of the other bodies, on the 12-bit scale), crop = the maker note's `FullImageSize` window centred in the frame (the file has no crop tags), as-shot white balance from a plain block in the maker note (read only when that block has the exact size seen in the sample and both green levels are unity).
- `crates/engine/src/media.rs`: `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 22 -> 24. Main is at 22 and other open PRs use 23, so 24 is the next free number here; it will need adjusting at merge.

## How the rule was established

Only from values measured in the sample file and LightCraft's own code (full record in the investigation log).

- **Size.** 6080 x 4048 x 1.5 = 36 917 760 = the single strip, exactly; the strip ends at the last byte of the file; no row padding (a padded row would drift the decode, and the per-row smoothness is the same on all 4048 rows). Of the 115 Sony files with Compression 32767 in the archive, the A900 is the only one at 1.5; the others are exactly 1.000 (decode as today) or the 0.93 - 1.32 sizes of the older bodies (still refused).
- **Bit order.** Eight orders tried; for each, the me…

title: LR-IMP-CAMERA-COVERAGE: Sony ARW white balance and black level from one SR2SubIFD decryptor
author: AlexChambers
body:
Part of #535 (item 1).

**Stacked on #542** (SR2 black levels, branch `arw-black-levels`, 3100cc1, #535 items 2 and 3). Please merge #542 first. This branch adds one commit on top of it, and every "before" below is #542's head (4f350c4).

**Supersedes #542's positional keystream tables.** #542 reads the black level with a 14-byte head keystream plus four 8-byte keystreams at known value positions. This PR adds a general decryptor for the whole `SR2SubIFD`, which the white balance needs anyway, and moves the black-level read onto it, so the codebase has one SR2 decryption path instead of two. The black levels are identical to #542's on every Sony file we have (see *Equivalence with #542* below).

## Problem

A sweep of all 100 Sony bodies on raw.pixls.us (116 CC0 files) found two white-balance bugs in `crates/raw/src/vendor/arw.rs`:

- **No as-shot white balance on 14 bodies:** DSLR-A450, A500, A550, A560, A580, A700, NEX-3, NEX-5, NEX-C3, SLT-A33, A35, A55, ILCE-6001 and UMC-R10C. They decoded with unit gains, so they render green whenever the camera-look fit is rejected or the file has no usable JPEG.
- **The wrong source on most other pre-2017 bodies.** Without a plain `0x7313` in the raw IFD, the gains came from the maker note's enciphered `Tag2010` block, and those are often not the white balance the camera applied. ILCE-3500 at 5600 K was off by R −34 % / B +100 % and ILCE-7S on Shade by −8 % / +14 %. SLT-A37 and SLT-A57 were off by 20 to 53 % even in Auto.

## Approach

`WB_RGGBLevels` (`0x7313`) is the white balance the camera applied. Bodies from about 2017 on write it in plain form in the raw IFD, which the decoder already reads. Every ARW from the DSLR-A200 on also stores it inside the encrypted `SR2SubIFD`. On all 57 CC0 files that have both (31 bodies) the two are identical. The decoder now takes:

1. the raw IFD's plain `0x7313` (unchanged);
2. else `0x7313` from the decrypted `SR2SubIFD` (new);

title: LR-IMP-CAMERA-COVERAGE: Sony 16:9 crop on pre-crop-tag bodies
author: AlexChambers
body:
Part of #535 (item 4). Item 5 (DSC-R1 SR2) moved to #640, which decodes it.

## What was wrong

Sony bodies from before about 2017 have no crop tags, so the decoder takes the image size from the maker note's `FullImageSize`. A file shot in the camera's 16:9 mode broke this in two ways:

- **ILCE-7SM2:** `FullImageSize` says 4240×2384. That failed the decoder's "trim of at most 64 px" check, so the whole 4288×2848 frame was used, including 32 constant padding columns at the right edge.
- **DSLR-A580:** `FullImageSize` still says 3:2 (4912×3264); only the Exif image size says 4912×2760.

Both rendered 3:2 against a 16:9 camera JPEG. The camera-look fit's aspect check then refused to run, so they opened with the neutral fallback, dark and grey. The A580 was also green, because that body has no as-shot WB yet (#535 item 1).

## Evidence (black box)

- **Where the 16:9 crop sits.** I registered each camera JPEG on its raw: normalised cross-correlation of log luminance at 2 px steps.
  - ILCE-7SM2: the 4240×2384 JPEG field sits at y 228–232 of 2848.
  - DSLR-A580: the 4912×2760 field sits at y 258–262 of 3280.
  - That is the vertical centre of the frame: (2848 − 2384) / 2 = 232 and (3280 − 2760) / 2 = 260.
- **Which bodies are affected.** Across the 69 pre-crop-tag files on raw.pixls.us that record a `FullImageSize`, only these two have a `FullImageSize` height more than 64 px below the frame's, or an Exif size narrower than `FullImageSize` at the same width.

## Fix

`recorded_size_crop` in `crates/raw/src/vendor/arw.rs`, used by `default_crop`:

- The width comes from `FullImageSize`, anchored at the left as before, which drops the right-edge padding.
- The height comes from `FullImageSize`, or from an Exif image size of the same width when that is smaller (DSLR-A580).
- A height that is a plausible trim (within 64 px) stays top-anchored, as before. An in-camera aspect height (at least half the frame) is centred vertically at an even offset, keeping the CFA phase.
- An…

title: LR-IMP-PROFILES: XMP channel curves only with the master and all three channel curves
author: Exalted5373
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #416, which read the red / green / blue point curves of an XMP packet whenever it also had the master curve. More probes show Lightroom Classic is stricter: it reads the channel curves only when the packet has the master curve **and** all three channel curves, which is how its own packets are always written. Any partial set imports with no channel curves.

```diff
 to_partial(props)                                  # crates/engine/src/crs.rs
   if ToneCurvePV2012 present
     curve.master = ToneCurvePV2012
-    curve.red/green/blue = each ToneCurvePV2012Red/Green/Blue that is present
+    if ToneCurvePV2012Red, Green and Blue are all present
+      curve.red/green/blue = them
+    else
+      no channel curves
```

`docs/xmp-interop.md` (field table) and `docs/whats-new.md` say the same.

## Evidence

**What Lightroom does.** Lightroom Classic 15.6 imported a camera JPEG that carried each packet below as its own embedded settings. Its develop settings were then dumped, and the photo was exported and compared with the unedited export. The test curves were a steep red curve, a darkening green curve, and an identity or bent master curve.

| Packet | Channel curves after import |
|---|---|
| red only | dropped (`ToneCurveName2012` → Linear) |
| identity master + red | dropped (seen twice, in separate runs) |
| identity master + green | dropped |
| bent master + red | master kept, red dropped |
| 3-point identity master + red | master kept, red dropped |
| identity master + red + green | dropped |
| red + green + blue, no master | dropped |
| master + red + green + blue | **all read** (red changes the export by a mean of 0.217 in R, as the curve should) |

A dropped curve has no effect on the render. When Lightroom couldn't re-apply settings after import, the export of "identity master + red" came out bit-identical to the unedited export. The same is true of an Apple ProRAW DNG carrying a lone red, green or blue S-curve: all three exports are bit…

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: a partial camera look instead of the dark neutral fallback when the full look misses the gates
author: radialmonster
body: **TL;DR:** when a raw's camera look fails the acceptance gates, it no longer drops straight to the dark, grey neutral rendering. A partial look (the photo's tone curve, its chroma curve and a half-weight colour matrix) is used instead, but only when it is clearly closer to the camera JPEG on held-out pixels. On the CC0 raw.pixls.us archive, 49 of the 55 photos that reach this step get it, and every one moves closer to its camera JPEG (median CIEDE2000 14.0 -> 2.1). The 1,087 photos with a full look render byte for byte as before. Stacked on #528. Part of #515 and #535. *CC0 samples from raw.pixls.us: Panasonic ZS200D (6710), Sony ILCE-1M2 (7833), Panasonic G10 (4008).* ## Change `crates/engine/src/camera_preview.rs`, `fit_look`: when no full look passes the gates, `fit_partial` is tried before falling back: - **Tone:** the quantile tone curve from #499. It needs no pixel-exact registration and fixes the largest part of the error: the fallback is about one stop too dark. - **Colourfulness:** the existing chroma curve, kept only if it lowers the held-out error. - **Colour:** when the scene has enough colour to learn one (the full look's own condition), the photo's own colour matrix at half weight, the other half the identity. There is no hue/saturation table. - **Gates:** the partial look is used only when it cuts the held-out squared error to under 0.7 of the neutral fallback's, in linear and in gamma-encoded values. The camera JPEG's luminance must also rank the pixels like the scene's (Spearman rank correlation >= 0.5), so an unrelated preview can't pass just by matching its brightness. It is tried on all pixels, then away from edges, like the full look. The full look's gates, search and clipped-pixel handling are unchanged. There are no per-model tables. Render cache …

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: treat DNG samples piled up below the stated white level as clipped (#548)
author: radialmonster
body:
**TL;DR:** The iPhone 15 Pro Max DNG in #548 states a white level of 4095, but its sensor really clips at 3567. LightCraft did not see those samples as clipped, so white balance tinted blown highlights magenta (strongly with Highlights at -100). On decode, samples that pile up at a value clearly below the stated white level are now raised to the white level, so the existing highlight reconstruction treats them as clipped. Part of #548 (the magenta is gone; a mild cyan cast in a bright cloud at Highlights -100 is a separate, older limitation of the reconstruction).

## Change

- New `crates/raw/src/saturation.rs`: `RawImage::saturation_points()` finds, per colour, the value the samples saturate at, and `lift_clipped_samples()` raises samples at or above it to the stated white level. It runs when a DNG (or CFA TIFF) is decoded, so every path (full, binned, denoised, DNG export) sees the same data.
- A saturation point is only accepted when it is a real plateau: at least 0.01% of the colour's samples (and 100) on one value in the upper half of the range, 16 times as populated as the values just below it, with (almost) nothing above it, and clearly below the stated white level (more than 3% of the range). Files whose data reaches the white level, or that have no plateau, are untouched.
- `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 22 -> 25 (open PRs use 23 and 24; needs adjusting at merge).
- `docs/parity.md` LR-IMP-FORMATS row notes the behaviour.

## How it was established

The file states BlackLevel 528, WhiteLevel 4095 and carries a GainMap in OpcodeList3. Measuring the samples: red and blue peak at 3567 (23,290 and 42,966 samples exactly there), green has 213,686 samples at 3567 and a tail up to 3586; nothing is above 3586. 3567 is 85% of the way from black to the stated white (0.852 after normalising), so the plateau was never at the 0.99 level the highlight code treats as clipped. title: LR-CLOUD-SMARTPREVIEW: smart previews record the camera-look fit version and are rebuilt when it is older
author: radialmonster
body:
**TL;DR:** this is the follow-up @echelon raised on #499 (and landed in #546): a smart preview keeps the camera look it was built with, so previews built before a fit change kept the old look until someone rebuilt them. Each smart preview now records which version of the look fit wrote it, and an older one is rebuilt from its original when the original is available. If the original is offline, the preview is left exactly as it is.

## Change

- `LOOK_VERSION` (new, next to the fit code in `camera_preview.rs`) is the version of the camera-look fit. It must be bumped whenever a change makes the fit give a different result for the same file. The comment on the constant and `docs/camera-preview-colour.md` say so. #528 and #583 change the fitted look again and should bump it.
- Smart previews write `look_version` into their header line. A header without the field counts as version 0, so everything built before this change (including previews built after #546) is treated as older. Anything that is not a non-negative integer also counts as 0. A version newer than this build's is left alone, so two builds don't keep rebuilding each other's previews.
- Out-of-date previews are rebuilt by the code that already builds and repairs smart previews, not by a second path. It runs when a library is opened (on a background thread, no new setting, no UI) and when Build Smart Previews is used. Only existing previews are touched: none is created. After an update that bumps the version this is a one-time pass over the existing previews, paced like Build Smart Previews (one rebuild at a time through the same code); later opens find nothing stale and only read the header lines.
- A preview is only ever rebuilt from the original, never from another preview. If the original can't be read (an unplugged drive), the preview and its curve stay as they are, and the old version in the header is what marks them out of date, so the next time the original is available they are rebuilt. title: LR-EXP-DIM: exports render at twice their size, at most full size, then downsize
author: Exalted5373
body:
## Summary

Exports smaller than the photo now render at twice their size (at most the cropped full size) in 16 bits, then downsize the way Lightroom Classic does. This is the export-sizing part of #327, reworked after the review note on `export.rs:1074`. The full-size render it had before cost 2.0 GB per 2000 px export. The browser build still renders exports at their own size.

```text
export(photo, out):                                     # out < full size
-  render(out, depth)                                   # 8-bit, at the export size
+  inter = min(full, 2 × out)                           # intermediate_size; wasm: inter = out
+  deep  = render(inter, max(depth, 16-bit))            # CPU (high-bit-depth path)
+  img   = deep.downscaled(out)                         # Catmull-Rom on gamma-1.8 values
   encode(img)
```

- `crates/raster/src/resample.rs`: adds `Filter::CatmullRom` (bicubic, a = −0.5).
- `crates/pipeline/src/output.rs`: adds `DeepImage::downscaled`, which decodes to linear, encodes as gamma 1.8, resizes with Catmull-Rom, then encodes back into the output space's curve.
- `crates/pipeline/src/lib.rs`: adds `Rendered::from_deep`.
- `crates/engine/src/export.rs`: adds `intermediate_size` and `EXPORT_SUPERSAMPLE` (2.0 native, 1.0 wasm). `RenderWork` carries the target size for the downsizing.

Exports at full size or larger and non-rendered formats are unchanged. Previews are unchanged, so the render cache version stays the same.

## Evidence

### Accuracy: mean ΔE00 against Lightroom Classic 15.6's 2000 px exports (absolute, 16-bit ProPhoto)

Before = `origin/main` 88ea1a8 (accuracy runs used 3e76713; the commits in between don't touch rendering), after = this branch rebased on it. Measured with `lightcraft-cli render --size 2000 --opt colorSpace=prophoto --opt bitDepth=16`.

title: LR-EDIT-COLOR-VIBRANCE: Vibrance and Saturation fitted to Lightroom, in linear ProPhoto
author: Exalted5373
body:
## Summary

One tool pair from #327, split out as asked: Vibrance and Saturation move from hand-tuned OkLCh chroma gains to
models fitted to Lightroom Classic 15.6 renders, applied in display-linear ProPhoto (CPU and GPU). Includes the
neutral-axis fade from #327 (`e432fd6`). Nothing else from #327: the mixer, Point Color, the B&W mix and colour
grading stay exactly as on `main` and in the same order.

```diff
 ColorOps::apply(rgb)
-  OkLCh: mixer → points → c *= 1 + vib·(1 − c/0.22)²·skin(OkLCh hue)·1.2 → c *= 1 + sat + mask_sat → mask hue → B&W → grading
+  OkLCh: mixer → points                       (skipped when unused; one pass, as before, when Vibrance and Saturation are 0)
+  linear ProPhoto (Rec.2020 → ProPhoto D50):
+    vibrance(p, a): (h, s, v) = hsv(p)
+      a > 0: s *= exp(a·0.751·(1 − s)^0.736·skin(h)),  v *= 2^(a·0.15·skin(h)·fade(s))   # skin(h): Gaussian at 20° ± 35°, weight 0.391
+      a < 0: s *= exp(a·1.288·(1 − s)^0.323),          v *= 2^(a·0.608·s^0.263·fade(s))
+      fade(s) = min(s / 0.3, 1)                       # greys keep their brightness (Lightroom: ≤ 0.004 log2 at ±100)
+    saturation(p, a): y = ProPhoto luminance(p);  p = y + (p − y)·f
+      a > 0: f = 1 + a·0.927·(1 − s)^0.076;   a < 0: f = 1 + a   (−100 = that grey)
+  OkLCh: mask saturation → mask hue → B&W → grading   (skipped when unused)
```

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: read the two-field 12-bit ORF layout of old Olympus compacts
author: radialmonster
body:
**TL;DR:** Six old Olympus compacts (C-5060 Wide Zoom, C-7070 Wide Zoom, SP-510UZ, SP-550UZ, SP-565UZ, SP-570UZ) write uncompressed 12-bit data, but laid out in two interleaved fields with a gap and a hidden last row, so they opened preview-only. This PR reads that layout, only when every size and position checks out exactly. The layout was derived by black-box analysis of the six CC0 sample files; the record is the investigation log.

## Why they were refused

The files say Compression 1 (none), 12 bits, 16 rows per strip, and their strip byte counts add up to exactly width x height x 1.5. The existing 12-bit branch in `crates/raw/src/vendor/orf.rs` handles that size only with a single strip (the XZ-2 layout), and these files have 122 to 172 strips, so the branch was skipped and they fell through to `Unsupported("Olympus compressed ORF")`. They are not compressed at all.

## Change

- `crates/raw/src/vendor/orf.rs`: a new branch (after the single-strip one, so nothing that decodes today is touched) reads the layout when **all** of these hold: 12 bits, one sample per pixel, even width, odd height, strips that are whole rows (width x 1.5 bytes each) summing to exactly width x height x 1.5 bytes, exactly one gap between consecutive strips and it falls after (height + 1) / 2 rows, and one more row inside the file right after the last strip. Anything else is refused as before.
- Samples are packed most-significant-bit first, two in three bytes: `b0 << 4 | b1 >> 4` and `(b1 & 15) << 8 | b2`.
- The strips hold two fields: stored rows `0 .. h0` are output rows 0, 2, 4, ... and stored rows from `h0` on are output rows 1, 3, 5, ... with `h0 = (height + 1) / 2`. The strip table has the gap at the seam (the offsets are followed, the gap is skipped) and omits the last row of the second field, which is the `width x 1.5` bytes right after the last strip (it falls just outside the picture; it is read so the second field is complete).
- The whole strip table is used, not the strips…

title: LR-EDIT-LIGHT-HIGHLIGHTS: partly clipped highlights take the colour of bright neighbours; previews clip before averaging (#548)
author: radialmonster
body:
Binned previews and thumbnails now decide clipping per sensor sample **before** averaging. On coarse bins, that removes the green speckles and colour noise in clipped areas reported in #548. Rebased onto #607, which rewrote `highlight::reconstruct`, and reduced, as asked in review, to what #607 doesn't cover.

## Change

- **`develop_binned_masked`:** when the raw is binned for a preview or thumbnail, each colour keeps its block mean together with a mask of which colours had a clipped sample. Previously, averaging first let a few clipped samples hide in the mean, and the reconstruction couldn't see them.
- **`reconstruct_masked`:** main's `reconstruct_with` (#607) now takes the "which channels are clipped" check as a parameter. The plain path passes main's own value test, so #607's logic runs unchanged: dark-detail weighting, the demosaic ring, desaturation as more channels clip, and neutral cores. A test proves that a mask built from the values gives byte-identical output to `reconstruct_with`.
- **Fully masked blocks:** a block where every colour is masked becomes neutral at its own brightest channel, not lifted to the full clip level. Lifting it would turn a specular point into a white speckle.
- **Denoise:** the denoised version of a photo uses the same mask.

This is decoder-side: it changes the camera RGB that comes out of binning and reconstruction, before any settings apply. It also fixes broken output, so under `docs/process-versions.md` it isn't gated on a process. **Exports and 1:1 views don't bin and are byte-identical to main.**

## Measurements

CC0 Huawei DNGs from raw.pixls.us. A speckle is a bright pixel whose green exceeds red, blue and its 3 × 3 median by more than 8 levels. C* is the mean chroma in the bright areas of main's render.

| File, 500 px | Speckles, main → this PR | C*, main → this PR |
|---|---|---|
| WAS-LX1A, default | 4032 → 311 | 27.8 → 10.6 |
| WAS-LX1A, Highlights −100 | 4058 → 86 | 32.1 → 12.7 |
| PRA-LX1, default | 1299 → 5 | …

title: raw: name Nikon High Efficiency NEFs instead of blaming a missing table (#193)
author: DWAA1660
body:
Refs #193 (closed as completed, but the Oct 9 report is a real gap).

## What's going on in #193

The reporter's screenshot is LightCraft's own **Preview only** notice: *"can't decode this raw variant yet (Nikon compressed NEF without a linearization table)"*. Their export's EXIF says **Nikon Z f**. So the raw data was never decoded. They were editing the camera's embedded JPEG, with the camera's Picture Control, Active D-Lighting and white balance baked in. That's the "really weird color" they see compared with a real raw conversion.

I checked the three CC0 Z f samples on raw.pixls.us and the Z 8 ones:

| File | Size | maker note `0x0096` | strip starts with | LightCraft before |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Z f `DSC_0040` (Lossless compressed) | 31 MB | yes | Huffman data | decodes ✅ |
| Z f `DSC_0042` (HE★) | 19.6 MB | **no** | `FF10 FF50` … `CONTACT_INTOPIX_` | preview only, "without a linearization table" |
| Z f `DSC_0043` (HE) | 13.5 MB | **no** | `FF10 FF50` … `CONTACT_INTOPIX_` | preview only, "without a linearization table" |
| Z 8 HE | 24 MB | **no** | `FF10 FF50` … | preview only, same message |

These are **High Efficiency NEFs** (Nikon's TicoRAW / JPEG XS-based wavelet codec), not Huffman NEFs with a missing table. The message pointed at the wrong thing and gave the user no way forward.

I also checked that the preview fallback itself doesn't distort colour: rendering the HE samples with default settings matches their embedded JPEG within a mean of about 3/255.

## This PR

- `nef.rs`: before asking for the `0x0096` table, check whether the strip starts with the JPEG XS SOC + CAP markers (`FF10 FF50`). If it does, return `Unsupported("Nikon High Efficiency NEF (HE / HE★, … shoot RAW Lossless compressed to edit the raw data)")`. The badge shows **"Nikon High Efficiency NEF"**, and the full reason carries the workaround. The marker read uses `get()`, so a short or truncated strip stays on the old path and can't panic.

author: nledford
body:
> **Stacked on #597** (folder colour labels). The first 5 commits are #597's; review from `Engine: Synchronize Folder (folder.scanChanges, folder.synchronize)` on. Once #597 merges, this rebases cleanly onto `main`.

LRC-LIB-LIBFOLDERS: **Synchronize Folder**, as in Lightroom Classic. Right-click a folder in the sidebar's **Folders** section (or a disk other than the startup disk) ▸ **Synchronize Folder…**.

  A folder that isn't there (an unplugged disk) is reported as such, not as every photo missing.

title: LR-EDIT-LIGHT-HIGHLIGHTS: clipped highlights stay neutral when darkened (#523)
author: AlexChambers
body:
## Symptom

#523: on a Sony ILCE-7RM4 photo edited with Exposure -0.88, Contrast +5, Highlights -75, Shadows +52, Whites +6, Blacks -37, the sky next to a clipped area turns magenta in LightCraft, while Lightroom renders it white. The same thing happens with Highlights -100 on its own, or a negative Exposure or Whites: any darkening of sensor-clipped content shows a colour cast that was hidden at Neutral.

Lightroom, observed as a black box: fully clipped cores export neutral at Highlights -100 (to 3 decimals), partly clipped content keeps a plausible hue when it is strongly coloured, and a pale partly clipped sky comes out white.

Testing the first version of this branch on 1,917 ILCE-7RM4 photos (thanks @rock-meister) found it safe and fixed the magenta patch (tinted whites 97 to 65), but on a river photo the partly clipped sky between bare branches and near the frame leaned cyan to teal where Lightroom shows white. That photo was shared for local testing only, so it is described here in words and numbers.

## Cause

Clipped pixels are rebuilt at raw decode (`crates/raw/src/highlight.rs`, `reconstruct`). The tone map rolls everything above white off to white, so whatever colour the rebuilt pixels carry is invisible at Neutral and appears as soon as they are pulled below white. They carried colour for four reasons:

1. **Partly clipped pixels took the colour of whatever unclipped pixel was nearest.** The chromaticity field was diffused from every unclipped pixel, so a sky clipped in green between bare branches got the branches' colour, the purple and green lens fringes along them, and the pixels next to the clip that were demosaiced from clipped samples. Branches give pink blobs; a tree gives a green halo on one side and a magenta one on the other.
2. **Two clipped channels were left at their clip levels.** Those differ by the white-balance gains (green clips at 1, red at about 2.5), so red plus green clipped behind a warm light came out red or pink.
3. **Fully cli…

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: HEIC decodes like libheif; release builds include it
author: Exalted5373
body:
## Summary

HEIC was already decodable behind the codecs' opt-in `heif` feature (heic-rs, #853ada7), but its colours were wrong and the release builds didn't turn it on. This PR:

- **Colour like libheif.** heic-rs reconstructs iPhone HEVC tiles bit-exactly (checked tile by tile against libde265), but its YCbCr→RGB stage ignores the HEVC VUI and assumes BT.709 limited range. On real iPhone photos that put it 2–27 code values off libheif, with a +8 bias. `lightcraft-heif` now does the conversion itself:
  - signal: `colr nclx`, falling back to the grid's first tile, then the SPS VUI (new `vui.rs` parser), then the H.265 defaults. An unspecified matrix is read as BT.601.
  - chroma: nearest-neighbour upsampling, switching to centred 9/3/3/1 bilinear when a `clap` starts on an odd pixel, which is what libheif does.
  - transforms and metadata: `imir` and `clap` rounding follow libheif, and a grid takes its tiles' ICC profile (some iPhones put it there).
  - output: 16-bit RGB.
- **Codec API.** HEIF gets a header reader, so import reads the size from the container instead of running a full decode. Small decodes (`fit` ≤ the thumbnail) use the file's thumbnail item if its aspect ratio matches. The nclx/VUI primaries and transfer reach the colour pipeline through a CICP mapping now shared with PNG. 4:2:2/4:4:4 files fail with a clear `Unsupported` error. `Format::not_decodable()` is now the one place that says why a format can't be opened.
- **Builds.** Following the maintainer decision, `heif` stays opt-in upstream. The macOS, Windows, Linux and FreeBSD packaging scripts and the Nix package now build with `--features lightcraft/heif,lightcraft-cli/heif`, which makes the claim in whats-new true. A build without the feature lists each `.heic`/`.heif` as failed at import, with the reason "Heif files can't be opened: HEIC/HEIF support isn't included in this build of LightCraft". `.heif` is now an import extension.

title: LR-PREF-DISPLAY: monitor ICC profiles (display colour management)
author: kelanna
body:
Until now, LightCraft showed every preview as sRGB. On wide-gamut monitors, that makes photos look inaccurately oversaturated, and on a calibrated monitor it ignores the calibration, making LightCraft unusable for color work on wider gamut monitors (which are becoming more common with the increasing popularity of OLED). With this PR, photos can be accurately displayed through the monitor's ICC profile. 

**Settings ▸ Display ▸ Choose Profile…** picks an `.icc` / `.icm` file. The dialog opens in `~/.local/share/icc` on Linux, ColorSync's folders on macOS, or `spool\drivers\color` on Windows. **Use sRGB** turns it off. The choice is saved in `ui.json`. Agents can use the UI command `app.displayProfile {path}`.

### How it works (details in `docs/display-profiles.md`)

- **The Detail view renders into the display's own gamut.** This covers the loupe, Before, Compare / Reference, preset and profile hover, and the second window. `RenderRequest::display` (`DisplaySpace`) makes the per-pixel stage convert into the display's linear RGB, gamut map into the display's gamut, and encode with the sRGB curve. Only `FinishParams::to_out` / `out_luma` change, so the CPU and GPU paths stay in step. Colours that an sRGB render would clip keep as much saturation as the display can show. For a display that is exactly a standard space, the result equals an 8-bit render into that space (tested).
- **Then the image is converted to the display's device values** (`lightcraft_codecs::display`, using moxcms, which was already a dependency):
  - matrix/TRC profiles go through three 256-entry curve tables, or nothing at all when the profile uses the sRGB curve (e.g. Display P3);
  - LUT-based profiles go through a CMS transform. When a LUT-only profile has no colorant tags, its primaries are measured through its A2B tables.
- **Images made for sRGB are converted on the render workers** (`lightcraft_engine::display::present`): thumbnails, cached view previews, embedded camera JPEGs and the merge…

title: LR-BEHAV-RENDER-FIDELITY: Lightroom's tone chain on Apple ProRAW, as fitted analytic operators
author: Exalted5373
body:
LR-BEHAV-RENDER-FIDELITY: Lightroom's tone chain on Apple ProRAW, as fitted analytic operators

## Summary

Split from #327 (tone only). Apple ProRAW now renders its Light sliders through Lightroom Classic's own tone chain.
The chain is a set of closed-form operators, each with 5–14 fitted coefficients. **No sampled response tables:
`lr_tables.rs` is not part of this PR.** The operators are fitted to Lightroom Classic 15.6 renders of one CC0
iPhone 12 Pro ProRAW (raw.pixls.us) and of a synthetic chart that carries that file's colour tags. Each operator's
doc comment gives its form and residual. **Every other file renders exactly as on `main`**: byte-identical 16-bit
renders, other makers' DNGs with a `ProfileToneCurve` included.

```diff
 finish(pixel c):                                    # c: scene-linear Rec.2020, BaselineExposure + Exposure applied
-  y = luminance(c); d = c · tone(y) / y              # every raw: our filmic curve (or the camera curve) on luminance
+  if info.proraw:                                    # DNG, Make "Apple", with a ProfileToneCurve (SourceInfo::proraw)
+    p = to_linear_prophoto(c)                        # every stage hue-preserving: max / min channel through the map
+    p = lr_base(p, ev = BaselineExposure + Exposure) # toe + shoulder that follow the total exposure (14 coefficients)
+    p ·= 2^LrHs(lum(profile(p)), ctx)                # Highlights / Shadows; ctx = Gaussian of log luminance at
+                                                     #   6.4 % of the long edge, read through the same tone map (6 + 14)
+    p = lr_whites(p); p = lr_blacks(p)               # power-law maps of the base output; part luminance gain (12, 14)
+    p = profile_tone_curve(p)                        # the file's ProfileToneCurve per channel, 128 knots
+    p = lr_contrast(p, key)                          # Möbius S about a pivot set by the image's key: the 33rd
+    d = from_linear_prophoto(p)                      #   percentile of log luminanc…

title: LR-IMP-CAMERA-COVERAGE: CR2 black level from the masked columns only
author: Exalted5373
body:
## Summary

CR2 black level is now measured only on the columns that are really masked (no light reaches them), not on the whole border left of Canon's `SensorInfo` image area.

```diff
 cr2::decode
   active = SensorInfo borders            # unchanged: (84, 50, 5472×3648) on the 6D
-  black  = mean(columns 2 .. active.x-2)  # includes 10–36 columns that already hold image
+  cols   = masked_columns(data, active, white)
+           # from column 2, stop 2 columns before the first one whose mean rises
+           # more than max(16, (white - level)/256) above the leftmost columns' level
+  black  = mean(cols)
```

On all 8 decodable corpus CR2 bodies, light reaches 10–36 columns left of `SensorInfo`'s left border. Averaging them in pushed black too high. Per body (current estimate − true masked level):

| body | first lit column / border | black was too high by |
|---|---|---|
| EOS 6D | 71 / 84 | **+544** (2591 vs 2047, 4 % of the range) |
| EOS 40D | 30 / 40 | +141 |
| EOS 5DS R | 160 / 196 | +131 |
| EOS 5D Mark II | 158 / 168 | +73 |
| EOS 5D Mark III | 122 / 140 | +47 |
| EOS 7D | 158 / 168 | +29 |
| EOS 80D | 264 / 276 | +16 |
| EOS 550D | 142 / 152 | +9 |

The framing does not change: our 6D frame lines up with Lightroom Classic's to within 0.05 px at 2000 px. Only the shadows were wrong (dark, with crushed black blobs in coloured fruit and the tablecloth pattern).

## Evidence

- **Test:** `cr2::tests::black_from_masked_columns_only` (synthetic sensor whose light starts 6 columns before the border). Before this change, the black included the lit columns (about 3040 instead of 2048). After, the range is `2..12` and the black is 2048–2049. Cases for a fully masked border, a too-narrow border and a headers-only decode are included.
- **Against Lightroom Classic 15.6.** EOS 6D still life (CC0), 2000 px, ΔE00. Before = origin/main 88ea1a8, after = this branch. Lightroom renders are measurement only; nothing is fitted to them.

title: Remember the last crop aspect as the default
author: danielspruce
body:
Crop currently forgets the last aspect ratio on photo navigation. Remember the selected ratio in UI preferences as a crop tool setting, including Original resolved against each photo's dimensions.

Opening Crop and browsing photos leave their settings, edited status, history, and undo stack unchanged. The remembered ratio appears in the panel, but is applied only when the user starts a crop drag, inside that gesture's single undo transaction. Explicit aspect selections still apply to the active photo. Existing crops retain their own settings.

This addresses the review concern about navigation creating edits, undo entries, sidecar writes, or automatic 1:1 crops.

Validation:
- All 9 crop-focused tests passed, including read-only browsing, preference persistence, per-photo Original, a real pointer drag applying the remembered ratio, and one-step undo restoring the untouched photo.
- Visually inspected headless screenshots before and after dragging: browsing shows the remembered 1:1 tool setting with the full image; the square crop appears only after dragging.
- Formatting, workspace clippy, HEIF checks, parity references, layers, assets, and WASM passed.
- Full `cargo xtask ci` stopped at the unchanged upstream Windows-path assertion in `headless::tests::browse_a_local_folder` (backslashes versus forward slashes). The UI suite otherwise had 394 passing tests and 2 ignored. The complete workspace test run passed with only that known test excluded.

Only LR-CROP-ASPECT is included; unrelated fork and working-tree changes are excluded.

title: LR-EDIT-AUTO: Lightroom-like Auto, calibrated on Lightroom's Auto results
author: AlexChambers
body:
Addresses #318 ("won't do a proper auto correction") and the Auto half of #209 (Auto + Clarity looks much worse than Lightroom).

## Why

Auto (`develop.auto`, `crates/pipeline/src/auto.rs`) was a short percentile rule. On 24 Sony raw photos, it set Exposure about 1.4 EV higher than Lightroom's Auto on average (+1.81 against +0.44 EV) and barely used Shadows. Its results were about 18 L* brighter than Lightroom's Auto results, and further from them than the unedited render (median dE76 22.02 against 7.92).

## What

Auto now follows the shape of Lightroom's rule, with values chosen so that our *results* match its results (our sliders have their own scales, so copying its numbers is not the goal):

- **Exposure** = -0.58 - 0.41 x the scene's log-average luminance, clamped to -2..3 EV. The log average is in EV relative to middle grey, measured on a 512 px proxy, scene-linear, under the photo's white balance. It is computed before any tone curve, so the rule stays valid if the base tone changes (#514, #568, #607). The slope is Lightroom's: the Exposure its Auto chose, against our log average, gives -0.41 EV per EV (r = -0.92 over the 24 photos).
- **Highlights -66 and Shadows +52**: Lightroom's own average Auto values on these photos (our sliders aim at the same thing as its).
- **Contrast +68 and Vibrance +30**: fitted. Our scales differ and our base tone is flatter (#146), so Contrast is far above Lightroom's +6. Whites, Blacks and Saturation stay at 0.
- **Invalid pixels:** pixels that aren't finite (a damaged decode) are left out of the log average through the proxy's resampling and white balance. With no valid pixel at all, Exposure is 0.

Auto only applies when someone asks for it, so existing edits keep their look. HDR merges with Auto Settings use the same rule.

## How it was fitted and tested

**Targets.** The targets are Lightroom 9.5.1's observed behaviour, measured black-box: the values its Auto chose and its exported results on the 24 photos of the owner'…

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: decode Nikon "lossy after split" NEF
author: radialmonster
body:
Some Nikon NEFs store a "split row" in maker note `0x0096`: rows above it use the usual lossy Huffman code, and from that row on the camera switches to a different code. main refuses these files with "lossy after split" and shows only the embedded preview. This PR decodes them.

All 11 raw.pixls.us NEFs with a non-zero split now decode: Nikon 1 J5, D3400, D5, D5000, D5200, D5500, D5600 (12- and 14-bit), D7000 and Z 6_2 (12- and 14-bit).

## The rule

These were measured on the 11 files and are documented in `crates/raw/src/vendor/nefc.rs`.

- **Split row:** `split` is the u16 at byte 562 of `0x0096`. Rows `0..split` decode exactly as before.
- **Fixed rate from the split row:** from the next bit on, every pixel is one word of `bits - 4` bits (8 for 12-bit, 10 for 14-bit).
  - No byte alignment, row headers or padding, until the strip ends.
  - The remaining bits are always `rows × width × (bits − 4)` plus 0–7 one-bits of byte padding, in all 11 files.
- **Word layout:** a complete prefix code for the difference category, followed by the top bits of that category's extra bits. Large differences lose their low bits.
  - Those differences are dequantised to the centre of the kept bin.
  - The predictor is the same as above the split (same colour, two to the left), and the running value is not clamped.
- **Safety check:** the decoder checks that the fixed-rate section ends within the strip's last byte. If it doesn't, the file stays preview-only with the same reason as before, so a file that breaks the rule is never decoded wrongly.

## How it was checked

- **Same samples as the analysis decoder:** all 11 files decode to exactly the same samples as the standalone analysis decoder the rule came from.
- **No regressions:** the other 42 NEFs in the corpus decode to identical output on this branch and on main.
- **No seam:** the mean |row − row two above| is the same in the 100 rows after the split as in the 100 rows before it (ratio 0.95–1.12). There is also no drift over …

title: catalog: random photo/album/stack ids (step 1 toward multi-machine catalogs, #294)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Part of #294, groundwork for #472. This adds an id generator that can hand out random photo, album and stack ids, for catalogs shared between machines. Sequential ids stay the default, so existing libraries don't change.

Counter ids are the first thing that breaks when two machines add to copies of one catalog: both hand out the same next number. Random ids don't need coordination. This PR only adds the option; nothing turns it on yet.

Changes:
- `catalog::ids::IdGen` has two modes.
  - Sequential is the default and is exactly the old `next + 1` allocator.
  - Random draws splitmix64 ids in `[1, 2^53)`, which stay exact in JSON doubles. It re-draws ids already in use, and is seeded from std's `RandomState` plus the clock.

  No new dependency. The generator isn't serialized and doesn't affect `Catalog` equality.
- `Catalog::use_random_ids()` opts in. Its doc says it's not safe to enable yet (see the follow-up below). `use_sequential_ids()` and `seed_ids()` (for tests) are also available.
- The demo library uses sequential ids explicitly. Tests check that demo ids are 1..N and that the ids in `docs/showcase/demo.jsonl` exist in `Session::with_demo()`.
- Ties sort by file name, then id, instead of import order. That covers `Catalog::query` ties, a batch in Recently Added (with either sort direction), and frame order and cover in auto-stack. File name is the order cameras number frames, and it means the order doesn't depend on how ids were allocated. The comparison doesn't allocate (`catalog::query::cmp_name`). This is a visible change: photos with equal ratings now sort alphabetically.

Unchanged: existing ids, the catalog format (no bump), and literal-id tests on main. The diff only adds tests.

Follow-up before anything enables random ids: explicit rules for keyword and person spelling, and for which photo a duplicate import points to. Both currently follow the lowest id.

title: LR-EDIT-LIGHT-HIGHLIGHTS: keep local contrast under Highlights and Shadows
author: radialmonster
body:
Highlights no longer flattens the detail in bright areas, and Shadows no longer flattens it in dark areas. Fixes #634 (reported in #632).

## What was wrong

Both sliders shift tone in log luminance according to an edge-aware base layer (`crates/pipeline/src/local.rs`, fast guided filter). The guided filter keeps any edge stronger than about 0.6 EV, however thin. So twigs, trim and wires against a bright sky end up in the base, and get a different shift than the sky around them.
- In the bright pixels of a CC0 Nikon D5 file (raw.pixls.us 2218), the base carried **78 %** of the 9 × 9 log-luminance detail.
- At Highlights −100 the shift falls about 0.45 EV per EV of base, so it removed **40 %** of that detail. Bright skies and walls came out dull and flat instead of recovered.

## Change

The base is now the same guided filter run on a **median of log luminance**:
- **The median:** along rows, then columns, with a radius of 0.15 % of the long edge (8 px at 5568 px, capped at 24). A median removes features thinner than its radius but keeps the steps between regions exactly where they are. So thin detail takes the same shift as its surroundings, and edges stay sharp.
- **Effect on 2218:** the base now carries 8 % of the detail, and the shift removes 3 %.
- **CPU:** `median_hv` (a sliding sorted window) and `tone_base` in `crates/pipeline/src/local.rs`.
- **GPU:** `median_h` / `median_v` kernels in `crates/gpu/src/wgsl/blur.wgsl`, wired in through `render.rs` / `ctx.rs`. The median is a pure selection, so the CPU and GPU paths agree exactly. The GPU equivalence tests pass, max 1 LSB at 3000 × 2000.
- **Untouched when unused:** with Highlights and Shadows at 0, no base is computed, and renders are bit-identical to main on all 10 files below.

## Measurements

Pixels between 80 % and 98.5 % brightness (bright) or below 20 % (dark) in the unedited render. "Detail" is the standard deviation of a 9 × 9 high-pass of luminance, divided by the region's mean. Renders are 4000 px.…

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: decode the padded 12.8 bpp Olympus ORF layout (E-300, E-500, E-330; E-M5 II and PEN-F high res)
author: radialmonster
body:
Olympus E-300, E-500 and E-330 ORFs, and the high-resolution shots of the E-M5 Mark II and PEN-F, now decode correctly. Main renders the first three with fine vertical stripes and a magenta cast. Part of #233.

The layout is the padded high-res layout that @voshart established in #360, where echelon asked for it as a separate PR. voshart agreed to us sending it with attribution. This PR is that layout on its own, without #360's compressed-ORF decoder. It also adds the three older bodies.

## The layout

Single strip, 12.8 bits per pixel: StripByteCounts × 10 = pixels × 16. Each row is `width × 8 / 5` bytes of 16-byte blocks:
- **Samples:** bytes 0–14 of a block hold ten 12-bit samples as one little-endian 120-bit string. Sample *i* sits at bits [12*i*, 12*i* + 12): per 3 bytes, `s0 = b0 | (b1 & 15) << 8` and `s1 = b1 >> 4 | b2 << 4`.
- **Pad byte:** byte 15 is always zero.

Main's 12-bit branch (`crates/raw/src/vendor/orf.rs`) also caught these strips, because 12.8 bits per pixel lies between 12 and 13. It sent them to the 32-bit-word MSB path, which ignores the pad byte. The new branch runs first and only when the block identity holds exactly. The XZ-2 (exactly 12.0 bpp) and every other ORF keep their current paths.

The CFA, black level (maker note `0x2040`/`0x600`: 63 on E-300/E-500, 69–70 on E-330) and crop (`0x612`–`0x615`) are LightCraft's existing handling. They were already right for these files.

## Checks

Binned green against each file's camera JPEG; stripes measured as the column-profile FFT peak over its median:

| CC0 file (raw.pixls.us) | r vs camera JPEG | stripe peak | main today |
|---|---|---|---|
| E-300 (2878) | 0.998 | 3.7 | striped, magenta |
| E-500 (3540) | 0.996 | 6.7 | striped, magenta |
| E-330 (3624) | 0.989 | 12.3 | striped, magenta |
| E-M5 II high res (2856) | 0.992 | 7.1 | striped |
| PEN-F high res (2977) | 0.993 | 6.1 | striped |

title: LR-VIEW-ZOOM: zoom windows cover a canvas wider than 2048 px (issue #652)
author: HarrisXiu
body:
Fixes #652.

## What was wrong

Zoomed in on a canvas wider than 2048 physical px (HiDPI, 4K, a large window), the loupe was sharp in a centred band and showed blurry strips beside it. It has nothing to do with the Navigator or the photo in the report: panning only makes the strips noticeable.

`texture_side()` read the GPU's texture limit from the frame's raw input (`i.raw.max_texture_side`). A native host (egui-winit) reports that limit in the **first frame's input only** (`RawInput::take()` takes it), so from the second frame on the loupe fell back to 2048. `region::max_span` then cut every window render to 2048 × 2048 px, and whatever the canvas shows beyond that came from the magnified whole-frame render. The whole-frame render and the second-window and Compare renders were capped by the same value.

Reproduced in the desktop app (Windows 11, DX12, the ARW from the issue, 100 %): `ui.inspect` reported the window as `[3584, 2048, 2048, 2048]` on a 2607 px wide canvas, and the sharp band in the screenshot ends where that window ends.

## The fix

- `texture_side()` reads the limit egui keeps (`InputState::max_texture_side`, 2048 until the host reports one) instead of the frame's raw input.
- The headless host reported the limit in every frame, which is why no test saw this. It now reports it once, and again when it changes, as a window does, so the existing zoom tests run against the desktop behaviour.

## Tests

- `the_texture_limit_outlives_the_frame_it_was_reported_in`: the limit is still known in the frames after the one that reported it.
- `a_window_covers_a_canvas_wider_than_2048_px`: at 1:1 on a 2600 px canvas the window render covers the canvas.

Both fail without the fix (`the window 768..2816 leaves part of the canvas 723.25..3276.75 to the preview`) and pass with it.

## Checks

- Desktop app built from this branch (Windows 11, DX12, same photo and layout): the window is now `[2816, 2304, 3840, 2816]` on the 2607 px canvas and the view is sharp edge to…

title: LR-BEHAV-GPU: no render is inside the GPU driver when the app quits (issue #620)
author: HarrisXiu
body:
Addresses #620.

## What was wrong

A render still running on a worker thread while the process exits crashes inside the GPU driver (reported as a SIGSEGV in the NVIDIA Vulkan driver on Linux). Neither the panic hook nor `catch_unwind` can catch that. I checked the report against `main` and it holds:

- `JobPool` workers (`lc-job-N`) were detached, and `Drop` only signalled them.
- The compute devices are statics that are never dropped, and the only in-render counter was thread-local.
- `on_exit` saved settings and the library and returned; the macOS menu-bar Quit then called `process::exit(0)`.

One case the report doesn't list: quitting in the first ~0.4 s leaves the `lc-gpu-init` thread creating the device.

## The fix

- **`crates/gpu`** (`exit.rs`): every entry into a device counts as work in flight, on any thread: `render`, device creation, pool trim, the denoise runner and each denoise tile. `begin_shutdown()` lets nothing new in; `wait_idle(timeout)` waits for what is inside.
- **`crates/preview`**: `JobPool` keeps its workers. `shutdown(timeout)` and `Drop` discard queued jobs and wait for running ones, bounded (2 s on drop). They never wait for the calling thread, and a drop after a shutdown doesn't wait again.
- **`crates/engine`**: a render job caught by the shutdown returns an error instead of rendering on the CPU, so quitting doesn't wait for it.
- **App**: `on_exit` ends with `LightcraftApp::shutdown` (2 s for everything), after settings and library are saved. The macOS menu-bar Quit goes through `on_exit`, so it is covered.

## Not in this PR

The export, merge, denoise and import threads are still detached (direction 2 of the issue). Their GPU work goes through the gate; their CPU work is cut off at exit as before. PR #601 reworks those tasks, so I left them alone to avoid conflicts.

## Tests

- Pool: drop waits for a running job and discards queued ones; drop is bounded when a job never ends; shutdown reports live workers; a panicked job and a poo…

title: Synchronize Folder tests: expected paths spelled as the OS does (Windows)
author: HarrisXiu
body:
One test-only fix. (This PR first also changed `export_progress_and_cancel`; that commit is reverted here, see below.)

## Synchronize Folder tests: expected paths with mixed separators

Seven tests in `crates/engine/src/tests_sync.rs` fail on every Windows run:

```
  left: ["C:\...\lc-sync-new-30076\trip\c.png", ...]
 right: ["C:\...\lc-sync-new-30076\trip/c.png", ...]
```

The helper `Scratch::path("trip/c.png")` joined the whole relative path onto the scratch folder, so the expected value kept the `/`, while a scan reports paths as the OS spells them. The helper now joins the parts one by one. The paths the scan reports are unchanged. Same kind of problem as #538, in tests that landed after it.

## What was taken out: the MCP export-cancel race (#674)

The second commit enlarged the cancelled export in `export_progress_and_cancel` to 24 photos at long edge 2000. It is reverted by the third commit, so `crates/mcp` is identical to `main` in this PR. The larger batch only gave the cancellation more time and stayed timing-dependent; @ingolfteetz has a deterministic fix (hold the export at a photo boundary) that is better, and #668 touches the same lines. This PR no longer conflicts with either.

title: HDR: PNG export as 16-bit Rec. 2020 PQ (cICP, cLLI)
author: JordyUSA
body:
Follow-up to #646 (requested in #466): **HDR PNG export.** With HDR output on, a photo edited in HDR now exports as a **16-bit PNG with the PQ curve in Rec. 2020**, like the HDR AVIF.

- `codecs::encode_png_pq` sits next to `encode_avif_pq` and takes the same input (linear Rec. 2020, SDR white = 1.0), with SDR white at `HDR_REFERENCE_WHITE_NITS`.
- The colour is described by a **`cICP`** chunk (PNG third edition: BT.2020 primaries, PQ, RGB, full range). A **`cLLI`** chunk carries MaxCLL / MaxFALL, computed the same way as the AVIF's `clli`.
- EXIF, XMP and print resolution are kept. No ICC profile is written next to `cICP`, which readers prefer.
- Export: `hdr_output()` and `effective_space()` include PNG (Rec. 2020), and the render is `F32Hdr`. The dialog shows the HDR checkbox for PNG with a "Rec. 2020 PQ, 16-bit (HDR PNG)" note. The MCP tool descriptions and the parity rows are updated.
- Photos without an HDR edit, and HDR edits with HDR output off, export exactly as before (8/16-bit sRGB or the chosen space).

**Checked on a real HDR display:** Linux, KDE Plasma Wayland, Vivaldi/Chromium. The exported PNG's highlights show as HDR.

**Testing:**
- `roundtrip::pq_png_*`: decodes the file and checks the cICP values, 16-bit RGB, PQ samples decoding back to their luminance, cLLI, XMP / pHYs kept and no iCCP; plus short buffers and hostile samples.
- `tests_export::hdr_png_export_is_16_bit_pq_rec2020`: an SDR edit stays a plain 8-bit PNG; an HDR edit gets cICP, 16-bit and a MaxCLL above SDR white; HDR output off gives the SDR rendition.

title: UI: star rating previews the hovered rating, Info tab and bottom bar (#647)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #647.

The star row had no hover feedback: `widgets::stars()` worked out which star was under the pointer and then discarded it (`let _ = hover_n;`).

Now `stars()` allocates the five star rects first, notes the hovered one, then paints. While the pointer is over a star, stars 1..=hovered are drawn filled, previewing the rating a click would set, and the hovered star gets the same hover square `icon_button` draws (`t.hover` at 0.7), so hovering the current rating, where the preview looks unchanged, still shows feedback. With no hover the drawing is unchanged. Click behaviour is unchanged too (clicking the current rating still clears it). Both the Info tab (`panels/right.rs`) and the bottom toolbar (`panels/bottombar.rs`) use this helper, so both get the preview.

I also removed a leftover `painter().text(..)` call that drew an empty string.

The fill decision is a small pure function, `star_lit()`, with a unit test covering: no hover shows the rating, hover 4 over rating 2 lights 4, hover 1 over rating 5 lights 1, hover over rating 0.

title: Headless sessions honour LIGHTCRAFT_SAM3_DIR for the SAM 3 model folder (#619)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #619.

Headless sessions (`lightcraft-cli`, the headless MCP server) never set `session.segmenter.dir`. Only the desktop app set it, from `LIGHTCRAFT_SAM3_DIR` or `<settings folder>/models/sam3`. So in a SAM-enabled build, `segment.model.status` reported `dir: null` and a Describe mask failed with "no folder is set for the SAM 3 model", even with the override set.

The SAM 3 folder now has a shared default in `crates/engine/src/config.rs`, next to the face and denoise model ones: `default_sam3_dir()` (`LIGHTCRAFT_SAM3_DIR` if set and not empty, else `<config>/models/sam3`) and `Session::with_default_sam3_model()`, which also sets the mirrors file `<config>/models/sam3-mirrors.txt`. `Headless::default` and `Headless::demo` use it, as they already use `with_default_face_models`. The desktop app uses the same helper in place of its own copy, so a model installed from the app is found by the CLI and the MCP server too (as `docs/ai-masks.md` "By hand" and the `config.rs` module doc describe). The only behaviour change on desktop: an empty `LIGHTCRAFT_SAM3_DIR` now falls back to the default folder, like `LIGHTCRAFT_FACE_MODELS`.

Tests:
- `config::tests::sam3_dir_prefers_the_override`: a set override wins; unset or empty falls back to `<config>/models/sam3`.
- `headless::tests::headless_sessions_get_the_sam3_model_folder`: `Headless::default` and `Headless::demo` get that folder, and `segment.model.status` reports the configured `dir`.

title: LRC-LIB-CATALOG-IMPORT: find moved root folders relative to the catalog
author: mrpdaemon
body:
## Problem

Importing a Lightroom Classic catalog copied from another computer (here: saved on Windows, imported on Linux) left every original missing, because the importer only used each root folder's `absolutePath` (`C:/Users/…/Project/RAW/`), which doesn't exist on the new machine.

## Fix

Lightroom also records `AgLibraryRootFolder.relativePathFromCatalog` (e.g. `../RAW/`) for root folders on the catalog's volume; it's how Lightroom itself finds originals after a project folder moves. When a root's `absolutePath` isn't a folder here, the reader now resolves `relativePathFromCatalog` against the catalog's folder (lexically normalised) and uses it if that is a folder. Each remapped root is reported as a warning in the inspect/import report:

```
root folder RAW: C:/Users/…/2026-09-22-Mission-Creek/RAW/ not found; using /home/…/2026-09-22-Mission-Creek/RAW (relative to the catalog)
```

Roots still not found fall back to the existing missing-file placeholders and Find Missing Photos.

## Testing

- New unit test `a_root_missing_here_is_found_relative_to_the_catalog` (synthetic catalog: relative root used when present; recorded path kept, no warning, when it leads nowhere). The native SQLite fixture builder is factored out so both tests share it.
- Real catalog from Windows imported on Linux: 17 photos, 17 imported, 0 missing (previously 17 missing).
- `cargo xtask ci` green.

Docs: `docs/lightroom-catalog-import.md` and the `LRC-LIB-CATALOG-IMPORT` row in `docs/parity.md`.

title: MCP: cancel the e2e export at its first progress notification
author: mrpdaemon
body:
## Problem

`crates/mcp/tests/e2e.rs::export_progress_and_cancel` failed every run on a 32-core Linux machine (also on unchanged `main`):

```
assertion `left == right` failed: cancelled request must not reply: {"id":4, … all 8 files …}
```

The test waited for a progress notification with `progress > 0` before sending `notifications/cancelled`. With many cores the batch renders four photos side by side (`export_parallelism`), and progress notifications are throttled to one per 100 ms, so the first notification past 0 was often the final 8-of-8 one, sent just before the reply. The cancel always arrived too late.

## Fix

Test only: cancel at the first notification (`progress == 0`). Progress is reported before each photo is placed, so photo 0 is still written and the test's "only completed photos remain, at least one" assertions hold, while the rest of the batch is now margin for the cancel to arrive.

## Testing

- 20/20 passes of `cargo test -p lightcraft-mcp --test e2e export_progress_and_cancel` (previously 0/3).
- `cargo xtask ci` green.

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: decode table-less Nikon 34713 NEFs stored as packed 12/14-bit data
author: radialmonster
body:
Covers packed NEF/NRW layouts, including the Z 6II geometry reported in #769.

Some NEFs labelled compression 34713 contain packed samples rather than a compressed stream, with no linearization table. This extends the existing Nikon reader to select the layout from bit depth, dimensions and complete strip length: LSB-packed rows, 16-byte padded rows, D100 groups and big-endian 16-bit NRW words. High Efficiency codestream detection and the current compressed decoder stay in the same routing chain.

Rebased onto main’s `Mode`/`MASK_ROWS` implementation. Header probes decode only the needed prefix; header/full geometry agrees. Width/bit/stride arithmetic is checked and strips outside the file are rejected. Render-cache version is 65.

Raw tests, all-target raw Clippy and raw wasm checks pass. Together with stacked #673, a fresh comparison covers 86 CC0 Nikon raws and controls: 22 newly decode (all 20 known packed-layout files and two small-RAW files from #673), and the other 64 retain identical decoded sensor samples. Synthetic regressions cover layout geometry, overflow, truncated strips and bounded header probes.

The packed reader validates the complete declared strip range before both Header and Full behavior. A strip clipped at EOF is corrupt even when all metadata is intact. A metadata-first tail-truncation regression fails with the guard disabled; valid decoded samples remain unchanged.

Validation limitation: `cargo xtask ci` passes formatting, then stops at the unchanged `tests_export.rs` Clippy `drop_non_drop` error reproduced on main. The full workspace baseline also has Windows export-path and folder-drop test failures. Only 62 of the 447 pinned corpus files are available here; unavailable cases are skipped.

Credit: @radialmonster.

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: decode two-field Coolpix NEFs (E5400, E5700 CYGM, E8400, E8800)
author: radialmonster
body:
Some legacy Coolpix NEFs store two complete interlaced fields one after another. This extends the existing Nikon reader to interleave that layout and convert the CYGM filter tag through the existing bounded four-plane conversion. The measured E5700, E8400 and E8800 files retain the corrected sensor output.

Scene statistics alone can also misidentify an ordinary horizon. Rearrangement is now restricted to the measured legacy maker-note version 0.2.0.0, uncompressed 12-bit samples and a single tight strip, then independently confirmed against the file's own camera JPEG. The version scopes the test; it does not declare field storage. A fixed 64 x 48 spatial grid compares original and proposed log-luminance structure. Every quadrant must correlate at least 0.8 and improve by at least 0.2. No registration search or colour fitting is used.

How the rule was established: all 271 archive NEFs were inspected; only the three measured field-stored originals use that binary maker-note version. Their proposed geometry has camera-preview quadrant correlations above 0.86, substantially above the original ordering. An independently packed ordinary mild horizon using the same maker-note dialect is corrupted by the published detector, with or without a matching JPEG; this update preserves every sample. Strong-horizon and ordinary raw controls are also unchanged.

The check has fixed input and JPEG dimension/sample budgets, with a header preflight before pixel allocation. Missing, invalid or oversized previews, non-normal orientation, aspect mismatch and ambiguous spatial structure leave stored rows in place. This deliberately conservative behavior can leave a two-field file unrearranged when its preview cannot establish the geometry. Header probes remain bounded and retain the same crop geometry as Full decoding. CYGM colour remains approximate: gray-world balance and bilinear interpolation are unchanged.

Raw tests, all-target raw Clippy and raw wasm checks pass. Fresh source-ident…

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: decode Nikon small raw (sRAW) NEFs as 4:2:2 luma/chroma
author: radialmonster
body:
Nikon D810/D4S small RAW uses packed 12-bit Y0/Y1/Cb/Cr pairs, rather than a CFA mosaic. This extends the Nikon reader’s existing compression routing to recognize the exact strip size and decode the pairs into linear RGB.

Rebased on the refreshed #671 branch. Header probes retain full RGB geometry without allocating or decoding the image, size arithmetic is checked, and truncated strips are rejected. Render-cache version is 66, one beyond its #671 parent.

Raw tests, all-target raw Clippy and raw wasm checks pass. Both camera-original small-RAW files in a fresh 86-file Nikon/control comparison now decode. The other newly decoded files belong to #671; all 64 files supported on main retain identical sensor samples. Synthetic tests cover chroma interpolation, neutral output, depth/size refusal, header geometry and malformed dimensions.

The measured chroma gains are approximate and differ between the two bodies. This does not claim calibrated colour. Merge #671 first.

The small-RAW reader independently validates its complete declared strip range before Header or Full behavior. Missing tail rows cannot turn zero-filled chroma into manufactured pixels. Its metadata-first regression and the inherited packed-strip regression fail with their guards disabled; valid decoded samples remain unchanged.

Validation limitation: `cargo xtask ci` passes formatting, then stops at the unchanged `tests_export.rs` Clippy `drop_non_drop` error reproduced on main. The full workspace baseline also has Windows export-path and folder-drop test failures. Only 62 of the 447 pinned corpus files are available here; unavailable cases are skipped.

Credit: @radialmonster.

title: HDR: HDR histogram for HDR edits (fixed 5-stop scale, Lightroom layout)
author: JordyUSA
body:
Follow-up to #646 (item 2 of the list in #466): **an HDR histogram for HDR edits.**

With #646, an HDR edit's preview shows its SDR rendition, so the histogram only showed the SDR range and nothing about the highlights above SDR white. Now, for HDR edits:

- `pipeline::hdr_histogram` renders the edit small (384 px long edge, `OutputDepth::F32Hdr`, same framing, no overlay/proof/window). It bins the result with **SDR on the left half** and the **HDR range on the right** (`Histogram::of_hdr` / `HdrBins`).
- The HDR side is a **fixed scale of `Hdr::MAX_EV_LIMIT` (5) stops** above SDR white, so it doesn't rescale when the headroom slider moves. The headroom shows as an orange line, with the range past it dimmed.
- Used where renders finish: the engine's `develop()` (CPU and GPU previews) and the web worker. High-bit-depth, windowed and proofed requests keep the image's own histogram, and a display profile's histogram doesn't replace it. The web workers carry the HDR bins across their wire (`Histogram::to_words` / `from_words`, which also reads the old layout).
- SDR edits are unchanged.

**Panel (Lightroom's layout):**
- a solid line at SDR white and dashed lines between the stops;
- a bar under the plot: white, and one band per stop in `visualize::HDR_BANDS` colours **only while Visualize HDR range is on**, so it works as the overlay's legend;
- "SDR" / "HDR" labels, and an info tooltip using our own icon.

**Cost:** HDR edits do one extra small CPU render per preview.

**Testing:**
- `tests_hdr::hdr_histogram_shows_the_range_above_sdr_white_on_a_fixed_scale`: none for SDR edits or deep/window/proof requests; a fixed 5-stop scale; content above white; a lower headroom pulls the highlights down without changing the scale.

title: Issue #99: lock tests: keep the child-process test from overlapping the others
author: AlexChambers
body:
`tests_lock::second_opener_is_refused_until_the_first_lets_go` (crates/catalog) fails now and then on macOS with `InUse(None)` at the last `acquire`. It failed a `cargo xtask ci` run of mine on a branch that doesn't touch the catalog crate.

**Cause.** `lock_held_by_another_process_is_released_when_it_dies` spawns a child process. A new process starts with a copy of the parent's open files, which its exec then closes (the lock file is close-on-exec). If the other test drops its lock in that moment, the child's copy still holds the `flock`, and acquiring it again is refused. The owner note was already removed, hence `InUse(None)`.

Measured with the built test binaries on an M3 Max. It shows up when the machine is busy: while a build ran, `tests_lock` failed 4 of 80 runs, and 0 of 80 with `--skip lock_held_by_another`. With four loops of 100 runs in parallel: 6 of 400 failed before the fix, 0 of 400 after. On an idle machine it didn't fail in 200 runs either way.

**Fix.** The three tests that hold a lock in the test process take one mutex (`SERIAL`), so none of them overlaps the spawn. Test-only; the library lock itself is unchanged. Nothing else in the crate spawns processes.


`cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, heif, parity, layers, assets and wasm pass. The workspace tests pass except `export_progress_and_cancel` in `crates/mcp/tests/e2e.rs`, the race in #674 (2 of 3 runs fail here, with or without this change, which touches only the catalog's unit tests).
