title: DNG bad-pixel opcodes: cap the pixels they repair
author: haranishi
body:
`FixBadPixelsConstant` lists every pixel equal to its constant, and `FixBadPixelsList` expands its rectangles, into `bad: Vec<(usize, usize)>`; `fix_pixels` then copies them into a `HashSet`. The constant arm had no cap at all, and the list arm's cap (`bad.len() > 1 << 22`) was checked only after a whole rectangle had been pushed. So a DNG whose mosaic is uniform and equal to the constant, or a single `FixBadPixelsList` rectangle over the image, lists all w × h pixels: 16 bytes each plus the set, tens of GB at the decoder's size limit (`MAX_SAMPLES`). The allocation failure aborts the process when the photo is opened or thumbnailed.

## What changes

- `crates/raw/src/opcodes.rs`: `MAX_BAD_PIXELS = 1 << 22`, the number the list arm already used. The constant arm takes at most that many pixels. The list arm stops adding pixels at the cap, inside a rectangle and for the explicit points too. Pixels past the cap, in list order, are left as they are. Lists under the cap behave exactly as before; the only other difference is that the old check let the list overshoot the cap by up to one rectangle. Two limits: pixels past the cap count as good neighbours when the listed ones are repaired, and the cap applies per opcode, so it bounds memory, not the total time of a list that holds many opcodes.

## Tests

`bad_pixels_constant_is_capped` and `bad_pixels_list_is_capped_inside_a_rectangle` use a 2048 × 2054 mosaic with a good first row and a good last row and bad rows between them, four rows more than the cap. Row 1, within the cap, must still be repaired; the second-last row, past the cap, must stay as it is. Before the fix both fail (that row was rewritten from the last row); after it both pass. Each test holds about 220 MB for about a second, because the fixed code still builds a list and a set of the full capped size.

`cargo test -p lightcraft-raw --lib` (231 pass, 3 ignored), `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-raw --all-targets -- -D warnings` p…

title: XMP merge: keep refusing repeated attributes, in linear time
author: haranishi
body:
`xmp.rs` and `gpx.rs` iterate attributes with `.with_checks(false)` because quick-xml 0.38 compares every new attribute name with all earlier ones on the element, which is quadratic in the attribute count (RUSTSEC-2026-0194, fixed in 0.41). `scan` in `xmp_merge.rs` kept the check on, and it runs on the existing sidecar and on the packet being merged. Its 200,000-element cap does not bound the attributes of one element: a single `rdf:Description` with 200,000 attributes took 22-41 s to scan on my machine.

`scan` is strict on purpose (a sidecar that is not well-formed is backed up and replaced), so unlike the lenient readers it must keep refusing a repeated attribute. That is why this is not just `with_checks(false)`.

## What changes

- `crates/meta/src/xmp_merge.rs`: `.attributes().with_checks(false)` plus a `HashSet` of the names seen so far on the element. A repeated name is still an `XmpError::Xml("repeated attribute …")`. Same behaviour, linear time.

## Tests

- `many_attributes_scan_in_linear_time`: one description with 200,000 attributes; every attribute is read and `scan` returns within 5 s. Before the fix it fails (22-41 s); after it, `scan` takes about 30 ms.
- `refuses_a_repeated_attribute`: a repeated owned attribute (`xmp:Rating`), a foreign one (`foo:Thing`) and one on a nested element (`stEvt:action`) make `merge_xmp` return an error. It passes before and after the change; a plain `with_checks(false)` fails it.

`cargo test -p lightcraft-meta` (58 unit tests and 4 integration tests pass), `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-meta --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass. I did not run the whole `cargo xtask ci`.

title: LR-IMP-CAMERA-COVERAGE: Sony DSC-R1 reads its SR2SubIFD (black, white balance, crop): seed derived from the key
author: radialmonster
body:
Follow-up to #575 and #640, as agreed on #580. The Sony DSC-R1 stores its `SR2SubIFD` under a key other than `11 22 33 44`, so main skipped the block and lost the R1's black level, white balance and crop. This PR derives the keystream seed from the key and reads those three values.

**Provenance (proof route):** the key→seed derivation in `seed_from_key` is a recalled scheme, generic memory with no code copied, written in our own Rust. It is accepted on two independent checks:
- **Reproduces #575's measured seed:** for key `11 22 33 44` it gives `SEED` word for word. That keystream was measured by known-plaintext from 126 CC0 files, so a match by chance has probability about 2⁻⁴⁰⁶⁴.
- **Decodes the R1's block:** for the DSC-R1's key `63 be 01 3e`, the 11932-byte block becomes a well-formed 101-entry directory.

The module docs carry the same disclosure. The existing recurrence and the key `11 22 33 44` path are unchanged.

**Changes**
- `sr2.rs`:
  - `seed_from_key` and `seed_for`: `SEED` for the known key, the derived seed for any other.
  - `SubIfd::read` decrypts blocks under any key.
- `arw.rs`:
  - black level from `0x7300` when `0x7310` is absent;
  - white balance from `0x7303` (G R B G), the last fallback;
  - crop from `0x74c3`, used only when there is no default crop, and only with an even origin and a window inside the frame.
- `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 44 (adjust at merge).

title: LR-PREF-PERFORMANCE: cover every GPU kernel build with the crash marker, catch internal compile errors (#250)
author: radialmonster
body:
Related to #250. #250's crash report (0.2.1, which had no marker yet) shows Apple's Intel Metal compiler aborting on a **compute kernel**: `reportUnsupportedMaxWorkGroupSizeMetadataError` from `processKernelFunction`. That points at LightCraft's own kernels, not the window's shaders. naga writes `max_total_threads_per_threadgroup` for each compute entry point, and most of our kernels use 256 threads. Since 0.4.0, device and kernel creation run inside the init marker (`gpu-init.marker`). If the process dies in the driver, the next launch starts on the CPU. This PR makes sure that also holds for the kernels built later, and for compile failures that come back as errors instead of a crash. **Capping workgroup sizes on Intel Metal would be the real fix, and that needs a Mac to verify.**

What this fixes, found while checking that path:
- **Denoise kernels:** the AI denoise network's kernels (`nn.rs`, `build_pipelines`, compiled on the first denoise) ran outside the marker. A Metal compiler crash there would repeat on every launch. They now run under it.
- **Shared marker:** `with_marker(what, f)` counts overlapping scopes, so the window-side warm-up and a first denoise share one marker file and neither clears it early. A drop guard removes the file on a panic, since the process survived.
- **Internal errors:** the kernel build in `Gpu::new` only popped a Validation error scope. An Internal compile error now also returns `Err` with the reason, so rendering falls back to the CPU cleanly.
- **Logging:** a failed GPU init is now logged (`gpu: rendering on the CPU: <why>`).

Docs: the crash-sentinel paragraph in `docs/gpu-pipeline.md` and the `LR-PREF-PERFORMANCE` row.

**Tests:** two new marker tests that need no GPU (overlapping scopes share one marker; a panic still removes it), plus the existing marker test, adjusted.

**Checks:** `fmt` and clippy `-D warnings` pass. `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` shows only the known Windows failures (7 `tests_sync`, `export_pr…

title: In-window menus: a scrolled menu draws no scrollbar over its shortcut text (#691)
author: bitshiftza
body:
Fixes #691.

**Problem.** A menu taller than the room under the menu bar scrolls inside it (`menu_level.rs`, issue #189). Its rows live in an egui vertical `ScrollArea`, whose floating scrollbar is drawn *over* the rows' right edge, exactly where the shortcut text ends. At 1.0× it's a 2-point handle that grazes the last glyph; at 1.75× the bar is in its wide hovered state with a semi-opaque background and hides the last character of every shortcut (`Shift+C` → `Shift+`, `D` / `N` / `F` gone), which reads as clipping. Menus that fit never show the bar, so they were fine.

Confirmed by instrumenting the level: the scroll content, its clip and the rows are all exactly the level's width in both modes, and the frame border is in the same place; the only extra thing in scroll mode is the bar at the last two points. Screenshots in #691.

**Fix.** The scroll area hides its scrollbar (`ScrollBarVisibility::AlwaysHidden`). The ▲ / ▼ strips, the wheel and dragging were already the designed ways to scroll a menu, like native menus on a small display, so nothing is lost. Platform-neutral: it's the in-window menu bar (Linux, Windows, web, macOS with the native bar off); the native macOS menu bar doesn't go through this code.

**Menus that fit** are untouched: no bar was ever shown there, and the test checks that a View menu that fits has the same width as one that scrolls.

**Test.** `tests_menubar::a_scrolled_menu_draws_no_scrollbar_over_its_shortcuts`: opens the View menu in a 700 pt and a 1400 pt window with the pointer resting on it, and asserts no tall narrow rectangle is painted along the level's right edge (nothing else in a menu has that shape: hover highlights span the level, separators are one point tall, ▸ and text aren't rectangles), plus equal widths. Fails on main with the bar's track `[512, 59]–[514, 660]` and handle. Adds `HeadlessView::painted_shapes` for it.

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: decode Kodak DCS520C raw TIFF (two-component lossless JPEG with response curve)
author: radialmonster
body:
Today the Kodak DCS520C's raw TIFF fails to import: "OtherTiff files are not decoded yet … without an embedded preview". This PR decodes it.

**Format** (black-box analysis of the CC0 sample, clean route: analyst gate "vague" with no recall used, and evidence only from the file, TIFF 6.0 and ITU T.81):
- **Raw data:** the CFA IFD holds one strip with a lossless-JPEG (SOF3) stream. It has 2 components, is 12-bit, and is 868 × 1160 per component. Component 0 holds the even columns and component 1 the odd columns of the 1736 × 1160 frame, so `ljpeg::decode`'s interleaved output is already the mosaic. The stream ends exactly at the strip end.
- **Response curve:** the stored values are companded, and tag `0x123` (GrayResponseCurve, 4096 entries) expands them to linear 12-bit, with stored 622 mapping to 4095. KodakIFD tag 2316 is the exact inverse table.
- **CFA:** GRBG, from `CFAPattern`.
- **Black level:** measured per CFA position from the darkest 0.01 %, because the frame has no masked border: 220 G, 223 R, 197 B.
- **White balance:** from KodakIFD `0x848`, chosen over four other neutral-looking triples by matching the thumbnail's neutral pixels: G/R 0.96 vs 0.94 measured, G/B 1.99 vs 1.96.

**Detection** is narrow, and all of these must hold:
- Kodak make, a CFA IFD with compression 7 and a single strip;
- a 2-component SOF3 stream whose width × 2 equals `ImageWidth` and whose height equals `ImageLength`;
- a 4096-entry curve.

The code is in a new `crates/raw/src/vendor/kodak.rs`, plus `RawFormat::KodakDcs`. `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` is 47 (adjust at merge).

![DCS520C: main (import error), this PR, IFD0 thumbnail](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/55e58082-3ed5-433e-90de-388e2c12760f)

- **Component agreement:** the two JPEG components' greens agree within 1 %.

title: Read Lightroom spot removal (crs:RetouchAreas, RetouchInfo) from sidecars and presets
author: aayusharora
body:
## Read Lightroom spot removal (`crs:RetouchAreas`, `crs:RetouchInfo`) from sidecars and presets

Heal and clone spots stored by Lightroom Classic now become LightCraft spots when a sidecar, DNG-embedded XMP, XMP preset or `.lrtemplate` is read, next to the local corrections that already map. Until now the packet's `RetouchAreas` was reported as unmapped and the spots were lost.

**What is read** (`crates/engine/src/crs_masks.rs`, `spots`; wired in `crs::to_partial_report`):

- `RetouchAreas` items: `SpotType` (`heal` / `clone`), the first mask component as the target (`Mask/Ellipse` with `X/Y/SizeX`, `Mask/CircularGradient` with `Top/Left/Bottom/Right`, or a brushed `Mask/Paint` whose dabs become the path), `SourceX` / `OffsetY` as the source's **absolute** position (converted to our offset; only with `SourceState="sourceSetExplicitly"` or no state, otherwise the source stays automatic), `Opacity` and `Feather` (0..1 → 0..100).
- The legacy `RetouchInfo` list (`centerX = …, centerY = …, radius = …, sourceState = …, sourceX = …, sourceY = …, spotType = …`), read on its own when a packet carries no `RetouchAreas`.
- Horizontal sizes are fractions of the width in the packet and of the long edge in LightCraft; converted with the target's aspect like radial masks are.
- A spot with any other mask kind is reported as `Spot: <kind>`, never guessed.

**How the format was established:** by observing what a sidecar written for a healed photo contains (the public XMP data model has field names but no documentation of the spot structure). The verified form is a `Mask/Ellipse` component with Poisson method and absolute source coordinates; the `Mask/CircularGradient` form that other tools' schemas allow is accepted too.

**Tests** (in the existing `crs_masks` test module): a packet with a healed circle with an explicit source, a cloned circle with an automatic source, a brushed removal, a circular-gradient spot and a spot with an unsupported mask; portrait-target size scaling; t…

title: spot.findBlemishes: heal small blemishes on detected faces (classical, no new model)
author: aayusharora
body:
## `spot.findBlemishes`: heal small blemishes on detected faces (classical, no new model)

A sibling of `spot.findDust` for portraits. With the YuNet detector installed (the existing opt-in download), the command finds small, round spots on each face's skin that are darker or redder than the skin around them and adds a heal spot on each, one undo step, so a retoucher can review and delete pins exactly as with dust.

**How it works** (`crates/pipeline/src/blemish.rs`, `crates/engine/src/cmd/masks.rs`):

- The detector's box and five landmarks define the skin: an ellipse over the face, gated by skin colour, with the eye band, brows, nostrils and mouth cut out around the landmarks, so lashes, nostril edges and lip corners never count.
- A blurred copy gives the surrounding skin; a candidate must stand out from it in luminance or redness beyond a sensitivity threshold **and** beyond 2.5× the local texture, then grow into a small, roundish blob (same blob logic as the dust finder).

title: Catalog lock: release the library lock explicitly on drop, not by closing the handle (#680)
author: bitshiftza
body:
Fixes #680.

**Problem.** `tests_lock::second_opener_is_refused_until_the_first_lets_go` fails intermittently with `InUse(None)` ("already open in another LightCraft program") right after `drop(first)`. The cause is in the product code: a dropped `LibraryLock` could leave the library locked for a moment.

**Mechanism** (as the issue worked out). `LibraryLock` released the lock by closing its `File`. On Unix an `flock` lock belongs to the open file description and lasts while *any* descriptor on it is open. When another thread spawns a process, `posix_spawn` copies the fd table into the child and `O_CLOEXEC` only closes the copies at `execve`, so the lock outlived the drop until the child exec'd. In the test binary, `lock_held_by_another_process_is_released_when_it_dies` spawns the test binary on a parallel thread at exactly that moment.

**Fix.** `Drop` removes the owner note while still holding the lock (so it can't delete the next holder's), then calls `File::unlock()`: `LOCK_UN` through our descriptor frees the lock whatever copies a child still holds. An unlock error is logged, never a panic; the handle still closes afterwards, so the old behaviour is the fallback. `File::unlock` is stable since Rust 1.89 (the workspace is on 1.99).

**Tests** (`cfg(unix)`, both fail every run without the fix):
- `the_library_is_free_once_dropped_even_if_a_child_holds_a_copy`: holds a `try_clone` of the lock's descriptor across the drop (the same open file description a child gets between fork and exec), then re-acquires. Deterministic.
- `dropping_the_lock_frees_the_library_while_another_thread_spawns_processes`: one thread spawns `/bin/true` in a loop against ~2 s of acquire/drop cycles on its own directory; no acquire may be refused. Without the fix, 70 % of cycles were refused on this machine (the issue measured 2 % on a slower lock cycle).

The flaky pair went from 3/100 to 0/100 failures here (no strace on this machine, so the deterministic recipe wasn't run); the catalog …

title: LRC-LIB-CATALOG-LOCK: release the library lock explicitly on drop (#680)
author: valenfys
body:
Fixes #680.

## Problem
`LibraryLock` released the library by closing its `catalog.lock` file. On Unix that's an `flock` lock, which lasts while **any** descriptor for that open file is still open. A process that another thread is spawning holds a copy of every descriptor until it reaches `execve`, where close-on-exec closes it. If a `LibraryLock` was dropped inside that window, reopening the library failed with `InUse(None)` ("already open in another LightCraft program"), even though nothing had it open. That's the flake in `tests_lock::second_opener_is_refused_until_the_first_lets_go`, which runs next to the test that spawns a lock-holder child.

## Fix
`Drop` removes the owner note, still under the lock, then calls `File::unlock()`. That frees the lock whatever copies a child still holds, and it's `UnlockFile` on Windows. If unlocking fails it logs a warning instead of panicking. `_file` is now `file`.

## Tests
- New `the_library_is_free_once_dropped_even_if_a_child_holds_a_copy` (Unix): it holds a `try_clone()` of the lock's descriptor, which is what a child holds between fork and exec, drops the lock and reacquires it. **Fails with `InUse(None)` without the unlock**, passes with it.
- Catalog test binary: 20/20 full runs green on macOS.
- `cargo xtask ci` green: fmt, clippy, heif, test, parity, layers, assets, wasm.

Note: on macOS the flaky pair from the issue doesn't fail even without the fix, so the regression test is what shows the bug on this machine. The issue's numbers for Linux are 0 failures after the fix.

## Docs
`docs/parity.md` → `LRC-LIB-CATALOG-LOCK`: the lock is released explicitly on close (issue #680). Its status stays ✅. The parity summary table was already out of date on `main`, so it's left for its own `cargo xtask parity --write` commit.

title: docs: point to the two Olympus patents as a clean-room base for compressed ORF
author: feffef
body:
Docs only. No code, no assets.

Compressed Olympus / OM System ORF is documented as preview-only in `docs/gaps.md` (gap 6) and `docs/raw-parity.md`. This adds a short section there pointing to two Olympus patents (inventor Takashi Ishikawa) that describe the compression *method* in prose, as a possible base for a clean-room implementation:

- [US7333035B2](https://patents.google.com/patent/US7333035): lossless RAW compression with median-edge-detector prediction from the left, upper and upper-left neighbours, a separately coded sign, and Golomb-Rice codes whose parameter `k` comes from flatness run counters.
- [US7715639B2](https://patents.google.com/patent/US7715639B2/en): a sibling with predictor variants, `k` from neighbouring positions, raw low-order bits and a correction filter.

Neither names ORF and neither gives the file layout, constants or stream header; those still have to come from CC0 sample files. This is a pointer for contributors, not legal advice, and I haven't verified the patents' legal status.

We are aware of the ongoing discussion and don't want to cut across it:

title: Hold Shift while dragging a crop handle to keep proportions
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Holding Shift while dragging a crop handle now keeps the crop frame's current proportions for that drag, like Lightroom and Photoshop. Letting go of Shift goes back to free cropping, and the Lock toggle is never touched.

`crop.drag` takes a new optional `keepRatio` boolean (default false). When true, the drag is constrained to the frame's current aspect even if the aspect lock is off. With the lock on, nothing changes. The command's params doc is updated, so the control protocol and MCP see it too. The crop panel sends `keepRatio` from the Shift state on every drag update.

On a corner handle the opposite corner stays put and the frame keeps its shape. On an edge handle it reuses what `drag_crop` already does when locked: the frame grows or shrinks about its midline on the other axis, so the opposite edge stays fixed. In both cases the drag still stops at the image edge.

Alt-drag from the centre, the optional part of the issue, is not included.

Two engine tests cover it. One mirrors the locked-ratio test on every handle but with the lock off and `keepRatio: true`, and also checks the lock stays off. The other checks that without `keepRatio` (or with it false) and the lock off, the ratio changes freely. `cargo xtask ci` passes. I did not try the Shift drag by hand in the app.

docs/parity.md notes the new modifier on the aspect row.

Closes #614

title: Linux/FreeBSD: file dialogs are children of the app window (Wayland portal parent)
author: jazzautomations
body:
## Problem

On Linux/Wayland, every rfd file dialog (Import Photos…, Open Library, Export, presets, keyword lists, …) opens as an **unparented top-level** window. xdg-desktop-portal-gtk logs:

```
xdg-desktop-portal-gtk[1943]: Unhandled parent window type
xdg-desktop-portal-gtk[1943]: Failed to associate portal window with parent window
```

A tiling compositor (sway here) then tiles the picker *beside* LightCraft, and with LightCraft fullscreen the picker is hidden behind it: the menu item looks like a hang (nothing appears, the control channel blocks until the invisible dialog is closed). This is the Wayland sibling of #191.

## Fix

`services` builds one `rfd::FileDialog` template with the main window as parent (`set_parent(cc)`, `CreationContext` implements `HasWindowHandle + HasDisplayHandle`) and every picker starts from it (`file_dialog()`). rfd exports the Wayland surface through `xdg_foreign` itself and `FileDialog` is `Clone + Send`, so the template also serves the picker that runs on its own thread (#191). No `unsafe`, no `unwrap`.

Only Linux and FreeBSD set the parent: on macOS a parented dialog becomes a sheet and on Windows a modal, a behaviour change this PR deliberately does not make.

## Verified

Build from this branch (fmt, `clippy -p lightcraft --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test -p lightcraft` green on ubuntu-22.04), run on Omarchy/sway with LightCraft fullscreen, `file.addPhotos` over the control channel, no compositor window rules:

| | portal log | sway tree |
|---|---|---|
| before (0.5.0) | `Failed to associate portal window with parent window` | `xdg-desktop-portal-gtk` **tiled**, hidden under the fullscreen app |
| after | nothing | `xdg-desktop-portal-gtk` **floating, visible**, centred over the app |

Changelog entry under *Reliability* in `docs/whats-new.md`.

Related, not fixed here: #718 (control channel stalls while the window is not visible).

title: Importing a deleted photo's file again brings it back from Recently Deleted (#706)
author: bitshiftza
body:
Fixes #706 (and the same knot in #298).

**Problem.** Import a photo, delete it from the library, import the same file again: the import skipped it as a duplicate, "already in the library", while the grid showed it in Recently Deleted. The review dialog's "In Recently Deleted" choice defaulted to *Leave them*, so the file stayed unchecked ("Import 0 Photos"), and files dropped on the window were skipped the same way. The reporter's contradiction exactly, reproduced headlessly in the same session, after closing and reopening the library, and with the photo in an album.

**Cause.** `photo.delete` only marks the photo deleted (Recently Deleted). `OnDeleted`, the import's rule for such a match, defaulted to `Skip` in the engine and the review dialog mirrored that default.

**Fix.** The default is now `restore`: importing the file brings the photo back with its edits, rating and albums, as one undo step. Someone importing the file wants the photo in the library; restoring loses nothing (Reset Edits gives a clean start), whereas importing afresh would silently drop the edits. A trashed photo matched by content whose recorded file is gone is relinked to the imported file. The review dialog checks such files ("Will be restored"), counts them as "in Recently Deleted" rather than "already in the library", and starts on *Restore them*; dropped files restore too and say "Restored 1 photo from Recently Deleted". `skip` and `fresh` remain available (`library.import` → `onDeleted`, MCP schema updated).

title: NEF: probe compressed files from their first 128 rows, not the whole Huffman stream (#708)
author: bitshiftza
body:
## Problem
`lightcraft_raw::probe_info` is the header-only read every import does (`probe_bytes` in `crates/engine/src/files.rs`). On a compressed NEF it took as long as a full decode (386 ms on a 24 MP D750 file, 65–92 ms on the 16–24 MP corpus files here), while every other format probes in under 1 ms. Importing 1,000 such NEFs spent minutes just probing. Fixes #708.

## Cause
`vendor::nef::decode` had no header `mode`: the masked-trailing-column test (M3.7, for uncompressed NEFs) needs samples, and once compressed NEFs decoded too, the probe ran the whole Huffman stream through `nefc::decode` just to feed that test.

## Fix
Option 3 (skip the test for compression 34713) is not possible: the D5100 (lossless) and D7000 (lossy) corpus NEFs do have 8 masked trailing columns (sample value 0) in their compressed files, and their maker notes carry no `0x0045 CropArea` or any other tag that says so; the raw IFD claims the full 4992 width. So the probe cannot know the active width from the header alone.

Option 1 instead, in a form that keeps `probe_info == RawImage::info` exactly: both modes judge the active width from the **first 128 rows** (`nef::MASK_ROWS`) against the nominal white level. The header probe decodes only those rows (`nefc::decode_rows`: the stream is sequential; uncompressed files unpack only the strips holding them) and the full decode applies the same rule to the same rows. On every corpus NEF/NRW the result equals the whole-frame result for any N from 8 to 512 rows: masked columns decode to exactly 0 (compressed) or ~19 (uncompressed) while live columns sit at or above the black level (~150 at 12 bit, ~600 at 14 bit), so the margin is large. The whole-image size and truncation checks still run in both modes; the "lossy after split" end-of-strip rule can only be checked when the whole strip is decoded (a body-corruption check, like other formats' probes).

title: Web: a failed render worker start no longer shifts the other workers' slots (#229)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #229.

`Workers::start` gave each worker's `onmessage`/`onerror` callback the loop index `i`, but a failed attempt (`Worker::new_with_options` throwing, or the init `post_message` failing) did `continue` without pushing into `workers`. After one failure every later callback pointed one slot too far: worker 1's replies landed on worker 0's entry, and the last survivor's replies hit `workers.get_mut(i) == None` and were dropped. That is the "3 alive, 2 ready, 0 remote jobs done" state in the report, with jobs stuck in flight.

Changes (`apps/lightcraft-web/src/workers.rs`, `wire.rs`):
- The index a callback captures is now the position the worker will take in `workers`. A small `WorkerSlots` counter in `wire.rs` (next to `CacheWatch`, so it is testable off wasm) hands it out, and it only moves on when the worker is actually pushed.
- Both failure variants from the report are covered: a constructor failure takes no slot, and a worker whose init `post_message` fails has its handlers cleared and is terminated, so it can never answer to the index the next worker takes.
- The worker's name and the warning keep the attempt number, so logs still say which attempt failed.

Test: `wire::tests::a_failed_worker_attempt_leaves_no_gap_in_the_slots`. A failed first attempt followed by three good ones gives slots 0, 1, 2. The old loop index gave 1, 2, 3. The worker code itself only builds for wasm32, so the browser path is not run by `cargo test`.

title: Denoise: a running job's picture is Ready only when the job reports, not when its file appears (#719)
author: bitshiftza
body:
Fixes #719.

**Problem.** `tests_denoise::a_photo_waits_for_its_turn…` fails about 1 run in 6 of the full engine lib binary on a loaded machine with `assertion failed: !x.s.denoise_busy()`, right after the photo reached `PhotoState::Ready`.

**Cause** (a product inconsistency, not an over-eager test). The denoise worker saves the picture, then tears down its rayon pool, drops its guards and unwinds through `catch_unwind` before it writes its outcome. A `denoise.pump` in that window finds the file on disk (`denoise_check_photo` for a selected photo, or a reindex) and marks the photo Ready, yet `running` is still set: Ready and busy at once, and the AI Denoise activity row stays up for a photo that says it is done. Load widens the window, hence the flake.

**Fix.** The running photo is its job's to report: `denoise_check_photo` and `denoise_reindex` skip `running.photo`, so `denoise_poll` makes it Ready in the same pump that clears `running`. Export is unaffected (`denoise_for_export` waits for the product itself through the slot).

**Test.** `a_picture_that_appears_while_its_job_runs_is_ready_only_when_the_job_reports` blocks the worker in the model loader, writes the picture in its place, and shows the photo stays Running (ready 0, busy) through a pump and a forced reindex until the worker reports, then is Ready and idle in the same pump. It fails without the fix.

The natural flake did not reproduce here in 8 runs; a temporary 300 ms sleep between the save and the outcome made the flaky test fail 3/3 alone, and 3/3 pass with the fix. Sleep removed: 7/7 full engine lib runs green. `cargo xtask ci`: all 8 steps pass.

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: refine partial looks with measured colour
author: QuirkyTurtle94
body:
An accepted partial camera look can contain an identity colour matrix, so it bypasses the measured spectral fallback even when the scene could not constrain colour. On my A7R IVA lion frame this leaves muted colour despite a useful tone fit. This change lets that narrow case try the camera's existing measured calibration, with freshly fitted tone and chroma.

Related to #535 and #515; this does not close either umbrella issue. Research and wildlife comparisons: https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/535#issuecomment-6097245073

### Behaviour

- Full JPEG fits, profile fits and partial fits with a learned matrix retain their exact result.
- Only an accepted identity-matrix partial with no hue/saturation table consults the existing spectral table. No camera data or private profile is added.
- Express the measured transform in the existing proxy's working space, preserving as-shot balance and baseline exposure. Refit tone/chroma rather than inserting a new matrix beneath the old tone.
- Require the normal full-fit gates, lower held-out gamma-encoded squared error and no increase in linear squared error. Keep the existing partial on failure; clipped samples remain excluded.
- Bump `LOOK_VERSION` 2→3 and `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 42→43. Per `docs/process-versions.md`, camera-colour source changes do not introduce a develop process version.

### Evidence and limits

64 private ILCE-7RM4A RAWs, reset edits, CPU, empty local-profile directory, 1600px exports: all 63 full-fit renders are byte-identical to baseline; only the known partial-fit lion frame changes. Baseline is upstream `b70ae174` plus #695's optical aspect guard (`9682caae`); all private files here are native 3:2. The change is based directly on upstream `b70ae174`.

title: M11.4: reject illuminated Canon CR2 border samples when estimating black levels
author: stiffo01
body:
Canon EOS 760D CR2 photos can render with crushed shadows and severe blue artifacts. In two tested files, illuminated border columns bias the arithmetic mean black-level estimate upward, clipping real shadow signal before camera-look fitting.

This change uses medians per CFA site for Canon Bayer CR2 masked-border samples. It preserves CFA-site anchoring, leaves other vendors’ estimators unchanged, and invalidates cached renders. The correction restores shadow detail in both tested files. Other Canon CR2 models may be affected, but have not been verified.

A synthetic regression covers distinct site pedestals, an odd sensor origin, and minority bright-border contamination. No photographs or model-specific offsets are included in the code commit. A sanitized CR2 sample is attached separately.
[lightcraft-canon-760d-samples.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33281937/lightcraft-canon-760d-samples.zip)


Validation: release desktop and CLI builds succeed; both private CR2 examples and a full-resolution export were checked. Formatting, workspace Clippy, HEIF, parity, layering, and asset checks pass. Native workspace tests: 1,963 passed, 0 failed, 25 ignored.

Full cargo xtask ci reaches the WebAssembly stage but cannot complete because this machine lacks the wasm32-unknown-unknown standard library. Browser validation remains pending.

title: LR-EDIT-OPTICS-PROFILE: apply embedded Fujifilm RAF distortion and vignetting tables
author: radialmonster
body:
Fujifilm RAFs store per-shot lens corrections in the raw IFD: GeometricDistortionParams (`0xf00b`), VignettingParams (`0xf010`) and ChromaticAberrationParams (`0xf00f`). 129 of the 143 CC0 Fujifilm files on raw.pixls.us have them (65 bodies). This PR applies the distortion and vignetting tables, using the same warp and vignette path as the Sony ARW and Panasonic RW2 corrections.

**How the tables were read.** Tag names are public. The layout was measured by comparing the cameras' own JPEGs with LightCraft's uncorrected renders. No other converter's code or docs were used, and the gate rating was "vague". Details are in `docs/fuji-lens-corrections.md`.
- **Layout:** distortion and vignetting are `[scale, n knots, n values]`. `scale × n` is the half diagonal of the recorded image, and the last knot is the farthest corner. Older bodies use 11 linear knots, newer ones 9 knots at √(k/8), and the GFX 50 bodies 8.
- **Distortion:** in percent, looked up at the source radius, with the zoom that fills the frame.
- **Vignetting:** percent of the axial illumination, applied as a gain of 100/V.

**Distortion, 67 body/lens/focal combinations** (correlation of high-passed luminance with the camera JPEG, median):

| warp | median |
|---|---:|
| no correction (main) | 0.941 |
| table, wrong sign | 0.493 |
| table, looked up at output radius | 0.989 |
| **table at source radius + frame-filling zoom (this PR)** | **0.991** |
| free 3-term radial fit (upper bound) | 0.994 |

- **Shape error:** through the shipped code, the radial shape error against the camera JPEG falls from a median of 0.72 % to 0.05 % of the half diagonal (max 2.60 % → 0.42 %). 54 of 57 corrected combinations end within 0.25 %, about 2 px at 1440 px.
- **Vignetting:** on 38 corrected combinations, the radial residual falls from a median of 0.184 to 0.031 log units. The JPEG's radial gain tracks −ln(V/100) at a median correlation of 0.987.

title: Linux: default to XWayland for file drag-and-drop on Wayland desktops
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Rationale & History

Under Wayland sessions, dragging and dropping photos and RAW files from desktop file managers onto LightCraft showed a "no" (prohibited) cursor and drops did not arrive.

This occurs because `eframe 0.36.2` depends on `winit 0.30.13`. In `winit 0.30`, Wayland drag-and-drop was not implemented ([winit#1881](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/issues/1881)). Native Wayland drag-and-drop was added for `winit 0.31` in [winit#4571](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4571) (merged July 2026, tagged in `0.31.0-beta.3`). However, updating to `winit 0.31` directly is blocked by breaking event loop API changes until upstream `eframe` adds support.

On X11 / XWayland, drag-and-drop is fully supported in `winit 0.30`. This pull request adopts the established pattern from `designcraft` and `deckcraft` by Brandon Thomas:
1. Adds `winit = { version = "0.30", default-features = false, features = ["x11"] }` under `cfg(all(unix, not(target_os = "macos")))`.
2. Adds an event loop builder hook before running the native event loop: when an X server is reachable (`DISPLAY` is set) and `LIGHTCRAFT_WAYLAND` is not set, configures `EventLoopBuilderExtX11::with_x11()` to route through XWayland so file drops work out of the box on standard Wayland desktop sessions.
3. Allows users desiring pure native Wayland to opt out and preserve the native Wayland backend by setting `LIGHTCRAFT_WAYLAND=1`.

### Verification
Verified local compilation and dependency resolution with `cargo check -p lightcraft` on Linux (0 errors, 0 warnings).

title: Crop tool: no dark wedges inside the crop box when the crop is rotated (#731)
author: bitshiftza
body:
Fixes #731.

**Problem.** In the crop tool, rotating the crop (Straighten) showed dark wedges inside the crop box and doubly-dark wedges outside it, growing with the angle, as in the reporter's screenshot. The exported image was fine: the artefact was only in the overlay.

**Cause.** The dimming outside the box was drawn as four quads, each joining one side of the photo to the matching side of the box (`crop_overlay` in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/detail.rs`). That equals photo-minus-box only while the two rectangles are aligned. Rotated, the quads become bow-ties that cross the box interior and each other, so their triangles dim wedges inside the box and overlap outside it. At larger angles the mesh also spilled past the photo.

**Fix.** `outside_crop_mesh`: the photo rectangle minus the box as one mesh of four disjoint half-strips (outside edge *i*, inside edge *i*+1, each clipped to the photo with Sutherland–Hodgman), fanned into triangles. A flat or non-finite box dims nothing; no indexing on input-derived values.

**Before / after** at −45° (the reporter's case) and +15°, headless, main b70ae174 vs this branch:

![crop overlay before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bitshiftza/lightcraft/issue-assets/crop-731-before-after.png)

**Tests.**
- `the_dimming_outside_a_rotated_crop_is_exactly_the_photo_minus_the_box`: three box sizes (inside, poking out, larger than the photo) × eight angles; every grid point of the photo outside the box lies in exactly one triangle, none inside the box or outside the photo.
- `a_degenerate_crop_box_dims_nothing`: point, line and NaN boxes, NaN photo rect.
- `tests_crop_rotate::rotating_the_crop_dims_nothing_inside_the_box`: headless pixel test at −45°; inside the box the frame matches the 0° frame and the photo's corner is dimmed. Fails on the old mesh.

**Docs.** `docs/parity.md` LR-CROP-STRAIGHTEN note. `cargo xtask ci`: all 8 steps pass.

title: LR-VIEW-COMPARE: a filmstrip click shows the photo in Compare
author: PiMinusMax
body:
Closes #744

### Change

In Compare, a filmstrip click used to make the clicked photo active without showing it, so edits and rating keys went to a photo on neither side. Now the click puts the photo into the active side (the candidate after entering Compare, the select after clicking the select's photo); a photo already on the other side swaps the two. The active photo is therefore always one of the two shown. Other views keep the usual selection clicks.

This implements the "active side" option from the issue. If you'd rather have a click always replace the candidate, that's a one-line change in `set_photo` (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/compare.rs`, the `None` arm of `to_select`).

### Commands / parameters

- New UI command `compare.set {id, side?: "select" | "candidate"}` (enabled in Compare): puts `id` into that side, or the active side when `side` is omitted; an unknown side is an error.

### Tests

New `crates/ui-egui/src/tests_compare.rs`:
- `filmstrip_click_in_compare_keeps_the_active_photo_on_screen`: at Fit and 100 %, a filmstrip click must leave the active photo on screen and a rating key must not change a hidden photo. Fails without this change (the hidden photo goes from 2 to 3 stars).
- `filmstrip_click_replaces_the_active_side_in_compare`: replace the candidate, swap with the select, `compare.set` with an explicit side, then replace the select; an unknown side is rejected.
- `cargo xtask ci` green on 9e65220f.

### Tracker

`docs/parity.md` → LR-VIEW-COMPARE: `cmd:compare.set`, filmstrip click replaces the active side.

title: LR-BEHAV-LOCALIZE: craft-fonts faces of other scripts are UI fallbacks (#736)
author: radialmonster
body:
Fixes the LightCraft side of #736 (Thai folder and file names show as boxes).

The UI only fell back on craft-fonts' **CJK** faces (`fonts::cjk_fallback`). A Thai face, which craft-fonts #15 adds, would never be used, and neither is the Arabic face craft-fonts already ships. So Thai text kept drawing boxes even in builds that carry the font.

- **Where it's used:** `theme.rs` builds the Proportional, SemiBold and Monospace families from it.

title: Crop angle set through develop.set / MCP / --set now keeps the crop inside the photo, as Straighten does (#742)
author: bitshiftza
body:
Fixes #742.

**Problem.** Setting the crop angle through the generic develop control (`develop.set`, `develop.adjust`, `develop.quickAdjust`, `develop.resetControl` on `crop.angle`) rotated the crop without fitting it, so the box took in canvas outside the photo. **Cause.** `crop.angle` is a plain develop control, so the generic path wrote the angle and nothing re-fitted the crop. `crop.set` also fitted by slightly different rules from `crop.straighten`.

The fit happens inside the same edit, so a slider drag fits on every step and stays one undo step. title: Kelvin white balance for raws whose camera has colour matrices, with a look-preserving migration (#730)
author: bitshiftza
body:
# LR-EDIT-COLOR-TEMP: Kelvin white balance for raws whose camera has colour matrices (#730)

Fixes #730.

## Problem

The white-balance scale was chosen by file extension: every ARW / NEF / RW2 / RAF / CR2 / CR3 / PEF / SRW / ORF sat on the relative −100…+100 scale (6500 K / 0 = as shot), and the render path chose the same before the spectral lookup. So the 52 bodies whose matrices `lightcraft_raw::spectral` has measured (ILCE-7M3, ILCE-7M4, ILCE-7RM3, D850, EOS 5D Mark III…) never got a Kelvin readout, unlike Lightroom.

## Design

- **One decision, two sides.** `lightcraft_raw::spectral::find_camera("Make Model")` looks the catalog's camera string up in the spectral table (every split into make/model, then the whole string as a model; tested to equal `find(Some(make), model)` for every row, alias and realistic Exif make). `lightcraft_catalog::relative_wb_camera(format, camera)` is the catalog's answer (`Photo::relative_wb`), `files::WbScaleOf` the decoder's (format + own matrices + Exif make/model); a corpus test asserts they agree, and `Photo::fitted_look()` keeps the old "takes the JPEG fit" predicate for smart previews.
- **The matrices only convert.** As Shot = the file's multipliers read through the model's `ColorMatrix1/2` (`spectral::as_shot_white_through`, the DNG `AsShotNeutral` reading). The colour look stays whatever it was (JPEG fit / profile / spectral fallback), and the Temp slider adapts from that as-shot white with Bradford, as every fitted look does. The camera-space `rebalance` stays reserved for files with matrices of their own (DNG); it is *not* used for spectral cameras, which is what makes the migration exact.
- **Writers**: every command that writes a white balance (`develop.set`, `develop.adjust`, `develop.quickAdjust`, `develop.wb`, `develop.wbPick`, `develop.reset`) first brings the photo's settings onto its scale (`local::normalize_wb`).

title: raw: find the saturation plateau despite stray samples above it (CR2 white level)
author: TicT4x
body:
## Problem

On a Canon EOS 70D CR2 (14-bit, ISO 100, harsh sunlight) Lightcraft renders the image noticeably darker and more contrasty than other raw converters, and the blown-out highlights get a cream cast instead of going neutral.

The cause is `white_from_data` (`crates/raw/src/vendor/mod.rs`), which CR2, NEF, ORF, RAF, RW2, SRW (and ARW without a `WhiteLevel` tag) use to estimate the white level:

| | value |
|---|---|
| Black level (masked columns) | 2048 |
| Actual saturation plateau | 13583 (≈9 % of green, ≈3–4 % of red/blue samples) |
| Samples above the plateau | 83 of 20.6 M, up to 14426 |
| White level before this PR | **16383** (fallback to the full 14-bit range) |
| White level with this PR | **13530** |

The function anchored the plateau search on the absolute maximum (14426, a single stray sample). The band just below it is empty, so the plateau test failed and it fell back to `2^bits − 1`. As a result:

1. everything is scaled by ≈ 0.8 (≈ 0.3 EV too dark), and
2. saturated pixels sit at ≈ 0.8 instead of ≥ 1.0, so `highlight::clip_neutral` / `reconstruct` never treat them as clipped.

## Fix

The function now builds a histogram of the (subsampled) in-range samples and takes the top of the data after skipping up to `min_plateau / 2` stray samples. That is half the number of samples the existing test already requires for a plateau, so a real plateau can never be skipped. The plateau test itself (band width, `top ≥ min_plateau`, `top ≥ 4·under + 4`, `mx > full/2`) is unchanged. The strays still count towards the top band, since they are saturated as well.

Files without strays are unaffected. I checked this with a port of the old and new logic against the existing `white_plateau` cases and the 70D file:

| input | old | new |
|---|---|---|
| ramp, no plateau | 16383 | 16383 |
| ramp + plateau at 15000 | 14942 | 14942 |
| empty, 12-bit | 4095 | 4095 |
| plateau at 13583 + 4 strays (new test) | 16383 | 13530 |
| IMG_9171.CR2 (EOS 70D) | 16383 | 13530 |

author: radialmonster

title: LR-IMP-PREVIEW-READ: a preview reads the raw's header, not the raw (56.5 MB → 5.9 MB, 10 s → 1 s over SMB)
author: lzjtugjc
body:
## What this does

A grid thumbnail and a loupe preview of an unedited raw show the **camera's embedded JPEG**, which sits
near the *start* of the file. For a 24 MP Fuji RAF that is **5.6 MB of a 56 MB file** (measured on
`DSCF9492.RAF`: JPEG at offset 148, length 5 857 109). The preview loader called `std::fs::read` on the
whole file and threw the sensor data away, so every preview paid for ~50 MB nobody looked at.

On a local disk that is merely wasteful. On a network share — where photographers keep libraries — it is
the wait. Same file, same build, only the path changed (GVFS/SMB over Wi-Fi):

| | read | preview |
|---|---|---|
| before | 59 277 632 B (100 %) | ~10 s |
| after | **5 857 257 B (9.9 %)** | **0.96 s** |

## How

- `lightcraft_raw::bounded_preview(bytes)` — locates the preview from the header alone and reports its
  byte range. For RAF the pointer is two big-endian `u32`s at fixed offsets **84/88**, the same fields the
  RAF reader uses.
- `lightcraft_raw::embedded_preview_from_range(window, range)` — extracts it, returning **byte for byte
  what `embedded_preview` returns for the whole file**.
- `engine::files::preview_window` — reads a 4 KiB prefix, then re-reads *exactly the extent the header
  declares*. That second step is not optional: the container reader clamps a slice to the buffer it was
  given, so a 4 KiB prefix reports a self-consistent but truncated **3 948 bytes** where the file holds
  5.6 MB. The window is then taken out of the prefix rather than read a second time (a naive version read
  11.7 MB — double).
- `fs_preview_loader` tries that quick path first and keeps the whole-file path as the fallback.

Nothing regresses and nothing is lost when the header cannot answer: CR3 (boxes), TIFF-family raws whose
pointer tag sits past the prefix, and CRW/MRW/X3F (found by scanning) return `None` and read the file as
before. A **lying pointer**, a **short read** or a file that changes underneath us ends in the same
fallback — a damaged head…

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: median Canon camera tone for CR3s without an embedded JPEG (HDR-PQ shots)
author: radialmonster
body:
Canon HDR-PQ CR3s can contain only a 4:2:2 HEVC preview, which the current preview decoder refuses. With no camera JPEG to fit, the existing spectral-matrix fallback uses the generic default tone and renders these files too dark.

This extends the central `starting_colour` fallback: a CR3 without its own matrices, a stored embedded JPEG or an accepted look receives the median Canon tone/chroma curve measured from 50 separate camera-original RF-mount files. The same tone selection feeds source loading and DNG colour tags. Existing JPEG-fitted looks and file matrices keep priority. This is an average starting look; it is not fitted to the inaccessible PQ preview.

Rebased onto main’s current starting-colour and white-balance model. `LOOK_VERSION` is 10 and render-cache version is 65.

Fresh validation:

- All 30 files render at 1440 px. The 24 non-PQ controls are pixel-identical to main.
- The six HDR-PQ files take the fallback: mean L* moves from 16.96–20.28 to 23.65–28.56. Before/after images were inspected. They have no decodable camera preview, so these brightness measurements do not establish colour accuracy.
- Both fallback regressions pass, including the shared start/DNG-tag path. Full engine tests: 1112 passed, with the same Windows export-path failure reproduced on main and six ignored tests.
- Parity, layers, assets and wasm checks pass. Full CI passes formatting and stops at main’s existing `tests_export.rs` Clippy `drop_non_drop` error.

No private photos are included.

title: LR-IMP-CAMERA-COVERAGE: Nikon D4 image area and white level, measured against its camera JPEG
author: Unemars
body:
Fixes two defects of Nikon D4 NEFs: purple stripes down both sides of every frame, and clipped highlights that turn magenta instead of white.

The D4 records no CropArea (`0x0045`), so the whole 4984 × 3292 active area was developed. Since #531 the D4 gets its camera look from the embedded JPEG, and its colour and tone are close to the camera's. The frame edges and the clip level were still wrong.

## Cause

- **Stripes.** The 4992 × 3292 sensor data holds 2 columns of optical black left of the image and 42 right of it, then 8 empty columns. The camera has already subtracted the black from the image pixels: the darkest ones reach 0. The optical-black pixels are stored without it (~700–900). `trailing_masked_columns` only drops columns below 1 % of white, so it trims the 8 empty columns and keeps the optical black. That optical black develops as purple.
- **Magenta highlights.** Green saturates at 15546–15672, while red and blue continue to 15687–16383 (digital gain). `white_from_data` finds the plateau near the data's top (~16300). Clipped green then stays at ~0.95 and never reaches white, so blown skies and windows turn pink/lavender.

## Changes

- `crates/raw/src/vendor/nef.rs`: `MEASURED_BODIES`, for bodies that record no CropArea, keyed by model, sensor data size and bit depth. Each entry holds the image area and the clip level measured on that body's files. The D4 entry is (8, 6, 4928 × 3280) and 15520. This is exactly where the camera's own full-size JPEG sits, so the developed frame matches the camera's. One clip level for all three channels makes clipped highlights white without moving the white balance. Other bodies, and the D4 at other sizes or depths, take the existing path unchanged.
- New test `measured_d4_image_area_and_white_level` checks three things:
  - a synthetic 4992 × 3292 14-bit "NIKON D4" gets the crop, the white level, the metadata size and a 4928 × 3280 develop;
  - another model with the same data is left alone;
  - a 12-bit D4 is left al…

title: LR-EDIT-DETAIL-SHARPEN: Radius and Detail work, and sharpening acts at pixel scale (#757)
author: radialmonster
body:

A reduced source retains the original photo’s dimensions for both CPU and GPU preparation. Subpixel sharpening follows the continuous Gaussian response without disappearing at a hard radius cutoff.

This is a new process, V3. Existing V1/V2 edits retain their original texture-band sharpening until explicitly updated. The sharpen plane is keyed by radius and process, and a noise-reduction change invalidates it even during a draft; the existing broad-plane cache reuse stays intact. Render-cache version is 65.

CPU pipeline/settings/raster regressions pass, covering working controls, old-process behavior, size/source-level handling, process/NR cache changes, subpixel response and hostile Gaussian inputs. All 18 GPU equivalence tests pass; the focused reduced-source/process/NR cases differ from CPU by at most one 8-bit level. Eight paired V1/V2 exports (raw and procedural sources, two output sizes) are pixel-identical to main. Radius/Detail crops were inspected. Parity, layers and assets pass. Wasm compilation passes. Full CI stops at the unchanged main `tests_export.rs` Clippy `drop_non_drop` error.

title: Brush mask: the live stroke places dabs like the committed one, no gaps on fast strokes (#517)
author: bitshiftza
body:
Fixes #517.

**Problem.** While painting a brush mask with the button held, the Detail view drew one hard tinted circle per pointer sample, so a fast stroke showed separate dabs with gaps. On release the committed stroke appeared: dabs interpolated a quarter radius apart, feathered, flow-accumulated.

**Cause.** `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/detail.rs` painted a fixed-alpha circle at each sample; `brush_dabs` in `crates/pipeline/src/masks.rs` fills in dabs between samples. The faster the pointer, the bigger the gaps.

**Fix.**
- `lightcraft_pipeline::masks`: dab placement (`push_dabs`, `dab_spacing`), falloff (`dab_alpha`) and flow accumulation (`accumulate`) factored out of `brush_dabs` / `rasterize_brush`, with no change in their output. `push_dabs` also caps a hostile segment (huge or non-finite coordinates in a `mask.brushStroke`) at 1 M dabs; before, it looped until memory ran out.
- New `crates/ui-egui/src/brush_live.rs`: the live stroke is painted with those same functions into a screen-resolution buffer (largest side capped at 4096) in the overlay's colour and opacity. Each frame stamps only the dabs of new samples and uploads only the touched rectangle; it is redrawn from scratch if the zoom, canvas or brush settings change mid-stroke.

![before (gaps), after with the button held, after release](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bitshiftza/lightcraft/issue-assets/brush-517.png)

**Tests.** Dab spacing on a long segment (live and committed placement identical, hostile cap); live-buffer unit tests (a fast segment has no gap, frame-by-frame equals painting the whole path, bad input doesn't panic); a headless fast drag with the button held: no gap along the centreline, live and committed pixels match. The headless test fails on main (60 of 74 centreline points are gaps).

**Docs.** `docs/parity.md` LR-MASK-BRUSH. `cargo xtask ci`: all 8 steps pass.

**Overlaps #518's PR** (holding the brush still hardens it): both change `brush_dabs` in `masks.rs` and the LR-MASK-…

title: Brush mask: holding the brush still adds no coverage; flow builds up by passes (#518)
author: bitshiftza
body:
Fixes #518.

**Problem.** With size, feather and flow unchanged, holding the brush still hardened the spot's feathered edge the longer the button was held. Camera Raw builds coverage by passes, not by time.

**Cause.** While the button is down, `resp.dragged()` is true every frame, so `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/detail.rs` recorded the same point once per frame (a 150-frame hold stored 73+ identical samples), and `brush_dabs` in `crates/pipeline/src/masks.rs` laid a dab for each, even after a zero-length move. Each dab adds `a·flow·(1−v)`, so the edge climbed toward 1 with hold time, even at flow 100.

**Fix.**
- `brush_dabs` (shared by the CPU, GPU and spot-brush paths) lays no dab for a sample that hasn't moved from the last one, so waiting adds nothing, including in strokes already saved with repeated samples.
- The canvas doesn't record a sample at the same position as the last one, which also stops the live overlay darkening during a hold.
- Spacing along a moving stroke is unchanged, and passes back over an area still build up by flow.

![quick press vs a 150-frame hold, before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bitshiftza/lightcraft/issue-assets/brush-518.png)

**Tests.** A stationary hold gives exactly the single-press mask (2, 5, 60 and 600 samples; flow 100 and 40), and a stroke that pauses midway lays the same dabs as one that doesn't; back-and-forth passes at flow 20 still build up (1 → 2 → 3); a headless UI test compares a quick press with a 120-frame hold (one sample each, same edge profile). The stationary tests fail on main.

**Docs.** `docs/parity.md` LR-MASK-BRUSH. `cargo xtask ci`: all 8 steps pass.

Worth knowing: saved edits that contain repeated stationary samples now render softer, which is the fix applied to existing data. Separate strokes still combine by maximum rather than adding up by flow; Lightroom probably accumulates across strokes too, which would be a separate issue. **Overlaps #517's PR** in `brush_dabs` and the LR-MASK-BR…

body:

title: LR-CROP-FLIP: Flip H / Flip V show in the crop tool
author: PiMinusMax
body:

None changed.

title: LR-IMP-CAMERA-COVERAGE: SRF and DSLR-A100 raws open again (#702)
author: AlexChambers
body:
Fixes #702.

Since #281's camera-TIFF reconciliation, `probe` takes a SONY file as a raw only with raw evidence (`has_raw_ifd`: a CFA photometric, a raw compression, tag 0x7010 or a CFA pattern tag). Two Sony layouts have none of those, so on `main` b70ae17 they are "not a readable photo", where `main` 5436951 opened them:

- **SRF** (DSC-F828): IFD0 looks like RGB but holds 14-bit samples (14 14 14, 3360 wide). The raw and its keys are in Sony's SRF blocks.
- **DSLR-A100:** IFD0 is the old-JPEG thumbnail, and tag 330 (`SubIFDs`) addresses the raw data directly.

**Fix:** for Sony, two more kinds of raw evidence, next to `has_raw_ifd`:
- IFD0 samples of 12 or 14 bits, raw sensor depths. A camera-authored or exported TIFF has 8 or 16, so #281's case stays an ordinary image.
- Model `DSLR-A100` with IFD0 an old-style JPEG thumbnail (compression 6, which today's TIFF writers don't produce) and a `SubIFDs` tag. A TIFF exported from A100 photos, with an ordinary thumbnail in SubIFDs, stays an image.

**Test:** `sony_raws_without_a_cfa_ifd_are_still_raws` probes synthetic files: SRF at 14 and 12 bits and the A100 layout are raws; an 8-bit and a 16-bit Sony TIFF, 8- and 16-bit A100 TIFFs with a SubIFDs thumbnail, and the A100's layout under another model are not. It fails on `main` (the SRF case), and the A100 TIFF cases fail if the compression condition is dropped. The existing camera-TIFF test (#281) still passes.

**Checked on the public files:** the raw.pixls.us DSC-F828 `DSC06227.SRF` and DSLR-A100 `DSC0258.ARW` open again through their embedded previews, as on `main` 5436951 (raw decoding still reports them unsupported), and render byte-identical to it (`lightcraft-cli render --size 600`). The other 133 files of my Sony sweep (127 raw.pixls.us files covering 98 Sony models, the 4 Sony corpus files and the two from #244) render pixel-identical to `main` b70ae17 at 1200 px.

title: LR-LIB-FOLDER: a refused command says why

Why one PR: one behaviour, a click the library refuses says why: the `act` wrapper, the move of every `let _ = app.run(…)` call site to it, and the `cargo xtask refusals` check that keeps new silent calls out. A partial move would leave some refusals silent, and the check couldn't be turned on until every call site is moved. About 1,945 changed lines, most of them the mechanical call-site move.

`LightcraftApp::run` hands the error back, and 326 call sites in the interface wrote `let _ = app.run(…)`. A click the library refused did nothing and said nothing: the reason went to the log and to `ui.status`, which only agents see. title: LR-BEHAV-GPU: no indirect-call validation pipeline, which Intel Metal fails to compile (issue #250)
author: radialmonster
body:
Fixes the remaining launch failure in #250 (2015 MacBook Pro, Intel GPU, Metal).

**What the log shows.** With 0.5.0 and `LIGHTCRAFT_GPU=0`, the window still never opens:

```
ERROR wgpu_core::indirect_validation: indirect-validation error: ComputePipeline(Internal("new_compute_pipeline_state: NSError { code: 2, localizedDescription: "Compiler encountered an internal error" ...
ERROR eframe::native::run: Exiting because of error: WGPU error: Parent device is lost
```

wgpu's **indirect-call validation** (`InstanceFlags::VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL`, on by default in release builds) builds an internal compute pipeline whenever a device is created. That includes the window's device, so `LIGHTCRAFT_GPU=0` can't avoid it. Metal's compiler on that Mac fails on this pipeline, the device is lost, and eframe exits.

**Change.** That validation only guards indirect draws and dispatches. Neither LightCraft nor egui issues any (no `*_indirect` call in the workspace or in egui-wgpu).
- **New:** `backend::instance_flags` clears the flag, unless `WGPU_VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL` asks for it.
- **Applied to every instance LightCraft creates:** the window's (`window_wgpu_options`), `Gpu::new` and the denoise device.

**Tests:**
- **New:** `indirect_call_validation_is_off_unless_asked_for` (the flag rule) and `window_has_no_indirect_call_validation_pipeline`.
- **GPU suite:** all `lightcraft-gpu` tests pass on a real adapter (Windows, DX12/Vulkan), including the CPU/GPU equivalence tests.
- **Gates:** `cargo fmt --check` passes, and clippy `-p lightcraft-gpu -p lightcraft --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.

**Not verified on the affected Mac.** I don't have one. title: LR-EXP-TYPE: JPEG XL export (#247)
author: robmdunn
body:
Fixes #247.

Photos can now be exported as JPEG XL from the Export dialog (Format ▸ JPEG XL), the CLI (`lightcraft-cli render in.raw -o out.jxl`), MCP and the control channel (`format: "jxl"`).

**Options:** Quality (1–100, as for JPEG) or **Lossless**; **Effort** Fast / Normal; **Progressive**; 8- or 16-bit; EXIF and XMP in `Exif` / `xml ` boxes. With **HDR output**, photos edited in HDR are written as 16-bit Rec. 2020 PQ. New `app.export` params: `jxlLossless`, `jxlEffort` (`fast` | `normal`), `jxlProgressive`; saved presets keep them.

**Colour:** lossy files declare an enum colour encoding: sRGB, Display P3 or Rec. 2020. The encoder can't declare Adobe RGB or ProPhoto, so lossy files in those are written as Rec. 2020, and the dialog says so. Lossless files keep any of the five spaces through the ICC profile.

**Encoder:** [`jixel`](https://crates.io/crates/jixel) 0.3.4, BSD-3-Clause OR Apache-2.0, pure Rust with no dependencies. It is a port of Google's BSD-licensed libjxl-tiny by the author of `moxcms`. It was the only permissive pure-Rust lossy encoder I found: imazen's `jxl-encoder` / `zenjxl` are AGPL (already listed as not used in `crates/codecs/README.md`), `jpegxl-rs` binds C++ libjxl, and `zune-jpegxl` is lossless only. Because it is young (first release 2026-05):
- every call runs under `catch_unwind`, since it has internal `assert!`s;
- it is native only: it starts `std::thread`s outside its `num_threads` setting, which wasm32 can't. The web build reports "JPEG XL encoding is not available in this build"; JXL import still works there.

**Decoder fix (import):** jxl-oxide 0.12 desaturates colours outside sRGB when it renders a lossy (XYB) image to wider primaries. A P3 red came back about 30 % less saturated, so any lossy P3 or Rec. 2020 JXL imported dull, not only ours. `crates/codecs/src/jxl.rs` now asks jxl-oxide for linear sRGB primaries, which it renders unclamped and correctly, and converts to Rec. 2020 itself.

**Left out: jixel's slowest effort.…

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: a partial look from the bright pairs for mostly-sky frames (#631, stacked on #699)
author: AlexChambers
body:
The other half of #631: the bird. **Builds on #699** and includes its commit; only the second commit is new here. I'll rebase once #699 lands.

Rebased onto main `0da998f2` after integration batch 40. This branch uses `LOOK_VERSION` 13 and `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 70. Main uses look 9 and render 64. This branch contains rebased #699 at look 12 and render 69, then its own bright-pairs change at look 13 and render 70. With #699's check for black-and-white JPEGs, `keeps` takes the whole `HighlightCheck` instead of its DRO flag, so it compares luminance for those too.

## What was wrong

rock-meister's DSC01480 (ILCE-7RM4, a bird on a bare tree against overcast sky) gets no camera look on `main`: ΔE76 14.8 against its camera JPEG, ΔL\* −13.6, with the sky a dull grey-blue where the camera renders it near white. 92% of the frame is sky at camera JPEG luminance about 0.93. The fits leave out JPEG luminance 0.85 and up, because the camera bleaches colour there. That leaves 473 midtone pairs, too few coloured ones for a full look. The partial look (#583) fits a curve to the branches alone, and its held-out squared error only drops by 23% (RMS 0.178 → 0.156), short of the required 30%. The sky, which decides the picture, is in neither the fit nor the check.

## Fix

When the partial look misses its gates, `fit_partial` tries once more with the frame's bright, unclipped pixels in its tone fit and its held-out check (`bright_tone_pairs`: camera JPEG luminance 0.85 and up). For colour the bleaching makes them unreliable, but for tone they are good evidence. They come from `collect_pairs`' wider set, which has no clipped sensor pixels when the clipped ones were left out of the proxy. A JPEG pixel clipped in the JPEG's own encoding only bounds the curve, so it is left out too (`jpeg_clipped`: any channel at 0.98 or more in sRGB or Adobe RGB, which is what camera JPEGs use; in Rec.2020, where the proxy holds them, a clipped sRGB red can read 0.96).

title: Sidebar sections: reorder, show/hide, pinned headers, shared section frame
author: nledford
body:
## What this does

The left sidebar's sections (Albums, Local, By Date, Folders, Keywords) are now drawn by one shared section frame from one saved arrangement, and the user can arrange them.

title: LR-PREF-DISPLAY: macOS previews follow the screen's profile, so they match exports (#787)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #787.

Previews looked more saturated than the exported files. The pixels are identical, though: the difference is how macOS shows LightCraft's window.

**Measured** (demo photo, Saturation 0 and +60, release build on macOS arm64):
- Preview vs export match to within one level per channel, on the CPU path (`lightcraft-cli snapshot`) and the GPU path (the app's window, Apple M4 Max / Metal). Mean chroma at +60: preview 42.80 (CPU) / 42.70 (GPU), export 42.55.
- The export embeds a correct ICC v4 sRGB profile (D50-adapted sRGB colorants, Bradford `chad`, sRGB TRC).

**Cause.** For an sRGB surface, wgpu 30 sets the window's `CAMetalLayer.colorspace` to `nil`, and `CAMetalLayer.h` says: "If nil, no colormatching occurs." On a P3 screen (every recent Mac), LightCraft's sRGB values are therefore shown as if they were P3, so they look too saturated. Preview, Photos and browsers convert the exports properly. That fits the report: every slider and every output format is affected, and a P3 export is only "slightly closer" because it clips less.

**Change:**
- `apps/lightcraft/src/screen_profile.rs` (macOS): the ICC profile of the screen the window is on (`NSWindow.screen.colorSpace.ICCProfileData`; the main screen when the window is hidden). It uses only safe objc2 / objc2-app-kit / objc2-foundation calls (versions muda and wgpu already pull in), so there's no `unsafe`, and it returns `None` off the main thread.
- `Services::screen_profile` (`ui-egui`): while no profile is chosen in Settings ▸ Display, previews are shown through the screen's profile using the existing display-profile path (`Display::from_bytes` → `Renderer::set_display`). It is read again about once a second (egui time), so moving the window to another screen is followed; an unchanged profile costs nothing (`set_display` only drops textures when the profile id changes).
- A chosen profile still wins. On macOS the Settings ▸ Display button reads "Use Screen Profile" instead of "Use sRGB". The Profile row…

title: LR-EDIT-RESET: Reset Edits returns a raw to its import defaults, sharpening and colour NR included
author: radialmonster
body:
**Bug:** **Reset Edits** (`develop.reset`, ⇧⌘R) on a raw set **Sharpening and Color noise reduction to 0**. Import gives raws Sharpening 40 and Color NR 25 (`DevelopSettings::for_raw`). @QuirkyTurtle94 noted this in #763: `develop.get` after import shows 40/25, and `develop.reset` gives 0/0.

**Cause:** for a photo without a default-preset look (`import_look`), reset rebuilt the settings from `DevelopSettings::default()` plus the as-shot white balance. That drops everything raw-specific, including the embedded lens corrections that import turns on.

**Fix:** reset starts from the photo's own built-in defaults, `Photo::camera_defaults()`, the same function import uses, and keeps the white balance of its current as-shot reference as before. Rendered files are unchanged, because their defaults are `DevelopSettings::default()`.

**Tests:**
- **New:** `reset_edits_restores_a_raws_import_defaults`. After raising Sharpening and Color NR, a NEF resets to 40/25 and a JPEG to 0/0.
- **Existing:** the reset tests pass (as-shot WB per format, the process versions, the default-preset look).
- **Gates:** `cargo fmt --check` and clippy `-p lightcraft-engine --all-targets -D warnings` pass.

No render-cache change: renders don't change, only what Reset produces.

title: LR-EDIT-OPTICS-PROFILE: apply DNG WarpRectilinear2 lens corrections (Pixel DNGs, #635)
author: radialmonster
body:
Fixes #635: a Google Pixel 8 Pro ultra-wide DNG rendered with a grey curved border whenever Lens Corrections were on.

**Cause.** The DNG's `OpcodeList3` is `WarpRectilinear2`, `WarpRectilinear2`, `WarpRectilinear`. `WarpRectilinear2` (opcode 14, DNG 1.6) wasn't parsed, so it was kept as `Unknown`, and only the trailing `WarpRectilinear` ran. The spec says that one is meant to be **skipped** after an optional `WarpRectilinear2`, so the frame was bent by the wrong model.

**Change** (DNG Specification 1.6.0.0, chapter 7, *WarpRectilinear2* and the skip rule):
- **Parsing:** `N` planes × (`kr0..kr14`, `kt0`, `kt1`, `min_valid_radius`, `max_valid_radius`), then the centre and `reciprocalRadial`. The model is `f(r) = Σ kr_p·r^p` at the clamped radius, applied as `d·f` (or `d/f` when reciprocal), with WarpRectilinear's tangential terms.
- **Malformed input:** parameters with the wrong size, N outside 1–4, non-finite or huge values, or an invalid radius range stay `Unknown`, never a panic.
- **Skip rule:** a `WarpRectilinear` right after an optional `WarpRectilinear2` is skipped (`applied_ops`). On this file that leaves WR2 with per-plane coefficients (lateral CA), then WR2 for single-plane geometry.
- **Optics:** `EmbeddedLens` carries up to 3 chained warp stages, evaluated last first, in `optics.rs`. The Enable Lens Corrections switch covers them.
- **GPU:** the f32 shader can't evaluate the degree-14 polynomial accurately (coefficients reach 1e5), so photos with this chain are warped on the CPU.

**Pixel 8 Pro DNG from #635** (long edge 1600; panel: corrections off | main | this PR):

![Pixel 8 Pro DNG: corrections off, main, this PR](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c1e6b3ca-bc1c-44d9-8a82-91aa9369a5e2)

| | grey border pixels in the 120 px corners | edge-map correlation with the embedded preview |
|---|---:|---:|
| main | 28,694 / 57,600 | 0.262 |
| this PR | **0** | **0.323** |
| lens corrections off | 0 | 0.308 |

**Regression:** 12 DNGs without opcode 14…

title: Catalog: the log is compacted by the snapshot's size, not every 2000 records
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`. It replaces #800's content: #800 held four changes (compaction by snapshot size, upgrades that keep what they replace, a library that states its develop defaults, and compact records / format 10), which I am splitting into four PRs, each off `main` once the one before lands. This is the first, and the only one with no format change.

## Problem

A snapshot rewrites the whole catalog, and the log was compacted every 2000 records, so the bytes written by an import grew with the square of the library: importing 100,000 photos rewrote a 370 MB snapshot 50 times (9.4 GB written, 38 s in the measurement below) and a 300,000-photo import about 84 GB. Quitting also rewrote the whole snapshot every time, however few changes there were.

## Change

`SnapshotPolicy` (`crates/catalog/src/journal.rs`) decides when the log is compacted:

- While working, the log is compacted once it is long (2000 records or 16 MB) and has grown to a quarter of the snapshot's size, or when it reaches 256 MB.
- On quit, a snapshot up to 64 MB is compacted as before; a larger one only when the log is long (2000 records or 16 MB). So after a quit the log is never longer than it was, and a quit after a few changes doesn't rewrite a large catalog (`Journal::wants_snapshot_on_close`, used by `Session::close_library`).
- The journal knows the size of `catalog.snap` (`snapshot_bytes`) from open and after every snapshot, sync or background.
- A library whose upgrade at open could not be written (a full disk) is still written in this build's format on quit, whatever the log's length (`behind`): closing must not leave an older snapshot with this build's records after it.

Nothing in the files changes. `persist_bench` gains an import phase (compacting as the app does, counting what it writes), two more photo mixes and a log-replay timing. Rules and measurements: `docs/catalog-persistence.md` (new).

title: Info panel map of the photo's location; click opens the Map view (LR-MAP-INFO, stacked on #797)
author: bitshiftza
body:
**Stacked on #797** (the map core and Map view). Until #797 merges this PR also shows its commits; the change here is the last commit, `LR-MAP-INFO: a map of the photo's location in the Info panel`.

Tracker: **LR-MAP-INFO** (P1, 🟡 → ✅), LR-META-LOCATION note ("no embedded map" no longer true).

For a photo with GPS, the Info panel shows a small map under the location fields: zoom 14, the photo's pin, the tile credit always visible. **A click opens the Map view centred on the photo**, with the Info panel still open beside it. **Show on Map** becomes **Open in Browser** (same widget id, still openstreetmap.org), and the coordinates get their own line. With several photos selected it shows the active photo's place and fetches nothing for the others; a photo without GPS has no map. With the offline tile source it stays grey with its pin and "Map tiles are off", so the panel keeps its shape and the click still works.

![Info panel mini-map, and the Map view opened from it (fake tiles from the test tile server)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bitshiftza/lightcraft/issue-assets/map-info-panel.png)

author: radialmonster
body:
Rebased onto main (31ee2643) and cut down to what main still lacks: validated colour terms for DNG camera-preview fits.

On top of the file's own matrix, white balance and profile tables, the fit now tries a hue/saturation table, luminance-band chroma matrices, a hue-chroma term and bounded offsets.
