title: AI Denoise: run tiles on another computer's graphics card (remote offload)
author: akvaithi
body:
Follow-up to #642 (as suggested there by @radialmonster): remote-GPU offload as a change to the existing `crates/denoise`, not a separate denoiser.

A laptop can hand AI Denoise tiles to a desktop's graphics card over a LAN or VPN (e.g. Tailscale). When the model is first used the laptop times a check tile on the server, there and back; if that beats its own time per tile, the server's slots are **added** to the laptop's runner (a tile goes to a free server slot, otherwise runs locally). If the server is slower, nothing is sent, so a photo never waits for it. A server that fails or disappears costs nothing: its tiles run locally, and it's dropped after three failures.

Measured with RawNIND on a 20.8 MP raw: M3 laptop alone 6.4 s; an RTX 3060 Ti over Tailscale takes 345 ms per tile there and back against the M3's 116 ms, so it's correctly left out (7.2 s including the one-time check). An earlier version that shared blindly took 34 s; that's what the speed check fixes.

**What's in it**
- `lightcraft_denoise::remote`: protocol v1 over plain TCP. JSON-line headers, tiles as half floats (byte-shuffled and deflated, roughly halving traffic), the existing tile contract unchanged (4 × T × T Bayer planes in, 3 × 2T × 2T out).
  - Client: `Remote`, a `TileRunner`-style runner with `try_run` for non-blocking slots, plus `Shared`.
  - Server: `serve`.
- Engine `Network`: with `LIGHTCRAFT_DENOISE_URL` + `LIGHTCRAFT_DENOISE_TOKEN` set, it greets the server on first use and checks the model's SHA-256 (the manifest's, else the file's) and tile size. It adds the server's slots to the tiles in flight. `denoise.status` → `device.remote` reports the address, the server's device, and used / unavailable (why) / given up.
- `lightcraft-cli denoise-serve`: serves the installed, selected model (or `--model ID`) the way the app runs it, on the card checked against the CPU, else the CPU.
- `docs/denoise.md` → *Another computer's graphics card*.

**Safety:** the transport is unencrypted, and…

title: Catalog: the snapshot in segments of about 2 MB and at most 4096 photos (format 11, stacked on #800)
author: nledford
body:
Stacked on #800 (compact records, format 10). Folds #846 (segment size and the checked folder sync), which is closed as folded.

Why stacked: it edits the snapshot code from #800 (the `FORMATS` table that format 11 is a row of, `Policy::due`'s snapshot-size parameter, `snapshot_bytes`, and the `ReadingOver` / `reading_over` settings reader in `stored.rs`), none of which is on `main`; its segments are built on those, so it can't be built without #800.

## What

The snapshot's photos move out of `catalog.snap` into **segment files** (`segments/<first id>-<seq>.json` in the library folder, each a run of photos in id order, plain JSON). `catalog.snap` keeps everything else and lists the segments with their size, CRC-32 and photo count. Catalog format 10 → 11. `crates/catalog/src/segments.rs`, `docs/catalog-persistence.md`.

- **A compaction writes only the segments whose photos changed.** Which ones is not worked out from the ops: the journal keeps the photos as the segments on disk hold them (shared `Arc`s) and compares pointers. Changing a photo copies it, so a segment is rewritten exactly when one of its photos was changed, added or removed, whatever did it.
- **Opening reads segments on several threads**, checking size, CRC, photo count, id range and the total. A damaged or missing segment fails the open with an error naming the file; nothing is modified.
- **Commit:** new segments under names no snapshot lists (written on several threads, each fsynced, one folder sync), then `catalog.snap` replaced atomically, then the files it no longer lists removed.
- **Upgrade:** a one-file library is split on first open; the segments are read back and compared with the loaded photos before `catalog.snap` is replaced. If they differ, the one file stays.
- **Stores without segments** (`Store::segmented()` false: the browser build, whose storage holds a fixed set of files) keep the photos in `catalog.snap`. `Store` gains `remove`, `list`, `segmented`, `write_new_with`, `sync`, al…

title: Catalog: equal develop settings are held once in memory (stacked on #814)
author: nledford
body:
Stacked on #814 (segments; it no longer needs #846, which is folded into #814).

Why stacked: its tests save and reopen a library in segments and in one file (`MemStore::single_file`, `Journal::policy.segment_photos`) and its new `shared.rs` reads through `stored::reading_now`, both from #814, and it replaces `read_optional_settings` from #800 in `stored.rs`; none of that is on `main`.

## What

Photos whose develop settings are equal now hold them once in memory (`crates/catalog/src/shared.rs`). No change to the files or the catalog format.

A photo holds its settings behind an `Arc`, and so do its history steps, versions and import look. Until now every photo read from a library or imported got a value of its own, though most photos of a library hold the defaults: 1.5 kB of the 2.9 kB an unedited photo's record takes.

- Every settings value that enters a catalog, read from a saved library (`deserialize_with` on the four fields) or given by a change (`Catalog::apply`), is replaced by the one already held when an equal one is: the defaults, what settings with nothing stated read as, the current photo's settings, or one of the last few seen on the thread.
- Settings saved as `{}` (every unedited photo) are not read at all when a library is opened.
- **Equal means the same down to the saved JSON.** `==` takes -0.0 for 0.0, which the JSON, `hash64` and a photo's fingerprint don't: settings holding a negative zero are never shared and never what others share.
- Sharing can't carry one photo's edit to another: settings behind an `Arc` are replaced, never changed in place (no `Arc::get_mut` on settings anywhere; `Arc::make_mut` copies a shared value).
- What a thread remembers to compare with is a handful of weak pointers: it keeps no settings alive.

Bytes requested from the allocator per photo, the library opened from disk (Apple M1 Max; before = #814):

title: LR-EDIT-OPTICS-PROFILE: Sony ILCE-7RM6 embedded lens corrections (distortion applied; CA and vignetting parsed)
author: dev-null-undefined
body:
## Scope
Sony ARW files carry three count-prefixed lens tables in the raw IFD: distortion `0x7037`, vignetting `0x7032`, lateral CA `0x7035`. For the **ILCE-7RM6** (A7R VI) this PR:
- turns the distortion table into a one-plane DNG `WarpRectilinear` (applied by the existing optics path, on by default like RW2 and the ILCE-7RM4A), measured on 54 photos against the camera JPEG: relative table indexed at the corrected radius, unit 1/15000, sensor-fixed knots at `hypot(9984, 6656)/30` px (full-frame 16 knots, APS-C crop 11), frame-filling zoom, crop centre; fit gate 0.25 px at 1440 px evaluated only on displayed radii;
- parses and converts the lateral CA table to red/blue planes but keeps them **off by default**: the demosaic already hides ~70 % of the lens CA and the post-demosaic warp overshoots (corner R/G–B/G residual rms 0.032 → 0.052 px at 1440 when on). Follow-up: warp the CFA colour planes before demosaic;
- parses the vignetting table but never applies it: the camera JPEG applies no compensation (regression slope 0.009 ± 0.063 against the table over 39 photos) and no radial model fits.
Shares the radial least-squares fit with Panasonic RW2 (`vendor::warp_from_forward_map` / `fit_radial_warp`; RW2 bit-identical, measured on 2000 maps). `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 62 → 63.

## Two conventions
Main's `arw_lens.rs` (ILCE-7RM4A, #498, validated against Sony Imaging Edge On/Off exports) is untouched; the modules are selected by exact model. title: CR3: decode CRX quantisation step 44 (QP 168), Canon EOS R50 C-RAW
author: radialmonster
body:
Fixes #828

## What changed
- The adaptive QP map accepts QP 131..=168 (was up to 167).
- The quantisation step accepts quant_step 4..=44 (was up to 43); step 44 uses step size 102, continuing the existing step sequence. Anything above stays rejected.
- `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` bumped, since such files change from the embedded preview to a raw decode.
- Tests in the CRX decoder cover the new range and the rejection above it; `docs/cr3.md` updated.

## Measurement
The step-44 size was measured on the R50 file's own coefficient statistics with GPU sweeps. Prior knowledge of how other converters handle this value was vague, so nothing was taken from them; this is a clean route.
- Pooled estimate of the step: 99.7.
- Control-calibrated 95% CI: [96.4, 102.6].
- A clamp at 90 is excluded by the data.
- The continuation of the step sequence, 102, lies inside the interval.
- Of 110 CR3 files checked, only this R50 file reaches QP 168; none reach 169 or higher.

## Colour on the R50 is a separate matter
The decode looks right, but the render is flat/blue-grey with dark greens. Reading the code on this branch: the R50 has no row in the spectral camera table and no pooled camera profile, so it starts from the neutral fallback matrix. The guarded per-photo fit against the embedded JPEG then supplies the matrix, hue/saturation table and tone curve (it passed its held-out gate on the sample, RMS 0.219 -> 0.020). There is no Canon-specific median tone curve or camera matrix for it. The sample is an ISO 32000 shot, which makes that per-photo fit noisy. Not addressed here.

## Tests
- Raw crate tests (including the CRX tests): all pass.
- Known unrelated failures: 7 `tests_sync` tests, and `lightcraft-mcp` `export_progress_and_cancel` (tests/e2e.rs), which also fails on current origin/main (checked twice in a clean worktree).

title: fix(previews): shard new smart previews while retaining legacy files
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

LightCraft currently stores all smart preview files directly inside
one directory.

Large photo libraries can accumulate tens of thousands of files in
that directory, making the storage layout difficult to manage.

Changing this layout also requires backward compatibility: existing
smart previews must remain accessible, including when their
original photos are offline.

## Root cause

Smart preview filenames use content-addressed hexadecimal hashes,
but their storage paths do not use those hashes to distribute files
across directories.

The existing lookup, migration, and statistics paths also assume
a flat directory layout.

## Changes

- Store newly generated smart previews in directories identified
  by the first two hexadecimal characters of their content hash.
- Preserve support for existing flat-layout smart previews.
- Update smart preview lookup and offline-original fallback.
- Update preview statistics to recognize both storage layouts.
- Support moving existing flat-layout previews into the sharded
  layout when changing smart preview locations.
- Update discard, stale-preview refresh, and related library paths.
- Avoid traversing unrelated directories and symlinked directories.
- Avoid recursively recreating missing parent directories on
  disconnected external drives.
- Add regression coverage for mixed legacy/sharded storage and
  preview migration.

Existing flat-layout previews remain accessible without requiring
an immediate migration. Moving previews to another location through
the existing location command reorganizes them into shards.

## Validation

- Reviewed the affected application and filesystem code paths.
- Confirmed the branch contains two commits based on upstream main.
- Added and updated regression test source; not executed.
- Filesystem integration tests, offline-drive scenarios, Cargo checks,
  and CI remain pending.

author: spsaustin

…, noise cutoff

A new L2 crate of pure algorithms ported as a design from the VERA studio (docs/VERA-SEARCH.md in rlp-main): a BM25 inverted index with prefix matching for the keyword lane; clean-room PDQ (256-bit, with the quality metric) and DCT pHash (64-bit) digests with the studio's same-picture decision (tight 31/6, loose 63/12); reciprocal rank fusion at k = 60; and the background-sampled noise ceiling (2000 deterministic pairs, lower-half MAD × 2.5, sqrt(2 ln n) + 0.674 + 1 sigmas, engaged at 8 candidates).

- **Nothing half-made counts**: written as `<name>.partial`, renamed when whole; a failed or stopped backup removes it; one cut short by a crash is cleared away by a later backup once it is an hour old.

title: web: stop the release zip shipping Cargo build artifacts (#793)
author: eliets2
body:
**Bug:** The lightcraft-web-0.5.0.zip release artifact shipped the Cargo build output for the web profile inside the site bundle. The archive carried deps/ (81 files, 90.6 MB), build/ (149 files, 22.4 MB), and .fingerprint/ (297 files) — roughly 113 MB of unreferenced build output that also leaked absolute build paths and internal crate names into a published release.

**Cause:** The site bundle was written to <target>/web while the build ran under --profile web. When cross-compiling with --target wasm32-unknown-unknown, Cargo places that profile's HOST artifacts — build scripts, proc-macro crates, and their deps/, build/, and .fingerprint/ bookkeeping — under <target>/<profile>/, which is exactly the bundle directory. packaging/web/package.sh then zipped that directory wholesale.

**Fix:** The bundle now goes to <target>/web-site, a name that is not a Cargo profile, so Cargo's host artifacts can no longer land inside it. A new unit test, site_dir_is_not_a_cargo_profile, asserts this invariant against Cargo.toml (the site dir must never match a declared profile name). packaging/web/package.sh points at the new directory and fails if deps/, build/, or .fingerprint/ ever appear in the site dir again. The profile name, the rust-cache keys, and the CI web job are unchanged.

**Tests:** New: cargo test -p xtask runs 34/34, including the new site_dir_is_not_a_cargo_profile test. The packaging guard was dry-run both ways — it fires on a planted deps/ directory and passes a clean site dir. Gates: cargo fmt and cargo clippy -p xtask -- -D warnings are clean, and a stale-reference grep for the old bundle path returns zero hits.

VERIFY:
- cargo test -p xtask -> 34/34 pass, including site_dir_is_not_a_cargo_profile
- cargo clippy -p xtask -- -D warnings -> clean
- packaging/web/package.sh on a clean site -> zip contains no deps/, build/, or .fingerprint/

title: smart previews: store proxies at JPEG quality 97 and version the encoding (#709)
author: eliets2
body:
**Bug:** Proxy previews carried a visible error against the original, as reported in #709. Its dominant term is the JPEG-quantised 8x8 DCT DC (each block's own mean, on luma and chroma), which walks block steps across the frame plus a small constant colour shift that grows with saturation.

**Cause:** At quality 92 the DC coefficient of each 8x8 block is quantised coarsely enough that its deviation shows as a per-block step.

**Fix:** Proxy JPEG quality goes from 92 to 97 (block-mean dE76 0.138 vs 0.202 on the fidelity test's smooth scene; about twice the file size). The proxy header gains `enc` (encode version 2) and the folder's look marker becomes `<look> <enc>`. A proxy or marker written before the encode version is treated as stale. Old files still decode bit-identically (decode ignores `enc`), and a proxy from a newer build is left alone by an older one, so there is no rebuild loop.

**What this does not cover (please read):** the refresh that runs when a library is opened only looks at the proxies of raw files that take the per-file camera look, the only ones the camera-look fit reaches. JPEG, PNG, TIFF and DNG proxies, and raws that do not take the per-file look, are not rebuilt by it, and a proxy whose original is offline is kept as it is. Build Smart Previews rebuilds a stale proxy once its original is readable. So an existing library ends up with a mix of quality-97 and older proxies until Build Smart Previews has run; it does not become uniform by itself, and I have not claimed that it rebuilds exactly once.

**Tests:** a frozen copy of the old encoder plus a block-mean dE76 metric (per-pixel dE is dominated by the shared 8-bit sRGB floor); the 0.8 bound is the geometric midpoint between the no-op ratio 1.000 and the 0.632 floor, and the metric measured 1.000 at q92 and 0.683 at q97. An encode-version staleness test covers the rebuild trigger. `smart_preview_look_marker_is_read_safely` was written for the one-number marker and failed on this change (the …

title: control protocol: document the Wayland visibility stall (#718)
author: eliets2
body:
**Bug:** On Wayland (sway/wlroots), a queued control or MCP request can time out even though the app is running. A surface on an inactive workspace or under a fullscreen window receives no frame callback, so App::logic never runs and queued requests stay undelivered until the surface is shown again.

**Cause:** Requests are dispatched on the UI thread between frames. The repaint fallback that covers the hidden case elsewhere cannot fire here: eframe 0.36.2's timer-driven direct-paint path requires is_visible() == Some(false), but winit 0.30.13's Wayland backend returns None (unknown) for is_visible() and is_minimized(). Windows, macOS, and X11 are unaffected.

**Fix:** Documentation only — no code change. The stall is decided in eframe/winit control flow the app cannot reach, so the new paragraph documents the limitation and points unattended drivers at headless rendering. Upstream directions, if wanted: eframe could treat a visibility of None like the hidden case on the timer-driven path, or winit could derive visibility from xdg state.

**Tests:** Docs-only change; cargo fmt is clean.

VERIFY:
- cargo fmt --check -> clean
- read the control-protocol doc -> Wayland visibility stall documented, unattended drivers pointed at headless rendering

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: read an untagged camera JPEG in the colour space the raw's EXIF states (#778)
author: radialmonster
body:
Fixes the colour-space part of #778.

**Cause.** The Sony A7 II file was shot in Adobe RGB. Its embedded JPEG has no ICC profile or EXIF colour tag; the colour space is only in the raw's own EXIF (ColorSpace 0xA001 = Uncalibrated, InteropIndex "R03", the DCF Adobe RGB option file). LightCraft read that fallback only from the Nikon maker note, so the Sony JPEG was decoded as sRGB, and the camera look was fitted to colours that were too dull.

**Change.**
- `embedded_preview_color_space` now reads the raw's EXIF ColorSpace / InteropIndex for every make. A Nikon maker note still wins, and the JPEG's own ICC/EXIF declaration still takes precedence.
- DNGs are skipped: their EXIF describes the original capture, while their previews are rendered by the converter.
- `LOOK_VERSION` 2 → 3 and `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 42 → 43, so cached looks and renders refresh.
- Test: Sony R03 → Adobe RGB; ColorSpace 1 → sRGB; 0xFFFF with R98 or no interop → none; Canon R03 → Adobe RGB; the Nikon note wins; Nikon without a note falls back to EXIF; DNG → none.

**Measured on the #778 file** (render vs the camera JPEG decoded as Adobe RGB):

| | Mean chroma | Median ΔE |
|---|---|---|
| main | 6.4 | 5.57 |
| this PR | 7.2 | 5.44 |
| camera JPEG | 7.7 | – |

**Why it doesn't fully close the gap.** On this dark, muted scene the full colour fit (matrix + hue/sat) is refused before and after the fix, so only a partial look applies (tone + chroma curve). DRO was on in camera, so the tone curve is also replaced. Possible follow-ups, not in this PR:
- an ILCE-7M2 camera profile;
- loosening the colour-fit gates for dark scenes;
- DRO-aware tone on this body.

Tests: `lightcraft-raw` all pass; engine has only the existing `tests_sync` failures (same on main).

title: Catalog: restore a library from a backup, and keep what it replaces (stacked on #841)
author: nledford
body:
Stacked on #841 (backups), which is on #814 → #800.

Why stacked: it restores the backups that #841 makes: `catalog/src/restore.rs` calls `backup::check`, `backup::MARKER`, `backup::valid_name`, `backup::valid_extra`, `backup::sync_dir` and `backup::Watch`, and `engine/src/cmd/backup.rs` extends #841's `library.backup` code (`s.backup_dir`, `backup::list`, `backup::is_backup`), none of which are on `main`.

## What

#841 makes backups; this puts one back.

- **`library.restore {dir}`** makes the open library what the backup holds (catalog, log, presets, view and preferences; not the photos) and the session goes on in it. The folder the library's backups go to stays as it is now.
- **`library.restore {dir, to}`** restores into another folder instead and opens nothing. That is how to look at a backup without giving up the library. `to` is a folder that isn't there or is empty, or a library nothing has open.
- **`library.backups {dir?}`** lists a folder's backups, newest first.
- **A backup folder no longer opens as a library where it is.** Working in it changed it, after which it failed its own check. The error says to restore it.

No menu item yet: this is reachable from the command line, the control channel and MCP. The UI entry belongs with the backup folder picker in the next PR.

## How it keeps a library safe

- **Only a sound backup is restored.** It is read against its marker, and each file again as it is copied. One that was edited or damaged, or whose catalog or log a newer LightCraft wrote, is refused with the library untouched. The backup is only read; nothing is shared with it or made in its folder.
- **What the library held is kept**, including changes not yet saved, in `Replaced/<the time (UTC)>` in the library folder. That folder is a library folder itself.
- **All or nothing.** The backup is copied into `restore.partial`, then a note (`restore.json`) is written, then files are moved: the library's out with the snapshot first, the backup's in with the …

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: near-black pixels no longer turn white in the camera look
author: PiMinusMax
body:
Refs #820

### Change

`crates/engine/src/camera_preview.rs` (`HueSat::apply`):

- After the hue/saturation table, luminance is restored with `before / after`. Near black, where noise makes some channels negative, the table can bring `after` close to 0, and the gain turned single pixels white: isolated white dots in dark areas, most visible at fit, where the preview is binned without averaging.
- The table colour is now applied in full only if the table kept at least 25 % of the luminance (`MIN_LUMINANCE_KEPT`). At 15 % or less (`NO_LUMINANCE_KEPT`) the pixel keeps its colour, as black and non-finite pixels already did. In between the two are blended with a smoothstep (`restore_weight`), so noisy shadows show no step. Every pixel at 25 % or more renders exactly as before.

### Commands / parameters

None changed.

### Tests

- `camera_preview::tests::hue_sat_never_turns_near_black_noise_white`: 200,000 near-black colours with mixed-sign channels through a saturating table; no output channel may exceed 20× the input's largest. Fails without this change (2263×).
- `hue_sat_restore_weight_blends_smoothly_between_the_thresholds`: 0 up to 15 %, 1 from 25 %, monotonic, no step larger than 0.02 between shares 0.001 apart.
- `hue_sat_keeps_colours_the_table_leaves_bright_exactly_as_before`: colours the table keeps above 25 % render bit for bit as before.
- The two files from #820 (ILCE-7M4, ISO 3200 and 25600), isolated white dots in a 1200 × 1200 px crop: 57 → 0 and 107 → 0. Two own α77 II files at ISO 8000, whole frame: 209 → 0 and 181 → 0. With the blend all four still have 0. Unchanged at Color noise reduction 0, so not caused by it.
- `cargo xtask ci` green on 385348b2.

### Before / after

See #820 (comment with crops).

title: fix(ui): cap dialog height to the viewport so tall ones (Export) scroll (close #781)
author: rollroyces
body:
## Summary

On a 1366×768 screen, every dialog except Import was a fixed, centred `egui::Window` with no height cap and no scroll. The Export dialog (with the new HDR output row in 0.5.0) overflows first: title off the top, **Save preset** and **Cancel / Export** off the bottom. Nothing scrolls, the user can't confirm, and there's no interface-scale setting to make it fit. Reported on Discord, reproduced headlessly on `main` @ b70ae174.

Closes #781.

title: LR-HDR-EXPORT: HDR renders keep the camera tone curve in the midtones
author: robmdunn
body:
## Problem

HDR renders of raws that have a fitted camera tone curve (e.g. Nikon NEF with the camera-JPEG look) dropped the curve and used the generic HDR tone map, which is 1–2 stops darker through the midtones than the SDR render of the same edit:

- **PQ AVIF / JPEG XL** exports looked dark on every display.
- **Gain map JPEGs** stored negative gains (HDR ÷ SDR below 1 for most pixels), so they looked fine on SDR screens but went dark on HDR ones (e.g. iPhone Photos).

`base_tone` only used `ToneMap::camera` when `peak <= 1.0`. The existing `hdr_midtones_match_the_sdr_render` test uses a synthetic scene without a camera curve, so it never exercised this path.

## Fix

`ToneMap::camera_hdr`: the camera curve up to 1.5 EV over grey (identical to the SDR render, so a gain map only lifts highlights), then the same highlight lift as `ToneMap::hdr` up to the headroom peak. At peak 1 it is bit-identical to `ToneMap::camera`, so SDR renders don't change. CPU and GPU share the LUT.

## Measurements

A Nikon NEF at default settings with HDR on (3-stop headroom), luminance in nits with SDR white at 203:

| | median | 90th pct |
|---|---|---|
| SDR render | 7.7 | 71.9 |
| HDR render, before | 3.4 | 20.3 |
| HDR render, after | 7.75 | 71.9 |

Gain map JPEG, log2 gain: before, median −0.66 (as low as −1.8); after, 0 for 90% of pixels and up to +1.66 in the highlights. Checked on an iPhone (HDR display): the gain map JPEG and PQ JPEG XL now look right.

## Tests

- `tone::camera_hdr_keeps_the_camera_look_and_lifts_highlights`: same as SDR at peak 1 / NaN, monotone, bounded by the peak, the camera's midtones, highlights lifted.
- `tests_hdr::hdr_keeps_the_camera_tone_curve_in_the_midtones`: an HDR render with a camera curve matches the SDR render below the highlights. **Fails before this change.**

`cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Related

- #646 (HDR editing and export), where this path was introduced.
- #868 (HDR photo support): this makes HDR JPEG XL / AVIF exports of raws look r…

title: fix(windows): preserve legacy MSI install folders via App Paths
author: THEtheChad
body:
Upgrading an older Windows MSI installation (including 0.5.0) without repeating `INSTALLFOLDER` moves a custom installation back to Program Files. Those installers recorded the executable in App Paths but did not write the newer `Software\LightCraft\InstallFolder` value.

Read the parent directory from the legacy App Paths value when neither an explicit destination nor the newer stored folder is available, and only when `lightcraft.exe` still exists there. The action runs after the existing folder-selection action in both MSI sequences. This follows up on #520 / #399.

The existence check matters: the directory-only App Paths search doesn't verify the executable, and when the old installers' unquoted path no longer exists, Windows Installer falls back to the text before its first space. A default install whose `C:\Program Files\LightCraft` folder was deleted without uninstalling resolved to `C:\`, so an upgrade would have put the executables in the drive root. A second search of the same value with a `FileSearch` for `lightcraft.exe` gates the fallback; a stale value now falls through to Program Files.

The packaging workflow now exercises the actual WiX searches/actions through isolated per-user MSI probes on x64 and x86. It covers fresh installation, legacy App Paths, a legacy path whose folder or executable is gone, the newer stored folder, and precedence when both stored locations or an explicit destination exist. It does not modify an installed LightCraft application's registry entries, and it removes its test registry key afterwards.

Validation:

- The legacy-only regression failed before the fix and passed afterward. The stale-folder regression (`legacy-folder-deleted`) resolved to the parent of the text before the space without the existence check and passes with it. All eight cases pass on x64 and x86.
- Upgraded an official 0.5.0 x64 MSI installed in a path containing spaces and Unicode to a locally built patched MSI, without `INSTALLFOLDER`: the original…

title: fix(query): prevent catalog pagination overflow on 32-bit web builds
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

The catalog.query command accepts pagination offsets and limits
as unsigned 64-bit integers.

Currently, these values are converted to usize using unchecked
narrowing casts.

On 32-bit WebAssembly builds, values greater than u32::MAX can
wrap around.

For example, an offset of 4294967296 becomes zero, potentially
returning the first page instead of an empty result.

Large limit values can similarly wrap to zero.

## Root Cause

The query handler uses:

    as usize

for input-derived pagination values.

This conversion truncates out-of-range integers on 32-bit targets.

## Changes

- Replace unchecked casts with checked integer conversion.
- Saturate out-of-range values at usize::MAX.
- Preserve existing behavior for valid pagination values.
- Keep the change local to catalog query processing.

## Regression Coverage

Added unit tests covering:

- Zero offset.
- Normal pagination limits.
- Maximum unsigned 64-bit values.
- Values exceeding the 32-bit usize range.

## Validation

- Confirmed the branch was pushed successfully.
- Verified the change is restricted to the catalog query handler.
- Added regression coverage; tests have not been executed.
- Cargo tests, wasm32 compilation, formatting, and CI remain pending.

## Compatibility

No API changes or catalog format changes.

The correction specifically prevents pagination wraparound on
32-bit targets without changing valid pagination behavior.

## Issue

No public issue. Independently identified application correctness defect.

title: feat(ui): standardize custom titlebar and window decorations with VectorCraft
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
Resolves #881

### Context & Motivation
Following visual chrome inspection across the Craft application suite, application title bars and window chrome were inconsistent. Apps like VectorCraft and PhotoCraft feature an integrated undecorated app shell on Windows and Linux where the top chrome serves as the window titlebar (drag gesture, double-click maximize, code-drawn 46pt caption buttons, and edge/corner resize zones), while other apps exhibited native window manager decorations above their internal top bars.

Note on `craft-libs#2`:
As analyzed in storytold/craft-libs#2, that shared library effort is strictly targeted at headless cross-app domain logic (fonts, color math, PDF parsing, atomic IO, grammar) and **explicitly excludes application shells and window chrome**. Application chrome and decorations must therefore be standardized directly across the respective app repositories.

### Changes
- Implemented `CUSTOM_TITLEBAR` handling and `.with_decorations(!custom_titlebar)` in `apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs`.
- Added caption buttons (Minimize, Maximize/Restore, Close), drag area gesture, and invisible edge resize zones in `crates/ui-egui/src/titlebar.rs`.
- Connected caption buttons and window drag area into the top bar panel (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/topbar.rs`), offsetting right-hand icons to ensure clean alignment and spacing.
- Added design tokens for caption button close state to `Tokens` in `theme.rs`.
- Added and verified unit tests in `crates/ui-egui/src/tests_titlebar.rs`.

title: Decode Nikon High Efficiency NEF sensor data
author: chiefjawa
body:
Nikon High Efficiency NEFs currently open from the embedded JPEG. That leaves exposure and white-balance editing tied to a rendered preview instead of the sensor data.

This adds native 14-bit sensor decoding for the verified HE/HE★ profile. It uses the MIT-licensed, pure-Rust `oxideav-jpegxs` primitives with an original Nikon header, packet-layout and reconstruction adapter. Black/white levels come from the native sample domain. Unknown profiles still return a specific error and keep the preview fallback.

All sensor pixels match an independent decoder on two CC0 Z50 II fixtures (HE and HE★), a private Z50 II photo, and a public Z6 III HE★ photo. The Z6 III array also matches the photographer’s reference DNG at every pixel. Private photos are not included in this contribution.

Validation:
- 254 raw unit tests passed; 3 pre-existing tests ignored.
- Both SHA256-pinned Z50 II corpus regressions passed.
- Synthetic coverage includes raw GCLI, partial groups, multiple slices, TIFF byte order, native levels, rounding, truncation and randomized corruption.
- Headless app check passed: native NEF import (`previewOnly: null`), Edit view renders from raw data, and a +1 EV edit changes the rendered output. No window or GPU was used.
- Additional native Linux desktop check passed: imported the same private NEF, captured actual window frames without headless fallback, and exercised exposure editing through the app control channel.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 8 stages passed (fmt, clippy, HEIF, workspace tests, parity references, layers, assets, WASM).

`docs/nikon-he.md` records provenance, reproducible public fixtures, exact results and the supported profile. Other Nikon bodies/crop modes still need reference checks; this does not claim Lightroom color or rendering parity.

Refs #193.

title: Metadata: All Metadata shows the raw image's compression, Nikon's in words (#830)
author: vbasky
body:
The Compression row read IFD0, which in a TIFF-based raw describes the built-in preview — so every compressed NEF claimed "Uncompressed" (#830, seen on a Z 6II Lossless in #769).

- The TIFF group's Compression row now comes from the **main image IFD** — the same full-resolution NewSubfileType 0 CFA/LinearRaw IFD the raw decoder opens — so NEFs read "Nikon NEF (Huffman compressed)", DNGs "Deflate"/"Lossy JPEG"/etc, and Sony ARWs their codec. Non-raw TIFFs have no such IFD and keep their own row; plain files are untouched.
- Nikon files additionally get a **Maker note** group: NEF Compression is read from maker-note tag **0x0093** (not 0x0002 — that's ISO) through the existing `parse_makernote` (V1/V3 layouts) and spelled with the published Nikon value table — Lossless, Lossy (type 1/2), Packed 12/14 bits, High Efficiency (Z-series), Uncompressed (reduced to 12 bits) … — unknown values print as stored, and only NEFs get the row.

Tests build an NEF-shaped file with the existing TIFF writer and pin: compressed/uncompressed/high-efficiency combinations, the unknown-value fallback, the Sony (no-note) and plain-TIFF paths. meta/engine/raw/catalog suites, fmt, clippy and `cargo xtask layers` clean.

For the reporter's Z 6II: the row now reads "Nikon NEF (Huffman compressed)" with "NEF Compression: Lossless" under Maker note.

title: LR-VIEW-ZOOM: sharp 1:1 in Compare and Reference (zoom windows per pane)
author: cookingwithsimon
body:
Before: zooming Compare or Reference to 1:1 to check focus showed each photo's whole-frame render, at most 2,560 px, magnified. On a 24–33 MP raw that is a soft picture at about 40 % of the real pixels, so two frames could not be compared for sharpness. Detail and Before/After already had zoom windows (#323). Compare and Reference did not.

After: past what the whole-frame render holds, each pane of Compare (Select / Candidate) and Reference (Reference / Active) also renders the part on screen, cut from that photo's own pixels. It is drawn over the pane, as in the loupe. 1:1 through 8:1 are sharp on both sides. Fit views and Survey are unchanged: no extra render and no original decoded.

How:

`Slot::CompareRegion(pane)`: one window texture per pane. `panels/compare.rs` plans it with the loupe's own geometry (`window_frame_edge`, `region::window_for`, `WINDOW_RATIO`, `same_aspect`), asks for `Session::region_job`, and draws the tile at its place in the frame, clipped to the pane.
`MediaCache` now keeps up to `full_capacity` full-resolution originals instead of exactly one (default 1, LRU, still evicted by the memory budget). Compare and Reference set it to 2. Otherwise every window render on one side would evict the other side's original and decode it again on the next pan. Leaving those views sets it back to 1 and frees the window textures.
A pinch or two-finger scroll holds the windows there are until it has been quiet for `HOLD_SECS`, as in the loupe. In Reference view, a slider drag on the active photo keeps its last window rather than rendering the photo's full pixels on every tick, and a fresh one follows when the drag ends.
If a window's reads (spots, Auto Mask strokes) are too far apart for one render, the pane keeps its whole-frame render, as it did before.
Tests: `media::tests::full_size_originals_are_kept_up_to_the_capacity;` in `tests_preview_limit::in_the_loupe`, one window per pane at 1:1 cut from each photo's own pixels with both originals held, none …

title: Open Library recognises a Lightroom catalog and offers to import it (#891)
author: bitshiftza
body:
Fixes #891.

**Problem.** Choosing a Lightroom Classic catalog folder in **File ▸ Open Library…** (or `* Previews.lrdata`, `*.lrcat-data`, `Backups/`) closed the current library and created a new, empty LightCraft library inside Lightroom's folder. Choosing the `.lrcat` file itself closed the current library and then failed ("File exists"), leaving no library open.

**Now** the current library stays open and a dialog says *"This is a Lightroom catalog, not a LightCraft library. Import it into a LightCraft library instead?"*, with **Cancel** and **Import Lightroom Catalog…**, which starts the existing import of the catalog found (no file picker).

![The Lightroom Classic Catalog prompt over the current library](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bitshiftza/lightcraft/issue-assets/open-library-lrcat-891.png)

### How
- **Engine:** `lightroom_folder::lightroom_catalog_at` (new `crates/engine/src/lightroom_folder.rs`) recognises a Lightroom catalog from names only, never opening the catalog: a path named `*.lrcat` (any case) or its `-wal`, `-shm`, `-journal` and `.lock` files; a folder named `*.lrcat-data` or `*.lrdata` (`X Previews`, `Smart Previews`, `Helper`, `Sync.lrdata` point to `X.lrcat`, else the first `.lrcat` beside them); a folder with an `.lrcat` at its top level; `Backups/` next to one. The scan is top level only and capped at 10,000 entries; non-UTF-8 names are skipped and any I/O error counts as "not found", so the check never fails.
- **Precedence:** a folder holding `catalog.snap` or `catalog.log` is a LightCraft library and always opens as one, even with an `.lrcat` beside it.

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: decode Canon EOS R5 Mark II C-RAW (CRX QP-map first literal and escape)
author: ingolfteetz
body:
Fixes the R5 Mark II part of #832: many EOS R5 Mark II C-RAW files open as previews with `Canon CRX adaptive QP value -21087` (or another out-of-range value).

**Cause.** The CRX 0x200 QP map starts with its first symbol as a 32-bit literal. Every later symbol is Rice-coded with a limited-length escape: 23 zeros, the terminating 1, then the symbol in 8 bits. That is the ITU-T T.87 escape layout for a 32-bit limit and 8-bit symbols, without its −1 offset. Main treats any 16-zero prefix as an escape followed by a 16-bit literal. That reads the first symbol the same way, which is all the R8 and R7 maps need. R5 Mark II maps (QP 150–162), though, jump by up to 12 where the Rice parameter is 0. That gives 18- to 22-zero prefixes, which are ordinary symbols, and real escapes (symbols 23 and 24). No QP value outside the verified 131–167 table is involved.

**Tested with**
- 33,665 R5 Mark II C-RAW files from my library (version 0x200, 8480 × 5650; not shareable): every QP map decodes to the exact end of its entropy stream, QP 150–162. Both tracks of a 306-file sample do too; on main, 174 of those 306 (57 %) open as previews, all with out-of-range values and none at 168.
- One of them (`_A3A2841.CR3`, ISO 1000), fully decoded and rendered: it matches the camera's embedded 8192 × 5464 JPEG at 100 %, with no steps in the bottom rows. The Bayer planes are 2825 rows, odd at every wavelet level.
- raw.pixls.us 7881–7884 (R5 Mark II RAW, C-RAW, crop-mode RAW and crop-mode C-RAW; CC0, sha256 checked), added to the xtask corpus. Their hashes pin this decoder's sensor samples; no external decoder was run on them. These low-ISO files decode on main too, so the escape is covered by synthetic unit tests: an 18-zero prefix, a 23-zero escape and every truncation.
- The six oracle fixtures (M50, R100 and R8, RAW and C-RAW): hashes unchanged.
- Escapes appeared in 100 of 612 maps, always at Rice parameter 0. At a larger parameter they are assumed to use the same layout (unobserved).

**Wha…

title: Add Ctrl+Shift+O / Cmd+Shift+O to show all mask overlay regions at once

body:
## Summary

Add a keyboard shortcut (**Ctrl+Shift+O** on Windows/Linux, **Cmd+Shift+O** on macOS) and a UI toggle that shows **every mask's overlay region at once** — the coloured tint that marks each mask's area — instead of only the selected mask's region.

Scope clarification: LightCraft already applies every mask's **adjustments** to the photo (the masks stack), so this does **not** change how masks are evaluated or applied. What was missing is the **diagnostic overlay** — the coloured region indicator the Masking panel draws — being shown for all masks simultaneously. This change only affects that overlay display.

The overlay is drawn using the existing **mask-overlay colour / opacity / mode** setting (default red `[230, 30, 40]`), i.e. the same "overlay display" colour already used for a single mask — just painted for every visible mask at once.

- New `Overlay::AllMasks { view, color, opacity }` variant in `lightcraft_pipeline`. `visualize::apply` layers each visible mask's evaluated alpha in one tint (the current mask-overlay colour).

  - **GPU** (`gpu/src/render.rs`): reads the whole masks buffer back in a single GPU→CPU transfer and splits it on the CPU into one plane per visible mask (same `visible && !components.is_empty()` order the single-mask path uses), instead of one synchronous readback per mask.

title: Drafts keep the wide planes across a noise-reduction change (CPU NR drag)
author: emmertex
body:
## What
Draft renders keep the wide spatial planes (base, clarity, dehaze, chromaticity) across a noise-reduction change. The plan now also carries the scene-linear key without the NR settings; when a draft's image differs from the cached one only in NR, it reuses those wide blurs and recomputes only log luminance and the fine texture band. Full-quality renders never take this path.

## Why
An NR change invalidated the scene-linear stage and with it every spatial plane, so each tick of an NR slider drag on the CPU rebuilt all of them.

## Measurements
Draft NR drag, single thread: prepare 18.7 -> 7 ms (whole render ~135 -> ~125 ms CPU).

## How tested
- New unit test in `crates/pipeline/src/tests.rs` covering the NR-only reuse.
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-pipeline --lib`: 142 passed.

Sources: own design.

title: Camera database (camdb): per-model colour data with provenance
author: emmertex
body:
## What
- New crate `lightcraft-camdb`: per-model camera data with provenance — dual-illuminant colour/forward matrices, white-balance presets, black/white level overrides, and a `provenance` per entry (`native-dng`, `chart`, `manufacturer-doc`, `maker-note`, `spectral-sensitivities`, `estimated`). - `camera_preview::starting_colour` consults the database: measured entries come before the JPEG fit, spectral ones keep their place after it, level overrides always apply. Matrices go into the raw's DNG colour data so the input transform interpolates them by the white's temperature.

Gives camera colour data a reviewable home with provenance, so measured data can be contributed per model without Adobe DCP/converted-DNG data or GPL tables.

title: Export: Remove location info also covers Original and DNG formats
author: emmertex
body:
## What
With **Remove location info** checked, exporting as **Original** or **DNG** still leaked the location:
- the XMP sidecar (Original) and the DNG's embedded packet carried GPS, sublocation/city/state/country and the app's own location field;
- an Original export copies the file byte for byte, so GPS embedded in the original went out unchanged.

Now the sidecar/DNG packet is written without any location (`sidecar_packet_with(.., remove_location)`), and an Original export whose file embeds GPS is refused with an actionable error (export as JPEG, TIFF or DNG instead) rather than silently leaking it. A `removes_location` helper is the single decision point.

## Why
Privacy: the user explicitly asked to strip location and we were shipping it anyway.

## How tested
Two new engine tests: `remove_location_holds_for_original_and_dng_exports` and `remove_location_refuses_a_raw_that_embeds_gps` (`cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib location`, both pass). Full CI not run.

title: Content-aware Remove: inpaint crate (PatchMatch) and a Fill spot mode
author: emmertex
body:
## What
Content-aware Remove: a new L1 crate `lightcraft-inpaint` (multi-scale PatchMatch patch completion plus a membrane fill fallback) and a new `Fill` spot mode ("Content-Aware" button in the Remove panel; `spot.add {"mode":"fill"}`).

## Why
Heal/Clone/Remove copy from one source offset, which fails on larger or structured blemishes. Fill rebuilds the spot from patches of its surroundings, like Lightroom's Content-Aware Remove.

## How
- `crates/inpaint`: `complete()` (Wexler-style completion, NN field via PatchMatch, fixed-seed RNG, thread-count independent) and `membrane_fill()`. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, no-panic lint attributes; mismatched sizes return `None`/input unchanged.
- `pipeline/spots.rs`: Fill reads a 2-radius window around the stroke, completes it, then feathers/blends as usual; source offset ignored. Scale set by spot size so preview and export match.
- Engine: no auto source picked for Fill. UI button + i18n entries in all catalogs. Registered in `xtask/src/layers.rs` as L1.

## How tested
`cargo check` of the touched crates; `cargo test -p lightcraft-inpaint` (5 tests) and the pipeline Fill tests (structure rebuilt deterministically, preview vs export size match, hostile spots: NaN/inf/out-of-frame/zero size). Clippy `-D warnings` clean on the new crate. Engine test `a_content_aware_spot_has_no_source`. Full CI not run locally.

Sources: C. Barnes, E. Shechtman, A. Finkelstein, D. B. Goldman, *PatchMatch: A Randomized Correspondence Algorithm for Structural Image Editing*, SIGGRAPH 2009; Y. Wexler, E. Shechtman, M. Irani, *Space-Time Completion of Video*, PAMI 2007; P. Pérez, M. Gangnet, A. Blake, *Poisson Image Editing*, SIGGRAPH 2003 (membrane fill). Ported from PhotoCraft (MIT OR Apache-2.0, same organisation).

title: Perf: parallel preview builds and faster hue/saturation tables
author: emmertex
body:
## What
Two performance changes:

1. **Preview builds** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/previews.rs`): `library.buildPreviews` now renders photos in parallel lanes (as many as an export batch; two for 1:1 previews), renders the view first and reuses its decoded source for the thumbnail instead of decoding the file a second time. A panic in one photo counts as that photo's failure rather than aborting the build.
2. **Hue/saturation tables** (`crates/raw/src/profile.rs`): `HsvTable::apply` skips the linear → sRGB → linear round trip when the value scale is 1 (every hue/sat-only table, e.g. fitted camera looks) and reuses the sRGB-encoded value otherwise; hue wrapping uses a helper equal to `rem_euclid` bit for bit, without the `fmodf` call in the common range.

## Why / measurements
- 100 × 24 MP ARW, standard previews (loaded machine): 49.4 s → 38.4 s wall, CPU 3m28 → 2m49.
- 2048 px render of a 24 MP ARW, single thread: 16.4 → 15.1 G instructions, 4.94 → 4.76 G cycles.

## Equivalence
- `wrap_is_rem_euclid_bit_for_bit` sweeps both periods (6, 360) incl. ±0, boundaries, next_up/next_down, NaN/inf/huge.
- `unit_value_scale_with_srgb_values_keeps_the_value`: with a unit value scale the value now equals the input exactly; previously it differed only by the float round-off of the sRGB round trip (≤ ~1e-6 relative).

## How tested
`cargo test -p lightcraft-raw --lib` (250 passed) and `cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib preview` (56 passed). Full CI not run locally.

Sources: own design.

title: Soft proofing against printer ICC profiles: intent, Simulate Paper & Ink, device gamut warning
author: emmertex
body:
## What
Extends the existing soft proofing (standard spaces) to printer / paper ICC profiles:
- Soft Proofing's Profile menu gains **Other…** to pick an ICC profile (RGB or CMYK, matrix or LUT); `view.softProof` takes `profile` (path or null), `intent` (perceptual|relative) and `paperInk`.
- **Intent** (Perceptual / Relative) and **Simulate Paper & Ink** controls appear when a device profile is active.
- Destination gamut warning comes from the colorimetric round trip through the device profile.
- Proof copies are named after the profile.

## How
moxcms builds a 33³ proof table over the working space: forward with the chosen intent, back relative colorimetric. Simulate Paper & Ink renders absolute colorimetric (the profile's media white replaces screen white, ink black unscaled). The pipeline looks the table up by id (`Proof::profile`, `register_proof_profile`), so `Proof` stays `Copy` and render keys include it. Hostile/malformed profiles return errors.

## Testing
`cargo check` of ui-egui/codecs/pipeline; proof tests in codecs, pipeline and engine (incl. hostile-profile errors) pass. Locale strings added for all catalogs.

Sources: ICC.1:2022 (rendering intents, media white point, absolute colorimetric); own design for the proof table.

title: Windows uninstall: opt-in data cleanup and a confirmation, also from Settings → Apps (#892, #895)
author: HarrisXiu
body:
Fixes #892, fixes #895. The Local folder fix (#893) that this PR first carried is now #968.

## Uninstall: cleanup choices and a confirmation

Removing LightCraft opens a **Choose what to keep** page and ends on a page saying **LightCraft has been uninstalled**.

- Both cleanup choices are unchecked by default: *Clean settings, edits, library indexes and caches*, and below it *Also permanently delete photos copied into these libraries*. An ordinary or silent uninstall keeps all data.
- **Uninstall in Settings → Apps shows the same pages.** Windows uninstalls an MSI product's own Apps entry with a bare progress bar and no dialogs, so neither the choices nor the confirmation could ever show there. The package hides that entry (`ARPSYSTEMCOMPONENT`) and lists its own, whose `UninstallString` runs the package in maintenance mode (`MsiExec.exe /I{ProductCode} LIGHTCRAFTUNINSTALL=1`) and opens on the options page. `QuietUninstallString` stays a plain `/X … /qn`.
- The completion text is set after the wizard pages, where Remove is chosen, not before them.
- When the cleanup refuses (for example LightCraft still has the library open), Windows Installer rolls the uninstall back. Error 1722 says that LightCraft was not uninstalled, to close it and retry or uninstall without cleanup, and where the log is.

## The cleanup helper (`apps/lightcraft-uninstall`)

A small pure-Rust binary embedded in the MSI (not installed, not in the portable zip), run as the invoking user in a checked commit action. It deletes named catalog and settings files and recognized thumbnails and smart previews, never a whole library folder; refuses symlinks and junctions; checks every target and takes the library lock before the first deletion.

title: Tests: hold the MCP export-cancel test's export after its first photo until cancelled (#674)
author: ingolfteetz
body:
## Problem

`crates/mcp/tests/e2e.rs::export_progress_and_cancel` fails on machines with enough cores for four export lanes (#674). The 8 demo photos export inside the 100 ms progress throttle, so the first `progress > 0` notification is the final 8 of 8, and the cancel arrives after the export has finished. Here (macOS, Apple M5 Max, 18 cores) 3 of 3 runs on main failed at `e2e.rs:231` ("cancelled request must not reply"), with all 8 files in the reply.

## Fix

Test only, the "hold the export back" option from #674:

- `HoldAfterFirst`, a `Backend` wrapper around `Headless` used only by this test, holds the export at its first photo boundary. There it keeps calling the server's real progress hook, which answers pings and reads cancels, until the cancel is read or the test releases the hold. The hold is capped at 20 s, so a cancel that is never read fails the test instead of hanging it.
- The first export is released once the mid-batch ping is answered, since that check had the same race. The second export only ends by the cancel.
- With the timing gone, the check tightens from "1 to 7 files remain" to "exactly the one completed photo remains". That also shows the photos the other lanes had already rendered are never written. The other checks are unchanged: no reply to the cancelled request, every remaining file decodes, the unrelated file is untouched and the earlier export is kept.

## Testing

- On main 0ba118de: `cargo xtask ci` green (all 8 steps), and `export_progress_and_cancel` passes 20 of 20.
- Before the rebase, on 964d9338: the whole e2e suite passed 8 of 8 with all 18 cores busy (~1.4 s per run).
- Mutation check: with a cancel that suppresses the reply but doesn't stop the batch, the test fails with 8 files.

## Related

- Fixes #674 (the flaky test). As agreed there, @HarrisXiu took the test part out of #660, so the two no longer conflict, and @mrpdaemon will close #668 if this one is taken instead.
- @anarion80's point in #674, that the `done = 0` n…

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: a tone curve from black-and-white camera JPEGs (#577)
author: AlexChambers
body:
Fixes the black-and-white case in #577 (@jojo23-coder's report).

## What was wrong

A raw shot in a monochrome picture style (Canon Monochrome, Sony B/W, Nikon Monochrome) records full colour, but its camera JPEG is grey. The JPEG fit needs colour (`collect_pairs` wants 5% of the pixels coloured: a channel spread above 0.05, or above 0.005 with a camera profile), so neither the full look nor the partial look (#583) is fitted. The photo starts from the spectral matrices, or the neutral fallback, with LightCraft's default tone curve. On @jojo23-coder's Canon EOS RP files that is about 1.3 EV darker and flatter than the same body's photos shot in colour: ΔE76 12.0 against their own JPEGs, against 4.3 for the colour-shot files.

## Fix

The grey JPEG still shows the camera's tone curve. When no look was fitted and the camera JPEG is black and white, the tone curve is fitted alone, luminance against luminance, on top of the colour the photo would get anyway: the model's camera profile when there is one, else its spectral matrices, else the neutral fallback's.

- **Black and white** (`monochrome`): every pixel of the JPEG proxy but one in a thousand has its channels within 0.002 (linear) of each other. A sepia-toned JPEG has colour, so it isn't one. The check reads pixels, not the picture style, so a colour JPEG of a scene that colourless counts too; such a photo gets no look today either.
- **Fit:** the quantile tone curve (`fit_tone`, as in the partial look). The chroma curve stays neutral, since the JPEG has no colourfulness to learn from.
- **Checks:** the partial look's: the JPEG has to rank the pixels like the scene (Spearman ≥ 0.5), and the curve has to cut the held-out squared luminance error below 0.7 of the default curve's, in linear and gamma-encoded values, on all pixels or away from edges. Clipped sensor pixels are left out, and Sony's DRO is handled as for colour JPEGs. The rank correlation here gives tied values their mean rank and is 0 when either side ha…

title: UI: dialogs fit the screen: fixed header and footer, scrolling body

## Problem
Users report the Export dialog is taller than the screen: on a 1366×768 laptop its Cancel / OK buttons are off screen and the dialog can't scroll. Any dialog with enough content (Settings tabs, All Metadata, What's New) has the same problem.

One reusable helper, `crates/ui-egui/src/dialog_frame.rs` (`ModalLayout`), gives every modal dialog three parts:

title: Dropping photos with XMP sidecars no longer imports the sidecars as presets (#936)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #936.

Dropping files on the window sent every `.xmp` to `file.importPresets`, so photos dropped together with their sidecars (for example from Photo Mechanic) each added a preset.

The drop handler now uses `split_presets`. An `.xmp` that sits in the same folder as a dropped photo of the same name (`IMG_1.xmp` or `IMG_1.CR2.xmp` next to `IMG_1.CR2`, case-insensitive) is treated as that photo's sidecar. It is not imported as a preset, and the photo import still reads it as before. An `.xmp` dropped without a matching photo (a real XMP preset) is imported as a preset, as before. Other preset formats are unchanged.

- `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`: `split_presets` replaces the `partition(is_preset_file)` in the window drop handler. This is the only place where dropped files go to the preset importer. The browser build sends dropped files only to `library.import`.
- `docs/parity-checklist.md` (LR-IMP-PROFILES): notes that drag & drop leaves sidecars out.
- Test `photo_sidecars_are_not_presets`: stem and full-name sidecars, an upper-case `.XMP`, a preset beside the photos, and a same-named `.xmp` in another folder (still a preset).

title: Improve RAW starting detail and Nikon tone with versioned processing
author: chiefjawa
body:
Nikon RAW files can decode correctly and still start with weak detail, visible colour noise and a flat tone. Reset also dropped RAW capture defaults, while Sharpening Radius and Detail were stored without affecting the render. This adds versioned processing to improve that starting point and keeps presets as ordinary editable adjustments.

This draft depends on #896. Its decoder commit is currently included in the branch; the rendering work is the three commits after it: [review the quality changes](https://github.com/chiefjawa/lightcraft/compare/7ddbd11ca840fd25855ee2b04565a9bfb2b7b99c...02267cf). The decoder PR remains separate.

Changes:

- V2 separates fine sharpening from Texture, makes Radius and Detail effective, and strengthens colour-noise reduction at low Amount values.
- V3 adds noise-aware luminance reduction with matching CPU/GPU implementations. A bounded whole-source estimate keeps the strength consistent when rendering different windows. New RAW imports start at luminance Amount 25.
- V4 refines the tone of accepted Nikon camera-JPEG fits at a fixed proxy size. It retains the original colour model and accepts the new curve only when held-out matched regions show an improvement. Smart previews store both curves.
- Reset restores current RAW defaults and as-shot white balance, or the recorded import preset. Saved edits keep their process; applying a preset preserves the receiving photo's process.

Validation on this branch:

- `cargo xtask ci`: all eight stages passed, including workspace tests, Clippy, assets and WASM.
- All 17 actual-GPU equivalence tests passed, covering the supported processes, detail controls, white balance and render windows.

title: Library: create folders on disk and move photos between folders
author: emmertex
body:
Part of #765

## What
- **`folder.create {parent, name}`**: creates a folder on disk. One undo step: undo removes it again (only while it is empty; a folder with anything in it is never removed), redo creates it again. A taken name, a missing parent or a name with slashes is refused.

title: Fix/exif histogram overlap
author: squareSphere29
body:
Fixes #913 - EXIF values under histogram run together

The histogram's EXIF strip previously rendered 4 fixed-position items (ISO,

title: Fix #812: the window's renderer can't kill the start-up (DX12 shader errors)
author: emmertex
body:
Fixes #812

## Problem
On some Windows machines FXC fails to compile egui's own shaders on DX12 ("Shader translation error ... The parameter is incorrect. (0x80070057)" in `egui_pipeline`). wgpu's default uncaptured-error handler panics, so the app dies at startup. `WGPU_BACKEND=vulkan` works around it.

## Design
- **Probe before the window opens** (`apps/lightcraft/src/window_gpu.rs`): each renderer in order DX12 → Vulkan → GL → glow (eframe's OpenGL renderer) creates a device and builds egui's pipeline inside wgpu error scopes, with a logging error handler instead of the panicking default. A failing one is logged and skipped; the user gets a notice naming the renderer in use.
- **Remembered renderer**: the one that worked is stored in the settings folder (`window-renderer`) and tried first next time.
- **Failed-start marker + bounded relaunch**: a start that dies before the window is up leaves `window-init.marker`; the app relaunches itself (at most 4 times, `LIGHTCRAFT_WINDOW_RETRY`) and tries that renderer last. `run_native` is also wrapped in `catch_unwind` so an escaped panic becomes an ordinary failed start.
- **`LIGHTCRAFT_GPU_BACKEND=dx12|vulkan|gl|glow`** (or `WGPU_BACKEND`) forces one; `glow` leaves compute on its default.
- **Why DX12 stays first**: with Vulkan loaded, a broken Vulkan driver can crash the process uncatchably (#136), so Vulkan is only touched after DX12 failed.
- Ordering logic is pure (`lightcraft_gpu::backend::window_renderer_order`, `WindowRenderer`, `forced_window_renderer`) and unit-tested. eframe's `glow` feature is enabled (so `on_exit` takes the `glow::Context` argument); `pollster` drives the probe.

Docs: `docs/gpu-pipeline.md`.

## Testing
- `cargo clippy -p lightcraft -p lightcraft-gpu --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- new tests `window_renderer_fallback_order`, `window_renderer_names_round_trip`; existing `lightcraft` tests pass
- `cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu -p lightcraft`

Not yet verified on an affected Windo…

author: cookingwithsimon

Before: Photo ▸ Edit in External Editor (⇧⌘E) rendered a 16-bit TIFF copy and opened it in whatever program was typed into Settings, or the system default. It was not on the photo's right-click menu, and to use PhotoCraft you had to type its path. PhotoCraft's File ▸ Save writes back only to PSD, PSB or .pcraft, so on the TIFF it opened Save As, and the copy in LightCraft never changed unless you saved over it by hand.

After: right-click a photo (grid, filmstrip, Detail, Compare) ▸ Edit In ▸ Edit in PhotoCraft, or Photo ▸ Edit In (⇧⌘E). LightCraft renders a copy with the photo's edits, stacks it on the original, and opens it in PhotoCraft. LightCraft finds PhotoCraft itself. title: LRC-LIB-CATALOG-IMPORT: describe raws from their headers without reading pixel data (step 1 of #832)
author: ingolfteetz
body:
## What this does

Step 1 of the two proposed in #832: a self-contained building block, no behaviour change yet.

`lightcraft_raw::sparse::header_plan(bytes, loaded)` says which byte ranges of a raw file `probe_info` and `lightcraft_meta::extract` read. It is asked about a buffer of the file's full length in which only the ranges in `loaded` hold the file's bytes (the rest is zeros). The caller loads the ranges it names and asks again; once it answers `Ready`, probing the buffer gives what probing the whole file gives. `preview_plan` also covers what `embedded_preview` reads, for raws shown from their embedded preview.

Nothing calls it yet. Step 2, the batched catalog import from #832, will probe originals with it, and #755's preview loader could use `preview_plan`.

## What is left out

Only bulk sample data:

- **TIFF raws** (DNG, CR2, ARW, SRW, CFA TIFF): the strips and tiles of each image of 256 KiB or more, keeping the first 64 KiB of its first chunk, where the lossless-JPEG / JPEG XL frame headers the header probe validates sit. An older CR2's raw IFD without image tags is located through its strip tags. **RW2**: from `RawDataOffset` to the end.
- **CR3**: everything except `moov`, the XMP `uuid` box, the first sample of each CTMD track (the as-shot white balance lives there) and the main raw track's CRX headers and QP maps (`crx::header_ranges`: the bytes `crx::validate` reads).

- **NEF, ORF, PEF** (their header probe reads samples) and anything not recognised: `Whole`. So is a structure that is incomplete, inconsistent, or keeps IFD tables or out-of-line values inside sample data. The plan never guesses.

The TIFF IFD walk mirrors `lightcraft_tiff`'s reader (chain, SubIFDs, Exif, GPS, Interop, same bounds) and asks for every IFD table and for the values that locate IFDs and chunks. The CR3 box walk mirrors `parse_cr3`.

title: Rotate left/right turns the crop with the image instead of cutting it (#962)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #962.

**Cause.** `photo.rotateLeft` / `photo.rotateRight` (`rotate()` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/library.rs`) changed only `orientation`. The crop rectangle is stored normalized in the *oriented* frame (`CropGeometry::rect`), so after a quarter turn it kept the old width and height. A crop that was tall on the upright photo ended up tall on the now wide photo and cut most of it away, which is what the screenshots in the issue show. Turning back did not fix it either: the crop had been carried along unchanged, not turned.

**Fix.** `rotate()` now maps the crop rectangle through the same quarter turn with `Orientation::map_norm_rect`, the helper face regions already use (`face_job`), and swaps a locked crop aspect (w, h) → (h, w), as `crop.rotateAspect` does. The straighten angle stays as it is: it is a rotation about the image centre, so a quarter turn of the whole frame does not change it. Flips are applied to the output after the crop, so the rectangle (stored before the flips) needs no flip handling.

Every way to rotate (menu, Cmd+[ / Cmd+], grid and right-panel buttons, control channel, MCP) runs these two commands, so all of them are covered.

**Test.** `rotate_carries_the_crop_with_the_image` (`crates/engine/src/tests.rs`): crops the left half with a locked 2:3 aspect, rotates right, and checks that the crop is now the top half and the aspect is 3:2. It then rotates left and checks that the original crop and aspect come back. Without the fix the crop stays as the left half and the test fails.

title: ci: refactor workflows to use storytold/craft-common-actions
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Summary
Refactors repetitive CI/CD workflows across LightCraft to call centralized reusable workflows and composite actions hosted in the organization repository [`storytold/craft-common-actions`](https://github.com/storytold/craft-common-actions).

### Design Decisions
- **Hosted in Organization Repository**: Workflows live under `storytold/craft-common-actions` (no personal fork/repository).
- **Intentionally Tracks `@main` (Not SHA Pinned)**: Callers deliberately track `@main` with an inline explanation comment so that org-wide CI improvements, security fixes, and build optimizations propagate across all 13+ craftapps automatically without requiring individual PR churn in every repository.
- **Explicit Secrets**: Only the exact required signing secrets are passed explicitly (`secrets: inherit` is avoided).
- **Node 24 Runtimes**: All composite and third-party actions inside `storytold/craft-common-actions` are updated to Node 24 (and pinned internally to immutable commit SHAs), eliminating Node 20 deprecation warnings.
- **Strict Verification**: Build utilities like `nfpm`, `actionlint`, and `trunk` are verified against SHA256 checksums.
- Preserves 100% of existing packaging, release matrix, and linting semantics for LightCraft.

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: recheck stale preview-only raws when a library opens (#662)
author: valenfys
body:
Fixes #662.
Fixes #473.
Fixes #556 (the colour noise reported later in that thread is tracked in #840).

Also covers the original reports in two issues that stay open for problems raised later in their threads, which this PR doesn't touch:
- #314: RW2s left preview-only after an update. It stays open for the lens distortion and vignetting reported later.
- #681: compressed RAFs left preview-only after updating to 0.5.0. It stays open for the Highlights slider, banding and HEIF reports.

## Problem
A raw imported while its format or variant couldn't be decoded is stored with `preview_only` set. Nothing re-reads its file later except a manual **Reload from Disk**, and nothing tells the user it's needed. So when a release adds a decoder, photos already in the library stay preview-only. That's what #556, #473, #314 and the Pixel 8 Pro JPEG XL DNG case in the issue all ran into.

## Fix
This follows the design agreed in the issue: each flag carries an app-version stamp, not a hand-bumped `DECODER_VERSION` constant.

**Catalog (format v8 → v9)**
- v9 because #730 took v7 for Kelvin white balance (`Op::SetAsShotWb`) and the History cursor change took v8 (`Op::SetHistoryCursor`).
- ⚠️ **Format number clash with #800**, which now also adds format 9 (compact records) and replaces the format table with a `FORMATS` list. Whichever PR merges second has to renumber to 10, or two different formats would both be v9. If #800 lands first, I'll rebase this onto its `FORMATS` list as row 10. Its guard test treats a row whose `adds` mentions "`Op::`" as adding an op, so this row will be worded as a field on an existing op (`SetContent`'s `preview_checked`), not as a new op.
- `Photo::preview_checked` holds the app version (`CARGO_PKG_VERSION`) that set `preview_only`. It's empty when the flag isn't set.
- `Op::SetContent` carries the stamp too, and undo swaps it back.
- Older catalogs read an empty stamp, so every existing preview-only photo is rechecked once.
- A photo counts as stale …

title: Sort ties by file name, then id
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Split out of #641 as asked there. Part of #294.

When photos tie on the sort key, they now sort by file name and then id, instead of by id (import order). This covers:

title: Improve RAW normalization, native lens corrections and mask integrity
author: grlessa
body:
RAW source scaling, lens availability and asynchronous mask handling could produce inconsistent edits: DNG planes shared a mean black denominator, Canon files never reached the pooled calibration CLI, many lenses had no automatic correction provider, and a mask result could arrive after the photo geometry changed.

This contribution addresses those paths with original Rust code, using RawTherapee and darktable as architectural references without incorporating their implementation. It adds a separately licensed, pinned Lensfun data provider rather than a C/C++ dependency.

### Changes

- Resolve camera/mount/complete lens names against 1,039 camera records and 1,540 rectilinear calibration sets. title: Vignette: distinct styles join process V2 (#905)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
The Paint branch of a darkening vignette computed `c * (1 - (-amount) * t)`, which is the same multiply the Color branch does, so Paint and Color gave identical pixels. A lightening vignette (amount > 0) ignored the style altogether. Both the CPU path (`finish.rs`) and the shader (`finish.wgsl`) had this.

Fixing it changes how existing edits look (Highlight is the default style, so every lightening vignette would change), and docs/process-versions.md says such a change ships as a new process. Main already has an unreleased `Process::V2` (the Highlights/Shadows detail change from #632, not in any tag yet; the latest release is v0.6.0), so this goes into that same V2 rather than adding a V3. New photos and Reset get V2. Photos already edited stay on V1 and look exactly as before until someone runs Photo ▸ Update to Current Process. That command and its menu item were already generic over processes, so nothing in the UI needed changing.

What the styles do under V2, following Lightroom's descriptions:

- Paint, darkening: same brightness drop as Color, but the corners are also mixed towards grey by the same amount, so they lose colour as well as light.
- Paint, lightening: unchanged, a flat blend towards white.
- Color, lightening: an exposure-like gain (up to +2 stops at +100) on luminance, rolled off so white stays white. Hue and saturation are kept.
- Highlight, lightening: the same gain per channel, so bright colours drift towards white.
- Color and Highlight darkening are unchanged. Highlight with Highlights at 0 still matches Color, as in Lightroom.

Blending towards black in linear light is always a plain multiply, so Paint darkening can't differ from Color by brightness alone. The desaturation is my reading of Lightroom's "flat" Paint look. It is a judgement call and easy to change.

title: fix(meta): reject impossible EXIF and XMP capture dates
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

LightCraft accepts invalid capture dates from EXIF and XMP metadata.

The datetime validator checks whether a day falls between 1 and 31 but does not account for the actual number of days in each month.

Consequently, dates such as February 30 or April 31 can enter photo metadata and later be silently normalized during date calculations.

## Root cause

`DateTime::valid()` checks numeric ranges without validating the complete Gregorian calendar date.

## Changes

- Validate day ranges against the corresponding month.
- Apply Gregorian leap-year rules, including century exceptions.
- Reject impossible calendar dates before they enter capture metadata.
- Preserve support for valid leap-day timestamps.

## Regression coverage

Added tests covering:

- February 29 in leap and non-leap years.
- February 30 and April 31.
- Century leap-year rules for 1900 and 2000.
- Zero-day rejection.
- Valid EXIF and ISO 8601 timestamps.

## Validation

- Confirmed the source-level defect.
- Reviewed the committed diff against upstream.
- Added regression tests; execution remains pending.
- Not run: cargo test -p lightcraft-meta
- Not run: cargo xtask ci

No public issue.

title: fix(geom): reject non-finite perspective and affine transforms
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Invalid transformation matrices can produce NaN or infinite coefficients that propagate into image geometry operations.

The existing singularity checks do not reject non-finite determinants, allowing inverse operations to return invalid transformations.

These transformations can affect perspective correction, image warping, and panorama alignment.

## Root cause

Affine and homography inversions rely on determinant magnitude checks.

For NaN determinants, the comparison against the singularity threshold evaluates to false.

The perspective solver also lacks complete validation of input coordinates and calculated coefficients.

## Changes

- Reject non-finite determinants during affine and homography inversion.
- Verify that calculated inverse coefficients are finite.
- Reject non-finite source and destination coordinates in perspective solving.
- Reject non-finite pivot values during elimination.
- Verify that the solved homography contains only finite coefficients.
- Preserve existing behavior for valid transformations.

## Regression coverage

Added tests covering:

- NaN and infinite affine matrices.
- NaN and infinite homography matrices.
- Invalid source and destination coordinates.
- Successful inversion of a valid identity matrix.

## Validation

- Confirmed the invalid determinant and coefficient paths in source.
- Reviewed both modified geometry files.
- Added regression tests; execution remains pending.
- Not run: cargo test -p lightcraft-geom
- Not run: cargo xtask ci

No public issue.

title: fix(meta): reject truncated and mismatched GPX files
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

LightCraft's GPX parser can accept incomplete or structurally invalid XML documents.

A truncated GPS track containing valid points may be treated as a successfully parsed track, even when enclosing elements were never closed.

Mismatched closing tags can also interfere with the parser's element tracking.

## Root cause

The GPX reader explicitly disables XML closing-tag validation.

Additionally, reaching the end of the document does not verify that all opened elements have been closed.

## Changes

- Enable XML closing-tag validation.
- Reject documents containing mismatched closing tags.
- Reject incomplete documents with unclosed elements.
- Return an actionable parsing error rather than accepting incomplete track data.
- Preserve the existing handling of valid GPX 1.0 and 1.1 documents.

## Regression coverage

Added tests for:

- Truncated GPX documents containing valid timed points.
- Mismatched closing tags.
- The existing malformed-input handling.

## Validation

- Confirmed both parsing defects in source.
- Reviewed the committed changes.
- Added regression tests; execution remains pending.
- Not run: cargo test -p lightcraft-meta
- Not run: cargo xtask ci

No public issue.

title: Fix macOS build: menu-bar Quit no longer calls eframe's on_exit
author: mattsivak
body:
**Problem:** the desktop app doesn't compile on macOS on current `main`:

```
error[E0061]: this function takes 2 arguments but 1 argument was supplied
  --> apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs:67:13
   |     eframe::App::on_exit(self);
```

The macOS menu-bar Quit path (`#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]`, from PR #444) calls `eframe::App::on_exit(self)`. The app enables eframe's `glow` feature, and with it `on_exit` takes `Option<&glow::Context>` as well. CI doesn't build macOS, so nobody noticed.

**Fix:** the body of `on_exit` moves into `App::save_and_shut_down` (save settings, close the library, wait for background work). `on_exit` and the Quit path both call it, so the Quit path no longer depends on eframe's trait signature. Behaviour is unchanged.

Those are outside this change.
