title: Export: "Same folder as original photo" destination (#956)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #956

The Export dialog could only write a batch into one fixed folder (plus an optional subfolder). Exporting next to the originals meant re-pointing the Folder field every time you switched source folders, and a batch spanning several folders couldn't do it at all.

The dialog now has an "Export to" choice, as in Lightroom Classic: Specific folder (the old behaviour, still the default) or Same folder as original photo. In the second mode each photo goes into the folder its original is in, with the Subfolder appended if one is set (e.g. `<photo's folder>/Exports`). The Folder field is hidden in that mode.

- It's an export option, `destinationMode: "specificFolder" | "sameAsOriginal"`, so `app.export` takes it from the app, the control channel, the headless MCP backend and the MCP `export` tool. It's validated like the other params, and it gets saved in export presets and in Export with Previous along with the rest of the options.
- The folder is worked out per photo when the file is placed, so the "If file exists" policy (number / overwrite / skip) and the never-overwrite-an-original guard apply in each folder the same way they do for a fixed folder.
- If a photo has no folder on disk (a demo photo, or a photo in the web build's browser storage) or its folder is gone (moved, drive unplugged), that photo gets an error naming it. Nothing is written anywhere else. A foreground export stops on that error, and a background one records it for that photo and carries on. On the web build the choice is hidden because it can never work there.
- With this mode on, `app.export` no longer needs a `dir`, so the "Choose an export folder first" check is skipped. An exact `path` (single photo) still wins over either mode.

Docs: whats-new entry, the LR-EXP-LOCATION row and its revision history in the parity checklist, the control-protocol `app.export` row, and the MCP tool schema and param string.

title: Issue #989: clippy 1.99, fill_box reads its buffer with as_chunks::<3>() (item 4)
author: snofla
body:
Part of #989 (item 4 only; this PR does not close the issue).

`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` on rustc 1.99.0 stops at `crates/pipeline/src/spots.rs:250` with `clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` ("using `chunks_exact` with a constant chunk size"). The line came in with `fe6d7b01` (Content-aware Remove). The fix reads the flat buffer with `as_chunks::<3>()`, as #414 did for 1.98:

```rust
let (pixels, _) = out.as_chunks::<3>();
for (d, v) in src.iter_mut().zip(pixels) {
    *d = *v;
}
```

## Checked

- **Same behaviour:** `as_chunks::<3>()` yields the same elements as `chunks_exact(3)` and ignores the same remainder. Compared on buffer lengths 0-9 in a scratch file, including lengths that are not a multiple of 3.
- **Tests:** the 13 `spots` tests in `lightcraft-pipeline` pass, including `fill_rebuilds_structure_deterministically` and `fill_matches_between_preview_and_export_size`, which run `fill_box`.
- **Lint gone:** `cargo clippy --workspace --exclude lightcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings` exits 0 (rustc 1.99.0, macOS, Apple silicon). `cargo fmt --all --check` is clean. It is the only constant-size `chunks_exact` in the workspace.

## Not in this PR

- The full-workspace clippy still fails on the desktop app (`apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs:67`, `eframe::App::on_exit(self)` takes two arguments in eframe 0.36.2): items 1-2 of #989, PR #990.
- Item 3 of #989 (eleven engine tests fail on macOS) is untouched.
- So `cargo xtask ci` still cannot pass on this toolchain until #990 or an equivalent lands; I did not run the `test` and `wasm` steps.

title: Alt/Option-drag previews for clipping and sharpening (#937)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Holding Alt (Option on macOS) while dragging Blacks, Whites or the Sharpening sliders did nothing; the photo stayed as it was. Lightroom shows a temporary diagnostic view instead.

Now, with Alt held before or during a drag in the Edit panel:

- Exposure, Highlights, Whites: highlight clipping. Black image, white where all three channels clip, the clipped channels' colour where only some do.
- Shadows, Blacks: shadow clipping. White image, black where all three channels clip, the remaining channels' colour where only some do.
- Sharpening Amount: greyscale.
- Sharpening Radius / Detail: the fine detail band that sharpening amplifies, as grey plus or minus.
- Sharpening Masking: the mask, white where sharpening applies.

Releasing Alt or the slider brings the photo back. The edit, history and exports don't change.

How it works: these are new `Overlay` variants in `crates/pipeline/src/visualize.rs`, next to Visualize Spots and the mask overlay. Both renderers draw them on the finished 8-bit image. The clipping and greyscale views work per pixel. The sharpening views use each renderer's own log-luminance and texture-blur planes (the GPU reads its planes back, the same way it already handles hidden mask overlays). The Masking weight is now one shared function (`finish::sharpen_mask_weight`), so the preview and the CPU render can't drift apart. The UI checks `modifiers.alt` every frame, so pressing or releasing it mid-drag switches right away. The control-to-preview mapping (`Overlay::for_control`) lives in the pipeline, below the UI layer.

While doing this I found that Sharpening Radius and Detail aren't used by either renderer: they're saved and round-trip through XMP, but they don't change the image. Their preview therefore stays the same while you drag them. I moved LR-EDIT-DETAIL-SHARPEN to 🟡 in the parity checklist with a note. Making them actually work is a separate change.

title: Choose the thumbnail cache folder per library, like smart previews (#903)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #903

The thumbnail cache always went to `<library>/thumbs`. If the library sits on a network share or a slow disk, the grid waits on that drive and the cache uses space there. Smart previews already have their own folder setting per library. The thumbnail cache now gets the same one.

Settings > Performance > Thumbnail cache now has a Folder row and Choose Folder... / Use Library Folder buttons, right under the size limit and the In use row. They call a new command, `library.thumbnailCacheLocation {path?, reset?, existing?: move|leave|discard}`. With no arguments it returns `{path, default, custom, available, count, bytes}`. It follows the rules `library.smartPreviewsLocation` already has:

- The setting is stored in the library's prefs.json (`thumbsDir`). Leaving it out means `<library>/thumbs`, as before.
- The path has to be absolute. The folder has to exist, or its parent has to exist, and it has to accept a test write before anything changes (the same `check_writable` smart previews use).
- If thumbnails are already cached in the old folder, the command wants a choice: move them, leave them or delete them. The UI shows the same Move / Leave / Delete choice as smart previews. Nothing is deleted unless you pick Delete, and the new folder fills up as the grid renders.
- If the chosen folder is missing when the library opens, you get a library warning and Settings shows the path in red. Thumbnails then stay in memory only, and the folder is never created again.

That last point needed a change in `lightcraft-preview`. `DiskCache::put` used `create_dir_all`, so a cache folder on an unplugged drive would have been recreated on the system drive. Now it only creates the shard folder, plus the cache folder itself when its parent exists. A cache built with `DiskCache::chosen` never creates its folder. The default `<library>/thumbs` still gets created on first write, as before.

The smart previews hint used to say "The thumbnail cache stays in the library." I remov…

title: Issue #989: odd_folders_never_fail_the_check skips non-UTF-8 names on APFS (item 3, one of eleven)
author: snofla
body:
Part of #989 (item 3, one of its eleven tests; this PR does not close the issue).

`tests_lightroom_folder::odd_folders_never_fail_the_check` creates folders whose names are not valid UTF-8. APFS refuses such names (`EILSEQ`, os error 92), so on macOS `create_dir_all(&bad).unwrap()` panics at `crates/engine/src/tests_lightroom_folder.rs:159` before any assertion about the product runs.

## The change (test only, one file)

The test probes once with a `\xff` folder. Where the file system refuses it, the two non-UTF-8 cases (a folder named `caf\xe9 Previews.lrdata`, and a `\xff.lrcat` entry) are skipped, and the catalog-folder and symlink cases still run on a plain-named folder. Where the probe succeeds (Linux, FreeBSD) the test is unchanged apart from creating and removing the probe folder.

## Checked

On macOS (case-insensitive APFS, rustc 1.99.0, Apple silicon):

- `cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --release -- tests_lightroom_folder`: 5 passed, including `odd_folders_never_fail_the_check` (it failed before). This also shows the symlink assertions hold on APFS.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` is clean; `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean (run with `-A clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks`, the lint from item 4, because this branch is cut from `main` before #997).
- Not run here: the non-UTF-8 branch of the test on a file system that accepts such names. It is the original code path, unchanged.

## Not in this PR

- The ten sidecar repair tests of item 3. On a case-insensitive volume the production code renames `a.XMP`, while the tests' fault injectors compare exact paths and never fire. That needs its own change.
- Items 1, 2 and 4 of #989 (PR #990 / #994, and #997).

title: Issue #989: the ten sidecar repair tests also pass on a case-insensitive volume (item 3, ten of eleven)
author: snofla
body:
Part of #989 (item 3, ten of its eleven tests; this PR does not close the issue). Test code only: production code is not touched.

## Why the ten sidecar repair tests fail on macOS

They were written for a case-sensitive disk. `sidecars()` in `crates/engine/src/rename.rs` offers both `.XMP` and `.xmp` for each naming convention and keeps the candidates that exist. On case-insensitive APFS `a.XMP` "exists" for a file stored as `a.xmp`, so the code moves `a.XMP`, while the tests' fault injectors (`Faults` in `tests_repair_companions.rs` and `tests_repair_provenance.rs`, `PartialRename` in `tests_repair_saves.rs`) compare paths exactly with the lowercase one. The injected failure never fires, and the rename the tests expect to be refused succeeds (`assertion failed: ... .is_err()`).

This is a test-environment difference, but it also exposes a product quirk: on such a volume Rename Photos turns `a.xmp` into `Trip.XMP`. That is filed separately as #1006 and is not changed here.

## The change

In `crates/engine/src/tests_xmp.rs`, three small helpers:

- `same_path_or_file(a, b)`: equal paths, or the same file by identity (`RealFs.same_file`). The three fault injectors use it, so an injected failure fires whichever spelling the code under test uses. On a case-sensitive volume only identical paths match.
- `same_path_for_volume(a, b)`: equal, or equal ignoring ASCII case on a case-insensitive volume. Two assertions in `queued_stem_retry_preserves_shared_packet_after_batch_rollback` that compared an exact spelling use it.
- `case_insensitive(dir)`: whether `dir`'s upper-cased path still resolves. `autowrite_repairs_partial_rename_before_merging_foreign_xmp_across_library_switch` asserted that the lowercase packet is absent; on a case-insensitive volume both spellings are one file, so that assertion is skipped there.

## Checked

macOS, rustc 1.99.0, Apple silicon:

- **Case-insensitive APFS (the default):** the ten tests failed before and pass now.
- **Case-sensitive APFS*…

title: LR-VIEW-ZOOM: slider drags stay sharp where the GPU keeps up (#330)
author: mattsivak
body:
Fixes #330.

**Problem:** while a slider is dragged, the loupe renders the whole frame at 0.6 of its size (a bare `0.6` in `panels/detail.rs`). At Fit, that is all you see, so the photo goes soft while dragging and sharpens on release. Detail and sharpening adjustments are hard to judge. On a GPU this draft isn't needed: a canvas-sized draft takes a few ms there.

**Fix:**
- `region::DragScale` picks the draft size when a drag starts.
  - **Full size** when the GPU draws the view and no earlier drag of the same control on this photo went over the 16 ms slider budget at full size.
  - **0.6** otherwise.
- **What a draft's time counts:** its render plus the CPU time of the frame that uploaded and showed it. That frame time comes from eframe's `cpu_usage` (painting included), passed through as `Perf::host_frame_ms`.
  - The first draft is left out (it rebuilds stage caches) and the median decides.
  - Render times alone hide the texture upload. On the 1:1 benchmark below they said 231 of 234 drafts fit 16 ms, while no complete update did.
  - The check catches what the GPU rule alone can't see: LUT profiles or refined masks that fall back to the CPU per render, photos past a GPU limit, slow GPUs.
- **Mid-drag fallback:** the size stays put for the whole drag, so the resolution doesn't jump, with one exception. If full-size drafts take more than twice the budget, the drag drops to 0.6 after three of them. A refined-mask drag no longer runs at about 190 ms a step until release.
- **Zoomed in:** when a zoom window covers the view, the hidden whole-frame draft stays at 0.6. It only feeds the histogram and stands in where the window has no pixels yet. These drags aren't timed, because the frame time there is the window's upload.
- **Pixel conversion:** render workers now build the texture pixels (`ColorImage`) instead of the UI thread.
- `lightcraft_gpu::handles(depth, proofed, overlay)` is the one rule for which renders the GPU draws at all. `try_render` returns `NotTried`…

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: bundled Sony ILCA-99M2 camera profile
author: PiMinusMax
body:
Adds a bundled ILCA-99M2 (Sony α99 II) camera colour profile, fitted with `lightcraft-cli calibrate` the same way as the ILCE-7CR, ILCE-7M4, X-H2S and X-T4 profiles. Part of LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR.

**Why:** on this body the per-file fit is accepted on all of my photos, but it is fitted to one photo's colours at a time. A profile pooled from 144 photos brings 25 of 30 withheld photos closer to the camera JPEG, and none moves away by more than 0.24 ΔE.

**Data:** 150 of my own ILCA-99M2 ARWs from seven shooting days, all Standard creative style, DRO Auto, ISO 100–1600, compressed ARW, with no in-camera distortion correction. Lenses: Zeiss 24–70 mm F2.8 and 85 mm F1.4, plus Tamron and Sigma lenses. 144 were usable, giving 501,511 colour pairs. The other six, from one dark and nearly colourless indoor series, gave no usable pairs. The profile holds aggregate colour statistics only, no image content. It's licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0 and listed in `assets/ATTRIBUTION.md`.

title: LR-IMP-PREVIEW-READ: a CR3 or a TIFF raw's preview is read from the plan's ranges
author: lzjtugjc
body:
## What this does

Follow-up to #755 (merged in batch 31 as `e4a248c9`), which reads a Fuji RAF's preview from its
header. That path answers only when the pointer is in the file's first bytes: a **Canon CR3** keeps
its preview in a JPEG track, and a **TIFF raw** (CR2, ARW, DNG, RW2, 3FR …) can keep its preview tag
in an IFD the prefix cuts short. Both still read the whole file, so an unedited CR3 thumbnail — which
*is* the camera's own JPEG, since #755 — pulls tens of megabytes to show a JPEG of a few. Canon is the
largest bucket in the project's own gap ranking (33 % of photographers, [gaps.md](docs/gaps.md)).

This asks `lightcraft_raw::sparse::preview_plan` — the module #961 added for the import path, which
until now had no production caller — which ranges `embedded_preview` reads, and reads exactly those.
`@radialmonster` suggested the same in #832 ("#755 could also use `preview_plan` once it's in").

## How

- `planned_preview` ([crates/engine/src/files.rs](crates/engine/src/files.rs)): a buffer of the file's
  length, the ranges the plan names read into it (`Ranges`), asked again until `Ready`; then
  `embedded_preview` on that buffer. The header route (`bounded_preview`, the RAF pointer) is tried
  first and is unchanged.
- Only the planned ranges are read; the buffer's other pages stay zero and are never written. The
  loader's memory gate still counts the whole file, exactly as before — this path's cost is the bytes
  read. On macOS a freed buffer of that size may sit in the allocator's cache rather than go back to
  the OS (2–2.5 GB during a 38k-photo import, measured in #832), so this makes no promise about RSS.
- The loop gives up past **60 % of the file** — the bound step 2's `probe_partial` uses — and past
  1 GiB; a plan that says `Whole`, a range that does not fit, or a window that does not decode all
  return `None`, and the caller reads the file whole exactly as before.

title: Show progress and allow cancel while a large Lightroom catalog import reads its photos
author: rwoldberg
body:
## Problem

Importing a large Lightroom catalog looked hung. Reading the photos the catalog names
(headers and content hash) takes nearly all of the import's time, but that step reported
no progress: the count stood still (for example at "14 of 24554") until every file had been
read. Cancel had no effect during that step either.

## Change

- Reading the photos is now counted as its own step. The import's row in the activity
  list names the step under way (reading the catalog, reading the photos, adding them)
  and shows that step's own count, so it keeps moving while the photos are read.
- Cancel now stops the reading step, not only the steps after it.

`main` has since moved the import's progress from its own window to the activity list.
This branch is merged with that: an earlier version of this change added a second
progress bar to the old window, which no longer exists.

## Tests

- Progress moves while files are being read, and every file read is counted.
- Cancel stops reading within a few files instead of after all of them.
- The activity row shows the step's count, and can't be cancelled once photos are being
  added.
- Tried on a real Lightroom catalog of 25,540 photos before the merge with `main`:
  progress advanced through the whole import, and Cancel stopped it. Not yet repeated
  on the merged build.

title: Catalog: a library is backed up by itself while it is open, and when LightCraft quits (stacked on #1004)
author: nledford
body:
Stacked on #1004: the second follow-up from #870's "Remaining work on backup and restore".

Why stacked: it builds the backup schedule on top of the backup folder chosen in Settings from #1004 (`backup_folder`, `Session::backup_dir`, the `library.backupPreferences` command and the Backups section of Settings), none of which is on `main`, so a scheduled backup would have no folder to go to.

## What it adds

Two choices of their own, **both off until made**, saved with the library, set in **Settings ▸ General ▸ Backups** or with `library.backupPreferences`:

**While open** (`every`: never, day, week, month). The app backs the library up in the background when its last backup is that old (a month is thirty days). The backup has its row in the activity stack and can be stopped, and the usual toast says where it went.

- "Last backup" means the last one made **to the folder the library's backups go to**, whoever made it (File ▸ Back Up Library and agents count). Its time is kept in the library's preferences (`lastBackup`) and shown in Settings. Another folder, or that folder gone, and the library has not been backed up there.
- A backup by itself that fails, or can't be started, says so and is tried again an hour later, not on every look.
- Only the app a person has open does this. A headless session (a snapshot, an agent's, the command line) may end moments later and cut the backup off, so it backs up when it is told to.

**When quitting** (`onClose`: never, ask, always).

- **Ask:** Back Up, Skip or Cancel.
- **Always:** the backup starts without a question; a small window says so and offers Quit Without Waiting (which stops it) and Cancel.
- LightCraft quits when the backup is made. A backup of the library that runs already is the one it waits for; no second one is started.
- A backup that can't be made asks whether to quit anyway. Never a quit as if the library had been backed up, and never an app that can't be quit because a drive is unplugged.

title: M5: colour NR at half resolution (CPU and GPU), 100k grid frame budget
author: emmertex
body:
## What
- **Colour NR at half resolution (CPU and GPU).** From a blur radius of 3 px (the raw default, Color 25, on a full-size render), `local::denoise_color` box-averages chromaticity 2x (`chroma_half`), blurs it at half the radius (variance-corrected for the box and the upsample), and samples it back bilinearly inside the mix pass (`sample_half`). The full-size chromaticity buffer (288 MB at 24 MP) is gone. The GPU twin (`render::denoise`) takes the same path through two new `map` kernels, `chroma_half_k` and `nr_col_half`. The decision (`nr_color_half`) is shared, so CPU and GPU agree.

title: LR-VIEW-DETAIL: the loupe says "Rendering…" while what it shows is not the render yet
author: dev-null-undefined
body:
## What

The loupe often shows something that isn't the finished photo yet, and nothing says so:

- the raw's embedded JPEG or a thumbnail while the raw decodes,
- the previous render while an edit (a slider, Auto, a preset) renders,
- the magnified whole-frame render while the 1:1 window is on its way.

They all look like a slightly soft photo, so you can't tell "still loading" from "this photo is blurry".

Now, once a render has been on its way for 0.5 s with nothing new on screen, a **"Rendering…" pill** appears at the bottom of the photo (widget `loupe:rendering`). It disappears as soon as the render arrives.

- **It doesn't flash for quick renders.** The 0.5 s is the activity stack's own threshold. The wait starts when a render starts coming, not at the last frame drawn: an idle app draws no frames, so that frame can be seconds old. A slider drag whose drafts keep up never shows it. Once shown, it stays until nothing is coming, so drafts slower than the wait don't make it blink.
- **It watches what's actually on screen.** That is the After or the Before (`\`, Before/After views), plus the windows in use. It is hidden over a hover preview, and when the centre already says "Rendering…".
- **Placement.** It sits 12 pt above the bottom of the visible photo (the After pane in two-pane views), or in the crop tool's margin. When the Navigator is in the way (narrow windows, zoomed in), it moves just above the Navigator.
- **No new strings.** It reuses the existing translated "Rendering…".

Refs #654 (soft at 100 %, "not loading in full image") and #330 (blurry and slow while sliders move). Neither is fixed by this, but in both cases users couldn't tell whether a better render was still coming.

Lightroom Classic has the same overlay as an option. Adobe's help says to select *Show Messages When Loading Or Rendering Photos* to display overlays in the Loupe view during a process (Library View Options ▸ Loupe View ▸ General): https://helpx.adobe.com/lightroom-classic/deskt…

title: LR-MASK-BRUSH: pen pressure scales brush size and flow
author: emmertex
body:
## What
- **Pen pressure for brush masks.** While **Brush ▸ Pen Pressure** is on (the default), a stroke records the pen pressure (0..1) at each point from egui's touch `force`. Each dab's radius then runs from a tenth of the brush at the lightest touch to the full brush, and its flow is proportional to the pressure. The live stroke and the committed render use the same functions, so letting go doesn't change what's covered.
- `BrushStroke.pressure: Vec<f32>` is skipped when empty. A mouse stroke stores nothing, so existing documents and renders are byte-for-byte unchanged. Hostile values (NaN, out of range, a short list) are clamped or extended and never panic.
- `mask.brushStroke` takes `pressure: [p,…]`. A non-list, a non-number, or more values than points is a `BadParams` error.
- GPU: the mask kernel takes one radius and one flow per stroke, so strokes with pressure are rasterized on the CPU (the existing fallback). Strokes without pressure still render on the GPU.
- Brush panel: a "Pen Pressure" checkbox, translated into all nine locales.
- Docs: hardware-parity (per-platform status), gap 22, the LR-MASK-BRUSH row.
- Also includes the same one-line `spots.rs` fix for clippy 1.99's `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` lint, which otherwise fails `cargo xtask ci` on main.

**Platform reach:** this works wherever winit reports a pen as a touch with force. That's Windows (WM_POINTER pen input) and pointer-event force on the web; neither has been tested on real tablet hardware. On macOS and on X11 / Wayland, winit 0.30 reports no tablet pressure, so pens paint at full pressure there until winit adds tablet events. There's no tilt.

## Why
Gap 22 in docs/gaps.md: brush users with tablets expect Lightroom's pressure-sensitive size and flow.

## How tested
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-pipeline pen_pressure_scales_dab_size_and_flow`: a stroke ramping from light to full pressure is thin and faint at the start and full width at the end. Full pressure equals no pressure. It never p…

title: Catalog: a library can keep its backups for a time, and old ones go after a new one is made (stacked on #1025)
author: nledford
body:
Stacked on #1025 (backup schedule), which is on #1004 → #870 → #856 → #841 → #814 → #800.

Why stacked: the time a library keeps its backups is `keepDays` in the backup schedule's preferences from #1025 (`BackupSchedule`, `Session::backup_schedule`, `library.backupPreferences`), and it refuses backup folders with #1004's `not_for_backups`; none of that is on `main`.

Third item from the "Remaining work on backup and restore" list in #870: old backups can go by themselves.

![Before and after: Backups in Settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nledford/lightcraft/7968881fde6c08ddc7afb10449d4432f7dafb9a8/keep-backups-before-after.png)

*Top, BEFORE: Backups in Settings ▸ General. Bottom, AFTER: with Keep backups, on Forever until chosen otherwise. Choose Folder… and Use Library Folder are greyed out here because these headless shots have no folder dialog; in the app they are live.*

## What it does

- **Settings ▸ General ▸ Backups ▸ Keep backups**: Forever (the default), 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, 1 year. Agents: `keepDays` in `library.backupPreferences` (any number of days, `null` for forever).
- After a backup is made to the folder the library's backups go to, the library's own backups older than that are removed, each as a whole folder. The backup's answer lists them (`removed`, `notRemoved`), and the app's "Backed up the library to…" note says how many went and how many could not.
- `library.pruneBackups {keepDays?, remove?}` says which backups are that old without removing any; `remove: true` removes them.

Nothing changes for a library that doesn't choose a time: the default is to keep everything.

## What is never removed

The rule is "only what is certainly an old backup of this library". A backup is left alone when:

- it is one of the library's newest three, however old (age is told by clocks; a clock that jumped ahead costs the backups beyond those three and no more), or it is the backup just made;
- its `backup.json` doesn't say it is of this librar…

title: LR-PREF-DISPLAY: Monitor profiles: keep zoomed views sharp
author: kelanna
body:
Sorry I missed this bug in my original PR implementing ICC monitor profiles. It's a small/quick fix thankfully. Follow-up to the monitor ICC profile PR: with a display profile set, zooming in to 1:1 or closer gave a blurry view in Detail and Compare. The view showed only the whole-frame render, magnified, instead of the sharp window cut from the photo's own pixels, and switching back to sRGB made it sharp again.

**Cause:** a render made for a display profile gets its own render key (`RenderJob::with_display`, applied by `Renderer::request`). The zoom window tiles were recorded in `region_tiles` / `compare_tiles` under the key the job had *before* that, so `draw_window` never found the texture it was looking for and drew nothing over the whole-frame render.

**Fix:** record the tiles with the job as the renderer runs it (`Renderer::job_for`), in `panels/detail.rs` and `panels/compare.rs`. That's two lines.

**Tests:** `a_display_profile_keeps_the_sharp_window_at_one_to_one` and `a_display_profile_keeps_the_compare_windows_at_one_to_one` (in `tests_preview_limit.rs`) load a Display P3 profile, zoom to 1:1, and check that the window texture is painted over the whole-frame render. Both failed before the fix and pass with it. The rest of the `ui-egui` suite passes, apart from the `tests_model_setup` denoise tests, which can't load a denoise model in a `cargo test -p lightcraft-ui-egui` build. Clippy and fmt are clean.

Found by me on my wide-gamut monitor after the release, was more apparent on very high resolution photos/film scans.

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: decode Minolta MRW
author: emmertex
body:
## What
Minolta / Konica Minolta **MRW** files now decode from sensor data instead of opening preview-only.

- `crates/meta/src/mrw.rs`: bounds-checked walker for the `\0MRM` block container. The `TTW` block now feeds Exif (`lightcraft_meta::embedded`), so MRW imports get capture date, camera and exposure.

The image size is the default crop. Black is 0; white comes from the saturation plateau, else 4095. As-shot WB comes from `WBG`, whose coefficients follow the cell order. Orientation and metadata come from `TTW`. The embedded preview already worked through the existing scan.
- Corpus: 4 CC0 raw.pixls.us samples (DiMAGE 7Hi, A1, A200, Dynax 7D) added to `RAW_SAMPLES` with sha256. A new test, `corpus_minolta_mrw`, checks size, crop, CFA, white, WB, green balance and the preview.

Long-tail raw formats (gaps.md #20). MRW was the cheapest one: 11 Adobe-listed models, all simple uncompressed layouts.

title: fix(export): render exports at exactly their resolved size (LR-EXP-DIM)
author: THEtheChad
body:
### Problem

An export's size was rounded to integers by `Resize::apply` and then fitted again by the renderer.
`export::prepare_guarded` passed the resolved `w × h` to `Session::export_job` as an ordinary fit box,
and `pipeline::plan` called `Frame::fit` on it a second time, against the aspect of the source it was
rendering. If the rounded pair's aspect fell just short of the source's, one edge lost a pixel:

- `lightcraft-cli render in.png -o out.png --size 4` on a 5 × 3 PNG wrote **3 × 2**. `export::output_size`
  and the CLI help both say 4 × 2. `app.export` reports and writes the same 3 × 2.
- A 6000 × 4000 photo exported at long edge 800 renders from the 2560 × 1707 preview source. That
  source's aspect is a little under 3:2, so the result was **799 × 533**, not 800 × 533. Any photo
  exported from a reduced source can hit this; for example 1500 × 1000 at 400 px gave 400 × 266
  instead of 400 × 267.

### Fix

`RenderRequest` gets an explicit `sizing: Sizing` field. `Fit` is the default and keeps today's
behaviour for views, thumbnails, previews, contact-sheet cells and web workers. `Exact` is new and
only exports use it.

- `Frame::sized(max_w, max_h, sizing)` keeps an `Exact` pair when it is a rounding of the frame's
  aspect. It allows extra slack for a reduced source's own rounding to whole pixels. If the pair
  isn't such a rounding, `sized` falls back to `fit` and never stretches the image. That happens
  when the catalog's dimensions disagree with the decoded source, or when Upright changes the crop.
  `Frame::fit` itself is unchanged.
- `pipeline::plan` uses `Frame::sized`, and so does `pipeline::output_size`. The CPU and GPU
  renderers both build their plan through `pipeline::plan`, so both honour the mode, including
  16-bit, float and HDR output. The gain-map HDR rendition uses the same exact size as its SDR base.
- `Session::export_job` and `render_export` now take a `Sizing` argument, so the compiler checks
  every caller. `export::prepare_guard…

author: nledford
body:
Stacked on #1034 (it is not under #1054 any more).

Why stacked: the list says which backups are of the open library and newest first by `BackupReport.made` and the library id's use in `library.backups` (`ofThisLibrary`), which #1034 adds, and it uses `backup::is_made_backup` from #1004; neither is on `main`.

Fourth item from the "Remaining work on backup and restore" list in #870: a list of backups to choose from.

*AFTER only (the list is new; before, the menu item went straight to a folder dialog): File ▸ Restore Library from Backup… with three backups of the library, the newest chosen.*

**File ▸ Restore Library from Backup…** now opens a list instead of going straight to the folder dialog:

- the backups in the folder the library's backups go to, newest first by when each says it was made: the time (UTC), how many photos, the size;

title: LR-IMP-CAMERA-COVERAGE: verify 117 Nikon and Fujifilm bodies on CC0 files
author: emmertex
body:
## What

- **117 Nikon and Fujifilm Adobe models verified**, plus the Nikon 1 AW1, which isn't on Adobe's list. That is one CC0 raw.pixls.us file for each body that already decodes; the CC0 status was checked against the site's licence column. Files are added to `RAW_SAMPLES` with URL and SHA-256. The new `crates/raw/tests/body_corpus.rs` pins each file's sensor hash. These are LightCraft's own decodes; no external decoder was run. Against the camera, the check is black-box: the decoded green, on a 24 × 16 grid of the active area, must follow the camera's embedded JPEG. On these files r is 0.77–1.00, while a misread layout or stream gives r near 0.
- **Found by the sweep: COOLPIX 5700, 8400 and 8800 decode wrongly.** The image comes out as two stacked half-height fields with a CMYG mosaic read as RGB, and r against the JPEG is 0.12–0.36. These are recorded as `unsupported` in `evidence.tsv`; there is no decoder change here.
- **Other CC0 files refused, not touched here:**
  - "compressed NEF without a linearization table": Z 6, Z 7, D6, D100, D1X, P330, P7700, P7800. This is the #769 / PR #671 family.
  - HE NEF: Z 8, Z5_2, Z6_3.
  - Pre-X FinePix RAF: S2Pro, S3Pro, S5Pro, S5000/5200/5500, S6000fd/6500fd, S7000, S9500/9600, S100FS, S200EXR.
- **#702** (A100 / F828 regression) is already fixed by #774. The A100 evidence row now says `preview`, and the F828 row is updated.
- **#535 DSLR-A200…A390 is not attempted.** Their strips use Sony's version-1 ARW compression (TIFF compression 32767). I know of no public prose description, and my knowledge of the format comes from decoder source, so it cannot be implemented clean-room here. The A300, A330 and A850 samples on raw.pixls.us are not CC0.
- Re-measured with `coverage.py`:
  - 236 → 354 verified models (24 %); 941 → 824 unverified.
  - Use-weighted share whose camera decodes: 85 % → 86 %. Share on a verified body: 42 % → 58 %.

title: LR-EXP-RENDERDNG: Render to DNG export format
author: emmertex
body:

Render to DNG (Lightroom Classic 15.5) as an export format: `format: "rendereddng"` in `app.export` and the MCP export tool; in the export dialog, Format DNG then "DNG of: Rendered photo" (next to "Raw data", so the format row keeps its width).

title: LR-PREF-DISPLAY: on Linux, previews use the display profile from colord
author: emmertex
body:
## What
- **Linux: the display profile from colord.** While no monitor profile is chosen in Settings ▸ Display, the desktop app reads the profile that GNOME / KDE Settings ▸ Color (or a calibrator like DisplayCAL) assigns in colord. The call chain is `org.freedesktop.ColorManager.GetDevicesByKind("display")`, then each device's first (default) `Profiles` entry, then that profile's `Filename`. Previews are shown through it via the existing `Services::screen_profile` path, the same one macOS uses (#787). The button reads **Use Screen Profile**.
- It uses `zbus`, which the Linux app already depends on, so there's no new dependency and no `unsafe`. A background thread polls every 3 s, so the UI thread never waits on D-Bus. Without colord it retries every 30 s. Profile files are capped at 16 MiB.
- **Several displays:** eframe doesn't say which monitor the window is on, so a profile is used only when every display that has one shares it. A mixed set stays sRGB rather than guess.
- **Windows** (WCS `GetICMProfile` / `WcsGetDefaultColorProfile`) needs FFI, which would mean `unsafe` outside `crates/sysmem`, so it stays manual and is noted as blocked in the docs. X11 `_ICC_PROFILE` isn't read either.
- Docs: display-profiles.md, hardware-parity (Monitor profile row; the macOS cell now reflects #787), gap 22, the LR-PREF-DISPLAY row.
- Also includes the same one-line `spots.rs` fix for clippy 1.99's `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` lint, which otherwise fails `cargo xtask ci` on main.

## Why
Gap 22 in docs/gaps.md: "OS monitor profiles". Calibrated and wide-gamut Linux displays showed previews as sRGB unless the user found the `.icc` file by hand.

## How tested
- `cargo test -p lightcraft colord`: tests for the profile choice (none, one, several sharing one, a mixed set) and for reading the file (empty, missing, over the cap).
- `cargo clippy -p lightcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

title: Windows: case-insensitive sidecar/rename fixes; Windows test and toolchain fixes
author: OneSlips
body:
Split out of #1012 at a reviewer's request.

## What and why

On clean `main`, 20 engine tests failed on Windows. Most came from three real bugs that affect any case-insensitive volume (Windows, and macOS APFS by default):

- **Sidecar spelling on rename.** Renaming a photo looked for `a.XMP` before `a.xmp`. On a case-insensitive volume the upper-case spelling "exists" even when only `a.xmp` is on disk, so the sidecar was moved as `Trip.XMP` and its retained-packet record was stored under the wrong spelling. Upper-case candidates are now used only when the folder lists that exact name (new `MoveFs::listed`).
- **`same_file` symmetry.** On Windows, `RealFs::same_file` (std has no file id there) gave different answers depending on argument order: `same_file("Trip.XMP", "Trip.xmp")` was false when `Trip.xmp` was the real entry, so saving after a partial rename reported a collision that wasn't there. It is now symmetric. It also requires the two names to differ only by case, because before this two different files with the same size and mtime counted as "the same".
- **Save spelling.** Saving metadata chose the sidecar spelling with `is_file()`, trying lower case first, so the atomic write renamed an existing `Trip.XMP` to `Trip.xmp`. Whichever spelling the folder lists now wins.

The remaining failures came from test fixtures that wrote paths with `/` (FakeFs fault paths, catalog paths, expected paths), while the code joins paths with the host separator.

Small Windows and toolchain fixes, in a second commit:

- `apps/lightcraft/src/editors.rs` `desktop_exec`: a freedesktop `Exec` path counts as absolute when it starts with `/` on every platform. `Path::is_absolute` expects a drive letter on Windows, so `editors::tests::desktop_entries_give_their_program` failed there.
- `crates/pipeline/src/spots.rs` `fill_box`: `as_chunks::<3>()` instead of `chunks_exact(3)` (`clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` on newer toolchains).
- `crates/catalog/src/lock.rs` `descriptor_copy`: n…

title: LR-IMP-CAMERA-COVERAGE: measured image area for Nikon bodies without CropArea
author: robmdunn
body:
Fixes #976
Fixes #914
Fixes #1236

## Problem

Nikon bodies from before about 2016 record no `CropArea` in the maker note, so the decoder keeps their whole sensor data, less trailing dark columns. Where that data holds masked lines above black or optical black, they are developed as a coloured or dark bar on that edge (the top edge in portrait):

- **D7000 / D5100** (#976): 36 masked columns at ~600 over a black level of 0, then 8 of 0. The dark-column trim removed only the 8.
- **D800 / D800E** (#914): 14 masked columns on the right.
- **D600 / D610** (#1236): 8 masked columns on the right.
- The same holds on many more bodies (D3200 46 columns, Df 42 + 2, Coolpix A 36, D300 / D300S up to 32, D3100 6 + 22, D3 / D3S / D700 2 + 2, …).

None of these files records the picture's area anywhere. A pixel-statistics heuristic was tried first and failed on real images: deep shadow at the edge looks just like masked lines. The fix is therefore measured per body, as the D4 entry already was.

## Fix

`MEASURED_BODIES` (`crates/raw/src/vendor/nef.rs`) gains **44 model / data size / depth groups**, next to the D4, D7100 and D90 entries already on `main`. Each gets the frame of its own camera JPEG inside the sensor data:

D7000, D5100, D800, D800E, Df, D4 (12-bit added), D3, D3S, D700, D300, D300S, D600, D610, D810, D4S, D5600, Coolpix A, D3000, D40X, D60, D80, D2Xs, D200, D3200, Nikon 1 V1.

- **Best guesses**, short of the evidence rule below, each with a comment naming its evidence:
  - D3100: 3 of 4 clean files agree.
  - D5000: 4 of 5 agree, and the D90 has the same sensor.
  - D40: 2 of 2 agree.
  - D50 and D70: one file each, and they agree.
  - D70s: its files align between pixels next to the D50 / D70 frame.

  Every best-guess frame keeps the masked lines out by at least 11 px.
- An entry matches model, data size and bit depth exactly. Every other body decodes as before.
- Bodies whose data holds only picture beyond the camera frame get **no entry**, so their output is…

title: Catalog: what restores replaced goes with the old backups of a library that keeps them for a time (stacked on #1034)
author: nledford
body:
Stacked on #1034 (keep-for-a-time). It no longer sits on #1043 (restore list), which it did not use.

Why stacked: it removes the folders of `Replaced` by the rule #1034 adds (`keepDays`, `library.pruneBackups`, `restore::outdated`'s age rule and `KEEP_AT_LEAST`) and extends #1034's `tests_backup_prune.rs`; none of that is on `main`.

Fifth item from the "Remaining work on backup and restore" list in #870: pruning `Replaced` folders.

## The problem

Each restore keeps the whole catalog it replaced in `Replaced/<the time>` in the library folder, and nothing ever removed those.

## What it does

`Replaced` folders follow the setting #1034 added, rather than getting one of their own: a library that keeps its backups for a time (**Settings ▸ General ▸ Backups ▸ Keep backups**, `keepDays`) removes what its restores replaced by the same rule, at the same moment its old backups go (after a backup is made to its own folder). A library that keeps its backups forever, which is the default, keeps all of it, as now.

- Folders of `Replaced` whose names say they are older than the keep time go, never the newest three.
- The backup's answer says what went (`replacedRemoved`, `replacedNotRemoved`), and the app's "Backed up the library to…" note adds a line for each.
- `library.pruneBackups` says which would go before any is removed (`replaced.outdated`), which are as old but stay and why (`replaced.kept`), and removes them with `remove: true`.

## What is never removed

A folder of `Replaced` goes only when it is as the restore left it:

- **renamed** → it has no age to go by, and stays;
- **anything in it that a restore did not put there** → it stays. That covers a folder that was opened as a library since (opening leaves its lock file), anything a person put into it, a nested folder, and a file in `segments/` that is no segment;
- **its time is yet to come** → it stays, and is not counted among the newest three;
- **a restore of the library is cut short** (`restore.json` is the…

title: fix: Before側クリックのズーム位置を正しく計算する
author: haranishi
body:

title: PERF-PRESETS: libraries with thousands of presets stay responsive
author: OneSlips
body:
Split out of #1012 at a reviewer's request.

## Problem

A Lightroom preset collection imported whole (11,113 presets, a 42 MB `presets.json`) made every interaction take seconds:

- `Session::persist` ran after every command and serialized the whole preset list just to compare it with the last write: **609 ms per slider tick** (release build, the real collection).
- The Presets panel deep-cloned every preset into a `BTreeMap` and built a row, widget id and (with thumbnails) a variant render job for each of them, every frame.
- The preset pickers (Import dialog, Settings > Import) built a row per preset every frame while open.
- `add_presets` and opening a library compared every preset with every other (quadratic).

## Fixes

- `Session::presets` is now a `PresetList` whose `generation()` changes on mutable access. `persist` serializes only when it (or the profile lists) changed, and skips the write when the bytes hash the same. Opening a library no longer serializes the list once just to remember it.
- Presets panel: grouping is cached per `PresetList::generation()` (`grouped()`), and only rows in view are laid out (`rows_in_view()` + `allocate_space` for the rows above/below). Move to Group reads its targets from the cached groups. The panel keeps upstream's current (docking / UI.9) layout.
- Preset pickers in `import.rs` and `panels/settings.rs` use a shared `picker_rows()` that builds only the rows in view (`ScrollArea::show_rows`).
- `add_presets` and library open use hash indexes instead of pairwise comparisons.

## Measured (release, the real 11,113-preset collection)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `develop.set` | 609 ms | 2.3 ms |
| `preset.apply` | 598 ms | 3.1 ms |
| Presets panel rows built per frame (5,000 presets) | 5,041 | ~20 (2.3 ms) |

title: LR-EDIT-EFFECTS-GRAIN: particle film grain, resolution independent
author: OneSlips
body:
Split out of #1012 at a reviewer's request. Only the film-grain work (LR-EDIT-EFFECTS-GRAIN), cherry-picked onto current `main`.

## Why it was built

I'm a professional wedding photographer. In Lightroom Classic I kept grain very low, because Lightroom's grain does more than add texture: it also blurs detail, and the image looks softer, as if it had been shot at a lower resolution. Faces, lace and hair lose crispness as soon as the grain becomes visible. I wanted a grain that gives a photo filmic texture and keeps the detail underneath.

LightCraft's old grain was a value-noise overlay (two octaves of smoothed noise in screen space). It looked like a noise texture rather than film, and preview and export did not match.

## Why this is good

- **Texture without destroying detail.** Grain is added as particles on top of the finished image, not by smearing it, so edges and fine detail stay where they were. That means a wedding photographer can use a visible amount of grain without the photo looking softer.
- **It looks like film.** It renders clumps of irregular grains whose density follows the tone, instead of a uniform noise pattern.
- **What you see is what you export.** It is resolution independent: a fit-to-window preview shows the export's grain downscaled. The same grains are drawn at any render size or crop.
- **Existing edits don't change.** The particle grain is a new process (V3, `docs/process-versions.md`). Photos on V1 or V2 keep exactly the grain they were edited with, on CPU and GPU. A photo moves to the particle grain only through Update to Current Process (one undo step). New photos and Reset get V3.

## What changes

The particle grain is rendered per output pixel as clumps of irregular grains, from the published Boolean model (Newson, Delon & Galerne, *Realistic Film Grain Rendering*, IPOL 2017). No code was taken from any implementation. Full write-up: `docs/grain.md`.

- **Model.** Clump centres form a Poisson process on a fixed cell grid. A clump…

title: LR-PROF-IMPORT: import the user's own DNG camera profiles (.dcp)
author: OneSlips
body:
## Policy question for maintainers (please decide before merging)

This PR **reverses the documented "Adobe profile formats deliberately unsupported" stance, for user-supplied files only.** Before reviewing the code, please decide whether LightCraft should accept this. The case for it:

- DCP (DNG Camera Profile) is defined in the **openly published DNG specification** (chapter 6). The app already reads the same tags (ColorMatrix/ForwardMatrix 1-2, HueSatMap, LookTable, ProfileToneCurve…) inside DNG files today.
- **Nothing ships.** No profile is bundled, nothing is auto-scanned (no Adobe/Camera Raw folders are read), and the repository holds no `.dcp` file. Unit tests build their profiles in memory with `lightcraft_raw::dcp::write_dcp`; the one real profile used in tests is a CC0 file fetched into the gitignored `corpus/` (below).
- A profile only enters the app when the user imports a file they have, e.g. one they made with a colour-checker tool.
- `cargo xtask assets` still rejects `.dcp` files in the repo.

If the answer is no, this PR can be closed as-is. The docs here (file-format-parity, raw-parity, roadmap, xmp-interop, parity-checklist) describe the new stance and would need to be left unchanged.

## Why this was built

A professional wedding photographer shoots several bodies at every wedding and has to make their colour match. The usual way to do that is to photograph a ColorChecker with each body and build a camera profile from it. Every profiling tool (Calibrite PROFILER, the photographer's own RADcamProfiles, dcamprof, Lumariver…) writes that profile as a DCP. Until now LightCraft could not use one, so a photographer who switched lost the calibration they had made for their own cameras. LightCraft's own colour for many bodies is still an estimate (fitted to the camera's JPEG, or spectral data), so a measured profile of the photographer's own body is the most accurate colour available to them.

## Why it is good

- **Measured colour, the user's own.** A…

title: UI: targeted adjustment says how to leave it; wheel notch scrolls 100 points
author: OneSlips
body:
Split out of #1012 at a reviewer's request.

## Targeted adjustment says how to leave it

A user report: with a Color Mixer Hue targeted-adjustment tool (TAT) left on, the canvas looked frozen. Click-to-zoom and panning stopped working, because the tool takes every click and drag on the photo. Esc already turned the tool off, but nothing told you so, and the mixer's TAT buttons look like tabs.

Turning on any TAT (Color Mixer HSL, tone curve) now shows a toast: *Targeted adjustment on: drag up or down on the photo · Esc to stop*. The mixer and the curve buttons share one helper, `set_tat` in `panels/edit.rs`. Esc handling is unchanged: since KEY-ESC, the first Esc leaves the tool and stays in Detail.

## A mouse-wheel notch scrolls 100 points

egui scrolls 40 points per wheel line, and an open Edit panel is 2000+ points tall, so getting through it took 50+ notches. Lightroom moves about 100 points per notch. `theme::apply_kind` now sets `line_scroll_speed = WHEEL_LINE_POINTS` (100), so every theme gets it. Trackpads report points and still scroll as before.

Two places on main depended on a notch being 40 points. This PR adjusts both so they keep their current per-notch behaviour:
- **Wheel zoom** (Ctrl+wheel, and the loupe's plain wheel from "Smooth the plain mouse-wheel zoom"): both use `scroll_zoom_speed × points`. Left alone, a notch would zoom 1.65x instead of 1.22x. `scroll_zoom_speed` becomes `WHEEL_ZOOM_PER_POINT` (40/200/100), so a notch still zooms about 1.22x.
- **Wheel nudges on a focused slider** (#864, KEY-SLIDER-WHEEL): these counted 40 points as one step, so a notch would have jumped 2–3 steps. `wheel_nudges` now uses `WHEEL_LINE_POINTS` per step, so one notch is still one nudge. A trackpad now needs 100 points of movement per nudge instead of 40, and a single event is still capped at 10 steps.

title: GPU-FULL: more of the render on the GPU, loupe drafts from GPU textures
author: OneSlips
body:
Split out of #1012 at a reviewer's request.

More of the render runs on the GPU, and when the GPU renderer shares the window's device the loupe's interactive drafts are drawn straight from GPU textures instead of being read back and uploaded again.

## What moved to the GPU
- **GPU-FULL-1:** LUT profiles, Refine Edges masks and soft proofs to a colour space (with the destination and display gamut warnings). Before this they always went to the CPU.
- **GPU-FULL-2:** spot removal (Clone / Heal / Remove, plus automatic source search scored on the device), defringe (`minmax` kernel in `blur.wgsl`, next to upstream's `median_h`/`median_v`) and the histogram (`hist.wgsl`). `spots.rs` now has a shared `SpotLayout` (it carries a `fill` flag: Fill uses a 2r window and offset (0,0), and `heal` is Remove|Heal), so the CPU and GPU lay out spots the same way.
- **GPU-FULL-3:** thumbnails, preset and profile previews use the GPU once `lightcraft_gpu::ready()` is true. They never wait for device creation; until then they render on the CPU (`tests/thumbs_bench.rs`, ignored: 3.6 ms vs 4.3-5.2 ms each on 32 threads).
- **GPU-FULL-4:** `RenderJob::on_screen()` drafts can come back as a `ScreenFrame` texture on the window's device (`render_display`), which egui-wgpu draws directly (`App` gets `WindowTextures`, and `Tex::id()` is used for every texture draw). `window_gpu` asks for the adapter's own limits off GL, so a 24 MP buffer fits. **`LIGHTCRAFT_GPU_WINDOW=0`** turns this off: the renderer gets its own device and renders are read back as before.

## What deliberately stays on the CPU
- Content-aware **Fill** spots (`spots::fill_box`, inpainting): `try_render` returns `Fallback::NotTried`.
- Soft proofs against an **output-device profile** table (`Proof::profile != 0`): `NotTried`.
- High-bit-depth exports and Visualize HDR, as before.

`run()` returns `Result<Output, Fallback>`; `render_display` is `run(..).ok()`; `try_render` and `develop_reporting` keep upstream's fallback reason…

title: LR-EXP-RENDERDNG: Photo > Render to DNG (stacked on #1047)
author: emmertex
body:
## What
Photo ▸ Render to DNG (Lightroom Classic 15.5), command `photo.renderToDng`:
- Renders each selected photo (or `ids`, at most 500) with its edits as a linear 16-bit float DNG `<name>-Rendered.dng` next to its original. It never overwrites an existing file, and a generated demo photo needs `dir`. The DNG writer is #1047's `write_rendered_dng`.
- Adds each new DNG to the library, stacked on top of its original and expanded (the same path Edit In copies take), then selects the new photos.
- `colorSpace`: proPhoto (default), rec2020, adobeRgb, displayP3 or srgb; anything else is an error.
- A batch holds a cancellable `renderDng` activity row with progress. A cancel stops between photos and keeps the copies made so far (`cancelled: true`). A photo that fails in a batch is listed in `failed` and the rest carry on; a single photo reports its error.
- Result: `{copies: [{path, id, original}], failed: [{id, error}], cancelled}`.
- **Off the UI thread (second commit):** the engine work is split into `render_dng::prepare` (on the session), `RenderDngJob::run` (no session: render, encode, write) and `render_dng::finish` (on the session: import, stack, select). The desktop app intercepts `photo.renderToDng` when it has a thread-safe writer and hands `run` to a worker thread, the same way background exports work (`crates/ui-egui/src/render_dng_task.rs`). The request answers at once with `{background: true, total}`. The `renderDng` activity row shows progress and its ✕ cancels between photos. Each frame polls for the result, then adds the DNGs and shows a toast. A panic in the worker is caught. Without a shared writer (CLI, MCP, web, headless scripts) the command runs synchronously, as before.
- Docs: LR-EXP-RENDERDNG → ✅, gap 25 and file-format-parity updated.

## Why
docs/gaps.md gap 25: Lightroom's Render to DNG adds the DNG to the catalog next to the original; #1047 had only the export format.

title: Keep parser guards compatible with Rust 1.95 and macOS CI
author: grlessa
body:
Rust 1.95 rejects several nested parser matches under `clippy -D warnings`. Move the existing validation conditions into match guards without changing accepted bytes or fallback behavior, simplify two equivalent boolean expressions, and fix the desktop glow `on_exit` call.

Make the existing macOS CI fixtures portable: resolve `true` through PATH, inject sidecar failures against the same physical file despite case aliases, check actual directory entries for duplicate packets, and exercise unavailable non-UTF-8 paths on APFS while retaining the normal catalog and symlink checks. Account for the macOS-only Apple Photos row in the existing export geometry assertion. Collision, provenance, catalog and undo assertions remain in place.

This separates the CI portion of #979. No external lens catalog or photo-processing feature is included.

Validation: `cargo xtask ci` passed on macOS with Rust 1.95: formatting, Clippy with warnings denied, HEIF checks, workspace tests, parity, layers, asset attribution and WASM checks (all eight gates).

title: Normalize DNG black levels per plane with finite-range guards
author: grlessa
body:
DNG normalization used the mean black level across sample planes and ignored active-area deltas. Sensor white could therefore normalize above 1 in linear RGB, while near-clipped CFA samples could fall below the highlight detector's threshold. Compute the phase-aware maximum black independently for each sample plane, then share the scales between full and binned development. Vendor RAW scaling remains unchanged.

Empty active areas, non-finite/non-positive ranges and overflowing reciprocals fall back to a unit scale; empty images still return a validation error. This addresses the never-crash review on #979. Bump the render-cache version to invalidate previously normalized thumbnails; existing offline smart previews need their originals to be rebuilt.

Synthetic and property regressions cover per-plane white levels, repeat-pattern phases, signed deltas, cropped/binned opcode paths, clipping, shadow noise, highlight headroom and vendor behavior. No Lightroom-fidelity or additional camera-coverage claim is made.

Split from #979. Based on #1068's shared Rust 1.95/macOS CI fixes; merge #1068 first. The feature commit is independent of the Canon and mask PRs. No external profiles or lens database are bundled.

Validation: `cargo xtask ci` passed on macOS with Rust 1.95: all eight gates (fmt, Clippy with warnings denied, HEIF, workspace tests, parity, layers, assets, WASM). The new DNG property/synthetic tests and empty/non-finite-range unit regression passed.

title: Control channel: give up requests a hidden Wayland window can't answer, never run them late (#718)
author: emmertex
body:
## What
- `apps/lightcraft/src/control_server.rs`: a request now waits in short slices and watches the app's frame counter. If the app has not started the request and has drawn no frame for 5 s, the server gives the request up and replies:
  > the app drew no frame for 5 s, so the request was not run: its window is probably not visible (on Wayland a window on a hidden workspace or minimized is not redrawn, which pauses the app). Bring the window on screen and send it again

  A request the app has already started still gets the full 60 s, because a long command blocks frames while it runs.
- `ControlRequest` now carries a state (pending, taken or abandoned, set atomically by whichever side gets there first). `drain_control` skips abandoned requests, so a request that timed out no longer runs later when the window comes back (the double document in the report).
- `docs/control-protocol.md` describes the behaviour and what to do instead (keep the window on screen, or use headless or `lightcraft-cli mcp` without `--connect`).
- `crates/pipeline/src/spots.rs` uses `as_chunks::<3>()`, because main fails the newer clippy `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` lint (same change as #997).

## Why
#718: on Wayland, the control channel and `mcp --connect` stalled for 60 s per request while the window wasn't visible, and the stalled requests ran later, a second time.

## How tested
- New unit tests in `control_server.rs`:
  - an app drawing no frames gets the request given up quickly, with the reason, and the request can no longer be taken;
  - a taken request waits for its reply even though frames stop;
  - an app that keeps drawing is simply waited for.
- Ran the desktop app on Linux (Wayland, AMD Radeon 8060S, Vulkan) with `--control 18731 --demo`: `ui.inspect` answered in 0.1 s. I couldn't reproduce the hidden-workspace case end to end, since that needs OS-level window moves, which the project rules forbid.

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: EOS R6 Mark III as-shot white balance (ColorData version 66)
author: josenbobby
body:
## What
- `crates/raw/src/vendor/cr3.rs`: the EOS R6 Mark III writes `ColorData` version 66, which `camera_levels` did not know, so every R6 Mark III CR3 opened with no as-shot white balance (`wb_multipliers: None`) and black levels measured from the masked columns. Version 66 now reads its as-shot WB (word 105) and black levels (word 383), the same offsets as version 64. The white-level offset becomes optional: version 66's word 661 is not the clipping point, so its white level stays measured from the data.
- `docs/cr3.md`: a paragraph on version 66 and the evidence below.
- `docs/parity-checklist.md`: the LR-IMP-FORMATS row and the revision history.

## Evidence (33 R6 Mark III files from 12 shoots, ISO 100–12800, 1/1250 s–25 s)
- **As-shot WB:** words 105–108 change from shot to shot, and word 109 holds the matching colour temperature (3271 K in fog, 4200 K for a night sky, 5300–7400 K in daylight). It is followed by the fixed preset table (Daylight 5200 K, Shade 7000 K, Cloudy 6000 K, Tungsten 3200 K). All 33 files now open with their as-shot white balance.
- **Black:** word 383 equals the masked-column level in every file (512 at low ISO, 2047–2048 above).
- **White:** word 661 reads 14351 or 13995, but highlights pile up at 16383. In a blown ISO 100 frame, 368,937 samples sit in 16256–16383, and the counts run smoothly through 14351 with no step. Using word 661 would clip real highlights.

## Checks
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-raw` passes (330 + integration tests), with the version 66 case added to `color_data_uses_versioned_as_shot_offsets`. `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-raw --all-targets -D warnings` is clean, and `cargo xtask parity` is OK.
- `cargo xtask ci` stops at clippy on current `main` with Rust 1.99, before reaching this change: `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` in `crates/pipeline/src/spots.rs:250`. I left that out of this PR.
- No media committed; the test is synthetic.

title: Include Canon CR2/CR3 in reproducible camera calibration
author: grlessa
body:
`lightcraft-cli calibrate` previously ignored Canon CR2/CR3 files even though the engine can fit them to their own embedded camera JPEGs. Include these extensions in case-insensitive discovery and document the supported inputs.

Parallel workers now collect per-file pools and merge them in sorted discovery order. This keeps the fitting holdout and floating-point accumulation reproducible across worker scheduling. Malformed files remain reported per file without aborting the rest of the run.

CLI regressions cover CR2/CR3 discovery (including uppercase extensions), malformed-file reporting and repeated parallel fitting from synthetic RAW fixtures. This does not add a decoder or certify all Canon variants, and incorporates no external camera profiles.

Split from #979. Based on #1068's shared Rust 1.95/macOS CI fixes; merge #1068 first. Independent of the DNG and mask feature commits.

Validation: `cargo xtask ci` passed on macOS with Rust 1.95: all eight gates (fmt, Clippy with warnings denied, HEIF, workspace tests, parity, layers, assets, WASM), including the Canon discovery, malformed-file reporting and reproducibility CLI regressions.

title: LR-VIEW-ZOOM: diagnostic overlays render zoom windows; soft proofing on the GPU (stacked on #1027)
author: emmertex
body:
**Stacked on #1027 (`pr/zoom-detail`).** It includes #1027's two commits; only the last commit, "diagnostic overlays render zoom windows; soft proofing on the GPU", is new. Review that commit after #1027 lands.

## What
- **Diagnostic overlays get zoom windows.** Visualize Spots, the Point Color range and Visualize HDR now use the same 1:1–8:1 window as the plain loupe, mask overlays and soft proofing. Before, they rendered the whole frame at the drawn size.

title: Backup and restore: the smaller items left on #870's list (stacked on #1054)
author: nledford
body:
Stacked on #1054 (→ #1034 → #1025 → #1004 → #870 → … → #800).

Why stacked: its restore into another folder is tried with `forget_id` (#1034) and names a failed one `(not opened)` in `Replaced`, which #1054's pruning handles (`NOT_OPENED`, `Replaced`), and `lightcraft-cli run` waits on the background backup / restore of #841 / #870; none of that is on `main`.

The smaller items from the "Remaining work on backup and restore" list in #870. With this, that list is done except for the two things noted at the end.

## 1. A backup restored into another folder is checked to open there

`library.restore` with `to` opened nothing, so a backup whose files all pass their checksums and are still no catalog was left in the folder as a library that doesn't open (the restore of the open library already found that out and took it back).

- The restored catalog is now tried: read as opening would read it, with everything that opening writes (an upgrade to this build's format, a repaired log) held in memory. Nothing in the folder changes.
- One that doesn't open is taken back as the in-place restore is: a library that was there is as it was, with the backup's files in `Replaced/<the time> (not opened)`; from a folder that held nothing, what the restore put there is removed again.
- While doing this I tightened how `to` is judged, since the take-back removes files: the folder is never emptied wholesale (only the names the restore placed are removed); a `to` with `..` in it is refused (it can come to mean another folder once part of the path is made); a folder that can't be looked at is refused rather than taken for missing or empty; and one lock is held across the restore, the check and the take-back.

title: fix(preview): avoid double-counting overwritten thumbnail files
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

When a thumbnail is regenerated using an existing cache key, the cache
replaces the JPEG on disk but adds the new file's entire size to its
recorded total.

Repeated writes to the same key therefore inflate the reported cache
usage even though only one JPEG exists on disk.

This can trigger premature cache pruning, unnecessary thumbnail
regeneration, and additional disk writes.

## Root Cause

`DiskCache::put()` updates its size accounting with:

    *total += bytes.len() as u64;

It does not account for the previous file occupying the same cache path.

## Changes

- Account for the previous JPEG size when replacing a cached thumbnail.
- Keep file replacement and size accounting synchronized under the
  existing mutex.
- Use saturating arithmetic to avoid accounting underflow or overflow.
- Release the accounting lock before pruning.
- Preserve the existing temporary-file and rename behavior.

## Regression Coverage

Added `disk_cache_overwrite_accounts_for_replaced_jpeg_only_once`.

The test checks that:

- Rewriting the same thumbnail does not increase recorded usage.
- Replacing a thumbnail with different encoded dimensions updates
  the size correctly.
- The recorded cache size matches the actual JPEG files on disk.
- An unrelated cached thumbnail remains accessible.

## Validation

The source changes and regression test are committed.

Not executed:
- cargo test -p lightcraft-preview
- cargo xtask ci

The Rust toolchain was unavailable in the working environment.
CI remains pending.

title: fix(import): exclude symlinked library folders from recursive scans
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Recursive folder imports are supposed to exclude LightCraft's own
library directory.

However, the current folder walker only checks whether a visited
directory's path exactly matches the excluded path.

When the library is reachable through a symbolic link, junction, or
an alias to its parent directory, this comparison can fail.

Consequently, a recursive import may enter the library and encounter
its existing originals or generated files.

## Root Cause

`files_in()` in `crates/engine/src/walk.rs` checks the excluded
directory using a lexical path comparison:

    path == skip

Different paths can refer to the same underlying directory.

Although the walker already resolves symlinks to prevent traversal
loops, that resolution was not used when enforcing the excluded
directory boundary.

## Changes

- Canonicalize the excluded library directory once.
- Compare resolved visited directories against that exclusion.
- Exclude both the library itself and directories beneath it.
- Preserve the existing lexical comparison.
- Keep the existing traversal limits and symlink-loop protection.

## Regression Coverage

Added
`skipped_library_stays_skipped_through_symlinks_and_ancestors`.

The test creates:

- An ordinary source photograph.
- A separate library containing an existing original.
- A symlink pointing directly to the library.
- A symlink pointing to the library's parent.

It verifies that the ordinary source photo remains discoverable
without including the library's existing original.

It also checks that a scan starting inside the excluded library
does not return files.

## Validation

The source changes and Unix regression test are committed.

Not executed:
- cargo test -p lightcraft-engine
- cargo xtask ci

The Rust toolchain was unavailable in the working environment.

Windows junction behavior and platform-specific filesystem behavior
have not been tested.
CI remains pending.

title: feat(shortcuts): add Lightroom Classic F6/F7 panel toggles
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Lightroom Classic supports function-key shortcuts for quickly
showing and hiding interface panels:

- F6: Show or hide the filmstrip.
- F7: Show or hide the left panel.

These interactions were missing from LightCraft's default keyboard
shortcuts.

Users transitioning from Lightroom Classic therefore have to use
different shortcuts or mouse controls for these common actions.

## Reference

Adobe's official Lightroom Classic keyboard shortcut documentation:

https://helpx.adobe.com/il_en/lightroom-classic/desktop/introduction-to-lightroom-classic/keyboard-shortcuts.html

## Changes

Add two secondary shortcut bindings:

- F6 -> view.filmstrip
- F7 -> view.leftPanel

Both commands already exist in LightCraft and manage the corresponding
UI state.

The implementation uses the existing secondary shortcut mechanism,
rather than introducing new commands or changing the panel system.

This preserves:

- Existing primary keyboard shortcuts.
- User-defined shortcut assignments.
- Existing panel visibility behavior.
- The keyboard shortcut editor's conflict handling.

## Regression Coverage

Added `classic_f6_and_f7_toggle_the_filmstrip_and_left_panel`.

The test checks that:

1. F6 toggles filmstrip visibility.
2. F7 toggles left-panel visibility.
3. Each shortcut affects only its intended panel.
4. Pressing each shortcut again restores the original visibility.

The existing shortcut tests also check that secondary bindings resolve
to valid commands and do not conflict with declared shortcuts.

## Validation

The source changes and regression test are committed.

Not executed:
- cargo test -p lightcraft-ui-egui
- cargo xtask ci

The Rust toolchain was unavailable in the working environment.

title: Reject stale mask results and disclose approximate selections
author: grlessa

title: perf(catalog): cache folded filename sort keys
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Filename sorting repeatedly allocates lowercase strings inside
the comparison function.

Previously, every comparison performed:

    a.file_name.to_lowercase()
        .cmp(&b.file_name.to_lowercase())

Sorting large photo collections requires O(n log n)
comparisons, generating many unnecessary temporary strings.

This contributes to the expensive library-wide query
rebuilds described in #1057.

## Changes

- Use `sort_by_cached_key` for filename sorting.
- Compute each photo's lowercase filename once per sort.
- Preserve case-insensitive ordering.
- Include the photo ID in the cached key for deterministic
  ordering when filenames compare equally.
- Preserve ascending and descending behavior.
- Leave all other sorting modes unchanged.

The number of lowercase-string constructions changes from
approximately O(n log n) to O(n).

## Regression Tests

Added tests covering:

- Case-insensitive filename ordering.
- Equal lowercase filenames.
- Stable ID tie-breaking.
- Ascending ordering.
- Descending ordering.

## Scope

This is a focused performance improvement.

It does not resolve the broader library cache-invalidation
problem in #1057, which still requires separate work.

## Validation

Regression test added but not executed.
Performance benchmarks and CI remain pending.

title: Import: what the photos themselves carry can be left in the files
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

Why one PR: the five kinds (keywords, ratings and labels, titles and captions, location, develop settings) all use one mechanism, `Photo::left_in_file` and one import option; splitting per kind would duplicate the option UI and the import branch.

## Problem

An import always took everything a photo says about itself into the library: the keywords, title, creator, copyright and GPS in the file, and the rating, label, keywords and develop settings of the sidecar beside it. This makes each of those a choice. Everything is still read unless chosen otherwise, so nothing changes for anyone who doesn't touch it.

The case behind it: moving a large library over from another manager, where the keywords and labels that matter live in that program's database and the ones in the files are stale or unwanted.

## Change

Five kinds can each be read, or left in the files:

- **Keywords** (with the named face regions that go with them)
- **Ratings and labels** (stars, pick / reject flags, colour labels)
- **Titles and captions** (with creator, copyright and its terms, and the accessibility texts)
- **Location** (GPS and the place by name)
- **Develop settings** a sidecar carries (LightCraft's own or another editor's `crs:`)

Where:

- **Settings ▸ Import ▸ Read from photos** sets it for the library (`library.preferences` → `import.read`).
- The **Import Photos** review has a **Read** row that opens with the library's choice and can differ for that one import (`library.import` → `read`, also on the MCP `import` tool).

Which camera and lens, the exposure, the capture time and the orientation are always read.

What the import itself adds still applies: the keywords typed in the review, a metadata preset, a develop preset, raw defaults.

### What "left in the files" means

This is the part I'd most like looked at.

- A kind that is not read is not brought into the library, and nothing is taken out of the file or its sidecar at import.
- **It also stays there afterwards.*…

title: LR-IMP-CAMERA-COVERAGE: verify 21 Sony and Leica models on CC0 files

title: fix: a folder listed twice in Local can't be collapsed (#1093)
author: mattsivak
body:
Fixes #1093.

## Cause
The video in the issue shows Local with **Home** open, which lists `C:\Users\…\Pictures` a second time inside it. Every Local row keyed its open state and its disclosure triangle's egui id by the folder's path only. So the two Pictures rows shared one triangle id: egui keeps one hit rect per id, and the copy drawn last (inside Home) took the clicks of the one drawn first. The top-level Pictures could no longer be collapsed. They also shared the open flag, so both copies opened and closed together. It looked tied to "many folders" because it only happens once a tree that contains another Local place (Home) is open.

## Fix
`folder_tree` now gets the top-level place it hangs from, and keys the open state, the reveal-once flag and the triangle's id by place + path. Every row opens and closes by itself. Widget names for the control channel (`folderToggle:<path>`, `source:local:<path>`) are unchanged.

## Test
`tests_masking::local_folder_listed_twice_opens_and_closes_each_row`: two Local places, one inside the other. It clicks each copy's triangle and checks that only that copy opens and then closes. It failed before the fix ("copy 0 opens": 0 rows) and passes now, along with the existing Local tree tests.

Local `cargo xtask ci` stops at clippy on `crates/pipeline/src/spots.rs:250` (the new `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` lint in Rust 1.99), which also fails on main and isn't touched here. In `lightcraft-ui-egui`, the only failing tests are the AI-denoise model-setup tests and one export-dialog layout check. They fail because this local build has no denoise runtime and no craft-fonts, and are unrelated to this change.

title: Preview cache: cached thumbnails are no longer taken for the person's photos (#610, #1066)
author: nledford
body:
Fixes #610 and fixes #1066.

## The problem

The thumbnail cache writes ordinary `.jpg` files into `<library>/thumbs`, and a library is usually inside the person's Pictures folder. Windows Photos / Gallery indexes that folder, so every cached thumbnail (one for each photo, size and state of its edits) is listed as a photo of the person's. On top of that, every cache hit set the file's modified time, so each launch made every thumbnail in view look new, which is what #1066 reads as "new copies on every launch".

I traced the cache key (content hash, settings hash, size bucket, render version, camera-profile key, the hasher) and found nothing that changes between launches; a demo library's 24 photos keep the same content and settings hashes across three reopens. So the files #1066 sees are real cache entries piling up and being re-dated, not the same thumbnail rendered again at each start. **I have not been able to test on Windows**; it would help if @egsk4 or the reporter of #610 could confirm with this build.

## What changes

1. **Cache files are no longer named as pictures.** `<2 hex>/<32 hex>.lcthumb`, the same JPEG data inside. This is the fix the maintainer outlined on #610.
2. **The `.jpg` files already there are taken over, not rendered again.** One that is asked for is renamed on the spot. The rest are renamed by a tidy pass that runs once per cache folder when its library opens: on its own thread, with a "Tidying the thumbnail cache" row in the activity stack that shows progress and can stop it (a 2 GB cache is some 100 000 files). A pass that was stopped, or could not rename something, is gone on with at the next open.
3. **Reading writes nothing.** The date is only brought forward for a file that went unused for a week. So that a full cache still lets go of what is not in use first, the thumbnails read in this session are remembered in memory and evicted last.
4. **A folder that holds nothing but the cache says so**: a `CACHEDIR.TAG` (the Cache Directory …
