title: HEIF: move the heic-rs pin from 0.1.1 to 0.1.4
author: s17sh70x2jfl031ag
body:
heic-rs 0.1.2 to 0.1.4 fix six panics on malformed files, which I found by fuzzing and reported privately upstream (credited in the [heic-rs changelog](https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)). Four panic in release builds: a `uuid` box too small for its extended type, a block starting right of the picture, a conformance window larger than the picture, and a reference row below the picture. Two only panic with overflow checks on: a PCM bit depth above the sample bit depth, and a slice QP out of range. heic-rs reports the API, MSRV and output as unchanged.

As `apps/lightcraft-web/Cargo.toml` notes, panics abort on wasm32, so the `catch_unwind` guard doesn't apply there. With 0.1.4 those files return an error instead. This mirrors the same change in PhotoCraft (storytold/photocraft#3637).

**The change:** both exact pins in `crates/heif/Cargo.toml` move to `=0.1.4`. `Cargo.lock` changes only heic-rs.

**Checked**, as the pin comment asks, on 0.1.1 and then on 0.1.4:
- `cargo test --release -p lightcraft-heif --features testdata`: 24 passed both times.
- `cargo test --release -p lightcraft-codecs --features heif --test heif --test corpus`: 8 passed both times, with the corpus from `cargo xtask corpus --download`.
- `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-heif -p lightcraft-codecs --features lightcraft-codecs/heif --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Unrelated, but noticed while fetching the corpus: `orf-olympus-e1.orf` no longer matches its pinned sha256 (got `79292964…`, expected `04228665…`), so `cargo xtask corpus --download` deletes it. The file at the source URL may have changed.

title: fix: left panel slow with a large keyword list (#1011)
author: mattsivak
body:
Fixes #1011.

The reporter found the slowdown goes away when the left sidebar's **Keywords** section is collapsed (58,000 photos, a very large keyword list).

**Cause**
- The Keywords section drew every keyword row on every frame (layout, text measuring, widget info, hover text, context menu), including the thousands out of sight.
- Every catalog edit bumps `revision`, and `Catalog::keyword_tree` was rebuilt from all photos with several `String` allocations per keyword level.

**Fix**
- **Shared helper `out_of_sight`** (`left.rs`): a tree section calls it before a row's per-row work. For a row out of sight, the row:
  - still takes its height (the layout and scroll range don't change),
  - is still registered as `source:…` (the control channel, agents and tests find it as before),
  - still notes its measured width (egui's text cache), so the content doesn't widen and narrow as you scroll.

  Keywords and Folders use it. Each loop is now "skip or draw, then recurse", with the drawn row in `keyword_row` / `folder_row`. Leaves no longer look up an open state.
- **A keyword made from the header's +**: its row is always drawn, and the sidebar scrolls to it instantly. The mechanism is general: a per-frame "scroll to row `<id>`" request (`SCROLL_TO_ROW`), set before the sections are drawn and cleared after, so there is no frame stamp and nothing is left behind. Before this, `the_keywords_header_creates_a_keyword` only passed because rows out of sight were registered too.
- **`keyword_tree`** works out each distinct keyword string's levels once and then only counts:
  - a per-level "last photo counted" stamp replaces the per-photo `HashSet<String>`,
  - the children lists are built as levels are created,
  - sorting uses the lower-case name it already computed.

  The output is unchanged; all 40 catalog keyword tests pass.

**Numbers** (58,000 photos × 6 keywords out of 4,000; release build on Apple Silicon; `probe_keyword_sidebar_cost`, ignored by default)

title: LR-EDIT-OPTICS-PROFILE: Sony ILCE-7RM6 lateral CA corrected on the raw mosaic before demosaic
author: dev-null-undefined
body:
Stacked on #824 (its six commits come first; this PR adds the last five). Draft until #824 merges.

## Why
#824 parses Sony's lateral-CA table (`0x7035`) but applies no CA: warping the red and blue channels *after* demosaic overshoots, because the demosaic borrows green's edge structure for red and blue and already hides ~70 % of the lens CA (measured corner R/G–B/G residual rms 0.032 → 0.052 px at 1440 when the three planes were on). Previews, which bin the mosaic instead, showed more than half of the lens CA while full renders showed about a third, so previews and exports disagreed.

## What
- **`crates/raw/src/lateral_ca.rs`:** a `LateralCa` map (serde, validation, radial LUT) resamples the red and blue **mosaic sites** before demosaic, each from same-colour sites only (4×4 Catmull-Rom; clipped or non-finite taps keep the site; green untouched). Applied in `RawImage::normalized()` after opcode list 2 and on the binned Thumb/Preview path, so every demosaic, every preview and the AI-denoise twin see aligned colours. ~90 ms per 24 MP on 4 cores.
- **`arw_lens_rm6::lateral_ca`** builds the map from the table (red half, blue half; knots on sensor radii at the distortion spacing; relative scale `c/3.36e6`, provisional; plausibility bound). None for linear-RGB files, non-3:2 crops (same gate as the distortion warp), empty crops, unknown bodies. The post-demosaic R/B planes are deleted. Wired in `arw.rs::decode`; `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 63 → 64.
- **Engine:** the camera-look fit and the pooled camera profiles keep seeing uncorrected proxies (fits unchanged, no `LOOK_VERSION` bump); the AI Denoise product key is salted for ARW / `.arw` photos (products made from the uncorrected mosaic are re-made once); DNG export is unchanged and guarded by a test (one-plane warp, no CA — Convert / Copy as DNG lose the CA correction, documented).
- The correction is part of decoding (like a DNG's OpcodeList2); **Enable Lens Corrections governs distortion only**.

title: CLI --import <folder> uses the engine's import extensions (#1080)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #1080

`lightcraft-cli run --import <folder>` walked folders with its own `PHOTO_EXTENSIONS` list in `crates/mcp/src/headless.rs`. That list was a copy of the engine's `import::EXTENSIONS` and had fallen behind: it was missing heic, heif and nrw. So the flag silently skipped HEIC files that `library.import` on the same folder took. The MCP tools that expand folders go through the same `expand_paths`, so they had the same gap.

`expand_paths` now filters with `lightcraft_engine::import::is_supported` and the copied list is gone, along with its `pub use` from `lightcraft-mcp`. Nothing else in the workspace used it. The desktop file pickers and the import dialog already used the engine list. I left the other extension lists alone because they are meant to differ: `xtask/src/assets.rs` is the asset attribution check, and `raw_files` in the CLI is a raw-only subset for its own command. HEIC without the `heif` feature works the same as `library.import`: the file is picked up and the import reports it as failed with the reason.

New test `expand_paths_takes_the_engine_extensions`: it makes one file for every engine extension plus `B.HEIC` and a `.txt` in a temp folder and checks that the walk returns exactly the supported ones. It failed before the fix (heic, heif, nrw and HEIC were missing) and passes now. I ran fmt, clippy -D warnings on lightcraft-mcp and lightcraft-cli (with `--no-deps`), and the tests for both crates. I didn't run the full `cargo xtask ci` locally and left that to GitHub CI. Workspace clippy fails here on an unrelated lint in `crates/pipeline/src/spots.rs` (`chunks_exact_to_as_chunks`, new in my local clippy 1.99). I didn't try it by hand with real iPhone HEICs.

## Share to Flickr (LRC-LIB-PUBLISH ⬜ → 🟡)

Share chosen photos to a Flickr account, rendered with their edits, from **File → Share ▸ Flickr…** or the top
bar's share icon. It's a one-way upload for showcasing work, not a publish collection: nothing on Flickr is tracked,
republished or deleted afterwards. The menu is called Share so more destinations can be added beside Flickr
(Google Photos is the likely next one).

### What users get
- **Settings → Accounts → Flickr** walks through connecting, step by step: open Flickr's non-commercial API key page,
  paste the key and secret, **Continue** opens Flickr's approval page in the browser, and pasting the code Flickr
  shows (`123-456-789`) finishes the sign-in by itself. LightCraft never sees the Flickr password. The account is
  kept in `<config>/flickr.json` (atomic, owner-only on Unix), not in the library; `--memory` sessions don't load it.
- **Share to Flickr** dialog: size (1024 / 2048 / 4096 px / full), JPEG quality, visibility (public, friends,

  every time).

  signs out; a photo that can't join the album still counts as uploaded and the toast says so.

title: LRC-LIB-UPDATEFOLDER: Update Folder Location for agents (folder.updateLocation, #1116)
author: mattsivak
body:
Part of #1116 (first step). Also the engine half of #1112.

## What

`folder.updateLocation {path, to}`: Lightroom Classic's **Update Folder Location**, for agents and MCP. A library folder or disk that is now somewhere else can be pointed at its new place as **one undo step**. That covers a folder moved or renamed outside LightCraft, a USB disk or NAS that came back at another drive letter or mount point, `/Volumes/tokyo` back as `/Volumes/TOKYO`, and a library made on another machine (`D:\Photos\…`).

- Every photo in the folder, and in the folders inside it, is relinked to the same names under `to`.
- Colour labels (folder records) go along: `folder_records_follow`, as Rename / Move Folder already does.
- A chosen folder (source or filter) follows, and so do undo and redo.
- No file is touched, and the old place doesn't need to exist.
- Folders are compared by identity (`folder_key`), so either separator works and so does Windows case.
- The command is refused, changing nothing, when:
  - one folder is inside the other;
  - a photo would land on one the library already has there;
  - it's the library's own folder;
  - `to` isn't a folder.

## How

This is `move_folder` (Rename / Move Folder) without the disk rename. It's a `Batch` of the existing `Op::Relink`s plus the folder-record ops, so **there's no new op and no catalog format change**. It doesn't touch `journal::VERSION`, so it can't collide with #800 / #814 / #974.

The one engine change outside the command: `FolderMove` gains `on_disk`. The undo entry still carries the folder, so undo and redo make the chosen folder follow, but with `on_disk: false` they never rename anything on disk.

#1116 proposed a root table (`(root, relative path)`) first. While writing this, I found the existing relink + folder-record machinery already gives the user-visible result, without a format bump. The root table can still come later, if you want it for #880 (per-device paths) or to keep a whole-disk move small in the log. E…

title: LRC-LIB-LIBFOLDERS: catalog queries and streamed file hashing for locating a folder (part 1 of 3)
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

This is part 1 of 3 of locating a library folder that is somewhere else now (#1112, #1194). It changes nothing a person or an agent can see: the other two parts open off `main` one after the other, each when the one before it has landed.

## Problem

A folder of the library that was moved, renamed or mounted under another name can't be pointed at its new place. The feature that fixes it needs three things that the library does not have yet, and they are easier to review apart from the engine and the menus that use them:

- a way to carry a folder's records (colour labels) to a place where the library already knows other folders, without clearing those;
- a way to tell, for a set of files, which Local records (photos that were only browsed) can give way to library photos and which hold something of the person's;

## Change

- `Catalog::folder_records_located(from, to)`: like `folder_records_follow`, but records of other library folders at or below the destination stay (nothing arrived there). Both share one body; `folder_records_follow` is unchanged (clears the destination, as before).

title: LR-MERGE-HDR: merges of raws without colour matrices keep their colour (#965)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #965

An HDR merge of Canon CR2 files came out green and dark, while each CR2 on its own rendered fine. The merge decoded every raw itself and wrote the reference frame's own colour tags into the DNG. A CR2 has none: its colour is a look fitted to its embedded camera JPEG when it is opened. So the merged DNG had no camera colour and no white balance.

Now each source goes through `starting_colour`, as when it is opened alone, and the result is written as DNG tags:

- one forward matrix (the look's matrix on top of the camera transform), with a colour matrix and `AsShotNeutral` that agree with it at the as-shot white
- what the look does to the brightness of white, as baseline exposure
- the look's hue/saturation table as `ProfileHueSatMap`
- its tone curve as `ProfileToneCurve`, which `files::dng_tone_curve` already reads back

Raws with colour matrices of their own (DNG) keep their tags, and nothing extra is computed for them. Without a fitted look, the tags give the colour the raw falls back to (spectral matrices or the neutral fallback). HDR, panorama and HDR panorama all load frames the same way, so panoramas get this too. #917 (A6600 panorama colour shift) may have the same cause; that has not been checked against an ARW panorama.

**How:** `lightcraft_merge::load_frame_with` takes a callback that can supply a raw's colour tags (`load_frame` is unchanged), because the merge crate sits below the engine. `MergeJob::load` passes `camera_preview::starting_colour_tags`.

**Not quite identical to the single photo:**
- A DNG hue/saturation table doesn't keep each pixel's luminance the way the fitted table does (`HueSat`). Writing it anyway was measured to be closer than leaving it out, on every measure below.
- The look's chroma curve has no DNG tag, so it is left out.

title: Synchronize Folder: the scan can continue in the background
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

Why one PR: "Continue in Background" needs the activity-stack row, the done notice and the click-to-reopen result together; each part is meaningless without the others. Size: 963 changed lines, of which about 290 are logic (engine `sync.rs`, UI `sync.rs`, `activity.rs`, `lib.rs`, `dialogs.rs`), about 425 are tests and about 220 are the 17 locale catalogs; the rest is docs. The logic is well under 800, and the part that could be cut off (the engine's change) has no behaviour of its own.

## Problem

Synchronize Folder… scans on a worker thread, but its dialog is modal and closing it stops the scan. On a large folder over a network share that holds the app for minutes with nothing to do but watch the count.

## Change

- **While the folder is scanned** the dialog's button is **Continue in Background**. The dialog closes and the scan goes on under its row in the activity stack.
- **When the scan is done nothing pops up.** A notice in the activity stack says how many changes were found, or that the folder isn't there. It stays until it is clicked or dismissed.
- **A click on the notice** opens the dialog with that result and what was ticked, without scanning again. ✕ lets go of it.
- **A scan with nothing to do** only says so in a toast.
- Cancel and the row's ✕ stop the scan as before.

Rules it keeps:

- **One folder at a time.** Synchronize Folder on another folder is refused, with the reason, while a background scan runs or its notice waits. The same folder is scanned afresh.
- **A stale result is not acted on.** This was already so: Synchronize refuses a scan whose folder's photos changed meanwhile and scans again.
- **Another library opened** lets go of the scan and its notice.
- **Synchronize waits 0.6 s after the scan ends.** The one button reads Continue in Background and then Synchronize; a click meant for the first, landing as the scan ends, can't start the second.
- A dialog that is open is not replaced by the notice's result.

title: LR-EDIT-OPTICS-PROFILE: in-camera crop modes get the frame's crop factor, not the body's
author: Madcat71
body:
## What

Lens profiles from a lensfun-format database (`LIGHTCRAFT_LENSFUN_DIR`) were scaled by the **body's** crop factor whenever the camera was in the database. A full-frame body shooting a crop of its sensor (APS-C / Super 35 mode, or switched there by an APS-C lens) therefore had the full frame's corner distortion and vignetting applied to the corners of the crop.

`lookup` now uses the crop factor of the **recorded frame** (`frame_crop_factor`): when the EXIF 35 mm equivalent focal length implies a crop factor more than 10 % above the body's, that wins; within 10 % the difference is the tag's whole-millimetre rounding and the body's value stands. Without the body in the database the 35 mm equivalent is used, as before.

## Evidence

- Sony ILCE-1M2 + FE 100-400mm F4.5-5.6 GM OSS at 400 mm: the r³ warp coefficient in APS-C mode was the full frame's 0.0215; it is now 0.0096 (= 0.0215 / 1.5²).
- Checked on 19 private ILCE-1M2 ARWs (FE 100-400mm GM and Sigma 24-70mm F2.8 DG DN | Art, full frame and APS-C, firmware 2.01–4.00). Every APS-C coefficient is the full-frame one scaled by 1/1.5². The files are not included.

## Tests

- New: `lens_profiles::tests::in_camera_crop_mode_uses_the_frames_crop_factor`. It fails on `main`: in its profile the APS-C frame's vignetting gain is 0.40 instead of 0.18. It covers APS-C mode, full frame, a rounded 35 mm equivalent, no body in the database and a hostile focal length.
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-engine -p lightcraft-lensdb`: lensdb 17/17. In engine, the lens profile tests and everything else pass except 20 sidecar / rename / filesystem-history tests that fail identically on unmodified `main` on Windows 11 (not related to this change).
- `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-engine -p lightcraft-lensdb --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean apart from `clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` in `crates/pipeline/src/spots.rs`, a new lint in Rust 1.99 that is unrelated to this change. `cargo fmt --check` is clean.

title: perf(gpu): LR-BEHAV-GPU: horizontal box blur reads adjacent pixels (Windows Radeon export 3.7 s → 1.9 s)
author: THEtheChad
body:
## Summary

Full-size GPU exports with noise reduction and spatial edits were about 1.9× slower than CPU exports on a Windows Radeon 780M iGPU (DX12). With `LIGHTCRAFT_PROFILE`, the NR stage and the spatial planes accounted for about 92 % of the GPU render time. Both are built from `gaussian()`, and its horizontal box pass (`box_h`) caused most of the slowdown.

`box_h` gave each thread 16 consecutive pixels of a row to slide a running sum over. Adjacent threads therefore read pixels 16 apart (64–192 bytes apart, more for wide windows where the stretch grows to 128 px), so the reads were not coalesced. On the same buffers the vertical pass (`box_v`, adjacent threads in adjacent columns) ran 9–15× faster.

This PR changes `box_h` to one thread per pixel, which sums its 2r + 1 window. Adjacent threads now read adjacent pixels, which the cache serves. The workgroup shape (64×4), bindings, parameters and dispatch limits are the same as before. `box_v` is unchanged. Quality is unchanged too: there are no new settings, tolerances or fallbacks, and the CPU pipeline is untouched.

## Measurements

Hardware: Windows 11, AMD Radeon 780M (DX12). Measured with release builds of `0ba118de` (before) and of this change on that base (after). The branch has since been rebased onto current `main` without conflicts. The test suites and `bench_kernels` were re-run on the rebased commit; the end-to-end export timings were not repeated.

`bench_kernels` (ignored test, 6000 × 4000, best of 5):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| box_h, 1 / 2 / 3 channels, r = 2 | 48.0 / 121.6 / 128.7 ms | 5.1 / 5.8 / 8.5 ms |
| (box_v, same inputs) | 3.2 / 8.5 / 13.6 ms | unchanged |
| Gaussian σ = 2, 1 / 2 / 3 channels | 149.7 / 388.0 / 448.8 ms | 17.4 / 52.5 / 94.9 ms |
| guided filter σ = 1.75 (luminance NR) | 827.7 ms | 146.3 ms |
| Gaussian 3 ch σ = 4.5 (colour NR) | 494.9 ms | 103.9 ms |

During the investigation I also compared one-thread-per-pixel summing with the old sliding kernel at r = 2…400…

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: a float raw with NaN or infinite samples no longer panics the demosaic
author: dev-null-undefined
body:
## The bug

A floating-point CFA DNG with NaN samples panics the AHD and PPG demosaics. A pre-existing never-crash violation, found by the never-crash probe in the lateral-CA review.

- AHD and PPG clamp each green estimate between its two neighbouring greens: `est.clamp(a.min(b), a.max(b))`.
- When both greens are NaN, the bounds are NaN, and `f32::clamp` panics (`min > max, or either was NaN`). The panic is at `demosaic/ppg.rs:45` and in AHD's green pass under `ahd.rs:27`.
- **How a hostile file reaches it:** float DNG samples go from the strip or tile straight into `RawData::F32`, and nothing checks them. Two adjacent NaN greens are enough to crash `decode` → `develop(Method::Ahd | Method::Ppg)`. AHD is the default method.
- Bilinear does not panic, but its output is NaN.
- ±∞ alone does not panic, but it turns into NaN in the demosaic arithmetic (∞ − ∞).

## The fix (two layers)

1. **Demosaic** (`crates/raw/src/demosaic`): a `clamp_between(v, a, b)` helper replaces the three clamps (PPG once, AHD twice).
   - With non-NaN bounds it makes the same `v.clamp(a.min(b), a.max(b))` call, so finite results are bit-identical.
   - With NaN bounds it returns `v` unclamped.
   - This removes the panic whatever puts NaN into the mosaic.
2. **DNG decode** (`crates/raw/src/dng.rs`): non-finite float samples are replaced at the point where the white level is known.
   - NaN and −∞ read as black (0).
   - +∞ reads as the white level (a clipped highlight).
   - No sensor records NaN or infinity, so a valid file is never touched. Finite samples, negative or above white included, stay as stored. The image therefore develops to finite values instead of NaN pixels that spread through later blurs and statistics.
   - Float `RawData` only comes from `tiffraw::read_image`. Of its callers, only the DNG / DNG-layout decoder keeps float data: ARW rejects it, and the semantic-mask reader converts it with its own finite check. `dng.rs` is therefore the one place that needs the change.

##…

title: perf(pipeline): #1145 keep mask alphas in the stage cache (Exposure drag with 3 masks: 176-332 ms to 32-60 ms)
author: THEtheChad
body:
## What and why Fixes #1145. The two architecture proposals in that issue (tiled rendering, cancelling renders) aren't addressed here and could move to their own issue. Every render evaluated every visible mask from scratch, on the CPU and the GPU, because the stage cache held no mask alphas. A global Exposure drag on a 24 MP photo with three ordinary masks therefore cost 176–332 ms per loupe tick, against about 27 ms without masks. Most of that time went to masks whose alphas hadn't changed. This PR caches the evaluated alphas in the existing stage cache, and mirrors the cache in `GpuStages`. Each alpha is keyed by exactly what it reads, so warm renders stay bit-identical to cold ones. - **`masks::alpha_key`** hashes the mask's components (full `Debug`, so brush dabs and stored segmentations are included), Refine Edges, Invert and Amount, and `geo` (frame incl. crop, orientation, zoom window and output size). It adds `lin_key` only for masks that read the image (Luminance / Colour Range, Sky / Subject / Background / People heuristics, Object without a stored segmentation, Auto Mask brushes, Refine Edges). It adds the global exposure only for masks that read it (Luminance / Colour Range, Sky). `masks::reads` decides this with an exhaustive `match`, so a new `MaskShape` has to declare its inputs before it compiles, and doubtful cases count as "reads it". The mask's other sliders, name and id are not in the key, so dragging a mask's own Exposure or Clarity reuses its alpha. - **`masks::AlphaCache

`** (`P` = CPU `Plane` or device `Buf`) holds only the last render's visible masks, one plane each. It is tied to the source's segmentation mattes by `Arc` identity, and is kept per `CacheEntry` / GPU `Entry`, so a draft size and a loupe size each keep their own. `Evaluated::alpha` becomes `Arc`, so a hit is a reference count, not a copy. On the GPU, a hit is one buffer copy into the combined alpha buffer, and it skips the `lin` / `log_l` readback that CPU-evalua…

title: LR-BEHAV-BG-TASKS: a render job that panics fails instead of never answering
author: dev-null-undefined
body:
## Bug

A panic inside `RenderJob::run` or `QuickJob::run` (a raw decoder or CPU pipeline bug) unwound the job-pool worker without sending a result.

- **The view waited forever.** The slot stayed pending and its key was never asked for again, so the loupe kept rendering and the thumbnail stayed blank.
- **Rendering could stop altogether.** The pool never replaces a dead worker, so after as many such panics as it has workers (2–6), no photo rendered until LightCraft was restarted.

## Fix

- **Both `run`s go through `guard::catch`.** A panic comes back as the job's failed `RenderResult`, with the same request id, key and photo.
- **The renderer treats it like any failed render.** The photo fails like one that can't be opened, with the reason. It isn't retried until the catalog changes, so there's no panic loop, and the workers live on. The panic is still logged with its location.
- **Why `RenderJob::run` and not `JobPool`:** the pool is generic and can't make a result out of a panic. `run` is the one place every render goes through: the pool, export, Build Previews, contact sheets, and the face and AI-mask workers. `lightcraft_raw` has no guard of its own (unlike `codecs` and `heif`), so this is where raw-decoder panics land. It's a safety net; a real decoder panic still needs its own fix.
- **Cleanup:** the watermark preview's own `catch_unwind` is now redundant, so it's gone.
- **Web:** the web build is `panic = "abort"`, so nothing changes there.

## Tests

Both tests panicked or hung before the fix:

- **`media::…::a_render_that_panics_fails_instead_of_never_answering`:** a render and a stand-in whose loader panics. Pins the request id, key, level and the message.
- **`render::…::a_panicking_render_is_a_failure_not_a_dead_worker`:** uses the real job pool. Checks that the slot stops waiting, the failure is kept, nothing is retried, and the workers survive.

## CI

`cargo xtask ci` steps pass. Two exceptions, both already on main:

- **Clippy:** Rust 1.98's new `…

title: LR-VIEW-DETAIL: the loupe says when the render behind a stand-in fails
author: dev-null-undefined
body:
**Stacked on #1032.** Review the last commit only: `LR-VIEW-DETAIL: the loupe says when the render behind a stand-in fails`.

## What

When a photo's render failed while the loupe showed its embedded JPEG, a cached render or a thumbnail, that stand-in stayed up as if it were the photo. "This photo can't be opened" only appeared when nothing at all could be drawn.

Now a caution pill appears where "Rendering…" goes (widget `loupe:renderFailed`):

- **What it says:** "Original offline · no smart preview" when that's the reason, otherwise "This photo can't be opened". Both strings already exist and are translated.
- **Where the reason is:** on hover, and in the screen-reader label.
- **For agents:** `ui.inspect` → `loupe.failed`. `docs/control-protocol.md` now tells agents waiting for a finished loupe to stop when it's set; before, such an agent would wait forever on a failed photo.
- **Retries:** a library change (a rating, an import) retries failed renders. While a retry of the same key runs, the pill stays and "Rendering…" doesn't take over, so it doesn't blink.
- **One photo's error isn't another's.** The renderer now records which photo a failure belongs to (`Renderer::failure_of`). The centre message no longer flashes the previous photo's error after a step.

## Tests

`headless::tests::the_loupe_says_so_when_the_render_behind_a_stand_in_fails`:

- A render offload fails every loupe render. The test checks that the pill appears over a stand-in, `loupe.failed` is set, the pill stays (with no "Rendering…") while a rating retries the render, and it's gone back on a photo that rendered.
- The retry assertion fails without the retry rule.
- The test offload is shared (`headless::RenderGate`), and #1032's test uses it too.

Plus a unit check that one photo's error isn't another's.

`cargo xtask ci` steps pass, with the same two exceptions already on main as in #1032.

title: LR-VIEW-COMPARE: Compare and Reference panes say "Rendering…" as the loupe does
author: dev-null-undefined
body:
**Stacked on #1032 and #1150.** Review the last commit only: `LR-VIEW-COMPARE: Compare and Reference panes say "Rendering…" as the loupe does`.

## What

Compare and Reference View are where focus is checked at 1:1. Their panes show the same stand-ins as the loupe: a thumbnail while the photo renders, the last render after an edit, and the magnified frame under a window that hasn't arrived yet. Each pane now behaves like the loupe:

- **"Rendering…" pill:** once a render has been on its way for 0.5 s with nothing new (widget `compare:rendering:<pane>`).
- **Failed pill:** when the render failed behind a thumbnail, with the reason on hover (`compare:renderFailed:<pane>`).
- **Survey:** its small fit tiles don't show either pill.

Details:

- **Slider drags.** Compare panes have no draft renders, so a slider drag on the photo would leave its pane saying "Rendering…" for the whole drag. The photo being dragged doesn't count until the drag ends.
- **Each pane's wait belongs to the photo in it.** A photo that moves in (swap, Make Select) starts its own wait.
- **Retries** keep the failed pill, as in the loupe.

## Tests

- **`tests_compare::a_compare_pane_says_rendering_while_its_edit_renders`:** holds renders, then checks no pill at first, the pill after the wait, and none once the render lands.

`cargo xtask ci` steps pass, with the same two exceptions already on main as in #1032.

title: perf: #1057 slider ticks keep views that read no develop state (on #1660's change tracking)
author: THEtheChad
body:
## What and why

#1660 and #1662 landed per-photo change tracking (`Catalog::aspects_since`, `touched_since`, `AlbumTally`): a small edit is followed by re-checking only the photos it touched. That fixed most of #1057, but a slider tick still paid for its follow. `Session::visible()` re-checked the touched photo, rebuilt the list and handed out a new generation 60 times a second, so the grid rebuilt its date runs, stack index and layout on every tick. Several sidebar caches were still keyed on the raw `catalog.revision`.

**This PR has been rebuilt on top of #1660 and #1662.** The earlier version added a second counter (`library_revision` / `view_revision`) next to the revision. That would now be a second invalidation mechanism alongside `Aspects`, so it's gone. What's left adds the one thing main's tracking lacks for views: knowing whether a view reads develop state.

- **catalog** (`crates/catalog/src/reads.rs`, new): `Filter`/`Sort`/`RuleSet::reads_develop`, and `Catalog::filter_reads_develop` / `album_reads_develop`. title: LR-LIB-DELETE: the engine can move a file to the system Trash and put it back
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

Why one PR: the Trash back-end is one module with no seam. The macOS, Linux and fallback back-ends and the disk-Trash safety judgement share one set of rules, and no part of it can land, be tested and be reverted alone. About 700 of the 1,197 changed lines are code, the rest are its unit tests.

Part of #565 (the "Delete from Disk" choice). This is the first of five pull requests that replace the one this was; each is off `main`.

## Problem

Every way out of the library leaves a photo's file where it is: Delete, Delete Permanently, Empty Recently Deleted, Remove Folder from Library. There is no way, in the app or for an agent, to take a photo out of the library **and** move its file to the system Trash, as Lightroom Classic's "Delete from Disk" does. Moving a file to the Trash is the first thing that needs to exist, and it has to be safe: on a disk's own Trash, a wrong judgement can put a photographer's file where someone else can swap or read it.

## Change

`crates/engine/src/trash.rs` (new), `crates/engine/src/lib.rs` (`pub mod trash;`), `crates/engine/Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` (`rustix` for the Unix file checks; `objc2-foundation` features for macOS).

- **`Bin`** is the Trash as the engine uses it: `trash` (says where the file went, when the Trash tells), `put_back` (never replaces what is at the place now), `erase` (only for a disk with no Trash, and only when a later question asks for it), `works_here` and `trash_here`.
- **`SystemBin`** is the real one. **macOS** uses the Finder's Trash through `NSFileManager`. **Linux and the other Unixes** use the freedesktop.org Trash in plain file operations: the home Trash for files on its disk, else the disk's own `.Trash-<uid>`. **Windows and the web:** not yet; asking is refused and no file is touched.
- **A disk's own Trash is used only where nobody else can swap it.** Our folder must be a real folder, never a link, owned by the process's user and private (`0700`). A top folder that is…

title: Import from cameras that don't mount as a disk (PTP/MTP) on Windows (#1005)
author: mrfredman
body:
Part of #1005: the Windows side of importing from cameras that don't mount as a disk.

## What it does

Cameras and phones that only talk PTP/MTP over USB (here a Fujifilm X100T; also Leica M11, most phones) now show up in **File ▸ Import from Device** next to cards. Choosing one copies the photos the library doesn't have yet off the camera (activity row with bytes and ✕), then opens the usual import review with **Move** checked, so each photo leaves the staging folder once it is verified and catalogued.

On Windows the OS's own MTP/PTP class driver (`WUDFWpdMtp`) owns these devices, so a raw-USB client (the `nusb` approach in #1005) would need users to swap drivers with Zadig/WinUSB. This reads them through **Windows Portable Devices**, the API Explorer and Photos use: nothing to install, and the device is opened `GENERIC_READ`, so nothing on the camera is ever changed.

title: LR-EDIT-OPTICS-PROFILE: decode Sony shading, CA and distortion tables (nothing new applied), plus a BigTIFF overflow fix
author: AlexChambers
body:
Sony ARWs record three lens corrections per shot in the raw image IFD: shading (vignetting), lateral chromatic aberration (CA) and distortion, each as a camera setting plus a radial table, with copies in the encrypted `SR2SubIFD`. Until now LightCraft read only the distortion table, and only for the ILCE-7RM4A. This PR decodes all three components with their settings and provenance for every body that records them, and keeps them with the image so later work can validate and apply them. **It applies nothing new**: the ILCE-7RM4A distortion stays exactly as it is, and no other body or component gains a correction.

Two commits, based on `main` 76b5377:

1. `LR-EDIT-OPTICS-PROFILE`: the decoder, its data model, the bounded `SR2Private` lookup and the TIFF reader rules it shares.
2. `LR-IMP-FORMATS`: a separate, pre-existing TIFF reader fix (a BigTIFF next-IFD overflow), last so it can be reviewed on its own.

## What it decodes

| Component | Raw IFD setting / table | `SR2SubIFD` setting / table | Accepted layout |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shading | `0x7031` / `0x7032` | `0x797c` / `0x797d` | SHORT\[1\]; SSHORT\[17\]: 16, then 16 samples |
| Lateral CA | `0x7034` / `0x7035` | `0x797f` / `0x7980` | SHORT\[1\]; SSHORT\[33\]: 32, then two 16-sample curves |
| Distortion | `0x7036` / `0x7037` | `0x7981` / `0x7982` | SHORT\[1\]; SSHORT\[17\]: 16, then 16 samples |

- The record is `RawInfo::lens_metadata` / `RawImage::lens_metadata` (`LensMetadata { sony: Option<SonyLensCorrections> }`, `crates/raw/src/lens_metadata.rs`), filled by `crates/raw/src/vendor/arw_lens.rs`. It is `#[serde(default)]`, so older JSON without it still deserialises, and header and full decode produce the same record.
- Settings keep their stored number and a documented meaning (ExifTool tag-name documentation): shading 256 Off, 257 and 272 Auto, 511 unavailable; CA 0 Off, 1 Auto, 255 unavailable; distortion 0 Off, 1 Auto, 17 Auto fixed by the lens, 255 unavailable. Anything else is `Unknown(value)`, never…

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: DNG CFAPattern is anchored at the ActiveArea, not the sensor (#1086)
author: radialmonster
body:
Fixes #1086. Also fixes #1161 (same cause).

**Cause.** A DNG's CFAPattern tag describes the pattern at the top-left of the ActiveArea, but `RawImage::cfa` is anchored at the sensor origin (the crop to the active area shifts it by the area's offset). The DNG reader used the tag as-is, so when the ActiveArea starts on an odd row or column, the CFA phase flipped (RGGB read as GBRG) and the image rendered magenta. Lightroom-converted Canon DNGs hit this: the 60D DNG on #1086 and the 600D DNG on #1161 both have ActiveArea `51 142 3516 5344` (top row 51).

**Change.**
- `dng.rs`: shift the tag's pattern by the ActiveArea offset, out to the sensor origin.
- `dngwrite.rs`: write the pattern back relative to the ActiveArea, so our own DNGs round-trip.
- `tests/dng.rs`: odd-offset read and write round-trip.
- Bump `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` (61 → 62) so stale magenta thumbnails re-render.

**Measured** (`lightcraft-cli render`, defaults, whole-image means):

| File | main 76b53778 R/G, B/G | this PR R/G, B/G | camera JPEG |
|---|---|---|---|
| #1086 Canon 60D DNG (ActiveArea top 51) | 130.8, 99.9 | 1.006, 0.998 | n/a |
| #1161 Canon 600D DNG (ActiveArea top 51) | 7.62, 6.38 | 0.875, 0.802 | 0.849, 0.809 |
| Leica S (Typ 007) DNG (even offset) | identical PNG | identical PNG | |
| iPhone 15 Pro Max Bayer DNG (even offset) | identical PNG | identical PNG | |

Follow-up, not in this PR: the #1161 render is a little darker overall than its camera JPEG (a tone question, not the CFA).

Tests: `cargo test -p lightcraft-raw` passes (Windows).

title: LR-BEHAV-RENDER-FIDELITY: tools/render_fidelity.py measures single-slider responses against your own Lightroom exports
author: AlexChambers
body:
Part of gap 3 (LR-BEHAV-RENDER-FIDELITY). As proposed in #523, this adds a way for anyone with Lightroom to measure how LightCraft's Basic-panel sliders respond compared with Lightroom's, on their own raws and their own Lightroom exports, and to share the numbers without sharing photos.

Rebased onto main `0da998f2` after integration batch 40. This branch inherits main's `LOOK_VERSION` 9 and `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 64.

`tools/render_fidelity.py` is a stand-alone Python tool. Its only dependencies are numpy and tifffile, pinned in `tools/requirements-render-fidelity.txt`. The guide is `docs/render-fidelity.md`. Nothing in the product changes.

## What it does

| Command | |
|---|---|
| `plan` | writes Lightroom develop presets for a recipe list (generated from the recipe values, nothing copied from Adobe), plus export instructions |
| `pair` | scans a folder of the user's Lightroom TIFF exports and their raws, and builds same-session pairs: a recipe (one slider moved) and a reference of the same photo from the same export session |
| `render` | renders the same two recipes with `lightcraft-cli` through a sidecar-free link to the raw, and registers each reference against LightCraft's render |
| `score` | compares each engine's own response (recipe minus reference, in stops of linear luminance) position by position, per band of tone |
| `report` | writes a numbers-only Markdown summary, with an appendix of every band and transition, that can be pasted into an issue |
| `selftest` | 216 synthetic checks, including a 20-mode fault-injection matrix; `selftest --cli PATH` adds 20 that run LightCraft's own importer |

## The method

The method is a public version of the private harness behind the numbers in #523. Its rules:

- **Responses, not looks.** Each engine is measured against its own reference, so the slider is compared and LightCraft's different starting look (gap 1) isn't counted as a slider error. The absolute ΔE is reported alongside.

title: fix(cli): --connect 7980 takes a bare port as loopback (#1178)
author: rollroyces
body:
Closes #1178.

**Cause.** `apps/lightcraft-cli/src/main.rs` parses `--connect [ADDR]` (optional address). The check `args.get(i + 1).filter(|a| a.contains(':'))` only consumed the next token when it looked like a full `HOST:PORT`, so a bare port like `7980` (the natural thing to type after starting the app with `lightcraft --control 7980`) was left unconsumed and parsed as a command id. With the app on the default address `127.0.0.1:7980`, the parser would still reach the app — but only by accident — and emit `{"error":"unknown command `7980`","ok":false}`.

**Fix.** Two parser sites have the same shape — the global `--connect` in `cli()` and the per-step `--connect` in `run_step()`. Both now consume a token that is either `HOST:PORT` (existing behaviour) **or** all-digits (a bare port), and format the bare port as `127.0.0.1:<port>`. Non-numeric, non-`HOST:PORT`-shaped tokens (e.g. `ui.inspect` after `--connect`) keep falling through, so `lightcraft-cli run --connect ui.inspect` (default address, then `ui.inspect`) still works.

**Test.** New `connect_bare_port_is_treated_as_loopback_port`: the failure hint must name the port the parser actually chose to use, for `--connect 7980`, `--connect 127.0.0.1:7980`, and `--connect=7980`. `cargo test -p lightcraft-cli` → 21 passed, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-cli --no-deps` clean.

author: Ni-zav
body:
The Presets panel retains its Amount slider after a preset is applied.

Previously, changing Amount always executed edit.undo before
reapplying the preset. If the user had edited another setting or
switched photos, this could undo an unrelated change.

The slider now tracks the preset's selection, active photo, and
undo-history state.

Amount adjustments are allowed only while the original preset
remains the latest undoable operation. The slider is invalidated
when another edit or selection change makes that assumption unsafe.

Also avoids retaining slider state after a failed preset application.

Adds regression tests for:
- An unrelated develop edit made after applying a preset.
- Switching to another photo before changing Amount.

Validation: Regression tests added; Rust tests not run locally.

title: LR-EDIT-COLOR-GRADING: Cmd/Ctrl-drag keeps the saturation, Alt/Option fine-adjusts the colour wheels (#1160)
author: atmikshetty
body:
Refs #1160

**Context:** #1160 asks for the colour-grading wheel to move only perpendicular to the tangent (along the spoke) so the saturation can change while the hue stays put. Shift-drag already does that: it has kept the puck's own hue since `d6cfab82` whenever its saturation is 1 or more. This PR pins that behaviour with tests and adds Lightroom's other two wheel modifiers, so the wheels now match Lightroom Classic's full set.

**What changes** (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/edit.rs`, `grading_wheel`):

- **Cmd/Ctrl-drag** keeps the puck's saturation and changes only the hue: the puck moves round its circle, and the circle is drawn as the guide (as Shift draws the spoke). Shift wins when both are down, since keeping both would freeze the puck.
- **Alt/Option-drag** fine-adjusts: the puck moves a tenth as far as the pointer (the sliders' fine-adjust factor), counted from the press so no travel is lost to egui's drag threshold. It combines with Shift and Cmd/Ctrl.
- Pressing or releasing a modifier mid-drag re-grabs the puck as it is at that moment (`WheelGrab`). `wheel_pick` takes a `WheelLock` (`Hue` / `Sat`) and returns finite values for any input (NaN/inf pointer, degenerate radius).
- A puck at the centre has no hue, so a Shift-drag from there now takes the angle where the pointer pressed rather than where egui first reported a drag.
- The wheel has a hover tooltip naming the modifiers. Double-click still resets, with or without a modifier held.
- `docs/parity-checklist.md`: the `LR-EDIT-COLOR-GRADING` row describes the three modifiers and cites the tests.

**Tests** (`crates/ui-egui/src/tests_grading.rs`): the wheel is driven through `ui.dragWidget` with each modifier, checking the develop values and exactly one undo step per drag:

title: LR-META-XMP: Read Metadata from File no longer auto-writes the sidecar it has just read
author: AlexChambers
body:
Part of #934 (item 2, "Read Metadata with auto-write on locks frames out of LRT"). Items 1, 3 and 4 are not addressed here; see the end.

## What was wrong

With XMP auto-write on, `photo.readMetadataFromFile` committed what it read as one undo step (`crates/engine/src/cmd/xmp.rs`), and the command handler then auto-wrote the photo's sidecar like after any edit (`Session::run_command` in `crates/engine/src/lib.rs`). That write merged our `lc:settings` into a sidecar that until then held only another app's `crs:` settings. From then on every read preferred `lc:settings` over `crs:` (`parse_sidecar` in `crates/engine/src/sidecar.rs`), so when LRTimelapse rewrote `crs:Exposure2012` the change was ignored.

Reproduced on `main` 76b5377 (by the tests below, and by the issue sweep with a CLI built from it) with a PNG and a sidecar holding only `crs:Exposure2012="0.5"`: after a read with auto-write on, the sidecar gains `lc:settings`; an external change to `crs:Exposure2012="1.2"` (the rest of the file kept, as LRT does) is then ignored by the next read, which leaves exposure at 0.5. In the sweep's control with auto-write off, the same steps pick up 1.2.

## Fix

- After a successful read the command sets `skip_auto_write`, the existing one-command switch that `photo.removeRegion` and `photo.setRegion` use, so the sidecar it has just read is not written back.
- Only the read command is exempt. An edit afterwards (a slider, a rating) is auto-written as before, and so are undo and redo.
- One side effect: a read keeps the catalog fields the sidecar doesn't state, and those no longer reach the sidecar during the read. The next edit or Save Metadata to File writes them, as it would for any sidecar.
- The command's description, the `LR-META-XMP` row of `docs/parity-checklist.md` and the Read row of `docs/xmp-interop.md` say so.

## Verification

Two tests in `crates/engine/src/tests_xmp.rs`; both fail on `main` and pass with the fix:

- `reading_metadata_leaves_the_sidecar_alon…

author: atmikshetty
body:
Part of gap 28 (docs/gaps.md): Classic panel keys.

- **View > Right Panel** (`view.rightPanel`, **F8**) hides the right panel and brings back the one that was there (Edit when nothing was remembered). Crop, Remove, Masking and Red Eye end when their panel is hidden and come back as Edit; every other panel returns as it was.

The next press brings back exactly what was shown, so a panel that was already hidden stays hidden. Showing a panel by hand while they're hidden makes the snapshot stale, so the next Shift+Tab hides again instead of bringing back old state. When the shortcut fires, it consumes the key and cancels the traversal (`move_focus(FocusDirection::None)`, the approach PhotoCraft uses). In a focused text field neither key is a shortcut and Shift+Tab keeps moving focus as before.

title: LR-IMP-DRAGDROP: photos opened from Finder or other apps reach LightCraft on macOS (#506)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Closes #506 (parity row `LR-IMP-DRAGDROP`).

As @radialmonster worked out in the issue, two things were missing on macOS:

- **The bundle didn't declare any photo types**, so Finder and other apps were told LightCraft can't open them. `Info.plist.in` now lists the types we import (camera raw, JPEG, HEIC/HEIF, TIFF, PNG, WebP, JPEG XL, PSD, GIF, BMP) with `LSHandlerRank` `Alternate`: LightCraft shows up in Open With but never becomes the default app.
- **winit doesn't pass `application:openURLs:` through.** The new `crates/opendocs` adds that method to winit's application delegate and queues the paths, the same way VectorCraft's `open_documents.rs` does. That needs `unsafe`, so per AGENTS.md it lives in its own small helper crate next to `sysmem`: safe API, `// SAFETY:` on each block, and a no-op on other platforms. AGENTS.md and `docs/architecture.md` name it.

In the app, files that arrive at launch go through `launch_imports` like command-line files. Files that arrive while it's running are handed to the UI as dropped files, so presets, face models and the Lightroom-import guard behave exactly as they do for a drop. The exception is while the window about a library that couldn't be opened is up. Then they wait with the launch files and are imported once the user has chosen: into the library opened with Try Again or Choose Another Library…, or into the temporary session with Continue Without Saving. Waiting files now also reach a library chosen through the desktop's background folder dialog, which used to drop them (launch files included).

## Tested

On macOS 27 (Apple silicon), with an ad-hoc signed `LightCraft.app` registered with LaunchServices:

- Open With now lists LightCraft for jpg, heic, arw, nef, cr3, dng and raf. Preview stays the default app.

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: dark, muted scenes learn their colour matrix (#865, stacked on #784)
author: AlexChambers
body:
Fixes #865. The rest of the #778 file's gap is DRO tone (#867).

Rebased onto main `0da998f2` after integration batch 40. This branch uses `LOOK_VERSION` 14 and `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 66. Main uses look 9 and render 64.

**Builds on #784, and so on #699.** It includes their rebased commits, followed by its three own dark-scene commits. It changes `fit_pairs_on`, `search_ordered`, `fit_attempt` and `fit_look_with`, which #699 changes too. The sweep below is against #784. I'll rebase once they land. Versions: `LOOK_VERSION` 14 and `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 66, after #699's look 12 and render 69 and #784's look 13 and render 70.

## What was wrong

A photo without a camera profile learns its own colour matrix only when 5% of its training pairs count as coloured, before any acceptance gate runs (`collect_pairs`). A pair counted as coloured when its camera JPEG channels spread by more than 0.05 (linear), at every luminance.

The same colour spreads a pixel's channels in proportion to its luminance, though. At linear 0.036 (L\* 22), a pixel's channels had to spread by 1.4 times its luminance to count, five times what a pixel at middle grey needs. So a dark scene almost never qualifies, however much colour it shows. It falls to the partial look (#583): tone and chroma curve, and no colour matrix.

The 0.05 dates from the first fit (05f242c), with no stated reason. The matrix itself is fitted to luminance-normalised colour (`fit_matrix`), which a dark pixel shows as well as a bright one.

I measured every gate with throwaway instrumentation on `main` 76b5377 (the same on #784). Only the colour count refuses these photos. Once a photo gets past it, its full look passes every other gate with a wide margin:

| | Coloured pairs at 0.05 (5% needed) | Median JPEG luminance | Partial look today (held-out RMS against the neutral fallback) | Full look with this change |
|---|---|---|---|---|

title: Nix: nix build and nix develop work again on NixOS
author: dev-null-undefined
body:
> **Rebased onto `main` (`b3d392b4`, 2026-10-13).** In the meantime, `main` fixed bugs 1 and 2 below:
> - #1314 added the same `cargoLock.allowBuiltinFetchGit`;
> - #990 made the lock test spawn `true` from `PATH`.
>
> Both changes are dropped from this branch. What's left is the CI evaluation workflow, so the next git dependency can't
> break the flake unnoticed, plus the doc note and the gsettings fix (bug 3).

## The bug

On NixOS, `nix build` and `nix develop` (README → Quick start) have both failed since 2026-10-10. The plain cargo binary can't open its window outside the dev shell, so on NixOS LightCraft only ran with a hand-built `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. Two regressions from that day stack up, and a third NixOS gap sits in the appearance code:

1. **Flake evaluation** (`9bfabc98`, UI.9; *fixed on `main` by #1314*): `Cargo.lock` gained its first git source, `craft-ui` from storytold/craft-libs.
   - `nix/package.nix` only sets `cargoLock.lockFile`, and its header says "only crates.io, no git sources".
   - `importCargoLock` needs a hash for every git dependency, so evaluation stops with `No hash was found while vendoring the git dependency craft-ui-0.1.0`.
   - That breaks `nix build`, `nix run` and `nix develop` alike. The dev shell is what sets `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` for the libraries winit and wgpu `dlopen`, so without it a `cargo run` window fails with "Failed to load one of xlib's shared libraries".
2. **Check phase** (`8166185a`, #680; *fixed on `main` by #990*): `tests_lock::dropping_the_lock_frees_the_library_while_another_thread_spawns_processes` spawns `/bin/true`.

title: Fix: import of metadata-less exports (Unknown Date, phantom 'already in the library', Grid Info)
author: emmertex
body:
A user report: a folder of about 4,700 Lightroom JPEG exports was imported into a brand-new, empty library.

**1. "8 already in the library" on an empty library.** The scan marks a file whose bytes match an *earlier file in the same source* as a `content` duplicate with no `existing` photo, and the dialog counted those as "already in the library". They are now counted apart: "· N identical copies", with a tooltip. Only the first copy is imported, as before.

**2. About 4,500 photos under "Unknown Date", while the loupe showed a date.** The exports carry no capture date. The loupe info overlay falls back to the *import* date, so it looked dated. The import review and the folder/rename templates use the same date. Tests that relied on the import clock now stamp their files' mtime.

**3. View ▸ Grid Info appeared to do nothing.** The captions are drawn on Square Grid cells only, and the user was in Photo Grid. Choosing a Grid Info option from Photo Grid now switches to Square Grid.

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: transparent areas develop on white instead of black (#1212)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Closes #1212 (parity row `LR-IMP-FORMATS`).

The decoders already keep the alpha plane (`Decoded.alpha`), but `to_working()` in `crates/codecs/src/lib.rs` converted only `d.image`, so a fully transparent pixel kept whatever colour it stores, usually black. Every in-app path for an ordinary image (render, previews and thumbnails, export, contact sheet) starts from that working image, so all of them showed the black. `to_working()` now flattens transparency onto white, as the issue asks (the way PhotoCraft and Photoshop flatten a transparent image). The compositing is `c * a + (1 - a)` on the linear values: the decoder has already linearised and un-premultiplied the image, the pipeline works in linear light, and white is (1, 1, 1) both in the source and in the working space, so it can be done in one place without going back to the file's own transfer curve. Only semi-transparent edges depend on that choice; fully opaque and fully transparent pixels come out the same either way. `Decoded::to_srgb8()` (and so `decode_thumbnail`) still returns real alpha for callers that want it.

Validation (macOS, Apple silicon):

- `png_transparency_develops_on_white` (codecs, `tests/roundtrip.rs`): opaque, transparent and half-transparent pixels; fails on `main` (`[0.0, 0.0, 0.0] != [1.0, 1.0, 1.0]`), passes with the fix. It also fails if the compositing is done on sRGB-encoded values.
- `files::tests::transparent_png_develops_on_white` (engine): the develop path (`load_bytes`) gives white for the transparent pixel; fails on `main`, passes with the fix.

title: LRC-LIB-CATALOG-IMPORT: the ARW6 plan keeps the probe's scattered strip reads
author: mdlmarkham
body:
## What this does

Fixes the sparse-equivalence break PR #1020 reported (`no issue exists for it`): `header_plan` / `preview_plan`
described a Compression-32766 (ARW6) strip from **part of it** while the header probe validates bytes scattered
through a 30-63 MB strip. The corpus's ARW6 pair was described from zeros (and again 0xFF) and the probe failed
where the whole file decodes:

```
crates/raw/tests/sparse_corpus.rs: arw6-sony-ilce7rm6-apsc-land-hq.arw: differs from the whole file
  left:  Err(Unsupported("ARW6 first-half row count outside 2..=7"))
  right: Ok(RawInfo { format: Arw, width: 6592, ... })
```

The probe's reads on an ARW6 strip are not a prefix (`docs/arw6-compression.md`): per tile, `parse_tile_header`
walks the 13 stream header words, `stream_halves` reads each stream's index table, and `first_half_shift` decodes
the residual stream's first half — which sits **behind** the earlier streams' data (megabytes in). The 64 KiB
prefix the plan kept does not reach any of that.

## How

- [crates/raw/src/sparse.rs](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/glm/arw6-sparse-plan/crates/raw/src/sparse.rs):
  when an IFD's image says Compression 32766 and has one strip, `tiff_plan` asks `arw6_keep` for the strip's
  scattered reads and holes only the rest. The walk runs in stages — each one answers with a single `Need`:
  1. the tile table (`u32` count + up to 16 24-byte entries),
  2. each tile's picture header and group tables (words 0..8),
  3. the 13 stream header words, at positions the group tables alone imply (new `arw6::stream_header_positions`,
     mirroring `parse_tile_header`'s group-table walk — the two walks must agree),
  4. with the header words loaded, the probe's own `parse_tile_header` places each stream's index table,
  5. finally each residual first half: its byte length `A` is its index's first entry, and `first_half_shift`
     decodes those lines for the anchor offset.

title: Preserve Lightroom edits and improve measured rendering fidelity
author: ilyador

title: Lightroom catalog import: stream tables; develop settings never dropped silently (#1234, stacked on #842)
author: bitshiftza
body:
**Stacked on #842** (FredApps: read large Lightroom catalogs by page). Until #842 merges, this PR also shows its commit; the change here is `LRC-LIB-CATALOG-IMPORT: stream catalog tables; develop settings never dropped silently`.

Closes #1234.

Large Lightroom Classic catalogs no longer lose edits or history to per-table size caps.

- **Rows are streamed.** `Database::for_each_row` hands each decoded row to a callback instead of building the whole table in memory. The 256 MiB payload and one-million-row caps per table are gone. Two sanity bounds that a well-formed table can't reach replace them: total payload within the database's bytes, and rows within bytes ÷ 5 (the smallest a row can be). They stop a file with overlapping or shared cells from walking forever. Depth, cycle, cell-pointer, per-record (64 MiB) and overflow-chain checks are unchanged.
- **The importer keeps only what it maps:** ids and path parts for root folders, folders and files; the settings text for develop settings; the decoded XMP for additional metadata; keyword names, turned into hierarchy strings as they stream. History and snapshots are kept for the recovery archive up to 256 MiB together; steps past that are counted in a warning, not kept.
- **Develop settings are never dropped quietly.** If `Adobe_imageDevelopSettings` exists but can't be read, the photos, ratings, keywords and collections still import, and any settings read before the damaged part are kept. `editsNotImported: N` appears in the inspect and import results, the first warning says edits weren't imported and how to recover (Optimize Catalog in Lightroom, then re-import with `updateExisting`), and the app's import summary leads with it (shown for 20 s instead of 6 s; translated in all nine languages). Importing rather than failing means a damaged catalog still yields its photos.

title: M5.6: zoomed 64 MP raws stay decoded and on the GPU (every 1:1 pan re-decoded the raw)
author: dev-null-undefined
body:
## The problem

On a Sony A7R VI (64 MP, 9984×6656), every pan of a 1:1 view and every slider move while zoomed takes seconds before the full-resolution window appears. At fit, slider drags were already fast (~8 ms on the GPU).

Profile (`LIGHTCRAFT_PROFILE=1`) of one pan before this PR: the whole raw is decoded again each time.
- `raw source 9984×6656 … develop 3300–7700 ms, highlights ~1000 ms, colour 1600–2800 ms`, once for the After window and once more for the Before.
- Then `gpu sample` takes 1.3–2.6 s to upload the 800 MB original again.

These numbers come from a 4-CPU cgroup quota on an Intel Core Ultra 9 185H with an RTX 4070 Laptop (Vulkan), so the CPU figures are pessimistic.

## Causes and fixes (four commits)

1. **The original is evicted as soon as it is stored.**
   - A decoded 64 MP original is 9984 × 6656 × 12 B = 797 MB. The default cache share is half of 1.5 GiB, i.e. 768 MiB.
   - `MediaCache::enforce_budget` protected only the newest preview, so the original it had just received was the one thing it could evict.
   - The GPU's shared copy (keyed by a `Weak` to the CPU image) went with it.
   - Raising the budget (`app.memoryBudget {mb: 3072}`) made pans fast, which confirms the cause.
   - **Fix:** the frontend tells the cache which photo Detail shows (`MediaCache::set_on_screen`, set every frame in `panels::compare::prepare`, `None` in other views). That photo's original is not evicted for the budget and goes as soon as another photo or view is shown.
   - Keying this on "no newer preview of another photo" instead does not work: the neighbour prefetch stores previews after the original.
2. **Two or three decodes per first zoom.**
   - The Before window waited only while the After's job was pending. Side by side, the Before is requested first in the frame, so both decoded.
   - A window requested again while the first was still decoding (a pan, or the layout settling at startup) started another full decode beside it. Three decodes were seen at …

title: HDR: the HDR histogram follows slider drags live
author: JordyUSA
body:
Follow-up to #677: **the HDR histogram follows slider drags live** instead of disappearing.

### The problem
A slider drag renders drafts, and #677 deliberately gives drafts no HDR histogram (a second render per tick would slow them down). So while dragging an HDR edit, the panel got the draft's SDR histogram: the SDR / HDR layout dropped out and came back when the drag ended. In grid view (Edit panel open) cached thumbnails and stand-ins did the same.

### The fix
- **A live HDR histogram beside the drafts:** during a drag of an HDR edit, the panel requests a small full-quality render (`Slot::HdrHistogram`, `HDR_HISTOGRAM_DRAG_EDGE` = 192 px, priority below the loupe). It has its own stage cache, like the other views, so it doesn't restart from the full-resolution source every tick. Like the loupe, a superseded result that is newer than the one shown still lands, so the histogram keeps moving during a long drag. Only the histogram is kept (`Renderer::live_hdr_histogram`), no texture.
- **The drafts are unchanged:** they still skip the HDR histogram, so the photo moves as fast as before. (A first try that put the histogram render inside each draft made the photo lag on real raws.)
- **The panel stays HDR:** for an HDR edit, a render without HDR bins (a draft, a cached thumbnail or stand-in) keeps the last HDR histogram shown for that photo instead of swapping to the SDR layout. Turning HDR off shows the SDR histogram at once.

### Testing
- Tried in the app on a real raw by @JordyUSA: in the loupe and in grid view, the histogram moves with the slider without switching to SDR, and the photo doesn't lag.
- New tests: `render::tests::a_drag_gets_its_live_hdr_histogram_beside_the_drafts` (superseded results still land, HDR bins, no texture) and `panels::edit::tests::an_hdr_edit_keeps_its_hdr_histogram_through_8_bit_renders`.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes: fmt, clippy, heif, test, parity, layers, assets, wasm.

title: LR-VID-TIMELAPSE: timelapse video from photos (#497)
author: emmertex
body:
Fixes #497

Tracker: new row **LR-VID-TIMELAPSE** (🟡); gap 18 notes it (gap not closed).

**File ▸ Timelapse Video…** and `export.timelapse {path, ids?, fps?, size?, fit?, hold?, crossfade?, format?, quality?}` turn stills into a silent movie:

- Photos: `ids` in the given order, else the selection **in the shown order** (the current sort).
- Each photo is rendered by the export render job with its own edits, then **fit** (letterbox) or **fill** (centre crop) into one frame size (`"WxH"` or `[w, h]`, 16–8192, even; default 1920×1080).
- `hold` frames per photo (1–1000), `crossfade` blended frames between photos (0–1000), 1–120 fps; frames = photos × hold + (photos − 1) × crossfade.
- **H.264 MP4** (default) or **ProRes 422 MOV** (the default follows the extension), quality 1–100. No audio.
- New crate **`lightcraft-video-encode`** (L1, native only): a `SequenceWriter` over FilmCraft's `filmcraft-h264enc`, `filmcraft-prores` and `filmcraft-isobmff` (pinned git rev, same organisation; roadmap M14 already plans video on FilmCraft crates). Not `filmcraft-codecs`, which pulls symphonia (MPL-2.0).

title: fix: deleting a photo asks first, also from the right-click menu (#1239)
author: mattsivak
body:
Fixes #1239.

## Cause
- Settings ▸ General ▸ "Confirm before moving photos to Recently Deleted" (`AppSettings::confirm_delete`) **defaulted to off**, so Delete moved photos to Recently Deleted without asking unless you found the setting.
- The photo context menu's **Delete Photo** (`panels/grid.rs`, used by the grid and filmstrip) ran `photo.delete` directly. It skipped `menus::confirm_delete`, so it never asked, even with the setting on. The key (`shortcuts.rs`) and the menu bar (`menubar::run_item`) already asked.

## Fix
- The setting is **on by default**.
- The context menu's Delete Photo runs through `menubar::run_item`, the code a menu bar click runs, which already asks before `photo.delete`. It no longer calls `app.run` directly.
- **Migration:** every earlier version wrote `"confirmDelete": false` into `ui.json` for people who never opened Settings, and a saved `false` can't be told apart from a deliberate choice. The setting is now saved as `askBeforeDelete` and the old key is no longer read, so existing installs ask too. A deliberate "off" was rare while the default was already off; anyone who wants it off can turn it off again, and that choice now survives a restart.
- `engine.execute` / `ui.menu.invoke` (agents, MCP) still run `photo.delete` directly, without the question.
- The parity rows `LR-LIB-DELETE` and `MENU-PHOTO-DELETE` no longer say "no confirmation".

Not changed: **Delete Permanently** in Recently Deleted still doesn't ask. It is one undo step that brings the photos back, and it removes catalog records, not files.

## Test
- `tests_panels::deleting_a_photo_asks_first_from_the_key_the_menu_and_the_right_click_menu`: checks that the key, the menu bar item and the right-click menu each open the "Move … to Recently Deleted?" dialog, that Cancel keeps the photo and OK deletes it, and that with the setting off the right-click deletes at once. **Before the fix it failed twice in turn:** first on "on by default", then, with the default fixed, on "t…

title: LRC-LIB-LIBFOLDERS: Folders skips the folders that only lead to your photos, with Show Parent Folder to list them
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

A design critique of the left sidebar put this first: Folders listed every folder from the disk down, so a library below a deep path began with a staircase of rows that only led on, each repeating one count, and the first folder anyone looks for was a screen down and far to the right.

## Problem

Folders lists every folder from the disk down to where the library's photos are. A library kept below a deep path (`/Users/me/Pictures/…`) opens on a staircase of rows that hold no photo and only lead on, each repeating the same count, and the folder the person is looking for sits a screen down and far to the right.

## Change

- **A disk opens at the first folder that holds photos or branches.** A folder that only leads there (no photo of its own, one folder inside, no colour label) has no row: what it leads to takes its place, one step inside the disk. A row's tooltip still gives its whole path.
- **Right-click ▸ Show Parent Folder** lists the folder above, one level each time; **Hide This Parent** on the topmost such row takes it away again. Both are Lightroom Classic's terms and do what they do there. Nothing on disk or in the library changes.
- **What is shown is always in view.** A passed-over folder that the grid shows (an agent chose it) has its row meanwhile, and Hide This Parent is off, saying why, while it is shown. A folder with a colour label always has its row.
- **Nothing changes below the first folder.** Further down every folder is a row of its own, as before, and a folder that holds nothing itself and leads to one folder still starts open. The catalog's folder tree (`library.folders`) is unchanged: this is what the sidebar draws.
- **For agents:** `view.folderParent` `{path, show?}` shows, hides or flips a folder that only leads to the library's folders. It refuses any other folder and says which case it is: always listed, listed because the one above it is, or holding no photo. Kept with the UI state as `folderParents`, at most 256. Widgets …

author: nledford

title: LRC-DEV-HISTORY: History cursor — going to a step adds no step
author: emmertex
body:
Lightroom Classic / Photoshop-style History panel.

- `history.restore` loads the step's settings and moves a per-photo cursor instead of appending a `History: …` step. New `history.previous` / `history.next` (no default shortcuts).
- Steps after the cursor stay listed (greyed in the History panel; current step highlighted) and can be returned to. A new edit made while the cursor is behind the end drops them, then appends.
- Undo/redo: each cursor move is one undo step; undoing an edit made behind the end restores the dropped steps and the cursor.
- Catalog: `Photo.history_cursor` (`None` = latest; absent in old catalogs) and `Op::SetHistoryCursor`; journal format bumped to v8. Clear History resets the cursor.
- XMP / export / sidecars keep using `photo.develop`, which is the settings at the cursor.
- `history.list` returns `cursor`.
- Tests: `crates/engine/src/tests_history_cursor.rs` (back without new entry, forward, truncation + undo/redo, undo coherence, op-log replay + old-catalog load); UI row-state test in `panels/right.rs`.
- Also fixes the new clippy `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` lint in `pipeline/src/spots.rs`.

Sources: own design (observed Lightroom Classic behaviour).

`cargo xtask ci` green.

title: Lightroom catalog import: stream table rows instead of per-table size caps
author: emmertex
body:
Partial fix for #1234 (helps some catalogs; another tester still sees the issue on one of theirs, so the issue stays open).

- `Database::for_each_row` streams a table's records to a callback, one at a time; `read_table` (schema, small tables) collects through it and keeps its one-million-row cap. The 256 MiB per-table payload cap is gone; per-record (`MAX_PAYLOAD`) and XMP limits stay.
- The importer streams `Adobe_imageDevelopSettings` (image -> text only), `Adobe_AdditionalMetadata` (xmp decoded per row) and history/snapshots (grouped per image) instead of collecting whole tables; BLOB columns are dropped per row.
- Develop settings that can't be read now fail the import with a clear error ("no photo would get its edits") instead of a warning. History, snapshots and metadata stay optional (warn and skip).

Tests: `large_tables_stream_past_the_collect_cap` (1.2 M rows under an interior page, more than `read_table` collects, counted by a sink that keeps nothing; a sink error stops the walk), `develop_settings_reach_the_photos_and_an_unreadable_table_fails_the_import`. `cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib lightroom` passes.

Sources: SQLite file-format spec; own design.

title: Ask before deleting a photo by default.
author: vbasky
body:
Fixes #1239.

Delete confirmation was off unless a saved ui.json turned it on, and the grid context menu deleted immediately even when the setting was on. The menu, the keyboard shortcut, and the menu bar now share one path, and a new library asks first.

The settings test turns the checkbox off and back on, then checks that Delete opens the confirm dialog.

title: Scroll the filmstrip when the same photo is opened in another source.
author: vbasky
body:
Fixes #1142.

The grid and filmstrip only scrolled when the active photo id changed. Opening that same photo from another album kept the old scroll position. The follow token now includes the library source.

title: Import HEIC, HEIF, and NRW files from a folder.
author: vbasky
body:
Fixes #1080.

Folder import used a shorter extension list than the engine, so HEIC, HEIF, and NRW files in a directory were skipped. Explicit file paths were already accepted.

title: Accept a bare port for --connect.
author: vbasky
body:
Fixes #1178.

`lightcraft run --connect 7980` and `lightcraft mcp --connect 7980` left the port as the next argument and dialed the default address. A number is now `127.0.0.1` with that port. A following command id is not consumed.

title: Read Exif and XMP embedded in HEIF and AVIF.
author: vbasky
body:
Fixes #1233.

Metadata extraction knew JPEG, PNG, WebP, TIFF, and CR3, and returned nothing for a HEIF or AVIF `ftyp`. The scan now finds the Exif TIFF payload and the XMP packet without decoding the image.

title: Composite straight alpha onto white in the working space.
author: vbasky
body:
Fixes #1212.

`to_working` kept a transparent pixel as the stored RGB, which is usually black. Straight alpha is now composited onto white in the linear working space. Outputs that keep an alpha channel are unchanged.

title: Ignore hidden and empty masks when choosing develop planes.
author: vbasky
body:
Fixes #1214.

Any mask with a highlights or shadows value made the pipeline build the tone base, including a hidden mask and a mask with no components. Those masks do not change the picture, so only a visible mask that has a component selects the planes.

title: Honor luminance noise-reduction contrast.
author: vbasky
body:
Refs #1129.

Luminance noise reduction ignored Contrast. Contrast 0 still blends the same way. Higher contrast keeps more of the original difference where the guided filter wants a large change, so fine texture survives. Shadow under-denoising from the same report is not part of this change.

title: Raise the deep-zoom preview margin cap.
author: vbasky
body:
Fixes #1146.

The preview window margin stopped at 768 pixels. On a wide frame the highlights, clarity, and dehaze kernels reach about 4.5 percent of the long edge, so the cap clipped them. The cap is now 3072 pixels, still snapped to the window grid.

title: Make a positive paint vignette blend toward white.
author: vbasky
body:
Fixes #905.

Paint Overlay only blended toward black when Amount was negative. A positive amount used the same lighten as Color Priority, so the style tabs matched. Positive paint now blends toward white, and negative paint stays a blend toward black.

title: fix(toast): draw the toast as widgets so the message can be selected
author: switch87
body:
## The problem

The toast at the bottom centre of the canvas was drawn straight onto its layer:

```rust
let galley = painter.layout(text, t.font(14.0), foreground, wrap);
painter.rect_filled(r, 6.0, background.gamma_multiply(fade));
painter.galley(r.center() - galley.size() / 2.0, galley, foreground);
```

Painted text is never hit-tested, so nothing in a toast could be selected or copied. That is a real loss for exactly the messages this surface exists for — they are paths and commands:

- `toast_error` carries `DownloadOutcome::Failed(e)` and `The SAM 3 download failed: {e}`
- `toast_for` exists for "messages that say where to look or what to do next"
- `Event::Toast` / `s.toast(…)` reach here as text like `Exported frame to /path/to/frame.png`

egui's `Label` is selectable by default (`style.interaction.selectable_labels`), and LightCraft never turns that off — but it only helps widgets. The other craft apps already render their toasts as labels; this one was the odd one out.

## The change

Same toast, drawn as an `Area` + `Frame` + wrapping `Label`. Everything visual is carried over unchanged: the centring on `canvas.bottom() - 60`, the 6 px radius, the 40/22 px of padding (now `Margin::symmetric(20, 11)`), the wrap width of `canvas.width() - 80` clamped to 200–720, and the 0.25 s fade, which now tints the frame and the text instead of the galley.

## Tests

`crates/ui-egui/src/tests_toast.rs`:

- `the_toast_is_a_widget_the_pointer_reaches` — the toast has an `area_rect` of its own, and moving the pointer onto it makes egui offer the text cursor. Painted text is never hit-tested, so this fails against the old code.
- `the_toast_still_wraps_a_long_message_inside_the_canvas` — a long message still wraps inside the canvas.

Both fail on the pre-change code (`the toast is laid out as a widget, not paint`) and pass after.

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: CR2 white level from the active area, not the saturated masked rows above it
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1272.

The CR2 decoder ran the plateau search over the whole sensor buffer, masked rows included, even though the active area from SensorInfo is already known a few lines earlier. On the 50D and friends those top rows hold a few thousand samples at 16383, which is enough for `white_from_data` to call them the plateau and settle on 16320. The white level now comes from the active area only, through the same `active_rows` sampler RW2 already uses for its junk borders; I moved it from `rw2.rs` into `vendor/mod.rs` so both decoders share it (happy to keep a local copy in `cr2.rs` instead if you'd rather not touch RW2). Its row step is now always odd, so it reads both row parities and every CFA site: with the old step of `height / 512`, active heights of 3072 to 3583 (these Canon bodies) gave 6 and only even rows. Affected bodies: EOS 50D, 60D, 450D, 500D / T1i, 550D / T2i, 1200D / T5 and 100D / SL1. Of the other `white_from_data` callers, RW2 and SRW already restrict to the active area; ORF, RAF and ARW are left as they are.

Validation:
- `vendor::cr2::tests::white_from_active_area_only` (synthetic CR2 with SensorInfo, four masked rows at 16383 above an image plateau at 13433): fails on main (white 16320), passes here
- `vendor::tests::active_rows_reads_both_row_parities` (2048×2048, plateau on the blue sites only): fails with the even step (white 16383), passes here
- The EOS 50D file from the issue (raw.pixls.us 1792), checked locally: white 13381 (was 16320), highest active sample 13433
- Four RW2s (GH1, GH5, GX80, G9 from raw.pixls.us): same white with the odd step as before
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-raw --lib vendor::`, `cargo test -p lightcraft-raw --test vendor_robust`, `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-raw --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)
