title: Dehaze: process V3 with a patch dark channel, eased response and no black halos
author: emmertex
body:
Fixes #1237

Dehaze estimated haze from a Gaussian of each pixel's darkest channel. As a result, ordinary tones were read as haze, and shadows next to bright sky were clipped to black from +10. This adds **process V3**, so photos already edited on V1 or V2 render as before (`docs/process-versions.md`).

**V3 dehaze:**
- **Patch dark channel.** The haze plane is now the Gaussian of a patch *minimum* of the darkest channel instead of the darkest channel itself. The patch radius is 0.5 % of the long edge, capped at 64 px. On the CPU it is a separable van Herk / Gil–Werman running minimum (O(1) per pixel); on the GPU it uses the new `min_h` / `min_v` kernels in `blur.wgsl`. Textured areas without haze always have a dark pixel nearby, so they now get t ≈ 1.
- **Eased response.** The strength is `k·(0.4 + 0.6·k)`, so +10 acts at about half of V1's strength. The transmission floor is 0.15 (V1: 0.12).
- **No black halos.** The veil removed is capped at 90 % of the pixel's darkest channel (`finish::dehaze_v3_pixel`, mirrored in `finish.wgsl`).
- **Negative dehaze is unchanged** from V1.
- **Cache key.** The dark plane's cache key now includes the patch radius (`local::dark_key`).

**Measured** on a synthetic scene (`tests_dehaze.rs`: bright sky beside a textured, haze-free ground), at +50:

| | ground brightness at +50 | black pixels next to the sky at +10 / +50 |
|---|---|---|
| V1 | −0.54 EV | 38 % / 50 % |
| V3 | −0.08 EV | 0 % / 0 % |

A uniformly veiled chequer still gains contrast as the slider rises.

**Tests:**
- New `tests_dehaze.rs`: V1 is frozen, V3 fixes both faults, the veil still clears, the pixel function never reaches black and eases in, and `min_hv` matches a brute-force minimum.
- `tests_window::dehaze_at_depth_matches_the_whole_render` still passes.
- The WGSL modules validate with naga 30.

title: NEF: as-shot white balance from the ColorBalance block on the D2H, D70 and D70s (not the D50)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1273: the D2H, D70 and D70s, not the D50.

These bodies don't write `0x000c` WB_RBLevels, so `nef.rs` came back with `wb_multipliers: None`. Their ColorBalance block (`0x0097`) isn't enciphered:
- version `0102` (D2H) holds the as-shot levels as RGGB `u16`s from byte 10;
- version `0103` (D70, D70s) holds them as RGBG from byte 20.

Both are in the maker note's byte order. The decoder now falls back to those levels when `0x000c` is missing. G is the mean of the two greens, and the same 0.1..10 plausibility range as the existing path applies. On the files from the issue this gives R 2.20 / B 1.46 (D2H), 2.17 / 1.52 (D70) and 2.30 / 1.43 (D70s).

Where the offsets come from: the ExifTool tag-name documentation names the block and its channel order per version, but not where the levels start. I first took bytes 10 and 20 from ExifTool's source (its ColorBalance0102/0103 tables in `Nikon.pm`); no code came from it. Then I checked them black-box: on the CC0 files 5227 (D2H), 2060 (D70) and 1117 (D70s), bytes 10 and 20 are the only places in each block where four `u16` hold two greens of 256 in the order's green slots and two gains between 1 and 4. As measured in the review, the gains they give are within 2 to 8 % of what neutral areas of each camera JPEG imply. The comment at the constant says this.

The D50 is not covered. Its block is version `0205`, which is enciphered, and the test pins it as not read.

Still open from #1273: the D50. The Olympus E-10 is in #1297, and the Canon G9 has its own PR.

Validation:
- `vendor::nef::tests::as_shot_white_balance_from_the_color_balance_block` (synthetic maker notes, both byte orders, plus enciphered/implausible/truncated blocks and `0x000c` taking precedence): fails on main (`left: None, right: Some([2.199, 1.0, 1.457])`), passes here

title: PEF: masked rows and columns at the black level are trimmed without crop tags
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1271.

Without crop tags, `dark_trimmed` compared raw column means with 5% of the interior's raw mean, so masked columns sitting at the black level (BlackPoint 64/128/256 on these bodies) only counted as dark when the interior was more than 20 times brighter than black, and it never looked at rows. It now takes the maker-note BlackPoint (already read here) and treats a line as dark when its mean is at most 1/256 of the remaining range (at least 16 DN) above it, the same tolerance `cr2::masked_columns` uses: masked lines sit at black plus noise, while dark real content such as a night sky is well above, whatever the interior's brightness. When the outermost line sits a little above BlackPoint (the K-70 and K-1 mask at 65 DN over it), the tolerance is measured from that line's level; saturated outer lines count when dark ones follow (the 645Z's 12 white columns outside its 46 masked ones); a frame whose interior is itself within the tolerance (a lens-cap shot) keeps its whole area. Rows get the same scan as columns, keeping even offsets so the CFA phase doesn't move. Files without BlackPoint keep the old 5% rule. Render cache version goes to 62, since these frames change size.

Bodies covered: KP, KF, K-3 Mark III (and Monochrome), K-70, K-1, K-1 Mark II, K-S1, K-S2, 645Z. On the three files from the issue: KP 6032 x 4032, KF 6024 x 4024, K-3 Mark III 6264 x 4176 (24/16 columns, 34/14 rows). Docs: the PEF row of `docs/raw-parity.md`, LR-IMP-CAMERA-COVERAGE in `docs/parity-checklist.md`, `docs/whats-new.md`.

title: LR-EDIT-COLOR-TEMP: Lightroom's non-linear scale for the Kelvin Temp slider (#1295)
author: MarkusFriedel
body:
Fixes #1295.

The Kelvin Temp slider (`wb.temp`, 2000–50000 K) now uses Lightroom Classic's track: 7000 K in the middle, 2000–7000 K evenly across the left half (100 K per 1 %), and a logarithmic right half up to 50000 K. As Shot on a Z 6II NEF (about 4850 K) moves from 6 % to 28 % of the track, and 10000 K from 17 % to 68 %.

**Changes**

- `crates/develop/src/controls.rs`: `ControlSpec::position(v)` (0…1 along the track) and its inverse `ControlSpec::value_at(p)`. Linear for every control except `wb.temp`. The curve is keyed to the control id, not to `Track::Temp`, because the relative Temp slider shares that track. These are methods on `ControlSpec`, outside the `controls!` table, so open PRs that add controls (#1220, #1060) don't conflict. A Kelvin range that doesn't contain 7000 K falls back to linear, and non-finite input is clamped, so there is no division by zero or NaN.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs`: the slider's `to_x` / `from_x` go through that mapping. It is used to draw the knob and the gap around it, and for clicks and drags.
- Shift fine-drag now moves in track positions (a tenth of the pointer's movement along the track). It keeps the unrounded position between frames. Without that, a slow fine-drag on the Kelvin track (about 4 K per point near the centre) rounded back to the same 50 K step every frame and never moved. This also helps slow Shift-drags on other sliders, which could stall on their own step the same way; normal-speed drags behave as before.
- Unchanged: stored values, typed values, the 50 K steps, double-click reset, and the relative Temp slider of JPEGs and raws without camera matrices (`wb.tempRel`, −100…+100, 0 = as shot in the middle, linear).
- `docs/parity-checklist.md`: the `LR-EDIT-COLOR-TEMP` row describes the scale.

**Not in this PR**

Wheel and arrow-key nudges, and Quick Develop's Temp buttons, still step a fixed 50 K / 100 K / 500 K. With `position` / `value_at` in place, they could later step by a fixed distance along…

title: ORF: as-shot white balance from maker-note 0x1017/0x1018 on the Olympus E-10 (part of #1273)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1273 (the Olympus E-10; the Nikons are in #1284).

The E-10 writes 16-bit words and has no ImageProcessing sub-directory, so neither its `0x0100` WB_RBLevels nor its BlackLevel2 can be read there. It keeps both in the main maker note instead.
- The red and blue gains are in `0x1017`/`0x1018` (first value, 256 = 1.0), as on the two-field compacts. The sample file has 384 and 406, so R 1.50 and B 1.59.
- The black level is `0x1012` BlackLevel (four values) in `0x102c` ValidBits units. The file has 32 at 10 bits, which is 128 on its 12-bit samples; they bottom out at 124 to 132.

`orf.rs` already read those gains, but only for the two-field layout. It now reads them when the file is two-field or has no ImageProcessing at all, and only accepts gains between 0.1 and 10. For those same bodies (no ImageProcessing) it now reads the maker-note black level. The compacts state 0 at 12 bits, so they don't change.

Without the black level, the gains alone made the render worse: the pedestal turned magenta. With both, the render against the camera thumbnail goes from ΔE76 18.5 (fit rejected) to 11.5 (fit accepted), as measured in the review. RENDER_CACHE_VERSION is bumped (61 to 62). Happy to drop the bump if you'd rather do it at merge.

Still open from #1273: the D50, whose ColorBalance is enciphered, and the Canon G9, which has its own PR.

title: M5.6: a view slot renders one job at a time, so a drag's renders don't pile up
author: mattsivak
body:
**Problem:** `JobPool::submit` replaced a slot's *queued* job, but a newer job for a slot whose job was already running started beside it on another worker. A slider drag submits faster than renders finish, so one view (the loupe, its 1:1 zoom window) had several renders on the GPU at once, and about 30 % of finished renders were thrown away as superseded. Found while profiling #1228 with a per-frame display: in an 8 s 1:1 Exposure drag on a 61 MP raw, 194 of 645 and 248 of 719 finished renders were discarded.

**Fix** (`crates/preview/src/pool.rs`): the pool keeps the slots that have a job running (`Shared::busy`, locked inside the queue lock). `take` skips queued jobs for a busy slot. A newer submission still replaces the queued one, so the slot runs the newest request next. A drop guard frees the slot when the job ends, also when it panics, and wakes the workers. Other slots aren't held up; thumbnails each have their own slot and are unaffected.

**Measured:** release app, M4 Max, `arw-sony-a7cr-compressed.arw` (61 MP) at 1:1, 8 s scripted Exposure drags (`ui.dragWidget`), frame intervals logged by the per-frame display. The runs are noisy on a working machine, but:
- thrown-away renders roughly halved (348 → 156 and 278 → 106 per run on one setup; 133 → 96 and 239 → 141 on the other);
- with this change, frames over 20 ms were 0 % in each of 4 runs (p95 8–13 ms, worst 18–36 ms). Without it, one of two runs dropped 10 % of frames (p95 92 ms, worst 755 ms).

**Tests** (`crates/preview/src/tests.rs`):
- `a_slot_runs_one_job_at_a_time`: a second and third submission for a busy slot wait (the third replaces the second), another slot runs meanwhile, and the newest runs once the slot frees. The concurrency high-water mark is 1. Fails without the fix ("a second job of slot 1 started beside the first").
- `a_panicking_job_frees_its_slot`.
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-preview`: 15 pass. `cargo test -p lightcraft-ui-egui`: 738 pass, 7 fail on `main` without this change too:…

title: RW2: decode tiled format 8 (DC-S1RM2 high-resolution mode) (#1276)
author: radialmonster
body:
Fixes #1276.

DC-S1RM2 high-resolution RW2 files (16296 x 10856, format 8, tag `0x0043` = 2) opened as the embedded preview only.

The file is tiled in 2 rows of 4. Tag `0x0045` holds (x, y) u16 pairs per tile; y is 0 in single-row files, so those read exactly as before. Tag `0x0043` is the number of tile rows. The decoder now places tiles from these lists and checks that every tile is inside the image, that no two overlap, and that together they cover it exactly. It also checks that `0x0043` equals the number of distinct tile tops; any other file is still refused as unsupported. The bit-stream decoding per tile is unchanged, and nothing is keyed to a camera body.

Checked on decoded sample arrays (md5 before and after):

- raw.pixls.us Panasonic/Leica RW2, RWL and .RAW (389 files): the other 388 decode byte-identical; the high-resolution S1RM2 file now decodes at 16296 x 10856 (active area 16288 x 10848) instead of failing.
- Reporter-supplied RW2 samples and a further 35 held-out RW2 files: byte-identical.
- The fixed file renders without seams at the tile edges (mean same-colour step across each edge matches neighbouring rows and columns), ΔE76 3.1 against its embedded JPEG; a normal-resolution S1RM2 file gives 3.7 on the same build.

Test: `format8_tiles_in_two_rows_round_trip` (synthetic, three tilings including 4 x 2; a wrong `0x0043` gives Unsupported, a gap gives Corrupt). It fails with the old offset reading.

`cargo test -p lightcraft-raw`, clippy (`-D warnings`) and `cargo fmt --check` pass (Windows). Worked out from the files and LightCraft's own RW2 decoder only.

title: DNG: decode 12-bit DCT JPEG tiles under compression 7 (Blackmagic) (#1278)
author: radialmonster
body:
Fixes #1278.

Some CinemaDNG files use 12-bit DCT JPEG (SOF1) for CFA tiles under compression 7. They currently fail without an embedded preview. The existing DNG tile/probe routing now selects a small DCT decoder for SOF0/SOF1; lossless JPEG keeps its current path. The decoder shares the existing JPEG bit reader and Huffman tables.

Rebased onto current main. Render-cache version is 65.

Fresh checks: raw tests, all-target raw Clippy and raw wasm checks pass. Of 11 camera-original DNGs checked, the three previously refused Blackmagic files now decode and develop; the other eight have identical decoded sensor samples. Visual inspection found no tile seams. Synthetic tests cover 12-bit sequential data, 8-bit baseline/restarts, lossless routing and truncation.

Malformed-stream validation now rejects a missing mandatory restart marker instead of returning a complete-sized zero tail. DC prediction uses checked addition and floating-point dequantisation; crafted streams reproduce both integer-overflow failures on the published code and pass or return corruption after the fix. Complete camera-original decoded samples remain unchanged.

Validation limitation: `cargo xtask ci` passes formatting, then stops at the unchanged `tests_export.rs` Clippy `drop_non_drop` error reproduced on main. The full workspace baseline also has Windows export-path and folder-drop test failures. Only 62 of the 447 pinned corpus files are available here; unavailable cases are skipped.

Credit: @radialmonster.

title: DNG: fit tone and chroma curves to the embedded preview (#1277)
author: radialmonster
body:
Part of #1277.

A DNG with its own colour matrices skips the camera-look fit, so it renders through the matrix and LightCraft's default tone and comes out darker and flatter than the camera's own JPEG. This adds a tone-only fit for those files.

## What changes

For a DNG that has a colour matrix but no tone of its own (identity or absent ProfileToneCurve, no LookTable, no ProfileGainTableMap), fit only the tone and chroma curves to the embedded camera preview. The file's colour model is left alone: DNG matrices, profile tables and white balance are untouched.

The fit is used only when all of these hold:
- the preview is at least 90% of the raw's long edge
- the preview shows the same picture (structure gate)
- the existing held-out acceptance passes
- the fitted render does not put more of the photo near white than both the plain render and the camera preview (highlight gate, tolerance 0.1% of the picture)

Otherwise the render is unchanged. Other formats and catalogued photos are untouched. Tone-only fits train down to luminance 0.004 so very dark scenes are not extrapolated in the toe. Render cache version is 62 (already covers the output change).

## Results

Measured against each file's embedded preview, 1440 px renders, median per group, before (main) to after.

raw.pixls.us CC0 DNGs: 52 of 257 accepted. Median dE 12.40 to 2.63, median dL* -8.77 to +0.04. No accepted file is more than 1 dE worse; 51 are better.

Galaxy S25 Ultra: 39 of 86 accepted. Median dE 3.85 to 1.47, median dL* -2.29 to +0.14. One file is more than 1 dE worse, and its registration to the preview is invalid in both builds (dL* improves there, 5.08 to 0.71).

Files that fail a gate render exactly as on main.

## Limits

- Most files are refused because the embedded preview is too small (159 of 257 pixls DNGs), so this fixes about a fifth of the DNGs in that set, not all of them.
- DNGs with a gain map are skipped (44 of 86 S25 Ultra files); their render is unchanged.
- The chroma curve mat…

title: fix(macos): cargo xtask ci passes on macOS
author: mattsivak
body:
On macOS, `cargo xtask ci` fails on `main` (0.7.1, rustc 1.99, APFS) in four places. None of them are seen by CI, which doesn't build macOS. This fixes all four; Linux and Windows behave as before.

- **`crates/pipeline/src/spots.rs`:** clippy's `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` lint now uses `out.as_chunks::<3>()`. That's stable since Rust 1.88, and the workspace MSRV is 1.90.
- **`crates/catalog/src/tests_lock.rs`:** the spawn loop ran `/bin/true`, which macOS doesn't have (it's `/usr/bin/true`), so it now runs `true` from `PATH`.
- **`crates/engine/src/tests_lightroom_folder.rs`:** APFS refuses non-UTF-8 file names with `EILSEQ` (os error 92). The non-UTF-8 checks now run only where the file system can create such a name. Any other error still fails the test, and the symlink checks always run.
- **`crates/ui-egui/src/tests_dialog_fit.rs`:** on macOS the Export dialog is 876 pt tall, because of the macOS-only "Add to Apple Photos" row (+30). Elsewhere the test still expects 846.

The `on_exit(self, None)` build fix is already in 0.7.1 (701f78ea).

**Testing:** `cargo xtask ci` passes all 8 steps on macOS (Apple M4 Max).

**Note for macOS contributors:** the engine `sidecar::tests_repair_*` tests create `a.xmp` and `A.XMP` side by side, so they need a case-sensitive `TMPDIR`. They fail on the default case-insensitive APFS volume. I ran CI with `TMPDIR` on a case-sensitive disk image:
```sh
hdiutil create -size 4g -type SPARSE -fs 'Case-sensitive APFS' -volname cs /tmp/cs.sparseimage
hdiutil attach /tmp/cs.sparseimage -mountpoint /tmp/cs -nobrowse
TMPDIR=/tmp/cs/ cargo xtask ci
```
This PR leaves those tests alone. Making them skip on case-insensitive file systems could be a follow-up.

title: 1281: calibrate --pairs exports colour pairs, --from-pairs pools them into the fit
author: radialmonster
body:
Part of #1281.

A camera profile is only as good as the variety of light and subjects behind it, and one person's library covers little of either. This lets photographers share the colour data a profile is fitted from, with no photos changing hands.

- `lightcraft-cli calibrate --pairs FILE FOLDERS…` writes the sampled colour pairs to a file. Without `--out` it only writes that file and installs no profile.
- `lightcraft-cli calibrate --from-pairs FILE…` pools any number of such files, mixed with raw folders if wanted, and fits as before.
- A pairs file is versioned JSON. Per photo it holds the Exif model, an id (a 128-bit hash of the raw's bytes, used only to count a photo once when it appears in two files), Sony's DRO flag when the file has one, and up to 4000 pairs (white-balanced camera RGB and the camera JPEG's linear Rec.2020), compressed. There are no images, file names, paths, GPS, serials or dates. About 89 KB per photo.
- Damaged or hostile files (bad ids, too many pairs, non-finite values, a size above the limit) are errors naming the file.
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/colour-pairs.yml` is an issue form for contributing a file: model, photo count, version, optional picture style, the zipped file, and a required CC0 checkbox. LightCraft itself never sends anything.
- The format is documented in `docs/camera-preview-colour.md` under "Sharing colour pairs".

Checks:

- Pairs are held at single precision wherever they come from, and photos are fitted in (model, id) order. The profile fitted from exported pairs was byte-identical to the one fitted from the same raws in all four cases tried: ILCE-7CR with 9 photos and an 8-photo subset, and ILCE-7M4 with 11 photos and a 9-photo subset.
- New tests in `camera_pairs.rs`, `camera_profiles.rs` and `apps/lightcraft-cli/tests/cli.rs` cover the round trip, deduplication, order independence and refusing bad files.
- `cargo fmt --check` passes, and clippy shows nothing new in the engine or CLI. The full test run fails only…

title: Perf: 64 MP raws decode faster (AHD 1.7×, ARW6 decode, camera-look colour 1.9×, no full-size copy), same pixels
author: dev-null-undefined
body:
## The problem

After #1235, the first 1:1 zoom on a Sony A7R VI (64 MP, 9984×6656) still pays for one full decode, and opening any photo pays for one raw decode. Profile of a full decode on `main` (`render_bench ONLY=source`, `perf record -e task-clock`):
- AHD demosaic: 1.8 s wall, 6.1 s CPU.
- ARW6 decode: 0.56 s.
- A 797 MB copy of the finished image that changes nothing.

These numbers come from a 4-CPU cgroup quota on an Intel Core Ultra 9 185H, so the CPU figures are pessimistic.

## Changes (five commits; output identical bit for bit)

1. **No full-size copy.** `load_bytes_now` ran every development through `resample::fit`, which returns a clone when the image already fits: 797 MB and ~0.3 s at full size. It now fits only a larger image, as the other paths in `files.rs` already do.
2. **AHD demosaic 1.7× faster.**
   - The hottest instructions were a store-forwarding stall: a candidate pixel was written channel by channel through an index and then read back whole for its Lab conversion. It is now built in registers.
   - Each step runs only where the tile's output depends on it (choice ±0, homogeneity ±1, Lab ±2, greens ±3, mosaic ±5, inside the 6 px margin), with direct neighbour indices instead of an index clamped on every read. The clamped values at the buffer edge never reached the output.
   - Tiles are written into the output one band at a time, instead of all 64 MP of tiles being collected and then copied (797 MB held twice). Tiles inside the image copy their mosaic rows instead of reflecting and taking a modulo per sample.
3. **ARW6 decode 20–33 % faster.**
   - The vertical inverse 5/3 lifts whole rows (`inverse_lift`, with samples `w` values wide) instead of gathering each column through a strided iterator. The horizontal pass was the same function with `w = 1`, until commit 4.
   - `0^n 1` codes are counted with one `leading_zeros`; each line reserves its values up front.

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: uncompressed Leaf MOS is a raw, the Hasselblad Lunar decodes as an ARW
author: AlexChambers
body:
Fixes #1275

## What was wrong

`lightcraft_raw::probe` misrouted two kinds of CC0 raw.pixls.us files on `main` at 25ef65c8.

- **Uncompressed Leaf MOS** (Aptus 22, [3197](https://raw.pixls.us/getfile.php/3197/nice/Leaf%20-%20Aptus%2022%20-%2016bit%20(4:3).mos)). IFD0 is the 16-bit mosaic itself: compression 1, BlackIsZero, one sample per pixel, no Make tag, no CFA photometric. Only Leaf's private block, tag `0x8606` (LeafData), says it is a raw. `probe` returned None, so the file imported as a 4008 x 5344 greyscale image of its mosaic: dark, sideways, no colour.
- **Hasselblad Lunar ARW** ([4051](https://raw.pixls.us/getfile.php/4051/nice/HASSELBLAD%20-%20Lunar%20-%2012bit%20(3:2).ARW)). A Sony NEX-7 ARW under Make HASSELBLAD, Model Lunar. Only `make.starts_with("SONY")` reached the ARW reader, so the file fell through to OtherTiff and opened as its 1616 x 1080 preview.

## The fix

- `probe` (`crates/raw/src/lib.rs`): an IFD0 that carries `0x8606` and has one sample per pixel is a raw. It is OtherTiff, preview only with the existing reason, as the lossless-JPEG MOS (3196) already is. The same grey IFD without the block, or a rendered RGB image that kept it, stays an ordinary image.
- `probe`: a HASSELBLAD file with Sony's raw coding goes to the ARW reader. The evidence is an IFD with compression 32767 (Sony ARW compressed) or the tone-curve tag `0x7010`; no 3FR or FFF has either.
- `vendor/arw.rs`: the only table there keyed by model, the `Tag2010` white-balance fallback, now takes the body from the maker note's `SonyModelID` (`0xb001`, ExifTool Sony tag-name documentation) when the file isn't Sony-branded. It lists the IDs of the Sony bodies Hasselblad rebadged: 289 NEX-7 (Lunar), 294 SLT-A99 (HV), 297 DSC-RX100 (Stellar), 308 DSC-RX100M2 (Stellar II). Only the Lunar is measured; the other three IDs come from the documentation, with no public sample to check them. The Lunar itself doesn't need the fallback: like a NEX-7, it reads its white balance from the SR2Sub…

title: LR-IMP-CAMERA-COVERAGE: verify 30 more camera models on public raw files
author: AlexChambers
body:
## What was checked

This adds 30 verified Adobe-listed camera models from the 41-model sweep shortlist. All 54 shortlisted files were downloaded again from raw.pixls.us, checked against the site's CC0 licence and SHA-256, and decoded from sensor data on main `25ef65c8`. The branch starts at `701f78ea`; its raw decoder, pipeline and engine sources match `25ef65c8`.

The accepted evidence has 40 files. Each default render reports a sensor-data source. Luminance correlation against the embedded camera image is 0.6801 to 0.9998, above the sweep's 0.6 threshold. Renders use a maximum dimension of 1200 pixels; comparisons use Lab L* at 200 pixels after the sweep's orientation and aspect alignment. The Mavic 4 Pro reference has different distortion/cropping. Ten references are embedded TIFF images and 30 are JPEGs. FFF TIFF previews are not display-ready; their correlation checks image structure, not tone or colour accuracy.

`docs/raw/coverage-sweep.tsv` records the URLs, SHA-256, sensor dimensions, FNV-1a hashes and correlation per accepted file. FNV-1a covers every decoded sample in row-major, little-endian order, including masked borders. These hashes pin LightCraft's own decode. No external raw decoder was used.

The files are listed in `RAW_SAMPLES`, and `coverage_sweep_corpus.rs` checks their file hashes, sensor hashes, dimensions, valid levels and header/decode agreement. The general corpus test now permits generic CFA TIFFs with an uncompressed preview instead of requiring a JPEG.

Coverage changes from 235 to 265 verified models (18% of 1,446). There are 918 unverified, 227 preview-only and 36 unsupported models. The estimated share of photographers on a verified body changes from 42% to 43%. The tracking documents and generated coverage table use these counts.

title: Show RAW starting-colour provenance in Profile panels
author: QuirkyTurtle94
body:

title: M-export: a resized export keeps the edge it was asked for
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1312.

Your pointer was right: it's double rounding. `Resize::apply` returns the rounded size (2000 × 1333), then the render fits the frame into that box again in `Frame::fit`. A raw's crop leaves the frame a hair narrower than 3:2 in floats (5999.999… instead of 6000), so the height-limited refit computes 1333 × 1.4999999 = 1999.49… and rounds down. Two small changes: `Frame::fit` returns the box unchanged when it already has the frame's aspect up to rounding (that's what an export size is), and `export::output_size` rounds the native size to whole pixels before resizing, so float noise doesn't decide the half-pixel tie for Short Edge / Height 1333 either (1999.5 → 2000, as a full-size export of the same photo would give). Previews and other `fit` callers are unaffected unless their box already matches the aspect, where the result differs by at most a pixel.

Validation:
- `export::tests::resize_size_survives_the_render`: fails on main (`(1999, 1333)` instead of `(2000, 1333)` for long edge 2000; also 2048 → 2047 and Megapixels off by one), passes here. It checks the issue's sizes on a frame a hair under 3:2, then every mode (Long/Short Edge, Width, Height, W × H, Megapixels, Percent) on 3:2, 4:3, 16:9 and 1:1, landscape and portrait: the rendered size equals what `Resize::apply` returns.
- Reverting either change makes the test fail again.
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib export::tests::resize`, `cargo test -p lightcraft-pipeline --lib geometry`, `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-pipeline -p lightcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (clippy 1.99 also flags an existing `chunks_exact(3)` in `spots.rs`, untouched here)
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: fit the camera-look toe from dark JPEG tones
author: AlexChambers
body:
Fixes #1307

## What was wrong

The colour training set excludes JPEG luminance below 0.015, about L* 13. Tone fitting reused that set, so it could not see the camera's darkest tones. Below the first knot, the curve interpolated in a straight line to black. That lifted deep shadows.

## Change

Tone fitting tries a separate set of luminance pairs from the existing binned proxies. It includes dark JPEG tones above a compression floor and uses the existing robust quantile medians. The conditional-median fallback uses the same wider set when its checks pass. The matrix, hue table, colour-pair eligibility and original colour training split are unchanged. Extra tone samples have a separate split, so no original colour holdout can enter tone training.

At least 96 dark pairs and 32 held-out dark pairs are required. The held-out dark luminances must correlate by rank at least 0.5. When the original curve can be fitted, the candidate must reduce its held-out dark error by at least 1%, measured as squared gamma-encoded luminance error. Sparse, flat, uncorrelated, below-floor or invalid data keeps the original curve.

If the original curve cannot be fitted, the wider curve can still be accepted after the sample-count and rank checks. In either case, the completed look must pass its existing held-out gates: a full look needs finite errors, linear-display squared error below 70% of the neutral fallback's and per-channel RMS no greater than 0.10. Partial and monochrome tone-only looks need luminance rank correlation of at least 0.5 and finite squared errors below 70% of the fallback's in both linear and gamma-encoded values. The monochrome comparison uses luminance; the full and partial comparisons use colour channels. Black JPEG samples do not force a flat black segment. Sensor clipping and edge exclusions still apply.

The curve keeps 32 knots and its existing serialization and CPU/GPU lookup path. LOOK_VERSION is 5 and RENDER_CACHE_VERSION is 62. The camera-look docs, parity …

title: Add a camera profile calibration wizard with validated named profiles
author: QuirkyTurtle94
body:
Adds the #1315 calibration wizard to the Photo menu and Profile panel. Users can build profiles from a folder, selection or current collection, compare whole-photo holdout results, install multiple named profiles per camera, and choose a profile for a photo or selection.

- Runs locally in a cancellable background job, with bounded sampling and memory-gated decoding. No uploads.
- Holds out every fifth usable distinct RAW. Installation requires improvement or an explicit override.
- Saves profile choices in catalog/XMP edits with undo; supports model defaults and reversible removal/restoration. Missing choices use a diagnosed built-in fallback.
- Includes profile identity in decoded, rendered and offline smart-preview caches; reload needs no restart.

Builds on #1332 (starting-colour provenance). Optional aggregate-pair export remains dependent on #1319; camera-style metadata is not exposed yet, so the wizard guides manual separation and warns about mixed styles.

Eleven RAWs were usable (9 training, 2 holdout); RMS was 0.031405 → 0.031377, a small difference, not evidence of a material colour-quality gain. Repeating with the installed profile as baseline produced equal error and correctly required an explicit override. No photographs are included.

Closes #1315.

title: LR-EDIT-COLOR-TEMP: Kelvin white balance from Sony's white-balance presets
author: PiMinusMax
body:
## What

Sony raws of cameras without measured colour matrices are edited on the relative white-balance scale (−100..+100, 6500 K / 0 = as shot), so the Temp slider shows no Kelvin (#296 for the general complaint). Sony ARWs carry the information for a Kelvin scale themselves: the encrypted `SR2SubIFD` stores the multipliers of every white-balance preset, five of them at a stated temperature (`WB_RGBLevels2500K`, `3200K`, `4500K`, `6000K`, `8500K`).

This PR reads those five presets (`vendor/arw.rs`, through the existing `sr2::SubIfd`) and uses them exactly where #730 uses the spectral matrices: they only turn the as-shot multipliers into a temperature and tint. Look, Bradford adaptation, pixel-identical upgrade of legacy settings (`legacy_white`), `Op::SetAsShotWb` and the catalog/file agreement are all unchanged and shared.

Covered: ILCA-99M2, ILCA-77M2, SLT-A33, DSC-RX10 (checked on 80–150 of my own photos each) and ILCE-3500, ILCE-7S (the public corpus samples). Cameras in `spectral` keep reading through their matrices.

## Model (`crates/raw/src/kelvin_presets.rs`)

In `(ln R/G, ln B/G)`:
- The five presets are joined piecewise linearly, mired linear along each segment, end segments extended (clamped to 2000–50000 K).
- Tint is the perpendicular offset from the curve, scaled by the locus's own (u, v) spacing per unit arc length.
- The isotherms lean against the curve's normal: an offset also moves mired by `ISOTHERM_TILT` = 0.74 × the mired the same distance along the curve would.

The two off-curve constants come from the 14 Sony bodies that have both `spectral` matrices and presets (one CC0 raw.pixls.us sample each for the presets, a grid of multipliers through `as_shot_white_through`): tilt 0.59–0.84 (mean 0.74), tint spacing 0.90–1.04 of the locus's (mean 0.98, taken as 1).

## Checks

Shots with the Kelvin set on the camera read back what the camera was set to:

| Body | Camera setting | Reads |
|---|---|---|
| ILCA-77M2 | 3400 K | 3396 K / 0 |
| ILCA-77M…

title: Colour noise reduction: joint linear chroma filter with speck brake, CPU and GPU (#815)
author: PiMinusMax
body:
Closes #815 once ready. The method is settled and measured; status at the end.

### What

A new colour noise reduction, the "joint" method. Colour is filtered as signed linear differences R−Y and B−Y. Nothing is clipped, and Y stays exactly as it was. A fixed, denoised guide decides which neighbours may exchange colour. The weights are the same for both colour differences and follow edges, so colour does not bleed into fringes. A speck brake takes out isolated, strongly coloured specks before the guide sees them. It changes their colour only, never their brightness, and keeps points that are also brighter (stars, small lights).

- CPU: `crates/pipeline/src/nrc_joint.rs`, with a bit-for-bit reference for the tests (`nrc_joint_reference.rs`).
- GPU: `crates/gpu/src/wgsl/nrcj.wgsl`. Large images run in bands of rows whose halo covers the filter's reach. The noise model is fitted on the CPU from ~130 000 samples only.
- GPU and CPU agree within 1/255 (equivalence tests).

Figures, measurements and timings are in #815, latest: https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/815#issuecomment-6132695438

### Cost

At 33 MP the colour NR takes about 3.5 s on the CPU (i7-7820HQ, 2017) and about 1.2–1.5 s on a Quadro M2200. Main's colour NR barely acts at the default 25 and costs much less. Opening a photo and exporting get slower; moving sliders with a warm cache does not.

### Status

- **Process V3.** The joint method is a new process, V3, and the latest. Edits on V1 and V2 keep main's colour NR (`local::joint_colour_nr`, test `colour_nr_follows_the_process`). Docs: `process-versions.md`, `nr-color-joint.md`, the parity checklist, what's new. #944 also claims V3 and V4; whichever lands first, the other renumbers.
- **Prototype switches removed.** `LIGHTCRAFT_NR_V2` and `NRV2_*` are gone, together with the square-root and per-channel variants they selected and their GPU kernels. `nrc_params` keeps the former defaults as constants, so V3 renders exactly as the prototype did. …

title: Luminance noise reduction: wavelet on linear Y with line protection, Contrast and Detail, CPU and GPU (#1129)
author: PiMinusMax
body:
Closes #1129. **Built on the colour NR PR (#1348)**: until that one is merged, this diff contains its commits too. The luminance NR's own changes are in `crates/pipeline/src/nrl.rs`, `crates/gpu/src/wgsl/nrl.wgsl` and the stage-cache part of `crates/pipeline/src/lib.rs` / `crates/gpu/src/render.rs`.

### What

A new luminance noise reduction on linear Y:

- Five à-trous (B3) wavelet levels. On each level the detail is shrunk against the noise expected at that brightness.
- Line and speck protection on the two fine levels: directional energy along eight directions, from the neighbours only. Thin lines at any angle are kept, isolated specks go.
- A noise model per level from the flattest blocks of the frame, with bounds against texture and, in small previews, content.
- **Contrast now works** (coarse levels); Detail acts on the fine ones.
- The change of Y is *added* to R, G and B. It does not darken shadows and does not touch chroma, except where a channel reaches its floor; that part goes to the other channels.

Also in this PR:

- **Stage cache.** It keeps the image before the luminance NR and the NR's statistics. Moving Luminance, Detail or Contrast does not redo the colour NR.
- **GPU port** (`nrl.wgsl`), within 1 LSB of the CPU.
- **Shared band planning for both NRs on the GPU** (`band_budget` / `band_rows`), with the reserve raised to 640 MB.
- **Y handoff.** The colour NR hands the luminance of its result to the luminance NR, bit for bit.
- **Statistics sampling.** The tiles are sampled from one oriented, prefiltered source: a 1920 px loupe went from 4.5 s to 0.2 s.

Figures, measurements and timings: https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/1129#issuecomment-6132695842 and, for the combined pipeline, https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/815#issuecomment-6132695438

### Tests

title: Detail: Remove Hot Pixels, on for newly imported raws (#1345)
author: PiMinusMax
body:
For #1345. A new box in Detail ▸ Noise Reduction, **Remove Hot Pixels** (raws only). It is on for newly imported raws and off for edits saved before it existed, so their look does not change. Independent of the noise reduction PRs (#1348, #1349).

### What it does

At high ISO, single photosites read far brighter than all their neighbours. Demosaicing turns each into a small red, green or blue dot, and noise reduction can only make it fainter. The box replaces them in the raw mosaic, before demosaicing (`crates/raw/src/hotpixel.rs`, `RawImage::suppress_hot_pixels`):

1. **Noise model per image.** On a sparse sample, each photosite is compared with the median of its same-colour neighbours. The spread per brightness gives `σ² = a·level + b`.
2. **Candidates.** A photosite more than 5 σ above every one of its nearest same-colour neighbours.
3. **Real light is kept.** A candidate with at least two direct neighbours more than 4 σ above their own surroundings is left alone; a hot pair has only one.
4. The rest are replaced by the median of their same-colour neighbours. If more than 0.2 % of the photosites would be replaced, nothing is changed.

On the α77 II ISO 8000 frame of #1345 it replaces 2044 photosites (0.009 %) in 0.77 s on an i7-7820HQ. The red dots drop from 367 to 201, and 5 of the 7 strongest are gone (Fig. 1 there).

### Why a box, on by default

Lightroom has no control for this. darktable and RawTherapee have a hot pixel filter that is off by default, and Capture One a "Single Pixel" slider at 0. Here it is on for new raws, because the dots are an artefact nobody wants. It stays a box, because a star field shot with a very sharp lens can have real points that light a single photosite. Whoever shoots those unticks it.

### How

- `Detail::nr_outliers` (`crates/develop/src/settings.rs`): `false` by default and for saved edits without the field (`#[serde(default)]`), `true` in `DevelopSettings::for_raw`. It is part of the settings, so the sidecar and the rende…

title: macOS: closing the window ends the process in on_exit, as menu Quit does
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1331.

The close button still goes through eframe's teardown: `on_exit` runs, then eframe drops the window while AppKit's run loop is still going (`run_and_return`). AccessKit's macOS adapter gives the content view back its original class, AppKit's Touch Bar support still has a KVO observation on it, and the next display cycle throws "not registered", which aborts the app. Menu Quit doesn't crash because #444 already ends the process right after `on_exit`. This does the same from inside `on_exit` on macOS, after settings and library are saved and background renders have stopped, so every way out takes that path. Same fix as storytold/gridcraft#117 (storytold/gridcraft#316) and storytold/vectorcraft#670, also open for storytold/deckcraft#279. `on_exit` only runs once the app exists, so a renderer that fails to start still relaunches on the next one. Windows and Linux are unchanged.

I left the explicit `std::process::exit(0)` in the menu-Quit path from #444 as it is. On macOS it is now never reached, but it keeps that path obvious. Happy to drop it.

Validation:
- `on_exit_ends_the_process_on_macos` (new, in `apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs`): runs `on_exit` in a child copy of the test binary and checks the process ends inside it on macOS (and returns elsewhere). Fails on main (`on_exit returned` is printed), passes here
- I couldn't reproduce the crash itself on an M1 Pro with no Touch Bar: on main, clicking the close button (AX `AXCloseButton`) exits 0 with no crash report. With the fix it still exits 0
- `cargo clippy -p lightcraft --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`. Without `--no-deps`, clippy 1.99 stops on `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` in `crates/pipeline/src/spots.rs:250`, which is already on main and not touched here
- (macOS 27, Apple silicon)

title: Fix Intel Mac crash: probe Metal shader language version support
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Summary

Fixes crashes on Intel Macs where all ArtCraft apps fail to launch with `Metal: error: invalid value 'metal3.2' in '-std=metal3.2'`.

The wgpu Metal backend was choosing MSL version purely from OS version, but legacy Intel GPUs have older Metal compilers that reject newer MSL versions.

## Solution

Vendors wgpu-hal 30.0.1 with the patch from gfx-rs/wgpu#10592:
- Probes the Metal compiler at adapter creation by compiling a test kernel
- Steps down from OS-selected version until compiler accepts it
- Modern Macs: tries Metal 3.2 → succeeds immediately
- Legacy Intel Macs: tries 3.2 → 3.1 → ... → 2.4/2.3 until one works

## Issues Fixed

Fixes storytold/photocraft#1859
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2126  
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2190

## Testing

- ✅ Compiles on macOS
- ✅ Passes clippy
- ⚠️ Untested on real Intel Mac hardware (awaiting community testing)

## Notes

The vendored wgpu-hal will be removed once upstream releases the fix and ArtCraft can bump to that version.

---
— sent on behalf of @mjohnson7cd by Claude Code

title: CR2: as-shot white balance of the PowerShot G9 from its WBInfo preset rows (part of #1273)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1273 (the Canon PowerShot G9; the Nikons are in #1284 and the Olympus E-10 in #1297).

The G9 writes no ColorData (`0x4001`), so `wb_from_color_balance` found nothing and the file opened with no as-shot white balance. Its preset levels are in maker-note tag `0x0029`, which the ExifTool Canon tag-name documentation calls WBInfo (the G9's WB tags). The values are int32 in the maker note's byte order, four per preset in G R B G order, at documented rows: 2 Auto, 10 Daylight, 18 Cloudy, 26 Tungsten, 34 Fluorescent, 50 Flash, 58 Underwater, 66 Custom 1, 74 Custom 2. ShotInfo (`0x0004`) value 7 says which preset was used.

The decoder now reads that row, but only when ColorData gives nothing. It applies the same plausibility test as the ColorData levels: greens at least 256 and within 5 % of each other, ratios 0.25 to 6. The test is factored out of `wb_from_color_balance` so both paths share it. Value 14 (Daylight Fluorescent) has no documented row and is left unmapped rather than guessed. On the CC0 file IMG_1188.CR2 (Custom 1, row 66: 848 1747 1676 848) this gives R 2.060 and B 1.976. AlexChambers measured the camera JPEG's neutral areas and they imply the same gains within 0.1 %. Only the Custom 1 row was checked on a real file; the other rows follow the documentation.

No RENDER_CACHE_VERSION bump: the camera-look fit was already accepted on this body and the render stays at ΔE76 1.41 (measured in the #1284 review). Only the as-shot white and As Shot change. Happy to add the bump if you prefer.

With #1284 and #1297 this leaves the D50 from #1273: its ColorBalance is enciphered.

title: Before/After wipe: the line stays in the middle of the view when zoomed in
author: marcoarnulfo

title: Display profile: zoomed-in windows are drawn again with a monitor profile in use
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1354.

With a monitor profile selected, the loupe's render jobs go through `Renderer::job_for`, which keys them for the display they render for (`RenderJob::with_display` changes `job.key`). The zoom window was remembered in `region_tiles` / `compare_tiles` under the key it had before that, while its texture came back with the display key, so `draw_window` never found a matching tile and the zoomed view kept showing the canvas-sized render, magnified. Without a profile the two keys are the same, which is why it only showed up after picking one. The window is now remembered under the key it actually renders with, in the loupe and in Compare/Reference panes.

Also fixes #1365. Since d7eb6b2a (#787) the macOS app shows previews through the screen's profile whenever none is chosen, so every Mac renders its views for a display and hits this bug without ever picking a profile: the 1:1 view stays soft, as 0.6.0 never did.

Validation:
- `in_the_loupe::with_the_screen_profile_the_window_is_drawn` (no profile chosen, the screen reports Display P3): fails on main (the window is rendered but never painted), passes here
- `in_the_loupe::with_a_display_profile_the_windows_are_drawn` (Display P3 profile, 1:1 in the loupe and in Compare): fails on main (the window texture is rendered but never painted), passes here
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-ui-egui --lib -- in_the_loupe::with_a_display_profile in_the_loupe::compare in_the_loupe::a_compare in_the_loupe::one_to_one in_the_loupe::reference_view in_the_loupe::side_by_side headless::tests::display_profile`
- `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-ui-egui --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Add Arabic (العربية) interface translation
author: hasan-sdaif
body:
`ar.json` and `ar-formats.json` for the interface, in the same shape as the other languages:

- **`ar.json`** — 2,152 messages, the union of every other catalog, with placeholder multisets kept identical. Photography vocabulary Arabic users know from Lightroom/Apple Photos (تعريض، توازن اللون الأبيض، معاينة ذكية، المحذوفات الأخيرة…).
- **`ar-formats.json`** — all 246 `tr_format!` templates, build-checked: English plural suffixes hidden with `{:.0}` the way Ukrainian does, the quit-toast verbs absorbed into the sentence with `{1:.0}` like ja/de/uk, and dates following the numeric conventions of the Spanish/German catalogs (`{weekday}، {day:02}/{month:02}/{year}`, `{month:02}/{year}`).
- **Registry** — the `language_table!` `Ar` entry (ISO 15924 `Arab`; the engine's craft-fonts fallback already ships Noto Sans Arabic), `app.language.arabic`, every `ar-*` locale resolving, tests for the tag parsing and the dispatch.
- **Docs** — README language list, refreshed `localization.md` table, and a `docs/localization-ar.md` note in the style of the es/ja pages.

No layout mirroring and no direction call: egui 0.36 has neither a global direction switch nor bidi reordering, so Arabic text in the shell reads with its words in reverse order however good the catalog is. I left that out of this PR rather than pretend at it — it needs its own pass first, and a catalog that compiles and reads correctly once that lands.

Validated against the repo's invariants (catalog union, placeholder multisets, the format-argument usage, no ▸/▾ in values, paintable punctuation). I can't build the Rust here; the two build errors you found were mine for writing against an API that doesn't exist in 0.36.2.

title: LR-IMP-CAMERA-COVERAGE: Nikon D90 NEFs drop their filler columns (no pink band)
author: menno-zeilstra
body:
## Problem
Nikon D90 NEFs open with a pink band down the right edge.

The D90 writes 4352 × 2868 samples. The last 42 columns (from 4310) are filler at a flat ~254 (sd ≈ 2–9 over all rows, whatever the exposure), while the image samples sit on black 0. `trailing_masked_columns` only trims columns near zero (< 1 % of white and < 10 % of the interior), so these stay in the image. White balance then turns them pink.

## Fix
The D90 joins the D4 in `MEASURED_BODIES` (`crates/raw/src/vendor/nef.rs`). Other bodies are unchanged: a crop needs the model, sample size and bit depth to all match.

| | Value | How it was measured |
|---|---|---|
| Image area | 4288 × 2848 at (10, 10) | Aligned the raw green channel with the embedded full-size camera JPEG on 10 of 550 NEFs from one body (r = 0.92–0.99; one file came out at x = 12) |
| White level | 3830 | Green saturates at 3840–3851 while red and blue run on to 4095, so the per-file maximum would leave clipped highlights magenta (same as the D4) |

A generic rule (trim trailing flat columns) was rejected: a dark frame in the same set has interior columns with sd ≈ 10, close enough to the filler to risk trimming real pixels.

Also checked: a D5600 (6016 × 4016, black 600, all channels clip at 16350) has no filler columns. It still shows 8 px more per side than its 6000 × 4000 camera JPEG at (8, 8); that's cosmetic and left for another PR.

## Tests
- New `measured_d90_drops_the_filler_columns`: crop, white level and reported size for a synthetic D90 frame.
- `lightcraft-raw`: clippy clean, all tests pass. `cargo xtask parity`, `layers` and `assets` pass.
- Rendered real D90 files with `lightcraft-cli render`: no band, 4288 × 2848.
- `cargo xtask ci` was run on Windows with Rust 1.99. Clippy fails in code this PR doesn't touch: the new `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` lint in `lightcraft-pipeline`, and an unused `descriptor_copy` in `lightcraft-catalog` tests on Windows. Because clippy failed, the `ci` run skipped the workspace tests …

title: LR-EDIT-LIGHT-CURVE-POINT: ⌥-drag moves a curve point a tenth as far, for fine adjustment
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1363.

Dragging a point-curve point always put it under the pointer, so there was no way to nudge it by a small amount. With ⌥/Alt held, the drag is now relative: each frame the point moves by a tenth of the pointer's motion, in both axes, still clamped between its neighbours. Being relative to where the point already is, pressing Alt mid-drag doesn't make it jump; releasing it goes back to following the pointer. A tenth matches the Shift fine-drag on the sliders; happy to switch to a different ratio if you'd rather.

Validation:
- `tests_curve::alt_dragging_a_point_moves_it_a_tenth_as_far`: fails on main (the point lands under the pointer, (0.4, 0.7) instead of ~(0.49, 0.52)), passes here; with the factor set to 1.0 it fails again
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-ui-egui --lib tests_curve`, `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: KEY-SLIDER-TYPE: a typed slider value keeps editing after the click is released
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1362.

When you click a slider's value, the press opens the text field over the readout, but egui still delivers the click on release to the readout (it owned the press), so the field isn't hovered and egui's surrender-focus-on-click takes its focus away. That was only recovered in the field's first two frames; any normal click held longer than that ended the edit with `Away`, which is why typing only worked while holding the button. The opening release now gets the same treatment as those first frames: the field takes the focus back after drawing, and the edit carries on.

Validation:
- `widgets::numeric_entry_tests::typing_after_a_released_click_still_edits` (press, hold a few frames, release, then type and Return): fails on main (the field has lost the keyboard after the release), passes here; removing the new condition makes it fail again
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-ui-egui --lib -- numeric_entry slider_values_can_be_typed opening_numeric_release the_straighten_value`
- `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: LR-PREF-INTERFACE: text sizes have names, the seven type roles of the theme

body:
Off `main`.

Part 1 of 8 of what was this one 3,200-line PR: it was too large to review in one sitting and held eight changes with their own behaviour, so it is split along those lines (the list is under **Not in this PR**). Text sizes are numbers written where the text is drawn: 44 places set a size past `Tokens::font` and `Tokens::semibold`, and there is no name for a size that a panel can use. The interface drew 17 sizes from 8.5 to 20 pt, 102 of 237 uses on half points, and nothing says which size has which job.

title: LR-EDIT-RELIGHT: Relight, lights placed on the photo with AI scene geometry (MoGe-2 in pure Rust)
author: fabian-co
body:
## What this adds

**Relight**: a new tool that adds lights to a photo after it was taken (a lamp placed on the scene, a low sun from one side, a spot on a face). It is the lamp button right under Edit in the tool strip (Window ▸ Relight), and it is non-destructive like every other edit. It is not a Lightroom feature, so it is tracked as a new row, `LR-EDIT-RELIGHT` (P2, 🟡), in the "beyond Lightroom" spirit of `LR-REM-BLEMISH`.

User guide and design notes: `docs/relight.md`.

### The lights

- Up to 8 lights per photo, each a **Point** (a lamp shining every way), a **Directional** (parallel light from far away) or a **Spot** (a cone from a place).
- Per light: Intensity, Angle, Elevation (a full turn, −180° to 180°), Depth (how far in front of the surface under its marker), Falloff, Cone.
- **Light Color** is one of two things, whichever was set last: a **Temperature** in Kelvin (2000–12000, 6500 neutral) or a **Color** picked from a colour picker or typed as hex (`#ff8800`, `#f80`). They don't mix; the other value is kept and ignored, and the panel says which is in use.
- For the scene: **Ambient** (the light the photo already had), **Softness**, **Shine** (specular), and **Cast Shadows** with Shadow Opacity and Shadow Softness.

### On the photo

- Every light has a marker. A light moves **only** when its own marker is dragged (one undo step per drag); a click on a marker selects it; nothing else on the photo moves or adds a light. Delete removes the selected light.
- Directional and Spot lights carry a small **figure turned in space** by their Angle, Elevation and Cone, on the photo and in the panel: a disc with parallel rays for a Directional light, a cone for a Spot. Moving a slider turns the figure.

### Where the shapes come from

A light needs to know which way every surface faces and how far it is.

- **Scene Analysis** runs **MoGe-2** (Microsoft, ViT-S, the `moge-2-vits-normal` checkpoint), which predicts per pixel the surface normal, the depth and whethe…

title: LR-BEHAV-RENDER-FIDELITY: calibrated Contrast and Blacks in process V3 (#523)
author: AlexChambers
body:
Addresses #523.

Rebased onto main `0da998f2` after integration batch 40. This branch inherits main's `LOOK_VERSION` 9 and `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 64.

This splits calibrated Contrast and Blacks from the larger V3 calibration branch. It
improves their response to the same Light-panel values used in Lightroom. Whites retains
V2 behavior for positive and negative amounts; its calibration is a planned follow-up.
Exposure and Highlights/Shadows also remain open under #523.

## Changes

On a raw with a camera tone curve, V3 applies fitted Contrast per channel and fitted Blacks
as a per-channel/luminance mix. Both work in linear ProPhoto through the sRGB transfer.
The camera curve keeps V2 Whites, then calibrated Contrast and Blacks run before the colour
stage. CPU previews compose the encoding and per-channel operators into one linear-input
table. If an operator uses luminance, the CPU retains the original evaluation for the
whole sequence, including Contrast before positive Blacks. This prevents interpolation
error from crossing the luminance cutoff after camera chroma scaling creates mixed-sign
components. Metal and high-bit-depth CPU exports retain the source operator tables.
Render windows use the same rules.

V1 and V2 keep their pixels and cache keys. Persistent keys for V3 and later include the
resolved rendering process, so a saved future process number cannot reuse pixels made by a
build that resolves it differently. New imports and Reset select the current process.
Update to Current Process keeps main's settings-only, undoable behavior and never downgrades
a future process number.

This split adds no photo statistic, decoder work, smart-preview metadata or format change,
opening refresh, per-photo check, or fixed-key fallback. Local adjustments and sources
without a camera curve keep their V2 operators.

## Calibration and agreement

The fits use black-box observations of @AlexChambers's Lightroom exports of Sony ILCE-7CR
photos. Each slider amount is paired wit…

title: LR-EDIT-OPTICS-PROFILE: enable Sony ILCE-7M3 (A7 III) embedded distortion correction
author: alvarohn
body:
## Summary

The A7 III's raw-IFD `0x7037` distortion tables have been read since #498 but refused by the model check, because
their corner warp was unverified in review. This validates them against the camera's own JPEG of the same exposure
and enables the body. One line in `arw_lens.rs` changes; everything else is tests, docs and the measurement tool.

## Validation

27 RAW+JPEG pairs from one ILCE-7M3 (Lens Comp. ▸ Distortion Comp.: Auto, so the JPEG is the camera's corrected
render): a checkerboard filling the frame on a TV (handheld) and a desktop monitor (tripod), compressed and
uncompressed raws, wide open to f/8, plus one textured wall. Lenses: FE 16–35mm F4 ZA OSS (16, 20, 35 mm),
FE 28–70mm F3.5–5.6 OSS (28, 33, 50, 70 mm), FE 50mm F1.8. Tables range from strong barrel (16 mm, −690 at the
corner) to strong pincushion (70 mm, +1161).

LightCraft renders each ARW with the profile correction on and off; sub-pixel board corners are matched with the
JPEG's and a similarity (zoom, rotation, shift) is fitted, since the camera fills its frame with its own zoom. No lens
coefficient is fitted.

title: LR-META-XMP: keep Lightroom's saved Upright geometry from XMP sidecars, and put sidecar crops in the photo's frame (#205)
author: AlexChambers
body:
Fixes #205 for XMP sidecars and DNG-embedded XMP with Upright Auto, Full, Level or Vertical:

- Auto is measured against Lightroom's exports.
- Full, Level and Vertical use the same matrices and convention, checked on their structure only.
- Guided Upright and Lightroom catalogs don't carry it over yet, and the import says so (see *Not covered*).

Along the way, this fixes older problems:

- `PerspectiveUpright` 2, 3 and 4 were read as the wrong modes.
- Sidecar crops landed in the wrong place on portrait raws and when straightened.
- Rotate Left / Right left a stored Upright correction behind.
- Paste, Sync and Auto Sync carried a correction into virtual copies in the wrong frame, and into other photos at all (one scene's correction applied to another).

Rebased onto main `0da998f2` after integration batch 40. This branch inherits main's `LOOK_VERSION` 9 and `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 64.

## What was wrong

- **Saved Upright ignored.** Lightroom saves its Upright analysis with the edit: `crs:UprightVersion`, `crs:UprightTransformCount` (6) and one 3 × 3 matrix per mode, `crs:UprightTransform_0` to `_5`. LightCraft read only `crs:PerspectiveUpright` and solved the photo again with its own Upright, so the framing differed from Lightroom's. On the public references below, main's result is 23 to 78 px away from Lightroom's export on average at full size. One photo, where Lightroom's Auto decided no correction was needed, is moved 78 px on average (131 px at worst) by main's solver.
- **Mode numbers.** `PerspectiveUpright` 2, 3 and 4 were read as Level, Vertical and Full. They are Full, Level and Vertical.
- **Sidecar crops.** These were taken as if Lightroom's edges were on the photo as shown. They are on the stored image, before its orientation, and Lightroom's straighten angle turns the other way. The catalog import already converted them (`catalog_crop`, #483); the sidecar path didn't.

title: LR-IMP-CAMERA-COVERAGE: Nikon D7100 NEFs develop at Lightroom's frame, so its crops line up
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1248.

The D7100 records no `CropArea`, and the extra data around its frame is picture rather than masked lines, so the NEF decoder kept all of it: 6036 × 4020 in full frame, 4812 × 3212 in the 1.3x crop mode. Lightroom develops the camera JPEG's size (6000 × 4000 and 4800 × 3200, which I checked against the full-size JPEGs embedded in the NEFs), centred, so a Lightroom crop applied to the larger frame landed a few pixels off. This adds two `MEASURED_BODIES` entries, the same mechanism as the D4, with the offsets from the issue's fits against Lightroom's exports: (18, 10) in full frame and (6, 6) in 1.3x crop. The D7100 has no measured white level, so `white` becomes optional and the body keeps the level from its data, as before. Only 14-bit files are matched, since those are the only ones measured; happy to add the 12-bit sizes too if you'd rather pool them.

Validation:
- `measured_d7100_image_area` (new, both image areas plus a D7200 control): fails on main (crop `0, 0, 6036 × 4020` instead of `18, 10, 6000 × 4000`), passes here
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-raw --lib vendor::nef`, `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-raw --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- on DSC_1316.NEF and DSC_2763.NEF from zjqc/photographing-art, main decodes 6036 × 4020 and 4812 × 3212 with no crop
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

This overlaps with #1053, which also turns `white` into an `Option`; whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

title: Fix on_exit arity (GUI does not compile) and embed craft-fonts by default
author: sblount2025-design
body:
Two small build fixes found while building 0.7.0 from a clean clone on macOS (Apple silicon, Rust 1.99.0).

## 1. The `lightcraft` GUI binary does not compile as shipped

`apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs:67` calls `eframe::App::on_exit(self)` with one argument, but `Cargo.lock` pins eframe 0.36.2, whose trait method is `fn on_exit(&mut self, _gl: Option<&glow::Context>)`:

```
error[E0061]: this function takes 2 arguments but 1 argument was supplied
  --> apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs:67:13
   |
67 |             eframe::App::on_exit(self);
   |             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^------ argument #2 of type `Option<&eframe::glow::Context>` is missing
```

Only the `lightcraft` target fails — `lightcraft-cli` builds fine, which is probably why it slipped through.

Passing `None` is behaviour-preserving: this impl's own `on_exit`, twelve lines below at `main.rs:79`, ignores the `_gl` parameter entirely — it saves prefs and closes the library. The call site is the macOS menu-bar quit path, saving before `std::process::exit(0)`.

## 2. A plain `cargo build --release` ships a CJK-blind binary

The engine's build script warns and carries on:

```
warning: lightcraft-engine@0.7.0: no craft-fonts embedded: Chinese and Japanese
text will render as empty boxes. Clone https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts
next to this repo and rebuild with CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=../craft-fonts
```

With craft-fonts already cloned beside the repo as the warning asks, the build still needs `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` passed by hand every time. A build-time requirement that lives only in a warning is one that gets forgotten and then comes back as a bug report about missing glyphs.

This adds it to `.cargo/config.toml`:

```toml
[env]
CRAFT_FONTS_DIR = { value = "../craft-fonts", relative = true }
```

- `relative = true` resolves against the repo root, so no absolute path is committed.
- No `force`, so a `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` already in the environment still wins for a one-off build against a different font set.
- If craft-f…

title: LR-CROP-STRAIGHTEN: a crop shrunk to fit by Straighten grows back as the angle returns
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1388.

`CropGeometry::with_angle` kept the current crop whenever it still fit at the new angle, and only shrank it when it didn't. So once a turn had shrunk the box to fit, that smaller box fit at every smaller angle and was kept, and each further swing could only shrink it more. Now a crop that is already the largest of its aspect at its own angle (the full photo, or one a turn shrank to fit) is refitted as the largest at the new angle, so it grows back as you return towards 0°, as in Lightroom. A smaller hand-drawn crop that still fits is kept as before. Every angle entry point (slider, Angle field, rotate handle, `develop.set` on `crop.angle`) goes through `with_angle`, so they all get this.

One behaviour change worth a look: `quick_develop_reset_and_batch_paths_fit_too` asserted that resetting the angle to 0° kept the crop shrunk at 12°. That was the bug, so it now expects the full photo. A free crop the user happened to draw exactly at the largest size also follows the largest size when the angle changes; I think that's right for "Constrain to image", happy to switch if you'd rather tie it to the drag's starting crop.

Validation:
- `tests_crop_angle::a_crop_shrunk_by_straightening_grows_back_towards_0` (slider out and back in one drag, and in two): fails on main (`the largest crop at 8°` gets the 20° box), passes here
- `crop::tests::with_angle_grows_a_fitted_crop_back_as_the_angle_returns` (original, 1:1, 16:9): fails on main, passes here

Text set strong (a heading, the chosen tab, a title) is drawn in Inter SemiBold. For other scripts the semibold family falls back on the same regular craft-fonts faces that regular text uses, so strong Arabic text is drawn at regular weight, beside bold Latin on the same line.

title: Lightroom import: count the originals while they are probed, not only after all of them
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1396.

The "14" is the catalog read: `read_with_progress` counts its 13 tables plus the validation step, and then `LightroomJob::prepare` hands every original to `ImportJob::prepare` in one go. `prepare_files` probes the whole list first (headers + content hash, the slow part) with a throwaway `ScanProgress`, and only counts files in the planning loop that follows, which is fast. So `done` sits at 14 for the entire probe and then runs to the total in a moment. It isn't specific to Windows; it just shows more there, where reading every file is slower. The import window never hit this because it already passes `batch_size()` files at a time. Now `prepare_files` probes and plans in batches of that same size, so a long list moves the counter as it goes. A list that's already one batch, which is what the import window passes, behaves as before. Cancelling now also stops before the next batch is probed. Happy to switch to batching in `LightroomJob::prepare` instead if you'd rather keep `prepare_files` as it was.

Validation:
- `tests_import::import_job_counts_files_while_a_long_list_is_probed`: fails on main (`no file counted while the others were probed: 0`), passes here
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib -- import lightroom`: everything passes except `tests_lightroom_folder::odd_folders_never_fail_the_check`, which also fails on main here because APFS won't create a non-UTF-8 folder name ("Illegal byte sequence")
- `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clean apart from an existing `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` lint in `pipeline/src/spots.rs` on my newer toolchain), `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: LR-CLOUD-SMARTPREVIEW: opt-in lossless smart previews (#709)
author: AlexChambers
body:
Fixes #709

Rebased onto main `0da998f2` after integration batch 40. This branch inherits main's `LOOK_VERSION` 9 and `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 64.

## Changes

Adds a per-library Lossless format using the existing pure-Rust float TIFF codec with Deflate. Compact JPEG remains the default. The Settings preference controls future builds; Build Smart Previews can override it for a selection.

Lossless stores the decoded, reduced scene-linear source before tone curves and edits. It preserves finite source floats exactly, including negative values and highlights above 1.0. This improves editing from an offline proxy while retaining the proxy's existing resolution limit. Online originals still take precedence.

Existing LCSP1 JPEG previews keep working. LCSP2 adds bounded parsing, payload length and checksum checks, and a completeness marker. Format conversion rebuilds from available originals and keeps offline proxies unchanged. Unknown header and tone fields, including `white_stat`, survive rewrites.

Builds verify payload integrity and successful decoding before reusing a proxy. A Compact proxy must also be complete: a JPEG cut short still decodes, with part of the picture made up, so a cut-short Compact proxy is not counted, rendered or kept over a complete copy, and Build Smart Previews repairs it, as on main (issue #106). Migration verifies the destination before removing the source, including after an atomic copy. The structural staleness hint and the full usability check have separate names. Builds, discards and look refreshes invalidate the cache currently attached to the same library, including cache replacement and reopening in another session. Render jobs capture their cache generation before acquiring a source and reject construction if it changes. Returned sources must also belong to the current cache object, because different cache objects can have the same generation. Size accounting includes both formats and layouts. title: Library on an SMB share: the catalog files are written where macOS can't fully flush them
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1407.

On macOS `File::sync_all` and `sync_data` are both `fcntl(F_FULLFSYNC)`, and smbfs answers that with ENOTSUP (os error 45). `FsStore` treated it as a failed write, so the new library's `catalog.snap` and `prefs.json` were never renamed into place and their `.tmp` files stayed behind (the log append and truncate go through the same sync). Now every file sync in `FsStore` goes through one helper: when the full flush is refused (ENOTSUP on macOS, `ErrorKind::Unsupported` elsewhere) it falls back to a plain `fsync`, which @youyoulyz confirmed works on the same NAS (`F_FULLFSYNC` → errno 45, `fsync` → 0). If `fsync` fails too, the error goes up as before, and local disks still get the full flush. `write_atomic` also removes its temp file when it fails, like `write_atomic_with` already did.

std has no plain `fsync` on macOS, so it's a libSystem call in `crates/sysmem` next to the existing one (safe API, `// SAFETY:` comment, retried on EINTR; `sync_all` on other platforms), with AGENTS.md and the architecture doc updated. ENOTSUP is checked by its code because std maps os error 45 to `Uncategorized`, not `Unsupported`.

Validation:
- `tests_journal::a_volume_without_a_full_flush_still_gets_its_files` (syncs fail with ENOTSUP through a test-only hook in `store.rs`, and the test counts the `fsync` fallbacks): fails on main (no `catalog.snap` after creating the library), passes here
- `sysmem` `fsync_flushes_an_open_file_and_reports_errors`
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-catalog --lib tests_journal::`, `cargo xtask layers`
- `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-catalog -p lightcraft-sysmem --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: LR-IMP-PREVIEW-READ: raw thumbnails and stand-ins decode the smallest embedded JPEG that is big enough
author: dev-null-undefined
body:
## The problem

An unedited raw's grid thumbnail and its first picture in the loupe are the camera's embedded JPEG (`embedded_preview_srgb`). `embedded_preview` always returns the largest one. A Sony A7R VI ARW holds a 1616 × 1080 JPEG (0.3 MB) next to a 9984 × 6656 one (5.6 MB), and a 512 px thumbnail still decoded the big one: 100–133 ms on the three A7R VI photos I measured in a quiet run, against 14–16 ms for the small one. Many Nikon NEF and Panasonic RW2 files keep a mid-sized JPEG too.

## Changes

- **`lightcraft_raw::embedded_preview_covering(bytes, min_edge)`.** Of a TIFF-based raw's embedded JPEGs, it returns the smallest whose long edge is at least `min_edge`, provided it looks like a copy of the largest one. Otherwise it returns the largest, as `embedded_preview` does. A smaller JPEG counts as a copy when:
  - its aspect ratio is within 1 % of the largest one's, so a letterboxed thumbnail of another shape is never used. Sony's 1616 × 1080 JPEG is 0.25 % off 3:2.
  - it has as many colour components. An iPhone ProRAW DNG keeps grey semantic masks of the picture's shape as JPEGs, and without this check the first version picked one.
- `embedded_preview` is unchanged and shares the candidate list. The JPEG frame header is read with `get()` and checked arithmetic. `is_dct_jpeg` now uses the same marker walk, with the same rules.

The colour-space handling stays in `decode_raw_preview`, which now takes a `covering` argument; there is no second decode function. `load_embedded_preview` (an unsupported raw's source for editing) and the camera-look fit still use the largest JPEG. That way a source's geometry and colour never depend on its size level, and previews still match exports.

title: LR-BEHAV-GPU: say once when no GPU is found, instead of quietly rendering on the CPU
author: dev-null-undefined
body:
## The problem

When wgpu finds no graphics adapter at all, LightCraft renders everything on the CPU and says nothing at start-up. The difference is large. `render_bench` on a 14 MP ILCE-7M4 raw, on a machine with an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER and a 4-CPU quota (busy with other builds), gives:

| Render | CPU path | GPU path |
|---|---|---|
| 1920 × 1280 loupe frame while dragging Exposure | 405 ms | 12 ms |
| Full-size export render | 7.2 s | 0.42 s |

The reason is shown only where you have to go looking: Settings ▸ Performance ("Rendering on the CPU: …"), Help ▸ System Info, `ui.inspect` → `perf.gpuReason`, and a `log::warn`.

The usual cause on Linux is a missing Vulkan loader. On NixOS a `cargo run` outside `nix develop` can't find `libvulkan.so.1`, so `lightcraft_gpu` reports `no GPU adapter among Backends(…) (… vulkan drivers/libraries could not be loaded …)`. The app works, only much more slowly, and nothing says why.

## Changes

- **`panels::notices::gpu_notice(reason, enabled)`**, a pure function. It returns the notice when GPU rendering is on and the reason is `no GPU adapter among …`, the error `Gpu::new` returns when wgpu has no adapter. It returns `None` in every other case:
  - the GPU is turned off (the preference, `LIGHTCRAFT_GPU=0`, `LIGHTCRAFT_GPU_BACKEND=off`);
  - only a software adapter was found and skipped;
  - the adapter has too few storage buffers;
  - the GPU failed after start-up.
- `panels::notices::logic` adds the notice to `app.notices` (the queue the renderer fallback and the GPU crash notice use) once per session, after the device has been tried. It checks `gpu::ready()`, so the UI thread never waits for the driver, and only does so when the GPU preference is on and `app.gpu_notice` is set. The desktop app sets that flag at start-up. Headless snapshots, MCP and tests don't, so CI machines without a GPU are unchanged.
- The text: "No graphics processor found: LightCraft renders on the CPU, which is much slower. Details in Help → System Info.…

title: M5.6: a slider drag no longer decodes the edited raw again for its filmstrip thumbnail
author: dev-null-undefined
body:
## The problem

The first slider drag on an unedited raw shows almost nothing until you let go: on a Sony ILCE-7RM6 (64 MP), 2 or 3 of a 30-tick Exposure drag's drafts reach the loupe, and the full render arrives 1–4 s after release.

The cause is the filmstrip thumbnail of the photo being edited:
- An unedited raw's thumbnail is the camera's embedded preview, so the raw's thumbnail-level source has never been decoded.
- Every drag tick changes the photo's settings, so the filmstrip asks for a new thumbnail render of it on every frame.
- Each of those renders decodes the whole raw (about 0.6 s on four CPUs: `load_bytes(512)` in #1320).
- On `main` a newer job for a slot starts beside the running one, so a drag starts several of these decodes at once. They take every worker, and the loupe's drafts wait behind them.

## Changes

1. **No thumbnail render of the photo being dragged.** `request_thumb` asks for nothing while a slider drag is on that photo and it already has a thumbnail. The thumbnail follows on the first frame after the drag ends.
2. **A thumbnail is cut from the decoded preview.** When the photo's preview-level source is in memory (the photo in the loupe), its thumbnail-level source is now fitted from that source (`SourceRef::Fit`, the box filter raw sources are fitted with) instead of decoding the file again. The source is kept in the thumbnail cache, as a decoded one is.
   - Not used when the photo has an AI Denoise picture, which the cut thumbnail would lose.
   - The web worker gets the same `max_edge` and decodes as before.

## Result

`main` → this branch. Each value is the median of 3 runs (all 3 runs listed for frames shown). First Exposure drag of the unedited raw, 30 ticks at 60 Hz, GPU drafts, driven headlessly through the real app (session, renderer, job pool, GPU):

|---|---|---|
| **1920×1200 @1×**: drafts shown | 2, 3, 2 of 30 | 20, 18, 21 of 30 |
| tick → texture, median / p90 | — (2–3 drafts) | 18 / 50 ms |
