title: M5.6: with a GPU, a slider drag's preview is drawn in the frame of the drag tick
author: dev-null-undefined
body:
## The problem

During a drag, a frame applies the tick (`develop.set`), the loupe asks for a draft, and the frame ends. On the GPU the draft is ready a few milliseconds later. `Renderer::poll` only collects it at the start of the next frame, so it reaches the screen one frame later than it could. At 1920×1200 that frame is most of the time from tick to texture: a median of 18.5 ms, while the GPU drafts take a few milliseconds.

## Changes

1. **`Renderer::wait_for_draft`.** Right after the loupe asks for its draft during a drag, it waits for it, turning finished jobs into textures as they arrive, so the draft is drawn in the same frame. The wait is at most 40 % of a frame (egui's `predicted_dt`, clamped to 1/240–1/30 s).
   - It only waits when the last loupe render took well under that budget (×1.5 margin: 4.4 ms at 60 Hz). A CPU render, which would only make the frame late, isn't waited for.
   - It doesn't wait with a render offload (the web's workers), on wasm, or zoomed in, where what changes on screen is the zoom window's draft.
2. **`JobPool::wait(timeout)`.** Waits for the next finished job and keeps it for `try_recv`.
3. **`Renderer::poll`.** Its loop over finished jobs moved, unchanged, into `collect`, which the wait also calls.

## Result

`main` → this branch. Each value is the median of 3 runs. Second Exposure drag on the raw, 30 ticks at 60 Hz, GPU drafts, driven headlessly through the real app:

| | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| **1920×1200 @1×** (draft 831×554): drafts shown | 23, 19, 28 of 30 | 27, 23, 21 of 30 |
| tick → texture, median / p90 | 18.5 / 43.9 ms | 6.2 / 10.2 ms |
| frames from tick to texture, median | 1 | 0 |

title: LR-EDIT-AUTO: per-photo Auto tone
author: emmertex
body:
Refs #318

Auto only varied Exposure: every photo got the same Contrast 68, Highlights -66, Shadows 52, Vibrance 30, and Whites/Blacks 0. Now, after Auto's exposure, the other sliders follow the photo's luminance distribution:
- Highlights and Shadows scale with how much of the frame is bright or dark (the square root of its share relative to a typical photo's, clamped to 0.2–1.5× the calibrated values)
- Contrast follows the 5–95 % luminance spread: flat photos get more, contrasty ones less
- Whites and Blacks move the 99.5 / 0.5 % luminance to just short of white / black
- Vibrance eases off a little when Shadows lifts a lot; Saturation stays 0

The constants are centred so that the median of 12 CC0 corpus raws (Sony, Canon, Nikon, Olympus, Pentax, Fujifilm) still gets the calibrated recipe from #628 (Contrast ~68, Highlights ~-60, Shadows ~55, Whites/Blacks ~0). Across those raws Contrast now ranges from 34 to 80, Highlights from -31 to -99, Shadows from 45 to 78, Whites from -32 to +9 and Blacks from -14 to +40.

I didn't have the 24-photo Lightroom reference set from #628, so this doesn't re-measure dE76 against Lightroom's Auto. That's why it's "Refs" rather than "Fixes".

Tests: two very different demo scenes (a night aurora and a sunlit canyon) now get different Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites and Blacks. A synthetic test checks that the bright and dark shares drive Highlights and Shadows, and that spread drives Contrast. The existing exposure and non-finite-pixel tests still pass.

Sources: own design; data: 12 CC0 corpus raws and the procedural demo scenes.

title: Edit in PhotoCraft: say why it didn't open; find PhotoCraft on macOS and Linux
author: emmertex
body:
Refs #918

Users report that Edit in PhotoCraft does nothing. There were three causes:
- **Errors were swallowed.** The grid's right-click Edit In dropped the command result (`let _ = app.run(…)`), and a failure in the copy step (`photo.editExternal`) never reached a toast. Now `edit_in` turns every error into a toast, whichever way it was invoked (menu, shortcut, context menu or control channel), and still returns it to the caller.
- **macOS always "found" PhotoCraft.** `find_photocraft` returned `open -a PhotoCraft` even when nothing was installed, and `open`'s exit status was never checked, so the menu silently did nothing. It now looks in /Applications and ~/Applications, then asks Spotlight (`mdfind` by bundle id or by `PhotoCraft.app`), and reports when PhotoCraft is missing. `open` is waited for (it returns once LaunchServices has the file), and its error message is shown. Checked on a Mac without PhotoCraft: `open -a` exits 1 with "Unable to find application named …", and the mdfind query returns nothing for PhotoCraft and finds `Safari.app` by the same form.
- **Linux missed common installs.** A desktop entry whose `Exec=` is a bare command name is now resolved on the PATH, and a `*PhotoCraft*.AppImage` in ~/Applications or ~/.local/bin is used (the newest by name).

This doesn't overlap #910: that PR changes the stacking, links and reload after a copy is opened, while this one changes finding and launching the editor and the error reporting.

Tests: the UI test asserts the toast for a missing PhotoCraft, both through the control channel and through `app.run` (the path the context menu takes). There are unit tests for AppImage names, mdfind output and `open` failures, and the desktop-entry test is updated.

Sources: own design.

title: M5.6: Dehaze while zoomed no longer resamples the whole original on every pan and slider step
author: dev-null-undefined
body:
## The problem

With Dehaze on, a zoomed view (a window render, #323) dehazes with the airlight of the whole frame, not that of the pixels in the window. `local::frame_airlight` estimates it on a 384 px proxy of the frame. Every window job sampled the whole original down to that proxy again: every pan at 1:1 and every slider step while zoomed.

On a 64 MP raw that is ~200 ms of CPU per window, several times what the GPU render of the window itself costs. The CPU pipeline plans windows through the same function, so it pays the same.

The numbers below come from a Sony ILCE-7RM6 64 MP raw on an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER (Ryzen 7 9800X3D) under a 4-CPU cgroup quota.

## Changes (one commit; same pixels)

1. **The proxy is kept.** `frame_proxy` keeps the sampled proxy for the last 4 (source fingerprint, frame, proxy size), using `optics::fingerprint` like the lateral CA and Upright caches. `Frame` now derives `PartialEq` for the key.
   - The proxy is taken before white balance, so a WB drag still hits.
   - White balance, the dark channel, its blur and the percentile still run on the 384 px proxy every time (well under a millisecond).
   - Each entry is at most 384 × 384 × 12 B ≈ 1.8 MB.
2. **No panic on an empty image.** `optics::fingerprint` indexed the first pixel of an empty image. It now hashes only the dimensions then. The change is byte for byte the one in #1286, so the two merge without a conflict there.

## Result

`main` → this branch, `render_bench ONLY=window GPU_ONLY=1 N=7` (a 3072 × 2304 window of the 9984 × 6656 frame, `typical()` settings with Dehaze 10), best of 7, two runs each:

| | CPU time | wall clock |

| Pan (new window, source on the GPU) | 208–212 → 9–11 ms | 143–190 → 38–39 ms |
| Exposure change at 1:1 | 200–204 → 4.1 ms | 90–109 → 5.1–5.7 ms |

title: LR-MERGE-HDR: keep the reference frame's lens corrections in HDR merges
author: alvarohn
body:
## Summary

A merged HDR DNG loses the lens correction its sources carry, so Optics ▸ Enable Lens Corrections does nothing on the
result. `load_frame` strips the lens opcodes from each source (frames are merged uncorrected, which is right), but
`write_linear_dng` writes no `OpcodeList3`, so the correction never comes back. This affects every source whose
correction LightCraft reads from the file: a DNG's own `WarpRectilinear` / `WarpRectilinear2` / `FixVignetteRadial`
(e.g. DJI drones), and the camera corrections raw readers convert (Sony ILCE-7RM4A, Panasonic / Leica RW2).

The merged DNG now carries the reference frame's corrections, re-expressed for the default crop the frame keeps,
so the correction stays switchable on the result as on the sources.

## Changes

- `crates/raw/src/opcodes.rs`: `Opcode::cropped(width, height, crop)` re-expresses a lens correction for a crop of the
  image it was written for. The centre moves into the crop and the coefficients are rescaled for the crop's farthest
  corner (the normalising radius): `WarpRectilinear` kr_i·s^2i and kt·s; `WarpRectilinear2` kr_i·s^i, kt·s, valid radii
  /s; `FixVignetteRadial` k_i·s^(2i+2).
- `crates/merge/src/frame.rs`: `Frame::lens` holds the lens corrections a raw source applies (after the DNG 1.6 skip
  rule, so no `WarpRectilinear2` is left optional), re-expressed for its default crop. `Frame::orient` drops them (the
  pixels turned).
- `crates/merge/src/hdr.rs` / `output.rs`: `HdrResult::lens` is the reference frame's; `write_linear_dng` writes it as
  `OpcodeList3`. Panoramas and HDR panoramas carry none (unchanged).
- `crates/engine/src/merge.rs`: passes the HDR's corrections to the writer.
- Docs: `docs/merge.md`, the LR-MERGE-HDR checklist row, `docs/whats-new.md`.

## Tests

- `cropped_lens_corrections_correct_the_crop_like_the_whole` (raw): applying the re-expressed opcode to a crop gives the

The Performance choices are idempotent, so the test now clicks until the setting takes (at most 5 tries) and asserts that each click was accepted.

title: Recently Deleted shows deleted Local (browsed) photos (Fixes #1430)
author: Claudio911015
body:
Fixes #1430.

**Problem.** In a Local folder, Delete / "Delete Photo" runs `photo.delete`, which sets `deleted = true`. `Filter::matches_in` (`crates/catalog/src/query.rs`) drops every browsed (`local`) photo from any view that has no folder, and that includes Recently Deleted. ## Problem and change

Browsing a byte-identical copy in Local could make an import incorrectly report “already in the library”, even after the library photo had been permanently deleted and the library reopened. title: Issue #1200: portable mode, a portable.txt beside the executable keeps settings in LightCraftData
author: ArekatlaNishanthchowdary
body:
Fixes #1200.

## What it does

A file named `portable.txt` (or `LightCraft.portable`) next to the LightCraft executable makes `config_dir()` return `<exe dir>/LightCraftData`, so settings (`ui.json`), logs and downloaded models stay with a portable copy instead of going to `%APPDATA%\LightCraft`. This follows PhotoCraft's `app_dirs.rs` (markers, folder name, write probe, fallback).

Order of precedence in `crates/engine/src/config.rs`:

1. `LIGHTCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR`, unchanged. With it set (or set empty), nothing beside the executable is probed, so isolated test and agent runs behave as before.
2. Portable mode: marker beside the executable and a writable `LightCraftData`.
3. The platform folder, unchanged.

If the marker is there but the folder can't be written (read-only medium, Program Files), a warning is logged and the platform folder is used. The check creates the folder and writes a probe file, so it runs once per process (`OnceLock`).

Because the change is in the engine's `config_dir()`, the desktop app, `lightcraft-cli` and the MCP server all follow the same marker, as they share the folder today.

## Not in this PR

- The Windows portable zip does not ship a `portable.txt` (PhotoCraft's does). That changes where existing portable-zip users' settings live, so I left it as a packaging decision; happy to add it here if wanted.
- Unlike PhotoCraft, the fallback warning is only logged, not also printed to stderr.

## Testing

Windows 11, Rust 1.99.

- New tests in `config_tests`: each marker moves the folder beside the executable and wins over the platform folder, the write probe is removed, no marker creates nothing, and a `LightCraftData` that can't be created is refused with a reason. The existing override tests now also assert that an override never asks for the portable folder.
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-engine -p lightcraft -p lightcraft-cli`: all pass (engine 824, app 64, cli 21).
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-engine -p…

title: People view: faces cut from the embedded preview, not the raw (#1440)
author: bitshiftza
body:
Closes #1440

Tracker: **LRC-LIB-PEOPLE** (note updated).

Faces in the People view of **unedited raws** are now cut from the camera's largest embedded preview, read the planned way (header and JPEG only, never the sensor data), when that preview holds at least ¾ of the tile's pixels across the face. Edited photos, other files, and raws whose preview is too small, the wrong shape, unreadable or offline are developed as before, so every face keeps the photo's look.


- `crates/engine/src/face_tiles.rs`: `PreviewCut`, tried by `RenderJob::run` before the job's source; it declines on a too-small or differently shaped preview, an unreadable preview, a degenerate face box or an offline file, and the normal render runs. It is only used while the photo still has its import look, the same condition under which the grid already shows that preview as the thumbnail; the camera JPEG can't take raw edits the same way.
- **The ¾ threshold:** the square around the face is enlarged by at most 4⁄3, invisible at the 56–180 pt tile sizes, and the same bound the raw path already accepts when it bins an X-Trans sensor for a preview.
- **Tile sizes round up to 16 px steps,** so moving the thumbnail slider reuses tiles already in the memory and library thumbnail caches. (Face tiles were already written to the on-disk thumbnail cache; the issue's "not kept between launches" was most likely the cache's LRU cleanup on a large library, not a missing write.)
- **Sony α1 / Adobe RGB previews:** the planned preview read (#1020) fell back to reading the whole file when a preview declares Adobe RGB. It now carries the colour space and applies it as the whole-file path does, which also speeds up α1 grid thumbnails. #1020's test for that case is updated to match.

title: LR-IMP-PREVIEW-READ: a raw whose embedded preview can't be read still gets a thumbnail
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1448 (@simondelacourt confirmed it with the R6 files).

Since the grid treats an unedited raw's embedded JPEG as its final thumbnail, nothing is rendered behind it. Whether that JPEG can actually be read is only known when the quick job runs, though, and `Session::quick_thumb_job` had no fallback: when the preview loader returns nothing the job fails with "no quick preview", the renderer remembers the failure for that key, and the cell stays empty until an edit changes the key (which is why a small edit brings it back). The quick job now carries the real thumbnail job as its last resort, the same way `quick_view_job` already does for the loupe, so a raw whose preview can't be read gets rendered instead. Photos whose preview does load don't change: they still stop at the embedded JPEG.

I couldn't tell why the R6 CR3 previews fail to load in the first place without one of those files. This fixes the empty grid either way, but if there's a preview-reading bug for that camera it's still there. @simondelacourt, if you can try this branch and the thumbnails show, a log line or one sample CR3 would help pin down why the embedded preview isn't read.

Validation:
- `files::tests::a_quick_thumbnail_without_an_embedded_preview_renders_the_raw`: fails on main (the quick job returns no image, `quick: None`), passes here

### Cause

`Overlay::AllMasks` in `visualize::apply` painted each visible mask's plane with `mask_view` in turn. Every mask view rewrites the whole image from its alpha (White on Black writes `255·a`, Image on Black multiplies by `a`, Image on White blends to white, Color compounds its tint), so each plane overwrote or compounded the ones before it and only the last visible mask showed as intended.

### Change

The planes of the image's size are merged into one alpha (per-pixel max, the same union `MaskOp::Add` uses in `masks.rs`) and painted once. The GPU path (`crates/gpu/src/render.rs`) calls the same `apply`, so it is covered too. No masks, or only mismatched planes, leave the image untouched as before.

The test's hidden-mask check also expected the *plain* pixel under White on Black, where everything outside the masks is black by definition (the same test asserts `mid` is black and `mask_overlay_shows_the_evaluated_alpha` asserts `outside == [0, 0, 0, 255]`); it now asserts black. The regression checks (both masks painted, the hidden one not) are kept.

### Tests

`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-pipeline --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p lightcraft-pipeline visualize` (5 passed). The test fails on `main` without the `apply` change (left mask black, `visualize.rs:432`) and again at the hidden-mask check without the test correction.

title: LR-RAW-DNG: DNGs exported by earlier LightCraft versions render with the right colours again (follow-up to #1177)
author: radialmonster
body:
#1177 fixed the CFAPattern anchor for DNGs from other software (#1086, #1161). It also made LightCraft misread the DNGs that earlier LightCraft versions exported. The old writer stored the pattern at the sensor origin, and main now shifts it by the ActiveArea offset as if it came from the ActiveArea. Any old export with an odd offset renders with the wrong colour phase.

## Example
`export_LightCraft.dng` from the #1110 report, a Fujifilm X-T2 file exported by an earlier LightCraft release. Whole-image mean ratios at 640 px:

- 0.7.1: R/G 0.996, B/G 0.970
- main (b3d392b4): R/G 1.471, B/G 2.994 (purple)
- this PR: R/G 0.996, B/G 0.970

## Fix
- **Writer:** it now sets Software to `LightCraft DNG 2` for the spec-anchored files it has written since #1177.
- **Reader:** a bare `LightCraft` Software tag marks the older files, and those keep the sensor-origin reading. Every other DNG reads the pattern as #1177 does.

One edge case: DNGs exported by a build of main between #1177 and this PR also say `LightCraft`, so they would be read the old way. That window holds no release.

## Checks
- **Renders:** the #1086 60D DNG and the #1161 T3i DNG render byte-identical to main.
- **Tests:**
  - new test in `crates/raw/tests/dng.rs` covering a legacy-tagged file with an odd active area;
  - #1177's round-trip test still passes;
  - `cargo test -p lightcraft-raw`: all pass.
- **Regression:** I rendered 2,296 raws and DNGs from the test sets with main and with this change. Only the legacy export changed.

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: full-size raw demosaic on the white-balanced mosaic, with a clip mask (#1328, stacked on #1400)
author: AlexChambers
body:
Fixes #1328

Rebased onto main `0da998f2` after integration batch 40. This branch uses `LOOK_VERSION` 9 and `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 65. Main uses look 9 and render 64.

Stacked on #1400 (issue #709, lossless smart previews): merge #1400 first. This branch contains rebased #1400 plus five own commits. Before this rebase, #1400 was at `cf1c803a`. #1400 now includes the shared thumbnail-clear fix found in this PR's review, and that revision was rebased on main `b3d392b4` (batch 33, and #850's Compact quality 97 with its encode version), which this branch therefore includes too (#1340's `LOOK_VERSION` 5 among it). Its smart-preview part reuses #1400's invalidation instead of having its own.

## What was wrong

Every full-size raw development demosaiced the mosaic as the sensor recorded it. That covers exports (which decode at full size and resize afterwards), the 1:1 view, and the previews for which `files::bin_factor` returns `None` (Bayer sensors under about 4600 px on the long side, X-Trans under about 5760 px, so 16 MP X-Trans bodies such as the X-E1 too). `RawImage::develop` demosaics `normalized()`, and the as-shot white balance only comes in later, in `CameraColourModel::apply`.

AHD, PPG and the X-Trans directional method complete red and blue from neighbouring colour differences (C - G). A neutral surface has C = G only once it is white balanced. In camera RGB its R - G is (1 / wb_r - 1) G, about -0.6 G at a Sony body's daylight multipliers, so it changes with brightness. Across a steep edge the bright side's colour difference lands on a darker pixel and drives its red (less often its blue) to zero or below: green or cyan outlines, and yellow or magenta ones in mirrored geometries.

An earlier revision of this branch introduced a dark checkerboard line just inside strongly coloured clipped highlights (the rim of a setting sun, the edges of neon tubes). That is fixed here; see (b) below for the numbers and how.

title: Bump quick-xml to 0.41 (RUSTSEC-2026-0194, RUSTSEC-2026-0195)
author: natocool2
body:
Bumps quick-xml from 0.38 to 0.41, which fixes two advisories:

- [RUSTSEC-2026-0194](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0194.html): `Attributes` with the default `with_checks(true)` takes O(N²) time on a start tag with N attributes.
- [RUSTSEC-2026-0195](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0195.html): `NsReader` allocates for every `xmlns` declaration on a tag with no limit.

**Exposure today: none that I can find.** #687 already made `xmp_merge::scan` linear, and `xmp.rs`, `gpx.rs` and `lensdb/xml.rs` read attributes with `with_checks(false)`. Nothing uses `NsReader`. The bump clears `cargo audit`/`cargo deny` for anyone who ships LightCraft (including the web zip), and leaves one copy of quick-xml in the lockfile instead of two.

## Changes

- `Cargo.toml`: `quick-xml = "0.41"`. No source changes: lightcraft does not call any API that 0.39 to 0.41 removed or deprecated.

## How this was checked

- The quick-xml API used here was diffed between 0.38.4 and 0.41.0 (`Reader`/`Config` fields, `Event` variants, `BytesStart`/`BytesText`/`BytesRef`, `escape`): the only changes that touch this workspace are the deprecations above. `Attribute::normalized_value*` is exactly what the deprecated methods call in 0.41, so behaviour is the same as a plain bump. One difference from 0.38 that comes with the bump itself: attribute values now get XML 1.0 normalisation (a literal tab/CR/LF inside an attribute value becomes a space; `
` is kept), as the spec requires.
- `Cargo.lock` was updated with `cargo update --workspace` only: quick-xml 0.38.4 is removed and every dependent now points at the 0.41.0 already locked for `wayland-scanner`. No other package moves.
- `rustfmt --check` passes on the changed files. I did **not** build or run `cargo xtask ci` locally; CI here is the first compile, so please treat its result as the check.

title: KEY-SLIDER-NUDGE: scrolling sideways over a slider adjusts it
author: PiMinusMax
body:
## Problem
Scrolling sideways already pans the photo, but over a Develop slider it does nothing. On a Mac trackpad a sideways swipe is the most natural way to move a slider a little; on Windows and Linux the same works with a tilting wheel or Shift+wheel (egui already turns Shift+wheel into sideways scrolling).

## Change
- Scrolling sideways over a slider nudges it by the same steps as the arrow keys and the wheel on a selected slider (one wheel notch = one step, small trackpad movements add up). Right raises the value, like dragging the thumb right.
- The slider doesn't have to be selected first: the right panel only scrolls vertically, so sideways scrolling isn't used for anything else there.
- Only a mostly sideways movement counts (|dx| > |dy|), so a slightly diagonal swipe that scrolls the panel leaves the sliders it passes alone. While a sideways scroll adjusts a slider, its small vertical part doesn't scroll the panel, so the slider stays under the pointer.
- Each nudge is one undo step, like the existing wheel / arrow-key nudges.
- Vertical wheel nudges on a selected slider are unchanged.

## Tests
- `sideways_scrolling_adjusts_the_slider_under_the_pointer` (`crates/ui-egui/src/tests_masking.rs`): swipe right raises Exposure, left lowers it, Shift+wheel raises it, and a mostly vertical swipe changes nothing (no undo step). Fails without the change.
- Existing wheel / numeric-entry slider tests still pass.
- `docs/parity-checklist.md`: KEY-SLIDER-NUDGE row and revision history.

Tested with synthetic scroll events in the headless app; not yet on a real trackpad or tilting wheel. The direction of a tilting wheel depends on what the OS reports.

title: LR-RAW-NEF: Coolpix P7000 NRW files decode without stripes and with their white balance
author: radialmonster
body:
## What was wrong
- Coolpix P7000 NRW files rendered with vertical stripes. The 12-bit samples are packed in 32-bit words; the packing was
  chosen from the bytes per row of the padded strip, not from the row itself, so the P7000 (rows padded to a different
  size than the data) used the wrong packing.
- P6000, P7000 and P7100 maker notes have no white balance tag (0x000c), so the render used gains of 1,1,1 and looked
  dim and nearly monochrome.

## Changes
- The word packing is decided from the row's own size (`(row_samples * 12)` bytes rounded up, a multiple of 4 or not).
- When 0x000c is missing, the white balance is read from the NRW data block (maker note tag 0x0014): a table at byte
  0x34 with entries of five u32 (kelvin, R, G, G, B, in 1/256 units). The first entry is taken as the as-shot white balance.
  It is only used when the table's fourth entry repeats the first entry's kelvin, which holds on the P7000 (5236 K).
- Tests: a padded-strip packing test and a white balance test, including a P7100-style table that must give none.

## Is the first table entry the as-shot white balance?
Checked on files that carry both 0x000c and the table (P950 x2, B700, P1000, P1100):
the first entry equals 0x000c in all of them (R and B identical, for example B700 1.4258 / 1.8086, P1100 1.7969 / 1.8125).
So entry 0 is the as-shot entry on those bodies (block version 0104).

On the P7000 (block 0101) entry 0 is 5236 K, R 430, B 567, and the fourth entry repeats 5236 K with zero gains, which fits
the same layout.
On the P7100 (block 0102) entry 0 is 3000 K, R 278, B 868, identical to the fifth entry (the 3000 K preset), and the fourth
entry holds 3195 K with zero gains. That looks like the as-shot kelvin is in the fourth entry with no gains, and entry 0 is
a preset. I cannot prove the P7100 as-shot gains from this, so the P7100 gets no white balance from the block (unchanged
from main). An earlier version of this change did use entry 0 for the P7100; that is removed.

title: Issue #1449: Search Photos finds named people, and quotes keep a name together (steps 1 and 2)
author: ArekatlaNishanthchowdary
body:
Part of #1449: steps 1 and 2 of its proposal. Steps 3–6 (People picker in the filter bar, multi-person Any/All, chips, presets) are not in this PR, so the issue should stay open.

## What changes

In `crates/catalog/src/query.rs`:

1. **People in free text.** An unfielded token now also matches `Photo::people()`, next to file name, title, caption, camera, lens, location, format and keywords. Pets and unnamed faces stay out, through `people()`'s own rules. This is the same field set as the smart-rule "Any Searchable Text".
2. **Quote-aware tokens.** `Filter::matches` splits the text with `search_tokens()` instead of `split_whitespace()`: whitespace separates tokens except inside double quotes. So `person:"Jane Doe"` and `who:"Jane Doe"` match the exact name, `"jane doe"` is one phrase, and the other fields take quoted values too (`keyword:"new york"`, `camera:"canon eos"`).

Every unquoted form matches as before: `person:Sam` still works, and `person:Jane Doe` is still `person:Jane` plus `Doe`.

## Malformed input

- An unclosed quote runs to the end of the text, so it can only narrow the match.
- A token that starts with a quote is free text even with a colon in it.
- A lone `"` or `""` is an empty phrase and filters nothing, like an empty search; `person:""` and `person:` match nothing.
- There are no escapes: a backslash is an ordinary character.
- The tokenizer is one pass over the text with no allocation, and splits only at `char_indices` boundaries.

## Testing

Windows 11, Rust 1.99.

- New `search_text_finds_people_and_quoted_values` in `crates/catalog/src/tests.rs`: free text by part of a name in any case, a non-ASCII name, a pet, AND of words against a quoted phrase, quoted `person:` / `who:` / `keyword:`, tokens after a quoted one, unclosed and empty quotes, a quoted colon, a backslash, a 100,000-character unclosed value, and Unicode whitespace.

title: LR-IMP-PROFILES: Presets apply the imported profile they name (#1001)
author: cookingwithsimon
body:
Before: a Lightroom preset that gets its look from a profile (`crs:Look`) imported with only its sliders, so packs whose sliders sit at zero (like the one in #1001) brought across little more than grain. Import just listed "Look" as not carried over.

After: the preset remembers the profile it names. If you've imported a profile with that name (File ▸ Import Profiles & Presets, a `.cube` today), applying the preset selects it at the preset's amount. It works whether the profile comes in before or after the preset. Lightroom's six basic profiles (Adobe Color, Neutral, Vivid, Landscape, Portrait, Monochrome) map to LightCraft's own. The import names any profile it can't use, per preset: `Profile “X” (not imported yet)` or `Profile “Artistic 01” (Lightroom's own)`.

How: `preset_import::build` keeps `crs:Look` (Name, Group, UUID, Amount; also the `Look` table in `.lrtemplate`s) as `profile.look` in the preset's partial settings. Settings deserialization ignores that key, so a preset that can't resolve leaves the photo's profile alone. The new `crates/engine/src/profile_refs.rs` resolves it to an imported profile by name, ignoring case and repeated spaces, with the group breaking ties. It does this in `preset.import`, and again after `profile.import` / `profile.deleteImported` (touching only the presets that change, so `presets.json` isn't rewritten for nothing). Docs: `docs/xmp-interop.md`, LR-IMP-PROFILES row.

Not in this PR: reading the colour tables inside `.xmp` creative profiles (`crs:RGBTable`, the format the #1001 profile and most commercial packs use). Profiles still come in as `.cube`. The UUID is kept so `.xmp` profiles can match by it once they can be imported.

title: LR-MERGE-PANO: a panorama or HDR merge of raws keeps the as-shot white balance of its frames
author: eliets2
body:
## What this changes

A panorama or HDR merge of raw files now keeps the as-shot white balance of its frames, chosen robustly instead of being whatever the first frame had.

- `Frame` carries the vendor as-shot multipliers (`wb_multipliers`, green = 1) from the decoded raw.
- The output's white balance is the median R/G and B/G over the frames that vote (all three multipliers finite and above zero; the mean of the middle two for an even count; frames without usable multipliers don't vote, and if nobody votes nothing changes). It is written as `AsShotNeutral`, the reciprocal of the multipliers, and the source's `AsShotWhiteXY` is cleared (a reader takes the xy first and the DNG spec makes the two exclusive, so a stale xy would hide the new neutral).
- Panorama: the median over the frames actually used. HDR merge: the median over its inputs; the HDR result carries the multipliers so merged brackets can vote in an HDR panorama.
- Docs: `docs/camera-preview-colour.md` and the parity checklist rows for the panorama and HDR merges.

Two commits: the panorama, then the HDR merge. The large `frame.rs` diff is mostly a move: the decoded-raw-to-`Frame` step of `load_frame_with` is split into a private `raw_frame` so it can be tested without a file (check with `git diff --color-moved`).

## Relation to #1144

I am not claiming this fixes #1144. On `main`, #965 (`090553d1`) already passes a colour hook in `MergeJob::load` that gives a CR2 an `AsShotNeutral` in the app and the CLI, taken from the first frame, so the cast reported on 0.5.0 probably no longer reproduces there. title: LR-RAW-NEF: stretch non-square pixels (Nikon D1X/D1H) to square
author: radialmonster
body:
The Nikon D1X (and D1H) raw is 4028x1324, and its raw SubIFD says XResolution 600 / YResolution 300, so each pixel is twice as tall as it is wide. Nothing read that, so the picture came out squashed to about 3:1. With the rows doubled it is a normal 3:2 frame.

## Fix
- `RawImage`/`RawInfo` get a `pixel_aspect` (pixel height / width, 1.0 for square).
- **NEF:** read from the raw IFD X/Y resolution ratio. **DNG:** read from DefaultScale (vertical / horizontal).
- Only ratios from 1.5 to 4 are accepted, rounded, so files with equal or slightly odd resolution tags are untouched.
- After demosaic and crop the rows are resampled to square pixels. `developed_size()` reports the stretched size, so the catalog photo size and lens-profile sizing match the render.
- The binned fast-preview decode is off for non-square pixels and falls back to the full develop.

## Example
D1X sample `1786` (uncompressed NEF):
- main (b3d392b4): 4024x1324 (3.04:1)
- this PR: 4024x2648 (3:2)

The compressed D1X sample (`1785`) is not decoded on main either and still falls back to its embedded preview.

## Checks
- **Survey:** across 2,296 raws and DNGs from the test sets, only three raw IFDs have unequal X/Y resolution: the two D1X files and a KanDao QooCam 8K DNG, whose DefaultScale is 1 1 and which is unaffected. No sample has a DefaultScale other than 1 1.
- **Tests:** new unit tests for the stretched height, a develop with aspect 2, and DefaultScale parsing. `cargo test` (raw, engine) passes and clippy is clean.
- **Regression:** I rendered the 2,296 files at 160 px with main and with this change. Only D1X `1786` changed.

Not in this change: the D1X still skips the camera-look fit, which would need a binned proxy with the same aspect.

title: LRC-LIB-CATALOG-IMPORT: an ARW6 is described from the whole file, not a partial read
author: dev-null-undefined
body:
## The problem

`crates/raw/tests/sparse_corpus.rs` fails on `main` (b3d392b4) as soon as the ILCE-7RM6 ARW6 corpus files are present:

```
arw6-sony-ilce7rm6-apsc-land-c.arw: differs from the whole file (skipped bytes 0)
  left: "Err(Unsupported(\"ARW6 first-half row count outside 2..=7\")) …
 right: "Ok(RawInfo { format: Arw, width: 6592, height: 4372, … })
```

`sparse::header_plan` skips a TIFF raw's strip except its first 64 KB, then says `Ready`. But the ARW6 header probe (`arw6::decode` in `Mode::Header`) validates every tile: its picture header, its stream tables and the first lines of its residual stream (`first_half_shift`). Those bytes lie in the skipped part of the strip. Probing the partly read buffer therefore fails where the whole file succeeds. The test names `apsc-land-c` only because it is the first ARW6 file it reads, and it stops at the first failure.

## Change

The fix is in `crates/raw/src/sparse.rs`. For NEF, ORF and PEF, whose header probes read samples, the plan already answers `HeaderPlan::Whole`. An ARW6 (compression 32766) now gets the same answer from the **header plan**.

The **preview plan** is unchanged: `embedded_preview` reads no tile. The 13 ARW previews in the corpus are still read from 20.7 % of their bytes. The app's partial reads (`planned_preview` in `crates/engine/src/files.rs`) use only the preview plan, so nothing changes for users; this restores the header plan's contract ("probing the loaded buffer gives what probing the whole file gives").

A new test, `sparse::tests::arw6_is_described_from_the_whole_file`, builds a synthetic two-tile ARW6 whose second tile lies past a first one of bulk size. It got `Ready` before this change and gets `Whole` now. CI doesn't have the ARW6 corpus files, so this is the check that runs there.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p lightcraft-raw --release` with the ARW6 corpus present: all pass, `sparse_corpus` included. All 8 ILCE-7RM6 ARW6 files are now read whole by the header plan; their p…

title: Raw source: no second copy of a full-size picture after the colour model
author: PiMinusMax
body:
A raw decoded at full size (an export) was copied once more after the colour model. The raw path in `crates/engine/src/files.rs` fitted the picture to `max_edge` unconditionally. When `max_edge` is not smaller than the picture, `fit` → `resize` returns `img.clone()`, so it made a second float RGB buffer of the whole picture (12 bytes per pixel). The JPEG and preview paths in the same file already call `fit` only when the picture is larger. This does the same for the raw path, which also covers the denoised twin.

**Measured** with `lightcraft-cli render` (CPU), `LIGHTCRAFT_PROFILE=1`, 3 runs each, on main b3d392b4 with and without the change:

| | `fit` stage before | after | copied buffer |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sony, 6000 × 4000 (24 MP) | 158–172 ms | 0 ms | 288 MB |
| Sony, 7008 × 4672 (33 MP) | 221–227 ms | 0 ms | 393 MB |

Peak memory (max RSS) is the same within noise (1.17–1.19 GB): the closure owns the input, so the old buffer was dropped right after the copy, and the peak comes later in the pipeline. The gain is the copy's time and a short-lived allocation of that size.

No new test: the output is identical (the clone returned the same pixels), and the existing raw-loading tests cover the path.

`cargo xtask ci` steps run locally: fmt, clippy, layers, assets, parity and wasm pass; 3204 tests pass, 1 fails: `visualize::tests::all_masks_overlay_shows_every_visible_mask_at_once` in `crates/pipeline`, which this change does not touch. It fails the same way on main b3d392b4, in the FreeBSD job of [run 38355981120](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/actions/runs/38355981120). Clippy ran with `-A clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks`: rust 1.99 flags upstream code in `crates/pipeline/src/spots.rs` on main as well.

title: LR-VIEW-ZOOM: drag-scale follow-ups from #1009 review; slow verdicts expire (#330)
author: mattsivak
body:
Follow-up to #1009 (merged). Brought up to date with `main`; the diff is now only this PR's changes, in `crates/ui-egui/src/region.rs`, `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/detail.rs` and the LR-VIEW-ZOOM row of `docs/parity-checklist.md`.

## `a2911a50`: review points
It takes the three minor points from @FredApps' review of #1009, kept out of that approved PR. All three are in `crates/ui-egui/src/region.rs`.

- **The slow-drag set forgets one drag, not all of them.** Once 256 (photo, control) pairs are remembered, adding one more forgets only the one remembered longest ago. Before, the whole set was cleared, which brought back one slow full-size drag per pair. A drag that's remembered as slow drafts small and is never timed again, so the oldest entry is also the least recently confirmed.
- **The doc says a slow drag is per photo.** `DragScale`'s doc comment now says a slow drag is remembered for its photo only: the same control on another photo starts at full size and is timed again.
- **Implausible frame times count as unknown, not clamped.** The review suggested clamping each sample at 10× the budget. The median here is an order statistic: it picks one sample and doesn't average. A sample clamped to 160 ms is still over both thresholds (16 ms when the drag ends, 32 ms to give up mid-drag), so the clamp wouldn't change any decision. Instead, a host frame time over 1 s (a hidden, occluded or stalled window, not a texture upload) is treated like a missing frame time, the same as NaN or negative values already are. The draft's render time still counts.

## `8d91abe6`: a slow verdict needs two strikes and expires
Before, one drag over the 16 ms budget made that slider draft small on that photo for the rest of the session, even when the machine was only busy for a moment (another app, a backup). Timing stays in wall-clock time, because that is what the user waits for. Measuring CPU or GPU time instead was considered and rejected:
- CPU time doesn't see contention from other app…

title: LR-EDIT-DETAIL-NR: noise reduction works in the original's pixels, so previews match the full-size render scaled down (fixes #960)
author: atmikshetty
body:
Fixes #960

Grid thumbnails and the filmstrip looked much more denoised than the loupe. Noise reduction now works in the original photo's pixels, so a preview at any size looks like the full-size render scaled down.

**Why it happened** (`crates/pipeline/src/local.rs`, `nr_params`)

- The radii were sized from the output's scale relative to the buffer the render was given, not the original. A 256-px cell drawn from the 512-px thumbnail level used half the full-size radius on pixels that each average ~23 sensor pixels, and below 0.4× (0.35× for colour) the radius stopped shrinking at all.
- The guided filter's eps (the variance it treats as noise) stayed at its full-size value, although downscaling divides the noise variance by 1/scale². Texture in small previews was flattened as noise.

**What changes**

- `SourceInfo::native_long`: the original's long edge. The engine fills it from the catalog's photo size (kept when the decoder supplies its own facts), and it is carried to the web workers (`wire.rs`). `Plan::detail_scale` = output pixels per original pixel, from `px_per_long`, so a crop no longer changes it.
- `nr_params(s, scale)`: radii × scale with no floor, eps × scale². Below 1 px the smallest blur the box Gaussian makes is blended in by the ratio of variances (`blur::box_sigma`); a fade under 1% skips the filter.
- At scale 1 the parameters are unchanged: 1:1 views and full-size exports render exactly as before. The GPU takes the same parameters.
- `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 62 → 63, so cached thumbnails are redrawn.
- Docs: LR-EDIT-DETAIL-NR / -CNR rows in `parity-checklist.md`, a "Noise reduction looks the same at every size" entry in `whats-new.md`.

**Measured** (1536×1024 noisy synthetic scene, `tests_nr_scale.rs`): error of the preview against the full-size render scaled down, as a fraction of leaving NR off, luminance NR 50:

| preview scale | 0.5 | 0.33 | 0.25 | 0.167 | 0.1 | 0.05 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

title: Add coverage tests for the AllMasks union fix (#1457)
author: csy2006
body:
Update: this PR now also covers all five `MaskView`s, the feathered-overlap union, order-independence, opacity applied once, and the empty/missing-plane cases (matching #1599). Fixes #1457.

The Overlay::AllMasks branch of visualize::apply drew each visible mask separately via mask_view, which repaints the whole image on every call. For the white-on-black / image-on-black views mask_view fills uncovered pixels with black, so a later mask overwrote the region of an earlier one where its own alpha was 0 - leaving only the last mask visible.

Merge all visible masks' alpha into a single plane (per-pixel union via max) and draw it once. This fixes both the CPU and GPU renderers, since both route through visualize::apply.

Fixes #1457

title: LR-EDIT-EFFECTS-DEHAZE: raster::morph square min / max filters (split from #1286)
author: mattsivak
body:
Split out of #1286, as @FredApps suggested in that review, so the filter can be reviewed and land on its own. Dehaze V3's haze map uses it, but nothing on `main` does yet. #1286 will drop these two files once it is rebased onto #1283 and this PR.

## What it adds
- **`raster::morph::min_filter` / `max_filter`:** square erosion / dilation of radius `r`, using separable van Herk / Gil-Werman passes. Each line is split into blocks of the window's width, with a running prefix and suffix extreme per block. That costs three comparisons per pixel per pass, whatever the radius.
  - Edges are clamped, which for a min or max is the same as clipping the window to the image.
  - NaNs are skipped like `f32::min` does.
  - The radius is capped at the line length, so scratch space stays bounded.
  - Rows run in parallel with one scratch buffer per worker.
- **`Image::transpose`:** row-parallel, used for the column pass. A buffer shorter than its size reads as `T::default()` where it runs out, so it never panics.

## Tests
- `morph`:
  - matches a naive window filter across sizes from 1×1 to 64×40 and radii from 1 to 100;
  - radius 0 and empty planes return copies;
  - a radius past the image gives the global extreme, including `usize::MAX`;
  - a dark dot grows to the window;
  - NaNs are skipped;
  - a short buffer comes back unchanged.
- `transpose_swaps_the_axes` (new): the axes swap, it round-trips, and a short buffer doesn't panic.

`cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, heif, parity, layers, assets and wasm pass. `cargo test --workspace` has two failures, neither in `crates/raster`:
- `visualize::tests::all_masks_overlay_shows_every_visible_mask_at_once` fails the same way on `main` (reported in the #995 review).
- `gpu::backend::tests::init_marker_is_written_during_creation_and_removed_after` failed once in the full parallel run. It passes when run alone, both on `main` and on this branch.

title: Never crash: Fix overflow in mask.move with a huge delta
author: endthestart
body:
mask.move adds the agent's `delta` to the mask index as an i64, so a delta near i64::MAX overflows. That panics in debug and test builds and wraps in release. I switched it to a saturating add so any delta just moves the mask to the bottom or the top, same as `to` already does.

I added a test with i64::MAX and i64::MIN for both `delta` and `to`, it panicked before the change.

title: Never crash: Fix i32 overflow in the NEF and PEF Huffman predictors (#1515)
author: endthestart
body:
Fixes #1515.

The NEF and PEF Huffman decoders add each difference to the row and column predictors with a plain `+=`, so a corrupt strip with a long run of large differences can push a predictor past i32::MAX. In debug and test builds that panics. Both decoders use `checked_add` now and return a corrupt data error instead. Valid files never get anywhere near the limit so they decode the same.

I added a test in each decoder that feeds a run of the largest difference along a row and then down two columns. Both panicked before the change.

title: LRC-LIB-CATALOG-IMPORT: Open catalogs whose tables are all still in the WAL
author: endthestart
body:
I found this while fuzzing the catalog reader with a handful of test catalogs made with Python's sqlite3. The one in WAL mode with nothing checkpointed yet (like a new catalog Lightroom still has open) failed with "unsupported SQLite schema format", even though SQLite opens it fine. The main file has schema format 0 in that case since there's no schema yet, and we refused anything outside 1 to 4 before overlaying the WAL.

It now accepts 0 as an empty schema and checks page 1 again after the WAL frames are applied, so a file that really has no tables still fails with the missing table named. I added a unit test with a format 0 header and checked that format 5 is still refused.

title: xtask parity: Fail when docs/gaps.md lists a gap more than once
author: endthestart
body:
Gaps 10, 22 and 23 each had two rows in the ranked table in docs/gaps.md. It looks like two branches edited the same entry and the merges kept both copies. I removed the older copies and made `cargo xtask parity` fail when a gap number shows up twice, the same way it already does for repeated tracker ids.

Heads up that batch 34 (#1441) has five copies of gap 10 right now, so it'll need the same cleanup if this goes in first.

title: Fix range-mask handle drags and color sampling settings
author: nevicia2010-hub
body:
## Problem and fix

Two range-mask interactions can change or sample a different range than the user intended:

- With Luminance Range at 20–80%, dragging the low handle past the high handle changes the high endpoint to 100%. The widget chooses the nearest handle every frame. Capture the endpoint at the original press position and keep it through the drag, clamping against the stationary endpoint and preserving one-step undo.
- Color Range sampling uses settings before section-eye toggles and the HDR/SDR rendition are resolved. After setting Exposure to +3 and switching Light off, the photo uses the default exposure but the picker still samples +3 EV. Disabled Color/white balance and HDR SDR Brightness have the same mismatch. Resolve the settings as the render does and read exposure from the resulting plan.

No selection formula, stored edit format, or new control is introduced. Update the two existing parity-checklist rows without changing their status.

## Regression evidence

All three added tests failed against the original implementation, then passed with the fixes:
- Real headless UI drags: both endpoints, crossing the opposite endpoint, a fast movement and one-step undo.
- Color sampling with Light/Color disabled; the sampled patch is selected in the actual mask overlay.
- SDR preview sampling of an HDR edit, with a separate HDR request confirming that the SDR offset is not applied there.

On macOS / Apple M3 Pro:
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy and HEIF checks pass. The workspace test stage stops at the unchanged `visualize::tests::all_masks_overlay_shows_every_visible_mask_at_once` failure tracked by #1457 / #1456 / #1494. **Unfiltered CI is not green.**
- `cargo test --workspace -- --skip visualize::tests::all_masks_overlay_shows_every_visible_mask_at_once`: **3206 passed, 29 ignored, 1 filtered**, no failures.

- `cargo xtask parity`, `layers`, `assets`, and `wasm`: pass (28 WASM packages). Parity reports an already-stale generated summary; feature counts…

title: Never crash: Fix demosaic panic on a NaN black level
author: endthestart
body:
A DNG can store BlackLevel as FLOAT or DOUBLE, and a NaN or infinite value there made every normalized sample non-finite. AHD then calls clamp with NaN bounds, which panics, and since AHD runs for 1:1 and exports that took the app down.

The DNG reader now reads a non-finite black level or delta as 0, and RawImage::normalized maps any non-finite result to black so nothing after it ever sees a NaN. This is separate from #1139, which handled NaN float samples. I added a test with FLOAT NaN, DOUBLE inf and partly NaN black levels, plus a float DNG with NaN samples. It panicked before and develops to finite values now.

title: LR-EXP-QUALITY: Use optimized Huffman tables for JPEG exports (#1373)
author: endthestart
body:
Fixes #1373.

Our JPEG encoder always used the example Huffman tables from the spec. It now does a first pass to count each image's symbols, builds optimal length-limited tables from them, and codes with those. The quantized coefficients don't change so the decoded pixels are identical, the files are just smaller. On a 24 MP test image it came out about 12-14% smaller at quality 80 to 100, at roughly the same speed.

The tests check the tables are valid (complete, at most 16 bits, no all-ones code) and that the new files decode to exactly the same pixels as before with both jpeg-decoder and zune-jpeg.

title: Never crash: Refuse raw data with two samples per pixel (#1511)
author: endthestart
body:
Fixes #1511.

A DNG with SamplesPerPixel set to 2 got through both the DNG reader and RawImage::check, and then the demosaic read `c[2]` past each pixel and panicked, in release builds too. Both now refuse 2 samples per pixel with an unsupported error, and I made the demosaic use `get` so a two-sample buffer can't index out of range even if it gets there some other way.

The new test builds a two-channel LinearRaw DNG and checks it's refused while 1, 3 and 4 sample DNGs still develop. It fails on main.

title: Never crash: Fix export size panic for very long strips
author: endthestart
body:
Resize::scale clamps between 1/short and 65535/long. For a photo more than 65535 times as long as it is short (a 70000 x 1 strip, which is a valid PNG or TIFF) the lower bound ends up above the upper one and clamp panics, both on export and in the watermark preview in the Export dialog.

I apply the two bounds one after the other now, with the encoder limit last, so the strip exports at 65535 x 1. Nothing changes for normal photos. The test runs every resize mode on a few of these extreme sizes, all of them panicked before.

title: Never crash: Cap enlarged exports at 512 MP and check memory first
author: endthestart
body:
With Don't Enlarge off you can type 20000 for a 2000 px photo, or percent 10000, and the export asks for a render around 65535 x 43690. The first float plane alone is 34 GB, the allocation fails, and that aborts the whole app instead of just failing the export.

Enlargements now stop at 512 MP (I believe that's Lightroom's limit too), and an enlarged export whose working memory is more than the computer's RAM is refused up front with a message saying how much it needs. Full size and smaller exports are never refused. I tried it with lightcraft-cli under an 8 GB limit, before it aborted and now it returns the error, and percent 400 still exports fine.

This touches the same function as #1542 but doesn't depend on it.

title: Never crash: Fix overflow on a BigTIFF IFD with a huge entry count (#1516)
author: endthestart
body:
Fixes #1516.

When a BigTIFF IFD says it has a huge number of entries we only read the ones that fit, but the next IFD position was still computed from the advertised count, so `table + n * entry_size` overflowed. It now only reads the next IFD offset when the whole table was read, using checked math. Complete and truncated tables behave the same as before.

The test builds a short BigTIFF with counts of u64::MAX, 2^62 and 2 and one readable entry, in both byte orders. It panicked at reader.rs:143 before.

title: LR-RAW-DNG: preserve lens corrections in the existing DNG tone-fit proxy
author: radialmonster
body:
A DNG whose camera preview includes lens corrections must use the same corrected sensor image while fitting its starting tone. This extends the existing central DNG fitter added by #1316.

The loader temporarily restores the original lens opcodes for that fit, then removes them from the editable source so the rendering pipeline applies them once. The proxy uses the existing full-resolution opcode implementation when mosaic binning is unavailable. Eligibility, preview selection and acceptance gates remain those of main. Existing fitted DNG smart previews are included in stale-look refresh without changing their white-balance scale.

`LOOK_VERSION` 10 and `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 65 are each one beyond current main. A later sequential rendering change must advance them again.

The earlier 405/405 identical-output and 231-equal-measurement statements are withdrawn: that comparison executable was not an exact build of the published source. Independent clean affected-crate builds of main and published #1545 now provide this corrected comparison:

- 424 available files rendered at 1440 px on each exact-source build: 419 successes and the same five decoder failures. Fresh main matches the previous main outputs byte for byte on all 419 successes.
- Published #1545 changes six successful outputs; the other 413 are byte-identical to main.
- All six changed cases pass registration using the same main-derived geometry. Median registered camera-JPEG ΔE76: Leica Q 6.05 → 6.15; SL 11.21 → 5.48; CL 2.27 → 2.27; Q2 3.10 → 3.00; SL2 6.24 → 6.44; iPhone 15 Pro Max issue #548 9.99 → 5.33. The Q and SL2 are small regressions in this metric, although mean signed lightness improves from 1.03 to 0.21 and 0.78 to −0.03 respectively. These measure agreement with the camera preview, not calibrated colour accuracy.
- The five common failures are two invalid lossless-JPEG Huffman files and three unsupported sequential-JPEG DNGs. This PR does not add those decoders.

title: Never crash: Cap the spot radius so huge spot sizes render (#1519)
author: endthestart
body:
Fixes #1519.

The spot radius is the spot size times pixels per long edge. Commands clamp the size to the slider range but sidecars don't, so a huge or infinite size gave an infinite radius, and the heal blur and the auto source offset went with it. On the demo photo it panicked in sample_bilinear.

I added a small helper that caps the size at two long edges, which covers the whole frame from anywhere, and used it in the three places that turn a size into pixels. Real spots are way under that so they render the same. The test adds heal, remove and clone spots with sizes of 10, 1e30, f64::MAX, infinity and NaN. The blur sigma side of it is also handled in #1561.

title: LR-IMP-LOCAL: Forget untouched records of deleted files when browsing a folder again (#1392)
author: endthestart
body:
Fixes #1392.

A Local folder kept every record it had ever seen, so if another app deleted or moved files after you browsed the folder they stayed there, failed to load and logged "file not found" on every visit. Synchronize Folder only helps for library folders, not Local.

Browsing the folder again now forgets the records whose files are gone, but only when nothing was done to them (the same check library.forgetLocal uses), the session isn't holding them and they don't have a smart preview. Rated, flagged or edited photos stay and show as missing. I added a test that deletes an untouched, a rated and a library photo, browses again and reopens the library.

title: LR-BEHAV-GPU: Turn GPU rendering off after the GPU is lost while running (#1337)
author: endthestart
body:
This is for #1337. On Windows with NVIDIA the driver reset the GPU during a 42 MP export. Rendering fell back to the CPU, but egui-wgpu panicked on the lost device and we reported it as "could not open its window", even though the window had been open the whole time. Restarting just led to the same crash on the next export.

I can't stop the panic inside egui-wgpu, so this handles what comes after. A failure after the window is up is now reported as LightCraft stopping unexpectedly, and if the GPU pipeline had lost its device it leaves a marker so the next start turns GPU rendering off and explains why once, like the crash sentinel from #136 does. I added a test for the marker and the dialog text.

title: LR-MERGE-PANO: Keep panoramas at full resolution when memory allows (#1455)
author: endthestart
body:
Fixes #1455.

Panoramas were capped at 40 MP by default, so five 51 MP frames came out at 9422 x 4248. They now keep the photos' resolution up to 512 MP and 65000 px on the long edge unless you ask for less, but limited to what fits in memory since a full size stitch can need a lot. I measured peak memory on some synthetic stitches to pick the numbers, and the merge now frees each photo's pixels as soon as it's projected, which lowers the peak for every stitch.

The result reports the megapixels and why it was limited, and the app's message says when a panorama came out smaller. `memory::total_ram` becomes pub(crate) here, the same one line change as #1543, so the two merge in either order.

title: Never crash: Fix panic dragging a tone curve point between close neighbours
author: endthestart
body:
The point curve editor keeps a dragged point 0.01 away from each neighbour with `x.clamp(prev + 0.01, next - 0.01)`. If the neighbours are less than 0.02 apart those bounds cross and clamp panics mid-drag. Two clicks close together can do it, and so can develop.curve, a sidecar or a preset. A sidecar point of NaN did it too.

Now the point just stays midway when there's no room, the editor works on the sorted finite points, develop.curve stores points sorted, and a NaN or infinite point makes a sidecar curve unreadable like any other bad point. The tests cover dragging between points 0.015 apart (panicked before), unsorted points from an agent, and sidecar curves with NaN and inf.

title: LR-CLOUD-SMARTPREVIEW: build smart previews several at a time (#1492, stacked on #1400)
author: mattsivak
body:
Closes #1492.

**Stacked on #1400** (lossless smart previews), because both change the same `smart_run` loop. Only the last 5 commits are this PR (`git log 3eada64e..HEAD`; rebased onto #1400's current head on 2026-10-16). I'll rebase again once #1400 merges.

## What changes

Build Smart Previews used to build one photo at a time, holding the global `SMART_WRITE` lock across each photo's whole decode, encode and write. Now:

- **Per-proxy locks.** `PROXY_LOCKS` replaces `SMART_WRITE` and is keyed by the proxy's file name. A sharded proxy and its pre-upgrade flat copy share a name, and so do copies of one photo (content hash). Build Smart Previews and the opening look refresh still never write the same file at once.
- **Lanes.** `smart_run` runs the jobs on `export_parallelism` lanes (cores/4, at most 4), the same count Build Previews and export batches use. The opening look refresh keeps 1 lane so it doesn't compete with the first renders.
- **#1400's guarantees are kept:**
  - The thumbnail marker (`Pending`) is shared behind a mutex and recorded before the first change.
  - A refused marker is now *sticky*, so another lane's retry can't write while the run reports the failure.
  - The marker is cleared once, after all lanes finish.
  - A missing custom folder is never recreated. Lanes racing to create the same new shard folder is fine.
  - Cancel is checked before each job, progress is counted per photo, and failures are listed in job order.
- **Panics.** A panic in one photo's decode or encode fails that photo alone. A stale proxy whose original panics is kept and counted like an offline one.

## Measured

Apple M4 Max, 16 cores (4 lanes). 24 different CC0 raws (ARW, CR2, CR3, NEF, RAF, RW2, DNG). Best of 3 runs, import excluded.

| Format | Before (serial) | After (4 lanes) | Speedup | Peak RSS before → after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Compact | 5.84 s | 2.57 s | 2.27× | ~1.0 → ~2.0 GB |
| Lossless | 8.34 s | 3.07 s | 2.72× | ~1.1 → ~1.5–1.9 GB |

title: LR-BEHAV-EDIT-PANEL-LOOK: readable Edit panel (cards, edited marks, pinned section header)
author: mattsivak
body:
The Edit panel was hard to scan: labels and values were all equally bright, and a sub-panel's sliders (Curve's Highlights / Lights / Darks / Shadows) sat loose under its header, so they read as part of Light, which has its own Highlights / Shadows.

## What changes
- **Brightness levels.** Slider labels and values are dim at rest. A **changed value is bright**, and so is the slider under the pointer. "Changed" is measured against the photo's starting settings (`Photo::import_defaults`), so a raw's default sharpening and colour noise reduction, a user import preset, and As Shot white balance don't light up.
- **Cards.** Curve, SDR Rendition, Color / B&W Mixer, Point Color, Color Grading and Defringe are each one inset, rounded box that holds the header *and* its controls (`widgets::card`). Rows inside use the card's own inset (`widgets::content_pad`).
- **Edited dots.** A section header or card shows a dot when it holds edits, open or folded (`DevelopSettings::panel_differs` / `section_differs`; widget ids `sectionEdited:<id>`, `flyoutEdited:<id>`).
- **Pinned section header.** While an open section's header has scrolled away, a copy stays at the top of the panel with a soft shadow, pushed up as the next header arrives. Clicking it folds the section and brings the next header to the top (`sectionPinned:<id>`).
- **Tighter rows.** Rows go from 45 to 40 pt, labels from 12.5 to 12 pt, and the panel inset is now 16 pt on both sides (`Tokens::panel_pad`, replacing the 24 / 22 margins hard-coded in Edit, Masking and Denoise).

Since every slider shares the same widget, Crop, Masking and dialogs get the dim/bright text and the 40 pt rows too.

## Tests
- `crates/develop`: `a_panel_differs_only_where_it_was_edited`.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/tests_edit_panel.rs`: edited dots, a card's sliders sit inside the card, the pinned header pins and a click on it folds the section, and the push-up math.
- `widgets::tests::slider_text_is_dim_until_changed_or_hovered`.

title: Library grids: Home/End and Shift+Left/Right selection keys; Cmd+O opens a library, Shift+H visualizes HDR
author: eliets2
body:

- **Home / End** in Photo Grid and Square Grid select the first or last photo of the view (and make it the active one).
- **Shift+Left / Shift+Right** in those grids add the neighbour of the active photo to the selection and make it active. They only add: pressing the opposite arrow does not shrink the selection, and at either end of the view nothing happens.

The grid keys stay out of every other view, the full-screen preview, text fields, dialogs, and any key the user has rebound. The four grid keys are also listed in Help ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts under Fixed keys, and shown struck through when the user rebinds them.

Three commits: the keys, the tests, the docs (`docs/library-shortcuts.md`, `docs/ui-parity.md`, `docs/parity-checklist.md`, `docs/gaps.md`). The parity rows touched are `KEYC-COMPARE`, `LRC-LIB-CATALOG-SWITCH` and `LR-HDR-VISUALIZE`; I added no new rows and changed no statuses or counts. title: LR-LIB-STACK: deleting a stacked photo drops it from the stack so i/n badges update (fixes #1493)
author: squareSphere29
body:
Soft-delete and remove-folder now unstack in the same undo step as Recently Deleted, so leftover members show 1/2 not 3/3. Restore-from-trash does not restack.

fixes #1493

title: Never crash: Render demo scenes at most at their own size
author: endthestart
body: A demo photo whose stored width read 4294967295 (from a damaged catalog snapshot) asked its procedural scene for a render that big, and the buffer size overflowed. A scene now renders at most at its own size, which is the demo photo's full resolution anyway. The test calls render_fit with usize::MAX on a small scene, it panicked before.

title: Never crash: Fix defringe radius overflow for amounts past the sliders
author: endthestart
body: defringe turned the purple/green amount straight into the min/max filter radius, so an amount way past the sliders' 0 to 20 (from a damaged catalog or a sidecar) gave a radius of usize::MAX and `x + r` overflowed on every render of that photo. The amount now acts like the slider's end and the radius stays within the picture. The test renders an amount of 1e300, which panicked before.

title: Never crash: Limit how much a preset zip can unpack
author: endthestart
body:
read_zip inflated each entry up to twice the size the archive says it has, and that size comes from the file itself. A small hostile zip could claim 4 GB per entry across thousands of entries, and when an allocation fails it ends the app, not just the import.

An entry can now unpack to at most 256 MB (DNG presets are the biggest and they're tens of MB) and a whole archive to 1 GB, past that the import stops with an error naming the entry. The archive offsets are added with checked math too. The test covers deflated and stored entries past the limit, the archive total, and an offset at the top of a u32.

title: Never crash: Give the loupe a finite aspect for a zero-size crop
author: endthestart
body: Frame::aspect divides the crop width by its height, so a crop of no size (crop.set with x0 = x1 and y0 = y1, or from a sidecar) gives NaN, and one under a pixel wide gives 0 or infinity. The Detail view then tried to lay the photo out at that size and egui's debug checks stopped on the NaN. Each side now counts as at least one source pixel, so real crops keep their aspect. I added a pipeline test and a headless UI test at Fit and 100% with a drag, both failed before.

title: Never crash: Fix blur overflow and hangs on sliver crops
author: endthestart
body:
The tone, clarity, texture and dehaze blurs use sigmas that are a fraction of the frame's pixels per long edge. With a crop a hair wide (or no size at all) that turns into tens of millions of pixels or infinity. box_radii then squared the box width past i32, which panics in debug, and in release it wraps to a radius of billions so the render just hangs.

radii_for now caps the sigma at twice the picture's long side for both the CPU blur and its GPU twin, and box_radii bounds the sigma and squares in i64. Normal renders keep exactly the same radii. The test renders a few sliver and empty crops with tone, clarity, texture and dehaze on. It panicked before and finishes quickly now. This also covers the blur side of #1519.

title: Never crash: Read the edge pixel for bilinear samples outside the picture
author: endthestart
body:
This one is stacked on #1561 because its test renders sliver crops with clarity and dehaze on, which needs that fix. So please just review the last commit, it'll be a single commit once #1561 is merged.

With a crop of no size the render's inverse mapping gives infinite coordinates. sample_bilinear and the masks' sampler cast floor(inf) to isize::MAX and then asked for the next pixel, which overflows, and in any build the weights come out NaN. The coordinate is now clamped to one pixel outside the picture first, so finite samples don't change and infinite ones just read the edge. The test renders the demo photo with a heal spot and masks at a zero-size and a 1e-9 wide crop, it panicked before.

title: Never crash: Repair damaged catalog snapshots on open
author: endthestart
body:
I found these by fuzzing catalog snapshots that still parse, mutating values in a real catalog.snap and then opening and using the library:

1) An album filed under one id but naming another as its folder could list itself inside itself, and albums.list recursed until the stack overflowed. That's an abort, not a panic, so nothing catches it, and it happened every time the library opened.
2) A stack whose id didn't match its key made arrange_stacks index a map with an id it doesn't have.
3) Id counters behind the ids in use handed out ids that were already taken, and one at u64::MAX overflowed.
4) Folders inside each other made the MoveAlbum cycle check loop forever.

Loading a snapshot now runs Catalog::repair, which puts everything back under its own id, cleans up stacks, moves albums with a missing or circular folder to the top level, and moves the counters past every id in use. It logs what it changed, and a good catalog loads unchanged. There's also some defence in depth (saturating id allocation, a bounded cycle check, album trees stop at 64 deep). The tests cover each case, they all failed or panicked before.

title: Packaging: submit winget manifests automatically for each release (fixes #487)
author: notdezzi
body:

title: fix(develop): reject invalid settings groups before mutation
author: NavidZamanKhan
body:
## Summary
Addresses the settings-group validation portion of #1506.

## Problem
The previous groups_param implementation converted invalid groups parameters into None, making malformed restrictions indistinguishable from omitted parameters.
Consequently:
- develop.paste could apply all copied settings when an invalid group was specified.
- develop.sync could synchronize default settings groups instead of rejecting malformed input.
- Related copy and preset commands had the same validation weakness.

## Fix
- Return Result<Option<Vec<SettingsGroup>>> from groups_param.
- Reject invalid supplied groups with EngineError::BadParams.
- Preserve defaults for omitted or null groups.
- Apply validation consistently across copy, paste, sync, and preset commands.
- Add regression tests demonstrating that malformed input is rejected without modifying settings, presets, or history.

## Testing
- LightCraft engine tests passed (820 tests reported).
- Formatting and Clippy checks passed.
- Parity, layers, assets, and WASM checks passed.
- Full workspace CI has an unrelated upstream test failure in crates/pipeline/src/visualize.rs, which this patch does not modify.

## Scope
This PR addresses only the settings-group portion of #1506. Validation of explicit id and ids targets remains unresolved.

title: Packaging: confirm a successful uninstall with the completion dialog (fixes #892)
author: notdezzi
body:
The MSI never included WiX's standard ExitDialog: the UI sequence's Publish events point at it, but a Publish alone does not pull the WixToolset.UI extension's dialog fragment into the package — only a `DialogRef` does. The extension's fragment is what shows the page (`<Show Dialog="virtual ExitDialog" OnExit="success"/>`), so without the ref every successful run — install, repair, and the uninstall this issue reports — ended silently.

This PR adds the missing `<DialogRef Id="ExitDialog" />` (the shared root cause with #790, which gets the same completion page on install) and documents in the fragment comment that every successful run — install, repair or remove — now ends on the visible completion page, so uninstalling from Apps & features ends with a confirmation dialog instead of the window just closing. packaging-lint gains a grep assertion that fails when the reference is lost again.

Validated locally: the .wxs parses (xml.dom.minidom), the workflow YAML parses (PyYAML), and the new lint assertion passes against the edited file; the packaging-lint Windows job builds a real throwaway MSI with WiX 5.0.2, which now covers the reference at build time.

title: LR-EDIT-OPTICS-PROFILE: Apply Nikon's in-file distortion correction for the Z 6II, Z 8 and Z f
author: endthestart
body:
Nikon writes its own distortion correction into NEFs from the mirrorless bodies (raw SubIFD tag 0xc7d5, NikonNEFInfo), and Lightroom applies it automatically. This reads it for the Z 6II, Z 8 and Z f and turns it into a WarpRectilinear, the same way the Sony, Fujifilm and Panasonic corrections already work.

ExifTool's docs only give the names of the DistortionInfo fields, so I worked out the rest by comparing our uncorrected render with the corrected JPEG embedded in each NEF. The stored coefficients go with r^6, r^4 and r^2 in that order (backwards from ExifTool's naming), they're normalized to the 21.6 mm half diagonal, the value at offset 64 is the zoom the camera uses to fill the frame, and entry 0x0008 is the optical center offset, which moves around with the in-body stabilization. docs/nikon-lens-corrections.md has the details.

I checked it against about 80 of my own Z 6II photos (not committed) with the Z 20mm f/1.8, the Z 24-70 f/4 and the 70-200 f/2.8G on the FTZ, plus the CC0 Z f sample. The 70-200 lines up with the camera JPEG within about 0.2 px. The Z lenses are within 0.5 to 1.5 px, except the 24-70 at 24mm where there's still around 20 px near the edges. As far as I can tell the camera applies some extra correction for Z lenses that isn't in the readable data (entry 0x000e looks encrypted, I left it alone). It's still a big improvement over nothing, which is about 130 px off at 70mm.

EDIT: I just got a Z 8 so I ran the same check on 45 of my Z 8 photos and added it too. Same story there, the 70-200 on the FTZ is within about 0.2 px and the Z 24-120 f/4 is within 0.6 to 1.5 px, with the same leftover error at the wide end.

It's limited to those three bodies and the full frame image area for now, and vignetting isn't in yet. Tests cover the polynomial and zoom, the stabilization offset, refusing other bodies and crops, a synthetic Z 6II NEF through header and full decode and DNG export, and a corpus test for the Z f sample.
