title: Fetch: refuse a redirect from https to http (#1531)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1531.

`Url::join` accepted an absolute `http://` `Location` from an `https://` URL, so a download that started over TLS could finish over plaintext. It now returns `HttpError::BadUrl` for that case, the same error `join` already uses for unsupported schemes, so the redirect loop moves on to the next mirror. Each hop joins against the current URL, so a downgrade anywhere in the chain is refused. Relative and `//host` redirects already keep the current scheme; plain `http://` mirrors still work and may still upgrade to https.

The fetch README now says https-to-http redirects are refused.

Tests (in `resolves_redirects`): https to http is refused; http to http and http to https still resolve.

Not in scope: tokenizer hash pinning, which #366 tracks.

title: Reject a LeakyRelu alpha that is not a single float instead of reading it as 0 (#1530)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1530.

The denoise ONNX reader kept a LeakyRelu `alpha` as a plain `f32` that defaulted to 0. The reader checked the declared attribute type but did not keep it. So an `alpha` declared as INT/STRING/INTS, or a FLOAT `alpha` with no float value, was read as slope 0. The model then ran with the wrong activation. Only a fully omitted `alpha` got the ONNX default of 0.01.

**Fix**

- `onnx_proto::AttributeProto` now keeps whether a float was present (`f: Option<f32>`) and the declared type (`kind`, 0 when the file does not give it). A second float value or a second type field for the same attribute is rejected, the same way as any other unexpected attribute field.
- When a LeakyRelu is fused into the layer before it, `alpha` is accepted only when it is a single attribute with a float value and a FLOAT type, or no declared type. No `alpha` still gives 0.01. Anything else (a wrong type, a missing float, two `alpha` attributes) returns `Invalid("LeakyRelu alpha is not a single float")`.

LeakyRelu is only read in this one place (`fuse_leaky` in `crates/denoise/src/onnx.rs`). No other attribute reader used `f`.

**Test**

`a_leaky_relu_alpha_that_is_not_a_float_is_rejected` uses the synthetic U-Net from `synthetic::unet_onnx` and patches the first `alpha` attribute in place, keeping its length:
- declared type changed from FLOAT to INT: rejected. Before the fix, the model loaded.
- float field replaced with an int field of the same size, so the type is FLOAT but there is no float: rejected. Before the fix, the model loaded with alpha 0.

The unpatched model still loads.

title: Check the SAM weight shape against the header before reading the tensor (#1529)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1529.

`Backend::get` (the candle `VarBuilder` backend for the SAM weights) called `get_unchecked` first, which reads the whole tensor from the file, converts its dtype and copies it to the device, and only then compared its shape with the requested one. A model file with an oversized wrong-shaped tensor could therefore use a lot of RAM/VRAM before the loader reported a mismatch that the header already showed.

- New `Weights::shape(name)` returns the shape stored in the safetensors header, without reading any data.
- `Backend::get` compares the requested shape with that header shape first and fails with the same `shape mismatch for {name}: expected .., got ..` error as before. Only a matching tensor is read and transferred. A missing tensor still goes to `get_unchecked`, which reports `missing tensor` as before.

`get_unchecked` gets no requested shape from candle, so it has nothing to compare against and is not changed. The issue's broader idea of model/tensor memory budgets is left out of this PR, because it needs a maintainer decision on limits.

Test: `wrong_expected_shape_fails_before_the_data_is_read` opens a valid file and checks that the correct shape still loads through `Backend::get`. It then truncates the file it so that any data read fails with an I/O error. It then asks for the wrong shape and expects `shape mismatch`. Before this change the read came first, so the test got the I/O error and failed. The existing outside-the-file tests are unchanged.

title: MCP: do not resend a request whose reply was lost, report an unknown outcome (#1526)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1526.

In connect mode, `Remote::call` sent a request again on a fresh connection after **any** I/O error in the round trip, including when the request had already been written and only the reply was lost. A mutating command (toggle, undo, ...) could then run twice.

Now `roundtrip` reports whether the request may have reached the app:

- **Not sent** (connecting failed, or the write itself failed, so the closing newline never went out and the app can't have run it): retry once on a fresh connection, as before.
- **Sent** (written in full, then the flush or the reply read failed, or the channel closed): no resend. The tool fails with "lost the LightCraft app at ... after sending `<method>` (...); the outcome is unknown and it was not resent, check the app".

So that the "reconnects if the app restarts" behaviour in `docs/mcp.md` still holds, a kept connection is checked before it is used: if the app has already closed it (it restarted, or it closed the connection after an error reply, as `docs/control-protocol.md` describes), a non-blocking `peek` sees that and the MCP server reconnects before sending anything. `docs/mcp.md` now also describes the unknown-outcome error.

Tests (`crates/mcp/src/backend.rs`), using a local TCP listener:
- `lost_reply_is_not_resent`: the server reads the request and closes the connection without replying. The call fails with "outcome is unknown" and the server sees the request once. Before the fix it saw it twice.
- `connection_closed_by_app_reconnects_before_sending`: the server answers one request per connection and then closes it. A second call reconnects and succeeds instead of failing with an unknown outcome.
- `unreachable_app_is_reported`: with nothing listening, the "not reachable" error is unchanged.

This does not add server-side idempotency (the issue's other option): request ids are still only used to match replies.

title: Do not read a sibling's shared stem sidecar for a non-owner photo (#1523)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1523.

When two catalogued files share a stem (`IMG_1.CR3` + `IMG_1.JPG`), one of them owns the stem sidecar `IMG_1.xmp` (`StemOwners`), and the save path already skips a stem sidecar that a sibling owns. The read path did not: `find_sidecar` always fell back to the other naming. So a non-owner with no `IMG_1.JPG.xmp` of its own read its sibling's `IMG_1.xmp` and took the sibling's rating, metadata and develop settings. Switching the library to Full naming did not help, because the fallback still went to the stem file.

Changes:
- New `SidecarLookup` (the naming plus `stem_ok`) and `find_sidecar_in`. `stem_ok` is false when another catalogued file owns the stem sidecar. This is the same ownership rule `save_sidecar_with` uses for its candidates.
- `Session::sidecar_lookup(s)` builds it. These catalog read paths now use it:
  - Read Metadata from File (`read_sidecar_op` / `read_sidecar_op_with_warnings` via `read_packet`)
  - the XMP list in `photo.allMetadata`
  - folder synchronize (`sidecar_has_news` and `read_sidecar`)
- `find_sidecar(original, naming)` keeps its old behaviour (`stem_ok: true`) for import, where the files are not in the catalog yet and ownership is not known.

Test (`a_non_owner_does_not_read_its_siblings_stem_sidecar`): `IMG_1.jpg` + `IMG_1.png` are imported. The JPEG (the owner) is rated and saved to `IMG_1.xmp`. Under both Stem and Full naming, the owner still reads its packet and the PNG reads nothing. Without the fix, the PNG reads the JPEG's sidecar.

title: Reject PEF streams that end before the pixels do instead of decoding zero padding (#1514)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1514.

The PEF bit reader (`Bits` in `crates/raw/src/vendor/pef.rs`) fills its lookahead with zero bytes past the end of the source, which is fine for peeking. But `Bits::overrun()`, the check `decode_huffman` runs after each row, only failed once the refill position was more than 8 bytes past the end (`pos > src.len() + 8`). Because the reader refills up to 8 bytes at a time, a stream could end early and still decode its last samples from up to about 64 padding bits, giving made-up pixels instead of an error.

`overrun()` now compares the bits actually consumed (`consumed_bits()`, which does not count unused lookahead) with the real source length (`src.len() * 8`). This is the same test the other users of this reader already make against their own bit budget (`rw2.rs`, `llvc.rs`). Padding that is only peeked at is still allowed, so a stream whose last byte has spare padding bits still decodes. `overrun()` is only called from `decode_huffman`, so no other decoder changes.

Test: `symbols_decoded_from_padding_past_the_end_are_rejected` uses the existing test Huffman table, where all-zero bits are a valid category-1 code:
- an empty stream for a 2×1 image is now an error. Before this change it decoded two samples from padding and returned `Ok`, so the test fails without the fix;
- the real 2-byte encoding of `[5, 9]` (13 bits, so the last byte has padding bits) still decodes to `[5, 9]`;
- the same stream one byte short is rejected.

The existing `huffman_round_trip` test, including its truncated-to-a-third case, is unchanged.

title: Reject RAW TIFFs with missing or undecodable image chunks (#1513)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1513.

`read_image` in `crates/raw/src/tiffraw.rs` started from a zero-filled buffer and returned success as long as one chunk decoded. A missing strip/tile/plane or a chunk that failed to decode came out as a black region in an image that looked complete.

How each case in the issue is handled:

1. **Fewer chunks than the geometry needs** (short offsets table, missing planar channels). `check_image` now compares the chunk count with `grid()` × planes and returns `Corrupt("N image data chunks, expected M")`. `check_image` is the shared pre-decode check, so the header-only read (`read_image_in` with `Mode::Header`) and the Sony tiled paths in `vendor/arw.rs` that call it reject the file too, not only the full decode.
2. **One chunk decodes and another fails** (e.g. a chunk offset past the end of the file, corrupt data). The first chunk error is now returned for every compression. Before, only JPEG XL did this; other errors were skipped as long as one chunk succeeded. The JPEG XL comment ("not a partial image: the file stays preview-only") now applies to all chunks.
3. **Short lossless-JPEG tiles.** The edge-tile tolerance stays: a frame coded only as tall as the part of the tile inside the image is still accepted. A frame with fewer rows than that visible part is now an error instead of being padded with zeros.

Not changed: an uncompressed or Deflate chunk whose bytes are cut short by a truncated file is still padded with zeros. `chunk_bytes` documents this tolerance ("truncated files yield a shorter slice"), so whether a truncated file should still open partially is a decision for the maintainers. I can add it here if you want it.

Tests (in `tiffraw.rs`):
- `missing_or_failed_chunks_are_errors`: a 4×4 image in two strips. Both strips present decodes. A missing second offset is an error in both the full and the header-only read. A second strip past the end of the file is an error.
- `short_lossless_jpeg_tiles_are_errors`: an edge tile coded at its in-image h…

title: Refuse Open/New Library while an import is running (#1509)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1509.

`app.openLibrary` and `app.newLibrary` only refused to switch while a Lightroom catalog import ran. An ordinary import (`app.import`) kept going after the switch, and its remaining batches were committed into the newly opened library with the old run's options and album ids. The folder scan that comes before an import (`app.scan`) had the same problem: it finishes into an import, or the review, against whatever library is open by then.

Changes in `crates/ui-egui`:

- `panels/settings.rs`: a new `can_switch_library` guard that both commands call. It keeps the Lightroom check and also refuses while `app.import` or `app.scan` is running. That matches the Lightroom import's own `busy()` check (`app.import.is_some() || app.scan.is_some()` → "an import is running"). The error asks the user to wait for the import to finish.
- `menus.rs` / `menubar.rs`: File ▸ Open Library…, New Library… and the Open Recent Library items use the same guard. They are greyed out during an import, as they already are during a Lightroom import. File ▸ Add Folder keeps its previous rule.

The switch is refused rather than cancelling or draining the import. Nothing in flight is thrown away, and this is the behaviour the Lightroom guard already has.

Tests (in `panels/settings.rs`):
- Open Library and New Library return the error while an import runs, and the import stays.
- Open Library is refused while an import scan runs.
- The Open/New Library menu items are enabled when nothing runs and disabled during an import.

title: Preview disk cache: ignore symlinked shard directories (#1504)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1504.

The disk thumbnail cache walked any two-hex shard folder in its directory, so a shard that was a symlink (or a Windows junction) to an outside folder made `prune` and `clear` delete matching `<32 hex>.jpg` files out there. `get` and `put` went through the same link too: `get` could read an outside file and, when it didn't decode, delete it, and `put` could write into the outside folder.

Changes in `crates/preview/src/disk.rs`:
- New `is_real_dir` helper (`symlink_metadata(..).is_dir()`): false for a symlink, and on Windows for a junction / symlink reparse point.
- `scan` skips a shard that isn't a real directory, so `size`, `prune` and `clear` never see files behind it (checking the child `DirEntry::metadata`, as before, didn't catch a linked parent).
- `get` treats a linked shard as a miss (no read, no deleting of an undecodable file); `put` refuses to write into one.
- Module docs and `docs/whats-new.md` mention it, next to the issue #98 rule the cache already follows.

Test: `disk_cache_ignores_symlinked_shard_directories` (unix only, since creating a symlink on Windows needs extra privileges) links a valid shard to an outside folder holding a matching sentinel file and checks that `size`, `prune`, `get`, `put` and `clear` all leave it alone. Without the fix it fails at the first assertion (`size` counts the sentinel), and `prune`/`get`/`clear` would delete it.

Not covered: an attacker swapping a shard for a link between the check and the file operation (the race the issue mentions). That needs directory-relative (`openat`-style) file operations, which std doesn't offer; this PR closes the static case.

title: Reserve the name with an exclusive create when hard links are unavailable (#1503)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1503.

`safe_file::publish_new` gives a finished temp file its final name without replacing anything. It uses a hard link, which fails on a taken name. On volumes without hard links (FAT/exFAT, some shares) it fell back to "check that the name is free, then `fs::rename`". `rename` replaces an existing file, so a file that another writer created between the check and the rename was overwritten. This affects `write_new` / `write_new_unique`, which DNG conversion (Convert / Copy as DNG) and merges use.

**Fix (fallback path only; the hard-link path is unchanged):** the fallback now claims the name with `OpenOptions::create_new` (atomic, fails with `AlreadyExists` on a taken name). Then it renames the complete temp file over its own empty placeholder. A failed claim returns `AlreadyExists`, so `write_new_unique` tries the next candidate name as before. If the rename fails, the placeholder is removed. The temp file is cleaned up by the existing code in `write_new_unique`. The module docs describe the new fallback.

**Test:** `fallback_publish_never_replaces_a_file_that_appears_at_the_same_time` calls the fallback directly (on the volumes CI uses, hard links always work). A hook makes a competing file appear right before the step that takes the name. The publish must fail with `AlreadyExists` and the other file must keep its content. Once the name is free, the publish succeeds and the temp file is gone. With the old check-then-rename, the same hook placed before the rename lets the other file be replaced.

title: Recheck file contents before deleting a moved original (#1500)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1500.

`import_move::finish` decided whether to delete a moved original by checking only that the source and destination were still files of the same length. If either file changed to other bytes of the same length after the copy was verified (or a hard-linked destination was replaced by a same-length file), the original was deleted anyway.

`finish` now compares the bytes with `same_bytes`. The sidecars a few lines below already use the same check. On a mismatch it returns the existing "is missing or changed: the original is kept" error, and the original stays.

Test (`finish_keeps_the_original_when_the_copy_changed_to_the_same_length`, copy path forced with `Fault::NoLink`):
- control: unchanged copy, the original is removed
- the copy is overwritten with different bytes of the same length, the original is kept
- the original is edited to different bytes of the same length, the original is kept with its edit

Without the fix, the last two cases delete the original.

title: Packaging: show the installer's completion page (fixes #790)
author: notdezzi
body:
The MSI never included WiX's standard ExitDialog: the UI sequence's Publish events point at it, but a Publish alone does not pull the WixToolset.UI extension's dialog fragment into the package — only a `DialogRef` does. The extension's fragment is what shows the page (`<Show Dialog="virtual ExitDialog" OnExit="success"/>`), so without the ref the interactive install ran Welcome → Destination Folder → Ready → progress and then simply closed, exactly as #790 reports.

This PR adds the missing `<DialogRef Id="ExitDialog" />` and fails packaging-lint when the reference is lost again. The companion PR for #892 is the same one-line root cause from the uninstall side; the two diffs merge cleanly together.

Validated locally: the .wxs parses (xml.dom.minidom), the workflow YAML parses (PyYAML), and the new lint item passes against the edited file; the packaging-lint Windows job builds a real throwaway MSI with WiX 5.0.2, which now covers the reference at build time.

Fixes #790

title: PERF-IMPORT: a scan, an import and a sidecar write no longer make a table of the whole library first
author: nledford
body:
## Problem

In a large library, Synchronize Folder, the import review and an import sit for seconds before they look at the first file, and each XMP sidecar written (Save Metadata to File, or automatically after an edit) takes seconds too. The time does not depend on the folder: it is spent on the whole library, on the session's thread.

The cause is three tables made of every photo in the library:

- `ScanInput::new` built a candidate record and a content-hash entry for every photo (import review, and Synchronize Folder through it).
- `ImportJob::new` built a path and a content-hash entry for every photo.
- `StemOwners::of` worked out who owns every shared sidecar name in the library (`IMG_1.CR3` + `IMG_1.JPG` → one `IMG_1.xmp`), to name the sidecar of one photo.

## Change

Engine only (`crates/engine/src/import.rs`, `sidecar.rs`, `sync.rs`, `cmd/xmp.rs`).

- **Scan:** `ScanInput` keeps the library as it is (photos are `Arc`s, shared, not copied). `scan_with` looks up the files it found (`library_files`) and, once they are probed, who has their contents (`library_hashes`): one pass over the library each, on the scan's thread, and a record only for what matched.
- **Import:** `ImportJob` keeps the library and whether trashed photos are replaced, as they were when it was set up, and makes its two tables with the first files (`look_up_library`, first thing in `prepare_files`).
- **Sidecar names:** `StemOwners::among(catalog, ids)` works out the owners of the stems of the photos asked about. All five callers (`save_sidecar`, `sidecar_naming`, `sidecar_namings`, the automatic write, `xmp.save`) only ever name those photos. A plain path's key is written into a reused buffer instead of being allocated (`stem_key_into`); any other shape of path goes the long way.
- **Synchronize Folder:** `SyncInput` carries the folder's photo ids; the scan names their sidecars (`sidecar::namings_in`) after it has seen that the folder is there, and shares one copy of the library with the …

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: Match the camera look against lens-corrected JPEGs
author: endthestart
body:
While working on the Nikon distortion correction (#1570) I noticed the camera look fit pairs the uncorrected sensor proxy with the camera JPEG, even when that JPEG is lens-corrected. Nikon Z lenses always correct the JPEG, and zoom it in up to about 9%, so near the edges the fit was comparing pixels from different parts of the scene. #232 works around it by retrying away from edges, but the colour pairs are still off.

So now when the raw carries an in-file lens warp (the Fujifilm and Panasonic tables, the A7R IVA, and Nikon once #1570 is in) the sensor proxy is also warped the same way, and the fit uses whichever version lines up better with the JPEG. That last part matters because not every camera corrects its JPEG. A few of the GFX samples aren't corrected and they just keep the plain proxy.

On the corpus raws that have a warp, mean ΔE against the camera JPEG went from 3.73 to 3.61, and the Panasonic GX80 sample went from 5.75 to 4.13. On 299 of my own Z 6II photos with #1570 applied it went from 3.22 to 2.68, with 241 of them closer. I added unit tests for the warp and a corpus test that checks the fitted proxies line up at least as well as before on every corpus file with a warp. Clippy and the engine tests pass locally with the corpus downloaded. I also bumped LOOK_VERSION since the fitted look changes for these files.

I also tried it on 25 photos from my Z 8, which I think is part of what #211 is seeing. With #1570 and this together they went from 8.28 on main to 2.51 (most of that is #1570 lining the render up with the JPEG, this PR takes it from 2.96 to 2.51). It might help a little with the A7R IVA colour differences in #763 too, the corpus A7R IVA file went from 2.57 to 2.53.

If there's a better way to measure the alignment let me know, I'm happy to change it. Thanks!

title: LR-META-INFO: Show the lens for Nikon DSLR raws
author: endthestart
body:
Most of my photos are from Nikon DSLRs (D700, D750, D80, D5300) and none of them show a lens in LightCraft, so I couldn't filter or search by lens. It turns out those cameras don't write EXIF LensModel or LensSpecification at all. Nikon keeps the lens in its own maker note instead, tag 0x0084 (Lens in ExifTool's Nikon tag names), as the same four values LensSpecification uses: shortest and longest focal length and the widest aperture at each.

So now when there's no LensSpecification and the camera is a Nikon, the metadata reader fills lens_spec from that maker note tag, and the catalog uses it for the lens name when there's no LensModel. I formatted it the way Lightroom shows a lens it doesn't have a name for, like "24.0-70.0 mm f/2.8" or "18.0-135.0 mm f/3.5-5.6". The lensfun lookup still only uses LensModel, so a generic name like this can't pick the wrong lens profile.

I checked it on files from all four of my DSLRs and it matches what ExifTool shows for the maker note Lens on each one. I added tests for reading the maker note (including other makes and lenses that report zeros) and for the name formatting. Clippy and the meta, engine and catalog tests pass locally.

Photos that are already in a library will need their metadata read again to pick this up. If there's a better place to hook that in let me know. Thanks!

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: Add a bundled Nikon Z 6II camera profile
author: endthestart
body:
This adds a bundled camera profile for the Nikon Z 6II, made with `lightcraft-cli calibrate` the same way as the ILCE-7CR, ILCE-7M4, X-H2S and X-T4 ones. The Z 6II is my main camera and right now every photo gets its colour fitted on its own, so colours that a photo only shows a little of can come out off.

This one is stacked on #1586, so please just look at the last commit. The pairs come from 296 of my own Z 6II photos (299 tried, 2024 to 2026, Standard and Auto picture controls, with the Z 20mm f/1.8 S, the Z 24-70 f/4 S and the 70-200 f/2.8G on the FTZ). I collected them with #1570 and #1586 applied, because the camera corrects every JPEG from these lenses and without that the pairs near the edges don't line up. The profile is only the matrix and hue/sat table, none of the photos are in the repo, and it's listed in assets/ATTRIBUTION.md.

To check it I held back every fifth photo (59) and fitted a profile to the other 240. On the held back photos mean ΔE against the camera JPEG went from 2.73 to 2.54, with 43 closer and 8 a bit farther (the worst by 0.64). With the final profile on all 299 it goes from 2.68 to 2.53, but that's in-sample. The ones that get noticeably worse are a couple of ISO 25600 night shots (up to +2.5), where the camera's noise reduction changes the colour a lot. I think that's part of what #1202 is about and probably needs its own look.

I also added the public raw.pixls.us Z 6II file to `xtask corpus` (it wasn't used for fitting) and a test that it picks up the bundled profile. It goes from 5.37 to 5.25 with it. I bumped LOOK_VERSION so smart previews of this model get rebuilt. Clippy and the engine tests pass locally with the corpus downloaded.

Let me know if you'd rather have more photos or a different mix of picture controls in it, I have a lot more Z 6II shots to pull from. Thanks!

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: Add bundled Nikon Z 8 and D5300 camera profiles
author: endthestart
body:
Two more bundled camera profiles, for the Nikon Z 8 and D5300, made the same way as the Z 6II one in #1592. This is stacked on #1592 (which is stacked on #1586), so please just look at the last two commits, one per camera.

The Z 8 profile comes from 261 of my own Z 8 photos (278 tried, almost all Standard picture control, mostly the Z 24-120 f/4 S and the 70-200 f/2.8G on the FTZ). Holding back every fifth one, mean ΔE against the camera JPEG went from 2.55 to 2.33 on the held back photos, 39 closer and 10 a little farther (the worst by 0.46). The public Z 8 sample I added to `xtask corpus` wasn't used for fitting and it stays about the same, 3.22 to 3.27, with a test that it picks up the profile.

The D5300 profile comes from 264 of my own D5300 photos from 2014 to 2017, mostly the 35mm f/1.8. On the held back ones it went from 2.86 to 2.66, 44 closer and 6 farther (worst by 0.63). There's no public D5300 sample to check it against.

I tried the same thing for my D700, D750 and D80 (about 300 photos each) and it didn't help, the D750 stayed the same and the D700 and D80 got a bit worse even when I only fit the Standard picture control photos. Their per photo fits are already pretty close, so I left them out. I wrote that down in docs/camera-preview-colour.md in case someone tries it again.

None of the photos are in the repo, the profiles are just the matrix and hue/sat table and they're in assets/ATTRIBUTION.md. Clippy and the engine tests pass locally with the corpus downloaded. Thanks!

title: fix(ui): report find-missing failures and timeouts correctly
author: NavidZamanKhan
body:
Fixes #1528

## Problem & Reproduction
When invoking `file.findMissing` with `{"wait": true, "folder": <path>}`, the command previously called `tasks::wait(app, &ctx, Duration::from_secs(600))` and returned `Some(Ok(app.ui.last_find_missing.clone().unwrap_or(Value::Null)))`.

Under this implementation:
- If the target folder is invalid (nonexistent or inaccessible), the background search worker fails, toasts an error, but never sets `last_find_missing`. The caller receives `Ok(null)` instead of a descriptive error.
- If the search times out or the worker disconnects unexpectedly, `last_find_missing` remains `None`, also silently returning `Ok(null)`.
- Callers (scripts, control channel, MCP) had no programmatic way to distinguish a successful search finding 0 photos from a failed or timed-out search.

## Solution

### 1. Typed Task Results & Error Propagation
- Added `last_find_missing_result: Option<Result<serde_json::Value, String>>` to `UiState`.
- On search completion, the result is captured as `Some(Ok(v))` or `Some(Err(e))`.
- When `wait: true` is requested, `file.findMissing` takes `last_find_missing_result`:
  - Returns `Ok(v)` containing `{found, missing, ambiguous}` on success.
  - Returns `Err(e)` with the actionable error message if the search or relinking failed.
  - Returns `Err("Find Missing Photos: worker terminated unexpectedly")` if the background thread terminated without delivering a result.

### 2. Task-Specific Waiting (`tasks::wait_for`)
- Replaced the global `tasks::wait` call with `tasks::wait_for(app, ctx, label, timeout)`.
- `tasks::wait_for` loops and polls tasks, returning `true` as soon as the specific `"Find Missing Photos"` task finishes.
- Unrelated background tasks (e.g. auto-import directory listings, catalog scans, preview generation) remain active and do not block or cause false timeouts for `file.findMissing`.

### 3. Strict Timeout Validation & Continuation Behavior

title: Fix all-masks overlay CI regression and cover every view

title: fix(tiff): don't compute next-IFD offset from a truncated BigTIFF entry count (#1516)
author: saadkhantareen
body:
Fixes #1516.

## Summary

`Ctx::ifd` in the TIFF reader computed the next-IFD position from the file-controlled advertised entry count before checking whether the whole table had been read. For a BigTIFF advertising a huge count with a truncated table, that arithmetic overflows `usize` — panicking in overflow-checked builds and wrapping in release builds — even though the position is discarded for truncated tables. The position is now computed only when the full advertised table was read, using checked conversion, multiplication and addition.

## Changes

- `crates/tiff/src/reader.rs` (+8/−3): compute the next-IFD position only when the full advertised table was read, with `usize::try_from` and `checked_mul`/`checked_add` (also removing a silent truncation on 32-bit targets).
- `crates/tiff/tests/roundtrip.rs` (+33): new regression test `bigtiff_huge_truncated_entry_count_does_not_panic`, covering both byte orders.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p lightcraft-tiff` — 20 passed, 0 failed (4 unit + 16 integration, including the existing proptest never-panic suites)
- Regression check: the new test fails on the unpatched code with an add-overflow panic and passes with this change
- `cargo fmt -p lightcraft-tiff -- --check` — clean
- `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-tiff --all-targets` — clean

title: LR-IMP-DEVICE: Show the import review when a card is connected

title: PERF-SYNC: a Synchronize Folder scan reads off the folder's listing whether a photo and its sidecar are there
author: nledford
body:
Its base, #1583, is now in `main`: after the rebase onto `main` (integration batch 35, `a4b53b28`) this pull request is its one commit, `540a281c` ("PERF-SYNC: …"). The rebase met only `docs/whats-new.md` (both entries kept); the code applied unchanged.

## Problem

A Synchronize Folder scan of a folder on a network share is slow though nothing in the folder changed. For every photo of the library in the folder it asks the disk whether the file is there and whether it has a sidecar under any of four names (`IMG.xmp`, `IMG.XMP`, `IMG.jpg.xmp`, `IMG.jpg.XMP`). Each question is a round trip, and the scan has just listed the folder to look for new files: the listing holds every one of those answers.

## Change

Engine only (`crates/engine/src/walk.rs`, `sync.rs`, `import.rs`, `sidecar.rs`).

- **The walk hands over what it lists.** `walk::files_in_noting` calls back with each folder it reads: the name and kind of every entry (hidden ones too) and whether that is all of them (not when the walk stopped inside the folder, or an entry could not be read). `files_in` is the same walk without the callback and returns what it returned.
- **The scan walks first, then checks.** `sync::scan_with` walks the folder once (`import::expand_noting`), then checks the library's photos beside the probing of the new files (`import::scan_files`, the body of `import::scan_with` after its walk). Before, the checks ran beside the walk.

title: M12: content search 1/8 — SigLIP 2 towers and tokenizer on candle (`crates/vision`)
author: bitshiftza
body:
Part of #1593 (local search by photo contents). First of a stack of eight PRs; each builds on the previous one.

## What it adds
A new L1 crate, `lightcraft-vision`, that runs Google's SigLIP 2 image and text towers in pure Rust on candle. Nothing in the app uses it yet; later PRs add the models, the index, the search UI and tags.

- `ContentModel` trait: embed images, embed texts, score them.
- A validated **content-model manifest** (`content-model.json`) with a built-in entry for `siglip2-b16-256` (each file's size and SHA-256), and a bounded reader for Hugging Face's `config.json`.
- SigLIP image tower (ViT with the attention-pool head) and text tower (last-token head), with sigmoid scoring from the checkpoint's own scale and bias.
- A pure-Rust Gemma/SentencePiece tokenizer read from `tokenizer.json`.
- Preprocessing that matches Pillow's resize exactly (the processor asks for bilinear with antialiasing, not bicubic).
- A `vision_bench` example for speed and memory.

## Design notes
- `crates/vision` is **Apache-2.0 only**: it is a port of Hugging Face transformers' SigLIP. `NOTICE` says so.
- `Towers {image, text}`: the indexer loads only the image tower and search loads only the text tower. The 256k × 768 token table (790 MB) stays on disk, and rows are read per text.
- The text tower gets no attention mask and pools the last position of the 64-token padded context, as the reference processor does. Texts are lower-cased in Rust, as the manifest says.
- Every input from a file (config, manifest, tokenizer, safetensors header) is bounded and an error, never a panic.

title: M12: content search 3/8 — content index and background indexing
author: bitshiftza
body:
Part of #1593. Stacked on #1606.

## What it adds
- With Settings → Search → **Index photo contents** on, LightCraft looks at every photo of the library in the background and stores an embedding for each. They go in `content-embeddings-<model>.bin` beside the catalog, about 1.5 KB a photo.
- The work shows in the activity stack as *Indexing photo contents*:
  - its ✕ stops it after the current batch and keeps what is done;
  - turning the switch on again carries on;
  - quitting does not ask about it (a new *resumable* activity row).
- Settings → Search shows progress and time left, a **Pace** (Low / Normal / Fast) and **Clear Index**.
- New photos are indexed as they arrive. Edits never cause re-indexing: the unedited photo is what is indexed. A replaced original (a new content hash) is indexed again. Raws are read from their embedded preview.
- Agents and the CLI can already search: `content.search {text}`, `content.similar {id}`, `content.status`, `content.pump`, `content.pace`, `content.reindex`, `content.clearIndex`. The search bar's Contents mode comes in the next PR.

- **Index file:**
  - header: `"LCCE"`, version 1, a tag `<model id>@<sha256 of the weights>`, the embedding size and the element type (f16);
  - records: photo id, a 16-byte hash of the photo's content key, then the f16 vector: 1,560 bytes a photo.
  - A torn tail is cut back before the next append.

  - one batch is prefetched;
  - the UI pump passes `pause` while the user drags or types, so no new batch starts then.

title: M12: content indexing reads a raw's preview from its planned ranges
author: bitshiftza
body:
Part of #1593. Stacked on #1611. #1443 (face pictures from the embedded preview, with the Adobe RGB planned read) is now in main, as is main's `embedded_preview_covering` (the smallest embedded JPEG that covers a display). This branch's own change is that the planned read follows that choice: `sparse::preview_plan_covering` reads only the JPEG that covers the display, where `preview_plan` read every preview.

## What it adds
Indexing reads only a raw's header and the small embedded preview it uses, not its full-size preview. A 70 MB Sony α1 ARW now costs under 1 MB of disk reads (8 MB before), so indexing a library on an external or network drive no longer saturates the drive and leaves the grid's thumbnails waiting. Grid thumbnails of those raws read the small preview the same way.

## Design notes
- **The mismatch:** the content scan asks the preview loader (`Session::scan_preview_of`) for 512 px. The whole-file path takes the smallest embedded preview that covers that (main's `embedded_preview_covering`): an α1's 1616 × 1080 JPEG, not the 8640 × 5760 one. Main's planned read already picks that JPEG, but `preview_plan` read every preview to do it: 7.5 MB read for nothing on an α1 at 512 px.
- **`sparse::preview_plan_covering(bytes, loaded, min_edge)`** reads in three steps:
  1. the header ranges, with every large preview skipped except its first 64 KiB (preview strips, and the `JPEGInterchangeFormat` blobs where a Sony ARW keeps its full-size JPEG);
  2. each candidate's head up to its frame header (size and component count, which main's choice compares);
  3. only the preview the choice takes.

  A CR3 or a RAF carries one preview and gets `preview_plan`.
- `files::preview_window(path, max_edge)` (main's signature) plans with it below a full-size load; a full-size load keeps `preview_plan`. So thumbnails, face tiles and both scans hand on the whole-file path's preview.
- The planned-read round limit goes from 8 to 12 for the two extra rounds. The 60 % share limi…

title: LR-MERGE-HDR: merged DNGs declare the white balance their source shows (follow-up to #1123)
author: alvarohn
body:
## Summary

#1123 gives HDR and panorama merges of raws without colour matrices (CR2, NEF, ARW…) the colour they open with, and
the render at As Shot is right. But `dng_colour` writes `ColorMatrix1` from the forward matrix, so the as-shot white
the DNG declares lands wherever the fitted look and the generic camera model take it. The merged photo then opens at
a white balance its source never had, and any white-balance edit starts from there. I reported this on #1123 after
it had merged; this PR is the fix.

The colour matrices now declare the white balance the source shows, as `files::WbScaleOf` decides it:

- **Camera with measured matrices** (`lightcraft_raw::spectral`, e.g. ILCE-7M3): those matrices, so the DNG reads
  every white as the source does.
- **Otherwise:** a matrix under which the as-shot neutral is the white the source's scale shows. That is Sony's
  presets' reading (#1344), 6500 K / 0 on the relative scale, or the file's own white.

The forward matrix and `AsShotNeutral` don't change, so neither does the render at As Shot.

## Real brackets

Three Sony ILCE-7M3 brackets of my own (FE 16–35 F4 ZA at 16 mm, ARW, 0 / −2 / +2 EV), merged with `lightcraft-cli
merge hdr` and compared with the reference ARW (renders at 1500 px, CIEDE2000 on 4 × 4 block means of mid-tones):

| | Main (#1123) | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| As Shot the HDR opens at (ARW: 4813 K / +8, 5268 K / +8, 3932 K / +7) | 6913 / 7307 / 6113 K, +115 to +117 | **4813 / 5268 / 3932 K, +8 / +8 / +7** |
| Declared white, Duv | +0.038 | +0.003 |
| Same Temp/Tint on HDR and ARW (5000 K, 3200 K; tint 0), CIEDE2000 | 11–13 (green, Δa\* −10 to −14) | **0.8–1.7** for most; about 5 for the largest changes |
| Render at As Shot, CIEDE2000 against the ARW | 0.41 / 0.82 / 0.50 | unchanged |

The remaining ~5 comes from the largest changes (5268 → 3200 K, 3932 → 6500 K). The ARW adapts its fitted look with

title: LR-MERGE-HDR: frame-order independent merges, and no magenta bias next to clipped pixels
author: alvarohn
body:
## Summary

Two HDR merge fixes, found on real ARW brackets (Sony ILCE-7M3 + FE 16–35 F4 ZA at 16 mm, 0 / −2 / +2 EV, interiors
with bright windows). Each is in its own commit with its own test.

### 1. The result no longer depends on the order the frames come in

The same three photos merged in the app (in selection order) and with `lightcraft-cli merge hdr` (in file order)
gave byte-identical files when the order matched. When it didn't, they differed on 0.58 % of the pixels, by up to
102 levels in the kitchen set. The alignment seeds were the frames' input positions (`i as u64 + 1`). The sums, the
deghost masks and the tie-break between equally bright frames followed the input order too.

`merge_hdr` now sorts the frames by brightness first (ties by median, then a content fingerprint, never by
position), runs everything in that order, and returns the per-frame results (EV, alignment, reference index) in the
caller's order.

### 2. Pixels next to clipped ones lose their weight with them

Measured against the darkest frame, far from clipped pixels each frame is linear to 1 % up to the clip. Within 2 px
of clipped pixels, though, the +2 EV frame's green reads 3–5 % low: demosaicing interpolates it from clipped
photosites. Those pixels weren't clipped themselves, so that frame kept its weight there (k = 4, the largest), and
bright windows took a magenta tinge.

A frame's weight now goes by its brightest channel within 1 px (3 × 3 max) instead of the pixel's own. A wider
margin changed nothing more.

| Bright pixels whose green (against red + blue) is > 10 % below the darkest frame's, camera RGB | Dining room | Kitchen |
|---|---|---|
| main | 0.32 % | 2.86 % |
| this PR | **0.08 %** | **0.28 %** |

Rendered at −3 EV with main's colour tags (#1123), window pixels with G < 0.85·min(R, B) go 50 → 3 (dining room)
and 16 → 10 (kitchen); the darkest frame alone has 2 and 205. With #1123 the strongly magenta pixels are few
either way. The bias shows when the highlights are …

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: near-black frames get a tone curve when no colour look fits (#1587)
author: AlexChambers
body:
Fixes #1587

Rebased onto main `0da998f2` after integration batch 40. This branch uses `LOOK_VERSION` 10 and `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 67. Main uses look 9 and render 64.

## What was wrong

The reporter's darkest Nikon D610 sample (`DSC_0961.NEF`, 12-bit lossy) opened about 2.8 stops brighter than the camera JPEG at the median. The NEF decode is correct: all 391,843,840 decoded samples across the 16 supplied NEFs match LibRaw exactly.

The failure is in camera-look selection. A nearly black frame has only 105 eligible colour pairs, below the 256 every existing look needs, so no fit runs and the raw falls back to the default tone curve, which is far too bright for that scene.

## Change

`fit_dark_tone` in `camera_preview.rs` is a tone-only fallback, tried in `starting_colour_with` only after every existing look (full, partial, tone-only, black-and-white) has failed. It applies only when:

- at least 90% of the JPEG proxy is below luminance 0.015 (about L* 13) and no JPEG pixel reaches 0.85;
- at least 256 unclipped luminance pairs pass the camera toe's signal floors;
- the pairs correlate with the JPEG by rank, and the curve fits a held-out third of them better than the default curve;
- no clipped pixel ends up further from the JPEG than with the default curve.

It keeps the source colour transform and learns no matrix or hue table. `LOOK_VERSION` 10 and `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 67 refresh fitted smart previews and renders.

## Results on the reporter's test set

All 16 NEFs (12 and 14 bit, lossless and lossy, bright and dark). Errors are against the camera JPEG, in stops.

| File | Mean before | Mean after | Median before | Median after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| DSC_0961.NEF | +2.274 | +0.325 | +2.806 | -0.091 |
| The other 15 | within ±0.07 | byte-identical | within ±0.05 | byte-identical |

The remaining +0.33 mean on DSC_0961 sits at the image margins: main keeps a 6048 x 4028 crop while the camera JPEG is 6016 x 4016. Excluding the outer 1% gives -0.03 stops. #…

title: LR-BEHAV-WINDOW: the window opens at the size it was left at, zoomed if it was
author: nledford
body:
## Problem

LightCraft's window opens at 1600 × 1000 every time. Resize it, or double-click the top bar to zoom it, quit, and the next launch has forgotten: nothing about the window is kept.

## Change

The desktop app remembers the size its window rested at and whether it was zoomed (macOS) / maximized, and opens like that again.

- `crates/ui-egui/src/window_place.rs` (new) decides what to remember from what the window reports each frame; `apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs` builds the window from it (`as_remembered`) and feeds it (`PrefsWriter::tick`, and once more at exit). It is kept in `ui.json` as `window: {size, zoomed}`, in the system's points.
- **A zoomed window keeps the size it goes back to.** It opens zoomed, and un-zooming returns to the size it had before.
- **A size is remembered once the window has rested at it** (half a second), so the sizes a resize or the zoom animation passes through are not. A size the window was given just before quitting is taken at exit.
- **macOS:** the "maximized" flag egui-winit gives the app is only refreshed when the window opens and when the app zooms it itself (the top bar's double-click); reading it later deadlocks there (emilk/egui#3494). Window ▸ Zoom and a drag of the window's edge go unseen. So on macOS the watch also goes by size: a window is zoomed when the system said so, or when it was seen to come to fill its screen (as wide as it, and no more than a menu bar and a Dock shorter), and for as long as it then keeps its size. It errs to one side on purpose: whatever is in doubt is a window of the size it has, which opens as large as it was left.
- **Read leniently:** a `window` in the settings that is not one (a hand edit, another version's shape) reads as none and costs no other setting. A size below the app's smallest is brought up to it.

**Not in this PR:**

title: #1617: placeholder GPS block (NUL refs, 0/0 rationals) reads as no location
author: AbdullahAboElHija
body:
Fixes #1617

## Problem
Android phones without a position fix write a GPS IFD whose `GPSLatitudeRef`/`GPSLongitudeRef` are NUL and whose rationals are all `0/0`. `dms()` read the triplet with `Ifd::f64s`, and `Value::to_f64_vec` turns a zero-denominator rational into `0.0`, so the block was read as **0° N 0° E**. Default exports then wrote that location into the EXIF GPS IFD and the XMP.

## Fix (`crates/meta/src/exif.rs`)
- `dms()` reads each component with `Value::get_f64`, which already returns `None` for `0/0`. A component that is present but not a number makes the coordinate unusable. Missing minutes or seconds still count as 0.
- New `hemisphere()`: `read_gps()` now requires an `N`/`S` latitude ref and an `E`/`W` longitude ref. A missing, empty, NUL or other ref means no location.

Libraries that already imported such photos keep `[0.0, 0.0]` until their metadata is read again (as the issue notes).

## Tests

title: Protect originals and preserve existing files when exporting presets
author: SarimSyed
body:
Preset and point-curve exports previously wrote directly to the requested path. A path naming a catalogued original or its XMP sidecar could replace that file with preset JSON; a failed write could also truncate an existing preset export.

Reuse the engine's existing original/sidecar guard and atomic durable writer for both commands. The change is limited to the two export handlers and their behavior tests; no documentation, branding, dependencies or unrelated fork changes are included.

This PR intentionally does not duplicate that fix.
- The complete workspace suite passes with only that known test excluded. Parity, layering, assets and WASM checks also pass separately.

title: Avoid rescanning overlapping photo and preset import roots

Passing a folder, a directory alias and an overlapping parent in one import request could revisit the same files. Photo import reported another content duplicate; preset import could generate several copies/groups for the same physical preset.

Share canonical directory identities across the request, retain the first path spelling, and deduplicate expanded preset files (including repeated explicit paths). Keep the existing lexical/canonical library exclusions, symlink-cycle protection and walk limits; the request-wide directory set is capped too. This is distinct from #1077's already-merged library-exclusion fix and #1425/#1552's content-duplicate policy changes.

Five code/test files only; no documentation, branding, dependencies or other fork features.

title: Preserve manual edits when adjusting or removing presets

title: Search: clearing the filters empties the search field too
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1648.

The label in the video is the loupe's "Filtered: …" pill. Clicking it runs `library.clearFilter` but leaves the old text in the search box, so the box shows a search that no longer applies. Enter does nothing because the box only filters when its text changes. title: Fix zero-feather spot boundaries producing black pixels
author: eliets2
body:
A zero-feather spot produces a zero-width blend transition. At pixels exactly on the radius, division by zero creates NaN alpha and black pixels—even when opacity is zero. Use an explicit hard edge for this case, preserving ordinary feathered transitions.

Two image regressions reproduce the failure before the fix and pass afterward. They cover zero opacity across Clone/Heal/Remove/Fill and exact-radius behavior at two render sizes. Formatting, workspace Clippy, HEIF and an application smoke check passed.

Full workspace CI reaches the existing mask-overlay failure tracked by #1599; 175 pipeline tests pass and that one fails. The new regressions pass in the full run. Later parity/layers/assets/WASM gates remain pending because CI stops at that failure. This draft records the change for review while the upstream blocker remains open.

title: Bound interpolation for extreme brush segments
author: eliets2
body:
`push_dabs` clamped the number of intermediate dabs of one brush segment to 1,000,000, so a finite but extreme segment (for example a point 10,000,000 px away) still allocated a million dabs. A segment that would need more than that many now keeps only its endpoints. Ordinary spacing and the segment's end point are unchanged.

**Test:** `oversized_brush_segments_skip_intermediate_dabs` checks the extreme case (2 dabs, end point kept) and an ordinary feathered-brush segment (21 dabs, end point kept, spacing within the dab spacing). It fails on the old clamp (1,000,001 dabs against the expected 2) and passes with the change.

**Docs:** gap 24 and `LR-MASK-BRUSH` record the fix; the parity status stays 🟡 and broader masking feel is still open.

**Checked locally (Windows):** `cargo test -p lightcraft-pipeline` 192 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored (the masks module has 18 tests); `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-pipeline --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `assets` and `parity` pass. **Not checked:** `ui-egui` calls `push_dabs` for live strokes (`brush_live.rs`); its signature is unchanged but its tests were not built here, and the full `cargo xtask ci` was not run.

title: Reject non-finite denoise inputs and tile overflow
author: eliets2
body:
The denoise backend can accept non-finite mosaic samples or produce overflow after gain matching and overlapping-tile blending. Reject these cases with an error before invalid pixels reach rendering or caching, while retaining valid finite negative and HDR inputs.

Three regressions cover rejection before inference, overflow during gain matching, and overflow during tile blending. The denoise-core suite passes 39 tests with one ignored; formatting and all-target Clippy with warnings denied also pass.

This is a bounded denoise safety change, not an implementation of Raw Details or Super Resolution. It adds no assets or dependencies. The branch is based on current main; full workspace CI remains pending while the existing overlay failure tracked by #1599 is unresolved. This draft is for review with that limitation disclosed.

title: PERF-EDIT: an edit is followed from what it touched, not worked out from every photo (stacked on #1656)
author: nledford
body:
Stacked on #1656 (both change `Session::visible`): the first commit here is its. The commit "PERF-EDIT: an edit is followed from what it touched, not worked out from every photo" is new.

## Problem

Everything derived from the catalog is keyed on its revision, which every op raises. So each edit, however small (a keyword, a rating, every tick of a slider), costs several passes over the whole library:

- the grid's list is queried and sorted again from every photo;
- the source is counted by a second full query, sorted only to take its length;
- the side panels tally the library again: folders, keywords, dates, people, counts.

Keywording through a large library is where it shows: each keyword is followed by a visible pause.

## Measured

`crates/ui-egui/src/tests_view_cost.rs` (ignored; `cargo test -p lightcraft-ui-egui --lib what_one_keyword_costs -- --ignored --nocapture`): a synthetic library of 67,000 photos, a third of them keyworded from 500 keywords, showing a smart album of the 44,666 without keywords at random. Test profile (optimized), Apple M1 Max, in memory.

| The frame after one keyword | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Grid, left panel and Keywords panel | about 156 ms | about 54 ms |
| Grid and left panel | about 138 ms | about 40 ms |
| Grid and Keywords panel | about 90 ms | about 18 ms |
| Grid alone | about 71 ms | about 2 ms |

An idle frame is about 2 ms. By stage: the view's list 37 ms → 0.6 ms; the source's count 37 ms → 0; folder tree 13.5 ms, date groups 14 ms and library counts 6.5 ms are no longer tallied after a keyword.

It is a synthetic library: a real one has its own albums, keywords, stacks and a disk under it, so the shape should carry over, not the numbers.

## Change

- **The catalog remembers what its latest ops touched** (`crates/catalog/src/lib.rs`): which photos, at which revision, and what of them (`Aspects`: rating, flag, label, develop, metadata, capture date, file, analysis, presence). `Catalog::touched_since(revision)`…

title: PERF-EDIT: a smart album's count follows an edit, asking only the photos it touched (stacked on #1660)
author: nledford
body:
Stacked on #1660 (which is on #1656): the first two commits here are theirs. The commit "PERF-EDIT: a smart album's count follows an edit, asking only the photos it touched" is new. It needs #1660: it uses the catalog's record of what the latest ops touched.

## Problem

The left panel shows a count beside every album. On each catalog revision every album was counted again, and a smart album's count asks every photo of the library whether its rules hold. So each smart album costs one pass over the library after each keyword, rating or slider tick: about 25 ms an album in a library of 67,000 photos, and more with every smart album a library has.

title: Faces: GPU (wgpu) path for detection and recognition convolutions
author: emmertex
body:
Fixes #1008

Face detection and recognition can now run their convolutions (most of their time) on the GPU through wgpu, with the CPU interpreter as the reference and fallback.

- `lightcraft-faces`: an `Accelerator` hook on `Net` for Conv nodes. `Net::attach_checked` runs the model on the CPU and through the accelerator on a fixed probe input and keeps the accelerator only if every output agrees within 1e-3 (relative) and, when asked, it was faster. The first accelerator error detaches it and that run continues on the CPU. `Detector::accelerate` / `Embedder::accelerate` wrap this.
- `lightcraft-gpu::faces`: a device of its own (same switches, adapter choice and crash sentinel as denoise). It has a WGSL implicit-GEMM conv for any stride, padding and grouping, gathering im2col straight into workgroup memory; split-K plus a reduce pass when a layer has too few tiles (7×7 / 14×14 maps); and a direct kernel for depthwise layers. Weights stay resident per model, up to 768 MB.
- engine: after a detector or recogniser loads, a background thread offers it the GPU and logs which device it ended up on.

Measured on Linux with a Radeon (Vulkan) and a 32-thread CPU. The machine was under heavy load from other jobs, so absolute numbers are noisy:

| Model | CPU | GPU |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| YuNet 640² | 33–36 ms | 35–61 ms |
| SFace | 25–31 ms | 22–30 ms |
| AuraFace | 204–265 ms | 81–122 ms |

AuraFace is about 2–2.5× faster. YuNet and SFace are about even, because each layer still goes to the GPU and back, so the speed check usually keeps them on the CPU. Not in this PR: keeping activations on the GPU between layers, batching faces per dispatch, and showing the device in Settings ▸ Faces.

Tests: the GPU kernel against the plain convolution definition (dense, strided, depthwise, grouped, pointwise, odd sizes; skips without an adapter); the real models GPU against CPU (`LC_FACE_MODELS=<dir>`: YuNet scores, embedding cosine > 0.9999); and accelerator agreement and mid-run fall…

title: Avoid duplicated camera make in exported DNG identity
author: skybluu
body:
Fixes the **UniqueCameraModel subissue only** in #840; deliberately does not close that issue.

DNGs written from Make `Canon` and Model `Canon EOS R6` now contain UniqueCameraModel `Canon EOS R6`, not `Canon Canon EOS R6`. Prefix matching is ASCII-case-insensitive and requires a whole-word boundary, so `Canonic`, `Canon2`, `Canon_…` and a following Unicode letter are not mistaken for the make. Multiword makes are matched in full. Independent Make/Model tags and the empty `LightCraft` fallback are preserved. Borrowed make/model slices avoid intermediate string clones.

### Evidence
- Failing-before regression observed: serialized tag was `Canon Canon EOS R6`.
- All 27 DNG integration tests pass, including actual serialized tags in both TIFF byte orders, case/multiword/boundary cases and absent fields. Formatting passes.
- Release CLI actual smoke: procedural 1800×1200 DNG with Canon/R6 metadata exported through `lightcraft-cli render … -o …dng`; independent ExifTool readback gives Make `Canon`, Model `Canon EOS R6`, UniqueCameraModel `Canon EOS R6`. Synthetic input only; no photographs committed.

No colour-matrix/calibration/noise processing changes. This is not a fix for the principal R6 chroma-noise issue, and no Adobe profile data was used.

Full Windows CI on this branch passed formatting, then stopped at the existing `pipeline/src/spots.rs:250` chunks_exact lint. Parity references, layering and assets passed separately. An earlier baseline run also found test-only `catalog/src/lock.rs:140` unused descriptor_copy. HEIF/full tests/WASM were not reached; no full-CI/cross-platform claim. Changelog updated.

Current-main integration: merged `b3d392b4` without changing either branch’s behavior; resolved additive changelog text. All **29** DNG tests now pass; rebuilt release CLI and independently read back the actual exported identity again. Earlier 27-test count refers to the original baseline.

title: Never-crash fixes: #1511, #1515, #1516, #1519 and the AllMasks overlay union (#1658)
author: mdlmarkham
body:
## Summary

Never-crash hardening: four hostile-input crash bugs from GitHub issues, each fixed with a regression test that was proven to panic before the fix, plus one real product bug found via its own failing test.

Fixes #1511, fixes #1515, fixes #1516, fixes #1519, fixes #1658.

## Crash fixes (each verified to panic on unfixed HEAD via scratch tests)

- **#1516 — BigTIFF reader:** next-IFD offset arithmetic is now checked; a malformed/corrupt BigTIFF produces an error instead of an overflow panic (862b2d10).
- **#1515 — PEF / Nikon NEF decoders:** predictor accumulation uses checked arithmetic; hostile predictor values error out instead of panicking (007c3b9b).
- **#1511 — demosaic:** raws with two samples per pixel are refused with an "unsupported" error instead of panicking in the demosaic (a84ed4e2).
- **#1519 — hostile spot radius / Gaussian sigma:**
  - `spot_radius` is capped at the long edge in both call sites (`apply` and `window_for_reads_checked`), so a spot of size `inf`/`1e30` can no longer drive an unbounded Gaussian (b7b13f91).
  - `box_radii` is rewritten in f64 with sigma clamped into `[0, 1e4]`, bounding every intermediate (radii ≤ 10 000, window sums ≤ ~2e4 adds) on both the CPU and GPU paths; `gaussian` short-circuits non-finite or tiny sigma with an exact copy (143ff648).

## Product bug: AllMasks overlay showed only the last mask (#1658)

`mask_view` *replaces* pixels, so painting one plane per mask made the last mask erase every earlier one — with two masks only the last showed. The test added with the feature in 8e61ad6b had been failing since it landed. The planes are now combined into their element-wise maximum (union) and drawn once; the test's hidden-mask expectation was also corrected (it compared against the photo pixel where the WhiteOnBlack view paints black) (b55766ed, fd6d49a3).

## Housekeeping

- Four clippy `nonminimal_bool` simplifications (67273c19).

title: Process V3: new sharpening, Masking and colour noise reduction (CPU and GPU)
author: mintakka
body:
## The problem

- **Sharpening** used the Texture band: a Gaussian of 0.0018 × the long edge, ~17 px on a 61 MP frame. It acted as local contrast, with thick light halos round every edge, and **Radius and Detail did nothing** (no code read them).
- **Colour noise reduction** at its default (25) mixed in only a fifth of a plain chromaticity blur and left most of the colour noise.
- No Option-drag previews for the sharpening sliders.

Both renders change how existing settings look, so they ship as **process V3** (`docs/process-versions.md`). V1 and V2 render exactly as before; new photos and Reset get V3, existing edits move with Update to Current Process.

## Changes

**Sharpening** (`crates/pipeline/src/sharpen.rs`, `local::sharpen_band`, `finish::SharpenParams`)
- A filter of the square root of luminance whose lift of each detail size is `exp(c·(G_s1 − G_s2))`, shaped by Amount, Radius and Detail. Radius is in the photo's own pixels (`SourceInfo::native_long`), so previews rendered from a smaller level scale it.
- Designed per setting and output scale: the response's kernel by inverse DFT, cut to the smallest reach within 1.5 % of it, split into at most four separable passes (its eigenvectors), plus a centre term that keeps flat areas exact.
- Run on √ of scene luminance before exposure (the planes survive an exposure drag), applied after the tone map as one factor on display luminance (hue and saturation kept), with a soft cap on the change and deep shadows left alone. Local Sharpness scales the band.
- Masking: `E² / (E² + t²)` of a pixel's sharpening, `E` the gradient of √luminance after a 1.5 px Gaussian.

**Colour noise reduction** (`local::nr_color_guided`, `crates/pipeline/src/chroma_noise.rs`)
- A guided filter of chromaticity steered by the cube root of luminance, at full strength from 25: flat colour is smoothed, colour edges that are luminance edges are kept, luminance is restored exactly.
- What the filter removes is put back where its local energy is a…

title: LR-VIEW-MOBILE-LAYOUT: an opt-in mobile arrangement (photo-first, panels in a bottom accordion)
author: ericcayers-ai
body:
## What this changes

Adds an **opt-in, photo-first workspace arrangement** and a single command to reach it.

`Workspace::mobile()` composes the existing docking primitives into a different shape: `Canvas`
alone across the top, and one `Node::Stack` strip along the bottom holding `Tools`, `Presets` and
`Library` as accordion rows. A row's header opens and closes it, and the renderer shares the
strip's height between the open rows. This replaces the permanent left and right columns of
`Workspace::default()` for anyone who asks for it.

`Arrangement::of(id)` maps `ui.dock.reset` to the desktop starting point, `ui.dock.mobile` to the
mobile tree, and **every other id to the user's current workspace** — so a user who never invokes
the command sees no change at all. The mobile tree is validated before it is published, and
`ui.dock.reset` is the way back.

One row is added to `UI_COMMANDS`: `("ui.dock.mobile", "Mobile Layout", None, "Window")`.

## Why this shape, and not something larger

The docking renderer is an **out-of-tree dependency** — `craft-ui` from `storytold/craft-libs`,
pinned by rev. Changing how panels *render* would require a second pull request against a
different repository. So this change is deliberately **arrangement-as-data**: it uses
`Node::Stack`, which the pinned renderer already draws as an accordion and already unit-tests.
That keeps the diff to two files, adds no fifth `Panel` variant, and needs no change to the
renderer, the persistence path, or `Workspace::validate`.

It is also deliberately **not** a claim of Lightroom-mobile parity. See "Scope" below.

## Files

|---|---|
| `crates/ui-egui/src/docking.rs` | `Workspace::mobile()`, the `Arrangement` enum and its `of(id)` mapping, and the arrangement branch in `command_impl`. |

body:
Closes #446.

**Depends on #1208** (HEIC / HEIF / AVIF EXIF and XMP from the container). The detection lives in the container reader that PR adds, and this branch is built on its head (`036646f9`), so the diff here shows #1208's two commits plus the ten `HEIF-STEREO:` commits of this PR, and it inherits #1208's current conflict in `docs/parity-checklist.md` (none of the ten commits touch that file). title: Import: find sidecars whose photo extension or .xmp differs in case
author: emmertex
body:
On a case-sensitive file system (Linux), a sidecar named `DSC_1.nef.xmp` or `DSC_1.Xmp` beside `DSC_1.NEF` was never found at import. The photo then came in with only the file's own metadata (embedded IPTC and keywords), so the sidecar's star rating and crop were silently lost. A user of the downstream fork reported exactly this symptom (emmertex/lightcraft-classic#43).

- `find_sidecar` also tries the full name with the photo extension in lower and upper case, and `.Xmp` alongside `.xmp`/`.XMP`. It only adds a few `is_file` probes and doesn't scan the folder.
- `sidecars_of` (Import ▸ Move) treats `IMG_1.cr3.xmp` as the full-named sidecar of `IMG_1.CR3`, so a move no longer leaves it behind.
- Test: a raw imported beside sidecars named `.NEF.xmp`, `.nef.xmp`, `.NEF.XMP` and `.Xmp`, and one with a BOM, an XML declaration and a comment, gets its rating and crop in every case; a move takes the lower-case sidecar along.

title: fix(mcp): stop stdio cleanly after output failure
author: euisuh
body:
## Problem and change

When protocol output fails while stdin remains open, the scoped input reader can keep the MCP CLI stuck during shutdown. An export progress hook retained after a backend panic can also keep the output worker alive.

Add a process-stdin entry point used by the CLI, with one owned input worker per process. Output write/flush failures wake the serving loop, stop direct headless exports at the next photo boundary, and preserve the actual output error. An explicit output shutdown message permits normal backend/library cleanup even if a progress-hook sender is retained.

The existing generic borrowed-input entry point remains scoped: callers must arrange input EOF/error. The new stdin entry point is single-use, and callers must finish the process after it returns. A synchronous command, current photo, or normal backend cleanup can still finish before exit; output failure is detected on a write attempt.

## Validation

- Reproduced blocked-input shutdown hangs and incorrect output-error precedence before the fix.
- Bounded subprocess regressions cover idle/progress write and flush failures, retained progress hooks, input error/EOF/panic, output-error precedence, and single-use stdin ownership.

- Full workspace tests: **3,332 passed, 0 failed, 30 ignored**; the ignored subprocess helper is exercised explicitly by bounded parent tests. Separate HEIF gate: 128 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (857 filtered).

title: Preserve shutter precision through import and export (#1619)
author: FredApps
body:
Fixes #1619

Import no longer rounds shutter durations to whole seconds or integer reciprocals. The shared formatter uses a reciprocal only when it recovers the original duration exactly; otherwise it keeps the decimal precision. All Metadata uses the same formatting. The existing catalog schema is unchanged.

Previously rounded catalog values cannot recover discarded precision automatically. Reload metadata from the original files to correct those existing entries.

title: Loupe: the info overlay's shadow is dark, not a second white copy of the text
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1690.

The info overlay lays each line out in white and then paints it twice: a "shadow" one point down-right with a black fallback colour, then the text. egui's `Painter::galley` only uses that fallback for text laid out with `Color32::PLACEHOLDER`, so the shadow came out as a second opaque white copy. `rawinfo` prints decode/develop errors but exits successfully, allowing failed validation batches to appear green. An unreadable input instead panics and stops the batch.

title: HDR: the SDR rendition rolls highlights off instead of clipping
author: emmertex
body:
An HDR edit's SDR rendition (`DevelopSettings::sdr_rendition`), which thumbnails, the Navigator, SDR exports and the loupe on SDR displays show, clipped highlights hard at default SDR settings (e.g. exposure +1.5): everything the HDR edit keeps above SDR white became flat white.

**Change:** the rendition now carries the HDR peak (`Hdr::rolloff_peak`, never serialized) and `finish::base_tone` builds the HDR tone curve and rolls it off into SDR (`ToneMap::sdr_rolloff`, own design): display values up to a knee of 0.5 stay as they are; above it a rational shoulder in stops over the knee maps `[0.5, peak]` onto `[0.5, 1]`, monotone, slope 1 at the knee. The existing SDR sliders (Whites, Highlights, Brightness…) still act through the rendition's settings. CPU and GPU share the tone LUT, so they stay equivalent. **Tests:** a bright ramp's SDR rendition keeps >10 distinct 8-bit values past the point where the SDR edit is flat 255, monotone; SDR edits unchanged (also with a damaged field); a GPU↔CPU equivalence case (skips without an adapter; here mean 0.0000, max 1 LSB).

**Measured:** 30 MP CR2 at exposure +1.5 with HDR on: pixels at 255 in the SDR export 9088 → 0; render time unchanged (1.33–1.45 s before, 1.28–1.45 s after). SDR edit export byte-identical before/after.

title: LR-CROP-STRAIGHTEN: the crop box stays put while the photo turns and moves under it (#1643)
author: emmertex
body:
Addresses #1643 (laggy crop & rotate); related to #962 / #991.

## What changes
- **The box stays put, the photo moves.** The crop tool now shows the crop box upright and the whole photo turned around it, as Lightroom Classic does. While straightening (slider, Angle field, rotate drag) or moving the crop, the box keeps its place on screen and the photo turns or slides beneath it; dragging inside the box makes the photo follow the pointer. Resizing by a handle holds the photo still. The view refits to the turned photo when the drag ends. The photo always covers the box: angle changes still shrink the crop to fit (`CropGeometry::with_angle`), and a move is clamped to the photo by `crop.drag`.
- **No re-render per step.** The crop tool's uncropped render was keyed on the crop box and angle, so every straighten or move step re-rendered the whole photo (the render itself never used them). Its render key and view-cache key now leave the crop geometry out, so a drag just draws the texture it already has, turned by a 4-vertex mesh on the GPU.
- The Straighten tool's level line is measured against the turned view; the dimming outside the box takes the photo as a quad.

## Measured (headless, 6000×4000 photo, 1600×1000 window, 20 drag steps, release)
| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| straighten: new renders of the photo | 20 / 20 | 1 / 20 (the drag's first draft) |
| straighten: frame time avg | 3.4 ms | 1.8 ms |
| straighten: until screen current, avg | 6.6 ms | 2.7 ms |
| move: new renders | 20 / 20 | 1 / 20 |
| move: frame time avg | 3.0 ms | 1.2 ms |

Headless renders are small CPU drafts, so the absolute times understate a real window (a 4K/HiDPI loupe re-rendering a 24 MP photo each step is where the lag showed); the render count is the cause.

title: Metadata: read the Panasonic lens name from maker note tag 0x0051 (#1671)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #1671

Panasonic writes no Exif `LensModel`; the lens name is maker note tag `0x0051` (LensType). In a RW2 (and a Leica RWL) that maker note is not in the raw's own Exif IFD at all, only in the Exif APP1 of the embedded JpgFromRaw (IFD0 `0x002E`).

`try_read_exif` now fills `lens_model`, when `LensModel` is absent, from:
- a `Panasonic\0` maker note in the stream's own Exif (Panasonic JPEGs), parsed with the existing `lightcraft_tiff::makernote` support;
- otherwise the Exif of the JpgFromRaw (RW2/RWL).

Exif's own `LensModel` still wins. `extract`, import (`files::probe_bytes`), the Info panel, `lens:` search, the `{lens}` token and exported `LensModel` all read through this.

### Tests
- `exif::tests::panasonic_maker_note_names_the_lens`: synthetic Panasonic Exif (both byte orders, value stored out of line relative to the TIFF header as Panasonic does); LensModel wins; a note without 0x0051 leaves the lens empty.
- `exif::tests::rw2_reads_the_lens_from_its_jpg_from_raw`: synthetic RW2-shaped TIFF with the maker note only inside the JpgFromRaw.

- `cargo xtask ci` on Linux (Gentoo): fmt, clippy, heif, test, parity, layers, assets all pass. The `wasm` step can't run here: Gentoo's Rust has no `wasm32-unknown-unknown` std.

title: Export: Original and DNG follow the metadata setting (#1505)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #1505

Original and raw-data DNG exports built their XMP with `sidecar::sidecar_packet_with`, which only honoured "Remove location info". Under `metadata: none`, `copyright` or `allExceptCamera` the Original's sidecar and the DNG's embedded packet still carried the title, caption, creator, keywords, capture time, location and rating.

### Changes
- `MetadataPolicy::restrict(&Metadata)` keeps only what a policy embeds (camera, lens and capture settings go under `allExceptCamera`; everything but the copyright info under `copyright`; all of it under `none`). Technical fields (dimensions, orientation, software) are kept.
- `sidecar_packet_with` takes the policy and applies it, including the `lc:location` field. The develop settings and the flag are always written, since they are what the sidecar and packet are for. `sidecar_packet` (the library's own sidecars) is unchanged (`All`).
- An Original is copied byte for byte, so its own embedded metadata can't be filtered. Like the existing refusal for an original that embeds GPS under "Remove location info", an Original export whose file embeds metadata the chosen policy leaves out is now refused with an error that points to JPEG or TIFF, instead of silently ignoring the setting. In practice this means any camera file (it names its make and model) under anything but `all`. Under `all`, and for files that embed nothing the policy excludes (e.g. a scan), nothing changes.

The desktop export dialog only shows the metadata choice for rendered formats, so this concerns the control channel, MCP and presets that combine a metadata policy with `format: original` or `dng`.

Not changed: a raw-data DNG still writes the camera's Make/Model/UniqueCameraModel in IFD0, which the DNG needs to pick its colour profile. Happy to follow up if you'd rather drop those under `allExceptCamera`/`copyright`/`none` too.

title: fix(export): a metadata/sharpen/conflict value that passes validation is the one exported
author: sperea
body:
## Summary

`metadata: "NONE"` passed validation but exported **all** metadata (GPS, location, camera and capture settings). The same validation/conversion mismatch silently ignored upper- or mixed-case values for `sharpen`, `sharpenAmount` and `conflict`.

This PR makes validation and conversion share a single parser, so a value that passes validation is exactly the value that gets exported.

## Root cause

| Step | Code | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Validation | `ExportOptions::validate` → `one_of` | Case-**insensitive**: `"NONE"` is accepted |
| 2. Conversion | `ExportOptions::from_json` → `enm` (serde) | Case-**sensitive** (`rename_all`): `"NONE"` fails to deserialize |
| 3. Fallback | `.unwrap_or(d.metadata)` | Silently uses the default, `MetadataPolicy::All` |

Every export entry point goes through `ExportOptions::from_params` (validate + `from_json`), so all of them were affected:

- MCP: `crates/mcp/src/headless.rs`
- Desktop control channel: `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs`
- CLI: `apps/lightcraft-cli/src/main.rs`

## Reproduction (before this PR)

1. Pick a photo with a location (e.g. `photo.setMeta {"gps": [48.85, 2.35], "city": "Paris"}`).
2. Export it with `{"format": "jpeg", "metadata": "NONE"}`.
3. The validation passes, and the JPEG contains GPS, city, camera model, lens and exposure settings.

The same mismatch affected the other three options:

| Input | Exported before | Exported now |
|---|---|---|
| `metadata: "NONE"` | `all` ⚠️ (privacy leak) | `none` |
| `metadata: "ALLEXCEPTCAMERA"` | `all` | `allExceptCamera` |
| `sharpen: "SCREEN"` | `none` (no sharpening) | `screen` |
| `sharpenAmount: "HIGH"` | `standard` | `high` |
| `conflict: "SKIP"` / `"OVERWRITE"` | `unique` | `skip` / `overwrite` |

## Fix

- `MetadataPolicy`, `SharpenFor`, `SharpenAmount` and `Conflict` each get a case-insensitive `parse(&str) -> Option<Self>`, following the pattern `HdrCurve::parse` and `JxlEffort::parse` already use.
- `validate` checks these four keys with tha…
