title: LR-BEHAV-BG-TASKS: every job that ends says how it ended
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

Why one PR: it is one contract, "every job says how it ended". The engine half alone (`TaskGuard::finish`, `activity.finished`, `activity.dismiss`) would document a command that only exports and imports fill; the other jobs are what make it a real channel for agents and frontends. About 265 of the ~1,530 changed lines are tests and ~80 are locale lines.

## Problem

When a background job ends, its row goes and a toast of a second and a half is the only record of how it went:

- An export or import of an hour leaves nothing to come back to: you cannot tell whether it finished, failed or was stopped, or which files failed (an export names the first in the toast; the rest only an agent could read from `last_export_result`).
- A Synchronize Folder that could not do some files logs them and says "Failed 3"; which files, and why, was only in the log.
- A preview build stopped part-way, or one that could not make some photos' previews, looked like one that never ran.
- A model download that failed overnight, or a Photo Merge or Lightroom catalog that failed, said so only while the toast showed.
- A worker that panicked left nothing at all.

## Change

**Engine** (`crates/engine/src/activity.rs`, `cmd/activity.rs`):
- A job says how it ended: `guard.finish(Outcome { ending, summary, detail, failures, failed, path })`. `ending` is `Done`, `Problems` (not for every file), `Failed`, `Stopped`, or `Died` when its worker is gone. `Outcome::ended(ending)` and `Outcome::failed(why)` cover the plain cases; `TaskGuard::report` says it while the guard is still held (a preview build is marked finished before its running row goes).
- A row is kept in `activity.finished` when the task ran 10 s or more, or did not end `Done`, until `activity.dismiss` (`{id}` or `{all: true}`) lets go of it, for this session. Bounded: 50 clean endings, 200 rows in all, 500 failures a row (all are counted), capped texts and path.
- A guard dropped by a panic leaves a `Died` row; one that is on…

title: Add CPU Lens Blur with focus modes and refinement brushes
author: Clearfall
body:
## Problem and change

Main b3d392b4 reserves Lens Blur settings but does not render them. This draft adds a non-destructive CPU implementation with Circle, Bubble, Five Blade, Ring and Oval apertures, Highlight Boost, heuristic subject selection, radial/manual focus and focus/blur refinement brushes.

The Edit panel has English and Simplified Chinese controls, typed numeric values and the Cmd/Ctrl+6 section shortcut. Engine commands, undo/redo, settings-group copying, presets, rotation and LightCraft XMP roundtrips carry the edit. U8, U16, linear-float and HDR output share the effect; the blue focus overlay is view-only. Input sizes and interpolation work are bounded; the render cache version is advanced.

## Limits for review

- Subject Estimate is a colour heuristic, not a trained physical-depth model. Complex boundaries may require manual refinement. No Lightroom-fidelity claim is made; the checklist marks Lens Blur partial.
- GPU requests fall back to CPU. Region views render a full frame before cropping, and views above 100% magnify native pixels to avoid allocating a giant virtual frame. This can be expensive on large photos.
- The blur working grid is bounded to 1280 pixels on its long edge; subject analysis is bounded to 384 and cached separately. A future GPU/depth implementation remains separate work.

## Validation

- Twelve procedural pipeline regressions and five engine regressions passed on the preceding base, covering focus/halos, apertures, brushes, geometry, caching, hostile inputs, undo/reset/copy, legacy placeholder activation, deep/HDR outputs and full-frame/window agreement, including extreme zoom.

author: Clearfall
body:
## Alternative proposal and overlap

This is a **comparison draft**, explicitly overlapping existing work. It does not claim these issues are unassigned or close them automatically:

- #1259 makes Luminance Contrast effective through the guided-filter blend. Here Contrast changes the filter's edge tolerance (epsilon).
- #1348 proposes signed linear R-Y/B-Y joint chroma filtering, a noise model and a speck brake. Here colour filtering uses normalized RGB chromaticity, a fixed prefiltered guide and two edge-aware 25-tap neighbourhoods. It has no fitted noise model or speck classifier.
- #1349 (stacked on #1348) proposes five-level wavelet luminance filtering with line protection and per-level noise estimates. This draft retains guided luminance filtering. It does not incorporate those proposals' GPU band scheduler.

Please assess this as an independent algorithm option; the current evidence does not establish that it is better than those implementations or matches Lightroom.

Additional coordination found in the 2026-10-14 review: open #1489 changes noise-reduction scaling to use original-image pixels and scale-dependent variance. It overlaps `local.rs` and the CPU/GPU parameter paths; this draft does not include that fix and needs integration review if either proposal lands. #1672 also proposed a different V3 sharpening/chroma algorithm, but is currently closed without merging. The three principal alternatives above remain open and unmerged.

## Change and compatibility

Process V3 makes Luminance Contrast effective and provides separate Colour Detail/Smoothness roles. CPU and WGSL use the same parameters. Cache keys include the process and Contrast, so a warm slider change updates the render. V1/V2 keep their previous output; existing edits require Update to Current Process or Reset to adopt it. Other stages retain V2 behaviour.

title: LR-MERGE-HDR: moving clipped highlights stay, less memory, and HDR for Each Bracket Set
author: dev-null-undefined
body:
## The problem

I tested the HDR merge on real Sony ILCE-7RM6 brackets (67 MP, 14-bit lossless ARW) instead of only the synthetic scenes in `crates/merge/tests/hdr.rs`. The merge is radiometrically right: in linear camera RGB every frame agrees with the merged radiance within ~0.6 % (daylight) / ~1 % (night) from 3 to 90 % of its clip, in all three channels, and the measured exposure steps match EXIF within 0.03 EV. But three things went wrong on real files:

1. **Moving clipped highlights.** In a tripod night bracket (moon and a star at 200 mm, 2 s frames, the sky turning ~30 px over the bracket) the star became a black hole with a coloured rim plus a ring. Measured per pixel:
   - Where the reference had the star clipped, its weight is 0 and the brightest frame, in which the star had moved on, read dark sky with the largest weight: the reference's star was erased.
   - Where the brightest frame had the star, its clipped core was dropped but its unclipped halo kept, which left a ring.
   - Deghost High didn't help. Where the reference is below 1 % of its clip (a night sky), the deghost prediction came from the brighter frames themselves, so their ghosts looked consistent. On top of that, the deghost maps were ≤ 1024 px: for a 10,000 px frame a 20 px star is 2 map pixels.
2. **Memory.** A 7-frame bracket of 67 MP raws ran out of memory (killed at 6.9 GB resident under an 8 GB limit). 3 frames peaked at 4.8 GB and 4 frames at 6.3 GB, ~1.5 GB per frame: the frames were decoded four at a time, and AHD collected every tile before copying them into a second full-size picture.
3. **No batch merge.** Lightroom merges each stack of a selection in one go (Photo Merge on several stacks, with the last settings); we had to merge brackets one by one.

1. **`crates/merge/src/hdr.rs`:**

title: Linux: build an Arch package (.pkg.tar.zst)
author: ujo4eva
body:
Adds an Arch Linux package to the Linux release, next to the `.deb` and `.rpm`. Arch users (Manjaro, EndeavourOS, Omarchy, ...) can then `sudo pacman -U` it, and ArtCraft Launcher can install and update it through pacman (storytold/craft-launcher#389).

## What changes

- `packaging/linux/package.sh`:
  - adds an `arch` format, on by default;
  - builds `lightcraft-<ver>-linux-<arch>.pkg.tar.zst` with nfpm's `archlinux` packager from the same `nfpm.yaml`.

  nfpm can't rename a package per format and doesn't env-expand `archlinux.packager`, so the script writes a copy of the config with both set.
- `packaging/linux/nfpm.yaml`:
  - an `overrides.archlinux` block with Arch dependencies: `glibc gcc-libs hicolor-icon-theme libxkbcommon vulkan-icd-loader`;
  - `provides: lightcraft`;
  - `conflicts: lightcraft, lightcraft-bin, lightcraft-git`.
- **Named `ai.storyteller.lightcraft`, not `lightcraft`.** The AUR already has `lightcraft`, `lightcraft-bin` and `lightcraft-git`. An AUR helper treats an installed package with an AUR name as its own and would rebuild it on the next update. The bundle id is also how the launcher tells this package (which it updates) from an AUR build (which it leaves to the AUR helper).
- The README's Linux download table gains an Arch row.

**No workflow change is needed.** `craft-common-actions` uploads and checksums everything `package.sh` writes to `dist/release`, and the riscv64 job passes `--formats "deb rpm tar"`.

## Notes

- nfpm has no `optdepends` for Arch, so the Debian `recommends` have no Arch equivalent.
- Pre-releases sort correctly: `0.7.0-rc.1` becomes pkgver `0.7.0rc.1`, which pacman places before `0.7.0`. Arm64 maps to `aarch64`.

## Testing

- I ran `package.sh --skip-build --formats arch` with the binaries from the published v0.7.1 x86_64 tarball, checked against `SHA256SUMS.txt`. It produced `lightcraft-0.7.1-linux-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst`.
- `pacman -Qip` reads the package, and `.PKGINFO` has the expected name, version, x86_64 …

title: MCP-CONTROL: validate remote reply framing and IDs (#1716)
author: G6bill
body:
Fixes #1716.

The remote MCP backend accepted a response for a different request, and accepted a JSON response closed before its newline. Both could make an agent proceed on a false success after a mutation.

The client now requires a complete newline-terminated response, limits its payload to 64 MiB (allowing encoded previews/screenshots), validates the integer request ID and response fields, and discards the connection on invalid replies. Such failures report an unknown outcome without automatically replaying the request. Valid results (including null), correlated server errors, and idless pre-dispatch refusals remain supported. The connect-mode documentation describes these rules.

Regression tests use a synthetic loopback peer, not a live app or personal photo library. On unchanged upstream main, the wrong-ID and unterminated-response tests both failed by returning `Ok` with the peer's result. The tests also cover invalid JSON/UTF-8 and response shapes, no resend on either the original or a new connection, byte-limit boundaries (including the full 64 MiB limit), and consecutive request IDs.

Validation: `cargo test -p lightcraft-mcp` (39 lib + 6 e2e tests) and the full `cargo xtask ci` passed locally on Linux (all 8 steps: fmt, clippy, heif, test, parity, layers, assets, wasm; built without `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR`). Branch base is `a4b53b28`; later upstream commits don't touch `crates/mcp` or `docs/mcp.md`.

AI assistance: this is a manually launched, one-off GitHub Copilot contribution on behalf of @G6bill. The implementation and tests were generated with AI assistance. No recurring automation or auto-merge is enabled.

title: Perf: DNG Deflate tiles at level 1, 4.8–7× faster writes for 3–12 % more bytes
author: dev-null-undefined
body:
## The problem

Writing a Deflate-compressed DNG spends most of its time in zlib at level 6. Profiling a 175-frame focus stack of Sony A7R VI raws (67 MP), writing the merged DNG took 3.9 s on 4 cores, and Deflate was 81 % of that phase. Level 6 saves only a few percent of the file over level 1.

## Changes

- `crates/raw/src/dngwrite.rs`: a `DEFLATE_LEVEL` constant (1) for both Deflate tile paths (float / half-float and 16-bit integer tiles), replacing level 6.

## Result

Sony A7R VI files (67 MP), 4 threads, best of 3:

| DNG | time L6 → L1 | size L6 → L1 |
|---|---|---|
| Photo Merge result (half floats, 3 channels) | 3.88 → 0.55 s (7.1×) | 265.7 → 274.8 MB (+3.4 %) |
| Raw export, Deflate option (16-bit CFA) | 0.89 → 0.18 s (4.8×) | 96.7 → 103.0 MB (+6.5 %) |
| Rendered DNG export | 4.60 → 0.69 s (6.6×) | 239.0 → 267.1 MB (+11.8 %) |

Lossless either way: the merge DNG and the raw export decode back bit-exactly. Lossless-JPEG DNGs (the default for convert / import) are unchanged. No test checks sizes or bytes; `dng_export_compression_choices` ("uncompressed is the biggest") still holds (103 MB at level 1 vs ~134 MB uncompressed for the ARW). `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Related

Found while profiling focus stacking (#1732).

title: LR-MERGE-FOCUS: Photo Merge ▸ Focus Stack merges photos focused at different distances into one sharp DNG
author: dev-null-undefined
body:
## The problem

Macro and product photographers shoot focus brackets (the camera steps the focus between frames) and stack them into one photo sharp front to back. Lightroom can't do that (Photoshop's Auto-Blend Layers ▸ Stack Images can); LightCraft had no way either. Brackets are long: the test set here is 175 lossless 67 MP Sony A7R VI raws.

## Changes

**`lightcraft-merge`: `focus::stack_focus`** reads each frame twice and keeps one full-size frame in memory at a time.
- **Alignment** on small versions (binned straight from the mosaic, 8 read at a time): each frame to its neighbour with a similarity (focusing changes the magnification; a homography fitted to features crowded into the sharp slice put corners 3–5 px off), steps chained. A failed step is bridged to one of the three frames before; frames that align to nothing are left out and reported. The most magnified frame is the reference, so every other frame covers it.
- **Brightness from the pixels**: ratio of luminance-thumbnail sums away from clipping along each link (blur keeps sums; per-pixel ratios of differently blurred frames lean one way), steps under 0.05 EV taken as none, EXIF only as the fallback. Auto ISO on the A7R VI changes the tags (160 → 125) but not the raw data.
- **Fusion**: frames warped straight onto the canvas, Laplacian pyramid in √ space; each band a weighted mean of the frames' bands, weight 1 up to twice the band's noise floor and `(1 + e/ε − 2)^16` above (sums kept relative to the largest log weight). Where frames carry detail the sharpest dominates (Burt & Kolczynski's max-activity rule, made steep and soft); where none does they average.
- Never crash: frames without pixels are errors, non-finite samples become 0, frames whose orientation tags differ still stack.
- Shared with HDR and panorama: small loads binned, pyramid `down`/`up` without per-tap clamping (bit-identical, tested against the definitions), DNG output converted in parallel.

title: render --settings applies the preset in a .lcpreset, and refuses files it can't read
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1730.

Thanks @nes-cape for the clear repro. `render --settings` handed the whole file to `develop.merge`, so a `.lcpreset` from `preset.export` was merged as a settings object: its `format`/`version`/`presets` keys matched no setting and were dropped, and the render came out unedited with exit 0. Now `--settings` recognises a preset file (the `.lcpreset`/`.xmp` extension, or the JSON shape: a `presets` wrapper, a bare preset with `settings`, or an array) and reads it with the same `parse_preset_file` that `preset.import` uses, then applies its preset through `preset.apply`, as the app does. A bare settings object is still merged as before. A preset file that can't be read (unknown `format`, no presets) now fails with an error naming the file, and so does a file holding several presets, since it isn't clear which one to apply. Happy to switch that to "apply the first" if you prefer.

I left unknown top-level keys in a bare settings object alone (still ignored, as `develop.merge` does everywhere else); rejecting them would need a list of settings keys the CLI doesn't have today. Happy to add it if you want it stricter.

Validation:
- `render_settings_applies_an_lcpreset_and_refuses_unknown_files` (new, in `apps/lightcraft-cli/tests/cli.rs`): exports a preset with exposure +1 through `run … preset.export`, renders with `--settings` and checks the output is brighter than a plain render; then checks an unknown-format `.lcpreset` exits non-zero and writes nothing. Fails on main (the render with the preset is identical to the plain one), passes here
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-cli --test cli render_`, `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: LRC-LIB-CATALOG-IMPORT: Lightroom catalogs import in batches from the originals' headers (step 2 of #832)
author: ingolfteetz
body:
## What this does

Step 2 of #832, on top of step 1 (`lightcraft_raw::sparse`, landed with #961) and of #1024 (@rwoldberg), whose read progress and cancel it keeps. A Lightroom catalog import no longer reads every original whole and hashes it before adding anything: originals are described from their headers, and photos are added batch by batch while the rest is read.

**Measured** on the catalog from #832 (38,545 photos: EOS R5 Mark II CR3, Leica M11-P DNG, ORF, JPEG; 1.1 TB of originals on a USB SSD, exFAT, ~850 MB/s), macOS, Apple M5 Max, CLI:

| | time |
|---|---|
| every original read whole and hashed (main before #961) | ~25–30 min (estimated from the read rate) |
| this branch | **2 min 2 s**, 38,545 photos and 13 collections |

The same catalog with its drive unplugged imports as 38,545 relinkable placeholders in 12 s.

## How

- **Originals described from their headers.** `ImportOptions::headers_only` makes the import probe with `fs_header_probe` (`files.rs`). It loads what `sparse::header_plan` names into a buffer of the file's length and probes that; a raw shown from its embedded preview is read with that preview (`preview_plan`). NEF, ORF, PEF, ARW6, rendered files and files under 4 MiB are probed whole, as before. The read loop is now shared with #1020's `planned_preview` (`read_planned`), as discussed with @lzjtugjc in #832.
- **Batches.** `LightroomJob::start` reads the catalog; `next_batch` then prepares 256 photos at a time: it probes their originals and parses their XMP and maps their develop settings for the shape each photo is expected to have (`MappedPhoto`), off the owner thread. On the owner thread `LightroomImport::commit` adds each batch as it arrives (remapping only when a photo turns out different), and `finish` adds the collections and merges the undo steps. The UI keeps at most two batches in flight and adds up to four per frame, so the window no longer pauses for seconds at the end.

title: fix(control): bound synthetic UI events and protect input queue
author: NavidZamanKhan
body:
Fixes #1525

## Problem & Reproduction
In `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs`:
- `push_drag` iterated over user-supplied `steps` without bounds validation (`0..=steps`), generating unbounded `PointerMoved` events directly into `app.synthetic`.
- `ui.click` and `ui.clickWidget` iterated over user-supplied `count` without bounds validation (`0..count`), generating unbounded `PointerButton` pairs into `app.synthetic`.
- Invalid parameter types (e.g. `count: "five"`, `steps: -1`, `steps: 1.5`, `count: true`) silently fell back to defaults via `unwrap_or(1)` and `unwrap_or(10)` instead of returning JSON-RPC parameter errors (`-32602`).
- In `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` (`raw_input_hook`), synthetic pointer events (`PointerMoved`, `PointerButton`) and `MouseWheel` events drain **strictly one event per frame** to preserve natural gesture cadence. Enqueueing an unbounded number of events (e.g. 10,000 steps or clicks) starves the UI thread frame loop for thousands of frames (~166 seconds at 60 FPS) and exhausts memory.
- There was no aggregate queue capacity check on `app.synthetic`. Repeated accepted calls could grow the pending event queue without limit.

## Solution

### 1. Strict Parameter Validation & Conservative Bounds
- Added conservative upper limits:
  - `MAX_CLICK_COUNT = 10` (permits single, double, triple, and burst clicks; at 60 FPS drains in <= 0.35 s).
  - `MAX_DRAG_STEPS = 50` (default 10; 50 steps provides smooth slider and curve dragging while keeping draining strictly sub-second, <= 0.88 s).
- Added `parse_bounded_u32(p, key, default, min, max, method)`:
  - Validates positive integer bounds.
  - Defaults to `default` when omitted or `null`.
  - Rejects `0`, negative numbers, floats, huge integers (`> u32::MAX`), strings, and booleans with descriptive `-32602` parameter errors.
- Consolidated `parse_click_count` and `parse_drag_steps` onto `parse_bounded_u32`.

### 2. Aggregate Pending-Event Budget
- Added `MAX_PENDING_EVENTS = 128`: caps the pending synthetic…

title: packaging: RPM requires library sonames, so openSUSE can install it
author: tydude001
body:
## What and why

LightCraft's RPM requires Fedora package names: `libxkbcommon`, `(vulkan-loader or libglvnd-egl)`.
openSUSE has no `libxkbcommon`, `vulkan-loader` or `libglvnd-egl` package, so zypper refuses it with
`nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` (exit 4, which the ArtCraft Launcher shows as "error 4";
storytold/craft-launcher#341).

This requires the libraries' sonames instead, as PhotoCraft and VectorCraft already do, so the same RPM
resolves on Fedora/RHEL and openSUSE. It also declares the binaries' glibc floor, matching the deb's
`libc6 (>= 2.35)`. The floor names libm, not libc: the
binaries' only GLIBC_2.35 symbols are `hypot` and `hypotf` from libm, and RHEL 9's current glibc
(`2.34-283.el9_8`) provides `libc.so.6(GLIBC_2.35)` through backports but not libm's.

## How it was tested

LightCraft 0.7.1's released x86_64 binaries, repackaged with nfpm 2.47.0 and this branch's `nfpm.yaml`, then
installed with the distro's own package manager in a fresh x86_64 container and run with `lightcraft-cli --version`.
The released RPM is the same test on the release's own package.

| | released 0.7.1 RPM | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Fedora 44 | installs, runs | installs, runs |
| openSUSE Tumbleweed | `nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` | installs, runs |
| openSUSE Leap 15.6 | `nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` | installs, runs |
| Rocky Linux 9 (glibc 2.34) | installs; `lightcraft-cli`: ``libm.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.35' not found`` | refused: `nothing provides libm.so.6(GLIBC_2.35)(64bit)` |

The aarch64 RPMs get the same requires. I checked that side on FilmCraft only: its 0.7.2 arm64 binaries need
GLIBC_2.35 for the same two libm symbols, and its branch RPM installs and runs on arm64 Fedora 44,
Tumbleweed and Leap 15.6 (qemu-user).

`cargo xtask ci` passes. This tests installation and the CLI, not the GUI. The same results for every
Crafting App: https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/issues/341#issuecomment-6171570045

title: LR-IMP-LOCAL: Record folders browsed from the sidebar as browsed

title: DNG export and Convert / Copy as DNG write the colour a raw without matrices opens with
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1745.

Thanks @JuergenTenckhoff for the clear report: the cause is where you pointed. A NEF has no colour matrices of its own, and Export as DNG and Convert / Copy as DNG handed the decoded raw straight to `write_dng`, so its empty `ColorData` turned into a DNG with no `ColorMatrix1`. LightCraft itself never renders a NEF from that empty data. It starts from `camera_preview::starting_colour`: a look fitted to the embedded JPEG, the measured spectral matrices (#560), or the neutral fallback. Photo Merge already turns that starting colour into DNG tags for #965 (`starting_colour_tags`), so this PR reuses it in both DNG paths through a small `with_starting_colour` helper. The helper is a no-op for files that do carry matrices, and it keeps the lens-correction opcodes in the DNG, removing them only for the fit, as the photo does when it opens. Copy as DNG goes through the same `write_dng_with` as Convert to DNG.

Worth knowing: the Z 9 isn't in the measured-matrix table, so its DNG gets the colour fitted to its own JPEG (single-illuminant `ColorMatrix1` / `ForwardMatrix1`, `AsShotNeutral`, and the look's table and tone curve), the same tags a merged DNG gets. For cameras that are in the table, the DNG also gets the single matrix at the as-shot white rather than the table's two-illuminant pair. I kept that to match the merge path. Happy to switch to writing the spectral pair directly when a camera has one.

Validation:
- `tests_xmp::dngs_of_raws_without_colour_matrices_carry_the_colour_they_open_with` (synthetic matrix-less raws for a Z f and a Z 9, through export and conversion; the written DNG must carry `ColorMatrix1` and render like the raw it came from): fails on main (`NIKON Z f export: ColorData { illuminant: [0, 0], color_matrix: [None, None], ... }`), passes here

title: LRC-LIB-KEYWORDS: the Keyword List holds its place as the Keywords box above it changes
author: nledford
body:
## Problem

When you scroll down a long Keyword List and tick or untick keywords, the Keywords box above it grows or shrinks (a row of chips, the suggestions). The tree then slides down or up under the pointer, by a row or more with each tick, so the next click has to find its row again.

## Fix

The panel now holds the list in place, the way a browser's scroll anchoring does. When the box changes height, the panel moves its scroll offset by the same amount, and the pass is drawn again (`request_discard`) so the list never shows a frame out of place. It holds only:

- while the box's top is scrolled out of sight. At the top of the panel the box grows in view, as before.
- while the change doesn't come from the box itself. With the pointer on the visible part of the box (a chip's ×, a keyword-set button, a suggestion) or the cursor in its field, the box grows in place.

Details that tracing turned up (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/right.rs`):

- **How the offset is set.** It is set on the scroll area as the redrawn pass starts (`vertical_scroll_offset`). A scroll requested during a pass (`scroll_with_delta`, even with no animation) only lands a frame later, so one frame was drawn out of place and a click could hit the wrong row.
- **What the hold counts from.** It starts from the offset the previous pass started at, not the one it ended at. Near the bottom, egui pulls a shrunken panel's offset back by the end of a pass, and counting from there subtracted the shrink twice.

This is the app's first `request_discard`, so the second commit makes `App::logic` drain control requests (and take the fps sample) only on a frame's first pass. A redrawn pass has no input of its own and still holds the discarded pass's widget rects, so a request answered there would click where a row used to be (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`).

title: gpu: init-marker tests use their own scope counter so parallel device tests cannot join them (#1721)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1721.

`init_marker_is_written_during_creation_and_removed_after` set the process-wide marker and ran on the process-wide scope counter (`ACTIVE`). On a machine with a usable GPU, the device-creating tests in `lib.rs` and `nn.rs` run in parallel and enter `with_init_marker` too. When one of them was inside its scope, `ACTIVE` stayed above zero after the test's own scope ended, so the file was not removed and the `!m.exists()` assertion failed. The `GLOBAL` lock only covered the tests in `backend.rs`.

This takes the second fix from the issue:

- `with_marker` now passes the global marker and `ACTIVE` to a new private `with_marker_on(marker, active, what, f)`. `Armed` keeps the counter it was armed on. Production behaviour does not change.
- The removal test and `a_panic_inside_the_scope_still_removes_the_marker` call `with_marker_on` with their own `Mutex<u32>` (the overlapping-scopes test already does this with `arm`/`disarm`). They no longer set the global marker, so the `GLOBAL` lock is gone.
- A new test, `with_init_marker_writes_the_process_wide_marker`, still checks the path through `set_init_marker` and `with_init_marker`. It checks only that the marker is there during the scope, because a parallel device test can keep the file until its own scope ends.

This only changes tests and how `with_marker` is put together. The race shows up only with a real GPU, so CI can't reproduce it. The tests pass alone, and their result no longer depends on what other tests do with `ACTIVE`.

title: Widen offline reverse-geocoding longitude search at high latitudes
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/geocode/src/lib.rs:172-195` (no existing issue): Offline reverse geocoding misses cities within 50 km at latitudes above ~63° (1° cell search is too narrow).

## Cause
`GeoNames::reverse` only searched the 3×3 block of 1°×1° cells around the query. A degree of longitude shrinks with latitude (about 38 km at 70°N), so a city within 50 km could sit two or more cells east or west and was never examined.

## Fix
The longitude cell range now depends on latitude. It spans the query longitude ± asin(sin(50 km / R) / cos(lat)) degrees, wrapped across the antimeridian. Near the poles, where that bound exceeds the circle of latitude, it covers every longitude cell.

## Verified
- Regression test `high_latitude_cities_two_cells_away`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-geocode --lib high_latitude_cities_two_cells_away`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The ±1 latitude cell span is unchanged, since 50 km is under 1° of latitude everywhere. The cell index and the 50 km limit are also unchanged.

Also adds my entry to `contributors/people.toml`.

title: LR-IMP-CAMERA-COVERAGE: Nikon D600, D610 and D5000 NEFs drop the columns past the image (#1627)
author: endthestart
body:
The D600 and D610 write 6080 x 4028 samples where columns 6034 to 6047 are filler and noise and only the last 32 are dark, so the masked-column check keeps them and they show up as the bright line on the right from #1627. I measured both bodies on the CC0 NEFs on raw.pixls.us (4 of each, 12 and 14-bit, lossless and lossy). The camera JPEG is 6016 x 4016 and sits at (8, 6) in all 8, so they join the D4 and D90 in MEASURED_BODIES. The noise columns were also being read as a saturation plateau. For example, the white came out at 3182 on a D600 file whose picture goes up to 3450. So for measured bodies without a fixed white level, it's now measured inside the image area only.

The D5000 has the same sensor and filler as the D90, so it gets the D90's area and white level. Both raw.pixls.us samples had Auto Distortion Control on, so only the center of their JPEGs lines up, and it lines up at (10, 10) like the D90.

I added a test with synthetic D600, D610 and D5000 data, and all 10 samples now render at the camera JPEG's size with no line. If there's a better way to handle these bodies let me know, I'm happy to change it. Thanks!

Fixes #1627

title: LR-META-XMP: Retry automatic XMP sidecar writes that failed
author: endthestart
body:
I edit photos in place on a NAS, and when the share dropped out, an edit with automatic XMP writing on only went into the library and the sidecar stayed behind, with just a warning in the log. This keeps those photos in a list and tries them again every 10 seconds once their files are reachable. It uses the availability cache, so it doesn't keep hitting an offline share. It shows a toast when sidecars start waiting and another when they're written, and there's also `library.retrySidecars` to do it on request.

I added a test that makes the folder read-only, edits a photo, and checks the sidecar gets written once the folder is writable again. I also tried it by hand with a disk image I detached and reattached. The two toasts are new UI, so if you'd rather this be quieter or shown somewhere else let me know, I'm happy to change it. Thanks!

title: Commands: Refuse malformed photo ids instead of using the selection (#1506)
author: endthestart
body:
When `id` or `ids` was there but the wrong type, for example `{"id": "5"}` or `{"ids": [3, "x"]}`, `Session::targets` fell back to the selection or kept only the valid part of the list. So something like `photo.deletePermanently` meant for one photo could hit everything selected. `targets` now returns an error for those and the commands pass it on, while leaving them out still means the selection like before. #1567 took care of the settings groups part of #1506, and this is the ids part.

Most of the diff is call sites adding a `?`. I added a test that a malformed id gives an error and leaves the selected photos alone. Let me know if you'd rather have this split up or done another way. Thanks!

Fixes #1506

title: LR-IMP-MOVE: Sync the copy's folder before removing the original (#1501)
author: endthestart
body:
When importing with Move, the copy's contents were fsynced but not its entry in the destination folder, so a crash or power loss right after the original was removed could keep the deletion and lose the copy's name. This syncs the destination folder (and any folders it had to create) before removing the original, and keeps the original if that sync fails. Moving a file across volumes in `rename.rs` does the same. On Windows a folder can't be opened to sync it, and NTFS journals those entries, so it does nothing there.

I added a test that makes the folder sync fail and checks the original is still there. Thanks!

Fixes #1501

title: Never crash: Check raw data size before allocating in PEF, TIFF tiles and ARW6 (#1512)
author: endthestart
body:
Three places allocated the full picture before checking the data could fill it. A compressed PEF now has to have at least one bit per sample, since every Huffman code is at least that long. An uncompressed TIFF tile or strip holding less than 1/64 of what its samples need is refused (short ones are still padded with zeros like before). ARW6 collects the tile results and stops at the first failed tile before allocating the mosaic. So a few KB can't ask for gigabytes anymore.

I added tests for the PEF and tile cases, for example a 4 KB PEF stream claiming 30000 x 30000 is refused right away. The ARW6 one only moves the error check before the allocation, and the raws in the corpus still decode the same. Thanks!

Fixes #1512

title: Never crash: Write preview cache files from one bounded writer (#1522)
author: endthestart
body:
Each deferred preview-cache write started its own thread holding its image, so when the disk was slower than rendering (a network drive, a busy disk) threads and images piled up outside the LRU budget. Now each cache has one writer thread that takes the writes in turn, and once 128 MB of images are waiting, a new write is skipped. The image stays in the memory cache, so a later render writes it again. The writer only holds the cache weakly, so it ends when the cache is dropped. On wasm it still writes right away like before.

I added a test that puts a burst of 24 big renders (32 MB each) and checks the queue never goes over the limit, that it drains to disk, and that every image is still in memory. Thanks!

Fixes #1522

title: Model downloads: Time out and cancel the name lookup (#1532)
author: endthestart
body:
The downloader looked up the host name with no timeout before checking for cancel, and then gave every address the full connect timeout, so a bad network could hang a download far longer than the timeout says and Cancel did nothing during the lookup. The lookup now runs on a helper thread and is given up on at the connect deadline, checking cancel while it waits, and all the addresses share that same deadline. A lookup that is given up on leaves its thread until the system resolver returns, since that call can't be interrupted.

I added tests for a lookup that hangs (times out and cancels quickly) and for several addresses that don't answer sharing one deadline. Thanks!

Fixes #1532

title: Catalog and downloads: Don't write through a link at a temp file's name (#1502)
author: endthestart
body:
Saving the catalog writes `<name>.tmp` and then renames it, and model downloads resume from `<name>.part`, but both opened those names in a way that follows a symlink, so a link left there got the write instead and the file it pointed to was changed. Now whatever is at the temp name is removed first (the link itself, never its target), and the new file is created with `create_new`. A `.part` is only resumed if it's a plain file, and it's checked again right before appending.

I added a test for each, planting a link at the temp name to another file and checking that file is left alone and the save or download still works. Thanks!

Fixes #1502

title: Faces: Drop faces made from a photo's old file when it is replaced (#1524)
author: endthestart
body:
When a photo's file is replaced (Reload Changed Files after an outside edit, which changes its content hash), the face embeddings made from the old pixels stayed in the index and the face cache file, and a scan still running on the old file could put its faces on the new one and mark it searched. Now the worker job carries the photo's content key and its result is dropped if the key changed while it ran. Replacing the content also forgets that photo's embeddings and its searched mark, so it gets embedded and searched again, and the cache files are rewritten without it at the next save. Relinking a moved file keeps the same content hash, so its faces stay.

I added a test that holds a worker result, replaces the photo's content, and checks the stale result is dropped while one made from the new file is taken. There's also one that the forgotten photo doesn't come back from the cache files. Thanks!

Fixes #1524

title: LR-BEHAV-EMPTY-STATES: Help ▸ Add Sample Photos and Remove Sample Photos
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

This is part 1 of 5 of the work first opened as #1781 (≈2,700 lines, folded from eight earlier PRs). Each part is a PR off `main` of its own; parts 2 to 5 open once the one before lands. Numbers in this description that came from the earlier, combined version are marked *(earlier version)*.

## Problem

The 24 procedural demo photos could only come with a new library, and nothing took them out as a set. They carry realistic camera EXIF and dates and sit under "My Photos" like the person's own; removing them by hand leaves their six albums (three of them in a "Travel 2026" folder) and keywords behind.

## Change

- **`library.addSamples`** (Help ▸ Add Sample Photos) adds the demo photos, their keywords and their albums as one undo step. It is refused while samples are in the library, Recently Deleted included.
  - The albums come in one folder, "Sample Photos" (`demo::ops_in_folder`), named in the interface's language (`LightcraftApp::run` asks `tr`). An optional `{folder}` names it: 1 to 200 characters once trimmed, no control characters in the trimmed name; the error doesn't echo the input. The reply is `{added, albums, folder}`; `added` is as before.
  - A toast says "Added 24 sample photos, with albums under “Sample Photos” and keywords to try" and stays 4 s (other toasts 1.4 s).
- **`library.removeSamples`** (Help ▸ Remove Sample Photos) removes in one undo step every sample photo (virtual copies and those in Recently Deleted too), the albums only samples filled, and the folders left holding none. An album that also holds a photo of the person's own stays with that photo; a cover that was a sample becomes its first photo left. If a removed album was on screen, the view goes back to All Photos.
- **No catalog scans.** The catalog counts its sample photos by one rule for every op that changes a photo (`apply_counted`); `repair` recounts them on load. `Session::has_samples` is a counter read, safe to ask every frame.
- Selections are kept: Add Sample P…

title: LR-PREF-GENERAL: Keep the Settings window in place when switching tabs
author: endthestart
body:
The Settings window is centered, and its tabs have different heights and widths, so every tab change moved the window and the tab row jumped out from under the pointer. That made it hard to click through the tabs. This anchors Settings at its top edge (8% down the screen, between the usual margin and 96 px) and doesn't let it get narrower than the widest tab it has shown, so the tab row stays put. Other dialogs are still centered like before.

I added a headless test that clicks through the tabs and checks the window's top and width don't move. If you'd rather keep it centered and fix this another way, like a fixed size for Settings, let me know, I'm happy to change it. Thanks!

title: test(gpu): isolate init marker lifecycle tests from concurrent device work
author: Ni-zav
body:
Fixes #1721.

The GPU marker lifecycle tests previously modified process-wide marker
state. When other tests initialized GPU devices concurrently, their
active scopes could prevent the marker from being removed, causing
intermittent test failures.

This change:
- Gives the marker's cleanup guard an explicit active-scope counter.
- Uses test-local counters for marker creation and removal.
- Keeps the panic-cleanup regression independent of concurrent GPU work.
- Preserves the production marker's process-wide behavior.

Validation:
- Reviewed the changes against the current upstream main branch.
- Rust tests and cargo xtask ci have not been run.

title: fix(ui): prevent search text selection from dragging the window
author: Ni-zav
body:
Fixes #1646.

Dragging inside the search field could trigger the integrated title
bar's window-drag gesture instead of allowing text selection.

The title bar handles pointer interactions before the search field is
drawn, so its widget-hit information may not yet identify the field.

This change:
- Excludes pointer presses originating inside the search field from

title: cli: refuse non-object snapshot params instead of panicking
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
The CLI's headless `snapshot` workflow aborts on a script whose `ui.screenshot` line has a `params` that is not an object: the generated path is assigned with `params["path"] = …`, and `serde_json`'s mutable index panics (`cannot access key "path" in JSON array`). A script file is untrusted input (the workflow is documented in `docs/control-protocol.md`), and the CLI installs no `catch_unwind`, so the whole process dies with no usable error. The snapshot loop now only assigns into an object (or null, like an absent `params`); anything else is a script error naming the line, matching the existing malformed-line handling. Regression test `snapshot_script_with_non_object_params_is_an_error` runs the real binary on `{"method":"ui.screenshot","params":[1]}`, asserts a non-zero exit and no "panicked" in stderr, and checks the message; it fails before the fix with the panic above.

Partially addresses #1740 (finding 1, CLI snapshot param panic). Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: raw: check maker-note crop bounds with checked_add
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
A crafted PEF (Pentax AOC/CROP tags) or ORF (ImageProcessing CropLeft/CropWidth) maker-note crop with an origin of `u64::MAX` and a width of 1 makes `x + width` wrap to 0, so the bounds guard reads the rectangle as inside the image; `RawImage::check`'s identical comparison also wraps, so `validate()` passes and `normalized()` then reads past the sample buffer — an out-of-bounds panic in release, an "attempt to add with overflow" panic in debug at the guard itself.

The active-area check and both vendor crop guards now compare with `checked_add`, so a wrapping rectangle is a `Corrupt` error at validate time while exact fits still pass. Regression test `an_active_area_that_wraps_past_the_image_is_corrupt` asserts `validate()` and `normalized()` return `Err` for `Rect::new(usize::MAX, 0, 1, 1)` and for a rectangle one past the last column; it fails before the fix with the overflow panic.

Note: open PR #1162 independently hardens the ORF crop guard with `usize::try_from`; whichever lands second will need a one-line merge — this branch's `checked_add` on the same line covers the same site plus the PEF guard and the `RawImage::check` wrap that #1162 does not touch.

Partially addresses #1740 (finding 3, maker-note crop wrap). Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: engine: refuse negative indices instead of targeting element 0
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`version.delete`, `version.restore`, `version.rename`/`version.update`, `pointColor.delete` and `redeye.catchlight`/`redeye.delete` parse `index` with `f64_req(..)? as usize`; Rust's float-to-int cast saturates, so `index: -1` becomes 0 and the `i >= len` checks never see a negative. A caller over the control channel, MCP or CLI sending `index: -1` silently deleted, restored or renamed version 0 (or the first point-colour sample / red-eye correction) and got `ok` back.

`history.restore` already guards with `is_finite() && i >= 0.0` and `spot_index` uses `as_u64`; a new `index_req` helper applies the same guard to the five sites, with behaviour for valid indices unchanged. Regression test `negative_indices_are_refused` creates a version and asserts the three `version.*` commands with `index: -1` return an error and version 0 is untouched — before the fix the first call deletes it.

Partially addresses #1740 (finding 4, negative index). Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: Packaging: advertise HEIF images and repair the AppStream screenshot
author: IanHollow
body:
The official Linux package enables HEIF decoding, but its desktop entry omits HEIC and HEIF MIME types. File managers cannot offer LightCraft for those images through its declared formats. The AppStream screenshot also points to a missing file.

Add `image/heic` and `image/heif`, keep all existing MIME declarations, and use the existing Tetons screenshot with an accurate caption. Pin the screenshot URL to the source revision. No new image or artwork is added.

Validation: passed `desktop-file-validate` 0.28. Rendered the version/date placeholders and passed `appstreamcli validate --no-net` with AppStream 1.1.3. HTTP HEAD returned 404 for the old screenshot and 200 for the replacement. Static parsing confirms that every previous MIME declaration remains. Application builds, HEIF decoding and file-manager launch checks, and `cargo xtask ci` remain deferred.

Prepared with OpenAI Codex (GPT-6), with independent review of the patch and proposal. The contributor has reviewed this PR. The pending checks listed above remain required before merge.

title: codecs: decode lossless (SOF3) JPEGs correctly
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Lossless (SOF3) JPEGs decode wrongly or not at all: an 8-bit lossless file is routed to zune-jpeg, which refuses lossless, so a file listed as readable cannot open; files that do reach jpeg-decoder are still wrong because its lossless samples are native-endian (`to_ne_bytes`) but were read with `from_be_bytes` (a 12-bit 2048 decoded as 8), the raw `precision`-bit value was never left-justified into the 16-bit range `Buf::U16` feeds onward, and a 3- or 4-component frame over 8 bits reports `RGB24`/`CMYK32` while holding two bytes per sample, so it was wrapped as 8-bit data over double-length rows (the length check passes because the buffer is longer than expected). `d.scale()` is a DCT size, not a lossless resample, yet it was called for lossless frames when a thumbnail box was requested, cutting the output to the top-left of each plane.

Every SOF3 file now routes to jpeg-decoder, lossless frames skip `scale` (`finish` scales after), samples are read native-endian and left-justified, and high-precision RGB/CMYK become `Buf::U16`. Four hand-built SOF3 regression tests (12-bit gray/RGB/CMYK and 8-bit through the public `decode`) fail before the fix and pass after; the crate's other tests stay green.

Partially addresses #1740 (finding 5, lossless JPEG decode). Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: LR-CROP-STRAIGHTEN: turning a crop shrinks it about its centre instead of swapping it for the largest crop (#1794)
author: guillehr2
body:
Fixes the "crop goes back to original dimension" part of #1794.

## What was wrong

`CropGeometry::with_angle` keeps a crop that still fits at the new angle. When it doesn't fit, it replaced it with the
largest centred crop of its aspect (`crop_fit_angle`). For the full photo that is right (#1388), but for a crop the
user made it means the crop *grows*, and moves to the centre.

The steps in #1794 hit this at once. With the aspect locked, dragging a corner inwards keeps the opposite corner on the
photo's corner, so the crop touches two edges. The first fraction of a degree of rotation pushes that corner off the
photo, and the crop became the largest 3:2 crop at that angle, which is nearly the whole photo. Rotating back to 0°
then left the whole photo: the user's crop was gone.

## What changes

- A crop that no longer fits at the new angle now shrinks about its own centre, keeping its aspect, to the largest size
  that fits there (`fit_scale_about_centre`, closed form, no search). A small turn is now a small change.
- The full photo, or a crop an earlier turn shrank to the largest of its aspect, is unchanged: it stays the largest and
  grows back towards 0° (#1388).
- If the crop's centre is itself off the turned photo (a sliver in a corner at a large angle), or shrinking in place
  would go below the drag model's minimum crop size (`MIN_CROP_FRACTION`), it is centred at its own size at most.
  It never grows.
- Every way of setting the angle goes through `with_angle` (rotate drag, Straighten slider, Angle field,
  `crop.straighten`, `crop.set {angle}`, `develop.set` on `crop.angle`), so they all get this. The `crop.straighten`
  help text and the LR-CROP-STRAIGHTEN row in `docs/parity-checklist.md` now say what it does.

Not changed: the "rotation is inverted" part of #1794. That is about what turns on screen while rotating (today the
box turns over the photo), which #1699 changes, so I left that code alone to avoid a conflict. Also unchanged: a crop
shrunk by a tu…

title: ui: render the Show All Masks overlay in zoom windows
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
In a zoomed view, "Show All Masks" still rendered the whole frame at the zoom size, while a single mask's overlay was already shown through a native zoom window (#547): slower, and its detail stopped at the full-frame render's resolution. The window renderer already composes the union from the same mask alphas the selected-mask overlay uses, so only the loupe's gate kept it out; this admits `Overlay::AllMasks` to the window path. Two tests pin it: the zoomed loupe stays a canvas-sized frame plus a window (fails before with `native 6000: the whole-frame render is 6000`), and a window of the union matches the whole render's pixels for every mask view.

Fixes #1712

title: engine: keep the decoder facts a smart preview's offline edits need
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
A smart preview stored the pixels and the camera tone curve, but not the other decoder facts a render reads, so an offline edit kept the header facts instead: a Kelvin white balance came out on the relative scale (6144/6144 pixels of the issue's Bayer fixture differed), Camera local tone mapping lost its gain table map, and AI masks lost the file's semantic mattes. The facts now ride in a length-prefixed tail after the JPEG (JSON facts, then one byte plane per matte), counted from the file's end so an in-place header edit keeps working; `is_valid` requires the JPEG to end right before the tail, and `ENCODE_VERSION` 3 rebuilds older proxies when their original is readable. The regression test builds a proxy, renames the original and pins the offline render to the online one bit for bit; the unit test round-trips facts and mattes and checks a cut tail and a header that lies about the tail.

Fixes #1534

title: Fix crop.rotateAspect turning a zero-size crop into a NaN rect
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/develop.rs:676 (crop.rotateAspect); also crates/geom/src/lib.rs:180 (Rect::fit_aspect)` (no existing issue): crop.rotateAspect turns a zero-size crop into a NaN crop rectangle.

## Cause
`crop.rotateAspect` computed the new aspect as `height / width` of the current crop. For a crop with zero width and height, that is 0/0 = NaN. For a crop with zero width only, it is infinite. For a crop with zero height only, it is 0. `Rect::fit_aspect` only guarded `a <= 0.0`, and NaN passes that check. The stored crop rectangle therefore got a NaN height, which was saved in the develop settings and reached the renderer.

## Fix
`crop.rotateAspect` now discards an aspect that is not finite or not positive. It passes `None` to `crop_fit_angle`, so the crop falls back to the image's own aspect, as `with_angle` already does for a degenerate crop. As a second guard, `Rect::fit_aspect` now also returns `self` for any aspect that is not finite or not positive, not only for `a <= 0.0`.

## Verified
- Regression test `rotate_aspect_of_degenerate_crop_stays_finite`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib rotate_aspect_of_degenerate_crop_stays_finite`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I did not change how `crop.set` accepts a zero-size rect. I did not add a separate unit test for `Rect::fit_aspect`. With the `crop.rotateAspect` change in place, the regression test no longer passes a non-finite aspect to `fit_aspect`, so the test does not exercise the new `fit_aspect` guard directly.

title: Keep crop finite when crop.set gets a huge rect
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/geom/src/crop.rs:59 (CropGeometry::constrained, via crates/engine/src/cmd/develop.rs:524 crop.set)` (no existing issue): crop.set with an extreme rect stores a NaN crop.

## Cause
`CropGeometry::constrained` shrinks a crop that won't fit by the scale from `max_inscribed_scale`. For a rect like `[0,0,1e308,1e308]` the pixel width becomes infinite and that scale becomes 0, so `inf * 0` produced a NaN crop, which `crop.set` then stored and reported as a success.

## Fix
If the shrunk crop in `constrained` has any non-finite coordinate, it now falls back to `crop_fit_angle`: the largest centred crop that fits at the current angle. That crop keeps the rect's aspect ratio when the ratio is finite, and otherwise uses the image's own.

## Verified
- Regression tests `constrained_huge_rect_is_finite_and_inside`, `crop_set_huge_rect_stays_finite`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-geom constrained_huge_rect_is_finite_and_inside && cargo test -p lightcraft-engine crop_set_huge_rect_stays_finite`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`crop.set` still accepts any numbers and doesn't return a validation error. A huge rect is clamped to a finite crop inside the image, as other out-of-range rects already are.

title: LR-META-XMP: radial masks keep their inside/outside from Lightroom (fixes #1815)
author: bitshiftza
body:
## Radial masks from Lightroom keep their inside/outside

Fixes #1815

![A Lightroom XMP radial mask (+1 EV) before and after: the effect moves from outside the circle to inside, as in Lightroom](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bitshiftza/lightcraft/issue-assets/issue-1815-radial-mask.png)

### Cause
`crs_masks.rs` read `crs:Flipped` on a `Mask/CircularGradient` as LightCraft's `invert`. Lightroom Classic writes `Flipped="true"` on an ordinary radial mask, whose effect is **inside** the circle. Every radial mask imported from a catalog, an XMP sidecar, a DNG's embedded XMP or a `.lrtemplate` preset therefore came out inverted.

### What Lightroom's XMP means
These rules were established by round-tripping synthetic DNGs with known masks through Lightroom Classic 15.6, then rendering Lightroom's rewritten XMP in LightCraft:

| Where the radial is | Effect inside when | Inverting the mask |
|---|---|---|
| `crs:MaskGroupBasedCorrections`, `crs:Version` 2 (what Lightroom writes today) | `Flipped="true"` | `crs:MaskInverted` on the mask component (already read correctly) |
| `crs:MaskGroupBasedCorrections` without `crs:Version` | always: Lightroom ignores `Flipped` and rewrites it as `Flipped="true"`, `Version="2"` | `crs:MaskInverted` |
| `crs:CircularGradientBasedCorrections` (process-2012 Radial Filter) | `Flipped="true"` ("Invert Mask"); the default is outside | n/a |

The legacy Radial Filter row follows that filter's documented behaviour, which is outside by default with Invert Mask bringing the effect inside. It isn't measured, since no legacy files were available. The old mapping had it backwards too.

**Feather.** When Lightroom upgrades a version-less radial it halves `Feather` (50 → 25, 100 → 50) and renders both the same. So a version-less value is read at half; version 2 values are read as they are. With that, the middle of the fall-off lands within a few percent of the radius of Lightroom's: 0.86 vs 0.87 at feather 25, and 0.73 vs 0.76 at feather 50. The …

title: LR-IMP-LOCAL: browsing a Local folder keeps or picks the active photo (fixes #1447)
author: bitshiftza
body:
Fixes #1447

## What was wrong

Photo Grid is a grid-only view by design, as Lightroom's Photo Grid is: there is no large preview above the grid in any source, so that part of the report is expected. The bug behind it was the active photo. Choosing an album or another source already keeps the active photo if the new view shows it, and otherwise makes the first photo active. Showing a **Local** folder didn't do this. `library.browse` switched the source without touching the selection, so the photo from the previous view stayed active even though the folder doesn't hold it. As a result:

- Photo Grid marked no photo;
- the histogram and photo info described a photo that isn't in the folder;
- switching to Detail opened on that other photo, not on one in the folder.

## What changed

- `Session::keep_active_in_view` (engine) holds the rule every source follows. The active photo stays if the view shows it. Otherwise the view's first photo becomes the active and only selected photo, or nothing is selected when the view is empty. `library.source` now uses it instead of its own copy.
- `library.browse` applies the rule in the engine command and in the UI's background folder read: once when the view switches to the folder, and again as each batch of the folder's photos arrives, but only while that folder is still on screen. A photo you click in the folder while it loads stays selected.

This matches Lightroom: opening a folder or collection shows one of its photos as the active one, never a photo from another source.

title: KEYC-RATING: Shift+P picks and advances in every view (fixes #1707)
author: bitshiftza
body:
Fixes #1707

## What changed

In Lightroom Classic, holding Shift with a culling key applies it and moves to the next photo, in the Library and in Develop alike. LightCraft already did this for `Shift+X`, `Shift+U`, `Shift+0–5` and `Shift+6–9` in every view, and had Photo ▸ Auto Advance for the plain keys. `Shift+P` was the exception. It picked and advanced only in Photo Grid and Square Grid. In Detail (the loupe and develop view with its filmstrip), Compare and Survey it opened the Presets panel instead.

Now `Shift+P` picks and advances in every photo view, like `Shift+X` and `Shift+U`. It moves through the current grid and filmstrip order and stays put on the last photo. In Compare and Survey it flags the active photo and moves to the next candidate. With Auto Advance on, it still moves only once.

To resolve the key collision the way Lightroom Classic does, the Presets panel no longer has `Shift+P` as its default key. It still opens from Window ▸ Presets and from the edit strip's Presets button. Anyone who wants the old key can give `Shift+P` to Presets in Help ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts, and that assignment wins over pick-and-advance. With the key gone, the Presets-specific special cases in the menu bar, the shortcut help hover and the strip tooltip are gone too.

I checked the other Shift+P/X/U/0–9 combinations and found no other collisions.

Docs: `docs/library-shortcuts.md`, `docs/ui-parity.md`, `docs/whats-new.md` and the parity rows LR-LIB-FLAG, KEY-FLAGADVANCE and KEYC-RATING. KEY-PRESETS goes to 🟡 because Lightroom (cloud)'s ⇧P Presets key is no longer the default.

title: Denoise X-Trans raws through an RGGB re-mosaic
author: paolorizzo
body:
AI Denoise refused Fujifilm X-Trans files outright: the model contract is four RGGB planes, and `make_product` returned `Unsupported` for any non-Bayer colour filter array (gap 11, "Fujifilm users get no AI denoise"). This rebuilds a non-Bayer mosaic as an RGGB mosaic of the same size before the model sees it, so the picture keeps its resolution and everything after the model (tiling, gain matching, highlight protection, blending, the `.lcdn` cache, previews and export) is unchanged.

`lightcraft_raw::demosaic::remosaic_rggb` interpolates only the colour each site needs, through a new `xtrans::rggb` that shares the existing directional interpolation's per-colour step, without building the full RGB picture in between (12 bytes per sample at its peak instead of 20). Where X-Trans already carries the colour RGGB wants at a site, the sensor's own sample is kept bit for bit; the rest reach the model interpolated, so it sees noise that varies from site to site. This is an approximation of an X-Trans sensor, not a model trained on one, and `docs/denoise.md` says so.

In the engine:
- The re-mosaic runs after the decode's memory permit is released, under a permit of its own (mosaic, green plane and RGGB copy). A nested acquire on the same gate could deadlock.
- `layout_of` now requires a 2 × 2 Bayer pattern. 16 of X-Trans's 36 phases start with a 2 × 2 that reads as a Bayer cell, so an X-Trans file whose active area began at one of them would otherwise be packed as Bayer. The old code was safe only because of the `is_bayer` check in front of it.
- Monochrome raws get an accurate reason ("monochrome or already demosaiced") instead of "already demosaiced".

`product::ALGORITHM` is deliberately unchanged: Bayer products are byte-identical, so existing caches stay valid, and X-Trans files never had products to invalidate. Failed and unsupported states are held in memory only, so existing libraries pick up their X-Trans photos after the update without a retry.

title: LR-MASK-BRUSH: Shift-click draws a straight brush stroke from the last one
author: endthestart
body:
Lightroom lets you Shift-click with the brush to paint a straight line from where you last painted, and a LightCraft Classic issue asked for it (emmertex/lightcraft-classic#106). The brush is shared, so I'm doing it here first. A Shift-click with the brush now paints a straight line from where the last stroke ended, and more Shift-clicks keep going from the last point. It goes through `mask.brushStroke` with a new `connect: true`, so it's one undo step and agents can use it too.

If the size, feather or flow changed since the last stroke, the line tapers between them. A stroke only stores one size, so the tapered part is split into short pieces (at most 64) that step from the old values to the new ones, and since strokes combine by their max they join without building up. The taper was part of the request, but I'm not sure Lightroom itself tapers, so if you'd rather have plain straight lines let me know and I'll take it out.

I added an engine test for `connect` (plain, tapered, nothing to connect to, one undo step) and a headless test that clicks, Shift-clicks and checks the line gets painted. Thanks!

title: Add Craft AI: the family's built-in local assistant (Gemma 4 catalogue, loopback runtimes, shared models folder)
author: hasan-sdaif
body:
## What this is

**Craft AI** — one assistant across the ArtCraft family, as a right-hand panel in LightCraft. It talks to a local model runtime on this machine and never to a cloud service:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Local and private** | Every request is `http://127.0.0.1` — Ollama (11434), LM Studio (1234) or llama.cpp's server (8080), whichever answers. No account, no key, no telemetry, and no address a cloud service could be reached at exists in the code. |
| **Light by design** | No inference engine, no weights, no GPU code enters the app. The runtime the user already has (or installs) does the running — Craft AI is a loopback conversation. |
| **Optional** | Without a runtime or a model the panel says so and touches nothing beyond loopback. Downloading is a button, never a default. |
| **Specialised** | The system prompt tells the model it is inside LightCraft and names this app's world — the library, filtering and flagging, the develop panel (exposure, contrast, white balance, tone curve, colour mixer), presets and profiles, cropping, spot removal, masks, keywords and metadata, export recipes, raw/DNG/JPEG/TIFF — so answers are about this app, not generic advice. The ready-made tasks (develop advice, keyword and caption suggestions, export recipe, photo alt text, pick a preset direction) are framed for it, with the honesty clause: never invent panel or slider names. |
| **One download serves every app** | The model file lands in a shared folder the whole family reads — `<data_home>/ArtCraft/Craft AI/models` — so a model downloaded here is already there in every other ArtCraft app, no second download. Ollama's own store works the same way machine-wide. |

title: Detail: snap the 100% view to whole screen pixels
author: john01px2022
body:
Fixes #1683. A full-size JPEG looked soft in the editor at 100%, even though import, decode, render and export all keep its detail.

## Cause

At 100% the photo should map one texel to one screen pixel. `fit_rect` (in `panels/detail.rs`) centres the photo on the canvas and does not snap its corner to the physical pixel grid. When the canvas has an odd width, the corner lands between two pixels. In the file from the issue, on a 2x display, the canvas is 1279.5 pt wide, so the photo's left edge sat at x = -648.25 pt. That is -1296.5 physical pixels, half a pixel off. The GPU then drew every texel with its bilinear filter, which averages neighbouring pixels. That blurred the whole view.

The pipeline was not at fault. I checked each stage with the file from the issue (`2268623-qr6i.jpg`, 5152x7728, progressive, ICC profile, 4:2:0):

| Stage | Result |
|---|---|
| `lightcraft-cli render`, no edits, full size | 48.6 dB PSNR, 98% of the fine detail kept |
| 100% view, window render from the full-resolution source | `ui.inspect` reports `region.full` 5152x7728 and the full source held in memory, so the sharp render was already being used |
| 100% view, half-pixel offset | 39.5 dB PSNR, 68% of the fine detail kept |

## What changed

`fit_rect` now rounds the photo's top-left corner to a whole physical pixel when the photo is 1:1 with the screen. The rule is a `Zoom::Percent` zoom and `(w * ppp - img_px[0]).abs() < 0.5`. The size is unchanged. Only the position moves, by at most half a physical pixel.

- The sharp window render is placed from the photo's corner by whole-pixel offsets, so it lands on the pixel grid once the corner does.
- Fit and Fill are untouched. They always resample.
- Other percentages are untouched. At those zooms the texture is resampled anyway, so snapping would not sharpen anything. It would also make a pinch jump: `trackpad_pinch_anchors_fractional_zoom_and_scroll_pans` pinches by 0.1% and requires the point under the cursor to stay put within 1e-5…

title: LRC-LIB-LIBFOLDERS: drag photos from the grid onto a Folders row to move them there
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Why

Photos could be moved to a folder on disk only from a Folders row's menu (Move Selected Photos Here) or the photo menu (Move to Folder…). Dragging photos from the grid onto a Folders row, as you can onto an album or in Lightroom Classic's Folders panel, did nothing.

title: macOS: open photos from Finder, the Dock and Open With
author: gkistlergit
body:
## Summary

`open -a LightCraft photo.jpg`, a Finder double-click, Open With and a drop on the Dock icon arrive as the open-documents (`odoc`) Apple event, not as an argument. winit 0.30 owns the application delegate and never handles that event, and the bundle declared no document types, so AppKit fell back to its own document handling and showed "LightCraft cannot open files in the “JPEG image” format"; the photo never reached the app. The quit Apple event (Dock menu, log out, AppleScript) was ignored the same way. This ports PhotoCraft's handler.

```diff
 main
+  apple_events::install        # NSAppleEventManager 'odoc' + 'quit' handler (fmv-macos-events, safe API)
   eframe::run_native
+    app.services.os_events = Source::connect(egui_ctx)
 LightcraftApp::logic_inner
-  <dropped files: model → licence dialog, presets → file.importPresets, photos → import::start_paths>
+  open_paths_from_os(dropped files)      # the same routing, now shared
+  drain_os_events
+    OsEvent::Open  → open_paths_from_os (waits with the launch files while the library-problem dialog is up)
+    OsEvent::Quit  → ui.quit (the app's own quit path)
```

`packaging/macos/Info.plist.in` now claims the image types `lightcraft_engine::import::EXTENSIONS` supports (Editor, `LSHandlerRank` Alternate, so LightCraft never becomes the default app for images); every camera raw format is covered by `public.camera-raw-image`. `CLAUDE.md` names the external unsafe helper crate, as its unsafe rule asks. On other platforms `apple_events::Source` is inert.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `open -a LightCraft test-photo.jpg` → macOS alert *The document “test-photo.jpg” could not be opened. LightCraft cannot open files in the “JPEG image” format.* `osascript -e 'tell application "LightCraft" to quit'` did nothing.
  **After** (local build on macOS 27, Apple silicon): the photo is imported at launch (All Photos 24 → 25); a second photo sent to the running app is imported too (→ 26); the quit event exits the app…

title: Drop out-of-range GPS coordinates read from XMP
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/meta/src/xmp.rs:364 (parse_gps_coord, used at xmp.rs:539-544)` (no existing issue): XMP sidecar GPS coordinates are not range-checked: latitude 95° and longitude 200.5° are imported.

## Cause
`parse_xmp` set `Metadata::gps` from `exif:GPSLatitude`/`exif:GPSLongitude` whenever `parse_gps_coord` returned a finite value, and nothing checked the range. Impossible positions such as latitude 95° or longitude 200.5° were stored in the catalog and could be written back out on export. The EXIF and GPX readers already drop these.

## Fix
`parse_xmp` now sets `gps` only when latitude is within [-90, 90] and longitude is within [-180, 180]. This is the same check `read_gps` in exif.rs uses. A regression test covers values out of range in each field and accepts the exact ±90°/±180° edges.

## Verified
- Regression test `xmp_gps_out_of_range_rejected`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-meta --lib xmp_gps_out_of_range_rejected`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`parse_gps_coord` stays a plain DMS-to-degrees parser, and the range check sits next to where `Gps` is built, as in the EXIF reader. The GPS writer (`fmt_gps_coord`) is unchanged.

title: Match f:/aperture:/focal: search tokens at f32 precision
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/catalog/src/query.rs:130` (no existing issue): Search tokens f:/aperture: and focal: never match non-integer values such as f:2.8 or focal:5.6.

## Cause
`token_matches` widened the photo's `f32` aperture and focal length to `f64` and checked equality with a 1e-9 tolerance. 2.8f32 becomes 2.7999999523 as an f64, which is about 5e-8 away from the typed 2.8, so any value that isn't exact in binary (f/2.8, 5.6 mm, …) never matched. For the same reason, `f:<2.8` matched a photo shot at f/2.8.

## Fix
Added a `cmp32` comparator that narrows the parsed value to `f32` and does `=`, `<` and `>` in f32. The `f`/`aperture` and `focal` fields now use it.

## Verified
- Regression test `search_tokens_match_f32_aperture_and_focal`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-catalog --lib search_tokens_match_f32_aperture_and_focal`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The f64 `cmp` used by the integer-backed `rating` and `iso` fields is unchanged.

title: gpu: renders queue for device memory; out of memory never retires the GPU (#1764)
author: bogusyogi
body:
Fixes #1764.

GPU allocations, upload staging & kernel parameter buffers now use checked out-of-memory scopes. Failed uploads never enter shared source cache or bind groups. Renders reserve an adaptive memory budget; an out-of-memory retry holds exclusive admission until its permit drops, then falls back to CPU if needed.

Regression coverage includes later renders arriving during an exclusive retry, staging failure after destination creation & parameter destination/staging failures before binding. Earlier exclusive-retry & upload regressions failed with original behavior restored, then passed: [hosted proof](https://github.com/bogusyogi/thiserror/actions/runs/39052975028/job/117455136293).

At current head c4bf9b7cfbd30345dd1294924ca773c3e5ca2978, [parameter regression proof](https://github.com/bogusyogi/thiserror/actions/runs/39060246093/job/117476542555) restores only unchecked parameter allocation while preserving identical test bytes. That test fails on its expected OOM assertion; repaired code passes 1 parameter test, 2 fallback tests & all 7 budget tests.

GPU validation uses software Vulkan (llvmpipe) with an admission-only harness override allowing CPU adapters, identical for failing & passing runs. Override is absent from this PR; candidate source & lockfile hashes are restored afterward. Allocation failures use test-only fault injection; this does not claim real driver OOM reproduction.

Thanks to @aterveus for diagnosis & prototype in #1764.

AI-assisted implementation & review with Claude Code & Codex.

title: LR-LIB-DELETE-DISK: Delete asks Delete from Disk / Cancel / Remove, as in Lightroom (fixes #1706)
author: bitshiftza
body:
Fixes #1706

Follow-ups for Windows and macOS: #1849 and #1850.

## What changed

Pressing **Delete** now asks the way Lightroom Classic does. The dialog offers **Delete from Disk**, **Cancel** and **Remove**, with Remove as the default (Return).

- **Delete from Disk** moves each photo's file to the system Trash. Nothing is ever deleted outright, so the user can get it back from there. The photo also leaves the library.
  - **Linux / BSD:** the freedesktop.org Trash: the home trash, or for another disk its `.Trash/$uid` or `.Trash-$uid`. Each file gets a `.trashinfo`, so file managers can restore it.
- **Windows and macOS: turned off for now.** The code is there but has not been run on those systems, so the command, the menu entry and the dialog button are all disabled there. Follow-ups: #1849 (Windows) and #1850 (macOS).
- **Web:** not available.
- **Sidecars** go with the photo. `<file>.xmp` always goes. `<stem>.xmp` goes only when no other photo file shares the stem, so the sidecar shared by a raw + JPEG pair stays until both photos go.
- **Virtual copies** of a trashed file leave the library with it. A virtual copy selected on its own only leaves the library.
- **Remove** moves the photos to Recently Deleted, as Delete did before. The files stay on disk.
- **Failure:** if a file can't be moved to the Trash (no Trash on that disk, no permission), it stays where it is and so does its photo. The dialog says why and offers **Remove from Library** instead.
- **Undo** brings the photos back to the library but not their files. The dialog tells the user to restore the files from the Trash.
- **Photo ▸ Delete Rejected Photos…** (⌘⌫ / Ctrl+Backspace) asks the same question about the rejected photos on screen. In a normal album it only takes them out of the album, as the Delete key does there (#1818).
- **Photo ▸ Delete from Disk…** opens the dialog even when the confirmation is turned off in Settings.

title: Crop: save, name, reorder and delete your own aspect ratios, hide built-in ones (#1854)
author: switch87
body:
Lightroom only remembers your last five custom crop ratios, unnamed; people have asked Adobe to fix that since 2011 ([Adobe idea](https://community.adobe.com/feature-requests-676/p-ability-to-name-custom-crops-and-have-more-than-5-666398/index8.html), https://redd.it/1ncoacn). LightCraft's Custom W × H row applied a ratio once and forgot it. This PR lets you keep your own ratios in the crop tool.

## Behaviour

- **Save a ratio under a name:** the Custom row of the Aspect Ratio menu gets a Name field and **Save**. The ratio goes into the menu under that name and is applied. There is no limit on how many you keep, and saving under an existing name (in any case) replaces that ratio where it is.
- **Saved ratios in the menu:** they are listed below the built-in ratios. Picking one locks the crop to it, and the aspect button shows its name.
- **Edit List:** a button at the bottom of the menu switches it into an edit mode. You can move saved ratios up or down, delete them, and untick built-in ratios to hide them. Free and Original always stay. The menu stays open while you edit, and **Done** goes back to the normal list. Picking a ratio still closes the menu.
