title: Brush mask: one stroke densifies into at most a million dabs (#1520)
author: lincleejun
body:
Fixes #1520. A brush stroke with a few dozen points could take an export to gigabytes of memory, and a few thousand points exhaust it.

## Cause

`push_dabs` (`crates/pipeline/src/masks.rs`) densifies each segment of a stroke so dabs overlap, and caps one segment at a million in-between dabs. Nothing bounded the stroke as a whole, so the cap multiplied across the point list. `brush_dabs` collects every segment into one vector. The `MAX_DABS_CONSIDERED` guard in `spots.rs` runs only after that vector exists, and the GPU's `MAX_DABS` check also runs after `brush_dabs`.

Reproduced with the release CLI on main (`a82a001d`): import a 480x320 JPEG, add a brush mask, and stroke it with points that alternate between x = -1000 and x = 1000 (`size: 0.0001`), then export.

| Points in the stroke | Script size | Dabs | Peak memory on main | With this branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | < 1 KB | 1 M | 76 MB | 78 MB |
| 16 | < 1 KB | 15 M | 523 MB | not measured |
| 64 | 1.3 KB | 63 M | 2.06 GB | 74 MB |
| 1024 | 14 KB | ~1 G (projected) | not run (about 32 GB by the linear trend) | 78 MB |

```jsonl
{"command":"mask.add","params":{"kind":"brush"}}
{"command":"mask.brushStroke","params":{"points":[[-1000,0.5],[1000,0.5],…],"size":0.0001}}
{"command":"app.export","params":{"path":"out.jpg"}}
```

`lightcraft-cli run --import photo.jpg --script stroke.jsonl`, measured with `/usr/bin/time -l`. A stroke saved in a catalog, an XMP sidecar or a preset gets the same treatment wherever the mask is rendered: preview, thumbnails and export.

## What changed

- New `MAX_STROKE_DABS` (1,000,000, the old per-segment figure). `push_dabs` now caps a segment's in-between dabs at the stroke's remaining budget, `MAX_STROKE_DABS - dabs.len()`. A stroke therefore holds at most a million interpolated dabs plus one per sample: 16 MB of points instead of an unbounded vector.
- Every sample is still stamped, so a stroke over budget still ends where it was drawn. Past the budget, it paints its samples …

author: wstock
body:
Fixes #1752

## Before
`develop.auto` (Photo ▸ Auto Settings, ⇧A, the Auto button) always took `active(s)` and edited that one photo through `edit()`, whatever the selection. Applying Auto to a shoot meant pressing ⇧A on every photo in turn.

title: Crop: a fresh crop starts locked to the photo's own shape (#991)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #991

## Before
`ui.crop_default_aspect` already remembers the last aspect chosen explicitly (a ratio, Original, or "free" after the Lock is switched off), across photos and launches. But until something has been chosen it is `None`, and `None` meant *free*: on a fresh library every crop started unlocked, which is the friction the issue describes — re-engaging the Lock before every handle drag. Lightroom Classic starts with the padlock engaged, locked to Original.

## Change
`None` ("nothing chosen yet") now means *locked to the photo's own shape*, in the two places that read it (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`):
- `crop_tool_aspect()` — what the Lock button, the ratio label and the handles use — treats `None` as `"original"` (the orientation-aware W×H already handled for that value);
- `begin_crop()` applies the same default when a drag starts on an untouched photo.

Everything explicit is unchanged: the Lock switched off once is remembered as `"free"` (so cropping stays free from then on), a chosen ratio or Original is remembered as before, a photo that already has a crop keeps its own aspect, and a remembered value the command refuses is still dropped so the drag goes ahead. No new preference: one Lock toggle is the opt-out, and it sticks. Doc on the field in `state.rs`; parity row LR-CROP-ASPECT notes it.

## Tests
- New `tests_masking::a_fresh_crop_starts_locked_to_original_until_the_lock_is_switched_off`: with nothing chosen, the Lock shows engaged on an untouched photo and a handle drag keeps the photo's proportions (`crop.aspect` = its own W×H) without recording a choice; undo restores the photo; after one Lock toggle (`"free"` remembered) a drag crops with no ratio.

title: Fix/Crop rotate follows the pointer and keeps the drawn crop.
author: squareSphere29
body:
## Summary

Dragging outside the crop box rotates the crop the way the pointer moves, keeps the rectangle you drew, and no longer snaps to ±45° when the drag crosses the left of the box.

Geom still rotates about the photo centre (XMP / `crop_quad_norm`); an off-centre overlay can still sweep. That is not this PR.

Fixes #1794.

## What actually changed

1. **Pointer direction.** `CropRotate` added the atan2 delta instead of subtracting it, so the box turned opposite the drag. Straighten angle is a correction, so it has to run against the pointer's turn.
2. **Drawn crop kept (the rest of #1794).** Each `crop.straighten` step was measured against the previous step's shrunken rect, so a crop drawn in from the edges grew back toward the whole photo. The rotate drag, Straighten slider, and Angle-field drag pass `from` as the crop at press.
3. **Handle stays a handle.** Which handle was grabbed is taken from `press_origin`, not the first drag sample. Past the 12 px hit radius the live position missed the handle and the drag became a rotate into the ±45° clamp.
4. **atan2 wrap.** `Vec2::angle()` is in (-π, π]. Dragging down or up the left of the box crosses ±π; raw `a - a0` jumped by ~2π and the clamp snapped to ±45°. `shortest_turn` keeps the sign.
5. **Pointer origin.** Angle is measured about the overlay's corner centroid at press, not `map.screen(rect.center())` (that maps a straightened-frame point as image coords).
6. **The grow-back asked about the wrong angle (review fix).** Item 2 decided whether the crop the drag began on was "the largest of its aspect" by comparing it against the fitted crop at `self.angle`, the angle the crop had *reached*. On the first step the two agree; after that the drawn crop is never "the largest", so the grow-back stopped and the crop came home shrunk. `from` now carries the angle the crop was drawn at: `{rect: [x0, y0, x1, y1], angle}`, the shape `crop.set` already takes, instead of a bare rect. A rect without its angle is ignored rat…

title: LR-MERGE-HDR: click the merge preview to zoom in, drag to pan
author: mattsivak
body:
## What

The Photo Merge dialog's preview (HDR, Panorama, HDR Panorama) can now be zoomed like Lightroom's:

- **Click** zooms in on the point clicked: one preview pixel per screen pixel, and at least twice the fitted size (the preview is ≤ 1024 px, so at plain 1:1 it would barely grow in the 520×360 box).
- **Drag** pans while zoomed in. The image always covers the box; a wide panorama shorter than the box stays centred vertically.
- **Click again** fits it back.
- The zoom **stays while options change**, so deghost levels or projections can be compared at the same spot. It resets when the dialog opens.
- The cursor shows zoom-in at fit, grab / grabbing when zoomed.

## How

- `crates/ui-egui/src/merge.rs`: `MergeState.zoom` (the point at the box's middle, `None` = fit); a pure `preview_rect()` for the placement and clamping; `preview_input()` for click / drag / cursor. The preview box senses click-and-drag, and the image is painted clipped to the box.
- Docs: `docs/merge.md`, LR-MERGE-HDR row in `docs/parity-checklist.md`.

## Tests

- Unit: `the_preview_fits_until_clicked`, `a_click_zooms_in_on_the_point_clicked`, `a_zoomed_preview_stays_over_the_box`.

title: HEIF: bound aggregate decoded grid pixels (#1518)
author: justinjohn0306
body:
## What changed
Preflight every HEVC grid tile and sum its probed pixel count before parallel decode starts. Reject grids whose collective decoded tile area exceeds `Options::max_pixels`; this bounds the aggregate tile frames instead of only checking each tile individually. Add a synthetic regression where the cropped output fits the limit but the decoded tiles exceed it.

Refs #1518. The aggregate-grid budget portion is addressed here; the separate uncropped-SPS allocation path remains open.

## Verification
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-heif` (25 passed)
- `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-heif --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: LR-MERGE-HDR: sharp handheld HDR merges (Lanczos-3 warps, full-size and local alignment)
author: mattsivak
body:
## The problem

HDR merges of handheld brackets came out visibly softer than any single frame, with doubled detail. Measured on a real Sony bracket (33 MP, Schönbrunn: gravel a few metres away, the Gloriette ~1 km off) and on a new full-size synthetic test, the causes were:

1. **Bilinear resampling.** Every warp (HDR alignment, panorama projection, Boundary Warp) sampled bilinearly. At a half-pixel offset that is a [½ ½] filter: it keeps cos²(πf) of a pattern's fine detail, a third at 0.3 cycles per pixel.
2. **Alignment found on ≤ 1200 px versions only.** On a 24–60 MP frame that is 5–8× smaller, and a tenth of a work pixel is most of a full pixel.
3. **A frame too clipped to align was merged unaligned.** A +2 EV frame over half clipped gave the small-version features nothing to match, and it was merged as it was, 6 px off on the synthetic bracket.
4. **One homography for the whole frame.** Handheld, the camera also moves, so near and far things shift differently (parallax). On the real bracket the fit, dominated by the foreground gravel, left the building **2.3 px** off: its inscription was doubled.

## Changes

- **`lightcraft_raster::sample`:** a Lanczos-3 point sampler (tabulated taps), each sample held to the range of the 4 × 4 pixels around it so hard edges (clipped highlights, stars) don't ring. Used by `align::warp`, the panorama projection and Boundary Warp.
- **`crates/merge/src/refine.rs`:** the small-version alignment is refined at full size.
  - **Patches:** one 48 px patch at the most textured spot (smaller structure-tensor eigenvalue) of each of ~24 cells along the long edge.
  - **Matching:** masked normalised cross-correlation over the pixels usable in both frames (clipped ones aren't), with a sub-pixel peak; ambiguous and textureless patches are dropped.
  - **Fit:** RANSAC at 0.75 px, choosing the simplest of translation / similarity / homography as `align_pair` does.
  - **Recovery:** a frame the small versions couldn't align is recovered the s…

title: Masks: bound the total dabs of one brush stroke (#1520)
author: bogusyogi
body:
Fixes #1520. `push_dabs` limited each segment to 1 million dabs, but many large segments could still grow a stroke without bound. This change caps each stroke at `MAX_STROKE_DABS` (2 million centres, 32 MiB of point data).

Live painting now retains its emitted-dab count across frames, so its temporary buffers obey the same stroke budget as committed masks. Rejected samples leave position & pressure state unchanged; later frames cannot reconnect discarded samples.

Validation at `4d8f93585acbd4f20923250bd6de454ec1165f45` on Ubuntu 24.04 / Rust 1.98.0:

- 18 pipeline mask tests & 5 live-brush tests passed with `--locked`; `Cargo.lock` stayed unchanged.
- Restoring the original stamping helper/import while retaining the new regression reproduces the failure. Restoring exact candidate source passes.
- Regressions cover the whole-stroke limit, equivalent batch/incremental placement, pressure state & no additional coverage after exhaustion.

[Hosted run & downloadable evidence](https://github.com/bogusyogi/thiserror/actions/runs/39046865867). These are focused crate tests; this run does not establish full-workspace or platform coverage.

AI-assisted contribution using Claude Code & Codex.

title: JPEG XL: check dimensions during loading & bound tracked allocations (#1517)
author: bogusyogi
body:
Fixes #1517.

Initialize JPEG XL decoding with 4 KiB feeds, check image dimensions before rendering, then load remaining frames with bounded feeds until the final frame. `AllocTracker` limits tracked decoder allocations to 128 bytes per allowed pixel, with a 64 MiB minimum. This is a tracked-allocation budget; it does not cover every internal decoder allocation.

Bounded post-header feeds also avoid copying an entire trailing payload into jxl-oxide's untracked input buffer. Keep the builder's final-frame, partial-image & metadata behavior.

Validation on Ubuntu with Rust 1.98.0:
- Reviewer's 8×8 image plus 1 MiB tail: original PR peak **1,063,598 bytes**, base **22,128 bytes**, repaired source **18,920 bytes**; 128 KiB regression limit passes.
- Codec suite: **120 passed, 1 existing ignored** with default features.
- Added dimension-limit, final-feed metadata & progressive truncation comparisons. New encoder-dependent tests are native-only.
- [Before/after logs & test evidence](https://github.com/bogusyogi/thiserror/actions/runs/39044032276). Final follow-up changes only comments & the new test's WASM guard; production code & native test bodies are unchanged.

AI-assisted contribution using Claude Code & Codex.

title: HEIF: max_pixels on uncropped SPS sizes and grid totals (#1518)
author: bogusyogi
body:
Fixes #1518. heic-rs allocates each picture at its SPS's uncropped size, and a slice may select an SPS other than the first. \`max_pixels\` was checked against the declared size, and each frame only after decoding, while a grid held all its tiles at once.

\`Coded::decode\` now reads every SPS of every tile first (\`vui::coded_sizes\`, sharing the SPS reader \`vui\` already had):
- each uncropped size must fit \`max_pixels\`;
- the tiles together must fit \`2 × max_pixels\`;
- an unreadable SPS is \`Malformed\`.

Regression \`grid_tiles_are_held_to_the_pixel_budget_together\`: a 33×33 grid of four 32×32 tiles is refused at 1089 pixels and decodes at 2048.

Already in Ember (Orthic-Labs/ember#17, green on macOS and Windows); offered here in case it is useful.

author: mattsivak
body:
## What
The HDR, Panorama and HDR Panorama merge dialogs now open with the options of the last merge of that kind instead of the defaults, and those options survive a restart.

## Why
The last options were already recorded (`MergeState::last`), but only in memory and only read by "… with Last Settings"; opening a merge dialog always reset everything to the defaults.

## How
- `Session::last_merge` (per command → options JSON) is persisted in the library's `prefs.json`, next to `last_export`.
- `merge::last_options()` in the UI deserializes it (missing fields → defaults, unreadable → defaults) and is used by the dialogs, "… with Last Settings" and HDR for Each Bracket Set. Options are saved when a merge starts, not on Cancel.
- `MergeState::last` is removed.

## Tests
- `tests_prefs::last_merge_settings_persist_with_the_library`: round-trip through close/reopen.
- `tests_activity::merge_dialog_remembers_the_last_settings_per_kind`: a started merge prefills the next dialog of that kind; other kinds open with defaults; partial or junk settings fall back.
- `cargo xtask ci` green locally.

title: Plain labels are no longer drag-selectable, as in Lightroom
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1885.

The labels that highlight are plain egui `Label`s, and egui makes every label drag-selectable by default (`style.interaction.selectable_labels`). `theme::apply_kind` never turned that off, so any caption or heading drawn as a label could be selected, while the ones painted straight onto the panel could not, which is the mix the video shows. This sets `selectable_labels = false` in the theme, next to the other style tweaks, so labels behave like Lightroom's static text. Text that is meant to be copied keeps working where the code already asks for it: the Lightroom import result dialog marks the destination library path and its details `.selectable(true)`, and the explicit flag wins over the style default. (The toast is painted again since #1262 was reverted, so it isn't affected either way.)

One thing to note: the System Info values were selectable only through the default, so they no longer are; that dialog already has a Copy to Clipboard button. If there are other places where copying text by hand matters (error details, metadata values), I'm happy to mark those `.selectable(true)` here, or to switch to a narrower approach.

body:
Addresses part of #1300. title: LRC-PRINT-PAGE: Page Options print page numbers, page info and crop marks (gap 15)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Print: Page Options for page numbers, page info and crop marks (LRC-PRINT-PAGE, gap 15)

In Lightroom Classic, Page Options sit in the Print module's Page panel. They are offered for Single Image and Contact Sheet. Page Numbers prints the number at the bottom right of each page, Page Info prints the print settings (sharpening, profile, printer) along the bottom, and Crop Marks prints cut guides just outside the corners of each photo. The packages get Cut Guides (Lines / Crop Marks) in that place instead. This PR adds the three options as `print.set {page: {pageNumbers, pageInfo, cropMarks}}`. They are saved with templates, have checkboxes in the Print dialog's Page section (hidden for the packages, as in Lightroom), show in the preview and are composed into the PDF. A PDF has no printer to name, so the info line ends with the resolution where Lightroom names the printer. The marks are 0.25 in long, sit 1/16 in from the corner and are 0.5 pt wide. The text is 9 pt. Both are black, or white on a dark background. On narrow paper, Page Info shrinks to fit beside the page number, down to 6 pt, and is then cut short with an ellipsis. A crop mark stops 1/16 in short of the page text, so a photo that fills the printable area doesn't put its bottom marks through the footer. Marks never cover a photo, their own or a neighbour's. The preview draws all of this with the same rules as the PDF. I picked those values myself; Adobe's help doesn't give them. Happy to switch any of them. Identity plate, watermark (on the page; #1499 is the export watermark and doesn't overlap), photo info captions and the packages' Cut Guides are left for follow-ups. The new labels go through `tr()` like the rest of the Print dialog, which no catalogue translates yet. The info line is drawn in English, like other engine output.

title: LR-META-XMP: Write automatic XMP sidecars off the UI thread in the desktop app
author: endthestart
body:
With automatic XMP writing on, each edit wrote its sidecar inside the command, and a write reads the folder listing and the existing packet before the atomic write. On my NAS over SMB that's about 330 ms per edit (12 ms locally), and seconds over a VPN, so every rating or slider change held up the window. This is the part of the UI-thread disk access from emmertex/lightcraft-classic#123 that lives in the shared engine.

The desktop app now turns on a background writer (`Session::set_background_sidecar_writes`). Auto-writes go to one writer thread, and a photo changed again before its write started only writes its newest packet. The CLI, MCP and tests keep writing in the command, so nothing changes there. Queued writes are finished before anything moves a photo's file (renames, moves, undoing a move, relinks), before Save or Read Metadata, and when the library closes. A write whose original is gone by the time it starts is skipped. A write that fails goes on the retry list from #1772 like before. Background writes are only used when no sidecar repair is pending, since the repair bookkeeping stays with the command path.

I added tests that rapid edits end in one sidecar with the newest rating, that a write queued just before a rename never lands at the old name, and that a failed background write waits for a retry. Thank you.

## What

A new setting, **Settings → Dialogs → Close a dialog by clicking outside it**. It is **off by default**, so the current behaviour (and `modal_dialogs_block_background_clicks_and_preserve_choices`) is unchanged.

When it is on, a click on the dimmed backdrop around a dialog closes it the same way Esc does (Export, Settings, Rename, Create Album, About, …). Some clicks deliberately keep the dialog open:

- the click must be pressed **and** released outside the window, so a drag that ends outside (e.g. the Quality slider pulled past the edge) doesn't close it;
- a press while a popup is open (a dropdown such as Preset / Resize to, a date picker) only closes that popup;
- only a press made while the dialog is shown counts, so the click that opened the dialog never closes it;
- the import review never closes this way, so its hand-picked photos are safe;
- the click doesn't reach the panels below, which stay disabled as before.

## How

All dialogs go through `panels::dialogs::show`, so it is one helper, `clicked_backdrop`, called after the window is drawn. It reads the press and release positions from the raw `Event::PointerButton` events because egui 0.36 clears `press_origin` / `press_start_time` on release, and a quick click on a slow frame can press and release in the same frame. Clicks only count once the dialog was already on screen the frame before, so the click that opened it never closes it.

## Tests

- New: `tests_dialogs::a_click_outside_closes_the_dialog_when_settings_allow_it`. It covers off by default → stays open, a click inside → stays open, a drag from inside to outside → stays open, a backdrop click → closes without reaching the rating stars below, and the click that opens a dialog (press and release in one frame) → stays open. It fails with the call disabled.

title: Hasselblad FFF: colour matrix from the embedded 3FR header
author: 06needhamt
body:
An FFF (a 3FR converted on the desktop) has no colour matrix of its own: the camera's stays in the original 3FR header the FFF carries as a complete TIFF in private IFD0 tag 0xC51B. RGGB checked against the camera preview on the CC0 H4D-40 FFF and CFV 3FR (raw.pixls.us 931 and 709). Synthetic tests cover the embedded matrix, an own matrix winning, a missing or damaged header, and truncated files.

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: CRX high-frequency band width from the tile geometry …
author: pehonnet
body:
Fixes #899.

The CRX decoder tried each high-frequency band at its synthesis width and up to two more columns, keeping the first width whose entropy stream ended exactly. #899 shows two widths can both do that and give different coefficients.

**Measurement.** I traced every C-RAW plane in `cr3_corpus.rs` (CC0 raw.pixls.us files): each band decodes at exactly one width. A tile with a neighbour on its right codes bands 5 and 8 (the vertical high-pass of the level-2 and level-1 low-pass columns) at an odd width, so an even band gains one unused column. No other band is extended. Two-tile files: G5 X Mark II, M50, R100, 250D, RP, R, 90D, M6 Mark II. Single-tile 0x100 and 0x200 files never extend a band.

**Change.**
- `coded_band_width()` takes the width from that rule. A stream that does not fit it is a corrupt-data error, so the CR3 falls back to its embedded preview as before.
- Unit tests cover the measured cases and a stream that decodes at both 2 and 3 columns (the old probe took 2; the geometry takes 3).
- The `crx_properties.rs` encoder codes bands 5 and 8 the same way.
- `docs/cr3.md` documents the rule.

**Verification.** `cargo xtask ci` is green, and all `cr3_corpus.rs` sensor hashes are unchanged.

**Not verified.** No public file has a middle tile (three or more C-RAW tiles); it is assumed to follow the left-tile rule.

Clean-room: established by black-box measurement of the CC0 files only; no third-party decoder source was consulted.

title: Do not read a sibling's shared stem sidecar on import (#1905)
author: fanyzp
body:
Fixes #1905 (from Discord, reported by Valpurgius, Windows 11, v0.8.0).

## The bug

With the default Stem naming, `IMG_0001.xmp` is the sidecar of every file of that stem, and in a folder Lightroom has worked on it is the raw's. On import the packet was looked up with the library naming alone (`find_sidecar(&path, self.naming)`), which is the case radialmonster already described in #92: a TIFF or JPEG arriving beside a raw of the same name read the raw's packet, and took its rating, label, keywords and `crs:` develop settings onto a file that is not the raw.

## The change

An import now ranks the files it is adding as if they were catalogued already, in the order `StemOwners` uses for writing (a raw first, then the file name in lower case), with the library's files and the arriving ones ranked together:

- `crates/engine/src/sidecar.rs`: `ImportStems` (`for_import`, `owns`) and `find_sidecar_for_import`. A file that does not own its stem sidecar reads only its own `<file>.xmp` (`IMG_0001.TIF.xmp`), never the sibling's `IMG_0001.xmp`. A file that is not catalogued yet has no id, and the id it draws when the import commits is above every id in the library, so it loses a tie against a catalogued file; between arriving files the order they arrive in stands for it. The library is passed over once per import, and only the stems the arriving files map to are looked at closer (`StemOwners::where_wanted` does the same for a write). Also `rank_of` (the rank the two rules share) and `xmp_cases` (one definition of the `.xmp`/`.XMP`/`.Xmp` trio).
- `crates/engine/src/import.rs`: `look_up_library` hands the snapshot of the library back, `prepare_files` works the ownership out once before the files are planned, and the packet is read through `find_sidecar_for_import`. Folder synchronize and the Lightroom catalog import go through `prepare_files` too, so a file arriving there is ranked the same way.

title: Library: a cropped photo's thumbnail reads the source its crop needs, so tight crops stay sharp
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1918.

The reporter's guess is right. `Session::build_job` picked a grid thumbnail's source level from the thumbnail size alone (512 px at most), while the loupe sizes its source from the crop since #323 (`source_edge_needed`). So a cropped photo's thumbnail was cut from a 512 px source, or right after editing from the loupe's preview shrunk to 512 px, and then stretched back up: a crop to 20 % of each side became about 100 px stretched to 512.

Thumbnails now look at the same `source_edge_needed`, with two limits so the grid stays cheap:
- up to a 2x stretch, they keep the thumbnail source as before. A slight crop or a straightened horizon costs nothing more, and at the 512 px size only crops tighter than about half the long edge read more.
- past that, they read the preview level, decoded at the size the crop needs (at most 2560 px, never the original). If the preview is already in memory, as right after an edit, the thumbnail is cut from it.

A thumbnail's preview-sized source doesn't go into the session's preview cache (new `RenderJob::discard_source`). So the filmstrip's cropped neighbours don't push the photo being edited out of it, and the rendered thumbnail goes to the disk cache as before. The thumbnail cache key now includes the level when it isn't the thumbnail one: blurry thumbnails already cached for tight crops render again, and the rest stay valid.

This revisits a trade-off #323 made on purpose ("grid thumbnails of tight crops stay cheap"), so cc @nledford: tell me if you'd rather keep it as it was. The 2x threshold is a judgement call: crops between 50 % and ~98 % stay up to 2x soft in the grid. Happy to switch to a tighter threshold, or to use the preview only when it is already in memory.

Validation:
- `media::tests::a_tight_crops_thumbnail_is_as_sharp_as_the_crop_rendered_at_its_size`: compares neighbour-pixel detail of a 20 % crop's 512 px thumbnail with the same crop rendered at 512 px by the loupe path, from a 2 px stripe preview. Fail…

title: LR-BEHAV-BG-TASKS: a second preview build waits in line for the first, and a task that did not go well can be retried (stacked on #1649)
author: nledford
body:
Stacked on #1649 (which is stacked on #1642 and #1711). The first step towards a queue for background tasks: one lane, the preview builds, so the machinery has a real user from the start. Imports, Synchronize Folder, moves and exports follow in later PRs.

Why stacked: its line of waiting jobs and its Retry button need the finished rows from #1711 (`Outcome::failed`, `Ending`, `Finished` in `crates/engine/src/activity.rs`; a retry is a failed row that kept its request, `Finished::retryable`, `Activity::retry`) and edit the list that #1649 draws (`panels/activity.rs`: the "Waiting" group, the waiting row, the Retry link, `Rows`, `Act`) and the bell's line (`readout_parts`), so it can't be built without them.

## Problem

Only one preview build can run at a time. While one ran, File ▸ Previews greyed out Build Standard-Sized Previews, Build 1:1 Previews and Build / Discard Smart Previews, and an agent's second `library.buildPreviews` was refused ("a preview build is already running"). To build previews for two sets of photos, you had to wait for the first build, come back, and select the second set again. A build that stopped or failed for some photos could only be run again by selecting the same photos and asking again.

## Change

**Lanes and a line** (`crates/engine/src/activity.rs`):
- Jobs that must not run side by side share a `Lane`. There is one so far, `Previews`: Build Previews and Build / Discard Smart Previews in the background.
- One asked for while its lane is busy can wait in line (`Activity::enqueue`) instead of being refused. It keeps what it was asked (`Request`: the command and its parameters), with everything that depends on the moment written out. For a preview build, that is the photos: it builds the photos chosen when it was asked, not the ones selected when its turn comes.
- `Session::start_waiting` starts the first waiting task whose lane is free. It runs after every command and every frame. The task runs its command then, so it plans its work…

title: raw: alias Canon EOS R6 Mark II to EOS R6m2
author: naryzach
body:
### Summary
Add Exif model alias `("Canon", "EOS R6 Mark II", "EOS R6m2")` to `spectral_table::ALIASES`.

---

### Rationale & Problem Description
In PR #1466, `EOS R6m2` spectral matrices were tested in the catalog using the mock camera string `"Canon Canon EOS R6m2"`.
However, real-world Canon EOS R6 Mark II camera firmware writes its Exif model tag as:
- `Make`: `"Canon"`
- `Model`: `"Canon EOS R6 Mark II"`

After stripping the make (`"Canon "`), `lightcraft_raw::spectral::find()` searches for `"EOS R6 Mark II"`. Because only `"EOS R6"` and `"EOS R6m2"` were present in the table without an alias mapping, the camera lookup returned `None`.

This prevented real Canon EOS R6 Mark II CR3 files from resolving their measured sensor color matrices (`ColorMatrix1/2`, `ForwardMatrix1/2`) and Kelvin white balance, causing files to fall back or display preview-only warnings. Adding this alias follows the existing convention already in place for `("Canon", "EOS R5 Mark II", "EOS R5m2")` and `("Canon", "EOS R8", "EOS R6m2")`.

---

#### 1. Canon In-Camera JPEG vs. Canon DPP Exports

title: LR-BEHAV-TOAST: toasts stack instead of replacing one another, and a new state replaces the old one
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`. PR 2 of the background-task queue work (#1933 is PR 1): once tasks start by themselves from a queue, their messages arrive close together, and with one toast slot each new one hid the last.

## Problem

The toast at the bottom of the photo view was a single slot: a new message replaced the one showing. Two messages close together (a label set as an export ends; an import finishing while a preview build ends) left only the second on screen, often before the first could be read. The before screenshot below is "Red Label", then "✓ Clear Preview Cache" a moment later: the first is gone.

## Change

**Toasts stack** (`crates/ui-egui/src/state.rs`, `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/mod.rs`):
- `UiState::toasts` replaces the single `UiState::toast`. It holds up to three, oldest first. `UiState::toast()` is the newest.
- `push_toast` adds one below those showing. Each fades out at its own time. A fourth pushes the oldest out.
- The newest is drawn exactly where the single toast always was: 60 pt from the bottom of the photo view, or from the top during a slideshow. The older ones stack above it (below it in a slideshow), 8 pt apart, and never past the view.
- Widgets `toast:0` (the newest), `toast:1`… are registered for scripts and tests.
- The same message again (same text, same label) is one toast that moves to the newest place and keeps the later of its two times.

**State messages replace the old state** (`push_toast_on` / `LightcraftApp::toast_on`, with a topic):

body:
## Process V3: bright saturated colours keep their saturation

> ⚠️ **Process number collision — needs a decision at integration.** This PR adds `Process::V3`, and so do at least ten other open PRs, each with a different meaning (Dehaze, colour / luminance NR, sharpening, Lightroom-calibrated Contrast, …: e.g. #1226, #1283, #1286, #1348, #1349, #1383, #1441, #1714, #762, #944). They don't conflict textually yet, but they will when merged. Whoever integrates needs to either renumber this to the next free process or fold several of these changes into one new process. Here the process-specific part is small: one arm in `GamutMap::of` (`crates/pipeline/src/finish.rs`), the `Process` variant in `crates/develop/src/settings.rs`, the `V2 | V3` arm in `local::tone_base_detail`, and one row in `docs/process-versions.md`.

### Problem
Bright, saturated orange highlights render pale. On a private EOS R10 C-RAW sunset, the halo around the sun came out salmon to white: 16 px means R 255 / G 152–194 / B 98–158, where the camera JPEG has R 255 / G 156–200 / B 18–33. Red and green matched, blue was lifted. It is not the raw white level, which was measured and ruled out separately.

### Cause
Two stages pulled the lowest channel towards luminance:
1. **The finish stage's gamut maps.** There is one after the tone map (display-linear Rec. 2020 above `peak`) and one into the output space. Both desaturate towards luminance. At (2600,1000) the colour before mapping is linear sRGB [1.125, 0.275, 0.027]; bringing red to 1 while keeping luminance and hue raises blue from 0.027 to 0.101 (8-bit 45 → 89).
2. **The camera-look chroma curve (`camera_preview::fit_chroma`).** It was fitted on predictions that were not gamut mapped, against a JPEG that is always in sRGB, so it read the sRGB limit as the camera bleaching highlights. Its nodes at 0.43–0.86 display luminance were 0.81–0.89, which lifted blue further before the map.

author: deunderscorepaul
body:
## What

The Tone Curve panel's **parametric** tab now draws the curve the renderer actually uses, and you drag the line itself.

1. `ParametricCurve` is the one curve that both the graph and `pipeline::finish::curve_luts` describe: the four region bumps summed, then forced monotone by the running maximum, sampled at the renderer's resolution. title: M12: SAM 3 on the CPU ~3x faster: encode ~37 → ~11 s, a description ~6 → ~2 s
author: helgehelge123
body:
On Linux and Windows SAM 3 runs on the CPU (#932 is the GPU route). On a 12-core Ryzen 9 3900X:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| encode a photo (backbone) | ~37 s | **~11 s** |
| get ready for clicks (`prepare_clicks`, tracker neck) | ~2.3 s | **~0.9 s** |
| a description (Describe / text prompt) | ~6 s | **~2.1 s** |
| the first description on a photo (+ detector neck) | ~8.8 s | **~2.9 s** |

The CPU path is the only one that changes. Metal keeps the tensor ops (`Layer::forward_tensors`, `nn::sdpa_tensors`, candle's `GroupNorm` / `ConvTranspose2d`).

### Where the time went

candle's CPU backend handles three kinds of work poorly here:

- **Elementwise ops and strided copies** run on one thread: bias add, `gelu_erf`, `relu`, the RoPE muls and adds, the `* scale` on attention scores, window partition, head split and merge, and the detector's box-bias broadcast, permute and pad.
- **Batched matmuls** run one batch element after another, each spread over all threads. That is slow for 144 windows × heads of 576 tokens.
- **`conv_transpose2d`** runs one output channel at a time, about 50 GFLOP/s here.

For the detector, the attention over 5184 tokens was worst: 8 heads of 32, with 4 MB score blocks that don't fit in the cache.

### What changed: `crates/segment/src/cpu.rs`, used only when the tensor is on the CPU

**Bit-identical (the same float operations in the same order, fused, run in parallel on rayon, the pool candle's matmuls use):**
- `linear_act` / `linear_add`: matmul, then bias + `gelu_erf` / `relu`, or bias + residual add, in one pass.
- `heads`: window partition, head split, bias and RoPE in one pass. It also applies the ViT's score scale to q instead of the scores; the scale is 1/8, so this is exact.
- The merge back to the grid.
- `box_bias`: the detector's box relative-position bias.
- `group_norm_relu`: the pixel decoder's GroupNorm + ReLU, with candle's f32 sums in candle's order.

**Changes rounding only:**
- `sdpa`: one task per (batch, head, b…

title: Merged develop settings are kept in range, as XMP import keeps them
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1946.

`DevelopSettings::merged()` is what `develop.merge`, `lightcraft-cli render --settings` and `preset.apply` all go through, but only `apply_partial` re-clamped the sliders afterwards, and nothing looked at curves or the crop. This moves that clean-up into `merged()` itself and extends it to what crs XMP import already does on the way in: every slider through its control spec (so `light.exposure: 1e308` becomes 5, `geometry.scale: 0` becomes 50), point-curve coordinates clamped to 0..1, and a crop with no area (inverted or zero-width edges) ignored, keeping the photo's previous crop, as XMP import ignores a crop whose right edge isn't past its left. An unrotated crop is also clipped to the photo. A turned crop can legitimately reach past 0..1 in the rotated frame, so I left that to the crop tools, which know the photo's size. JSON can't carry NaN or infinity, so there's nothing extra to do for those here; out-of-range numbers like `1e308` are covered by the clamps.

I went with clamping rather than refusing the JSON with an error, to match XMP import and the direct setters. Happy to switch to an error naming the field if you'd rather agents hear about it. Masks' own values are not touched by this change.

Validation:
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-develop --lib merged_settings_are_kept_in_range`: fails on main (exposure, vignette, scale and distortion stored as `1e308, -1e308, 0, 1e308`), passes here
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-develop --lib`, `cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib -- crs preset`
- `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-develop --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: M12: Describe selections from SAM 3's semantic mask: sure inside, no lines between instances
author: helgehelge123
body:
Describe now uses SAM 3's semantic mask around what it found, so its selections come out fully selected inside, with no line where two instances touch.

![Describe sky and mountains, before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helgehelge123/lightcraft/pr-assets-describe-semantic/describe-tetons-before-after.jpg)

*Ansel Adams, The Tetons and the Snake River (public domain), cropped from `docs/images/hero-tetons.jpg`. Columns: the mask before, its coverage before (white = 100 %), its coverage after, the mask after.*

### The problem
Describe merges the detector's per-instance masks, and those stay near 0 even well inside what they found. So an exposure or color change applied to a Describe mask landed only partly:
- a sky came out about 87 % selected;
- a volleyball net about 70 %;
- a person about 94 %.

Where two instances touch, both fade out, so a thin line showed between two people standing side by side.

### The change
- **The detector's semantic head is ported.** It is `semantic_projection` over the pixel decoder, the `semantic_seg` of the transformers implementation. It is a 1×1 convolution with one output channel, which is small next to the pixel decoder it follows.
- **Each found instance takes the semantic logits where it is the strongest instance and near.** "Near" means its own logit is above −4.
  - The instances found are the same as before (score above 0.5).
  - The semantic mask is sure inside and runs on across the boundary between two instances.
  - An instance keeps its own logits where it is surer of itself.
- **Far from every instance nothing changes**, so Describe never selects something it didn't find before.
- **Fallback.** Without a semantic mask (e.g. outputs built elsewhere), `merge` behaves exactly as before.

### Results
16 prompts on three photos: the landscape above and two indoor volleyball photos. The volleyball photos aren't attached because they show players.

| prompt | median coverage inside, before → after | area before …

title: LR-EXP-BITDEPTH: app.export refuses a bitDepth the format doesn't have
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1952 (point 3: unsupported `bitDepth`). Points 1, 2 and 4–6 are untouched; point 2 is what #1691 (thanks @FredApps) covers.

`ExportOptions::validate` only checked that `bitDepth` was one of 8/10/16/32, never whether the format has that depth, so `effective_depth` quietly fell back: `format=jpeg bitDepth=16` and `format=png bitDepth=10` wrote 8-bit files and returned `ok`, against the "a value of the wrong kind is an error, not a default" contract that #181/#183 set up. The check now uses `ExportOptions::bit_depths`, the same per-format table the Export dialog offers (like Lightroom's Export window, which only lists the depths each format has), and the error names them: ``"`bitDepth` must be 8 or 16 for png"``. The format checked is the one exported, resolved once by `ExportOptions::export_format`: `format`, else the one `path`'s extension names, else the caller's format for a path that names none (JPEG in the desktop app, PNG in the headless/MCP backend). `app.export` in both takes its format from there (`from_params` / `from_params_or`), and a preset's params are merged with the call's before its depth is judged (`Session::export_params_or`), so a depth is always checked against the format that is written.

AVIF and JPEG XL become strict too (AVIF 8/10, JPEG XL 8/16, as the dialog offers). Their other values never gave the depth asked for: every AVIF depth above 8 maps to the same 16-bit render, which `avif_10bit` writes at 10 bits (a trial `bitDepth=10` export has `pixi` 10/10/10), so `bitDepth=16`/`32` wrote that same 10-bit file; JPEG XL `10`/`32` went through `encode_image_16bit`, i.e. 16-bit integer.

Small follow-ons so nothing that worked stops working:
- `lightcraft-cli render -o out.tif --opt bitDepth=16` (documented in `docs/mcp.md`) passes the format from the output's extension before validating, so the check sees TIFF rather than the default JPEG.

title: crop.set refuses a crop smaller than the crop tool allows, instead of exporting 1×1
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1952 (point 1, the zero-area crop). Point 3 is in #1966; points 2, 4, 5 and 6 are untouched.

`crop.set` only sorted the rect, so `[0.5,0.5,0.5,0.5]` (or a sliver like `[0.2,0.2,0.2,0.8]`) was stored and the next export came out 1×1. It now refuses a rect whose side is under `MIN_CROP_FRACTION` of the shorter side, the same minimum a drag of the crop tool already enforces, and keeps the crop the photo had. The check runs on the requested rect and again on the crop it becomes once constrained to the photo, so a rect far larger than the photo (`[0, 0, 1e6, 1]`) can't shrink into a sliver either; a huge rect that fits as a full-size crop is still accepted. I went with an error rather than growing the rect to the minimum because the caller is an agent or a script and a silent change is harder to notice; happy to switch to clamping if you prefer.

The degenerate-crop robustness tests from #1560 and #1813 set their crops through `crop.set`; they now store them directly, as a sidecar could, so they still cover the render, loupe and `crop.rotateAspect` paths.

title: Control port: require a per-run token before any request
author: LochLogic
body:
The `--control` server binds to 127.0.0.1, which keeps other machines out, but any process on the same machine that reaches the port can run any command (move or delete folders, export, quit). FilmCraft has the same gap tracked in storytold/filmcraft#163 (PR storytold/filmcraft#1172); PhotoCraft already closes it with an `auth` handshake. This brings LightCraft in line with PhotoCraft.

### What changes

- Every control connection must open with `{"method": "auth", "params": {"token": "<64 hex>"}}`. Anything else (another method, a missing or wrong token, an HTTP request line) gets one error reply and the connection is closed. The reply never contains the token, and the compare is constant-time.
- The app uses `--control-token HEX` or `LIGHTCRAFT_CONTROL_TOKEN` when given, otherwise 32 bytes from the OS random source (`getrandom` 0.3, already in the lockfile) for each run.
- The app writes the token to `control-token-<port>` in the settings folder (mode 0600 on Unix). I chose a file over printing it because Windows release builds use the GUI subsystem, so stderr goes nowhere there. Without a settings folder the token goes to stderr once.
- `lightcraft-cli run --connect` and `lightcraft-cli mcp --connect` send `LIGHTCRAFT_CONTROL_TOKEN` or the token in that file for the port they connect to, look it up again on each reconnect (so an app restarted with a new token is still found), and report a refused token as "refused the connection: wrong control token" instead of "not reachable".
- `docs/showcase/run.py` authenticates the same way.
- After answering, the server now closes a connection gracefully (FIN, then drains what the client already sent, bounded in bytes and time). On Windows a plain close with unread input resets the connection, and the reset could discard the error reply, so a client saw "connection reset" instead of "authentication required".

title: Tone: neutral display tone map is the identity up to white (#1945)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #1945

## Cause

`ToneMap::display_hdr` (through `ToneMap::display`, the tone map for JPEG, PNG and other display-referred sources) ran its SDR short shoulder (`o > 0.95`: slope 1 at 0.95, reaching 1.0 at 1.05) even with Contrast, Whites and Blacks at 0. Display-linear 1.0 came out as 0.9875 (sRGB 253.6 → 254), so an unedited export darkened neutral 255, 254 and 253 by one level, against the module's "identity at neutral settings" and the README's pixel-exact pass-through. The tests didn't see it: the identity test stopped at 0.95, and the ramp round trip allowed an error of 3 and never contains a neutral near-white.

## Fix

- With neutral sliders the curve is the identity up to white; values pushed above white (exposure) clip at 1.0. CPU and GPU both take the table from `finish::base_tone`.
- Edited curves (any of Contrast, Whites, Blacks ≠ 0) keep the shoulder unchanged, so photos edited under V1 keep their look; `docs/process-versions.md` notes the in-place fix and why it isn't a new process.

- `tone::tests::display_identity_and_monotone` now runs to 1.0 (tolerance 1e-3, the LUT's interpolation next to the clip, far below one 8-bit level) and checks that neutral values above white clip. It failed before the fix (`0.96 -> 0.9594901`).
- New `tests::unedited_neutral_near_whites_are_passthrough` renders the issue's neutral greys (255, 254, 253, 252, 250, 240, 200, 128, 0) and needs them back exactly. Before the fix: `[254, 253, 252, 252, 250, …]`, the issue's table.
- `tests::unedited_rendered_source_is_passthrough` now needs an exact round trip (was `≤ 3`).

title: GPU: recover safely after readback timeouts (#1948)
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
A GPU readback that exceeds 60 seconds currently disables GPU rendering for the rest of the process, even when the device is healthy. This change falls back to the CPU for that render, drains its outstanding GPU submission, and automatically allows later renders to use the same device again. Fixes #1948.

The wait targets the readback's exact submission. On timeout, destroying the staging buffer cancels its map while wgpu retains submitted resource uses until completion. Pending submissions retain shutdown accounting and are polled without blocking before another GPU render is admitted. Failed cached stages are discarded and later stages stop submitting. Profiling waits use the same bounded path, including submissions already flushed. Device loss, map failures, invalid submission indices and validation errors remain fatal.

Validation:

- Apple M1 Pro / Metal: a 96 × 64 procedural regression recovers from four injected timeouts after real submission/map requests, without resetting failures. Each recovered image has 0.000 LSB mean RGB difference from the CPU. Includes early dehaze readbacks, pooled-buffer reuse and `LIGHTCRAFT_PROFILE=1`.
- Real `device.destroy()` remains fatal, including destruction with a pending timeout ticket, `reset_failures`, and another thread. The destructive control runs in its own test executable. Restoring only the old fatal timeout classification compiles but fails the intended regression assertion; restoring the fix passes.
- Deterministic lifecycle tests cover independent pending submissions, shutdown accounting, invalid indices and driver-poll panic containment. A tiny four-word profiling test confirms that `sync` waits after a flush consumed its encoder. Rust 1.99.1 Metal/denoise suite: 56 reported passes, zero failures, five ignored; existing fallback controls pass. Independent review has no unresolved findings.
- Workspace tests on Rust 1.99.1: 4,121 reported passes, zero failures, 35 ignored. Optional-data gaps produced 137 corpus,…

title: Tests: fix the 11 Windows-only test failures on main
author: LochLogic
body:
On Windows 11 (MSVC, Rust 1.99.1), `cargo test --workspace` on main (0da998f2) fails 11 tests. None of them is a product bug; all are test assumptions that only hold on Unix:

- **`tests_export::same_folder_as_original_exports_next_to_each_photo`** built its expected paths with `Path::join`, which uses `\` on Windows, but export joins the subfolder and file name with `/` on every platform (`join_path`). The test now expects exactly what export writes.
- **`tests_folder_drop` (all 8 tests)** looked Folders rows up as `source:libfolder:C:\Users\...`, while the Folders section names them with `/` (`source:libfolder:C:/Users/...`), so no row was ever found. A small `folder_key` helper builds the id the same way.
- **`lightcraft-mcp` `backend::tests::{valid_replies_and_errors_are_preserved, malformed_replies_are_rejected_without_resending}`** pass alone but fail whenever the whole crate runs (`An existing connection was forcibly closed by the remote host` at the fake server's last read). Bisecting showed the trigger is the tests that start a copy of the test binary (`server::progress::shutdown_tests::*` and `tests::a_one_shot_process_never_ends_during_a_photos_import`): skipping them makes the failures go away. My reading is that the child inherits a socket the fake server just accepted, and when the child exits Windows closes its copy abortively, which resets the test's connection. A test-only lock (`serial_sockets_and_children`) keeps socket tests and child-process tests from overlapping: the crate passed 6 of 6 whole-crate runs, against 0 of 4 before.

With this, `cargo test --workspace` on Windows passes 4100 tests with one exception, `control_server::tests::tcp_connection_is_closed_after_junk`, which fails intermittently because the server closes a socket with unread input and Windows resets it; #1970 fixes that in the server with a graceful close, so I left it out of this test-only change. Clippy on Windows needs #1967.

title: GUM-3201: Reduce guided-filter coefficient allocations
author: ternarybits
body:
## Summary

The CPU fast guided filter currently expands both reduced coefficient planes to full resolution before applying them. Sample those coefficients with bounded row scratch instead, preserving the existing resizer weights and accumulation order. The full-resolution base returned to downstream stages remains unchanged, as do median detail filtering, process selection, and the GPU implementation.

Add exact comparisons against the prior algorithm and a reproducible, dev-only allocation benchmark. This is a focused CPU memory improvement, with a measured time tradeoff rather than a claim of faster rendering.

## Allocation and timing

| Isolated 24 MP filter, one Rayon thread | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Peak requested heap bytes | 289,125,000 | 97,780,856 |
| Total allocated bytes | 313,083,488 | 135,643,856 |
| Minimum wall time, 15 calls | 42.135 ms | 45.131 ms |

The peak reduction is about 191 MB (66%). Both peaks include the 96 MB returned base and exclude the already allocated input. RGB images, log luminance, median construction, other spatial planes, and application caches are outside this measurement. Timings came from a shared machine with concurrent builds; the approximately 7% difference is preliminary. The example and documentation explain how to reproduce allocation and unprofiled timing separately.

## Validation

- Pipeline tests: 193 passed, 2 existing ignored; new regressions exactly match the previous algorithm across sizes, edges, filter steps, and median radii.

title: GUM-3203: Stress-test previews against full-size renders
author: ternarybits
body:
## Summary

Same-size CPU/GPU equivalence does not show how closely a reduced preview predicts a full-size render. Add procedural stress cases that compare 800 and 1440 px previews with full-size U8 sRGB renders reduced afterward in linear light. Fine texture, hard boundaries, strong tone edits, and sources at or beyond the guided-filter subsampling cap exercise a different failure mode from the existing equivalence tests.

No production rendering changes are included. These are calibrated fixture bounds, not a promise of pixel parity for arbitrary photographs, export codecs, or resamplers.

## Cases and sensitivity

| Procedural source | Preview | Mean RGB code error | p99 of per-pixel maximum RGB error |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 3200 x 192 | 800 | 3.692 | 25 |
| 3200 x 192 | 1440 | 6.057 | 37 |
| 6400 x 768, opt-in stress case | 800 | 2.803 | 23 |
| 6400 x 768, opt-in stress case | 1440 | 3.212 | 25 |

The same predicate rejects omitted exposure, omitted highlights, and a thin single-channel row artifact that a globally averaged channel percentile can miss. A separately Mitchell-reduced source exercises the proxy-input path. All media is generated procedurally.

title: LR-EDIT-COLOR-GRADING: a wheel drag holds the pointer and puts it back where it was pressed (#1899)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Dragging a Color Grading wheel now holds the pointer: it hides while you drag and comes back where you pressed.

In Lightroom Classic the cursor disappears while a colour wheel is dragged and reappears where the drag began, so an Alt fine-adjust (ten times the travel) doesn't leave the mouse far from the wheels. Here the pointer hides for the drag, the puck follows the mouse's own travel, and on release the pointer is put back at the press point. On macOS it is also locked in place for the drag (`CursorGrab::Locked`), so it never runs into a screen edge; Windows and X11 can't lock, so there it moves unseen and is put back. Esc (egui ends the drag), the window losing focus, or the wheel going away mid-drag (flyout closed, view changed) give the pointer back straight away, so it is never left hidden or locked. Two platforms degrade: eframe's web host ignores pointer commands, so in the browser the pointer only hides and shows again where the drag ended, and Wayland only moves a locked pointer, so there it reappears where it was released. A plain click still sets the puck where you click and leaves the pointer alone. Happy to switch the macOS lock off if you'd rather keep one behaviour everywhere.

What I couldn't check by hand: the macOS lock (`CursorGrab::Locked`) and how the raw deltas feel while the pointer is locked. The tests drive the headless frame and see the window commands, and the platform behaviour comes from reading winit 0.30, so a quick try with a real mouse would be welcome.

title: GPU: a lost device is not polled again, and a poll that panics fails the render (#1858)
author: lincleejun
body:
Fixes #1858. After a GPU device loss, LightCraft aborted instead of falling back to the CPU. In the reporter's logs (0.8.0, Linux, Intel UHD 620, Vulkan) this happened each time an HDR merge lost the device, until the app barely stayed open.

## Cause

The reporter's log ends like this:

```
ERROR [lc-job-1] lightcraft_gpu::ctx: gpu: device lost (Unknown): Device is lost
ERROR [lc-job-1] lightcraft: panic at …/wgpu-30.0.1/src/backend/wgpu_core.rs:1924: Error in Device::poll: Validation Error
  Caused by: Parent device is lost
…
ERROR [main] lightcraft: panic at …/library/core/src/panicking.rs:233: panic in a destructor during cleanup
```

1. **wgpu 30 panics in `Device::poll` on a lost device instead of returning an error.** `wgpu_core.rs` `poll` returns only `Timeout` and `WrongSubmissionIndex` as a `PollError` (`WaitIdleError::to_poll_error`). A device error such as `Lost` goes to `handle_error_fatal`, which panics. The readback in `Gpu::finish_and_read` assumed the opposite (its comment: "A lost device makes the wait fail").
2. **The second panic comes from a destructor.** `try_render` catches the readback's panic. While that render unwinds, its buffers go back to the pool (`Buf::drop` / `RenderScope::drop` → `Gpu::pool` → `Gpu::trim`), and `trim` polls the device again. A panic that escapes a destructor during unwinding cannot be caught: the process aborts with "panic in a destructor during cleanup". The main thread gets there the same way, through the UI's `trim_pool(0)` and buffers it drops.

The window renderer is not involved: it runs on its own device, and egui-wgpu 0.36 never polls. `nn.rs` and `faces.rs` poll their own devices inside existing `catch_unwind` guards, with no polling destructor on the way.

## What changed

The render device's three polls (`finish_and_read`, `trim`, `RecordedWork::sync`) now go through a new `Gpu::poll`:

- **A lost device is not polled again.** A new `DEVICE_LOST` flag is set by the device-lost callback (wgpu fires it insid…

title: Imported LUTs no longer leave a copy in the temp folder without a library on disk
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1952 (the temp-file half of point 4; points 3 and 1 are #1966 and #1968).

In a session with no library on disk (`--demo`, `--memory`), `profile.import` wrote every LUT to `temp_dir()/lightcraft-<id>.cube` and never removed it. body:
Fixes #1983.

The file in the issue is an uncompressed 16-bit RGB TIFF stored as a single 138 MB strip. The `tiff` crate refuses any strip or tile whose declared byte count exceeds `Limits::intermediate_buffer_size`, which defaults to 128 MiB. `tiff_codec::limits()` already raises `decoding_buffer_size` from `max_pixels` but left that one at the default, so both the thumbnail and the full decode stopped with "decoder limits exceeded". The fix raises the intermediate buffer to the decoded image's cap (32 bytes per allowed pixel) when that's larger, and keeps the 128 MiB default otherwise, so small pixel budgets still read strips and tiles bigger than their visible pixels (JPEG headers, padded tiles). If you'd prefer a separate fixed cap, I'm happy to switch.

Thanks @M-Meffert for the sample file, it made this easy to pin down.

Validation:
- `tiff_single_strip_larger_than_128_mib` (crates/codecs/tests/roundtrip.rs, a synthetic 3923×5877 16-bit RGB single-strip TIFF): fails on main (`Malformed(Tiff, "decoder limits exceeded")`), passes here
- the file attached to the issue decodes here, both as a thumbnail and at full size (3923×5877, 16-bit); it isn't committed
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-codecs --test roundtrip`, `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-codecs --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `tiff_small_pixel_budget_reads_headers_and_padded_tiles` (crates/codecs/tests/roundtrip.rs, fixtures from @AlexChambers' review): a 1×1 JPEG-compressed TIFF with `max_pixels: 1` and a 16×16 TIFF in one 256×256 tile with `max_pixels: 256`; both failed with "decoder limits exceeded" on b67bb019 and pass now
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Control port: don't clone the connection's socket (Windows: launched programs kept it open)
author: LochLogic
body:
Follow-up to the side note in #1975, now checked.

On Windows, `TcpStream::try_clone()` returns an **inheritable** socket handle. std's own `bind`/`accept`/`connect` sockets are not inheritable, but the clone is. I checked with `GetHandleInformation` on Rust 1.99.1:

| socket | inheritable |
|---|---|
| listener, `accept()`ed, `connect()`ed | no |
| `accepted.try_clone()`, `client.try_clone()` | **yes** |

`control_server::serve` reads through `stream.try_clone()`, so every program the desktop app starts while a control client is connected inherits a copy of that connection. That covers the browser for a link (`rundll32 url.dll`), Explorer for Show in Explorer, and an external editor from Open With. A connection still in use keeps working. But when the server closes it (an error reply, a junk line, the app quitting), the close doesn't reach the client until the launched program exits, and then it arrives as a reset ("An existing connection was forcibly closed") instead of a clean EOF. With an external editor left open, that can be hours.

A standalone reproduction of the exact pattern (server `try_clone()`, child started while connected, server drops both handles) showed the client getting `ConnectionReset` after 3.7 s with a 4 s child. Without the clone, or without the child, the client gets a clean EOF at once.

**Fix:** read and write through the one stream (`&TcpStream` is both `Read` and `Write`), so there is no second handle to inherit. One line in `serve()`.

**Test:** `control_server::tests::a_program_started_meanwhile_does_not_hold_the_connection_open` (Windows-only: it starts `cmd`). It serves a real connection, starts a 4-second program while the client is connected, then sends a junk line. The client must see a clean close within 2 s. It fails on main with `ConnectionReset`, and passes with this change. `cargo test -p lightcraft --bin lightcraft` (69 tests), clippy and fmt pass on Windows 11.

title: macOS bundle: drop Info.plist types LightCraft cannot open (#1951)
author: sperea
body:
Fixes #1951.

## Problem

The macOS `Info.plist` template (`packaging/macos/Info.plist.in`) declares file types LightCraft cannot open:

- `UTExportedTypeDeclarations`: a "LightCraft Document" type, `ai.storyteller.lightcraft.document`, for the extension **`.pcraft`** and MIME `application/x-lightcraft`. `.pcraft` is PhotoCraft's document format; LightCraft never reads or writes it (the only other reference in the tree is a test temp-directory name).
- `UTImportedTypeDeclarations`: `com.adobe.photoshop-large-image` (`.psb`) and `ai.storyteller.lightcraft.qoi` (`.qoi`). LightCraft opens neither.

## Root cause

The declarations were copied from a sibling app's template. Because LightCraft exports the `.pcraft` type, Launch Services types PhotoCraft documents as LightCraft documents: `.pcraft` has three claimant apps among the Craft suite, each with its own MIME type, and which app "owns" the extension depends on registration order. On the other side, the bundle declares no `CFBundleDocumentTypes`, so Finder's "Open With" never lists LightCraft for the images it *can* open.

## Change

Remove both `UTExportedTypeDeclarations` and `UTImportedTypeDeclarations`. LightCraft has no document type of its own, and the formats it opens (JPEG, PNG, TIFF, HEIC and the raw formats) are already declared by the system or another app.

No `CFBundleDocumentTypes` is added: declaring viewer roles for the image and raw formats is a separate decision and out of scope for this bug.

## Tests

`packaging/check-app-specific.sh` — which the packaging-lint workflow runs via `extra-checks-script` — now:

- parses `Info.plist.in` with `plistlib`, which also validates that the template is a well-formed property list, and
- fails if the bundle declares any of `.pcraft`, `.psb`, `.qoi`, `application/x-lightcraft` or the three UTI identifiers above, while still checking the required bundle keys.

The check is a denylist of types LightCraft cannot open, so a future, legitimate UTI declaration is no…

title: DNG: lossy JPEG XL tiles that declare an sRGB, BT.709 or gamma curve decode at full size
author: EmpressAthleticus
body:
## What

Lossy (XYB) JPEG XL tiles in a DNG 1.7 file are only accepted when the codestream declares a **linear** transfer curve. Adobe DNG Converter's lossy JPEG XL DNGs (18.x) declare the **sRGB** curve with BT.2020 primaries, so LightCraft falls back to the 1024 px embedded preview:

```
preview_only: lossy JPEG XL tile with a declared encoding that is not linear RGB
```

With this change those tiles, and lossy tiles declaring a BT.709, DCI or pure gamma curve, decode at full size.

## Why the samples can be restored

A writer may tag linear raw samples with a perceptual curve so the lossy coder spends its bits where the eye notices. The stored samples are still the raw values (the raw IFD has no `LinearizationTable`), and decoding to the declared encoding gives them back, as libjxl does. `jxl.rs` already decodes XYB to linear sRGB and restores the declared primaries with a matrix, deliberately avoiding jxl-oxide's own conversion to the declared encoding (it gamut-maps and clips). This change re-applies the declared transfer curve the same way: odd-symmetric and unclipped, so lossy overshoot survives until the integer conversion.

## Changes

- `crates/raw/src/jxl.rs`
  - `Curve` (linear, sRGB, BT.709, DCI, pure gamma) derived from the declared `TransferFunction`. The gamma is read the way jxl-oxide's `apply_transfer_function` reads it: `inverted` is the header's encoding exponent, otherwise its reciprocal.
  - PQ, HLG and unknown curves stay `Unsupported` (they would need HDR tone mapping undone). Grey, ICC-profile and non-D65 encodings are unchanged.
  - `Output::FromXyb` carries the curve; `decode` applies it after the primaries matrix, on the integer and float paths.
  - Tests: the curve definitions; header → curve mapping; and four 16 × 16 lossy tiles coded by libjxl (distance 0.5), declaring sRGB, BT.709, gamma 2.2 and linear with BT.2020 primaries, that decode to their source samples (mean error under 1 %; libjxl's own decoder: 0.3 to 0.5 %). The tile test …

title: KEY-CROP-SWAP: X in the crop tool swaps the aspect once (#1866)
author: G6bill
body:
## Problem

Issue #1866 lists three things; this PR fixes one of them: **X in the crop tool does nothing.**

X is bound to both `photo.reject` and `crop.rotateAspect`. In the crop tool, both bindings fire in the same frame. Each one runs `crop.rotateAspect` (Reject is redirected to the swap while the Crop panel is open), so the crop turns portrait and immediately back to landscape. The "Swap Aspect (X)" button worked, because it runs the swap only once.

## Fix

`crates/ui-egui/src/shortcuts.rs`: when `crop.rotateAspect` fires itself, the redirected `photo.reject` no longer runs a second swap. Outside the crop tool, X still rejects.

## Not changed

- **"Custom 3:4 reverts to 4:3":** `crop.aspect` deliberately matches the crop's orientation to the photo's (a landscape photo gets a landscape 3:4 crop), as Lightroom does. With this fix, X now turns it portrait.
- **"Crop frame rotation does nothing on landscape images":** this is the X bug above. If the reporter means drag-to-rotate, that is #1794 / #1876.

## Tests

- New `tests_crop_tool::x_in_the_crop_tool_swaps_the_aspect_once` (headless). On a landscape photo with a 3:4 lock, X turns the crop portrait with the aspect `(400, 300)`. It adds one undo step and doesn't reject the photo, and a second X turns the crop back. The test **fails without the fix**: after X the crop is still landscape `(300, 400)`.
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-ui-egui --lib -- crop shortcut reject`: 103 passed.
- Full `cargo xtask ci` on Linux with Rust 1.99: passed (4265 tests, 0 failed). It ran without the corpus or `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR`, so those tests were skipped.

title: LR-BEHAV-BG-TASKS: Reload from Disk reads its files in the background
author: mattsivak
body:
## Problem
Reload from Disk on several photos froze the whole app until every file was re-read. `photo.reload` re-decoded each targeted file synchronously on the UI thread (`crates/engine/src/cmd/convert.rs`, `import::probe_paths`), and a raw DNG takes a second or more per file.

## Change
- **Engine (`cmd/reload.rs`):** the command is split into three steps. `plan` lists the photos (no disk access). `probe` reads the files without the session, with a cancel flag and progress. `apply` commits the result as one "Reload Changed Files" undo step and skips photos that were removed or relinked in the meantime. `photo.reload` runs all three in place, so CLI, MCP and headless behaviour is unchanged.
- **App (`ui-egui/src/reload.rs`):** the app intercepts `photo.reload` and runs the probe on a worker thread. It holds a TaskGuard with kind `reload`, a file count and `Cancel::Flag`, so the activity row's ✕ stops it. The command replies `{background: true, count}` at once. The result is applied on the UI thread, or dropped if another library was opened meanwhile. Toasts reuse the existing preview-only strings. `wait: true` keeps the synchronous behaviour for agents.
- **`tasks::spawn_tracked`:** a background task with a cancel flag and a progress handle.
- **Callers:** the Preview-only notice button and the grid menu now rely on the background task. The grid menu shows an error toast instead of dropping it silently.

Not changed: the reload that runs when the app regains focus after an external editor. It covers only those few edited files.

## Tests
`tests_recheck.rs`:
- the notice button now asserts a cancellable `reload` activity row right after the click, which the old synchronous code fails;
- new: a selection reload runs in the background, `wait: true` gives the engine's result, and a cancelled probe changes nothing;
- new: an empty selection starts nothing.

`cargo xtask ci` passes. Tried in the app on a library with Lightroom-made DNGs: the UI stays responsive and the …

title: Local: show a folder's files as they load; read only raw headers when browsing
author: mattsivak
body:
Opening a folder in Local used to show nothing until every file in it had been read in full and hashed. On a network share (measured on an rclone SFTP mount to a Hetzner storage box) that meant downloading every raw before the first photo appeared, and the window could freeze while it happened.

## What changes

**1. Photos show while the folder loads** (`72f9015b`)
- Browsing no longer runs the import review's whole-folder scan first. It starts the batched import straight away.
- The grid shows each new file as a placeholder (its name in a blank 3:2 cell) until it has been read and the photo takes its place. While a slow folder is still being listed, it shows "Looking for photos…" instead of "No photos in this folder".
- Records of files that are gone from the folder are still forgotten (#1392). The first photo still becomes active as it arrives (#1447).

**2. Only a raw's headers are read when browsing** (`bf0d1f82`)
- A probe used only for Local reads the byte ranges `lightcraft_raw::sparse::header_plan` names: about 3% of a DNG, CR2 or CR3 and about 8% of an ARW or RAF. It leaves the content hash unset.
- Anything it can't describe that way (NEF, ORF, PEF, JPEG and other formats, raws shown only from their embedded preview, a failing read) is read whole, as before.
- On the downloaded corpus, 319 raws were described from part of the file with results identical to the full probe; 128 were read whole.
- The hash is worked out once a photo joins the library (Add to My Photos, or an import of its file). In the app this runs on a worker thread with an activity row ("Checking added photos", kind `hash`); in the CLI and MCP it runs inline. title: Lightroom lossy DNGs: decode their JPEG XL tiles and render them like Lightroom
author: mattsivak
body:
## Problem
DNGs saved by Lightroom Classic 15.1 with **Convert to DNG → lossy compression** (seen on Sony ILCE-7CM2 files) opened as **Preview only**: "lossy JPEG XL tile with a declared encoding that is not linear RGB". After they decoded, they rendered about 0.8 EV darker than Lightroom, flat and dull.

## Cause and fix

**1. Decode (`crates/raw/src/jxl.rs`).** The lossy JXL tiles declare Rec. 2100 primaries with the **sRGB transfer curve**, and only a linear curve was accepted.
- These files store perceptually shaped samples. A cubic `MapPolynomial` per plane in `OpcodeList2` linearises them.
- So the declared curve is part of the stored values, and a lossy tile now means what a lossless tile with the same header would. After the primaries matrix, the declared SDR curve (sRGB, BT.709, DCI, gamma) is applied, mirrored for negative values and unclipped above 1.0. PQ, HLG and unknown curves stay unsupported.
- Measured against Lightroom's own embedded preview of two files, `polynomial(declared-curve values)` tracks Lightroom's rendering (midtone log-log slope 0.98 and 1.38). `polynomial(linear decode)` comes out 3.6 EV dark.
- LightCraft's decoded samples match libjxl (`djxl`) exactly at the pixels checked.

**2. Look (`crates/engine/src/camera_preview.rs`).** These DNGs embed *Adobe Standard*, which has a `LookTable` and no `ProfileToneCurve`.
- `dng_tone_eligible` treated any LookTable as "the file's own rendering" and skipped the DNG tone fit, leaving the nearly linear default tone.
- The fit also refused previews under 90% of the raw's size, while Lightroom stores a 1024 px preview (15% of 7008 px).
- A LookTable defines colour, not tone, and the fit already applies the profile tables to its proxy. It now runs for such profiles and accepts previews of at least 10% of the long edge and 384 px; the fit works on a ≤ 384 px proxy anyway.
- The structure, held-out acceptance and highlight-clipping gates are unchanged.
- `LOOK_VERSION` 9 → 10, `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 6…

title: LR-EDIT-COLOR-TEMP: Kelvin white balance for the Nikon Z5II from built-in presets
author: emmertex
body:
## What
The Nikon Z5II (Exif model `NIKON Z5_2`) now edits white balance in Kelvin. Before, its Temp slider showed the relative -100..+100 scale.

## Why
The body has no colour matrices (`raw::spectral`), and its NEFs carry no preset table that `raw::kelvin_presets` could read (Sony ARWs do). The NEF stores only the as-shot `WB_RBLevels` and, in the maker note, the colour temperature the camera states for the preset it shot with (`ColorTemperatureAuto`). (Reported in emmertex/lightcraft-classic#157.)

## How
- New `crates/raw/src/kelvin_builtin.rs` holds a per-model table of five (Kelvin, R/G, B/G) points. It feeds the existing `KelvinPresets` curve, so the model and constants are unchanged.
- The NEF decoder fills `ColorData::kelvin_presets` from the table, and `kelvin_presets::covers` accepts table models. These are the only two hooks, both one line, so this merges cleanly with other `kelvin_presets` work.
- Z5II points come from the body's own shots: Incandescent 3000 K, Direct sunlight 5210 K, Kelvin 5500 K, Cloudy 5990 K and Shade 8000 K. Each temperature is the one the camera wrote in `ColorTemperatureAuto`. Fluorescent (off the locus) and Flash are left out.

## How tested
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-raw --lib kelvin` and `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-raw --all-targets -D warnings` pass.
- Readback of shots that are not on the curve:
  - Natural Auto: the camera wrote 5030 K, it reads 5036 K with tint +1.
  - Flash (nominally 5410 K): reads about 6500 K with tint -2.
  - The 5990 K Kelvin shot with a G-M fine-tune of 3: reads 4895 K with tint -54. The tint shift is expected; the temperature is pulled by the Sony-derived isotherm tilt.
  - Cool-white FL: reads 4360 K with tint +52.
- Headless CLI on real NEFs: `wb.temp` is now the 2000-50000 K scale.

- `raw::kelvin_presets` takes any number of points (three or more) instead of a fixed five, and gains `KelvinPresets::from_unordered` (sorts by Kelvin, keeps each temperature once, drops a point that would turn the curve back). Hardened against a deserialized curve with repeated or too few points.

A reporter's issue in a downstream fork, with real samples: the G1 X Mark III has no colour matrices (`raw::spectral`), so its CR2s showed the relative −100..+100 Temp slider. Its files carry the presets, so they now show Kelvin, as Sony bodies do since #1344.
