title: LR-MERGE-HDRPANO: merge previews without the memory spike; option changes reuse decoded photos
author: mattsivak
body:
## The problem

An HDR panorama preview of 12 DJI DNGs (DJI FC8482, 48 MP, 4 brackets of 3) climbed to **40 GB** of memory while the dialog still said "Reading photos… 3 %". Switching the projection in the dialog then started everything again: reading and decoding every photo.

Measured, for one of these DNGs:

| step | time | peak memory |
|---|---|---|
| read the file | — | 0.10 GB |
| decode the raw | 0.24 s | 0.30 GB |
| the merge's preview frame (1024 px) | 2.1 s | **1.67 GB** |

Three causes:
1. **Full-size demosaic for every preview photo.** `raw_frame` demosaiced at full size (bilinear) and then shrank to 1024 px.
2. **Binning refused these files.** The preview renderer's binning (`develop_binned`) refuses any raw with an `OpcodeList3`, and these DNGs carry a lens-shading **GainMap** plus a WarpRectilinear there (uncompressed Bayer data, one strip). The app's own preview develop of these files took 6.8 s.
3. **Unbounded parallel decoding.** Previews decoded all photos at once, so 12 × 1.7 GB of decoder buffers were alive together.

## Changes

- **`Opcode::binned(k)` (raw):** re-expresses an `OpcodeList3` operation for the image binned by `k`.
  - The lens warps and `FixVignetteRadial` work in image-relative coordinates, so they stay as they are.
  - `GainMap`, `MapTable` and `MapPolynomial` get their pixel area scaled (a gain map's own grid is relative to the image).
  - Per-row / per-column tables, bad pixels, and areas that skip rows or columns return `None`, and the caller develops at full size as before.
- **`develop_binned`** bins the whole active area when there is an `OpcodeList3`, applies the re-expressed list, then cuts the default crop at the binned scale. This also speeds up app previews and thumbnails of these files: develop 6.8 s → 0.6 s, 2.1 → 0.76 GB, with the same image.
- **`lightcraft_merge::frame`:** preview frames are binned straight from the mosaic (`develop()`, the same as #1732's loader).
- **Preview loading:** previews decode at most…

title: Histogram: drag its tonal zones to adjust the Basic tones
author: deunderscorepaul
body:
Lightroom Classic's histogram is a control surface: its plot is split into five tonal zones and each one moves the Basic control it names. This makes the Edit panel's histogram do the same, wired through the engine like every slider.

| Zone | Span of the plot | Control |
|---|---|---|
| Blacks | 0.00–0.15 | `light.blacks` |
| Shadows | 0.15–0.35 | `light.shadows` |
| Exposure | 0.35–0.65 | `light.exposure` |
| Highlights | 0.65–0.85 | `light.highlights` |
| Whites | 0.85–1.00 | `light.whites` |

### Behaviour

- **Hover** — the zone is tinted and its name and value show in the strip under the plot ("Exposure: +0.45 EV"), replacing the EXIF line; the pointer shows the sideways-resize cursor.
- **Drag** — sideways travel moves that control live. The zone the press landed in stays locked for the whole drag, so the pointer can cross the others. Travel of the plot's whole width sweeps the control's whole range (the same distance-per-unit as the sliders' tracks); Shift is a tenth of that, as the sliders' fine drag. Values clamp to the control's spec.
- **Undo** — every step is a `develop.set` between `develop.beginInteraction` and `develop.endInteraction`, so the draft render follows the drag and the release lands the whole drag as one undo step; nothing is committed mid-drag.
- **Double-click** — that zone's control returns to its default, one undo step.
- The strip under the plot (the readout and the EXIF line) and the clipping chevrons in the plot's top corners are not zones. A body click still toggles the clipping warnings (unchanged).

### Implementation

- New `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/histogram.rs`: the zone table (control ids — range, default and step come from the panel's own `ControlSpec`s, nothing copied), the zone/rect/delta arithmetic, the frame's pointer input and the highlight painting. The pointer state is a new `Gesture::HistogramDrag` in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/detail.rs`, where cross-frame gestures already live, so a drag cut short (the panel closi…

title: Detail: Fit is as sharp as the photo
author: ubergeneric
body:
Fixes #1472 (the Fit part of it). Related: #1831 (the same whole-pixel snap for the 100 % view), #1042 (render sizing).

At Fit the Detail view is noticeably softer than the photo: fine texture (hair, foliage, grain) that is crisp at 100 % turns to mush at Fit, even though a good downscale of the same file keeps it. I measured it with a synthetic focus chart and found four causes stacked on top of each other, none of them in the develop pipeline's look.

## Causes

1. **The loupe texture is drawn a little larger than its place, and the GPU shrinks it with 2-tap bilinear sampling.** `AppSettings::loupe_edge` rounds the render edge up to the next 64 px step, so at Fit the render is up to 63 px larger than it is drawn and the window shrinks it by up to about 6 %. A bilinear shrink at that ratio is a blur over the whole frame.
2. **The texture is centred on a fractional pixel position.** Like #1831 for 100 %, the corner of the fitted image usually sits between two physical pixels, so even a texture of exactly the right size would be averaged with its neighbour.
3. **The render box has a truncated short side.** `(want, (want as f32 / aspect) as usize)` asks for e.g. 2560 x 1706 from a 2560 x 1707 source, so the render is a slightly anisotropic resample of its source: a 2-tap blur along one axis only. This is why the chart's horizontal bars come out much softer than the vertical ones at some window sizes (0.55 vs 0.13 contrast, below).
4. **The decode-time shrink of TIFF / PNG / WebP / ... uses a box filter at 2:1 and more** (`codecs::convert`), and so does `SourceRef::Fit` when a preview level is made from a larger decoded source. A box average at 2-3:1 halves the contrast of detail near the output's resolution limit and aliases what is finer.

On top of that, rendering at the drawn size means the pipeline itself shrinks the 2560 px preview source (Mitchell prefilter, then the bilinear sampling pass), a second soft resample before the window's.

title: LR-PRE-PANEL: starred presets are listed first in a Favorites group, as profiles are (#1999)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Starred presets now show up in a Favorites group at the top of the Presets panel, like starred profiles do.

In Lightroom, a preset added to Favorites is listed in a Favorites group at the top of the Presets panel and stays in its own group too; removing the star (or deleting a user preset) takes it out again. This follows the profile browser here: the group is shown only when something is starred, it collapses like any other group, and a starred preset keeps its star and its context menu in both places. Inside Favorites the presets are in the order the panel shows them below (group, then position in the group), since presets only carry a starred flag, not a starring order; happy to switch to name order or something else. Each row also has the star from #2017 (helgehelge123, co-author of that commit), as in the profile browser: always shown on a starred preset, on hover otherwise, and a click on it stars or unstars the preset without applying it, so no history step. A click elsewhere on the row still applies the preset. Its ids are `presetStar:<id>` in the preset's group and `presetFavStar:<id>` under Favorites. Known limit: the star can't be reached from the keyboard, since no preset row takes focus on main. Left out: the preset pickers (import review, raw defaults) are still plain lists by group.

title: #1944: keyword.export refuses library originals and writes durably
author: G6bill
body:
Closes #1944.

`keyword.export {path}` wrote with `std::fs::write` to any path, so over the control channel, MCP or the CLI it could replace a library original (or its XMP sidecar) with the keyword list. It now:

- calls `s.check_write_target(path)`, like `preset.export` and `curve.exportPresets`, which refuses originals and their sidecars (including `..` paths and symlinks) with the same "LightCraft never writes over an original" error as `export.checkTarget`;
- writes with `lightcraft_catalog::safe_file::write_atomic`, so a failed write keeps the previous keyword file. Unlike `export::write_file_durable` it doesn't create missing folders, so exporting to a folder that doesn't exist still reports an error (`tests_keyword_files::exporting_keywords_says_why_it_failed`).

## Tests
- `keyword_export_never_overwrites_originals_or_sidecars` reuses the guard harness of the two preset exports.
- `keyword_export_preserves_the_previous_file_on_write_failure` injects a write fault and checks that the old file survives and no temp files are left behind.

Both fail without the fix and pass with it. The existing keyword export tests (engine and `ui-egui` `tests_keyword_files`) still pass, and `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-engine --all-targets -D warnings` are clean (Windows).

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Keyword exports now avoid overwriting original photos and their sidecar files.
  * If an export fails, the previous export remains intact. A later export can succeed without leaving temporary files behind.

title: LR-LIB-SMARTALBUM: creating or giving a keyword no longer freezes the window while albums are counted
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

Related: #1057 (keyword edits and album counts here; develop edits still clear the caches, see #1152).

## Problem

In a large library with smart albums and the left sidebar open, some edits freeze the window for seconds. The one people hit most is in the Keywords panel: creating a keyword inside another one and giving it to the selected photo. On a library of about 160,000 photos with 28 smart albums, the frame after that edit took **2.6 s**.

There are two causes:

1. **The album counts.** `Caches::album_counts` keeps the sidebar's counts with an `AlbumTally`, which follows a small edit photo by photo. When it can't follow, it counted every smart album over every photo **on the UI thread**: 2.2 s of the 2.6 s.
2. **`Op::SetKeyword` was classed as a broad op** in `Catalog::apply_inner`, as if it could change any photo. So `touched_since` / `aspects_since` said "anything may have changed", and the album tally, the session's view (a full query and sort, 0.3 s), the folder tree, the date groups and people were all worked out again. Yet no smart-album rule, filter, sort, view query, folder tree, date group or person reads the keyword list. Its only readers are the keyword tree, export names and the keyword-list file.

Other edits the tally can't follow freeze the window the same way: an album's rules or photos changed, a stack, an edit to more than 256 photos, opening a library, and the first frame of each minute while a smart album uses an "in the last…" rule.

## Change

- **`crates/catalog`:** a new `Aspects::KEYWORD_LIST`. `Op::SetKeyword` records it (`Changes::keyword_list`) instead of marking the change memory broad, so what was touched stays known and the view and the album counts follow the edit from the photos it touched. `AlbumTally::update` now only follows: when it can't, it returns `false` and leaves the counts as they were, and the caller decides where to count whole.
- **`crates/ui-egui`:** `Caches::album_counts(cat, library, now, ctx)` runs…

title: Fix Lightroom catalog video classification and filtering
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
Lightroom catalog records marked `VIDEO` were created as `MediaKind::Image`, so the Videos filter hid them, including offline originals. Classify these records as videos and repair older records on reimport without changing IDs, edits/history, source facts or album/stack membership. The repair uses existing reversible catalog operations and stays in the import's single Undo/Redo step.

Addresses the filter portion of #1940. Video playback, frame previews and discovery through folder synchronization are outside this change.

Validation:
- Both new synthetic native SQLite regressions failed before the fix (`Image` instead of `Video`).
- All 21 Lightroom catalog tests pass after the fix.
- Headless egui smoke passed and screenshot inspected: synthetic native catalog imports 2 records; Videos returns only the video (1), Photos returns only the JPEG (1). Both sources are intentionally offline; no playback claim.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 8 stages passed (fmt, strict Clippy, HEIF, workspace tests, parity, layers, assets, wasm) on macOS arm64 / Rust 1.95.0. The report records 160 checks skipped for absent optional data: corpus 132, fonts 20, models 8.

Includes three small baseline CI corrections: two Rust 1.95 strict-Clippy cleanups (equivalent slideshow bounds condition; unnecessary closure `drop` in an export test), and the exact E-PL7 filename in the corpus test's known-unsupported list, consistent with `docs/raw/coverage.tsv`. The real CC0 E-PL7 sample remains in the test run and reports unsupported compressed ORF with a valid embedded preview; no decoder change or camera-qualification claim.

title: LR-IMP-LOCAL: Opening on Missing Photos no longer checks every original
author: alexbystrow
body:
## Problem

A library whose last view was **Missing Photos** froze the window on start-up. With 37k photos on a sleeping SMB share (macOS), LightCraft 0.6.0–0.8.0 stayed unresponsive for minutes; macOS hang reports show the main thread in `Session::open_library` → `open_stores` → `forget_local` → `in_use` → `visible` → `missing::is_missing` → `Availability::exists` → `stat` (smbfs).

`open_library` runs before the desktop UI switches availability to background mode (`run_in_background` in `ui-egui`), so working out the Missing view checks every original synchronously, about 60 ms each on that share.

Two places on the open path did that:

1. **`in_use` (cmd/browse.rs)** adds the visible photos to the set that forgetting Local records keeps. Missing Photos only lists library photos (`checked_path` needs `in_library()`, and the query drops Local records outside folder views), and `forget_local_plan` only evicts Local records, so on Missing Photos that set can keep nothing. Skipped there.
2. **`open_stores` (library.rs)** picks the first visible photo when no active photo was saved (an empty Missing view saves none). Skipped on Missing Photos; the app checks those files in the background once it runs.

## Behaviour change

Opened on Missing Photos with no saved active photo, the session no longer auto-selects the first missing photo (CLI/MCP included). Everything else is unchanged; `library.forgetLocal` keeps and forgets the same records.

## Tests

`tests_forget_local::opening_on_missing_photos_checks_no_originals` opens a library saved on an empty and on a full Missing view with a counting probe and asserts 0 checks; without either change it counts 5 (one per photo). `cargo test -p lightcraft-engine` (1116 passed), `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-engine --all-targets -D warnings` pass locally; I left the full `cargo xtask ci` to CI.

Checked on the real library (37,136 photos, NAS mounted): it now opens in 0.4 s with no hang report.

title: #1952: expire idle control connections
author: ronibalthazar
body:
## Summary

Idle TCP clients can occupy all 16 desktop control connections indefinitely, preventing other controllers from connecting. Close connections after five minutes without incoming bytes so abandoned slots are released while ordinary pauses between automation commands remain possible.

## Root cause

Accepted control sockets were read with a blocking `read_until` and had no read timeout. The server bounded the number of connections and request line size, but a peer that sent nothing could keep a worker and its slot forever. Existing command reply and no-frame timeouts do not cover this socket-read wait.

## Changes

- Add a five-minute read inactivity timeout for desktop control connections, including while a request line is incomplete; return a clear error and close without dispatching partial input.
- Keep the connection slot accounting tied to the worker lifetime and cover release/re-admission with regression tests.
- Verify persistent requests and slow command replies continue to work, and that MCP reconnects after an idle close without replaying a command.
- Document timeout behavior and reconnection guidance in `docs/control-protocol.md`.
- Add the contributor's requested public GitHub profile-name synchronization entry.

## Testing

- Desktop control transport tests: 12 passed.
- Desktop binary tests: 74 passed.
- MCP backend tests: 11 passed; MCP end-to-end tests: 6 passed; full MCP package tests passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Full `cargo xtask ci`: all eight steps passed (fmt, clippy, HEIF, workspace tests, parity, layers, assets, wasm; all 29 wasm packages checked). The run recorded 148 resource-dependent skips: 137 corpus, 8 model, 3 fonts.

title: LR-MERGE-PANO: residual vignetting, flare offsets and seam leveling from the overlaps
author: mattsivak
body:
## The problem

HDR panoramas of DJI drone photos showed three things Lightroom Classic's merges of the same photos don't:

1. **A band in the sky at every seam.** Each frame has its own slow brightness changes: the sky's gradient towards the sun, and vignetting the DNG's own lens-shading gain map leaves behind. One gain per frame can't line those up, and multi-band blending switches between frames within ~200 px, so each seam reads as a band. Kopf et al. (2007) describe the same "slight radiometric mismatches visible in smooth regions such as sky".
2. **Lifted shadows in frames facing the sun.** Those frames record the scene plus veiling flare: light **added** over the picture, not multiplied.
   - On a set of 12 DJI DNGs (4 brackets, sun in frame), the overlaps' shadow ratios differed from their midtone ratios by 7–8 %.
   - A gain lines up the midtones and leaves the shadows lifted, a step at the seams.
3. **A pink line** in dark forest along a seam, with the first offset attempt. An equal offset in camera RGB emptied a channel of the darkest pixels; it clamped to 1e-6, an extreme value in the log-space blend.

How other stitchers handle this: PTGui and Hugin fit vignetting and exposure from the overlaps (PTGui also "flare", undocumented). Gradient-domain stitching (GIST, Levin et al. 2004; Agarwala 2007) removes low-frequency differences across seams. Amazon patent US10009551 models veiling glare as a smoothly varying additive offset. Per-frame dehaze before stitching was considered and rejected: independent airlight estimates would create new seams. Only papers and docs were read, no GPL code.

## Changes (`crates/merge/src/pano/`)

- **`vignette.rs`: residual vignetting from the overlaps.**
  - A falloff shared by all frames, `ln V = c₁r² + c₂r⁴ + c₃r⁶` (r = radius from the frame centre, 1 at the corners), fitted with a log gain per frame from overlap pixel pairs.
  - The fit is linear least squares, excluding clipped pixels and the darkest quarter (where flar…

title: LR-MERGE-PANO: merged DNGs open with sliders at 0 and their auto crop as the DNG default crop
author: mattsivak
body:
## The problem

A merged DNG opened with edits already applied:

- **Sliders:** with *Auto Settings*, the merge ran Auto on the result, so Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks and Vibrance came pre-set. Each slider had less of its range left, for example Shadows +60 leaves 40.
- **Crop:** a panorama's *Auto Crop* was a develop crop. The crop tool opened on it, and getting back to the whole merge meant undoing it by hand.

## Changes

- **Auto Settings as the DNG's own brightness** (`crates/engine/src/merge.rs`, `auto_exposure`).
  - The Exposure Auto would choose is measured on a small copy of the result, cropped like it and opened as the library opens it.
  - It is added to the DNG's `BaselineExposure`, as a camera's own brightness is.
  - The merged photo opens well exposed with every slider at 0 and its whole range free. Contrast, Highlights, Shadows and the rest are left to the user.
  - The preview no longer applies Auto, so it matches the imported result.
- **Auto Crop as the DNG's default crop** (`lightcraft_merge::write_linear_dng_cropped`).
  - The crop is written as `DefaultCropOrigin` / `DefaultCropSize`, the way a camera's raw keeps its margins: the photo shows the cropped part with no crop edit, and the crop tool starts from it.
  - Previews still get a whole DNG, since the dialog draws the crop frame on it.
- **Show Full Image** (`crop.fullFrame {on?}`, the crop tool's *Show Full Image* button for raw photos).
  - A new develop setting, `Crop::full_frame`, shows the whole picture a raw holds, past its default crop.
  - `MediaCache::full_frame_loader` (installed by `with_fs`) decodes with `raw.crop` set to the active area; `source_ref_with` uses it for such photos.
  - Switching it on or off drops the photo's decoded sources and starts the crop rectangle over. It's undoable.

title: LRC-LIB-LIBFOLDERS: Synchronize Folder can bring in files already in the library elsewhere, and remembers the choice
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

Part of #1401: Synchronize Folder only. The Import dialog's duplicates are in #1425 and #1552.

## Problem

Synchronize Folder leaves out every file whose bytes match a photo the library already has under another name or in another folder. The dialog only says "Skipped: files already in the library elsewhere (n)" and gives no way to bring those files in. A library that keeps one picture in several topic folders can never show those folders complete, and synchronizing again changes nothing.

Lightroom Classic lets the person choose, with "Don't Import Suspected Duplicates". In LightCraft, a scan treats any file whose content matches a photo, at any path, as a duplicate, and `ImportJob::prepare` drops such files unconditionally.

## Change

- **Dialog (`crates/ui-egui/src/sync.rs`):** "Don't import files already in the library (n)" sits under Import new photos, ticked by default (`syncSkipDuplicates`, with a tooltip).
  - Unticked, those files count under Import new photos and come in with them, and the Skipped line goes away.
  - The dialog opens with the box as it was last left: the choice is saved when Synchronize is pressed.
- **Remembered setting:** `ImportDefaults::import_duplicates` (off by default, so the box is ticked), set with `library.preferences` `import.importDuplicates`. `folder.synchronize` takes `importDuplicates` and otherwise goes by the library's setting. `folder.scanChanges` now lists those files under `duplicates`, each with the photo it matches; before, it gave only a count.
- **Engine (`crates/engine/src/import.rs`, `sync.rs`):**
  - `ImportOptions::import_duplicates` and the library lookups that honour it.
  - A photo imported that way gets a content key of its own, `<hash>:dup<id>`, as Photo ▸ Duplicate's copy does. Relinking by content then keeps the two photos apart, and the photo that was there first keeps the plain key.
  - Only the import batch's own contents are looked up in the library, with no table of the whole library, …

title: Reject out-of-range start in photo.rename and photo.renamePreview
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/rename.rs:919 (start parsed at crates/engine/src/cmd/manage.rs:12)` (no existing issue): photo.rename / photo.renamePreview panic with 'attempt to add with overflow' when `start` is near u64::MAX.

## Cause
`rename_args` cast the JSON `start` to `usize` with no bound. `plan_rename_core` then numbered the photos with the open-ended range `(start..).zip(photos)`, which overflows when `start` is near `u64::MAX`. That panicked in debug builds and wrapped silently to 0 in release builds.

## Fix
`rename_args` now returns a `start out of range` error when the sequence `start..start + n` does not fit in `usize`. `plan_rename_core` numbers photos with `start.saturating_add(i)` instead of the open-ended range, so it can no longer overflow.

## Verified
- Regression test `rename_huge_start_is_a_bad_param`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib rename_huge_start_is_a_bad_param`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The Rename dialog and its `u32` start field are unchanged. Photos that share a file (virtual copies) still count toward the range check, so it can reject a start by a few photos too early.

title: Reject out-of-range hour, minute and second in normalize_iso
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/catalog/src/dates.rs:58 (root cause: crates/catalog/src/stacks.rs:297, iso_seconds)` (no existing issue): normalize_iso accepts out-of-range minutes and seconds and silently rolls them over (photo.setCaptureTime "12:75" becomes 13:15).

## Cause
`iso_seconds` range-checked month and day but not hour, minute or second. `normalize_iso` only compares the date prefix of its output with the input, so a time like `12:75:00` or `10:00:99` rolled over within the same day and was accepted as a different time (13:15:00).

## Fix
`iso_seconds` now returns `None` when hour >= 24, minute >= 60 or second >= 60. `normalize_iso`, `photo.setCaptureTime` and the capture-time dialog therefore report the input as not a date instead of storing a shifted time.

## Verified
- Regression test `normalize_iso_rejects_out_of_range_clock_times`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-catalog --lib normalize_iso_rejects_out_of_range_clock_times`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The date-prefix rollover check in `normalize_iso` stays as it is, because it still catches impossible dates like 2026-02-30. Leap seconds (`:60`) remain rejected.

title: Add Windows-only VRR flicker workaround setting
author: Kaan88
body:
Add a Display setting that keeps the app repainting continuously at the monitor's refresh rate. This avoids the brightness and gamma shifts that G-SYNC / FreeSync variable refresh rate changes cause on OLED and VA panels when the UI goes idle.

Behavior
- New setting `vrrFlickerWorkaround` (default: off), shown in Settings > Display under a "Refresh rate" heading, with a hint noting the extra GPU and battery usage.
- When enabled, `end_frame` calls `ctx.request_repaint()` every frame, but only while the window is focused and not minimized. An unfocused or minimized window goes back to normal idle behavior.
- The repaint is skipped on the headless host.

Platform scope
- The workaround is Windows-only. The repaint logic in `lib.rs` and the settings UI in `settings.rs` are gated with `#[cfg(target_os = "windows")]`, so the option does not appear and has no effect on Linux, macOS or the web build.
- The `vrr_flicker_workaround` field in `AppSettings` stays on every platform, so settings files stay portable between machines and no struct, default or serde handling needs per-platform variants. Off Windows the value is read and saved but never used.

Tests
- Add `vrr_flicker_workaround_setting_toggles_and_persists`: checks the default is off and that the value round-trips through serialization under the `vrrFlickerWorkaround` key. It only touches the settings struct, so it runs on all platforms.

title: Ignore zero or negative ISO when importing XMP
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/meta/src/xmp.rs:509-512` (no existing issue): XMP import stores a zero or negative ISO as `Some(0)` instead of ignoring it.

## Cause
`parse_xmp` filtered ISO to values above zero. It then re-read `exif:ISOSpeedRatings` with no positivity check and overwrote `m.iso`, so an ISO of 0 or a negative value became `Some(0)`. The `.or_else(...).filter(...)` chain also applied the filter after the fallback, so an invalid `exif:ISOSpeedRatings` hid a valid `exifEX:PhotographicSensitivity`.

## Fix
I deleted the unconditional reassignment. ISO is now the first positive value among `exif:ISOSpeedRatings` and `exifEX:PhotographicSensitivity`, otherwise `None`.

## Verified
- Regression test `non_positive_iso_is_ignored`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-meta --lib non_positive_iso_is_ignored`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I did not change the EXIF reader, which already treats ISO 0 as absent. I did not change how any other XMP field is parsed.

title: fix(camera-profiles): invalidate cached renders after subsecond profile changes
author: FooVoo
body:
## Problem

The camera-profile render-cache fingerprint truncates file modification times to whole seconds. Replacing a profile with different valid JSON of the same filename and byte length within one second can therefore reuse the previous render cache after restarting LightCraft.

## Changes

- Include the modification time's nanosecond component in the profile fingerprint.
- Preserve deterministic sorting, bundled-profile inputs, metadata-error handling and the existing process-lifetime cache.
- Extract a private directory-based helper to test fresh fingerprint calculations without mutating process-global environment variables.
- Add a generated-profile regression using an ILCE-7CR profile, equal-length matrix values and explicitly controlled timestamps.

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Same filename and byte length; different profile contents and subsecond timestamps within one second | Same fingerprint; stale renders can be reused after restart | Different fingerprint |
| Unchanged profile metadata | Stable fingerprint | Stable fingerprint |
| Profile replaced while LightCraft is running | Existing process-lifetime profile/cache behavior | Existing process-lifetime profile/cache behavior |

The change is confined to `crates/engine/src/camera_profiles.rs`. It adds no dependencies or public API and does not change RAW decoding, camera color matrices or sharpening. It does not detect edits that preserve both the exact timestamp and byte length, or add live profile reload.

title: LRC-LIB-SMARTCOLL: a Same Content as Another Photo rule finds photos whose file is in the library twice
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem

There is no way to find the photos whose file is in the library more than once: the same bytes under another name or in another folder. Such twins come from Photo ▸ Duplicate, from files copied between folders on disk, and, once #2034, #1552 or #1425 lands, from imports that bring copies in on purpose. Nothing groups or shows them. A smart album can only test a photo's own fields, and no rule asks about other photos' content.

## Change

- **A new rule:** File ▸ Same Content as Another Photo (`sameContent`, is yes / no), for smart albums and the library filter.
  - A photo matches when another photo of the library has the same file content, however many there are.
  - Content is the file's hash without the `:dup<id>` a Duplicate's key carries, so Photo ▸ Duplicate's copies and twins imported with their own key group with their original.
  - Virtual copies (the same photo, not another one), photos in Recently Deleted and photos only browsed in Local neither match nor count.
- **Contents index (`crates/catalog/src/index.rs`):** content → photos, so the rule is one lookup per photo.
  - The ops that change a photo's content as the library sees it (`AddPhoto`, `RemovePhoto`, `SetDeleted`, `SetLocal`, `SetContent`) keep it up to date. They also mark the photos with the same content as touched (`Catalog::touched_since`).
  - That matters because the sidebar's album counts (`AlbumTally`) and the grid's view follow an edit only through the photos it touched. Deleting one twin changes whether the other matches, though nobody edited the other.
  - This happens once a rule has built the index, or while a smart album uses the rule. A library that never asks carries no index and touches nothing extra. A count made on a copy of the catalog can still follow the edits made after it, which #2020 relies on.
- `RuleSet::reads(field)`.

title: Start crop drags in the zone the cursor showed at the press
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1930

## Cause
The hover cursor picks the crop zone (resize handle, move, rotate) from where the pointer is. The drag start picked it again from `interact_pointer_pos()`, and egui only reports a drag once the pointer has moved past its drag threshold. So a press near the edge of a handle's 12 px reach or near the crop boundary ended up in a different zone: it rotated (outside the box) or moved the box (inside it) while the cursor showed a resize.

## Fix
The drag start now picks the zone and the rotation's start angle from `pointer.press_origin()`, the point where the button went down, and only falls back to `interact_pointer_pos()` when that is missing. The zone the drag uses is now the one the cursor showed.

## Verified
- Regression tests `a_drag_from_just_outside_a_handle_resizes_not_rotates`, `a_drag_from_just_inside_a_handle_resizes_not_moves`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-ui-egui --lib tests_crop_rotate::a_drag_from_just`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The 12 px handle hit radius and the hover and double-click zone checks stay as they were. The zone logic is still repeated in a few places and was not pulled into one shared function.

title: LRC-LIB-LIBFOLDERS: Synchronize Folder says it is listing the folder instead of sitting at "0 of N"
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem

Synchronize Folder first lists the whole folder tree, then checks the photos in it. For a folder with tens of thousands of photos, above all on a network share, the listing alone can take minutes. All that time the scan's row in the activity stack showed **"0 of 64085"** with an empty bar, and the dialog showed "Scanning… 0 / 64085". The count of photos to check is known before the listing starts, but nothing is checked until it ends. To someone new to the app this looks frozen, and some will cancel a scan that was working.

## Change

- **`crates/engine/src/sync.rs`:** `SyncProgress` counts the folders and files the walk has listed (`folders_listed`, `files_listed`). `listed` says when the walk is over, and `listing()` gives the counts while it isn't.

title: LRC-LIB-CATALOG-IMPORT: header reads in fewer, larger reads (stacked on #1735)
author: ingolfteetz
body:
**Stacked on #1735**, only the last commit is new. Follow-up to the SMB measurements in #832.

@youyoulyz's run of #1735 over SMB read ~6× fewer bytes than the full read but took longer, because every planned range was a read of its own, each waiting for a network round trip. Counting reads over the raw.pixls.us corpus showed where they came from:

- **Tiled DNGs:** the plan asked for the one-byte alignment pad after every odd-length tile, so an Adobe-converted DNG took 49 to 241 reads. `tiff_plan` now skips a pad of up to 16 bytes between two skipped chunks of the same image. Nothing reads those bytes: the corpus test still checks every file with the skipped bytes zeroed and then set to 0xFF.
- **Small reads in several rounds:** `lightcraft_raw::sparse::reads` turns a plan's ranges into fewer, larger reads. Each is at least 64 KiB, since the next round usually asks for what follows a header. Ranges up to 16 KiB apart are read as one. `read_planned` uses it unless the larger reads would push the file over its share, in which case it reads exactly what the plan named.

Reads per file on the corpus (header plan, 512 KiB first read included):

| | before | after | bytes read |
|---|---|---|---|
| DNG | 35.2 | 2.0 | 2.4 % → 2.4 % |
| RAF | 7.0 (5 rounds) | 4.0 (2 rounds) | 6.4 % → 6.6 % |
| CR3 | 4.1 | 3.5 | 2.6 % → 2.9 % |
| ARW, CR2, RW2, SRW | unchanged | | |

The import dialog's preview reads (#1020's `planned_preview`) go through the same `read_planned` and benefit too.

**Measured on network shares** (reported in #832, `lightcraft-cli run … library.importLightroom`, fresh local library):

| | photos | originals | read | time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| @youyoulyz: SMB, 2.5 GbE, Lightroom-converted Sony DNGs | 8,711 | ~390 GB | ~15.5 GB (#1735: ~64.9 GB) | 3 min 39 s (#1735: 73.9 min) |

title: LR-VIEW-PHOTOGRID: the grid reads only the photos an import batch or an edit touched
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

Part of #1130: the grid reads only the photos a batch added, so they appear sooner.

## Problem

Every catalog change gives the grid a new list of photos. It then read every photo of the list again:
- each photo's date group, for the date headers: a catalog lookup, a date parse and a new string;
- each cell's shape: crop and orientation.

At 181,749 photos that took about 100 ms. An import or Synchronize Folder adds photos about 16 at a time, so the window lost a tenth of a second for every batch, for as long as the import ran.

## Change

- **`crates/catalog/src/dates.rs`:** `Catalog::date_runs` is split in two, and `date_runs` now calls both:
  - `Catalog::date_group` gives one photo's own group.
  - `date_runs_of` applies the stack rule (a stack's photos take the group of its first photo in the list) and makes the runs.

  The grid uses the same two functions, so its headers are the same as `library.groups`.
- **`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/grid.rs`:** `GridCache` keeps what it read of each photo of the list, position by position: its date group and its cell's shape. For a new list, the photos the catalog says changed since (`touched_since`, at most 4,096) are read again wherever they are now. The other photos are taken over, after checking that they are still in the same order with none added or removed. Otherwise the whole list is read, as before:
  - another view, sort or grouping;
  - a filter that widens or narrows the list;
  - an edit to more than photos (a stack, an album).

  The runs are made again from the groups and the stack index every time. The square grid reads no shapes. A new counter, `GridStats::photos_read`, counts the photos read.
- **Docs:** `docs/whats-new.md`, and a revision-history line for LR-VIEW-PHOTOGRID in `docs/parity-checklist.md`.

**Not in this PR:**
- The Missing Photos and Recently Added views still work out their whole list in `Session::visible()` for each batch. #1152 is reworking that code.
- An album or keyword-l…

title: Fix offline reverse geocoding for cities at longitude exactly 180
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/geocode/src/lib.rs:105-108 (cell) vs lib.rs:189-192 (reverse)` (no existing issue): Offline reverse geocoding never finds a place at longitude exactly 180.0 (antimeridian cell key mismatch).

## Cause
`cell()` filed a city at longitude 180.0 under longitude column 180. `reverse()` wraps every column it probes into -180..=179, so it never looked up column 180 and the city could not be found from nearby positions such as (0, 179.9).

## Fix
`cell()` now wraps the longitude column into -180..=179, so longitude 180 is keyed as column -180. Indexing and lookup now agree. The new test covers lookups from 179.9, -179.9, 180.0 and -180.0.

## Verified
- Regression test `city_on_the_antimeridian_is_found`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-geocode --lib city_on_the_antimeridian_is_found`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The `reverse()` probing logic and the GeoNames parsing are unchanged. I did not check whether the real cities15000 dump has any entries at longitude exactly 180.0.

In Detail, **holding Space** while a tool has the photo now lends the pointer to the view until the key is up, as Lightroom's temporary Hand / Zoom does. title: LR-MASK-OBJECTS: SAM 3 falls back to the CPU when the GPU can't run it (#1974)
author: helgehelge123
body:
Part of #1974 (the second point of the triage: no CPU fallback when the GPU can't run the kernels).

On the Intel MacBook Pro with an AMD Radeon Pro 5300M in #1974, SAM 3 loads on Metal. The first
encode then panics in `candle-metal-kernels` (`device.rs:111`, an `unwrap()` on the pipeline
compile error) because the AMD Metal compiler crashes on the `mlx_gemm` kernel that `conv2d` uses.
The worker catches the panic and says "the AI model failed unexpectedly (it will be reloaded on
the next try)". The next job loads the model on Metal again, so every try fails the same way and
Object / Describe never work on that Mac.

### What changed

`crates/engine/src/segment/worker.rs`:
- When a job fails on the GPU, the worker frees the model and runs the job once more on the CPU.
  A failure here is a panic or a `lightcraft_segment::Error::Candle`.
- If the CPU run works, the worker keeps the model on the CPU for the rest of the session. That
  job's outcome carries a notice, and `segment_poll` shows it once: "The GPU couldn't run the AI
  mask model, so it runs on the CPU until LightCraft restarts (slower). Details are in the log."
- If the CPU run fails too, the GPU isn't the cause. The original error is reported and the next
  job tries the GPU again, so a bug that hits both devices doesn't move a working Mac to the CPU.
- Some failures are not retried, because another device can't fix them: missing or damaged
  model files (`Error::Missing`, `Error::Model`), a photo that can't be rendered, and remote-worker
  errors.
- Only builds with a GPU path (`lightcraft_segment::GPU_BUILD`, i.e. macOS) retry. On Linux and
  Windows the model is on the CPU already and nothing changes.
- The worker keeps the job's `kind` and `render` for the retry, so a cache miss renders the photo
  again on the CPU.

Other changes:
- `crates/segment`: adds `Sam3::load_cpu`. `text_logits` now returns the crate's `Error` instead
  of a `String`, so a Describe that fails on the GPU is classified like a c…

title: raw(orf): decode lossless compressed Olympus ORF files
author: diegobaresphoto-dev
body:
Adds support for Olympus lossless compressed .ORF files (used by interchangeable-lens Olympus / OM System bodies such as the OM-D E-M1 Mark III) in crates/raw/src/vendor/orf.rs:

- **Compressed strip decoding (decompress_olympus / olympus_diff / olympus_pred)**: skips the 7-byte header and reads the MSB-first adaptive Golomb-Rice difference stream with two per-row parity states [prev_mag, avg_diff, small_run] (1 sign bit, 2 low residual bits, unary leading-zero count up to 12 for high quotient bits, and k adaptive low quotient bits) combined with the 2D gradient-adaptive same-colour predictor from (y, x - 2), (y - 2, x), and (y - 2, x - 2).
- **ValidBits (x0611)**: reads ImageProcessing x0611 when present so 12-bit and 14-bit compressed ORF streams report their exact sample depth.
- **Tests**: includes a self-contained compressed_orf_round_trip unit test and verified on full-resolution Olympus E-M1 Mark III (5240 × 3912, active 5184 × 3888) .ORF files.

title: Keep the profile dropdown and its submenus inside the window (#2059)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2059.

Imported LUT profiles are listed in a submenu per folder. A folder with many profiles made that submenu taller than the window, so the profiles below the bottom edge could not be reached.

The profile dropdown now draws each level with `menu_level::level`, the helper the menu bar already uses for the same problem (#189):

- the dropdown hangs from the dropdown button and scrolls if its rows don't fit below it (this also covers many folders or a long Favorites list);
- each group submenu (built-in and imported) is bounded by the window, opens upward when there is more room there, and scrolls with the wheel, dragging, or the ▲ / ▼ strips, like the menu bar's submenus. The submenu row is set as the anchor with `menu_level::set_anchor`, as `menubar.rs` does.

Short menus look the same as before: the scroll area shrinks to its rows.

Test: `tests_profile_menu.rs` imports 80 profiles into one folder, opens the dropdown and the folder's submenu in a 900 pt window, and checks that both end inside the window and that some rows are scrolled out of view. Without the fix, the dropdown has no bounded level (`menu-level:1`), so the test fails.

title: Show the applied profile when hovering it in the profile browser (#2057)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2057.

In the profile browser, hovering the applied profile kept showing the last other profile you had hovered, so you could not flick between a candidate and the current look to compare them.

Cause: hovering a profile that is not applied sets the loupe preview and remembers it as `last-profile-hover`. The applied cell sets no preview (the loupe already shows that look). But at the end of `show`, while the pointer is inside the panel and nothing set a preview this frame, the panel puts the remembered profile back. That fallback keeps the preview steady while the pointer crosses the gaps between cells. When the pointer was on the applied cell, it brought back the previous profile.

Fix (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/profiles.rs`): when the pointer rests on the applied profile's cell, the panel forgets `last-profile-hover`, so the loupe shows the applied look. Clicking a profile already clears it the same way. Hovering any other profile previews it as before. The profile menu in the Edit panel has no remembered hover, so it did not have this bug.

Not changed: in the gaps between cells, the panel still keeps showing the last hovered profile. That steadies the preview as you move from cell to cell, and the presets list does the same with `last-preset-hover`. With this fix, you get back to the applied look by hovering its cell (or by leaving the panel). If you would rather the gaps show the applied look too, that is a one-line change, and I can add it here.

Test (`crates/ui-egui/src/headless.rs`): `hovering_the_applied_profile_drops_the_last_hover` applies Vivid, hovers Portrait (a preview shows), then hovers Vivid again and checks that no preview is left. Without the fix it fails because the Portrait preview comes back.

title: Codecs: clip positive-infinity float samples to white (#1952, item 6)
author: AlexChambers
body:
## Summary

Part of #1952, item 6.

Float image samples now normalize positive infinity to 1.0 and NaN or negative infinity to 0.0 before colour conversion. The shared conversion also makes alpha and CMS inputs finite. Finite HDR and negative samples retain their existing range; alpha and CMS keep their existing bounds.

## Verification

- Four procedural 32-bit TIFF regression tests fail on the original code and pass with this change. They cover RGB and gray, mixed channels, ICC curves and CMS, resizing, alpha, finite HDR and negative values.
- The full codec suite passes: 70 unit tests and 50 integration tests, with one benchmark ignored.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes all eight gates on macOS aarch64 with Rust 1.99.0 and an Apple M3 Max Metal adapter: fmt, Clippy, HEIF, workspace tests, parity, layers, assets and WASM.
- CI records 165 prerequisite skips: 137 corpus, 20 fonts and 8 model checks. The new procedural TIFF tests run without external fixtures.
- A CLI export is pixel-identical to an explicit finite-sample reference. The headless app loads and renders the file without notices or queued work.
- An independent ImageIO check confirms the clipping semantics. The codec's direct sRGB output clips white to 255; the engine's existing neutral-white rounding produces 254 for both +Inf and the finite 1.0 reference.

The tests generate their TIFFs in memory. No binary fixtures are added.

title: LC-SAFETY: refuse Photo Merge inputs beyond the memory budget
author: ronibalthazar
body:
## Summary
Photo Merge now refuses input sets whose estimated working memory exceeds the existing merge budget, before decoding source pixels. For legacy RAW entries missing uncropped source dimensions, planning reads original headers sequentially so a small default crop cannot hide sensor allocations. This protects catalogs with many large originals from unbounded resident frame memory.

## Root cause
Merge planning accepted every requested photo path without a working-set check. The loader then retained all decoded frames in a Vec; HDR added per-frame working maps and output memory, while panorama's existing limit constrained output dimensions only. HDR panorama also loaded its inputs before processing bracket groups.

## Changes
- Added a checked, catalog-dimension-based estimate using the existing policy of 75% of RAM less the app cache budget (assuming 8 GiB when RAM is unavailable).
- Accounted for HDR, panorama, HDR panorama, preview decoder concurrency and retained preview memory. HDR-batch checks each bracket set through the shared planning path.
- Added synthetic tests with distinct photo IDs, including an instrumented reader that confirms an over-budget HDR command fails before reading bytes; added estimate growth, budget, invalid-dimension and overflow coverage.
- Probed imports retain uncropped decoder dimensions separately from cropped frame dimensions. Legacy RAW catalog entries missing source dimensions probe original headers sequentially without decoding pixels. Missing or unsupported originals return an error rather than using cropped dimensions. A legacy-snapshot regression covers a 512×384 source with a 16×12 crop for all merge modes, previews and full-size jobs.
- Preserved upstream’s duplicate-photo-ID filtering while rebasing the memory preflight, and updated the UI reload test’s `SetContent` constructor for the source-dimension fields. Set the accepted socket to blocking mode in the MCP idle-reconnect test so its configured timeout behaves co…

title: Reject signed hex digits in #rrggbb colour parsing
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/slideshow/src/settings.rs:296-300 (parse_color); same pattern in crates/engine/src/slideshow.rs:117-122 (fadeColor)` (no existing issue): Slide colour settings accept signed hex like "#+f+f+f" as a valid colour.

## Cause
The colour parsers only checked that the string was 6 ASCII bytes, then read it with `u8::from_str_radix(.., 16)` or `u32::from_str_radix`. Those accept a leading `+`, so `"#+f+f+f"` was read as `#0f0f0f` instead of being refused. `Rgb8::from_hex` also trimmed any number of leading `#`.

## Fix
`parse_color` (slideshow settings), the engine slideshow `fadeColor` parser and `Rgb8::from_hex` now require every character to be an ASCII hex digit. `Rgb8::from_hex` strips at most one leading `#`.

## Verified
- Regression tests `hostile_settings_are_rejected_or_clamped`, `rgb8_from_hex_rejects_signs_and_extra_hashes`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-slideshow --lib hostile_settings_are_rejected_or_clamped && cargo test -p lightcraft-color --lib rgb8_from_hex_rejects_signs_and_extra_hashes && cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib hostile_settings_are_rejected_or_clamped`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The `[r, g, b]` array forms and the optional `#` prefix are unchanged. `from_hex` callers that pass valid `#rrggbb` or `rrggbb` strings behave as before.

title: LR-META-XMP: hierarchical keywords saved as names and paths, never a | in dc:subject
author: jkalkstein
body:
- `LR-META-XMP: hierarchical keywords are saved as names and paths, never a `|` in dc:subject`
- `LR-META-XMP: a keyword removed here stays out of lr:hierarchicalSubject`

## Problem

Saving a sidecar wrote each keyword exactly as the photo carries it. A hierarchical keyword such as
`Animals|Birds|Heron` therefore went into `dc:subject` **with its pipes**, and `lr:hierarchicalSubject` was never
written. Because reading a sidecar turns its `lr:hierarchicalSubject` paths into keywords, even a plain save with no
edit copied Lightroom Classic's own paths into `dc:subject`.

That breaks Lightroom Classic: version 15.3 and later on macOS Tahoe **hangs at 100 % CPU** when it imports a photo
whose `dc:subject` contains a `|` (Adobe's bug report:
<https://community.adobe.com/bug-reports-674/p-lightroom-classic-v15-3-later-on-mac-os-tahoe-importing-a-photo-file-which-includes-a-pipe-symbol-in-dc-subject-metadata-causes-lightroom-to-hang-with-100-cpu-usage-1628800>).
So one Save Metadata in LightCraft on a Lightroom-keyworded photo was enough to make that photo hang Lightroom's import.

There was also no way to delete a hierarchical keyword for good: once the merge keeps the sidecar's paths (needed so
another app's keywords survive), a keyword removed in LightCraft came back from the sidecar on the next read.

## Fix

Sidecars now carry keywords the way Lightroom Classic writes them:

- `dc:subject`: each keyword's name and the names of the keywords containing it, each once whatever its case, and
  **never a `|`**.
- `lr:hierarchicalSubject`: every full path, followed by the paths the sidecar already lists that the photo doesn't
  have, so another application's paths survive a save. It is now an owned property (the merged list replaces the old
  one) and saving twice changes nothing.
- The split is the one exports already use: `Catalog::export_keywords` and a new `keywords::sidecar_keywords` share
  `split_for_file`. The sidecar variant applies no export options and adds no sy…

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: a HEIC's EXIF is read, and a file-date guess never reaches a sidecar
author: jkalkstein
body:
## Problem

An iPhone HEIC keeps its EXIF in an `Exif` item of the HEIF container. `lightcraft_meta::extract` doesn't walk HEIF
items, so an imported HEIC had **no camera, lens or exposure**, and its capture time fell back to the file's
modification time (as Lightroom does for files with no date at all).

That guess then leaked: saving the sidecar wrote the file's modification time as the photo's `exif:DateTimeOriginal`
and `photoshop:DateCreated`. From then on every other tool, and LightCraft itself on the next import, saw a "real"
capture time that nobody stated — typically the day the file was copied, not the day the photo was taken. A sidecar's
capture time read later could not replace it either, because the photo already "had" one.

## Fix

- `lightcraft_heif::read_metadata` reads the primary image's EXIF and XMP from the container alone (no picture is
  decoded; panic-guarded like the rest of the crate). `lightcraft_codecs::heif_metadata` exposes it (answers
  `Unsupported` in a build without the `heif` feature), and `lightcraft_meta::from_embedded` applies `extract`'s
  precedence to blocks another reader found. The import probe uses them for HEIF files.
- `Photo::captured_fallback` records the file date import used when neither the file nor its sidecar had a capture
  time. While `captured` is still that guess (`Photo::captured_stated()` is `None`), it is never written to XMP, and a
  sidecar's capture time read later replaces it. A time the user sets (or anything else that differs from the guess)
  is written as before. The field is `serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")`, so existing catalogs
  load unchanged.

Docs: `docs/xmp-interop.md` (reading rules), the LR-IMP-FORMATS and LR-META-XMP rows of `docs/parity-checklist.md`
and a revision-history row, `crates/heif/README.md`, `crates/meta/README.md`. No status changes.

## Tests

- `tests_import::heic_camera_and_capture_time_come_from_its_exif` — a synthetic HEIC (built with
  `lightcraft…

title: LR-META-XMP: a sidecar's GPS wins over the camera's, and a save keeps it
author: jkalkstein
body:
## Problem

LightCraft never read a sidecar's `exif:GPSLatitude` / `exif:GPSLongitude`. On import and on Read Metadata from
File the position embedded in the file (the camera's GPS, or none) stayed, and the next save wrote that camera
position **over the sidecar's**. A photo geotagged or corrected in another application (a geotagger, Lightroom's Map
module, a script) silently lost its place the first time LightCraft saved its metadata.

That is the opposite of how every other field works here: `docs/xmp-interop.md` says the sidecar wins for every field
it states.

## Fix

- `SidecarData.gps` is read from the sidecar, and `merge_into` applies it: the sidecar wins for GPS like every other
  field it states (the Metadata Working Group's guideline: XMP over Exif).
- Saving leaves a position the sidecar already states (to within about a centimetre, 1e-7°) exactly as written there,
  in its own precision and form (e.g. `12,30.5N`), so GPS is rewritten only when it was changed in LightCraft. This
  keeps saves from churning another tool's text and from drifting through float round trips.
- `sidecar_contents` now builds the packet itself from the photo and catalog (it needs the old packet to decide about
  GPS), instead of taking a ready-made string.

Docs: `docs/xmp-interop.md` (reading and saving rules) and the LR-META-XMP row of `docs/parity-checklist.md`, plus a
revision-history row. No status change.

## Tests

`tests_xmp::sidecar_gps_wins_over_the_cameras_and_survives_a_save`: a PNG whose EXIF places it at one position and a
sidecar at another (degrees-and-minutes form):

- after import the library has the sidecar's position, not the camera's;
- a save that didn't change the position (only the rating) leaves the sidecar's GPS text byte for byte;
- another app moves the photo: Read Metadata from File takes the new position (southern / eastern hemisphere);
- a position typed in LightCraft is written.

Coordinates are made up (open ocean); nothing comes from a real photo…

title: Use the browser's languages as the default UI language on wasm
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #2085

## Cause
`i18n::default_language()` only read the `LIGHTCRAFT_LANGUAGE` environment variable and otherwise returned English. The browser has no environment, so the web build always started in English, whatever `navigator.languages` held.

## Fix
Added `resolve_system_language(tags)`, which returns the first tag that `Locale::parse_tag` maps to a shipped language and English if none match. On wasm, `default_language()` now passes it `navigator.languages`, or `navigator.language` if that list is empty. `web-sys` (features `Navigator` and `Window`) is added to `lightcraft-ui-egui` as a wasm32-only dependency.

## Verified
- Regression test `system_language_tags_pick_the_first_shipped_language`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-ui-egui --lib system_language_tags`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Native `default_language()` is unchanged and still reads only `LIGHTCRAFT_LANGUAGE`. Saved user preferences still override the default. The test commit includes a stub of `resolve_system_language` that returns English, so the regression test fails there for a real reason and not because it doesn't compile. It is not a wasm or browser end-to-end test.

title: Reject trailing text after a bracketed IPv6 host in Url::parse
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/fetch/src/http.rs:87-102` (no existing issue): Url::parse accepts garbage after a bracketed IPv6 host and silently falls back to the default port.

## Cause
In the bracketed IPv6 branch of `Url::parse`, the text after `]` was read with `strip_prefix(':')`. Text that didn't start with `:` (such as `junk` or `8080`) gave `None`, which fell back to the default port, and the text was dropped without any check.

## Fix
After the closing `]`, `Url::parse` now returns `BadUrl` if the remaining text is non-empty and doesn't start with `:`. Valid forms `[::1]` and `[::1]:port` parse as before.

## Verified
- Regression test `rejects_text_after_a_bracketed_ipv6_host`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-fetch --lib rejects_text_after_a_bracketed_ipv6_host`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The non-bracketed host/port parsing, the port validation and `Url::join` are unchanged.

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: color and tone in pushed shadows
author: robmdunn
body:
Underexposed raws pushed back up (Exposure, Shadows) came out with muddy colour, too dark, and with magenta in the deep shadows. **Stacked on #2278** (raw decoding keeps negative channels, the magenta cause, split out of here): only the commits after its one are new here. This fixes the other two causes. The Nikon D780, D750 and D90 profiles that were part of this PR are now #2093, stacked on this one.

One commit per change:

1. **Dark photos keep their camera profile's colour.** When no look fits a photo (its camera JPEG is too dark or too colourless), `fit_preview` dropped the profile and fell back to the neutral matrix. Now the photo keeps the profile's colour, with the JPEG's tone curve when one fits and the default raw curve otherwise (`with_profile_colour`, `CameraTone::default_raw`). `LOOK_VERSION` 10.
2. **Camera profiles carry a pooled tone curve.** `calibrate` now also pools luminance samples, dark pixels included, and fits one curve per camera by quantile matching. Profiles store it as an optional `tone` field; older profiles and builds still load. A photo follows its own curve as far as its JPEG showed it, then fades onto the camera's curve over 1 EV (`extend_tone`). Before, the curve continued as a shoulder that rendered pushed photos 4–7 L\* too dark. `LOOK_VERSION` 11.

## Measured on a bracket

I shot two bursts of one scene on a D780: ISO 100, f/8, frames 1.1 to 3.7 EV under the brightest. I rendered each frame with Exposure raised by its measured offset and compared it with the properly exposed frame, using median CIEDE2000 in the L\* 40–70 band. "This PR" includes #2278 and uses the D780 profile from #2093, fitted from 255 other photos. Change 1 helps every model with a bundled profile; change 2 needs a profile with a pooled tone curve, which so far only the #2093 profiles (or a profile made locally with `calibrate`) have.

body:
**Stacked on #2092 (itself on #2278): only the last three commits are new here.**

Bundled camera profiles for the Nikon D780, D750 and D90, one commit each. Each has a corpus test against the public raw.pixls.us sample of its body. `LOOK_VERSION` 14. The docs' count of bundled profiles is corrected to 11; it still read 5.

On 40 held-out photos per body and the public samples:

| Body | Per-file fit | Profile | Public sample |

| D780 | 2.77 | 2.68 | 3.70 → 3.68 |
| D750 | 3.58 | 3.58 | 3.08 → 2.53 |

title: Fix Assisted Culling bursts that cross midnight at month end
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/cull.rs:17-20 (secs, used by the burst grouping at cull.rs:45)` (no existing issue): Assisted Culling (photo.analyze) never groups a burst that crosses midnight at the end of February, April, June, September or November.

## Cause
`secs()` in `photo.analyze` built a pseudo-timestamp that counted every month as 31 days. Two shots one second apart across midnight at the end of Feb, Apr, Jun, Sep or Nov looked days apart. The `<= BURST_GAP` check failed, so no burst was formed and `best` was never marked.

## Fix
`secs()` now returns `DateTime::unix_seconds()`, so consecutive calendar seconds differ by exactly 1. The new regression test checks every month-end boundary, including Dec 31 to Jan 1.

## Verified
- Regression test `assisted_culling_groups_bursts_across_month_end`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib assisted_culling_groups_bursts_across_month_end`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The burst gap (10 s), the similarity threshold, and the rest of the culling logic are unchanged.

title: Search words with an unknown field prefix as plain text
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/catalog/src/query.rs:146-177 (token_matches)` (no existing issue): Free-text search never matches a word containing a colon (e.g. "10:30", "Re:") unless the part before the colon is a known field name.

## Cause
`token_matches` splits every search word at its first ':' and treats the left part as a field name. When that name was not a known field (e.g. `10:30`, `Re:`), the `_ => false` arm rejected the photo. The plain text match over file name, title, caption, keywords, camera, lens, location and format was never reached.

## Fix
The plain text match is now its own function, `text_matches`. The unknown-field arm calls it with the whole lower-cased word, so `10:30` and `re:` are searched as text. Known fielded tokens such as `iso:>800` are handled as before.

## Verified
- Regression test `free_text_with_a_colon_searches_the_text_fields`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-catalog --lib free_text_with_a_colon_searches_the_text_fields`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Known fields with a value that doesn't parse or match (e.g. `iso:abc`) still match nothing. Matching and parsing of fielded tokens is unchanged.

title: Reject fractional command indices before mutation
author: AlexChambers
body:
Fixes #2097. Follow-up to #1740 finding 4 and merged #1793.

## Changes

- Require command indices to be non-negative, representable whole numbers. `version.delete {"index":0.9}` now returns an error instead of deleting version 0.
- Keep integer JSON values exact through checked `u64` conversion. Preserve integral floats such as `2.0` and reject fractions or overflow before casting.
- Use the same parser for `history.restore`.

## Verification

- Recorded failing public-command regressions for fractional version deletion and history restoration on unchanged main. Both pass with the fix.
- Covered all eight consumers, catalog/history/undo preservation, valid integer and integral-float inputs, exact integer precision above 2^53, and pointer-width bounds.
- Independent source review found no blockers. The 32-bit boundary cases were reviewed by inspection; native tests ran on aarch64 macOS.
- `cargo xtask ci` passed all eight gates, including HEIF and WASM. Workspace libtest totals: 4,120 passed, 0 failed, 35 ignored.
- CI recorded 165 resource skips: 137 corpus, 20 fonts, 8 model. The new index regressions ran.

title: Reject malformed mask and spot targets before mutation
author: AlexChambers
body:
Fixes #2098.

## Changes

- Reject malformed mask IDs, component indices and spot indices instead of substituting the active object or truncating a large value.
- Share checked mask-ID parsing with saved effects. Validate every used effect target before applying any change.
- Preserve omitted/null optional targets, selection clearing, each component default, and `all:true` precedence.

## Verification

- Recorded failing public-command regressions on unchanged main, including negative targets, component replacement, saved effects, and ID `4294967297` wrapping to mask 1.
- All 12 mask/spot tests pass. Rejection snapshots cover settings, history, selection, undo/redo, journal, effects, commit count and catalog revision.
- A real CLI script rejected 11 malformed commands and preserved exact `develop.get`, `history.list`, `library.state` and `mask.effects` snapshots.
- Independent source review found no blockers.
- `cargo xtask ci` passed all eight gates, including HEIF and WASM, on aarch64 macOS with Apple M3 Max Metal.
- CI recorded 165 resource skips: 137 corpus, 20 fonts, 8 model. The new target regressions ran. Successful `mask.refineDetail` defaults were checked by source review, without model inference.

title: Handle macOS native picker failures without aborting
author: AlexChambers
body:
Fixes #1996.

## Changes

- Enter the macOS main queue before calling rfd and catch Rust panics inside that callback. A constructor panic can return an error before unwinding across the C callback boundary.
- Return background chooser failures separately from cancellation. Report legacy dialog failures through the existing in-app error toast.
- Keep the current dialog and session intact. Never retry a failed background start synchronously.
- Poll chooser results in fullscreen preview as well as normal views.

## Verification

- A disposable process using the real macOS main queue and CFRunLoop aborts without the guard. The guarded version catches a fake constructor panic and answers another main-queue request with 42.
- The tracked callback regression and all seven picker tests pass. Headless tests cover startup/worker/legacy errors, normal/fullscreen views, cancellation, chosen paths, and hosts without the background picker.
- Inspected four error screenshots. The unfinished rename dialog and existing edit remain intact; a subsequent control command succeeds.
- Independent source review found one fullscreen polling gap, now fixed and covered by a failing-before/passing-after regression.
- `cargo xtask ci` passed all eight gates, including HEIF and WASM, on aarch64 macOS with Apple M3 Max Metal. CI recorded 165 resource skips: 137 corpus, 20 fonts, 8 model. All new picker regressions ran.

The test simulates the Rust constructor panic; it does not force macOS to return nil. The guard does not catch Objective-C exceptions or process aborts.

title: Show an empty view when Find Similar has no matches
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/cull.rs:115 (find_similar; empty-`only` semantics at crates/catalog/src/query.rs:328)` (no existing issue): Find Similar with no matches shows the whole library instead of no photos.

## Cause
`library.findSimilar` filters the view by setting `filter.only` to the hit ids. When there are no hits that list is empty, and an empty `only` means "no constraint", so the filter was cleared and the grid showed every photo.

## Fix
When Find Similar finds no hits and filtering is on, `filter.only` is set to the id `PhotoId(u64::MAX)`, which no photo has, so the view is empty. Clear Filters still restores the whole library. This is the same sentinel `lightroom_import.rs` already uses.

## Verified
- Regression test `find_similar_with_no_hits_shows_no_photos`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib find_similar_with_no_hits_shows_no_photos`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The empty-`only` = no-constraint semantics in `Filter` are unchanged. The `filter: false` path is unchanged. I did not change the filter chip, which will read "Only 1 photos" in this state.

title: MIDI controller input: a TOML map from faders, knobs and buttons to Develop sliders and commands
author: costin-zaharia
body:
## MIDI controller input

Refs #251. This covers the controller-input half (native MIDI to Develop sliders and commands). State feedback to the controller (LEDs) is not included.

A MIDI control surface can drive Develop sliders, run commands and step through photos. What each message does comes from a map the user writes, so it is not tied to one device.

### How it works
- `midi.toml` in the config folder (or `$LIGHTCRAFT_MIDI_MAP`) holds `bindings`: a source (`control_change`, `pitch_bend` or `note`, with optional `channel` and `number`) and one target.
  - `set`: absolute, the controller's travel spans the control's range
  - `nudge`: relative, `step` per tick, with `sign_magnitude`, `twos_complement` or `offset` encodings
  - `run`: a command id, run on a button press
- `inputs = ["Port name"]` limits which input ports are opened. A device can expose several ports that repeat each other (the SMC-Mixer has two on Windows), and listening to all of them ran commands twice.
- A turn of one fader or knob is one undo step.
- New `midi.reload` command re-reads the file without a restart. A map with a mistake is rejected with the binding named ("binding 3: ... is not a command"), and the map in use stays.
- `docs/midi/smc-mixer.toml` is an example for the M-VAVE SMC-Mixer in DAW mode (faders, knobs, rotate, previous / next, Auto, Black & White, delete). `docs/midi.md` documents the format.

### Decisions worth a look
- **MIDI is off by default.** Without a `midi.toml` no port is opened. Windows gives a MIDI port to one program at a time, so opening every port by default would take controllers away from a DAW.
- **TOML.** It reuses the `toml` crate already in the lockfile (the `ui-egui` build script uses it), so no new parsing dependency. The only new crates come from `midir`.
- **`midir`** (WinMM / CoreMIDI, pure Rust bindings) is a dependency of the desktop app on Windows and macOS only. **No Linux**: its ALSA backend is a C library, which the pure-Rust rule rules out…

title: Strip XML 1.0-forbidden characters from XMP sidecar output
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #2131

## Cause
`write_xmp_lc` passed strings through `escape`/`partial_escape`, which only escape `<>&'"`, so control characters (U+0000–U+001F except tab, LF and CR) and U+FFFE/U+FFFF were written raw. `entity()` also accepted numeric references such as `` on read, so those characters came back in. Strict XML parsers reject the whole sidecar.

## Fix
Added `is_xml_char` (the XML 1.0 `Char` production) and `xml_safe`, and applied `xml_safe` before every escape call in the writer: simple properties, `lc:*` properties and `rdf:li` items. `entity()` now returns `None` for numeric references to characters outside that production, so they are kept verbatim instead of decoded.

## Verified
- Regression tests `writer_drops_characters_xml_1_0_forbids`, `numeric_references_to_forbidden_characters_are_not_decoded`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-meta --lib xmp::tests::`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I did not change how the reader handles forbidden characters that appear raw in the input, since quick-xml does not check them. Characters are dropped, not replaced with a placeholder.

title: Stop export lanes when a panic unwinds the batch thread
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #2132

## Cause
In `run_batch_with`, `queue.stop()` only ran after the placing loop returned normally. If `progress` or `placer.place` panicked inside `std::thread::scope`, the lane threads stayed blocked in `Condvar::wait` and the scope's implicit join never returned. The export hung, and the command's last-resort `catch_unwind` never got control.

## Fix
Added a `StopOnDrop` guard that calls `Queue::stop()` when dropped. It is created at the start of the scope, so the lanes are stopped on unwind as well as on a normal return. The explicit `queue.stop()` call is gone, because the guard replaces it. The regression test runs a 5-photo, 2-lane batch whose `progress` panics on its second call. It asserts that the batch returns an error instead of hanging.

## Verified
- Regression test `a_panic_in_progress_does_not_hang_the_lanes`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib a_panic_in_progress_does_not_hang_the_lanes`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The panic still propagates out of `thread::scope` to the caller's existing `catch_unwind`, which turns it into an error. I did not add a new `catch_unwind` inside `run_batch_with`. The single-lane path is unchanged, since it has no waiting threads.

title: Keep the zone when shifting a capture time without seconds
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/catalog/src/dates.rs:52 (shift_iso, tail = iso.trim().get(19..)); used by crates/engine/src/cmd/manage.rs:222` (no existing issue): photo.setCaptureTime shift corrupts capture times that have a zone but no seconds (e.g. 10:00+02:00 becomes 11:00:02:00).

## Cause
`iso_seconds` read the seconds from bytes 17..19 even when the time had none, so for `10:00+02:00` it took the zone digits `02` as seconds. `shift_iso` then kept everything after byte 19 as the tail, which cut into the zone and produced `11:00:02:00`.

## Fix
`iso_seconds` now reads seconds only when byte 16 is `:`. `shift_iso` starts the tail at byte 16 when there are no seconds, so `2026-01-01T10:00+02:00` shifted by 3600 s gives `2026-01-01T11:00:00+02:00`.

## Verified
- Regression test `shift_keeps_the_zone_of_a_time_without_seconds`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-catalog --lib shift_keeps_the_zone_of_a_time_without_seconds`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Shifting times that already have seconds, fractions or no zone behaves as before. The `photo.setCaptureTime` command is unchanged, because it already calls `shift_iso`.
