title: Refuse catalog snapshots with an out-of-range seq
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #2130

## Cause
`Journal::open` accepted any `u64` as the snapshot's `seq`. With `seq` near `u64::MAX`, the unchecked `+ 1` in `append` panicked in debug builds and wrapped to 0 in release. After the wrap, new records had a seq at or below the snapshot's and were skipped as stale on the next open, so later edits were lost without an error.

## Fix
`Journal::open` now returns `CatalogError::Corrupt` when the snapshot's `seq` is above `u64::MAX / 2`. The remaining `+ 1` and `+ unlogged` on seq counters (`append`, `resync`, the replay in `open`, `snapshot_with_unlogged`) now use `checked_add` or `saturating_add`. `append` and `snapshot_with_unlogged` return an error instead of wrapping.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests_journal::snapshot_with_seq_near_u64_max_is_corrupt`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-catalog --lib snapshot_with_seq_near`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I did not add a separate test for the `checked_add` guards in `append` and `snapshot_with_unlogged`. The new range check on open means a loaded journal can't get close enough to overflow for them to fire. Snapshot and log formats are unchanged.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Keep face index records aligned after a torn or failed append
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #2129

## Cause
When `Index::load` and `Scanned::load` found a half-written last record, they skipped it but still marked the file as appendable. The next `save()` then appended after those leftover bytes, so every later record was read shifted: wrong photo ids, and garbage embeddings that still passed `is_finite`. A failed `write_all` (for example on a full disk) also left its partial bytes in the file, and the pending records were later appended after them.

## Fix
When a load finds leftover bytes after the last whole record, it now sets `rewrite`, so the next save writes the whole file fresh and atomically. Appends now go through a shared `append` helper. If the write fails, it cuts the file back to its old length, the way the catalog journal does, before returning the error.

## Verified
- Regression test `records_appended_after_a_torn_tail_stay_aligned`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib records_appended_after_a_torn_tail_stay_aligned`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The file format and the atomic full-rewrite path are unchanged. The failed-write path has no test of its own, because a full disk can't easily be simulated in a unit test.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Make TIFF chunk-length inference and header-plan merging fast
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #2128

## Cause
When a chunk had no byte count (or a count of 0), `ImageInfo::chunks` searched every offset to find the next larger one, which is quadratic in the chunk count. `tiff_plan` then added each chunk to `Ranges::insert`, which rebuilds the whole vector on every call and is also quadratic. A file of a few MB with about 10^6 strip offsets could stall the import probe for a long time.

## Fix
`chunks` now sorts and dedups the offsets once, and only when some byte count is missing. It finds the next larger offset with `partition_point`. A new `Ranges::extend` adds many spans with one sort and merge, and `tiff_plan` collects the chunk spans of all IFDs and adds them through `extend` in one call.

## Verified
- Regression tests `missing_byte_counts_run_to_the_next_larger_offset`, `many_strips_without_byte_counts_are_fast`, `many_strips_without_byte_counts_plan_fast`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-tiff --lib image::tests && cargo test -p lightcraft-raw --lib sparse::tests::many_strips_without_byte_counts_plan_fast`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`Ranges::insert`, `contains` and `overlaps` are unchanged, because their other callers add only a few ranges. The issue also suggested a cap on the chunk count, which I did not add because the work is now O(n log n).

title: Catalog: make damaged journal suffix recovery linear
author: skybluu
body:
Fixes #2124.

## Cause and fix

Failed-append recovery tried every `{"seq":` marker and validated/parsed the entire remaining line each time. Repeated markers made library opening quadratic.

Find the start of the final JSON object with one backwards, string/escape-aware brace scan, then validate that one suffix with the existing record decoder (UTF-8, CRC and sequence checks). No extra buffer or recursive parser. Recovery of invalid-UTF-8 fragments, CRLF, escaped text and nested smart-album values is retained. The catalog format is unchanged.

The issue's suggested last-marker-only shortcut is insufficient: arbitrary smart-album rule values can contain `{"seq":` too. A regression covers that case, including escaped quotes, backslashes and braces. A second exercises 300,000 repeated markers with and without a valid retried record. Existing every-tear legacy recovery, damaged-log preservation and format-version tests also pass.

- `cargo test --locked -p lightcraft-catalog`: **218 passed, 2 ignored**.

title: Never crash: Refuse an ERF or MEF whose raw strip runs past the file (#2119)
author: endthestart
body:
The ERF and MEF readers picked the raw IFD by checking that StripByteCounts matched width × height, but they never checked that the file actually holds that many bytes. A tiny file declaring a huge frame got through, and the header probe then allocated the full sample buffer to measure white balance, so a few KB could cost gigabytes during import.

Now both decoders refuse a strip that runs past the end of the file before they size anything from it.

I added a test for each format that takes a small valid sample, rewrites its height and strip length to claim a much larger frame, and checks that probe_info and decode return a Corrupt error. Both failed before the change. Let me know if you'd rather fix it another way. Thank you.

Fixes #2119

title: Never crash: Cap aggregate TIFF IFD entry allocations (#2136)
author: ronibalthazar
body:
## Summary

Cap aggregate TIFF IFD entry-vector allocations so distinct, overlapping IFD tables cannot multiply parser memory use far beyond the input file.

## Root cause

The reader limited entries per IFD, but allocated each directory vector with `Vec::with_capacity(dir.read)`. Recursive child IFDs at distinct offsets could overlap the same small input region and each consume the full per-IFD allowance. These slots were not charged to the decoded-value budget, so the total allocation had no aggregate bound.

## Changes

- Enforce a checked limit of 65,536 directory entry slots across the main IFD chain and child IFDs before allocating an IFD's entry vector.
- Propagate this specific resource-limit error through child parsing and the main IFD chain.
- Keep the existing per-IFD and decoded-value limits independent.
- Document the aggregate bound in the TIFF crate README and rustdoc.
- Add an in-memory TIFF regression test with distinct overlapping child IFD tables.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p lightcraft-tiff overlapping_ifd_tables_obey_total_entry_limit` — passed.
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-tiff` — passed (8 unit tests and 17 integration tests).
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — passed.
- `cargo xtask ci` — passed all stages: fmt, clippy, heif, test, parity, layers, assets, and wasm. It reported 165 data-dependent skips (137 corpus, 20 craft-fonts, 8 model).

## Manual validation

Reviewed the final four-file diff and the generated regression input. The regression test was run before and after the fix; before the fix, the parser accepted the oversized aggregate. No UI validation applies to this parser-only change.

## Compatibility and risk

The existing per-IFD and decoded-value limits remain in place. A TIFF with more than 65,536 aggregate directory slots now returns a resource-limit error. The bound is internal, so this does not change the public `ParseOptions` API.

## Related issue

Fixes #2136.

title: Never crash: Cap the property names one XMP packet can produce (#2120)
author: endthestart
body:
The XMP reader builds every property name from its full struct path, so long struct names nested deep over many fields get copied into each leaf's name. A packet of a few hundred kilobytes could grow into gigabytes of names during import.

I gave the reader a 64 MB budget for property names per packet. Past it, the packet is refused as too complex, the same error a packet nested too deep already gets. I added a test with 58 nested 2000-character names over 20 000 fields. On main it peaks at 2.6 GB and returns the metadata, and with the change it returns the error right away.

Let me know if you'd rather fix it another way. Thank you.

Fixes #2120

title: LR-VIEW-PHOTOGRID: the active photo's selection ring shows on light themes and differs from the other selected photos by weight
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem

In the grids and the filmstrip the active photo is framed in 2 px of pure white and the other selected photos in grey 170. On Silver and Paper the grid is light grey, so the white ring vanishes, and active and selected differ only in lightness. Compare, Reference and Survey frame the active tile in the same white; in Survey that frame is the only sign of which photo is active. A thumbnail still loading is a fixed dark grey (38) slab in every theme.

title: M12: SAM 3 on the GPU outside macOS (wgpu): a photo's analysis ~33 → ~0.6 s, a description ~5 → ~0.5–0.7 s
author: helgehelge123
body:
Part of #932. On Linux and Windows SAM 3 (Object, Describe, and later Subject) ran entirely on the CPU through candle. With this PR the image encoder, both feature-pyramid necks, the text detector's DETR encoder and its mask decoder run on the GPU through **wgpu** (Vulkan / DX12; Metal too, but macOS keeps candle's Metal by default), with LightCraft's own WGSL compute kernels. Pure Rust, no new dependencies: no CUDA, no ONNX runtime (as asked in #909), wgpu is already in the workspace.

On a Ryzen 9 3900X + RTX 5070 (Linux, Vulkan), release build, the app's order of steps:

| | CPU (`main`) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| load the model (once) | ~1.5 s | 0.9–1.8 s (device + kernels 0.2–1 s, weight upload ~0.9–1.1 s) |
| image encoder (once per photo) | 30–31 s | **0.45 s** |
| click features (necks, before the first click) | 2.1–2.3 s | **0.12–0.19 s** |
| **a photo's analysis before its first click** | 32–33 s | **0.57–0.69 s** |
| a click | ~0.14 s | ~0.14 s (CPU) |
| first description on a photo (+ detector neck) | 7.0–7.7 s | **0.5–0.8 s** (1.3 s the very first time, with the detector loading) |
| a further description (a new prompt) | 5.1–5.5 s | **~0.7 s** |
| a prompt used before (this or an earlier photo; e.g. Subject's "person") | 5.1–5.5 s | **0.45–0.46 s** |

What stays on the CPU per description: the DETR decoder (~0.4 s) and, for a new prompt, the CLIP text encoder (~0.25 s).

### Where

- `crates/segment` (`lib.rs`): a `BackboneAccel` trait (backbone; optional `neck`, `detr_encoder` and `mask_decoder`), `WeightReader` (cloneable read access to the checkpoint) and `Sam3::load_accelerated`. The candle backbone is only loaded when it's needed. Whatever the accelerator returns is checked (length, finite values); an `Err`, a wrong size or a NaN falls back to candle, logged once, and the reason is kept for the status. The necks and the DETR encoder fall back on their own, so a failing neck leaves the backbone on the GPU.

title: never-crash: deny the panic lints in every crate root; GPU asserts become fail paths (#2137)
author: eliets2
body:
Closes #2137.

**Bug:** The never-crash policy was documented but not machine-checked for the two largest crates: `crates/engine` (~86k lines) and `crates/meta` carried only `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, so a future `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` would pass `cargo xtask ci`. `xtask` itself carried neither attribute. Separately, `crates/gpu` had three production `assert!s` (binding count in `run`, readback bound in `finish_and_read`, curve length in `finish_block`), and `finish_and_read` would issue a zero-size `copy_buffer_to_buffer` for `len == 0`, which wgpu rejects.

**Fix:**
- `engine`, `meta` and `xtask` crate roots now also carry `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, clippy::unimplemented, clippy::todo, clippy::unreachable)]`. The guarded expects (`meta/src/xmp.rs` stack invariants, `xtask`'s `parity.rs` `summarize` and `root()`) use the documented `#[allow(clippy::expect_used)]` + invariant form.
- The three GPU asserts become `fail(FailKind::Fatal, ..)` + return, so a binding-count mismatch, an over-long readback or a wrong-length curve fails the render over to the CPU instead of crashing. `finish_and_read` early-returns zeros on `len == 0` (submitting the staged encoder first, so an earlier failure in the same render stays detectable), and `render.rs` gates on `failed()` right after `finish_block` so the malformed-curve path can never reach the band loop on an empty parameter block.
- New `cargo xtask roots` check (part of `ci`): every workspace lib root **and every binary main.rs** carries both attributes — kind detection covers `lib`/`rlib`/`cdylib`/`dylib`/`staticlib`, so the web build's `crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]` root is included; 34 roots checked today. `crates/sysmem` is the documented exception for `forbid(unsafe_code)` only (it already carries the deny list). Unreadable root files fail with the I/O error rather than a fake policy violation.
- Docs: `finish_block`/`finish_and_read` state their failure contracts; USAGE and A…

title: mcp: file-writing helpers report destructiveHint: true (#2139)
author: eliets2
body:
Closes #2139.

**Bug:** `annotations()` computed `destructiveHint: !read_only && !files`, so the three helpers that write to an agent-supplied path — `export`, `render_photo`, `screenshot` — were annotated `destructiveHint: false`. MCP clients use that hint to decide whether to ask the user before a call, so a prompt-injected instruction could overwrite an arbitrary file (a dotfile, a script) with image bytes without any prompt. Only catalogued originals and their sidecars are protected (`check_write_target`); every other path is silently replaced.

**Fix:**
- `destructiveHint` is now exactly `!read_only`: a tool that can mutate the library or overwrite a file at an agent-supplied path is destructive; the eleven read-only helpers stay `false`. Generated `cmd_*` tools were already destructive and are unchanged. No tool behaviour changes — annotations, descriptions and tests only.
- Descriptions now state the real overwrite semantics: `export` — an existing file at `path` is **always** replaced (`conflict` governs only derived batch names in `dir` mode, per `Placer::place`); `render_photo`/`screenshot` — `path`, when given, is overwritten. The untrusted-data note (photo metadata strings: titles, captions, XMP) sits on `export`, the only one of the three whose output can carry such strings.
- `core_tools_have_hints_and_reject_unknown_keys` pins every helper's exact `(readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint)` quadruple — the table fails on the old expression — and, through a UI-backed server, asserts `screenshot` (false, true, true) plus the read-only `ui_screenshot`/`ui_inspect`/`inspect_ui`/`list_widgets` rows unconditionally (the headless test server never registers the UI tools, so those rows were previously untestable).

**Tests:** `cargo test -p lightcraft-mcp --lib` (the extended test passes; `backend::tests::malformed_replies_are_rejected_without_resending` flakes under parallel test threads on Windows-gnu — passes in isolation, and the flake reproduces on…

title: tiff: bound total entries across a parse (#2136)
author: eliets2
body:
Closes #2136.

**Bug:** `ParseOptions` capped IFDs (1 024) and entries per IFD (8 192) but nothing bounded their product, and count-0 entries cost nothing from the value budget. IFD tables that overlap in the file — SubIFD pointers shifted by one entry, reusing the same bytes — let `Tiff::parse` allocate ~8 M `Entry` values (~400 MB) from a ~100 KB input, several times per file across parallel imports.

**Fix:** `ParseOptions` gains `max_entries_total` (default 65 536), accumulated with `saturating_add(dir.read)` in `Ctx::ifd` and checked **before** `Vec::with_capacity(dir.read)` — the only count-derived allocation in the reader — so a hostile file stops with `TiffError::Limit("entry count")` instead of amplifying. 65 536 cannot over-refuse any non-overlapping layout under ~786 KB of table bytes (65536 × 12 B), and the repo's own writer errors past 65 535 per IFD, so real scanned files stay far under it. BigTIFF's 20-byte entries flow through the same guard.

**Tests:** a hostile overlapping-table chain (IFDs at 8, 20, 32, … each declaring 8 192 entries) parses exactly 8 IFDs inside one `Tiff::parse` — the 9th is rejected by the cap before allocation, and the assertion fails on the unfixed code (9 parse) — plus a reality test that a chain + Exif/GPS children (6 total entries) still parses fully.

Independent review verdict: PASS with three low follow-ups (documented, none blocking): the cap is per parse invocation (`parse_ifd_at` mints a fresh `Ctx`; every current call site is O(1) per file, so the residual is bounded, but the field doc should say so); a chain that crosses the cap truncates silently inside `Tiff::parse`'s existing break-on-error semantics; and the reality-test fixture itself uses an overlapping child offset (assertions unaffected).

title: catalog: resync finds the retry record from the end, not every marker (#2124)
author: eliets2
body:
Closes #2124.

**Bug:** `resync` (the torn-append recovery on library open) scanned **every** occurrence of the `{"seq":` record-start marker in a damaged line, running `from_utf8` + `decode_record` for each. A line made of the marker repeated ~300k times (a ~2 MB damaged log) cost ~10¹¹ operations: 158.7 seconds for one open when it was first measured, and 613 seconds in a later run of the regression test against the old code on a Windows machine. At 16 MB it never finishes.

**Fix:** the writer always appends records newline-terminated and the retry re-encodes the same ops with the same seqs, so only the **last** marker occurrence can be the retry record. `resync` now takes `rposition` of the marker window (requiring `i > 0` so a fragment precedes it, exactly like the old `1..` range). The `seq <= last + 1` gate and the CRC-checked decode are unchanged; recovery behaviour is pinned by the existing exhaustive tear-byte sweep, which still passes.

**Tests:** a 300k-marker line followed by a valid retried record: `Journal::open` finishes in well under a second and still recovers the record (`torn_fragments == 1`, seq continues). The test has a 1 s bound and fails against the old `resync`.

**Assumption to review:** taking the last occurrence relies on no op type being able to emit the marker bytes in the middle of its body. A workspace search found none (a text search, not an exhaustive proof), and the exhaustive tear test would catch a future one.

**Checked locally (Windows):** `cargo test -p lightcraft-catalog` 221 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored; `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask layers`, `assets` and `parity` pass. `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-catalog --all-targets -- -D warnings` stops on one unused import in `crates/catalog/src/store.rs`, which `main` has too; with that lint allowed it is clean. **Not checked:** crates that depend on the catalog (engine, ui-egui) were not built here, and the full `cargo xtask ci` and the wasm check were not run.

author: eliets2
body:
Addresses #2085 for first-time visitors of the browser build (see "What this does not do").

**Bug:** in the browser build the interface always started in English: `default_language()` only read the `LIGHTCRAFT_LANGUAGE` environment variable, which does not exist on wasm, so the starting language resolved to `Locale::En` even when `navigator.languages` held a language the app ships (for example `it-IT`). The desktop build follows the operating system correctly.

**Fix:** `crates/ui-egui` gains an installable default, `set_default_language(Locale)`, and a pure `locale_from_tags(&[String])` that picks the first tag `Locale::parse_tag` accepts (the same parsing the app already uses). `apps/lightcraft-web` resolves `navigator.languages` (falling back to `navigator.language`) at startup in `start()`, before `WebApp::new` builds `UiState`. The browser read goes through the fallible `js_sys::Reflect::get` (the pattern `safety.rs` already uses), so it also works from a worker and silently keeps English where there is no navigator. Desktop never installs the override. No new dependencies: `ui-egui` stays off `web-sys`, and the web app already had `js-sys`.

**What this does not do:**
- It only reaches a first visit. `language` is stored in `ui.json` on every state change, so a returning web user who already has `"language":"en"` stored still starts in English; nothing re-reads the browser later.
- LightCraft has no "Auto" entry in the language setting (`panels/settings.rs` only offers `Locale::ALL`), so this is a better starting default, not an Auto mode. A real Auto (for example `Option<Locale>`) would be a separate change.

title: Decoder memory budgets: header-only GIF/BMP/JXL sizes, byte budgets, tile and lossy-JPEG limits (#2116, #2117, #2118, #2125)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Closes #2116, closes #2117, closes #2118, closes #2125.

A few-KB file could make the import probe or a decode allocate gigabytes from its header alone and abort the app. This bounds each of those paths before anything is allocated.

## Codecs (#2116, #2125)
- **GIF, BMP and JPEG XL sizes come from their headers.** `read_header` used to do a full-size decode for these formats; the 35-byte GIF from #2116 (32768² logical screen) asked for ~20 GiB. GIF/BMP up to 4 MP still have their pixel data read into a scratch buffer, so truncated small files are refused as before. JPEG XL needs a complete first keyframe.
- **`DecodeOptions::max_bytes`** (default 4 GiB, `#[serde(default)]`): the sample buffer a format decoder allocates from the header. GIF/BMP check it before the `image` crate allocates. The `tiff` and `png` limits use it instead of `max_pixels × 32` / `× 8` (32 GiB / 8 GiB).
- **TIFF counts SamplesPerPixel.** More than 32 bytes of samples a pixel is refused, in the header read and in the decode (4000 samples at 1 MP was a 4 GB buffer from a few KB).
- **Default `max_pixels` is now 512 MP** (was 1 Gpx), Lightroom Classic's own limit.
- The full-size float, alpha and CMYK buffers in `convert.rs` and PNG's output buffer are allocated with `try_reserve_exact`, so a refused allocation is `Error::TooLarge` instead of an abort (on systems that refuse, e.g. Windows; an overcommitting Linux can still OOM-kill).

title: engine: stop the export batch's lane queue on every scope exit (#2132)
author: eliets2
body:
Closes #2132.

**Bug:** `run_batch_with` drove its export lanes from inside `std::thread::scope`, and `queue.stop()` only ran after the caller's `placed()` closure returned — so a panic from `progress` or from `placer.place` left the lane threads waiting on the condvar forever: the scope's implicit join never returned, and the command's last-resort `catch_unwind` never got control. Any future panic in placement or progress reporting would turn into a permanently busy export task (and a stuck UI if awaited).

**Fix:** a `StopOnDrop` guard created before the work starts stops the queue on **any** scope exit — normal return, early `?`, or panic unwind. `stop` is idempotent (poison-tolerant lock + flag + `notify_all`, serialized with the lanes' check-then-wait by the same mutex), so the happy path's explicit stop is unchanged and the double stop is a no-op. `guard::catch` on the lane threads is unaffected — it only wraps per-photo work, never `progress`/`placer.place` on the calling thread.

**Tests:** the regression test pins hang-freedom for real: four photos with two lanes make the hang actually reachable (after `result(0)` sets `placed = 1`, a lane drains the run-ahead photos and parks at `next = 3`; the panic at `progress(1)` fires before it can advance), the batch runs on its own thread behind a `recv_timeout` so unfixed code fails with "export hung" in seconds instead of hanging CI, and the payload is asserted via `guard::panic_message`. **Machine-verified both ways: fails on the unfixed code in 10.0 s with the timeout message, passes on the fix in ~1.7 s.**

Notes: `tests_export::same_folder_as_original_exports_next_to_each_photo` fails on Windows with mixed path separators independently of this change (reproduced on clean f34c7a8a). One pre-existing clippy warning on the 1.99 toolchain (`extra_unused_lifetimes` on the `impl<'a> Drop for StopOnDrop<'_>` — the `<'a>` is droppable) can ride a follow-up.

title: Imported profiles: read and delete only the library's own copies in Profiles/ (#2123)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Closes #2123 (the LUT profile part; see "Not in this PR").

`prefs.json` records each imported LUT profile's file path, and the library trusted it:
- **Read path:** `register_all` ran `std::fs::read_to_string(&p.file)` on library open, synchronously and with no size cap or containment check. A crafted path made that hang or exhaust memory: `/dev/zero`, a FIFO, or a UNC share (NTLM exposure on Windows).

- **`read_cube`:** reads with a 64 MiB cap. A 129³ LUT, the largest size in common use, is about 60 MB of text.
- **Delete:** removes only that copy, and only when no other remaining profile resolves to the same file.
- **`register_all` takes the `Profiles` folder of the library being opened.** During `open_stores`, `s.library` is still the previous library (or `None`), so resolving through it pointed at the wrong folder.

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: smooth fitted tone curves; DRO lowering follows Sony's curve between knots
author: cyberhirsch
body:
## Problem

On Sony ARWs (ILCE-7CM2, DRO Auto) the default render showed posterization at 100 %: skin, hair and satin turned into flat patches with hard edges where the camera JPEG is smooth. It got worse with strong slider edits (Contrast / Highlights / Shadows −100), but it is already there at default settings. Same symptom as #1369. #454 and #1904 might share the cause; I haven't checked those files.

## Cause

Two problems in the per-photo camera tone curve (`camera_preview.rs`):

1. **The fitted curve itself can bend sharply.** Quantile matching puts the knots where the photo's pixels are. In a dark scene in front of a bright, clipped screen, most of the 32 knots land in the shadows and one or a few segments cover the brighter stops. Matching against a JPEG the camera tone-mapped locally (DRO) also bends the curve where no global curve bends. On one ILCE-7CM2 portrait the fitted curve's log-log slope went 1.49, **0.59**, 1.31 and 0.66, 0.97, **2.49** over neighbouring segments at skin luminance (up to ×2.57 between neighbours). Gradients across that stretch get squeezed, then stretched.
2. **DRO lowering only touched the knots.** `with_dro_off_tone` set each knot to `min(fitted, Sony DRO-off)`. Between two knots far apart, here one segment spanning about three stops, Sony's curve runs far below the fitted straight segment. So the curve jumped from Sony's curve to the fitted one at the second-last knot, right at skin luminance. In one case: scene 0.04 → display 131 (fitted) where Sony's curve gives 76.

## Fix

- **`with_smooth_tone`** (new; runs on every fitted look, before DRO):
  - evaluates the curve on a grid even in log scene luminance;
  - blurs its log-log slope with a Gaussian (σ = 0.5 in ln scene luminance, about ⅔ stop);
  - integrates back, keeping both ends;
  - puts the result on 32 knots spaced evenly in log scene luminance.

  The shoulder past the last knot keeps the fitted rate: the second-last knot is raised where needed, and that raise is eas…

author: PierrunoYT
body:
Closes #2122.

bb9d3d40 (#1502) stopped the `<name>.tmp` staging files from being written through a link. Files opened in place still followed a link planted at their name. This needs write access to the library folder: a shared or synced library, one unpacked from an archive, or another local user.
- **Lock owner note:** `catalog.lock.owner` → victim overwrote the victim with lock JSON on every open.
- **`catalog.log`:** `catalog.log` → victim emptied it in `Journal::open` (`truncate(LOG, 0)`), and later edits were appended into it.
- **`prefs.json`:** `prefs.json` → `~/.ssh/id_rsa` failed to parse, and the key was copied into the library as `prefs.json.corrupt-…`.

**`catalog::safe_file`: three new helpers, std only, no `unsafe`, no `libc`.** `open_existing`, `open_or_create` and `read_no_follow` work in three steps:
1. `lstat` the name and refuse a link, FIFO (whose open would block) or device with `InvalidInput`.
2. Open it.

title: Develop settings: limits on every list (masks, strokes, samples, spots, red eye, ...) (#2121)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Closes #2121 (both parts the triage bot listed: unbounded lists, and sidecar `lc:settings` not checked on import).

Develop settings had no bound on their lists, and each item costs per-pixel work or a full-size plane at render time. Settings arrive as JSON from sidecars (`lc:settings`), presets, `develop.merge`, `render --settings` and the catalog snapshot. 2,000 tiny linear masks in ~200 KB of JSON asked for 2,000 × 64 MB planes at 4096². 10⁶ empty strokes meant 10⁶ full-plane blends, and 10⁶ colour samples meant 10⁶ operations per pixel, which trips the Windows GPU watchdog.

## Changes
- **`crates/develop/src/settings.rs`:** a `MAX_*` limit for every list, far past what an edit uses:

  | List | Limit |
  |---|---|
  | masks | 100 |
  | components per mask | 64 |
  | colour samples (the UI's and Lightroom's limit) | 5 |
  | strokes per brush | 2,000 |
  | points / pressure per stroke | 100,000 |
  | spots | 1,000 |
  | points per spot | 10,000 |
  | red eye corrections | 64 |
  | curve points | 256 |
  | guides | 16 |
  | Object clicks | 256 |
  | People parts | 32 |
  | point colours (the existing `MAX_POINT_COLORS`) | 8 |
  | disabled sections | 64 |

- **`capped::<N>`** is a `deserialize_with` on every list. It keeps the first N items and skips the rest with `IgnoredAny`, without building them, so parsing a huge list costs neither memory nor time. Because it works at the serde level it covers every JSON path, including the sidecar import and the catalog snapshot, which deserializes `DevelopSettings` directly and doesn't pass through `from_json`.
- **`DevelopSettings::over_list_limits` / `cap_lists`** handle settings built in code, such as a script adding masks one command at a time.
- **`Catalog::apply` caps an `Op::SetDevelop` that is over the limits.** Every edit and interactive preview passes through it. The check is a length walk, and settings within the limits are kept as the same `Arc` with no copy.

title: SAM 3 worker: token handshake, concurrent handshakes, survive accept errors (#2134)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Closes #2134.

The remote SAM 3 worker (`lightcraft-sam3-worker`, docs/ai-masks.md → Remote Metal inference) had three problems:
- **No authentication:** any local process could hold it for 10 minutes or use the GPU.
- **Impostors:** a process bound to the editor's port while the SSH tunnel was down received the photo and could return any mask.
- **Fragile accept loop:** one transient accept error (`EMFILE`, `ECONNABORTED`) ended the worker.

## Changes (`crates/segment/src/remote.rs`)
- **Mutual token handshake.** Both ends read `LIGHTCRAFT_SAM3_WORKER_TOKEN` (16+ characters) and run this exchange before any request or pixels:
  1. The editor sends a nonce.
  2. The worker replies with its own nonce and an HMAC-SHA256 of both under the token.
  3. The editor checks it and answers with its own HMAC.

  Proofs are compared in constant time, and the token never crosses the socket. A plain token sent in the clear (the issue's suggestion) would hand the token to exactly the impostor the issue describes, so this goes one step further.
- **Token without a configured variable:** the worker generates one for the run and prints it. Nonces and the generated token come from std's `RandomState`, which is keyed from the OS RNG, so no new random crate is needed. HMAC is built on `sha2`, which is already a workspace dependency.
- **`accept_authenticated`:** handshakes run on their own threads, at most 32 at a time, with a 10 s deadline. Only authenticated streams reach the session loop, which still serves one editor at a time because there's one model and one Metal device. A silent peer no longer holds the worker.
- **Accept errors** are logged, followed by a 100 ms pause, and the loop continues.
- **The client** (`Client::connect`) runs the handshake under a 10 s timeout, then switches to the existing 9-minute request timeout. Its signature is unchanged.
- `docs/ai-masks.md` covers the token setup and what it protects; `docs/whats-new.md` has an entry.

title: denoise-serve: auth deadline over the whole first line; per-address back-off after bad tokens (#2133)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Closes #2133.

`lightcraft-cli denoise-serve` had two problems:
- **Slot holding:** it applied its 120 s read timeout per read call, and also before authentication. A peer sending one byte every ~100 s kept a connection slot for days, and eight of them (`max_connections`) shut the server.
- **Token guessing:** a bad token only closed the connection, so on a LAN tokens could be guessed at line rate.

## Changes (`crates/denoise/src/remote.rs`)
- **Auth deadline over the whole first line.** A `Deadline` reader sets the socket timeout to the time left before every read, so until its token is accepted a connection has `ServerOptions::auth_timeout` (default `AUTH_TIMEOUT`, 10 s) in all, however slowly the bytes arrive. After the first good token it switches to the configured `timeout`, as before.
- **Per-address back-off.** After a bad token the address is refused at accept for 1 s, doubling with each further bad token up to 5 min. A good token clears it, and at most 4,096 addresses are remembered, with expired ones dropped first.
- `docs/denoise.md` and `docs/whats-new.md` describe both limits.

What was already right stays as it was: the token is checked before any payload, the comparison is constant-time, payload and inflation are capped, and a non-loopback bind warns.

## Tests
- `a_trickling_peer_is_cut_off_at_the_auth_deadline`:
  - A peer writing one byte every 100 ms is closed soon after a 600 ms auth deadline.
  - A client with the token is unaffected and keeps its connection past that deadline.
- `bad_tokens_back_off_the_address`:
  - After a bad token, the same address is refused even with the right token.
  - After the back-off it's served, and a good token resets the count.
  - The wait doubles up to the cap.

The existing remote tests and the engine's remote-denoise test pass. Clippy on `lightcraft-denoise` (`-D warnings`), `cargo check -p lightcraft-cli` and `cargo xtask wasm` are clean.

title: Open Original: only file types LightCraft reads reach the system opener
author: skylartaylor
body:
# Open Original: only file types LightCraft reads reach the system opener

Fixes the launcher half of #2135.

`Open Original` and `Edit In` handed any path to the platform's opener, with `Path::is_file()` as the
only check. An imported Lightroom catalog decides those paths, so a `.lrcat` naming
`C:\…\evil.exe`, a `.lnk`, a `.bat`, or an `.app`/`.command` on macOS got it executed on one click.

A new engine gate, `lightcraft_engine::open_path`, now stands between any catalog-derived path and
the opener:

- the menu's enablement predicate requires `is_media`, so the extension alone decides and no disk
  or share is touched while a menu is drawn;
- the edit-copy path goes through `openable`, which also returns the absolute path;
- Lightroom catalog import drops originals that are not media, so a refused entry never becomes an
  openable library record.

Two tests fail without the change.

## Scope

This deliberately does **not** touch the `app` parameter on `photo.editInExternal` /
`photo.openOriginalInExternal` (`menus.rs:2303` and `:2397`). That is #2115 — a different vector
(the program, not the document path) — and is better fixed separately with the `ui.set` side.

The network-path half of #2135 was already closed separately: catalog paths now resolve through
`craft-docpath`, so a `\\host\share\…` original is refused at import. What remained, and what this
fixes, is a path to a *local* executable.

## Second commit

`e6587c3f` is unrelated: three rustc 1.96 clippy lints (`nonminimal_bool` ×2 in `slide_overlay.rs`,
a `drop()` on a non-`Drop` closure in `tests_export.rs`) that make `cargo xtask ci` fail on `main`
regardless of this change. Kept separate so it is obvious it is not part of the fix. With it,
`cargo xtask ci` passes all 8 stages.

title: Release workflow: pin the shared release workflow to a commit; Dependabot bumps it (#2126)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Closes #2126 (the repository side; the rest is settings, see below).

`release.yml` passes every code-signing secret to `storytold/craft-common-actions/.github/workflows/release.yml@main`: the Apple certificate and notarisation credentials, the Windows certificate, and Azure Trusted Signing. Anyone who can push to (or compromises) that repository's `main` would receive them on the next push to `release`, and could ship signed binaries.

## Changes
- **`release.yml`** calls the shared workflow at `43f4e83c68764f9d880f8a6c10328bc550465f2b`, the commit `main` points at today, so release behaviour doesn't change. The comment now explains why this one is pinned.
  - **This reverses the `@main` choice for this one workflow only.** The old comment said tracking `@main` was intentional, so that org-wide improvements propagate (#967). That still holds for `freebsd.yml` and `windows-arm64.yml`, which get no secrets, so they stay on `@main` as the issue suggests.
- **`.github/dependabot.yml`** sets up weekly, grouped `github-actions` updates. They propagate improvements to the release workflow through one reviewable PR, and also keep the other SHA-pinned actions current.
- **`docs/releasing.md`** describes the pin and that its bump should be reviewed against the craft-common-actions diff. `docs/whats-new.md` has an entry.

## Not in a PR: repository settings the issue also recommends
- Protect `craft-common-actions` `main`: required review, no force-push.
- Give the `release` environment (where docs/releasing.md says the signing secrets live) required reviewers, so a signing run waits for a person.

The ticket bot marked this as shared by other craft apps, so they would want the same pin.

`release.yml` and `dependabot.yml` parse as YAML. The workflow itself only runs on a push to `release`, so it wasn't run here.

title: Negative Craft: turn a scanned film negative into a normal photo
author: FugLong
body:
## What this is

Negative Craft turns a scan of a film negative into a normal photo. You photograph or scan the negative, and LightCraft prints the picture. It works for color negatives and black-and-white negatives.

It is meant to do the job that Negative Lab Pro does in Lightroom. Negative Lab Pro was not opened, copied, measured, or studied while this was built. The conversion is LightCraft's own.

## How to turn it on

Negative Craft stays hidden until you ask for it.

1. Open a photo and press `E` for **Edit**.
2. Choose **Window ▸ Edit Sections ▸ Negative Craft**.
3. The section appears above **Light**, and it stays there on later photos. The menu item stays checked.
4. Choose **Color Neg** or **B&W**, then click **Convert**.

To put it away, right-click the **Negative Craft** header and choose **Hide Negative Craft**. A photo you have already converted still shows the section, so you can keep working on that print.

## Getting a good print

Leave a strip of the blank film around the picture in the scan. **Convert** reads that border and builds the photo from it. A pale border is fine. A border that is pure white is clipped, and the orange film base is no longer in the file.

If scanning with a camera: Lock the camera's white balance for the whole roll (Daylight works) and use the same exposure, aperture, and ISO. A raw file keeps the film color more faithfully than a JPEG of the same negative.

After **Convert**, leave **Contrast** at **1**, then set **Exposure** and **Blacks**. The full scanning and printing steps are in `docs/user/guides/convert-a-negative.md`.

## What it does not do

- It cannot invent the blank film if the scan is cropped tight to the picture. **Match roll** does not fill that in. Each frame needs its own border.
- It does not ship a measured profile for each film stock. **Color Neg**, **B&W**, and the scan type (**Camera**, **Minilab**, **Flat**) are the choices.
- Slides are already positives, so they are not on this panel.

title: catalog: history steps and versions share segmentation grids (#2154)
author: eliets2
body:
## Bug

Every history step (and version) serialized its own copy of every segmentation grid of the photo. A photo with AI masks re-stored every unchanged grid (a 1024×1024 grid is about 220 KB serialized) with every slider change, because a step's `DevelopSettings` differ from the previous step's only in a slider value while the masks are byte-identical. On the reporter's library, 183.6 MB of a 187.8 MB `catalog.snap` was masks inside history steps — 830 copies of only 126 distinct grids — and each further slider change added another ~2.7 MB.

## Fix

Snapshots deduplicate: each distinct grid is stored once in `Catalog.grids` (format **v10**), and the masks in the photo's develop settings, versions, history steps and import look refer to it by index (`SegMask.grid`, with `data` omitted). The import look is included because a user default preset that contains masks writes them into the import look at import.

- `write_snapshot` collects the distinct grids (first-appearance order) from every settings holder of every photo (`Photo::settings_holders`) into the table, and serializes a shallow clone of the catalog under a thread-local interner, so masks whose exact bytes are in the table serialize as `{"side":N,"grid":i,"rect":…}`. The clone copies one pointer per photo (photos are `Arc`-shared); the other tables are copied.
- `Catalog::repair` (run on every snapshot load, by `Journal::open` and `Catalog::from_snapshot`) resolves the references in the same holders back to inline data and drops the table, so **the live catalog never changes shape**: rendering, `hash64`, cache keys, presets, XMP sidecars, log records, undo/redo and MCP are untouched. Grids serialize exactly as before everywhere outside snapshot writes.
- A reference past the table (a damaged snapshot) is cleared and reported in `LoadReport::repaired`; the mask renders nothing, like any other damaged grid. No panics on hostile input.
- Catalogs written before v10 load and are upgraded exactly as every earlie…

title: LR-BEHAV-DRAGDROP: photo drags say what a drop will do, refuse what it can't, and Esc gives them up
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

Why one PR: one drag-and-drop contract for photo drags (every row says what a drop does, refuses what it cannot take, and Esc gives the drag up); 984 changed lines, of which 494 tests, 272 translations, 20 docs, so about 198 lines of code. Album rows, Keyword List rows and the refused rows share `grid::drag_hint` and `grid::refuse_drop` / `left::refuse_photos` and Esc ending a drag (`LightcraftApp::end_drags`) is the same contract, so a part would leave some rows on the old rules.

## Problem

Each drop target decided on its own what to show while photos were dragged over it, so the most common drag had the weakest feedback:

- **Esc did nothing to a photo drag.** It cancels album, sidebar-section and keyword drags, but after Esc, letting go over an album still added the photos.
- **Only Folders rows said what a drop would do** ("Move 3 photos to “Trip”"). Over an album or a Keyword List row the label still said "3 photos".
- **Rows that can't take photos looked like empty space.** A smart album, an album folder, the sidebar's Keywords rows, and a keyword dragged over its own child all kept the grab cursor and drew nothing; letting go did nothing, silently.
- **A drop that changed nothing still counted as an edit.** Dropping photos on an album that already held them toasted "Added 0 photos to “Garden”" and added an Undo step; the Keyword List did the same.

## Change

- **Esc** ends any drag (photos, album, sidebar section, keyword), and only the drag: it no longer also runs Esc's own command (Back), and it no longer closes a dialog that opened during the drag. A drag can't outlive the mouse button any more: one started just before entering full screen or a slideshow used to stay "active" there.
- **Album rows** say how many photos a drop adds ("Add 2 photos to “Garden”"), or "Already in “Garden”" when the album holds them all; letting go then runs nothing (no undo step, no toast). When some were already there, the toast says so ("Added 1 photo to “Gard…

title: LR-IMP-DRAGDROP: files dragged over the window show what a drop will do, and a drop opens the import review
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

Why one PR: the overlay shown while files are dragged over the window says what the drop will do, and the drop routing does exactly that; landing one without the other would show an overlay that promises something else. About 350 lines of code, 231 of tests and 208 of translations.


## Problem

Dropping files from Finder or Explorer is the first drag a new user tries, and the empty library invites it. But:

- **Nothing reacted while files were over the window.** Nothing handled egui's `hovered_files`.
- **A drop imported at once,** skipping the review File ▸ Import opens (add / copy / move, destination, preset). Lightroom opens its Import dialog on a drop. The LR-BEHAV-EMPTY-STATES row listed both as gaps.

## Change

- **While files hover,** the window dims and a card says what letting go will do, sorted the same way the drop sorts them: "Drop to review 3 items for import", "Drop to import 2 presets", "Drop to open the face model" (one line each), or just "Drop to import" when the system doesn't say what the files are. title: Presets change only the settings they name (fixes #2159)
author: eliets2
body:
Closes #2159

## Bug

A preset was deep-merged into the photo's current settings. A second preset therefore inherited what an earlier preset (or a manual edit) had left in the settings it styles, and its amount was measured from the visible values. From #2159: applying a black and white preset and then a colour preset left the photo black and white.

The first version of this change composed whole groups on the photo's import state. That reset every setting of a group that a preset did not name (Blacks under Bright & Airy, mixer colours the preset leaves out, imported exposure, whites and blacks under Crisp Landscape). This head changes only the settings a preset names.

## Fix

- A preset changes only the settings it names. Each named setting is computed from the photo's import look when a default preset recorded one, otherwise from the photo's current value; at 100 % it takes the preset's value. Every setting the preset does not name keeps the photo's current value, edits included.
- A photo without an import look (its settings came from an XMP sidecar or a catalog import, which record none) composes on its current settings, so a preset does not reset imported values it does not name.
- Pixel repairs (masks, spots, red eye) compose on the photo's own values, as before. Masks named by a preset are still added.
- The built-in colour presets name their treatment, so applying one after a black and white preset brings the colours back.
- Amount: each named number moves from its base (the import look, or the current value when none is recorded) towards the preset's value. Amount 0 applies nothing to a photo without an import look. For a photo with an import look, amount 0 gives the look's value for the settings the preset names; this is a maintainer decision (see Not verified).
- `preset.apply`, the hover previews and the thumbnails in the Presets panel all use one function, `Session::preset_applied`.

title: Masking: outline every visible mask when the all-masks overlay is on
author: csy2006
body:
## Summary
Ctrl+Shift+O (the all-masks overlay) shows each visible mask's painted region at once, but only the selected mask drew its white outline — the others showed coverage without the boundary line. This extends #919 so that, while the all-masks overlay is active, every visible Radial/Linear mask also draws its outline (the same way the selected mask already does).

Handles and the rotation grip stay on the selected mask only, so nothing else becomes draggable.

## Motivation
I tried this out on the v0.8.0 release first: the all-masks overlay there only outlines the one selected mask, which made it hard to see at a glance where each mask's boundary falls. Drawing every visible mask's outline at once reads much better, so I decided to make it the behaviour for the all-masks overlay.

## Changes
- `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/detail.rs` (`mask_overlay`): relax the outline guard from `sel` to `sel || (mask_overlay_all && m.visible)`. Outline stroke alpha is 230 for the selected mask and 170 for the others to keep them distinguishable; handles/rotation grip remain wrapped in `if sel`.
- No pipeline (`visualize.rs`) changes — the outline is an egui foreground overlay; the all-masks overlay still only fills alpha.

## Scope / limitations
Outlines are drawn for `Radial` and `Linear` masks, which have a vector shape. Raster/parametric masks (Brush, Object/SAM, Subject, Sky, Color Range, …) have no vector path, so this does not draw outlines for them; that would need boundary extraction from the alpha plane (marching squares) and is left for a separate change.

## Testing
`cargo check -p lightcraft-ui-egui` passes. Manual: open a photo with several visible Radial/Linear masks, press Ctrl+Shift+O, confirm each visible mask shows its white outline while only the selected one shows handles.

Extends #919.

title: LR-IMP-DUPES: speed up folder imports with header reads and on-demand hashing
author: lightcraft-fork
body:
## Problem

Adding a folder of large raw photos is slow because LightCraft reads every file in full before adding it to the library. Even **Add** mode, which leaves files where they are, must read the entire collection from the drive.

Related to [#832](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/832).

Importing the same folder of **2,428 Fujifilm RAF photos** into separate empty libraries took:

| Build | Import time |
|---|---|
| Original build (`6e1880ca`) | **About 36m 54s**; 2,428 photos saved, no reported library error. |
| [Changed build](https://github.com/lightcraft-fork/lightcraft/commit/49e299656c3f3da96ce67ed7b6a7248666525ccd) | **3m 4.463s**; 2,428 imported, no failures or duplicates, library saved. |

Observed elapsed time was roughly **12× shorter**. Both runs used Add mode. The original was timed externally within a 1.021-second interval (36m 53.769s–36m 54.790s); the changed build used its import lifecycle log. A CI build overlapped the changed run. This is an observed comparison, not a controlled cold-cache benchmark.

> **Dependency:** this draft includes four commits from an earlier revision of unmerged #1735, plus this follow-up. Current `main` has been merged and the conflicts resolved. The dependency must still be reconciled after #1735 lands; this is not ready to merge.

## Why it happens

Import needs metadata, dimensions and preview locations, which can often be read from raw headers alone. Instead, the old path reads the whole file to compute a **content hash**—a fingerprint of all its bytes—for duplicate detection, copy verification and cache lookup. Every photo pays that cost upfront, even if the user never opens it.

## Design

Read only what import needs. Compute missing fingerprints during existing full-file reads, using the same bytes.

- **Add:** use the header probe; keep the photo hashless until a full read is needed.
- **Copy:** hash while streaming the source to its destination; keep copy verification.
- **Move:** use a hard…

title: LR-EDIT-OPTICS-PROFILE: look up Nikon DSLR lenses by their lens specification
author: nerdislb
body:
## Summary

Nikon DSLRs write no Exif `LensModel` — only the lens specification in their maker note (tag `0x0084`, which `lightcraft_meta` already reads into `lens_spec`, see #1590). `lens_profiles::lookup` returned `None` as soon as `lens_model` was missing, so the lensfun-format lens database (`LIGHTCRAFT_LENSFUN_DIR`) never corrected a Nikon DSLR raw, whatever lens was on it.

This PR lets such files look the lens up by a name built from the specification:

- `lightcraft_lensdb::spec_name([24, 70, 2.8, 2.8])` → `"24-70mm f/2.8"` (`"18-55mm f/3.5-5.6"`, `"85mm f/1.8"`).
- `Profile::names_exactly(name)`: one of the profile's names equals `name` (same tokens as the existing matcher, so case and punctuation don't matter; the maker's words count).
- `lens_profiles::lookup`: with a lens model nothing changes; without one, the spec name goes through `find_lens` and is accepted **only** when `names_exactly` confirms it.

## Why exact matches only

The specification says nothing about the maker: `24-70mm f/2.8` fits a Nikkor, a Sigma, a Tamron, a Tokina… With the stock lensfun database the best partial match for it is the *Sigma 24-70mm f/2.8 EX DG Macro* (score 0.625, an APS-C calibration) — a wrong profile would be worse than none. Maker-named entries are refused too ("Samyang 85mm f/1.4" is not "85mm f/1.4"). So a stock database changes nothing for these files; a user who owns one lens with that specification can name its lensfun entry that way (an extra `<model>24-70mm f/2.8</model>`), and their raws are then corrected automatically. A lens picker / per-photo lens choice (as started in #930) would be the friendlier follow-up; this PR is only the lookup.

## How tested

- New tests: `crates/lensdb/src/tests.rs` `spec_names_read_like_lens_names`, `spec_names_need_an_exact_profile_name`; `crates/engine/src/lens_profiles.rs` `lens_specification_needs_a_profile_named_by_it` (fails without the change: a file with only a lens specification finds no profile).

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR-CHOICE: Calibrated camera colour, a per-photo choice of a raw's starting colour
author: good-news-everyone
body:
## What

A first step toward #1207. A raw without colour matrices of its own (NEF, ARW, CR3, …) starts from a look fitted to its embedded JPEG. Its model's matrices from measured spectral sensitivities are only used when that fit fails. This adds a per-photo choice:

- **Profile ▸ Calibrated camera colour**, shown for a raw without matrices whose camera model has spectral matrices (`camera_preview::colorimetric_camera`). It sets `profile.camera_colour` to `colorimetric`. Unticked is `auto`, today's order, and is left out of the settings, so existing edits keep their JSON and hash and every cached preview stays valid.
- **Colorimetric never reads the embedded JPEG:** no per-photo fit, no camera profile's tone, no black-and-white tone. It starts from the spectral matrices with LightCraft's default tone curve, i.e. step 4 of the order in `docs/camera-preview-colour.md`, taken first. The same file then starts the same way whatever its JPEG shows (Picture Control, Active D-Lighting, DRO). A model without spectral matrices, or a file with matrices of its own, starts as Auto does, and the option isn't offered.

The data behind it is in #1207: Nikon Z f frames where the fitted curve turns steep in the shadows and posterizes fur and an out-of-focus rug that are smooth in the camera's own JPEG, and where the spectral path keeps more of the range at matched brightness.

## How

- **The option is part of the decode**, since the starting colour is applied while the raw is developed. `media::LoadOptions` (only the colour for now) reaches the file and pair loaders through `SourceRef::File`. `FileLoader` and `PairLoader` take it as a new argument, and `load_bytes_with` / `load_vec_with` sit beside `load_bytes` / `load_vec`.
- **Cache:** a `DecodedSource` records the options it was made with. `source_ref` decodes again when a cached source was made with others, and `Session::accept` doesn't take back a late render made with the old ones. A source the option can't change is reused: `…

title: X-Trans CMOS 4 bodies take the X-T3's spectral matrices
author: smyrgeorge
body:
## Problem

A Fujifilm X-T30 RAF (lossless compressed, shot in Acros) opened with muted, washed-out colour: a grey-blue sky where digiKam shows a deep blue one.

The raw decode is correct (black level 1019, white 16383, data max 14488, no artefacts). The cause is colour:

- The embedded camera JPEG is black and white (Acros), so the per-file look can only fit the tone curve (`monochrome_look`).
- The X-T30 has no spectral matrices, so the colour came from the neutral "camera RGB ≈ sRGB" fallback.

## Fix

`crates/raw/src/spectral.rs` gets a hand-kept `SAME_SENSOR` alias list next to the generated rawtoaces-data table, which says not to edit it by hand. The 26.1 MP X-Trans CMOS 4 bodies use the X-T3's measured matrices: X-T30, X-T30 II, X-Pro3, X100V, X-S10 and X-E4. Their white balance now reads in Kelvin through those matrices, as for other covered models.

Docs: `docs/camera-preview-colour.md`, `docs/raw-parity.md` and `docs/gaps.md` (gap 1) are updated, with revision-history rows.

## Testing

- Lookup tests extended: X-T30, X-T30 II and X100V find the X-T3, and every same-sensor alias resolves through `find_camera`. They fail without the change.
- Rendered the X-T30 sample with `lightcraft-cli render`: blue sky and saturated colours restored; the tone curve still comes from the Acros JPEG.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy and the heif step passed locally. The run was stopped during `cargo test --workspace`, so the workspace tests, parity, layers, assets and wasm steps have not run locally.

title: Lightroom import: skip images whose file record is missing instead of failing
author: bochetech
body:
## Problem

Importing a real Lightroom Classic catalog failed with:

```
Lightroom import failed: invalid parameters for library.importLightroom: image 60455: missing file record
```

The catalog had 82 `Adobe_images` rows whose `rootFile` pointed at an `AgLibraryFile` row that no longer exists. Lightroom leaves these orphans behind and ignores them, but `read_with_progress` returned an error on the first one, so the whole import failed. Missing `AgLibraryFolder` / `AgLibraryRootFolder` records and an empty original path (`incomplete original path`) failed the same way.

## Change

- `crates/engine/src/lightroom_catalog.rs`: such an image is skipped instead of aborting the import, together with its virtual copies (`drop_copies_of`), so `validate` doesn't fail later with `invalid virtual copy master`.
- Skipped images are reported as data, not English text: `skipped` (image id + reason: `missingFile`, `missingFolder`, `missingRoot`, `incompletePath`, `masterSkipped`) in the `library.importLightroom` and `library.inspectLightroom` reports.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/lightroom_import.rs`: the result window adds one line counting them in the UI language (`tr_format!`, all 13 locales); the eight-warning cap is unchanged.
- Docs: `docs/lightroom-catalog-import.md` and the `LRC-LIB-CATALOG-IMPORT` row in `docs/parity-checklist.md`.

## Tests

- `images_with_incomplete_records_are_skipped_not_fatal`: missing file, folder and root records and an empty path, each read from a native SQLite catalog; these used to fail the import.
- `a_virtual_copy_of_a_skipped_master_is_skipped_too`: a two-row `Adobe_images` read through the reader.
- `skipped_images_are_in_the_import_report`
- `skipped_images_are_one_line_in_the_ui_language` (English and Spanish) and `skipped_images_do_not_take_the_warning_slots`

title: Georgian: a symbol Noto Sans Georgian cannot paint
author: Hamza0101
body:
`cargo xtask ci` fails with the `craft-fonts` input supplied — the configuration `CLAUDE.md` says releases always build with:

```
CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=../craft-fonts cargo xtask ci

test i18n::tests::catalog_characters_are_paintable ... FAILED
  ka in Proportional (faces: ["Noto Sans Georgian"]) lack glyphs: ✕
```

Two strings in `ka.json` use **✕** (U+2715, heavy multiplication X). Noto Sans Georgian has no glyph for it and egui's bundled fonts do not either, so a Georgian reader gets a blank where the text describes the activity stack's stop control.

Without the fonts input those twenty tests skip, so a plain `cargo xtask ci` is green and this stays invisible. That is why it has survived.

## The fix

The two Georgian **values** use `×` (U+00D7) instead. It reads the same at text size and every face has it — verified by the repo's own test, which passes with the change and fails without it.

The English **keys** are untouched: they are the source text from `docs/whats-new.md`, and `catalog_characters_are_paintable` checks `messages.values()`, which is the right scope. An English reader's font covers ✕; the problem is only a translation carrying it into a script whose face does not.

## And a guard, since the repo already has one for this

`translated_catalogs_do_not_use_missing_menu_triangles` already forbids `▸` and `▾` in locale JSON, with the same reasoning ("a translation must not carry a symbol no installed font has"). ✕ joins them in one `UNPAINTABLE` list, so the next translation to reach for it is caught by a cheap test rather than by the font-dependent one.

That matters here: ✕ is in the English source of those two strings, so **every** language that translates them next would hit the same failure. Only `ka` has translated them so far.

## Verified

| | |
|---|---|
| `catalog_characters_are_paintable` with fonts | fails before, passes after |
| the extended guard | catches ✕ when I put it back (`uses the unpaintable '✕'`) |
| all `i18n::tests` | 36 passed, …

title: Library: Refuse an unknown filter key in catalog.query and library.filter (#2241)

body:
`catalog.query` and `library.filter` dropped any filter key they didn't know, so a typo like `cameraModel` gave back the whole library with `ok: true`. A script that then exports or keywords the result works on every photo.

title: Lightroom catalog import: turn masks into the photo's upright frame
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1806.

Lightroom stores mask positions on the image as the camera recorded it, before the photo is turned upright, the same way it stores the crop. The catalog import already converts the crop (`catalog_crop`), but it copied masks over unchanged and LightCraft placed them on the upright photo, so on a vertical shot (EXIF 6 or 8) every gradient, radial and brush came in 90° off, and on a 180° or mirrored photo they landed on the opposite side. @David990's XMP showed it clearly (thanks!): a Z 9 portrait with orientation 8, AI masks stored at 2880 × 1920, and a "horizon" gradient that varies along the sensor's long side.

`catalog_masks` now runs right after `catalog_crop` and puts masks through the same orientation the crop uses (`Orientation::map` on normalized coordinates): linear start/end, radial centre and brush points move; a radial's radii (in long-edge units) swap when the axes do; a mirror negates the radial's angle. The radii are now worked out with the stored image's aspect (`fileWidth / fileHeight`, as the crop already is): before, the import used LightCraft's own size of the photo, which for a photo already in the library is the upright one, so on a vertical shot a circle came in as a 2.25:1 ellipse. A quarter turn keeps the angle as it is, since an ellipse turned 90° is the same ellipse with its radii swapped, so this holds whatever the angle's sign convention is. Subject, sky and range masks carry no positions and are untouched.

What's left of #1806:
- The wrong crop on vertical shots isn't explained yet: with the reporter's values the crop lands where expected. Waiting for the reporter's sample files (DNG + catalog + export) to tell.
- The straighten angle shown with the opposite sign is LightCraft's convention, not a bug (Lightroom's sign gives the wrong crop size against Lightroom's own exports).

Not changed here:
- XMP sidecars go through the same mask reader but don't convert the crop to the upright frame either; #1386 adds that frame to…

title: Detail: The Before view waits for its own render instead of flashing the edits (#2248)
author: endthestart
body:
With the Before view on, stepping to an edited photo showed the edits for a moment before switching to the Before. The loupe falls back to stand-ins (the cached render, the thumbnail) while a render is on its way, and those carry the photo's current edits, so the Before side showed the After until its own render landed.

Now the Before side only uses a stand-in when the photo's settings are the same as its Before settings. Otherwise it waits for its own render and says "Rendering…" in the meantime, the same as the After side does when it has nothing to show yet.

I added a headless test that holds the renders, steps to an edited photo with the Before view on and checks that no edited stand-in is drawn. It fails on main with the cached render showing.

Let me know if you'd rather fix it another way. Thank you.

Fixes #2248

title: LR-META-XMP: fewer false "XMP adjustments were not imported" warnings for Lightroom raws
author: mattsivak
body:
Split out of #2008 at @nledford's suggestion, so it can land on its own while the bell is reviewed in #1642.

## Why

Importing raws with Lightroom Classic XMP sidecars warned "XMP adjustments were not imported for …" for every photo, listing fields like `CameraProfileDigest`, `LensProfileDigest` and `CompatibleVersion`. Most of them are Lightroom's own bookkeeping, not edits LightCraft failed to apply. On a ~1,100-photo Lightroom import nearly every photo was listed.

`crates/engine/src/crs.rs`. These fields no longer count as unimported adjustments:
- `CompatibleVersion`, `CameraProfileDigest`, `LensProfileDigest`

- `CropConstrainToUnitSquare` (a crop tool option, not the crop)
- `LensProfileDistortionScale` / `LensProfileVignettingScale` when they are at their default of 100

`Look`, unknown fields and a lens profile's strength away from 100 % are still reported.

Docs: the `LR-META-XMP` row in `docs/parity-checklist.md` (and its revision history), and What's New.

## Testing

- New test `crs::tests::lightroom_profile_bookkeeping_is_not_reported`: what Lightroom Classic writes next to every raw's edit gives no unmapped fields; with a `crs:Look` it still reports `Look`; `LensProfileDistortionScale="60"` is still reported. It fails without the change.

body:
**Stacked on #1642** (nledford's bell, `tasks-bell` at `83c733e9`). Review only the commits after `83c733e9`; until #1642 lands, the diff against `main` also shows its commit. The `crs.rs` fix (fewer false import warnings) is its own PR off `main`: #2257.

## Why

A long toast covered the photos. A Lightroom raw import listed every photo's "XMP adjustments were not imported for …: …" in the toast, which filled the canvas for 8 s and then was gone for good, with no way to read it again.

## What this adds on top of #1642

title: LRC-DEV-PROCESS: process V3, over-range colors keep their hue and saturation
author: robmdunn
body:
Moved here from #2093 (which now carries the Nikon camera profiles). This no longer depends on #2092.

Colours brighter than the output can show are moved toward their luminance until they fit. That keeps their brightness and gives up their colour, so bright saturated reds pushed up turn pink. Measured on a sunlit red flower pushed 2.5 EV: CIE hue 25° and C\* 48, against the camera JPEG's 33° and 83. The raw isn't clipped (red peaks at 16 % of the sensor range); the pink comes from the finish stage.

This adds **process V3**. When a colour's brightest channel is above white, that channel becomes white, the darkest channel stays where it is, and the middle one keeps its relative place between them (`finish::hue_clip`). That keeps hue and saturation.

Keeping the hue all the way has two problems:
- blown skies turn light blue where the camera JPEG and V2 show white;
- along a smooth exposure ramp, a saturated colour stays fully saturated right up to white and then switches at a hard edge.

So V3 fades back to the old mapping by the larger of two measures (`finish::hue_fade`):
- the colour's luminance, from 0.35 of white to white (`HUE_FADE_FROM`);
- how far its brightest channel is past white, from 0 to 2 stops (`HUE_FADE_EV`).

The result:
- colours just past white keep their hue;
- sunlit saturated colours keep their light and shade;
- blown skies, and colours far past white, go white gradually.

It applies after the tone map and in the output gamut mapping, where negative channels still move toward luminance, after the limit. It covers the CPU, the GPU (`HUE_CLIP`) and soft proofing. Colours within range render exactly as on V2. Per `docs/process-versions.md`, photos keep their process until Photo ▸ Update to Current Process; new photos and Reset get V3.

## Exposure ramps

A synthetic linear DNG with 12 saturated hues, a skin tone and grey, each ramping from 3 EV under to 5 EV over. V2 drops into pastel early and abruptly (red to pink, blue to lavender). V3 keeps …

title: LR-IMP-PREVIEW-READ: thumbnails of Lightroom HDR/panorama DNGs develop from their reduced raw copies (38 s → 1 s)
author: mattsivak
body:
## The problem

Grid and filmstrip thumbnails of DNGs that Lightroom merged (HDR, Panorama, HDR Panorama) took tens of seconds each. For a DJI drone panorama (`…-HDR-Pano-2-Pano.dng`, 23836 × 7078, JPEG XL LinearRaw, 132 MB):

| | time |
|---|---|
| 512 px render (`lightcraft-cli render --size 512`) | **38.1 s** (49.5 s CPU) |
| full-size render | 18.8 s |

Every thumbnail developed the whole raw image: `load_bytes_with` decodes the full JPEG XL raster, then fits it down to 512 px. While that ran, the pano's tile stayed blank and held up the thumbnails queued behind it.

These files already carry what a thumbnail needs. Lightroom keeps **reduced-resolution copies of the raw image itself** beside the full one: `NewSubfileType = 1`, `PhotometricInterpretation = LinearRaw`, 2048, 512 and 256 px, each with a matching transparency mask (`NewSubfileType = 5`). They are raw data in the main image's camera space, not rendered previews, so a thumbnail developed from one still applies every edit.

## Changes

- **`lightcraft_raw::decode_reduced(bytes, min_long)` (raw):** for a DNG whose main image is LinearRaw, decodes the smallest reduced copy whose default crop still has a long edge of `min_long` px.
  - It keeps the main image's colour, profile, metadata and levels, using the copy's own `WhiteLevel` / `BlackLevel` where it states them.
  - The active area and default crop are scaled to the copy's size. `metadata.width/height` stay the developed size of the full image.
  - It returns `None` (decode the whole image as before) for any of these:
    - no copy covers `min_long`;
    - the copy's aspect ratio or samples per pixel differ from the main image's;
    - the main image has opcode lists, a linearization table or black-level deltas, which are all in full-size pixel coordinates.
- **`dng::decode_ifd`:** `decode_as` now goes through it. Pixels and storage tags (compression, interleave, linearization) come from the copy; everything else comes from the main raw IFD. A norma…

title: Analyse a photo listed twice once in Assisted Culling
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/cull.rs:23 (analyze: ids come from Session::targets, crates/engine/src/lib.rs:1205, which does not de-duplicate)` (no existing issue): photo.analyze (Assisted Culling) puts a photo into a burst group with itself when its id is listed twice, and the stored analysis then says the photo is not the best of its group.

## Cause
Found by our own testing; there is no issue for this. `photo.analyze` (Assisted Culling) takes its ids from `Session::targets`, which keeps repeated ids. A photo listed twice became two rows with the same capture time and an identical signature, so the burst pass grouped the photo with itself. Two `SetAnalysis` ops were committed, and the later one stored `group: Some(1), best: false`.

## Fix
`analyze` now drops repeated ids before measuring and keeps the first occurrence of each. A repeated photo is analysed once, is not in any group, and gets one `SetAnalysis` op.

## Verified
- Regression test `assisted_culling_ignores_repeated_ids`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib assisted_culling_ignores_repeated_ids`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`Session::targets` still returns repeated ids, so other commands that use it are unchanged. Only `photo.analyze` de-duplicates.

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: raw decoding keeps negative channels
author: robmdunn
body:
Split out of #2092: pushed shadows of raws turned magenta. This is a decoding change on its own; it doesn't depend on camera profiles.

**Raw decoding keeps negative channels.** Decoding clamped each linear Rec.2020 channel at zero after the colour matrix. Near black that keeps only the positive half of each channel's noise, and through a saturating matrix red and blue have the widest noise, so pushed shadows went magenta. Negatives now flow on to noise reduction and the output gamut mapping. I checked that every later log, root and power is guarded. Pulling them toward luminance at decode instead still left them pink: any per-pixel rule keyed to the sign of the noise biases the mean. `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 65; no process version, since this is a decoding change.

Left: per-channel clamp; right: negatives kept. A lens-cap frame pushed 4 EV, a dim room pushed 2 EV, a night garden pushed 3 EV. Mean RGB of the darkest 40 % changes from (64, 28, 65) to (2, 4, 4), from (19, 5, 16) to (14, 5, 10), and from (47, 34, 53) to (44, 32, 28).

![Lens-cap frame, +4 EV](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/robmdunn/lightcraft/a6b85185f1c8325cfab5415c0689e7873e26c1a5/clamp-black-frame.jpg)

![Night garden, +3 EV](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/robmdunn/lightcraft/a6b85185f1c8325cfab5415c0689e7873e26c1a5/clamp-night-garden.jpg)

title: LR-LIB-CULL: Assisted Culling measures focus on the subject — face regions, focus point (#2276, stacked on #2279)
author: helgehelge123
body:
Fixes #2276. Stacked on #2279: its commit is the first one here, and only the second commit is new.

Assisted Culling scored focus on the whole frame (the 90th percentile of block detail). In sports, events and wildlife the crispest detail is often not the subject but a crowd, a board, a net or grass in the focal plane. The frame with the sharpest background then won its burst, and "Reject below focus" kept shots with a soft subject. LightCraft already knows where the subject is for many photos, so no new model is needed:
- face and pet regions, from XMP or from Detect Faces with YuNet;
- the camera's focus point (LR-VIEW-FOCUSPOINT).

### What changed

- **`cull::sharpness_in(img, rect)`** (pipeline): the same 0–100 focus measure, inside a normalized box. It is measured at the source's pixel scale and never enlarged. Bad boxes return `None`: NaN or infinite values, empty, outside the frame, or under 24 px a side. `cull::subject_px` gives a box's size in pixels. `luma` now reads with `.get()`, so a short buffer can't panic.
- **Subject** (`subject_boxes` in `cmd/cull.rs`):
  - Face and pet regions, each grown 15 % for hair, ears and chin, the largest 8 kept. Faces are scored one by one and averaged by area, not as one union box, which would swallow the background between two people.
  - Without regions, the camera's focus point, grown the same way. Otherwise the frame, as before.
  - Regions and the focus point are stored on the upright, uncropped frame, which is also the frame the thumb and preview sources are decoded in. The boxes are therefore used as stored.
- **Source level**: a box under 48 px on the thumbnail is measured on the Preview source. It is loaded once per photo, and only when a box needs it and the photo is larger than the thumbnail.
- **Best of a burst**: ranked by subject focus when every shot of the group has one. When only some do (a face the detector missed, a turned head), the group is ranked by frame focus, so a subject score is never compare…

title: LR-LIB-STACK: a double-click on a stack badge toggles the stack once (#2233)
author: chordpli
body:
Fixes #2233.

Double-clicking a stack badge in the grid did nothing. The badge toggles the stack on every click, so a double-click toggled it twice: the first click expanded the stack and the second collapsed it again.

Fix (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/grid.rs`, `stack_badge`): the badge ignores the second click of a double-click. A click and a double-click both toggle the stack once, so the Lightroom habit works and the single click keeps working. The badge sits above the thumbnail cell, so the double-click never reached the cell's "open in Detail" either before or after this change.

Test (`crates/ui-egui/src/tests_grid.rs`): `double_clicking_a_stack_badge_toggles_the_stack_once` collapses a stack, double-clicks its badge with one click per frame (as a real double-click arrives), and checks that the stack expanded and the grid stayed in Grid view. It then double-clicks again to collapse it and single-clicks to expand it. Without the fix it fails on the first double-click: the stack is still collapsed.

E2E: the same `lightcraft-cli snapshot --demo` script on `main` and on this branch groups three photos into a collapsed stack and clicks its badge twice. On `main` the stack stays collapsed (badge `3`, 22 photos); on this branch it expands (`1/3`, `2/3`, `3/3`, 24 photos). Screenshots in the comment below.

`cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, test, parity, layers and assets pass. The wasm step did not run here (this machine's Homebrew Rust has no `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target); the change is one condition on an existing egui `Response`.
