title: LR-CROP-DIMMING: adjustable crop-mask opacity
author: tylerphotos
body:
## Summary

Adjust how dark the area outside the crop appears, from the photo's crop context menu. The choice is remembered independently of photo edits.

```text
Crop photo → right-click → Crop Mask
  Off / 20% / 50% / 60% / 80% / 100%
  default: 60% (near the former fixed alpha-150 appearance)
  UI / control / connected MCP: view.cropMaskOpacity
```

Wrong-type or unsupported saved values fall back to 60% without discarding otherwise valid UI preferences. Both labels are translated in all 13 shipped catalogs. Parity, gap and control documentation accompany the feature.

## Evidence

- **Before:** outside-crop dimming was fixed, with no user preference. The five regression cases cover the context menu, validation, saved settings, all shipped catalogs and actual rendered pixels.
  **After:** supported choices change the outside area monotonically through fully black at 100%; inside-crop pixels stay unchanged. Malformed commands leave the preference unchanged, and malformed saved values recover.
- Reconciled with the new integration batch. `crates/engine/src/tests_export.rs`, `crates/ui-egui/src/tests_folder_drop.rs` and `crates/catalog/src/store.rs` all match main exactly; shared Windows fixes are inherited from upstream. The crop-aspect conflict retains both our opacity field and upstream's new aspect-default documentation and behavior.
- The opacity helpers and regression scenarios now document their contracts for the review coverage check. Rendering, preferences, commands and translations are otherwise unchanged by this follow-up; no new assets or dependencies.

title: #2284: read the Exif and XMP items of HEIF files
author: john01px2022
body:
Fixes #2284. Fixes #1233.

## The problem

A photo taken on an iPhone at 13:00 in UTC-5 was catalogued as 18:00, and one taken after 19:00 local time landed in the next day's folder. Photos from other cameras at the same event kept their local time, so a shoot with two cameras came out in the wrong order.

## The cause

`container::embedded` (`crates/meta/src/container.rs`) knew JPEG, PNG, WebP, TIFF-based files, Fujifilm RAF and Canon CR3. It had no branch for an ISO base media still image, so every HEIC returned an empty `Embedded` and carried no Exif at all: no capture time, no camera, no lens, no GPS (#1233).

With no date in the file and none in a sidecar, the import falls back to the file's modification time (`crates/engine/src/import.rs:1050`), and `files::file_modified` writes that as UTC. A HEIC whose modification time is the moment it was taken therefore shows the UTC time of the shot. That is the five hours the report describes.

The data was already in the file. The HEIF decoder reads it (`crates/heif/src/lib.rs`), but that crate is behind the optional `heif` feature and sits below the metadata path, so nothing on the import route ever asked for it.

## The fix

A new `lightcraft_meta::heif` reads the `meta` box's item information (`iinf`) and item location (`iloc`) boxes and returns two blocks:

- the `Exif` item, past its four-byte TIFF-header offset, as the Exif block the existing readers take;
- the XMP packet, which is a `mime` item whose content type is `application/rdf+xml`.

It parses the container only, so it is compiled into every build: a HEIC now imports with its date, camera, lens, ISO and GPS whether or not the build carries the HEVC decoder. `container::embedded` calls it after the CR3 branch, matching on the `ftyp` brands of HEIF, HEIC and AVIF. The ISO base media box walker that `cr3` already had is now `pub(crate)` and shared, rather than written twice.

title: Write ISOSpeed extension tag for ISO above 65534 in write_exif
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/meta/src/exif.rs:455 (write_exif)` (no existing issue): write_exif clamps ISO above 65535 and drops the real value.

## Cause
`write_exif` stores ISO in the ISOSpeedRatings SHORT and clamps it to 65535. It never writes the ISOSpeed extension tag (0x8833, LONG) that the reader uses when the SHORT is 65535. Exported EXIF for ISO 102400 or 409600 therefore read back as 65535.

## Fix
When ISO is above 65534, `write_exif` also writes `ISO_SPEED_RATINGS_EXT` (0x8833) as a LONG holding the real value. The SHORT stays clamped to 65535, so the existing reader recovers the true ISO. A regression test round-trips 65534, 65535, 102400 and 409600.

## Verified
- Regression test `exif::write_tests::iso_above_65534_round_trips`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-meta --lib iso_above`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The reader is unchanged. ISO values of 65534 and below are still written only as the SHORT tag.

title: xtask warm: start a new worktree's target/ from a clone of the main checkout's
author: mattsivak
body:
**Stacked on #2302** (uses its `ci_quick` package mapping and `ci_lock`; #2302's commits and a merge of it are included). Review the `xtask warm` commit; merge #2302 first.

Every new worktree rebuilt all of LightCraft. sccache can't share the workspace's own crates between checkouts: the absolute `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` is part of each key, and `SCCACHE_BASEDIRS` doesn't apply to Rust in 0.18 (upstream mozilla/sccache#2678 / #2794 are open). Measured with a private sccache server: a second checkout got hits for every registry crate and misses for every workspace crate.

## `cargo xtask warm [--from SEED] [--force]`
1. Clones the seed's `target/` copy-on-write (`cp -c` on APFS, `cp --reflink=always` on Linux). That takes seconds and uses no extra disk until files are rewritten. Other platforms get an "unsupported" error.
2. Every file whose bytes equal the seed's takes the seed's mtime, so cargo judges it exactly as it would in the seed. Cargo's hashes use workspace-relative paths, so its artifacts are valid here.
3. Every file of a package with any difference (added, removed or changed, fixtures included) gets the current time, so that package and its dependents rebuild.

The default seed is the main checkout (first entry of `git worktree list`). It refuses to replace a `target/` that already has workspace builds unless `--force` is given, and refuses to run in the seed itself.

`cargo xtask warm --seed` (run in the seed): ci's `clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `test --workspace --no-run`, with ci's settings (`ci_env`, moved out of `cargo()`), so `ci` in a warmed worktree finds them fresh. It holds the CI lock.

**Trade-off:** reused crates keep the seed's `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` (about 30 `env!` uses, plus debuginfo paths). A reused test reads its fixtures from the seed checkout, whose files are identical to this one's at warm time; packages with any difference are always rebuilt. Keep the seed on a clean `main`.

title: LR-CROP-RECT: a moved crop slides along a straightened photo's tilted edges (#2299)
author: chordpli
body:
Fixes #2299.

On a straightened photo, a crop that fills the photo's height could not be moved sideways: dragging it left did nothing, and only a smaller crop could reach the left side. A move went across first and then down (`drag_crop`, `CropHandle::Move`), each step stopping where the frame would leave the photo. On a tilted photo such a frame fits only along a tilted line, so no straight sideways step stays inside and the frame stayed where it was.

Fix (`crates/geom/src/crop_drag.rs`): on a straightened photo the frame goes to the place nearest the pointer's that keeps it inside, so it slides along the tilted edges to the photo's side. The places that keep a frame inside are a convex polygon of translations (each corner of the moved frame, turned back into the photo, within the photo: 16 half-planes); `nearest_move` builds it and takes the point nearest the wanted move. A move that fits goes exactly where the pointer says. The frame where it is always counts as inside, since a handle drag can leave it within `is_within_image`'s tolerance past a tilted edge, so such a frame still moves and a click inside it changes nothing. Unstraightened, the old across-then-down clamp runs as before, and if the polygon comes out empty the old path is the fallback. Like every drag, the result still lies inside the photo and keeps the frame's size.

Tests (`crates/geom/src/crop_drag.rs`):
- `given_largest_locked_frame_on_a_straightened_photo_when_moved_sideways_then_it_slides_along_the_tilt`: the largest 2:3 frame at 3° and −10° moves left to the photo's side (a further drag moves it no more), keeps its size and stays inside, and moves back right. Without the fix it fails: the frame doesn't move.
- `given_straightened_photo_when_a_small_frame_is_moved_inside_then_it_follows_the_pointer`: a move that fits follows the pointer exactly.

title: Fix trailing dot in All Metadata rational formatter
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/meta/src/tags.rs:148 (rational)` (no existing issue): All Metadata rational formatter leaves a trailing '.' for values that round to a whole number at 4 decimals.

## Cause
`rational()` formatted non-integer values with `{:.4}` and then trimmed trailing '0' characters. For values within 5e-5 of an integer, every decimal is zero, so the trim left a bare '.', giving "0." or "10.". Tiny negative values also printed with a trailing dot, as "-0.", because the trim stopped at the '.'.

## Fix
The 4-decimal string now has its trailing zeros trimmed and then its trailing '.' trimmed. A result of "-0" becomes "0". In the near-integer branch, a rounded value of zero, including -0.0, prints as "0". The new test covers tiny, near-integer, negative-tiny and ordinary values.

## Verified
- Regression test `tags::tests::rational_has_no_trailing_dot`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-meta --lib rational_has_no_trailing_dot`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Formatting of ordinary non-integer values (e.g. 0.3333, 2.5) and the divide-by-zero output are unchanged.

title: Import JPE/JFIF JPEGs and preserve mixed-case XMP sidecars
author: burhanmorningstar
body:
## Problem

Folder discovery excludes valid JPEGs named `.jpe` or `.jfif`, although importing those files explicitly works. A folder containing only these files reports **No photos found**.

XMP suffix handling also differs between reading, saving and renaming. Mixed-case packets can be read but then ignored when saving or left at the old pathname when a photo moves. This can lose foreign metadata from the active packet or leave its ownership outside repair bookkeeping.

Related to #2293. The report gives no extensions or OS, and the missing JPEG aliases already exist in v0.8.0. This PR addresses a confirmed filename case of the symptom; it does **not** establish or claim to fix the reporter's version-regression cause.

## How to reproduce

**JPEG discovery**

1. Put real JPEG images named `sample.jpe` and `sample.jfif` in a folder outside the library.
2. In Windows LightCraft 0.9.1, choose **File → Import from Folder…**: it reports **No photos found**.
3. Supply either file explicitly through `file.addPhotos {paths: [...]}` over the control channel/MCP: it appears in review. Renaming to `.jpg` also makes folder import find it.

Expected: folder discovery finds the same JPEGs the decoder accepts.

**Sidecar consistency**

1. On a case-sensitive filesystem, put `photo.jpg` beside `photo.Xmp` with a rating and foreign XMP properties.
2. Import, change the rating and save metadata: the existing mixed-case packet is ignored rather than merged. Renaming without saving can leave that packet at the old name.
3. Other mixed-case suffixes, such as `photo.jpg.xMp`, were not offered by the read lookup at all.

Expected: recognized packets retain their spelling and foreign properties when saved and follow the photo when renamed, including undo/redo and partial-move repairs.

title: #2270: a host bridge for pages framing the web build (?host=parent)
author: francoisgn
body:
Fixes #2270.

A same-origin page that embeds LightCraft in an `<iframe>` can now speak to it over `postMessage`, with the protocol PdfCraft, GridCraft and DeckCraft share (storytold/deckcraft#983), under `lightcraft:` message types. Active only with `?host=parent` and only with the parent window on the page's own origin.

| Direction | Message | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| app → page | `lightcraft:ready {version}` / `lightcraft:failed {error}` | the app listens / couldn't start |
| page → app | `lightcraft:open {name, bytes}` | adds a photo, as one dropped on the window (`name` gives the format; `photo.jpg` when missing) |
| app → page | `lightcraft:save {name, bytes}` | every file that would otherwise be a download: exports, preset and keyword files, the library backup (transferred `ArrayBuffer`) |
| app → page | `lightcraft:dirty {dirty}` | whenever closing now would start or stop losing something: a write to browser storage queued or running, or changes storage refused |
| page → app | `lightcraft:cmd {id, params}` | runs a command like `lightcraft.command(..)`; answered by `lightcraft:response {ok, value}` |

No `docClosed`: LightCraft has a library, not documents that close. The library still lives in the iframe's browser storage. The two open points on deckcraft#983 (a host save leaving the document dirty; the host uid set before a failed open) have no counterpart here: saved state comes from the storage flush, and `open` goes through the same import queue as a dropped file.

**Code:** `apps/lightcraft-web/src/host.rs` (message layer in plain Rust: `Incoming::parse`, `Outgoing::fields`, `DirtyReport`; the `postMessage` `Bridge` is wasm32 only), wiring in `web.rs` (`?host=parent`, `write` service, inbox, dirty report after each save pass), `safety::backup` takes a `Deliver` so the backup zip goes to the page too.

title: #2063: decode pre-X FinePix and SuperCCD RAFs
author: alvarogonjim
body:
Addresses most of #2063 (both parts: the legacy container and SuperCCD). The first SuperCCD SR bodies (F700, F710, S20 Pro) and the DBP for GX680 stay preview-only (see *Not decoded* below), so #2063 should stay open for them after this lands; it may want retitling to those bodies.

## What changed

Pre-X FinePix RAFs whose raw block is bare 16-bit samples, without the TIFF and its `0xf000` raw IFD, now develop from their sensor data instead of opening as the embedded JPEG. `raf.rs` sends any raw block that isn't a TIFF to the new `crates/raw/src/vendor/raf_legacy.rs`.

Sources: the ExifTool RAF tag names (`0x0100`, `0x0110`, `0x0111`, `0x0121` RawImageSize, `0x0130` FujiLayout, `0x2ff0` WB_GRGBLevels) and black-box analysis of CC0 raw.pixls.us samples, checked against each file's embedded camera JPEG. No raw decoder's source was consulted.

- **Container:** `0x0100` (rows, columns) of unpacked 16-bit samples. They are 14-bit little-endian, except in the S2 Pro, which is 12-bit big-endian. The byte order is the one that keeps the samples below 2^14. If a black or flat frame can't tell, the body decides: big-endian for the S2 Pro, little-endian for the others. The black level comes from record `0x4000`, which matches the dark floor where the camera left it in. White balance comes from `0x2ff0`.
- **S3Pro and S5Pro:** their files hold a second block, the raw block's size, right after it. It is much darker (median 60–110, at most 8192), most likely the second, low-sensitivity photodiodes. It isn't read: these bodies are decoded from their primary photodiodes alone.
- **FujiLayout 8–11:** an ordinary RGGB Bayer (S5500, and S200EXR in EXR-DR mode).
- **SuperCCD** (FujiLayout bit 7 set, or 0–2): the photosites sit on a grid turned 45°, so they fill every other point of a half-pitch picture grid. Three stored arrangements, each picked over its mirror images by the camera JPEG, and over the opposite row shift by colour fringes at edges:

  | Arrangement | Stored (r, k) → pi…

title: LR-CROP-RECT: a free crop corner on a straightened photo grows both sides (#2308)
author: chordpli
body:
Fixes #2308.

**Stacked on #2306.** The first two commits are #2306. Please review only the last commit, `LR-CROP-RECT: a free crop corner on a straightened photo grows both sides (#2308)`. I'll rebase this once #2306 merges.

## What was wrong

On a straightened photo, dragging a free (unlocked) crop corner out diagonally grew only one side. The corner grew across first and met the tilted edge. From there, no straight step down stayed inside, so the height never changed. At 6°, the corner stopped at (0.996, 0.600), where (0.970, 0.971) fits.

## The fix

`crates/geom/src/crop_drag.rs`:
- A free corner on a straightened photo goes to the place nearest the pointer that keeps the frame inside and at least the minimum size.
- This is the same convex nearest-place solve a move uses since #2306. `nearest_move` became `nearest_offset`, which takes points that move with one or both of the offset's components. A move passes its four corners, so it gives the same result as before.
- On each axis, the corner moves only between where it is and where the pointer asks. A sideways push past a tilted edge stops there and keeps the height, as before.
- Edge handles, locked aspect ratios and unstraightened photos keep the old path.

## Related

The bot linked #742 and #1388. Both are closed fixes to the angle path (`with_angle`), which this change doesn't touch.

## Tests

- `given_straightened_photo_when_a_free_corner_is_dragged_out_diagonally_then_both_sides_grow`: 6° and −10°, plus every other corner at 8°. The anchor stays, and dragging further changes nothing. It fails on main ("one side only", `y1` 0.600).
- `given_straightened_photo_when_a_free_corner_is_pushed_sideways_past_an_edge_then_the_other_side_keeps_its_size`: 6°, 12° and −8°.
- `given_straightened_photo_when_a_free_corner_moves_inside_then_it_follows_and_keeps_a_minimum_size`: inside the photo it follows the pointer, a click changes nothing, and crossing the anchor keeps the minimum size.

title: Search embedded metadata using a rebuildable cache
author: Ladypoly
body:
Search Photos currently misses readable metadata beyond its saved catalog fields. This change adds general embedded-metadata indexing to the existing search, using a disposable per-library cache. **The catalog format stays at 9: no new serialized catalog fields or journal operations.**

### Behavior

- Search readable EXIF/TIFF/GPS values (including software, serial numbers and supported UserComment text), custom XMP properties, PNG text and scalar JSON values. Supported IPTC/XMP descriptive fields continue to use the catalog's existing metadata.
- Keep ordinary case-insensitive substring search, phrases, combined filters and existing field syntax. Add `meta:term` and `meta:"property=value"`. ComfyUI graph parsing still supplies prompt/model/LoRA/sampler/seed/steps/CFG aliases; other generators' readable text/JSON is searchable without adding a parser for every generator.
- Populate the index during normal import. Photo → Reload from Disk rebuilds it for existing images and virtual copies even when source bytes are unchanged, preserving manual metadata and develop edits. Read Metadata from File refreshes custom sidecar annotations alongside the existing standard-XMP workflow.
- Custom AI annotations written by external tools are searchable without entering the Keyword List. Standard `dc:subject` remains ordinary keywords. No CLIP/YOLO inference, model downloads, tagging settings, custom annotation-writing schema or model CI is included.
- Reuse the existing All Metadata dialog for readable generation fields and original PNG text.

Examples: `cat chair`, `"moonlit forest"`, `meta:software=forge`, `meta:"tags=living room"`, `meta:city=berlin`, `comfy:true model:flux steps:>20`.

### Cache and compatibility

`metadata-search-cache.jsonl` is separate from `catalog.snap`/`catalog.log`; the runtime photo index is `#[serde(skip)]`. Older format-9 builds ignore the cache and can still open/edit the library. The cache has its own version, bounded records, append updates and …

title: #2312: culling goes on from a photo rated out of the view
author: alvarogonjim
body:
Fixes #2312.

## What was wrong

With a filter that shows only one-star photos, taking the star off a photo (1 → 0) took it out of the view but left it the active photo. The grid highlighted nothing and Detail kept showing it. The next step (→, Shift+0–5, Auto Advance) then started from the view's first photo: `step()` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/library.rs` can't find the active photo in the view, and falls back to index 0.

## What changed

- **Engine** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/library.rs`): a `cull` wrapper around every rating, flag and label command. When the edit takes the active photo out of the view (the filter bar, Picks, or a smart album no longer shows it), the photo after it becomes active, or the one before it if it was last. That's what Delete already does (`select_after_deletion`). The new active photo is the next one, so `advance` doesn't step past it.
- **Selection left alone:** commands that name their photos with `ids` / `id` don't move it, so Compare and Survey keep showing the photo they rate. With Hold View on, the photo stays in the view, so the selection stays too.
- **UI** (`panels/compare.rs`, `shortcuts.rs`, `menubar.rs`): Shift+key and Auto Advance pass the photo that was active before the edit, and don't call `library.next` when the engine has already moved on. Without this, Shift+0 skipped a photo.
- **Commands:** `photo.pick`, `photo.reject`, `photo.unflag` and `photo.label` now take `advance`, like `photo.rate` and `photo.flag`. The parameter text of all eleven rating, flag and label commands now says that, without `ids`, the selection moves on when the edit takes the active photo out of the view, so scripts and MCP clients see the change. Whether the engine, not only the UI, should do this is for a maintainer to confirm; `photo.delete` already does.
- **Docs:** the LR-LIB-RATING row and its revision history in `docs/parity-checklist.md`, and a `docs/whats-new.md` entry.

title: #2311: Linear and Radial Gradients are drawn by dragging on the photo
author: alvarogonjim
body:
Addresses #2311. It draws gradients by press–drag–release, as Lightroom does. The issue's last sentence can also be read as a two-click mode; whether that's wanted too is for the maintainers, so merging this doesn't close the issue on its own.

## What was wrong

Picking Linear Gradient or Radial Gradient (the tile, L / R, Window ▸ Tools, or a mask's + / −) created a mask at once, with `mask.add`'s default geometry: a linear one near the top, a radial one in the centre. In Lightroom you pick the tool and then draw the gradient by dragging on the photo. `git blame` shows the immediate placement came from the first masking scaffold. Keyboard support later relied on it: a gradient had to exist before its handles could be moved with the arrow keys.

## What changed

- **Picking a tool** (`panels/masking.rs`, `menus.rs`, `state.rs`): a pointer click only picks it. The pointer becomes a crosshair, and a toast says "Drag on the photo to draw the gradient · Esc cancels". `tool.linear` / `tool.radial` take an optional `op` (add / subtract / intersect, for a component) and refuse a bad one.
- **Drawing** (`panels/detail.rs`): once the pointer moves, the mask is created with the dragged geometry.

  - **Radial:** centred where the drag starts, with a corner of its bounding box at the pointer.

title: LR-EDIT-EFFECTS-GRAIN: replace grid noise with signed particle grain
author: SourceFelony
body:
## Summary

Replace the smooth grid/value-noise grain overlay with a small, independently authored signed-particle renderer. This is an alternative approach to the texture problem described in #801 and the existing particle-grain proposal in #1060, not a continuation of that PR.

The goal is a simpler film-inspired texture while retaining the existing Amount, Size and Roughness controls. This implementation has been visually evaluated on photographic sky and detail regions. It is an artistic approximation, not an exact Boolean-model implementation, measured film-stock simulation, or claim of Lightroom parity.

## Changes

- Sum seeded, continuously positioned Gaussian particle footprints in absolute oriented source coordinates, with native-source scaling and approximate reduction filtering.
- Remove the previous CPU grid-noise renderer and WGSL grain kernel/parameters. There is no legacy renderer selector.
- Route active grain through the existing CPU fallback. Zero grain and disabled Effects remain GPU eligible.
- Normalize missing, `legacy` and `mediumParticlesV1` process inputs to the sole current renderer, preserving existing numeric values. Unknown process names are rejected. Canonical serialization changes settings/cache keys to avoid reusing old-grain renders.
- Default Roughness and its control reset to 0; Amount remains 0 and Size 25. Suggested comparison settings: Amount 40, Size 25, Roughness 0, seed 2026.
- Add render/export, migration, presets, copy/paste, sync, Auto Sync, undo/redo and GPU-eligibility regressions; document the method and limits in `docs/experimental-medium-grain.md`.

## Intentional behavior change and limitations

**Existing edits containing grain render differently.** Numeric settings load unchanged, but the previous texture is not preserved. Older released applications do not understand the new process and should not be used to round-trip these edits.

title: Process V3: sharpening at the original's pixels and a raw base look (LR-BEHAV-RENDER-FIDELITY)
author: Sandermand
body:
**Updated after review:** the resample commit is now its own PR, #2340, and this one is only the base look and sharpening. #2340 keeps process V3 and lands first; this PR becomes V4 after it.

## Process V3: sharpening at the original's pixels, and a raw base look (LR-BEHAV-RENDER-FIDELITY)

This is a new process, so V1 and V2 photos render exactly as before until Update to Current Process. `v3_sharpens_every_photo_and_gives_only_raws_a_base_look` pins that: V1 and V2 get neither change, a V3 raw gets both, and a V3 JPEG gets the new sharpening but not the base look.

- **Sharpening, every photo on V3.** Before V3 it read the texture band (0.18 % of the frame at any size) and Radius did nothing. From V3 it is an unsharp mask at the original photo's pixels. A view smaller than the photo gets the sub-pixel blur that sharpening at full size and scaling down leaves (`finish::sharpen_taps`, five taps of `log_l` in the finish stage, CPU and GPU). It was calibrated against reference exports of the same raw at Amount 40 / Radius 1.0, and image-wide detail in the finest three octaves now lands within about 10 %.
- **Base look, raws on V3 only, under every profile.** It has three parts, all fitted by least squares:
  - a tone curve (`COLOR_CURVE`);
  - a colour matrix that keeps luminance and neutral (`COLOR_MATRIX`, before the tone map);
  - a 24×5×6 OkLCh hue / chroma / lightness table (`look_table`, display-referred, before the output conversion).

  Neutral is never moved, hues the photos lack stay unchanged, and JPEGs keep their own look.

**For the maintainers to decide.** V3 is the latest process, so every newly imported raw gets this base look by default. It is fitted on three photos from one camera. Whether that is enough to make it the default, and whether fitting to another product's output fits the project's clean-room policy, are your calls; I can hold the base look back (sharpening only) if you'd rather.

title: fix(tests): Windows path spellings, slideshow-template cache flake (+ contributor entry)
author: mahmatias
body:
Split of #2333 as requested in the review (part 1 of 5): the two test fixes that stand on their own, plus the contributor entry.

**What's in here**

1. `fix(tests): make Windows path spellings match folder-tree widget ids` — folder-tree widget ids were built from Windows path spellings; the tests now match the ids the tree actually uses, so `tests_folder_drop` (and the export tests that walk folders) pass on Windows.

title: Treat Unicode minus and dash characters as negative in parse_gps
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/library.rs:1723 (parse_gps)` (no existing issue): Typed GPS coordinates with a Unicode minus sign (U+2212) land in the wrong hemisphere.

## Cause
parse_gps only recognised an ASCII '-' as a negative sign. A Unicode minus (U+2212) was treated as a separator by the number splitter, so "−33.8688, 151.2093" was read as positive and landed in the wrong hemisphere without any error.

## Fix
parse_gps now replaces U+2212, U+2012, U+2013, U+FE63 and U+FF0D with ASCII '-' before parsing, so the existing sign detection handles them. The regression assertion is added to the existing parse test in gps_tests (run with `cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib gps_tests`).

## Verified
- Regression test `cmd::library::gps_tests::coordinates_people_type`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib coordinates_people_type`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The rest of the parsing is unchanged: the coordinate splitting, N/S/E/W letter handling and range checks.

title: Process V3: a sharp resample, and a sharp fit-to-screen and zoomed view
author: Sandermand
body:
Split out of #2332 at a reviewer's request. That PR keeps the raw base look and sharpening; this one is the resample. It keeps process V3 and is meant to land first; #2332 becomes V4 after it.

## A sharp fit-to-screen and zoomed view

A 22 MP Canon CR2 at Fit (drawn 1271 px wide) was visibly softer than the same photo in another raw developer. The detail in the finest octave of the render was about 1/15 of what the same render scaled down once with a good filter keeps. Four soft steps compounded, and each is fixed:

| Step | Before | Now | Gated |
|---|---|---|---|
| Resample to the output | Mitchell prefilter past 1.25×, then bilinear at a fractional phase | one separable Catmull-Rom resample from the source for unrotated, unwarped views (`resample::resize_window`, `SampleMode::Window`); otherwise a Catmull-Rom prefilter and bicubic sampling. CPU and GPU share the taps | process V3 |
| 1:1 (full-size export, 100 % view) | a crop edge at 1099.37 px interpolated every pixel by 0.37 px | a span within half a pixel of the output's size starts on a whole pixel; a near-native size (5990 px of a 6000 px crop) is still scaled | process V3 |
| Loupe texture | rendered up to 63 px larger, then shrunk by the GPU's bilinear filter | rendered at the size drawn, drawn texel for texel (`detail::pixel_exact`) | no: display only |
| Past 100 % | the GPU stretched the window bilinearly | the visible part is resampled to screen pixels with Catmull-Rom on a worker thread, with a margin so panning only moves it (`magnify`). Panning measured at the display's 144 Hz with real mouse input; it was ~55 fps with the resample done in the frame | no: display only |

**Process gating.** The first two rows change how existing settings render, so per `docs/process-versions.md` they are a new process. The `Frame` carries its `Resampling`, chosen from the settings' process by `Resampling::of` (an exhaustive match), and CPU `Frame::sample` and the GPU `sample` both take it from there; the GPU's `sa…

title: Fix parse_gps for hemisphere-letter-first coordinates without comma
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/library.rs:1723 (parse_gps)` (no existing issue): Typed GPS coordinates with the hemisphere letter first and no comma are rejected.

## Cause
Without a comma, parse_gps split right after the first N/S letter. When the letter came first ("N 51.5072 W 0.1276"), the latitude part was just "N", which has no digits, so parsing returned None.

## Fix
When the input starts with N or S, parse_gps now splits at the first E/W letter after it. Input with the letter after the number is split as before.

## Verified
- Regression test `cmd::library::gps_tests::coordinates_people_type`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib gps_tests`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

The comma-separated path and the degrees/minutes/seconds parsing are unchanged.

title: gpu, windows: fix DX12 readback polling on RTX Spark (Windows ARM64) and Windows test paths
author: mweinbach
body:
## Summary

Ensures full GPU hardware acceleration and Windows on ARM64 (arch64-pc-windows-msvc / NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X 6144-core Blackwell RTX GPU) support across the compute pipeline, neural network runners, and window renderer:

1. **DX12 / multi-threaded wgpu readback polling (crates/gpu/src/{ctx,nn,faces}.rs)**:
   - Pass the exact wgpu::SubmissionIndex from queue.submit into device.poll(wgpu::PollType::Wait { submission_index: Some(index), .. }) in Gpu::finish_and_read and NetRunner::execute instead of None (which waits only for the most recent submission at call time and can return before an earlier submission's map_async callback is invoked when multiple threads share the device).

2. **Window GPU probe test on Windows (pps/lightcraft/src/window_gpu.rs)**:

title: LR-MASK-PEOPLE: People masks with SAM 3: pick a face, then Entire Person / Face Skin / Body Skin / Hair / Clothes (#2357, step 1)
author: helgehelge123
body:
Refs #2357 (step 1). Draft until the questions in the issue are answered.

Masking ▸ **People**, as in Lightroom: pick one of the photo's faces, tick parts, get one mask (or an Add / Subtract / Intersect component). Everything runs on SAM 3 as it is; there's no new model.

**What it does**
- **Entire Person:** SAM 3 `person` instances (above 0.3). The instance whose mask covers the face centre wins; the fallback is the box holding the centre and most of the face. This separates people standing next to or behind each other.
- **Face Skin, Body Skin, Hair, Clothes:** SAM 3's own `skin`, `face`, `hair` and `clothes` concepts, each cut to that person. Face Skin is skin inside the face detection, Body Skin the rest ("Skin" names both). Only the detections the ticked parts need run, and `face` only when one skin is asked for alone. Logits combine as fuzzy sets (max / min / min with the negation).
- **UI:** a People tile under Create New Mask and People… in the + / − menu open a chooser listing the faces (by name, else Person 1, 2…) with the five parts. ## Problem

When a Synchronize Folder scan finds nothing to do, the dialog still looks like a form to fill in. It shows four greyed choices, each "(0)", with **Import new photos** and **Relink photos whose file was renamed or moved** still ticked. title: #2359: content-aware Fill keeps structure and grain, nothing ghosts through the feather
author: helgehelge123
body:
Part 2 of #2359. Content-aware **Fill** no longer smears large holes or lets the removed object ghost through the feather.

### What was wrong

I tested on real indoor-sports photos at 1600 px: a ball on the floor, a banner, a whole basketball backboard, a floor line painted over with the brush, a hoop in front of the net, and a shoe.

- **Ghosting.** The hole was every pixel with alpha > 0, but the result was blended back with the feathered alpha. At the default feather 50, the outer 40 % of the radius still showed part of the object: a visible ring, half a shoe sole, dark scallops along a removed line.
- **A coloured blob in big holes.** The window was the stroke plus `2r`. At the coarsest level that left a handful of source patches next to a hole half the level's size. That level started from a membrane, which blends two backgrounds into a third colour (blue wall + beige → olive). PatchMatch then copied the patch closest to that colour (a green stripe), and fine levels over 96 px only refined it with a search radius of 2.
- **No grain.** Every level ended with a weighted mean of the matches.

### Changes

`crates/pipeline/src/spots.rs`
- **Footprint.** Fill replaces everything under the brush and feathers *outside* it, up to `0.3 r` at full feather (`reach`). Heal and Clone are unchanged.
- **Wider read window.** Fill reads patches from as far around the footprint again as the footprint is wide (`read_pad`). `window_for_reads` uses the same helpers, so windowed renders still match the whole render.
- **Perceptual matching.** Fill compares and blends on the square root of scene-linear values, so shadows match as well as highlights.
- **Less work per pixel.** The per-pixel distance to the stroke is only computed inside the footprint's box, not the whole read window.

`crates/inpaint/src/patchmatch.rs`
- **Coarsest-level start.** The coarsest level is now filled ring by ring from the hole's edge inwards (`onion_init`). Each pixel takes the centre of the source patch…

title: LR-BEHAV-TOAST: toasts stay long enough to read, hold under the pointer, and errors stay 6 s
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

Why one PR: the reading-time rule matters where toasts carry long text, which is the error toasts, and routing them through one `toast_error` is how they get it; the ~25 call-site edits are that routing. About 470 lines of code and 310 of tests.


## Problem

Every toast lasted the same 1.4 s, whatever it said. The last 0.25 s of that is the fade-out, so about 1.15 s of it is readable. That is enough for "Library saved", but not for the instructions and errors that go through the same path:

- "Smart albums update automatically: change their rules, or use Photo ▸ Delete Photo" (13 words)
- "Painting "…": click photos to add or remove it · Esc stops", a mode instruction
- "Slideshow · Space pauses · Esc ends"
- many `Err(e) => app.toast(…)` branches: a failed keyword import or export, a refused drop, a failed scan or merge. These showed the error for 1.4 s even though `toast_error` (6 s) exists.

Moving the pointer onto a toast to finish reading it didn't hold it, and a toast appeared at full opacity in one frame although it faded out.

## Change

- **Reading time** (`crates/ui-egui/src/toast.rs`):
  - A toast stays `1 + words / 3` seconds (about 180 words a minute, plus a beat to notice it), capped at 10 s, and never less than the caller's floor: 1.4 s for a plain toast, 6 s for an error, or the seconds given to `toast_for`.
  - Each CJK, kana or hangul character counts as half a word, since those scripts don't separate words with spaces.

title: #2365: centre the search field on the window, not inside the bar's margins
author: john01px2022
body:
Fixes #2365.

## The cause

The top bar reserves room for the traffic lights in its own left margin, and full screen gives that room back (#1763):

```rust
let left = match (app.integrated_titlebar, app.window_is_fullscreen) {
    (true, false) => 78,
    (true, true) => 16,
    (false, _) => 10,
};
```

The search field was then centred on `ui.max_rect()`, which is what is left *inside* those margins, not the window. Its centre therefore sat at `window centre + (left - 12) / 2`, and its width came from `full.width() - 620`. In a 1200 px window:

| | field centre | field width |
|---|---|---|
| windowed | 633 (33 px right of centre) | 490 |
| full screen | 602 | 552 |

So the field was never centred, and entering full screen moved it 31 px left and widened it by 62 px. The comment above it already said "centred on the window" — that was the intent, not the behaviour.

## The fix

Place the field against the whole bar, margins included, instead of against the content rect. Its width is then twice the room between the window centre and the icons on its right, rather than the window width minus a symmetric reserve. Centre and width both become independent of the traffic lights: 600 and 556 in a window and in full screen alike.

`window_handle` was already rebuilding that same bar rect from the content rect and the two margins, so it now takes the rect instead.

The left buttons still move into the traffic lights' space in full screen; #1763's test covers that and still passes.

## Verified

The new test in `tests_titlebar.rs` fails on `main` with:

```
assertion `left == right` failed: windowed, the field is centred on the window
  left: 633.0
 right: 600.0
```

and passes with the change, across the whole full-screen toggle, for the field and for the filter icon that rides with it.

I also rendered the bar headlessly in the configuration macOS actually installs (integrated title bar plus native menu bar), before and after, and measured the field's left border in the p…

title: LR-BEHAV-BG-TASKS: detached readers for an import or scan (stall, skip, cap), tested and not used yet
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

Why one PR: the detached-reader pool, one unit-tested module (`import/reads.rs`) that nothing calls yet; 1,108 changed lines, of which 509 tests, 0 translations, 0 docs, so about 599 lines of code. ✕, stall detection, Skip and the cap on skipped and stuck reads act on the same job table, and the tests drive them together, so no rule can land without the others; the wiring that uses the pool is parts 2 to 4.

## Problem

An import from a network drive got stuck on one file. After ✕, its row in the activity stack said "Stopping…" and stayed that way, and Synchronize Folder had sat in "Looking for changes" for 34 minutes. Nothing ended them but quitting.

The cause is in how files are read. The probes and the copy/move transfers run on a `std::thread::scope`, and a scope can't end before every thread in it has. One read blocked in the operating system (a share that dropped its connection) therefore holds the whole import, and ✕ only sets a flag that is checked between files. The same scope is used by the Add Photos review's scan, a Local folder and Synchronize Folder.

## Change

This is the first of four parts of one change (LR-BEHAV-BG-TASKS), split at its dependency boundaries: this part is the unit-tested core, with nothing on screen or in the control channel changed.

- **The detached-reader core** (`crates/engine/src/import/reads.rs`, new): a pool that runs reads on detached threads while the calling thread only coordinates, looking every 250 ms at ✕, Skip and the readers.
  - **✕** ends the run within about a second. Jobs under way get 0.4 s, and queued ones never start.
  - **Stalled means no progress:** a job with no progress for `ReadWatch::stall_after` (10 s by default) is published (`ReadWatch::stalled`). `progressed()` restarts the clock (a chunk read or written, a step done), so a slow read that goes on is never reported.

title: LR-EDIT-DETAIL-DENOISE: GPU denoise gives the right result on DX12 with NVIDIA Pascal
author: insideTheFlux
body:
## Problem

On Windows with DirectX 12 (the default backend), AI Denoise on the GPU gave wrong results on an NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070, and reported no error. The GPU denoise tests in `crates/gpu/src/nn.rs` failed every time with the same numbers, off by 0.55–1.03 of the output's size where the tests allow 2e-4.

| Backend / compiler (same GTX 1070) | GPU denoise tests |
|---|---|
| DX12 + FXC (what LightCraft uses, issue #471) | 3 fail |
| DX12 + DXC (`WGPU_DX12_COMPILER=dxc`) | pass |
| Vulkan (`LIGHTCRAFT_GPU_BACKEND=vulkan`) | pass |

Release builds fail the same way, so the shipped Windows app is affected.

## Cause

Small test networks with exact answers narrowed it down. Any single-layer network was right, but two 1×1 layers that only copy channels came out wrong on every odd pixel, with that pixel's channels shifted. FXC merges the convolution's four separate output stores (`dst[o] … dst[o + 3u]`) into one 16-byte `store_raw U0.xyzw`. That DXBC is valid and the addresses are 16-byte aligned, but NVIDIA's DX12 driver runs it wrong on this card for a plain convolution's output (mode 0). Spacing the stores so FXC can't merge them made the result exact.

The transposed convolution's output (mode 1) is merged into the same instruction, but on this card that store runs right: its exact test passes with or without the change. Exactly what the driver gets wrong isn't known.

## Fix

`nn_conv.wgsl` now spaces the mode-0 stores by `one = 1u + p.zero`. `zero` is the always-0 uniform that used to be called `pad`. FXC can't prove `one == 1`, so it keeps the four stores separate. Mode 1 is spaced the same way as a precaution, since it's the same instruction. The cost is three extra integer additions per output pixel.

## Tests

- New test `nn::tests::a_layer_stores_every_pixels_channels_where_the_next_reads_them`: two channel-copy 1×1 layers on a 3×3 tile, checked for exact equality with the reference. It fails on the GTX 1070 without the fix, with exactly the shifted chann…

title: #2284: date files and the session clock in the host's time zone
author: john01px2022
body:
Follows #2290, which fixed the HEIC half of #2284. This fixes the other half that @emanaku reported in [that thread](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/2284#issuecomment-6260723268): a JPEG that went through a messenger carries no capture date, only a modification time of 2026-10-18 20:15:11 in UTC-5, and LightCraft 0.9.1 catalogued it as 01:15 the next day.

## The cause

The catalog stores local civil times — `Catalog::set_captured` says so — but two functions wrote an instant as UTC:

- `import::system_clock`, whose own doc comment admitted it ("UTC on targets without a clock offset");
- `files::file_modified`, which dates a file that carries no date of its own, "as Lightroom does".

So the reported five hours were not only on import dates. The same offset went into every photo's `imported`, every album's `created`, every edit's `edited`, and the `now` that "added in the last N days" smart rules count back from. In UTC-5 anything done after 19:00 local was recorded as the next day.

## The fix

`import::local_civil` converts an instant using the offset **in force at that instant**, not today's, so a file modified in July keeps summer time when it is read in January. `system_clock` and `file_modified` both go through it.

The zone comes from [`jiff`](https://docs.rs/jiff), added under `[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies]` beside `lightcraft-fetch`:

- pure Rust, and on Unix it has no dependencies of its own — it reads `/usr/share/zoneinfo` directly, so nothing new is linked on macOS, Linux or FreeBSD (`jiff` and `jiff-core` are the only crates the lockfile gains there);
- on Windows it embeds a copy of the IANA database, because Windows has no canonical one;
- `TimeZone::system()` falls back to a zone that behaves like UTC when the host has none, so there is no new failure path;
- the web build is untouched and keeps its fixed clock.

The zone is read once into a `OnceLock`. It holds the whole rule set, so each instant still gets i…

title: Smart album rules: + and − never cover a rule, and hovering a field doesn't wrap it
author: RevDonz
body:
Three reports about the smart-album rule editor. They come from two causes.

## + and − drawn over a long rule (#2353), and the end date's missing calendar (#2352)

The end date's calendar was never missing. It was drawn, but underneath the **+**, which took the click.

The dialogs share one window (`lightcraft-dialog`). A window that can't be resized keeps the width the last dialog left it at, because `default_width(680)` only applies the first time. Open any narrower dialog first (Create Smart Album from Filter… is 380 wide), then the rule editor, and the window grows only to the end of the rule's longest value: about 579 points, the width in the issue's screenshot. A rule row laid out its − and + with `Layout::right_to_left` in whatever room it had left. A date **is between** has none left, so the buttons went to the dialog's right edge, on top of the end date field and its calendar button.

**Fix** (`rules_editor.rs`): − and + now follow the value. When there is room they are pushed to the right edge, at exactly the same place as before (checked: 867.8–923 in a fresh 680-wide dialog). When there isn't, they sit right after the value and the dialog widens to fit the row, so every row's buttons still line up. The dialogs still share one window, and the 680 default is unchanged.

## Hovering a field wraps it onto two lines (#2354)

The theme gives resting buttons a 1-point border (`widgets.inactive.bg_stroke`). egui gives a frameless item at rest `button_padding − border width` of padding, but the full padding when hovered, so a hovered item needs 2 points more. egui's own menus avoid this by dropping the resting border (`menu_style`). `ComboBox` replaces that with its own `popup_style`, which is empty by default, and its submenus inherit it. title: LR-LIB-CULL: Assisted Culling measures photos on all cores (stacked on #2283)
author: helgehelge123
body:
Depends on #2283, which is stacked on #2279. Only the last two commits are new here (86f68a8d, 9873e3d4); the others are #2279 and #2283 and drop out once those are merged. It stays a draft until then, and I'll rebase it on main.

Assisted Culling (`photo.analyze`) decoded and measured one photo after the other on the calling thread. On a burst-heavy shoot, decoding each thumbnail-level source (and since #2283 a preview for small subjects) takes most of the time, while the measuring itself is cheap. A GPU wouldn't help here, because the measures run on 512 px images. So this spreads the decodes over the CPU cores.

### What changed

- **`photo.analyze`** (`cmd/cull.rs`) now works in batches. For each batch:
  1. It reads what each photo needs from the session, serially: how to load its thumbnail-level source, its capture time, its subject boxes and its size.
  2. On rayon's global pool, it decodes the photos side by side and measures focus, subject focus, clipping and the signature. Each worker returns only the small result row.
  3. Serially again, it keeps the decoded thumbnails and the as-shot white balance their decodes read, as `source_now` did.
- **Batch size**: a batch is sized by what its decodes count for at the memory gate, measured against the gate's limit (`work_gate`, budget/4). A thumbnail counts as 3× the file size and a preview as 6×, the same weights the file loader uses; they now live in the shared `files::gate_weight`. A batch also holds at most one photo per pool thread. The decodes count at the gate without waiting (`acquire_urgent`), so the batch size is what keeps them within it.
- **Preview for small subjects** (#2283): a second pass loads it only for photos whose subject box is too small on the decoded thumbnail and that have more pixels than the thumbnail, which is the same condition as before. These previews are no longer kept in memory, because a culling run would push the loupe's preview out.
- **Unchanged**: everything after measuring s…

title: #2359: Remove is content-aware, as in Lightroom (stacked on #2367)
author: helgehelge123
body:
Stacked on #2367: review that first, this PR's own change is the last commit. Answers the open question in #2359.

In Lightroom, **Remove** is the content-aware tool. Heal and Clone are the ones with a source. Here, Remove rendered like Heal with an automatically picked source. On a hand or a ball held against a jacket it copied a nearby piece of the photo (often another object) and blended it in.

### Changes

- **Render.** `SpotMode::content_aware()` is true for Remove and Fill. Those spots render through the content-aware fill from #2367. The source offset is ignored, and `window_for_reads` reads only their surroundings.
- **`spot.add`.** A Remove spot gets no automatic source.

title: Tone Curve: put a clicked new point on the curve

body:
Clicking the point curve to add a point put it at the pointer's height, so unless you hit the line to the pixel the curve bent and the photo changed before you'd dragged anything. title: Crop: the spiral guide is complete at every aspect ratio
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #2393.

The squares were carved off the crop rectangle itself, so the guide depended on the crop's shape. Counting the quarter-circle arcs the overlay produces:

| crop | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 1:1 | **1** | 10 |
| φ:1 | 10 | 10 |
| 3:2 | **3** | 10 |
| 2:3 | **3** | 10 |
| 16:9 | **4** | 10 |
| 9:16 | **4** | 10 |
| 4:5 | **3** | 10 |

A square loses everything after the first arc exactly as the report says: `s = cw.min(ch)` takes the whole width, the first subtraction leaves a zero-width rectangle, and the next iteration trips the `s < rw.min(rh) * 0.01` guard and stops.

### Why a fixed rectangle

Only a golden-ratio rectangle subdivides into squares forever — a `φ × 1` rectangle less a `1 × 1` square is `1 × 1/φ`, the same shape again. So it is the one shape that yields a complete spiral, and the construction now uses it whatever the crop is. The normalisation already at the end of the function divides by that rectangle, so the result stretches to fit the crop.

That distorts the curve on a crop of another ratio, which is the trade the report proposes and accepts:

> Unequal horizontal/vertical scaling would distort the mathematical curve, but would preserve its usefulness as a composition guide.

The portrait transpose and the orientation flips are untouched, so a portrait crop still gets a portrait spiral and all four orientations still mirror it.

### Tests

`the_spiral_is_complete_at_every_aspect_ratio` asserts the same arc count and the same curve length across eight aspect ratios and all four orientations, and that the paths stay inside the crop. Without the change it fails with:

```
1x1 orient 0: 1 squares, not 10
```

The two existing spiral tests (`every_overlay_stays_inside_the_crop`, `spiral_is_one_continuous_curve`) are unchanged and still pass.

### Validation

`cargo xtask ci`: **all 8 steps passed** (fmt, clippy, heif, test, parity, layers, assets, wasm).

One note from the first run: clippy's `approx_constant` rejected a hand-wri…

title: Keep file name when a redirect Location is query-only
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/fetch/src/http.rs:139 (Url::join)` (no existing issue): Query-only redirect Location drops the file name from the URL path.

## Cause
`Url::join` resolved every relative Location against the base path's directory, cutting off the last segment. For a query-only Location like `?page=2`, RFC 3986 says to keep the base path including the file name.

title: Remove dot segments when resolving redirect Locations
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/fetch/src/http.rs:136 (Url::join)` (no existing issue): Relative redirect Location with ../ keeps dot segments unresolved.

## Cause
Url::join built the next URL by appending a relative Location to the current directory. Url::parse never removed `.` or `..` segments, so a redirect to `../z` from `/x/y/file` produced the literal path `/x/y/../z`.

## Fix
Url::parse now runs the path through a new `remove_dot_segments` helper that follows RFC 3986 section 5.2.4. It leaves the query untouched and clamps `..` at the root. All join branches go through Url::parse, so they all get normalised paths.

## Verified
- Regression test `http::tests::join_removes_dot_segments`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-fetch --lib join_removes_dot_segments`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Query-only redirects were not changed. No percent-decoding or other normalisation was added.

title: Match URL schemes case-insensitively in Url::parse and Url::join
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/fetch/src/http.rs:71 (Url::parse), also Url::join at :115` (no existing issue): URL scheme match is case-sensitive, so HTTPS://… URLs and redirects are rejected.

## Cause
Url::parse and Url::join checked for the "http://" and "https://" prefixes with case-sensitive comparisons. RFC 3986 says schemes are case-insensitive, so URLs like "HTTPS://host/x" and redirects to them were rejected.

## Fix
Added a small `strip_scheme` helper that compares the scheme prefix with `eq_ignore_ascii_case`. It uses `str::get`, so it cannot panic on a non-char-boundary. Both `Url::parse` and `Url::join` now use it.

## Verified
- Regression test `http::tests::url_scheme_is_matched_case_insensitively`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-fetch --lib url_scheme_is_matched_case_insensitively`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Other scheme handling is unchanged. Unsupported schemes such as ftp: are still rejected, and the https-to-http redirect refusal is unchanged.

title: PERF-SELECT: a big selection no longer slows every idle frame
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem
On a library of 312,029 photos (release build, M1 Max) with all photos selected, every frame took about 368 ms (roughly 1.2 ms per 1,000 selected photos), even when idle. 99.5% of it was in `NativeMenu::update`, which rebuilds the menus every frame. Each command's enabled check walked the whole selection with a catalog lookup per id (`in_stack`, `has_library_selection`, `has_outdated_process`, `selection_deleted`, `ui_enabled`, `expanded`). The grid also did a linear `Selection::contains` per visible cell, and the keyword panels hashed and copied every selected id each frame.

## Change
- `Selection` and `Selection::ids` are unchanged: callers keep setting and reading `selection.ids` as before.
- `Session` fingerprints the selected ids (its length and a fast non-cryptographic hash, in order, so no two lengths share a key). A long selection (1,024 or more) is fingerprinted once per frame (`Session::begin_frame`, called at the start of the UI frame, of the native-menu update and of `execute` / `execute_fn`, before the enabled check) and in between only when its length or its first or last id differ; a short one is fingerprinted on every ask.
- A membership index (`Session::selection_view`) is rebuilt only when the fingerprint changes, so the grid and filmstrip cells get `contains` / `state_of` in constant time.
- `Session::selection_facts` caches the in-library, stacked, outdated-process and deleted answers per (fingerprint, active photo, catalog revision), computed lazily and stopping at the first photo that settles each. The stacked check walks the smaller of the selection and the stacks.
- The enabled checks, the local-only test and the per-frame count checks read those facts or `selected_count()` instead of copying and walking the selection.

body:
Off `main`.

title: Carry rounded GPS minutes into degrees in XMP writer
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/meta/src/xmp.rs:458 (fmt_gps_coord)` (no existing issue): XMP GPS coordinate writer emits 60.000000 minutes for values just below a whole degree.

## Cause
fmt_gps_coord truncates the degrees and formats the remaining minutes with 6 decimals. Minutes within 5e-7 of 60 round up to "60.000000" while the degrees stay truncated. For example, 10.9999999999 became "10,60.000000N", which is invalid because XMP requires minutes below 60.

## Fix
The minutes are now rounded to 6 decimals before formatting. If the rounded value reaches 60, the degrees go up by one and the minutes are set to 0. 10.9999999999 now gives "11,0.000000N".

## Verified
- Regression test `xmp::tests::gps_coords`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-meta --lib gps_coords`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The GPS parsing code and the rest of the XMP writer are unchanged.

title: PERF-SIDECARS: imports and moves answer sidecar lookups from the folder listing
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

Why one PR: one mechanism, sidecar lookups answered from a folder listing, used by imports and by renames and moves; both share the listing helper and its vouching rule. About 440 lines of code and 455 of tests.


## Problem

On a network share every name asked about is a round trip, found or not.

- An import asks the disk for up to nine sidecar names per file (`find_sidecar`).
- Renaming or moving photos, and undoing either, asks four names per photo, twice (`rename.rs` `sidecars()`).
- Measured on a library of 312,029 photos (files on an SMB share, M1 Max, release build): about 106 ms per file when the folder listing is no longer in the SMB client's cache, even when the folder has no `.xmp` at all.
- A real import that showed it: 8,530 JPGs in 143 folders on an SMB share, with no `.xmp` anywhere, imported from the Add Photos review with every photo selected. The import got 7,860 explicit file paths, not the folder. `ImportJob::expand` then called `is_dir()` on each path, one after another, before the first batch (the row sat at "0 of 7860" for minutes). After that every import reader spent all its time in `find_sidecar` (9 stats per file, about 76 ms each under load).

## Change

- While an import or the Add Photos review walks a folder, it keeps what the listing says: which names are files, and, for a folder listed completely with plain ASCII names, the lower-cased names ending in `.xmp`. `find_sidecar` is skipped when none of the photo's candidate names (any case) is among them.
- The review hands its listing to the import that review starts, and to no other (`ImportTask` → `ImportJob::with_listed`; nothing is kept in the session). A path the listing names as a file is taken as a file, with no `is_dir()`.
- A folder's `.xmp` names are trusted only while its modification time is what it was before it was listed. The walk reads the time before `read_dir` and vouches for it only if it is at least 2 s old (the coarsest folder-time grain: FAT and SMB1's…

title: PERF-SMART: File Path rules compare in place instead of building strings per photo
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem
A smart album's File Path rule built three new strings for every photo it looked at (`path.replace`, `want.replace`, `path.to_lowercase`), plus a lower-cased copy of the rule text that every rule makes before it looks at its field. On a library of 312,029 photos, opening a smart album whose only rule is `filePath contains <11 characters>` stalled the UI for 165 ms, against 89 ms for one whose only rule is `flag is reject`: about 75 ms (~240 ns per photo) for the path rule itself. Profiles of album switches were dominated by `to_lowercase`, `unicode … to_lower` and malloc/free.

## Change
- A File Path rule whose photo path and rule text are both ASCII is compared in place: `/` and `\` fold together and case is ignored byte by byte, with no allocation. `contains` skips eight bytes at a time looking for the first byte of the text. Handles `contains`, `notContains`, `is`, `isNot`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `isEmpty`, `isNotEmpty`.
- Any non-ASCII path or text, and any non-string value, takes the old code unchanged (`file_path_matches_slow`), so ß, İ, final sigma and the like give the same answers as before.
- The File Path rule is dispatched before the rule text is lower-cased, so it no longer pays for that copy.
- No cache is added; memory stays flat. The rule text is folded as it is compared (it is a few bytes) rather than stored normalised on the rule, which would have meant a new field on the public `Rule` enum.
- Tests: equality against a verbatim copy of the old code over ASCII, Unicode (ß, İ, final sigma, CJK, U+0085, U+000B), mixed case, backslash and UNC paths, empty and `\` texts, non-string values and demo photos, for all ops; and every piece of a long path at every offset, in both cases and both slash directions.
- What's New entry.

**Not in this PR:** the other costs of smart albums (chained `album is` rules re-evaluated per photo, sidebar counts), the search text cache, anything for non-ASCII paths.

title: PERF-SMART: count every smart album once per pass, not once per album that tests it
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem
A full count of every album (`AlbumTally::of`, the sidebar numbers; `albums.list`) counts each smart album with its own pass over all photos, and when many smart albums build on one shared smart album (each with `album is <base>` plus a rule of its own), the base album is worked out again for every photo by every album that tests it. On a synthetic 312,000-photo library with 77 smart albums, 51 of which build on one shared base album, the full count took 22.8 s and 24.6 s before and 15.7 s and 13.1 s after (machine under heavy load, load average 80–130; the remainder is the `filePath` rules themselves). For context: on a 312,029-photo library with the same shape, opening one of the albums built on the base also stalled the UI about 400 ms, against 89 ms for an album with a single cheap rule.

## Change
- `AlbumTally::of` counts the loop-free smart albums shortest chain first and keeps each one's photos (the existing `Members` bits) in a thread-local pass (`rules::AlbumPass`) that `smart_album_holds` reads before evaluating rules. The pass is ended inside `of`, so it can't outlive the catalog state counted.
- Only albums whose rules reach no loop are kept, with their chain height; a kept answer is used only when `stack depth + height <= MAX_ALBUM_DEPTH` where it is asked, otherwise the rules run as before.
- Albums in or reaching a loop, or past the depth limit, are counted after the pass has ended, so they run exactly as they did.
- `albums.list` counts through one `AlbumTally::of` instead of one `album_count` per album.

**Not in this PR:** the per-photo cost of the text rules, the evaluation when one album is opened (`Catalog::query`), and where the full recount runs.

- [x] `a_whole_count_equals_each_album_counted_alone`: tallies equal each album counted alone over plain albums, a folder of albums, chains, `isNot`, groups, `any`/`all`, a saved loop and albums testing it, a self-testing album, a 41-album chain past the…

title: PERF-SMART: test a smart album's rules cheapest first
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem
A smart album tests its rules in the order they were written. A common way to build smart albums is a base album (say, "not rejected, and not in these folders") that many others build on, each written as `all[album is <base>, filePath contains <name>]`: the shared condition first, then a narrower rule of its own. Every photo then runs all of the base album's rules (and any album it tests) before the cheap, selective path check. On a library of 312,029 photos with 51 smart albums of that shape, each stalled the UI for about 400–430 ms; with `album is <base>` moved last, the same rules took 160–235 ms for the same photos. `Rule::matches` for `filePath` also costs about 75 ms per pass on its own, so running it first for few photos would be wasteful, but running a whole album first is worse.

## Change
- `RuleSet::by_cost` returns the rules (and those of nested groups) cheapest first, keeping the written order among equals: numbers, choices and yes/no about the photo's own record; then lists, dates, short fields, a plain album or a folder (it holds no photos on main: an empty lookup); then text built from several fields and file paths; then a smart album, and a group as dear as its dearest rule.
- `Filter::prepare` and `prepare_one` take the catalog and work the ordered rules out once. A smart album's prepared form is remembered per catalog (`Catalog::plans`) until an op adds or removes an album or changes rules, so a photo asked about an album doesn't prepare it again. `Filter::matches` (one photo) still tests the rules as written.
- **Guard:** while any smart album tests itself, or a chain of smart albums is as long as `MAX_ALBUM_DEPTH` (`Catalog::keeps_written_order`, worked out once per catalog state; the app refuses loops, but a saved or damaged catalog can hold one; deep chains it allows) all rules are tested as written, so the results are literally the old ones. With a loop the answers memo can make an answer depend on which album is asked…

title: LRC-LIB-SMARTCOLL: the move engine for reordering smart album rules
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem

The New / Edit Smart Album window can add and remove rules and groups, but not move them. Reordering needs one tested place that decides where a rule or group can go: into a group, out of a group, past its neighbours, never inside itself, never deeper than the editor's group depth, with groups a move empties going away. Piling that into the drag and keyboard code would make it hard to check, so this PR lands it first, on its own.

## Change

- New `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/rules_move.rs`: pure functions on a `RuleSet`, and nothing else. It is the move engine the smart album editor's reordering will use.
  - `judge(rs, from, dest)` says what moving the row at path `from` to the place `dest` would do: it moves, it changes nothing (where it already is, or a path that isn't there), or it is refused (a group into itself, or deeper than `MAX_GROUP_DEPTH`). A group that is already deeper (rules written by an agent) can still be moved at its own depth or higher.
  - `move_node(rs, from, dest)` makes the move and returns where the row is now. It is all or nothing, a path that leads nowhere changes nothing, and a group the move leaves empty goes away (with any group that empties in turn, except one the row is moving into).
  - `key_dest(rs, from, dir)` is the place an arrow key sends a row to: ↑ / ↓ one place (out of a group at its ends), ← out of its group, → into the group next to it.
- 12 unit tests: down and up in a list, a move to where the row already is, into and out of a group, empty groups going away, a group moved whole and never into itself, the depth limit (and an already-too-deep group), paths that lead nowhere (including `usize::MAX`), every arrow key, and a row leaving nested single-rule groups.
- Nothing calls the engine yet, so nothing in the app changes.

**Not in this PR:** the editor integration (the grips, dragging with a drop line, Esc, the keyboard handling and focus, accessible names, locale strings, headless interaction tests…

title: Keep file name and query for fragment-only redirect Location
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/fetch/src/http.rs:139 (Url::join)` (no existing issue): Fragment-only redirect Location drops the file name and query from the URL path.

## Cause
Url::join resolved every relative Location against the directory of the current path. A fragment-only or empty Location became `{dir}/#top`, and Url::parse later stripped the fragment, which left only the directory without the file name and query.

## Fix
Url::join now returns a copy of the current URL when the trimmed Location is empty or starts with '#'. The redirect then targets the same document, including its file name and query. A regression test covers `#top`, an empty Location and a whitespace-only one.

## Verified
- Regression test `http::tests::fragment_only_or_empty_location_keeps_file_name_and_query`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-fetch --lib fragment_only`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Query-only Locations (`?x`) and other relative paths still resolve as before. The query-only case is tracked separately.

title: LR-PREF-DISPLAY: on Windows, previews follow the monitor's colour profile
author: insideTheFlux
body:
On Windows, previews now follow the colour profile Windows assigns to the monitor showing the window, as macOS (#787) and Linux (colord) already do. Part of gap 22 and LR-PREF-DISPLAY.

## Why
On an SDR desktop Windows passes what an app draws to the monitor unchanged. Until now LightCraft showed previews as sRGB unless you picked an ICC file by hand in Settings ▸ Display. A wide-gamut monitor therefore showed photos oversaturated, and a calibration was ignored.

## What changed
- **`crates/wincolor` (new, L0):** `monitor_color(hwnd)` finds the monitor the window is mostly on (`MonitorFromWindow`, `GetMonitorInfoW`) and gets its device id (`EnumDisplayDevicesW`). It then asks Windows Color System for that monitor's default profile: in the user's scope when they chose per-user profiles for it, otherwise the system's. The answer is one of:
  - `Profile(path)`
  - `NoProfile`: none assigned, so Windows treats the monitor as sRGB.
  - `ManagedByWindows`: Windows colour-manages the desktop itself, either HDR on or Auto Color Management, read from `DisplayConfigGetDeviceInfo`'s advanced-colour flags. Windows then treats an ordinary app's output as sRGB and converts it, so previews stay sRGB instead of being converted twice.
  - `Unknown`
- **`apps/lightcraft/src/win_screen_profile.rs`** provides `Services::screen_profile` on Windows. The UI already polls it about once a second while no profile is chosen. Each time the answer changes, the log records which case applies (`screen profile: …`).
- **`apps/lightcraft/src/profile_file.rs`:** the profile-file loader moved out of the Linux-only `colord.rs`, unchanged, so both platforms share it. A small cache re-reads the file only when its path, size or modification time changes, because calibrators rewrite profiles under the same name.
- **Settings and `app.displayProfile`:** on Windows, Settings ▸ Display now offers **Use Screen Profile**, and `app.displayProfile` reports `screen: true`. Both already depend on whether the servi…

title: LR-EDIT-OPTICS-PROFILE: read Fujifilm's nine-knot lens tables at the plain radius
author: JackalCOB
body:
## Summary

`raf_lens.rs` reads a Fujifilm distortion or vignetting table at `ρ = knot_last · r`, taking the last knot as the
frame's corner. The newer bodies write nine knots at `√(k/8)`, so the eighth knot is exactly 1 and the ninth,
`√(9/8) = 1.0607`, lies past the corner. Read at `ρ = r` instead, the X-T4's tables match the camera's own correction,
and the current reading takes every value from about 6% further out. Vignetting shows it most: corners come out up to
6.5% brighter than the camera's.

- `Geometry::bracket` and the vignette gain read the table at the plain radius, so `Table::last` is no longer needed
- Nothing changes for the 11-knot tables or the GFX 50's 8-knot ones, whose last knot is 1
- The X-T4 test expectations follow, and `matches_the_measured_x_t4_geometry` tightens from 0.004 to 0.0012 half
  diagonals, which the plain reading meets
- `docs/fuji-lens-corrections.md` describes the knots as radii and adds the evidence under "Knot radius"
- `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` goes to 66 (main reached 65 in 62e82479) so thumbnails redraw, as the Sony ARW table change did, and What's New has an entry

I found this while measuring the X-T4's film simulations for #380. The looks PR depends on this one, since LightCraft's
render can only match the camera's if the lens corrections do.

title: LR-PROF-CAMERA: measured looks for the X-T4's film simulations
author: JackalCOB
body:
## Summary

This builds the design proposed in #380 ([comment](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/380#issuecomment-6164141153)).
There's been no answer yet, so it's here to review or turn down. Either is fine: I'd rather know the reason than wait.

**It builds on #2444** (Fujifilm's nine-knot lens tables read at the plain radius), now merged. Without it, most
X-T4 zoom photos get no distortion correction and brighter corners than the camera's, so LightCraft's render can't
match the camera's whatever the look does. The figures below were measured with it.

- **Nine measured looks for the Fujifilm X-T4**, one per colour film simulation. Each is a 3D lookup from white-balanced
  camera RGB to the colour the camera writes, fitted to synthetic charts the camera itself converted. They are profiles
  (`look:x-t4/provia` … `look:x-t4/eterna-bleach-bypass`), listed in the profile browser and menu for X-T4 raws under

  their camera
- **A look is the whole rendering**, so it replaces the starting look's tone map and chroma curve in the finishing stage.

  table maps some camera colours to the same pixel (yellow greens around hue 120–150), so a look can't recover the
  camera colo…

title: Use chrono instead of hand-rolled UTC conversion
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
Follow-up to storytold/cadcraft#1785 (see reference PR storytold/cadcraft#1789).

## Summary
Many crates carried their own copy of Howard Hinnant's `civil_from_days` /
`days_from_civil` (the `719_468` / `146_097` magic numbers) plus a hand-written
leap-year / days-in-month table. This routes all of that through `chrono`
instead, as a new workspace dependency
(`chrono = { version = "0.4.45", default-features = false, features = ["std"] }`),
which is wasm-safe with only `std`. Every output format and parsing rule is
unchanged; the existing format tests pin them and still pass.

Replaced functions and their formats:
- `apps/lightcraft/src/logging.rs` — `timestamp(SystemTime)` → `2026-10-08T07:59:17.728Z`
  (UTC, milliseconds; a pre-1970 clock still clamps to the epoch). Deleted the
  `civil_from_days` helper.
- `crates/catalog/src/dates.rs` — `civil(i64 secs)` → `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` (UTC),
  and `weekday(iso)` now goes through `NaiveDate::weekday()`. Deleted the
  `civil_from_days` helper.
- `crates/catalog/src/stacks.rs` — `iso_seconds(iso) -> i64` (date → seconds).
  The day-past-month-length rollover (e.g. `2026-02-30` → `2026-03-02`) that
  `normalize_iso` relies on to reject impossible dates is preserved by adding
  `(day-1)` days to the first of the month via `NaiveDate::checked_add_days`.
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/face_recognize.rs` — `capture_secs(iso)` (native only;
  it lives in the non-wasm `imp` module, so chrono is added under that target).
  Same rollover handling.
- `crates/meta/src/datetime.rs` — `DateTime::unix_seconds()` and the calendar-day
  check in `DateTime::valid()`. The leap-year/days-in-month table is gone;
  chrono rejects impossible days. The time checks stay hand-written so a leap
  second (`second == 60`) is still accepted, and EXIF/XMP parsing semantics are
  unchanged.

`AGENTS.md` (and `CLAUDE.md`, which duplicates it) gain the non-negotiable that
time goes through chrono and nobody hand-rolls calendar math.

title: PERF-WALK: a folder walk on a network share lists up to eight folders at the same time
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

Why one PR: the completion-order walk (`files_in_parallel`) is a second consumer of the same reader pool, folded in at mattsivak's request ([comment](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/pull/2480#issuecomment-6366222611)) so that the app has one pool instead of two. It adds a variant in `walk.rs` and its tests, and shares the pool's state and reader loop, so it cannot land without the pool; the pool alone is the earlier commits. About 1,030 changed lines in all, a good part of them tests.

## Problem

Every folder walk (the import and Add Photos review, Synchronize Folder, Local's Include Subfolders, Find Missing Photos, preset and LUT folders, the MCP tools) lists one folder after another on one thread (`crates/engine/src/walk.rs`). On a network share each listing is at least one round trip, so a tree of many folders waits for them in a chain before the first photo is read.

Measured on an SMB share (M1 Max, gigabit LAN, cold: each run after at least 470 s idle, since macOS keeps directory listings for about 7 minutes):

| Tree | Folders | Entries | Listing, one folder at a time |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 22 | 1,607 | 6.0–6.6 s |
| B | 147 | 1,577 | 12.8–14.3 s (median 14.0, n=7) |
| C | 247 | 9,631 | 46.1–48.1 s (median 48.0, n=3) |

## Change

- Up to 8 reader threads (scoped std threads) list folders ahead of the walk. - Readers start only when a listing shows two or more subfolders, so a flat folder or a single chain starts no thread.
- Readers list plain folders only. A folder reached through a link is listed by the walk itself, after it has decided to enter it, so a folder two links lead to is never read twice.
