title: LR-VIEW-HQPREVIEW: View ▸ High Quality Preview
author: akulica
body:
## What

Adds **View ▸ High Quality Preview** (`view.highQualityPreview`, also via MCP / control protocol). Off by default, saved with the UI state.

## Why

Below 100 % the loupe develops a resampled source. For sparse, near-binary detail (star fields, line art, fractal renders) under a strong non-monotonic curve or a big exposure, "average then curve" is a very different picture from "curve then average": the fit view can show bright texture while the 1:1 view and a full-size export are black.

## How

- `Session::high_quality` turns a loupe job below 100 % (whole frame, zoomed windows, Before) into a native-resolution render, then area-averages it in linear light to the requested pixels (`HqDownscale`, new exact area resampler `raster::resample::area`).
- Slider drags stay draft renders; the HQ render follows on release.
- Native frames too big for memory fall back to the normal render (logged; reported by `ui.inspect` → `highQualityPreview`). Windows whose spots / Auto Mask reads would exceed one render are refused like normal windows.
- HQ jobs have their own result keys and never write the view preview / thumbnail caches; the histogram stays the native render's.
- Exports and settings rendering are unchanged (no process version).
- Not covered (follow-ups): Compare, Survey, second window, slideshow, thumbnails.

## Verification

- 14 new tests: area resampler (constant images, exact 2:1 linear average, mean-light conservation at fractional ratios, fractional / hostile rects), engine HQ jobs (fit view = full-size render scaled down, window matches whole frame, no-op at full size, no cache writes, display-profile histogram), UI toggle (command/menu, persistence, loupe only asks for HQ jobs while on).
- On an 8192² fractal render with an extreme master curve: fit view vs. the full-size export area-averaged to the same size — mean abs diff **80.7 → 4.0** 8-bit codes (mean level 100.8 vs. 24.8 off, 24.7 vs. 24.8 on).

title: TIFF: Read every plane of a planar TIFF (#2462)
author: endthestart
body:
Planar TIFFs (PlanarConfiguration 2) didn't open at all. The decoder called the `tiff` crate's `read_image`, which only reads the first plane of a planar image, so the buffer was a third of what we expected and the decode failed with "sample buffer too short".

I switched it to `read_image_to_buffer`, which reads every plane, and the existing interleave step then puts the samples back together. If the crate ever falls back to the first plane only, it now says the planar TIFF is too large instead of the confusing buffer error.

I added a test that builds a small 16-bit planar RGB TIFF with one strip per plane and checks every pixel. It failed with the reported error before the change.

Let me know if you'd rather fix it another way. Thank you.

Fixes #2462

title: Local: read only a browsed raw's headers; hash it when it joins the library (1/4 of #2001)
author: mattsivak
body:
Step 1 of 4 split out of #2001, as asked in review: the partial raw probe and the deferred content hash (engine only).

## What changes
- Browsing a folder (Local) used to read every file in full to describe and hash it. On a network share that meant downloading every raw before it showed.
- A probe used only for Local (`files::light_probe`) reads the byte ranges `lightcraft_raw::sparse::header_plan` names: about 3 % of a DNG, CR2 or CR3 and about 8 % of an ARW or RAF. It leaves `content_hash` unset.
- Anything it can't describe that way (NEF, ORF, PEF, JPEG and other formats, raws shown only from their embedded preview, a failing read) is read whole, as before.
- **What a catalog record holds changes:** a browsed raw has no content hash until it joins the library. Add to My Photos, or an import of its file, queues it (`crate::hashing`); where nothing runs in the background (CLI, MCP) the command works the hash out at once.
- **The smart-preview cache key moves:** before the hash it is the file's path and size. A smart preview made under that key is renamed to the hash's key, and only once the session records the hash: a result that no longer applies (Add to My Photos undone meanwhile) leaves it where the Local photo still finds it.

## Until step 2 lands
In the app, `hash_in_background` is still `false`, so photos that join the library (Add to My Photos, an import batch, an undo or redo that brings them back) get their hashes on the UI thread right away. Step 2 (#2479, stacked on this branch) moves that to a worker thread, so the two should land together.

## Tests
- `corpus_light_probe_describes_raws_as_the_full_probe_does`: over the downloaded corpus, 319 raws were described from part of the file with results identical to the full probe; 128 were read whole. It skips without the corpus; this branch was not re-run against it.
- `light_probe_reads_other_files_whole`.

title: Local: work out added photos' content hashes on a worker thread (2/4 of #2001)
author: mattsivak
body:
Step 2 of 4 split out of #2001: the app's worker thread for the hashes step 1 defers.

**Builds on #2477**; this PR's own change is [`split/local-raw-header-probe...split/local-hash-worker`](https://github.com/mattsivak/lightcraft/compare/split/local-raw-header-probe...split/local-hash-worker).

## What changes
- The app sets `session.hash_in_background`. `hashing::tick` takes queued photos to a worker thread each frame, one batch at a time.
- Activity row "Checking added photos" (kind `hash`) counts the photos. It has no ✕: the queue lives only in memory, so a stopped batch would never get its hash. The worker owns the row, so it goes however the worker ends.
- Results are recorded only into the library they were queued in (`library_generation`).
- A worker that can't start puts the photos back in the queue (no lost hashes, no stuck row).
- Switching libraries is refused while hashes are queued or being worked out.

Step 4 of 4 split out of #2001: slow-share handling, measured on an rclone SFTP mount to a Hetzner storage box.

title: LR-MERGE-HDR: merge warps sample Lanczos-3 instead of bilinear (1/3 of #1887)
author: mattsivak
body:
Split out of #1887 at @FredApps's suggestion: **part 1 of 3** (the shared `align.rs` refactor and the Lanczos-3 resampler). Part 2 (local alignment, `refine.rs` / `flow.rs`) and part 3 (the HDR merge using them, `metrics.rs`, the sharpness tests) are stacked on this one.

## The problem
Every warp in the merge crate (HDR alignment, panorama projection, Boundary Warp) sampled bilinearly. At a half-pixel offset that is a [½ ½] filter: it keeps cos²(πf) of a pattern's fine detail, a third at 0.3 cycles per pixel. A frame moved by a fraction of a pixel to line it up came out visibly softer.

## Changes
- **`lightcraft_raster::sample`:** `Rgb32f::sample_lanczos3`, a 6 × 6 Lanczos-3 point sampler (taps tabulated at 1024 phases). Each sample is held to the range of the 4 × 4 pixels around it, so hard edges (clipped highlights, stars) don't ring. NaN / infinite coordinates read the nearest edge, as `sample_bilinear` does.
- **`align::warp`**, the panorama projection (`pano/mod.rs`) and Boundary Warp (`pano/finish.rs`) use it.
- **`align.rs`:** the merge luminance (`luma`) and the choice of the simplest RANSAC model that explains (nearly) as many matches as the most general one (`choose_model`, with a minimum inlier share) become shared functions. `align_pair` behaves as before (share 0). Part 2's full-size refinement reuses both.
- **Docs:** `docs/merge.md`, LR-MERGE-HDR / LR-MERGE-PANO notes, What's New.

## Tests
`sample::tests`:
- a half-pixel shift keeps fine detail: ≥ 0.9 of it at 0.2 c/px, and twice what bilinear keeps at 0.3 c/px;
- no overshoot at a hard edge, and pixel centres come back exactly;
- odd coordinates (NaN, ±∞, `f32::MAX`), empty images and all-NaN pixels never panic.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
The panorama projection and Boundary Warp now do about 9× the sampling work of bilinear, unbenchmarked on 100+ MP panoramas. When a panorama is smaller than its photos it is still minified with no prefilter (aliasing, as with bilinear), and Boundary Warp sti…

title: LR-MERGE-HDR: full-size alignment refinement and local alignment (2/3 of #1887)
author: mattsivak
body:
**Stacked on #2481** (part 1: Lanczos-3 warps and the shared `align.rs` functions). Review only `2434525b`; until #2481 lands, the diff against `main` also shows its commit.

Split out of #1887 at @FredApps's suggestion: **part 2 of 3**, the local alignment (`flow.rs`, with `refine.rs`'s patch matching). These modules land on their own. Nothing on `main` uses them yet; part 3 wires them into the HDR merge and measures them there, as #1521 did for `raster::morph`.

## Why
- **Alignment is found on ≤ 1200 px versions only.** On a 24–60 MP frame those are 5–8× smaller, and a tenth of a work pixel is most of a full pixel.
- **A frame too clipped to align is merged unaligned.** A +2 EV frame that is over half clipped gives the small versions nothing to match.
- **One homography covers the whole frame.** Handheld, the camera also moves, so near and far things shift differently (parallax). On a real Sony bracket the fit, dominated by foreground gravel, left a building 2.3 px off.

## What it adds
- **`refine.rs`:** refines an alignment found on the small versions, at full size.
  - **Sites:** one 48 px patch per cell, at the most textured spot (smaller structure-tensor eigenvalue) of each of ~24 cells along the long edge.
  - **Matching:** masked normalised cross-correlation over the pixels usable in both frames (clipped ones aren't), with a sub-pixel parabola peak. Patches that are ambiguous, textureless, on the search border or less than half usable are dropped.
  - **Fit:** RANSAC at 0.75 px, choosing the simplest of translation / similarity / homography via part 1's `choose_model`. A second, narrower pass starts from that fit.
  - **Recovery:** `fit` from the identity at `RECOVER_RADIUS` (±16 px) recovers a frame with no alignment.
  - **Fallback:** `None` when too few patches match or the fit isn't a plausible handheld motion, so the caller keeps the alignment it had.
- **`flow.rs`:** handles what one model leaves.
  - **Measure:** ~96 tiles along the long edge, each …

title: LR-MERGE-HDR: sharp handheld HDR merges — refined and local alignment, the reference's finest detail (3/3 of #1887)
author: mattsivak
body:
**Stacked on #2482** (#2481 has landed). Review `bb98e24f`, `30f57d30`, `752d86c3` and `23ce99f8`; until #2482 lands, the diff against `main` also shows its commit `e1a4259b`.

Split out of #1887 at @FredApps's suggestion: **part 3 of 3**, the HDR merge changes in `hdr.rs`, `metrics.rs`, and the `sharpness` / `real_bracket` tests. The measured numbers in `docs/merge.md` come with this part, since they measure the merge.

## The problem
HDR merges of handheld brackets came out visibly softer than any single frame, with doubled detail. Parts 1 and 2 add the tools (Lanczos-3 warps, full-size refinement, local alignment); this PR makes the merge use them.

## Changes
- **`hdr.rs`, alignment:** for every frame but the reference:
  - **Refine:** the small-version fit is refined at full size (`refine::fit`).
  - **Recover:** a frame the small versions couldn't align (a bright frame mostly clipped) is recovered from no alignment, searching ±16 px.
  - **Local shifts:** what the one model leaves is measured tile by tile (`flow::estimate`).
  - **Warp:** the frame is resampled once through both (`flow::warp`).
  - **Report:** the merge info gives each frame's largest local shift as `localPx` (`engine/src/merge.rs`).
- **`hdr.rs`, reference detail (`reference_detail`):** with everything aligned, the merge was still a little softer than the single raw. Every frame but the reference is resampled and aligned to a fraction of a pixel, and the brightest frames weigh most in midtones and shadows.

  - The difference is blurred over the pixels it applies to only, so the reference's clipped highlights can't leave a bright rim around them.

title: Convert Negative 1/4: lightcraft-film, the negative conversion maths
author: smyrgeorge
body:
## Summary

Part 1 of 4 of Convert Negative (Photo ▸ Convert Negative, film-negative conversion), split from #2364 as suggested in review. Landing order:

1. **this PR**: `crates/film` (`lightcraft-film`, L1), a library with no caller yet
2. settings and the pipeline stage
3. engine commands
4. Photo menu entry, panel and docs

## What's in it

`lightcraft-film` is the negative-conversion maths, ported from [Film Lab](https://github.com/smyrgeorge/film-lab) (same author, MIT). It's Film Lab's core crate almost unchanged, without the PhotoCraft-only sharpening and JSON parameter scanning:

- **Film model** (`film.rs`): density grows with log exposure; each channel is read relative to the film base, which also removes the orange mask.
- **Levels** (`analysis.rs`): each channel's density range between its black and white points maps onto the same stops of scene brightness.
- **Colour and tone** (`look.rs`, `tone.rs`, `color.rs`): white balance, colour models, toning, tone profiles; `Converter` with an exact path and a table-driven path.
- **Film presets** (`preset.rs`): Standard, Portra 160 / 400, Ektar 100, Gold 200, ColorPlus 200, UltraMax 400, Superia 400, C200, Pro 400H, CineStill 800, Monochrome. Film names are their makers' trademarks and only say which stock a preset takes after.
- **New: whole-scan measurement** (`measure.rs`): the film base, per-channel black and white points and a neutral balance, measured once inside a border. A host stores the result with the photo's settings, so every render converts with the same numbers.

Other changes: `libm` becomes a workspace dependency (pure Rust, already in the lockfile), and `film` is registered as L1 in `xtask/src/layers.rs`.

title: security: enforce HTTPS on curl downloads (SonarCloud S6506)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
Enforces HTTPS on `curl` downloads flagged by SonarCloud rule **S6506** (`shell:S6506`, `docker:S6506`, `githubactions:S6506`, Security).

These `curl` calls use `-L`/`-fsSL` (follow redirects). A redirect could transparently downgrade to plaintext HTTP, exposing the download to MITM tampering. Adding `--proto '=https'` forces curl to refuse any non-HTTPS protocol, including across redirects, without changing behavior for the legitimate HTTPS endpoints already in use.

## Change
`curl <args>` → `curl --proto '=https' <args>` on each flagged line.

🤖 Generated to address SonarCloud findings.

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: decode Sony ARW version 1 (DSLR-A200 to A390)
author: insideTheFlux
body:
**TL;DR:** The 12-bit compressed ARW files of the Sony DSLR-A200, A230, A290, A330, A350, A380 and A390 now decode from the raw sensor data instead of opening from the embedded preview. Fixes #2484 and #461; closes the "A200–A390 preview-only" item of #535.

## Change

- New `crates/raw/src/vendor/arw1.rs`: a decoder for Sony ARW version 1 (see **Provenance** below). The strip is one most-significant-bit-first stream of lossless-JPEG-style differences: a Huffman code gives the difference's bit length, then come the bits, sign-extended the JPEG way. One running 12-bit predictor spans the whole frame. The frame is coded column by column from the right edge; within a column the even rows come first, then the odd rows. The coded frame is 8 rows taller than the image IFD's height, and those extra rows are dropped.
- `crates/raw/src/vendor/arw.rs`: a Compression 32767, 12-bit, single-strip file that is neither ARW2 (one byte per pixel) nor packed 12-bit (1.5 bytes per pixel) now goes to `arw1` instead of returning `Unsupported`. The decoder reads only the recorded strip; a strip that ends before the frame is decoded is `Corrupt`. Black 128, white from the data.
- `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 65 → 66 (main took 65 while this PR was open): renders of these bodies change from preview to raw.
- Docs: `docs/raw-parity.md` (format row → 🟡, Sony row, ranked list, revision history) and `docs/gaps.md` (gap 10).
- Separate commit: the `tests_staging` module in `crates/catalog/src/store.rs` is now `#[cfg(all(test, unix))]`. Its only test is Unix-only, so on Windows its `use super::*` was unused and `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` failed on main.

## Provenance

The code table (`CODES`) and scan order in `arw1.rs` were written by the AI assistant from its recalled knowledge of the format, before any analysis of the sample files. They match dcraw's Sony ARW v1 loader entry for entry, including the 16- and 17-bit codes that 12-bit data never uses. No other decoder's source was opened whil…

title: LRC-LIB-IMPORT: month names in date templates (%B January, %b Jan)
author: bdebyl
body:
## Problem

Date templates (Import ▸ Folders ▸ Custom template…, Rename Photos, export file names) only take numeric directives. A library already laid out by month name, such as `2026/September` (a common Lightroom/ON1 layout), can't be matched: `{date:%Y}/{date:%B}` makes a folder literally named `%B`, and `{date:%m}` makes `09` next to the existing `September`.

## Change

`format_date` in `crates/engine/src/rename.rs` adds two directives:

| Directive | 2026-01-14 gives |
|---|---|
| `%B` | `January` |
| `%b` | `Jan` |

- Names come from `lightcraft_catalog::dates::MONTHS` and are **English in every interface language**, so a library's folders don't change when the language does (`%m` isn't localized either).
- **Never crash:** a month that isn't `01`–`12`, or a short or non-ASCII date string, gives an empty name with no panic. A folder level then becomes `unknown`, like any missing value.

title: LRC-LIB-MISSING: the availability worker sweeps a list of files at low priority and gives way to file work
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`. Independent of `missing-photos-sweep` (the prerequisites): it uses nothing from it, and either can land first.

Part of the Missing Photos sweep (2 of 3).

## Problem

The sidebar's Missing Photos count checks every library file with its own thread, at most every 5 s while the catalog changes. On a large library on a network share, a better design is one low-priority stream of checks on the worker that already answers "is this file there?" for the grid. But a first version of that sweep ran for tens of minutes after every open, at a stat per file, while an import review scan's readers waited on the same share: 32 readers read 101 files/s alone and 65 files/s with one stat loop beside them. The sweep has to be able to give way, and it has to be droppable when another library is opened.

## Change

All in `crates/engine/src/availability.rs` (plus the one-line `gone_generation` use in `crates/engine/src/lib.rs`):

- `Availability::sweep(paths)`: a list checked one file at a time and only when nothing is asked; files checked less than 15 s ago are skipped; one sweep at a time.
- The files found gone are kept (`is_gone`, `gone_len`). `gone_generation` replaces `generation` and changes only when a file is found gone or back; a file found there at its first check changes nothing and wakes nobody.
- `restart_sweeps` / `sweep_in(epoch, paths)`: opening another library drops what is left of the old sweep, and a list that was being made for the old one is refused.
- `sweep_yields_to(callback)`: while it says file work is going on, the worker starts no sweep check; what is asked is still answered (within 250 ms), and the sweep goes on where it stopped (nothing is listed again).

Sweep and pause are one change on purpose: the sweep without the pause is the slow version above.

**Not in this PR:** nothing in the app starts a sweep or sets the callback yet (that is `missing-count-app`), so the Missing Photos count and the app behave as before. The worker tests exercise…

title: Edit Capture Time leaves a capture time it can't fully read as it was
author: clydecbrown
body:
Fixes #2505

Edit Capture Time no longer turns a capture time it can only partly read into a clean-looking wrong one. `shift_iso` now writes back only a time it fully reads. `iso_seconds` stays lenient, so sorting, grouping and date rules read the same strings as before. A photo whose time doesn't read is left as it was, `photo.setCaptureTime` counts it, and the dialog says so.

### What changed

- **`shift_iso`** (`crates/catalog/src/dates.rs`): a new `tail_start` checks the whole string first. It accepts a date alone, or a date and a time (`T` or a space) with `HH:MM`, optional `:SS` with an optional fraction, an optional zone (`Z`, `+02:00`, `-0500`, `+02`), and nothing after. Anything else is `None`. A fraction after the minutes (`10:00.5`) is refused too: it is half a minute, and it would come back as half a second after `:00`. All checks are on bytes through `get`, so a multi-byte character anywhere is a `None`, never a panic.
- **`photo.setCaptureTime`** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/manage.rs`): a photo it can't shift because its time doesn't read is counted in a new `unreadable` result key, which the help string documents. Setting a time for the active photo (not `each`) is refused when that photo's own time can't be read and other photos would move by an amount read from it. With that photo alone, or with `each`, it gets the time, which repairs it. The "outside the years 0000–9999" refusal now applies only to a time that reads (`shift_iso(&from, 0)`), so a malformed one no longer blocks the whole shift.
- **Edit Capture Time dialog** (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/dialogs.rs`): when the active photo's own time is the problem, the preview says "The active photo's capture time can't be read", not "Enter a date as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS". When OK skips such photos, a toast says they were left as they were. In Set mode with the unreadable photo alone, the preview shows the time it will get. title: lightcraft-web: postMessage host bridge (`?host=parent`)
author: halldave
body:
Lets a same-origin page embed LightCraft in an `<iframe>` to edit one photo, as WordCraft's and GridCraft's bridges do.

- `lightcraft:ready {version}` when the app is listening.
- `lightcraft:open {name, bytes}` (ArrayBuffer or Uint8Array, any format LightCraft imports: JPEG, PNG, TIFF, WebP, DNG, camera raws…) imports the photo like a drop, selects it and shows it in the Detail view.
- `lightcraft:save {name, bytes}` (transferred ArrayBuffer) replaces every download: Export, Export with Previous (JPEG `<stem>.jpg` by default; the Export dialog can pick another format) and the other exports. An export marks the photo clean.
- `lightcraft:dirty {dirty}`: whether the photo's edit settings differ from those it was opened or last exported with; `lightcraft:failed {error}` when the app can't start.
- Host mode keeps the library in memory only (no browser storage, no demo photos, no one-tab lock), and Export with Previous works from the start. LightCraft has no user name, so `?author=` is ignored.

Only messages from the parent window on the page's own origin are heard, and replies go only to it. The change is confined to `apps/lightcraft-web` (new `host.rs`, hooks in `web.rs`).

title: raw: decode Canon CRW (CIFF) files
author: radialmonster
body:
Draft: the format work is being re-derived from the CC0 files only; the private set will be used for testing only.

Canon CRW (CIFF, 2000-2004 bodies) imports as an embedded preview only today. This decodes the raw data for the bodies whose compression can be derived cleanly, and leaves the rest on the preview path.

Closes #2442 for the decodable bodies (see gaps below).

## What it does
- CIFF heap parse: sensor size, active and masked rectangles, make/model, rotation, camera white balance where the file records it.
- Raw decode: Huffman-coded blocks of 64 consecutive samples (DC cumsum across blocks, then two stride-2 row chains), a separate 2-bit low plane on the 12-bit bodies. Bayer RGGB at the frame origin. Black comes from the masked area per site; white from the data plateau.
- Routing: only `RawFormat::Crw` changes. The other formats are untouched; `crates/raw` tests (430 lib + integration) and the engine preview-only import tests pass. The one preview test that asserted CRW was unsupported now asserts the new state.
- Robustness: `tests/crw_fuzz.rs` runs truncations and bit flips (set `LIGHTCRAFT_CRW_FILES`, `;`-separated) plus synthetic garbage; no panics or hangs in debug and release.

## Results (decoded, 16 files, by body)
PowerShot G2, G3, G5, G6, Pro1, S30, S40, S45, S50, S60, S70: 1 file each. EOS D30, D60, 10D, 300D, Digital Rebel: 1 file each. Checks per file: no out-of-range samples, black from the masked pixels, no row/column banding in the masked areas, luminance of the active area correlates 0.93-0.996 with the embedded JPEG (geometry/brightness reference only).

## Not decoded (stay preview only, with an Unsupported message)
- Huffman table 2 (10D 3164/3165, 300D 3162; 3 files): the table is not stored in the files and could not be derived.
- PowerShot Pro70 (1 file): no sensor-info record.
- PowerShot G1 (1 file): complementary CMYG filter array, which the RGB pipeline cannot represent.

title: Kelvin for Fujifilm X-Trans III bodies from the RAF's own neutral pair (#730)
author: radialmonster
body:
Fujifilm X-Trans III bodies (X-T20, X-T2, X-Pro2, X-E3, X-H1, X100F) have no measured colour matrix, so As Shot showed on the relative scale (0 / 0). This gives them Kelvin and tint. Part of #730 (symptom a only).

## Route and provenance
- Source: the file's own tag 0xf00c, the camera's neutral multipliers for Illuminant A (2856 K) and D65 (6504 K). The tag number came from a black-box exiftool run on the files; no other tool or code was consulted.
- Model: a two-point line in (ln R/G, ln B/G). Mired is linear along it (extended past both ends), isotherms are perpendicular to it, tint is scaled by the CIE 1960 spacing of the Planckian locus. Only the file's pair and CIE colorimetry (Planckian/daylight locus, 1931 observer) are used. No fitted constants, no other camera's data, no attribution-licensed dataset.
- Bodies with measured matrices (X-T3 family and others) are unchanged: the presets are only used when no spectral row is found. Coverage is by name in `kelvin_presets::covers`, which the catalog's `relative_wb_camera` shares.

## Accuracy
Scored only (never fitted) against the measured matrices of X-T3, X-T4 and GFX 100, on 3200 to 9000 K and tints of +-20: 6.8 mired rms (21 worst) and 3.0 tint rms (8 worst); 11 mired rms over 2500 to 12000 K. As Shot and whites near the A-D65 line are exact by construction. The plain line is the accepted limit; the stored D65 pair and the X-T3-family matrices themselves disagree by about 12% in Kelvin, so this is a self-consistent scale rather than a match to another body.
Sanity only: an X-T20 sample reads 6193 K / +16 (Lightroom shows 6050 K / +22). One extreme X-T2 sample (R 1.53, B 4.19) reads 2602 K / +104, far off the line but inside the clamps.

## Not in this PR
Default colour (symptom b, greens and yellows) is unchanged: the look stays the camera-JPEG per-file fit. A proper fix needs a chart shot from an X-Trans III body (X-T20 or similar), raw plus the chart.

title: LR-META-XMP: Preserve foreign namespace collisions
author: ronibalthazar
body:
## Summary

Fix XMP namespace collisions so foreign properties survive saves and foreign values cannot impersonate LightCraft or standard XMP metadata. A sidecar may bind a familiar prefix such as `lc` or `xmp` to a vendor URI; prefix spelling alone must not grant ownership or metadata meaning.

## Root cause

`crates/meta/src/xmp.rs::canonical` mapped recognized namespace URIs to canonical prefixes but returned the raw QName for unknown URIs. A vendor property such as `lc:Secret` was therefore classified by the merge rules as LightCraft-owned and could be silently deleted. A vendor `xmp:Rating` could also be imported as a genuine rating.

## Changes

- Resolve recognized metadata names from namespace URI plus local name, retaining canonical keys and support for genuine aliases.
- Give colliding names from unknown namespaces an opaque URI-qualified identity, and use consistent namespace declaration handling in parsing and merge scanning.
- Preserve foreign attributes and element-form properties while continuing to update genuine owned properties.
- Add parser, merge, alias-stability and end-to-end save regressions, plus clarify the XMP interop docs and update the scoped gap/parity/what’s-new records.

title: Control port: close gracefully so the peer reads the last reply (Windows reset)
author: insideTheFlux
body:
Split out of #1970 (by @LochLogic) so the fix can land ahead of the per-run token work.

## Problem

After rejecting a line (junk, an HTTP request, an over-long line, an idle timeout) the control server closes its socket at once. If the client has sent more after the junk, that input arrives at a closed socket, which answers with a reset. On Windows the reset discards the replies the client has not read yet, so the client gets `os error 10053 / 10054` instead of the `… closing the connection` error that `docs/control-protocol.md` promises.

This is the Windows x64 failure of `control_server::tests::tcp_connection_is_closed_after_junk` in #2377's CI ([run](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/actions/runs/39727041327/job/119653216969)).

## Fix

`serve_stream` serves the socket, then `close_gracefully` shuts down the write side (FIN), reads and drops what is left (at most `MAX_LINE` bytes, 500 ms), and closes. `close_gracefully` is #1970's code unchanged; LochLogic is co-author on the commit.

#1991 (merged) removed the `try_clone` but did not include this close, so main still resets. When #1970 is rebased it can drop `close_gracefully` and keep its token changes on top of `serve_stream`.

## Test

The test sends its last line 100 ms after the junk and reads 100 ms later, so the input arrives after the rejection on every run instead of by chance. On Windows 11 (local):

- without the fix: fails 3 of 3 runs (`Os { code: 10053, kind: ConnectionAborted }`)
- with the fix: passes 5 of 5 runs (0.6 s, including the 500 ms drain)

`cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -p lightcraft --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test -p lightcraft` (71 tests) pass.

title: LR-MAP-TRACKLOG: Decode XML character references in GPX
author: ronibalthazar
body:
## Summary
GPX track logs can encode digits and punctuation in coordinates, elevations, and timestamps with XML character references. The parser previously dropped or misread those values, which could move a photo to the wrong track position or leave it untagged. This change decodes XML references before parsing the affected fields.

## Root cause
`quick-xml` reports entity references in element text as `GeneralRef` events. `parse_gpx` accumulated `Text` and `CData` but ignored `GeneralRef`, so referenced characters disappeared before elevation and timestamp parsing. The `lat` and `lon` attributes were read from their raw escaped bytes, so referenced characters were not decoded there either.

## Changes
- Decode and unescape consumed latitude and longitude attributes with the reader's decoder.
- Resolve decimal and hexadecimal character references and the five predefined XML entities exactly once; map invalid or undeclared references to `GpxError::Xml`.
- Preserve CDATA literally and retain the existing coordinate validation, segment handling, interpolation, and command behavior.
- Add parser regressions for elevation, latitude, timestamp, hexadecimal longitude, malformed and unknown references, and CDATA/predefined-entity behavior.
- Add a headless demo command test comparing plain and encoded dry-run results and verifying GPS tagging and one-step undo.
- Update `docs/gaps.md`, the `LRC-MAP-TRACKLOG` checklist row, and `docs/whats-new.md`.

title: Return None from shift_iso for impossible calendar dates
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/catalog/src/dates.rs:46 (shift_iso, via iso_seconds in crates/catalog/src/stacks.rs:290)` (no existing issue): shift_iso accepts impossible calendar dates and silently rolls them over.

## Cause
shift_iso relied on iso_seconds, which only checks that the day is in 1..=31. A date like 2026-02-30 therefore rolled over into March instead of being rejected, and normalize_iso disagreed because it already guards against this.

## Fix
shift_iso now converts the parsed seconds back to a date and returns None if the date part differs from the input. This is the same round-trip check normalize_iso uses. Valid leap days such as 2024-02-29 are still accepted.

## Verified
- Regression test `dates::tests::shift_refuses_impossible_dates`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-catalog --lib dates::tests::shift_refuses_impossible_dates`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
iso_seconds itself is unchanged, so weekday and the other callers behave as before.

title: Reject non-finite values when parsing .cube LUTs
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/pipeline/src/lut.rs:25 (Lut3d::parse_cube, the `three` helper)` (no existing issue): .cube LUT parser accepts NaN/infinite table entries, so the LUT profile renders NaN pixels.

## Cause
The `three` helper in `Lut3d::parse_cube` parses values with `str::parse::<f32>()`, which accepts `nan`, `inf` and `-inf` and turns too-large values like `1e39` into infinity. None of these were rejected, so data lines and `DOMAIN_MIN`/`DOMAIN_MAX` could hold non-finite values, and `Lut3d::apply` then returned NaN pixels.

## Fix
`three` now accepts a line only when it has exactly three values and all of them are finite. Bad data lines fail with the existing `bad line ...` error and bad domain lines with `bad DOMAIN_MIN`/`bad DOMAIN_MAX`.

## Verified
- Regression test `lut::tests::non_finite_entries_rejected`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-pipeline --lib lut::tests::non_finite_entries_rejected`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Tokens that are not numbers are still skipped silently by the existing `filter_map`, as before. Only non-finite numbers are newly rejected.

Found while testing `crates/meta/src/exif.rs:483 (write_exif, the `r` helper; via lightcraft_tiff::writer::rational at crates/tiff/src/writer.rs:261)` (no existing issue): Exported EXIF ExposureTime is wrong for fast electronic shutter speeds (1/12800, 1/16000, 1/32000 s).

write_exif encoded ExposureTime with lightcraft_tiff::writer::rational, which only tries the denominators 1, 10, …, 1e6 and rounds the numerator. Shutter times that are not a whole number of microseconds came out wrong: 1/12800 s was written as 78/1000000, 1/16000 s as 63/1000000 and 1/32000 s as 31/1000000.

## Fix
write_exif now writes ExposureTime as the exact rational (1, N) when the value is below one second and its reciprocal is a whole number that fits in a u32. This is the same check the XMP writer's frac() already does. All other values still use the generic rational() encoding.

## Verified
- Regression test `exif::write_tests::fast_shutter_speeds_round_trip_exactly`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-meta fast_shutter_speeds_round_trip_exactly`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
lightcraft_tiff::writer::rational and the encoding of FNumber, FocalLength and other rationals are unchanged, and so is the import-side handling of slow shutter speeds.

title: Take photos removed by Synchronize Folder out of their stacks
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/sync.rs:851 (SyncStep::Remove; compare mark_deleted in crates/engine/src/cmd/library.rs:168)` (no existing issue): Synchronize Folder's Remove Missing Photos leaves the removed photos in their stacks.

## Cause
Found while comparing with `mark_deleted` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/library.rs` (no existing issue). Synchronize Folder's Remove Missing Photos leaves the removed photos in their stacks. When `folder.synchronize` runs with `removeMissing`, it sends photos whose files are gone to Recently Deleted using only `Op::SetDeleted` ops. Unlike `photo.delete`, it never adds `remove_from_stacks_ops`, so the removed photos stay in their stacks. The members left behind keep showing them, and `bracket_sets` puts them back into HDR merge sets.

## Fix
`SyncStep::Remove` now collects the ids of the photos it removes and adds `s.catalog.remove_from_stacks_ops(&ids)` to the same batch as the `SetDeleted` ops. This is what `photo.delete` does, and one undo step restores both the photos and their stacks.

- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`Catalog::bracket_sets` still does not filter deleted members out of a stack. With this fix, deleting a photo through either command takes it out of its stack, so deleted photos no longer reach it that way.

title: Issue #136: applying the GPU setting never waits for the device on the UI thread
author: OneSlips
body:
## Problem

The window's first frame waits for the GPU device on the UI thread.

`LightcraftApp::apply_settings` runs `app.gpu {enabled}` on the first frame. The command's reply calls `lightcraft_gpu::available()`, which blocks until the device that `gpu::warm_up()` is creating on its own thread is ready. That undoes what issue #136 set out to do: device and kernel setup is supposed to happen off the UI thread, so a slow or broken driver never holds up the window.

**Why it matters in real work:** every launch, and every time GPU rendering is switched back on in Settings, the window freezes until the device and its kernels are ready. On a busy machine that is several seconds. I measured 8 to 11 s on an RTX 5070 while builds were running. A photographer opening the app on a wedding day sees a frozen window with no feedback.

## What changed

- `app.gpu` takes an optional `wait` parameter. `wait: false` answers at once when the device is still being created; `available`, `adapter` and `reason` are then `null`. Without `wait`, the command behaves as before, so agents and scripts that rely on a definite answer are unaffected.
- The UI applies the setting with `wait: false`. The device is still created by `warm_up()` off the UI thread, and the no-GPU notice still appears once `gpu::ready()` is true (`panels/notices.rs`).

Two files, 13 lines.

## How it was tested

- `headless::tests::a_slow_photos_import_never_blocks_the_window` caught it. The test times a control request that includes the first frame, and failed at 7.9 s under load. With the fix it takes 0.9 s. Timing each frame showed the first frame at 11.25 s with the GPU on and 4 ms with `LIGHTCRAFT_GPU=0`, so the wait was entirely the device.
- `panels::notices::tests::the_gpu_notice_is_only_for_a_missing_adapter` passes.
- `cargo xtask ci` on Windows 11 (RTX 5070): fmt, clippy, parity, layers, assets and wasm all pass. The workspace tests pass except tests that also fail on `main` without this change. Two are Win…

## Summary

PSD files produced by external editing could carry the correct EXIF capture date but LightCraft ignored their embedded metadata and fell back to the file creation date. title: Dehaze no longer crushes dark pixels next to bright ones (#2504), split from #2174
author: francoisgn
body:
Fixes #2504.

This is commit `7025d7dd2` by @mdlmarkham, taken unchanged out of #2174 (25 bundled fixes, 12 code conflicts with main) so this priority-high fix can merge on its own. Authorship is kept on the commit. @mdlmarkham, if you'd rather open it yourself, say so and I'll close this one.

**What it fixes.** The dark channel is a Gaussian blur, not a patch minimum, so next to a bright neighbour it credits a dark pixel with more veil than its own minimum channel holds; `(c - air*(1-t))/t` then goes negative and is clamped to black (the blotches in #2504). The veil is now bounded by the pixel's own minimum channel, which keeps every channel non-negative for any gain or airlight, on the CPU (`crates/pipeline/src/finish.rs`) and GPU (`finish.wgsl`) paths alike. It also guards a 0/0 on an all-black frame.

**Checks (on this branch, rebased on today's main `31ee2643c`):**
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-pipeline`: 196 passed. The new `dehaze_does_not_crush_dark_regions_next_to_bright_ones` fails without the `finish.rs` change and passes with it.

- `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-pipeline -p lightcraft-gpu --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`: clean.

**For the maintainer.** Renders change only where Dehaze was crushing pixels to black (positive Dehaze), and negative Dehaze adds slightly less haze in dark pixels. I treated it as a bug fix, not a Process V3 change; #1283 (Dehaze V3) is the longer-term rework.

title: LR-META-XMP: Read referenced JPEG Extended XMP
author: ronibalthazar
body:
## Summary

JPEG import and `photo.allMetadata` now include metadata from a valid, referenced Extended XMP packet. Original export with **Remove location info** refuses files with embedded GPS and files whose referenced extension cannot be inspected, preventing a byte-for-byte copy from bypassing location removal.

## Root cause

The JPEG container walker collected Extended XMP bytes by sorting chunk offsets, without validating the standard packet's reference, chunk GUIDs, lengths, or coverage. Production metadata extraction parsed only the standard XMP packet, so extension GPS and descriptive fields were invisible. ## Changes

- Validate the namespace-qualified `xmpNote:HasExtendedXMP` selector and matching chunk GUIDs, consistent full lengths, complete nonoverlapping coverage, APP1 completeness, checked offsets, and bounded assembly.
- Compose standard and extension properties and structured values before projecting to LightCraft metadata, preserving split GPS coordinates and standard-packet precedence.
- Preserve parsed standard XMP for best-effort reads when extension validation fails, while returning an error that lets Original export fail closed.
- Route `photo.allMetadata` through the shared parser while preserving sidecar precedence; document that manual Read Metadata from File remains standard-APP1-only.

title: fix(camera-preview): prefer better accepted per-photo colour fits
author: FooVoo
body:
## Problem

An accepted pooled camera profile can produce a worse starting look than the photo's own accepted colour fit. The ordered search stops at the first profile that passes the neutral-fallback gates, without comparing it with the per-photo alternative. A Sony A6000 foliage diagnostic reproduced this: both fits used the same sensor/reference samples, but the profile had higher gamma-domain fitting error and worse rendered camera-JPEG appearance.

## Changes

- Compare the accepted profile look with an accepted per-photo colour fit using the same final fitting samples, tone method, edge filter and dark-scene setting.
- Score both completed looks, including hue, tone and chroma, with the existing gamma-domain colour-pair selection objective. Select the per-photo fit only when its finite error is strictly lower; retain the profile on a tie, an unusable alternative or nonfinite scores.
- Preserve the existing absolute/highlight acceptance gates, clipped-pixel refit behavior, unprofiled and partial fallbacks, and DRO handling.
- Bump camera-look version 12 to 13 and render-cache version 69 to 70, since selection can change stored looks and rendered pixels without changing profile files.
- Add synthetic regressions for both selection outcomes, successful/failed clipped refits, the unclipped-only search path and sparse-colour profile fallback; document the selection limits.

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Accepted profile and better accepted per-photo fit | First accepted profile wins | Lower gamma error wins on the same fitting samples |
| Better profile, unusable alternative, tie or nonfinite comparison | Profile retained | Profile retained |

title: Library lock: Don't write through a link at the owner note's name
author: Matoo125
body:
Opening a library writes `catalog.lock.owner` with `std::fs::write`, which follows a symlink at that name. A library folder someone else prepared (a shared drive, an unpacked archive, a synced folder) could carry `catalog.lock.owner` as a link to any file the user can write, and opening the library replaced that file's content with the owner JSON. This is the same pattern #1502 fixed for the catalog's staging files; the owner note was missed.

**Fix:** the note is now written through `store::create_staging` (made `pub(crate)`), the helper from #1502. It removes whatever is at the name (a link itself, never its target), then creates the file with `create_new`. `Drop` already removes the note with `remove_file`, which never follows a link.

**Test:** `tests_lock::a_link_at_the_owner_note_is_never_written_through` (Unix). A link at `catalog.lock.owner` pointing at a file outside the library leaves that file unchanged through `acquire` and drop, and the note lands in the library as a regular file naming this process. It fails on `main` (the target gets the owner JSON) and passes with the fix.

**Checks:** `cargo test -p lightcraft-catalog` passes (229), and `cargo fmt --check` is clean. `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-catalog --all-targets -D warnings` reports one `collapsible_else_if` in `journal.rs:439`, which is identical on `main` with my local clippy 1.93; this change adds no warnings. I didn't run the full `cargo xtask ci`.

`docs/whats-new.md` has an entry under 2026-10-22, written like the #1502 one.

Part of #840.

Colour noise reduction blurred the per-pixel ratio rgb/Y, which does not preserve channel means where Y is small or noisy. It now blends toward blur(rgb)/blur(Y) taken at each pixel's own luminance (so every pixel's luminance is kept exactly and the local mean colour is kept). CPU (`pipeline/src/local.rs`) and GPU (`gpu/src/wgsl/map.wgsl`, `render.rs`) paths both change; slider mapping and defaults are unchanged.

Measured against the previous code, same metric (ΔE vs the camera JPEG, each JPEG read in its own colour space; lower is better), as the change in ΔE relative to colour NR off, by ISO. Set: 26 R6-family CR3 plus 216 of 219 other CR3 (26 bodies; pixls CC0, user samples, submissions). P:/raw-pixls-ncsa has no CR3, so there is no held-out set for this format.
- ISO >= 12800 (28 files), default slider: +0.244 -> -0.032 (regression gone)
- ISO 3200-12800 (10), default: -0.122 -> -0.214
- ISO 800-3200 (40), default: -0.046 -> -0.065
- ISO < 800 (137): chroma-noise cut unchanged (R/G 0.0521 -> 0.0520 at default); ΔE gains kept
- 26 R6-family files, default: ΔE 3.112 -> 3.094, chroma noise unchanged (R/G 0.0440)

Not fixed: the default (25) still removes only ~17% of chroma noise. A stronger blend (t=0.5, 4.5 px) cuts it 32-36% with ΔE -0.03 up to ISO 3200 and is now at -0.29 at 3200-12800, but still costs +0.45 ΔE at ISO >= 12800, so the default is left alone. Hence "Part of", not "Fixes".

Tests: new `colour_nr_keeps_means_in_noisy_shadows` (means and per-pixel luminance kept, chroma noise cut); `cargo test` for lightcraft-pipeline and lightcraft-gpu (incl. CPU/GPU equivalence) pass.

Reproduce: render each file with the CLI (`render f -o out.png --set detail.nrColor=0|25|50 ...`), flat 16 px blocks chosen on the NR-off render, chroma noise = within-block std of log(R/G), log(B/G); ΔE (CIE76 at 342 px) vs the camera JPEG. Details and per-round logs in #840.

title: LR-EXP-LOCATION: an export subfolder never leaves the destination folder (#2571)
author: insideTheFlux
body:
Fixes #2571.

## Problem

The export subfolder could lead outside the chosen folder. It reaches the export three ways, and none was safe:
- command / control / MCP parameters: `from_json` turned `\`, `:` and NUL into `_` but kept `/` and `..`;
- the Export dialog's Subfolder field: written to `ExportOptions::subfolder` directly, not cleaned;
- saved presets: deserialized with serde, not cleaned.

`join_path(&base, &subfolder)` then gave e.g. `out/../../escaped/x.png`.

## Fix

`clean_subfolder` (`crates/engine/src/export.rs`) turns `\`, `:` and NUL into `_` and drops empty, `.` and `..` parts, so no root, drive or parent step survives. It is applied in `Placer::folder_for`, which every export goes through, and to the parameter in `from_json`. Nested subfolders (`Client/Jobs`) still work.

## Test

`tests_export::a_subfolder_never_leaves_the_destination_folder` exports with options built directly (as the dialog and presets do) and checks the written path for `../../escaped`, `..`, `/etc`, `C:\Windows`, `a/./b/../c` and ` Client / Jobs `, plus the parameter path. Without the fix it fails (`out/../../escaped/x.png`).

`cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-engine --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test -p lightcraft-mcp` and `cargo xtask parity` pass. On Windows, `cargo test -p lightcraft-engine` has one unrelated failure, `tests_import::recursive_discovery_includes_sony_sr2_and_srf_case_insensitively`, a path-separator bug in that test that #2377 fixes.

Not covered here: #2564 (`mask.exportEffects` destination), a separate path.

title: Write capture time UTC offset and sub-seconds in write_exif
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/meta/src/exif.rs:462 (write_exif; compare the reader in from_tiff at crates/meta/src/exif.rs:96-107)` (no existing issue): write_exif drops the capture time's UTC offset and sub-seconds (OffsetTimeOriginal / SubSecTimeOriginal never written).

## Cause
write_exif wrote DateTime and DateTimeOriginal using to_exif(), which is only YYYY:MM:DD HH:MM:SS. It never wrote the OffsetTime* or SubSecTime* tags, so the time zone offset and milliseconds were lost on export.

## Fix
write_exif now writes OffsetTime and OffsetTimeOriginal as ±HH:MM when the capture time has an offset. It writes SubSecTime and SubSecTimeOriginal as three digits when millis is non-zero. Reading the result back with read_exif now returns the same capture_time.

## Verified
- Regression test `exif::write_tests::capture_time_offset_and_subsec_round_trip`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-meta --lib capture_time_offset_and_subsec_round_trip`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
DateTimeDigitized and its OffsetTimeDigitized and SubSecTimeDigitized tags are still not written. Reader behaviour is unchanged.

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: GIF and BMP sizes from the header; a canvas the file can't fill is refused (#2553)
author: insideTheFlux
body:
Fixes #2553 (also the earlier report #2116, closed without a fix when #2182 was abandoned).

## Problem

`read_header_unguarded` had no header reader for GIF or BMP and fell back to a full decode under the default `max_pixels = 1 << 30`. A file of a few dozen bytes declaring a canvas just under that limit passed `check_size`, and `DynamicImage::from_decoder` allocated `w × h × 4` (~4.3 GB) before reading any pixel data. A failed allocation aborts the process, which `catch_unwind` can't catch, so an import of a folder holding such a file could take the app down with unsaved work. A full decode had the same allocation.

## Fix (`crates/codecs/src/other.rs`)

- **`header`**: the import probe reads GIF and BMP sizes from the header. A canvas up to 4 MP is still decoded there (at most 16 MB), so truncated small files are refused at import as before. `tests/header.rs::truncated_files_agree_with_decode` keeps passing.
- **`check_fillable`**: a canvas larger than the file's pixel data can describe is `Malformed`, in the probe and in `decode`, before the decoder allocates. Coverage comes from what the pixel data draws, never from the file's length, so padding (comments, bytes after an end code, trailing bytes) covers nothing:
  - Uncompressed BMP: every row the header describes (its bits per pixel, rows padded to 4 bytes) must be present after the pixel-data offset; `image` reads each row in full.
  - RLE8/RLE4 BMP: the commands are walked as `image` paints them (runs clipped at the row's end; end-of-row, delta and end-of-bitmap leave the rest blank).
  - GIF: a first frame larger than 2,731 pixels per byte of its LZW data is refused outright (a code expands to at most 4,096 pixels and takes 12 bits once the table is that large). Its codes are then walked up to the end code, keeping only each table string's length, to count the pixels they draw. The bound applies to the first frame's own width × height, so a valid GIF with a small first frame on a larger screen still imports…

title: Control port test: send the second request while the first reply is pending (#2538)
author: helgehelge123
body:
Closes #2538.

`control_server::tests::persistent_requests_and_slow_replies_outlive_the_idle_read_timeout` fails now and then in the FreeBSD 15 workflow (`assertion failed: eof.is_empty()`), on PRs that don't touch `apps/lightcraft`.

## Why it failed

The server is doing what #1952 asks of it; only the test had a race.

The test gives the connection a 100 ms idle read timeout. After the server writes reply 2, it goes back to reading, and the 100 ms start. Within that time the test thread had to read reply 2 and call `shutdown(Write)`. On a loaded runner the thread was sometimes scheduled later than that. The idle timeout then fired as designed, the server wrote `{"ok":false,"error":"control connection idle read timed out; closing the connection"}`, and that line is what `read_to_string` returned as `eof`.

## The fix (test only)

The client now writes request 2 and half-closes **while the server is still waiting for reply 1**. By the time the server reads again, everything the client will ever send is already in the socket, so no client delay can let the idle timeout fire in between.

The test still checks the same two things:

- two requests are served on one connection;
- a reply that takes longer than the idle timeout (250 ms against 100 ms) does not close the connection. A server that counted the reply wait against the idle timeout would still fail it.

No server code changes.

## Verification

- **The race, reproduced:** with a 150 ms delay added on the client after each reply (to simulate late scheduling), the old test fails and the new one passes.
- **Repeated runs:** `cargo test -p lightcraft --bin lightcraft -- control_server` passed 5 runs in a row on macOS (M4 Pro), 12/12 each time; the whole `cargo test -p lightcraft` passes (74 tests).
- **Lint:** `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy -p lightcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean.

author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem

`tests_activity::a_photo_chosen_during_an_import_stays_selected` (from #1452) fails now and then with `still importing` on a busy machine. It turned up once in a `cargo xtask ci` run on another PR and passed on the rerun, so unrelated PRs can turn red for it.

The test starts an import whose file probe sleeps 100 ms per file, waits until the first batch has joined the catalog, selects one of those photos, then asserts that the import is still running. Nothing holds the import there: 20 files at 100 ms take about two seconds on the import thread whatever the UI thread does. If the frames between the first batch landing and the assertion take longer than the rest of the import (a loaded runner, a slow software-rendered frame), the import ends first and the assertion fails.

- `slow_import` becomes a wrapper over a new `gated_import(tag, n, gate)`. While the gate is false, its probe holds every file after the first batch (`batch_size()` files, which join the catalog together); the hold gives up after 60 s, so a failed test never leaves the import thread spinning.

title: Find Missing Photos matches Windows paths by file name on macOS and Linux
author: clydecbrown
body:
Fixes #2617

## What

On macOS and Linux, Find Missing Photos (`library.findMissing`) couldn't match photos whose recorded path is a Windows path, such as those in a library made on Windows. It took a missing photo's file name with `Path::file_name`, which doesn't treat `\` as a separator there, so the "name" of `C:\Users\me\Photos\a.jpg` was the whole path. Photos with a content hash on record were still found by content; photos with none (Lightroom-catalog imports, files edited since) were never found.

`plan_find_missing` now names both the missing photos and the files it finds on disk with one rule, `name_key` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/missing.rs`): the part after the last `/` or `\`, in lower case. Using the same rule on both sides means a macOS or Linux file name holding a literal `\` (`a\b.jpg`) isn't silently relinked to a `b.jpg` beside it: the two are reported as ambiguous. title: MENU-BAR: the native menu really gives its keys up to a text field and to shortcut recording on macOS
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem

On macOS the native menu is meant to give its keys up while a text field has focus (`G`, `P`, `U`, the digits, ⌘A, ⌘C, …) and while the Keyboard Shortcuts editor is recording a key. It calls `set_accelerator(None)` on each item. In muda 0.21.0 (and 0.21.2, the newest release) that call does nothing on macOS: `setKeyEquivalent` only runs for `Some` (`platform_impl/macos/mod.rs`, `PlatformMenuItem::set_accelerator`). So the item keeps its key and AppKit can still run the menu command instead of passing the key to the field or the editor. Reading the real NSMenu shows it: with a field focused, every item still lists its key.

## Change

- `apps/lightcraft/src/native_menu.rs`: when an item has to lose its accelerator on macOS, it is replaced in its parent submenu by an identical item without one, at the same position with the same id, text, enabled and checked state. When the key comes back, `set_accelerator(Some)` (which does work) is called on that item. Elsewhere `set_accelerator` is used as before.
- The swap only happens when focus or recording changes, and only for the items whose accelerator actually changes, never per frame. Each item remembers the accelerator it has now.
- Settings… (⌘,) and Quit (⌘Q) in the application submenu are tracked like the other items, so they give up their keys to the shortcut recorder too. Items in the Help menu are not swapped (see How it was checked), and muda's predefined system items (Hide, Hide Others, Close Window, Minimize) cannot be swapped at all.
- The decision of which accelerator an item should have is a small pure function with a unit test.
- `docs/whats-new.md` and the MENU-BAR parity row.

**Not in this PR:** #2218 (⌘A and the other text-editing keys sent to the focused field when the menu still takes them). title: LR-CROP-RECT: sidecar settings kept in range; a turned crop bounded to the photo (#2555)
author: insideTheFlux
body:
Fixes #2555 (the sidecar part was reported before as #2121; #2190 attempted it and was closed unmerged).

## Problem

Two gaps let a crop far outside the photo through:
- **The sidecar load skips the range checks.** A sidecar's `lc:settings` becomes the photo's settings through `DevelopSettings::from_json` (`crates/engine/src/sidecar.rs:205`), plain `serde_json::from_value`. #1960 added `keep_in_range`, but only to `merged()` (presets, `develop.merge`, `render --settings`). So sliders, curves and the crop angle in a sidecar kept any value.
- **`keep_in_range` leaves a turned crop unbounded.** It clips the crop to 0..1 only when the angle is exactly 0, so any non-zero angle keeps an arbitrary rect. This applies to `merged()` too.

With a crop rect of 0..1000 at 5°, `native_output_size(6000, 4000)` is 6,000,000 × 4,000,000 px. The export memory check exempts exports not larger than native size, so a full-size export allocates it and the app aborts.

## Fix

- **`DevelopSettings::from_untrusted_json`** (`crates/develop/src/lib.rs`) is `from_json` + `keep_in_range`. The sidecar's `lc:settings` loads through it. Other `from_json` callers (catalog loads etc.) are unchanged.
- **`keep_in_range`** now also keeps the crop angle within ±45°, the crop tools' range; a value that isn't finite becomes 0.
- **`CropGeometry::bounded`** (`crates/geom/src/crop.rs`) clips the crop to the bounding box of the photo turned by its angle (`w·|cos| + h·|sin|` × `w·|sin| + h·|cos|`, centred). Every crop that stays on the photo lies inside that box, so a real crop is returned bit for bit, including the zero-size crops `degenerate_crops_have_a_finite_aspect` relies on. A rect past the box is intersected with it; one with nothing left, or not finite, becomes the whole frame. The pipeline's `Frame` applies it (`crates/pipeline/src/geometry.rs`), so it covers every source of settings (sidecar, agent, `develop.merge`), and native size can't exceed ~1.41× the source per side.

title: #1952: the idle-close MCP test reads blocking and waits for the close
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem

`backend::tests::idle_close_reconnects_without_replaying_a_command` (from #1952) fails now and then, and turned another PR's FreeBSD run red: https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/actions/runs/39842768664. It has two causes, both in the test:

1. The fake server's listener is non-blocking (it polls `accept` with a deadline). On macOS and FreeBSD an accepted socket inherits that flag (Linux does not), so the server's `read_line` for the first request fails at once with `WouldBlock` (os error 35) whenever the request has not arrived yet. The idle check right after it also passed without waiting the 50 ms it means to wait.
2. Once that is fixed, the second `call` can still fail. The server writes its goodbye line, closes, and signals the test, but the bytes reach the client's socket asynchronously. The client reconnects only when it can see the close (`peer_closed` peeks without blocking), so a call made in that gap sends on the old connection and reads the server's idle error as its reply.

## Change

- The server calls `stream.set_nonblocking(false)` on each accepted stream.
- Before the second `call`, the test waits (5 s limit, 1 ms steps) until the client's `peer_closed` sees the close, so the test checks the reconnect without replaying a command, not the delivery delay of loopback bytes.
- Test-only: 8 added lines in `crates/mcp/src/backend.rs`. No production code changes.

**Not in this PR:**

- Any change to `Remote::roundtrip` or `peer_closed`. A close that lands at the exact moment the client checks can still produce the app's idle error for a command that never ran (it is never resent, so nothing is applied twice). That window exists in production and is not something a pre-send check can close.
- `crate::serial_sockets_and_children()` for this test (the other socket tests take it for a Windows-only child-process reset); no failure from that has been seen.

title: raw: CR3 preview box scan checks 32-bit lengths for overflow (#2569)
author: radialmonster
body:
Fixes #2569.

`cr3_preview_boxes` added the 32-bit `PRVW` / `THMB` box size and JPEG length to `usize` offsets unchecked. On wasm32 a length near `u32::MAX` wraps, both bounds checks pass, and `&bytes[j..j + len]` panics, which aborts the web build. The sums now use `checked_add` and the slice uses `bytes.get`, so a bad box is skipped like any other invalid one. This is the site left over from #2138 / #2180.

Tests: a new `cr3_preview_box_huge_lengths_are_rejected` feeds boxes with size and length near `u32::MAX` and expects no preview. `cargo test -p lightcraft-raw --lib preview` passes (18), and `cargo check -p lightcraft-raw --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` is clean. On 64-bit the old code never wrapped, so the new test passes there either way; it guards the 32-bit arithmetic.

title: LRC-LIB-MISSING: library.missing from the control channel checks the files off the UI thread
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem

`library.missing` looks at every photo's file. From the control channel (an agent, `mcp --connect`) it ran inside `Session::execute` on the thread that draws the window, so on a large library on a network share the app stopped answering for as long as the walk took: a library of about 440,000 photos on an SMB share froze the window for over 10 minutes. The existence check is a blocking `stat` per file, and nothing could stop it.

A person's own long jobs (Find Missing Photos, Reload from Disk, Synchronize Folder) already run on a worker thread under a row in the activity stack. This command, reachable only over the control channel, did not.

## Change

- The desktop app answers `library.missing` from the control channel (`engine.execute`, `ui.menu.invoke`, `command`) on a worker thread: a "Missing Photos" row in the activity stack counts the files and its ✕ (or `activity.cancel`) stops the check. The request is answered with the same `[{id, path}]` when the check ends. `Outcome::Later` in `control.rs` lets a handler answer a request after the frame; the reply sender is the one the control server already waits on.
- A second request while a check runs shares it (one walk of the share). A check that stops, panics or ends after another library was opened answers its callers with an error instead of leaving them to time out.
- The control server gives a request 60 s, and a check on a big share takes longer. An answer that nobody was waiting for any more is kept for ten minutes and given once to the next request, so asking again after a timeout is not another walk that times out again.
- Engine: `missing()` (the command itself, for the CLI, the headless MCP server and tests) asks the session's existence check (`media.availability.probe()`, the one the availability cache uses and tests replace) instead of calling `Path::exists` directly, with the same result. New `cmd::missing::checked` / `sweep` / `missing_json` carry the list, a stop and progres…

title: LR-EDIT-DETAIL-DENOISE: GPU denoise doesn't hang when its tiles in flight fail (#2577)
author: Bruno-Alumn
body:
The GPU runner's workspace pool kept its free list and its count of made workspaces behind two mutexes, and forget() lowered the count without the free list's lock that a waiting caller holds. If the tiles in flight failed between a caller finding every workspace in use and that caller starting to wait, the wakeup was lost and the denoise thread blocked forever, out of reach of cancel. The free list and the count now share one lock in a small Workspaces type, so a give or a forget can't slip in between the check and the wait. A caller woken that way after the device was lost returns the GPU's error instead of making a new workspace on it. Fixes #2577.

title: MCP: render and screenshot PNGs go through a private temp folder (#2573)
author: Bruno-Alumn
body:
The render_photo, render_preview and screenshot tools had the backend write their PNG to lightcraft-mcp---.png right in the temp dir. On Linux and FreeBSD, where that is the shared /tmp, other users could read the rendered photos and screenshots, and a name someone else created first made the render fail. Each image now goes in a new lightcraft-mcp-- folder, made 0700 on Unix and never reused when the name already exists, and the folder is removed with anything left in it once the image is read or the call fails. On Windows, and on macOS with its usual per-user TMPDIR, the temp dir was already private; there the PNG just sits one folder deeper. Fixes #2573.

author: Bruno-Alumn
body:

title: Never crash: lossy-JPEG tiles and embedded previews are refused from their JPEG header (#2560)
author: Bruno-Alumn
body:
lossy_jpeg let zune-jpeg decode any frame its header declared, up to 65535 x 65535, so a lossy DNG tile or the embedded preview that ERF and MEF measure white balance from could make it allocate about 12.9 GB before any size check, and on wasm32 the overflowing buffer size hit zune's own unwrap. lossy_jpeg now reads the header first and returns a Limit error for a frame past the caller's edge and pixel caps, or one whose output size overflows usize, before anything is allocated. A lossy tile or strip may declare no more than its nominal size rounded up to whole 16-pixel MCUs, so a last strip coded at the full RowsPerStrip still decodes, and a preview no more than MAX_PREVIEW_PIXELS, which from_rgb already required after decoding. A dhat test probes a synthetic ERF whose preview claims 8192 x 8192 and checks that the peak heap stays under 2 MiB; before the fix it was about 192 MiB. Fixes #2560.

title: Never crash: a keyword nested thousands of levels deep keeps its top 64 levels (#2558)
author: Bruno-Alumn
body:
A keyword from a file's XMP or IPTC metadata, a sidecar or a snapshot was stored with however many levels it had, and the keyword tree, the sidebar and the keyword list file all walk it one call per level, so a keyword some thousands of levels deep overflowed the stack and aborted LightCraft on every launch. clean() now keeps the top 64 levels (MAX_LEVELS, the bound keyword list files already had), and adding a photo or setting its metadata cuts a deeper keyword the same way while every other keyword stays as written. title: Catalog: library files are never read, cut or appended through a planted link (#2552)
author: Bruno-Alumn
body:
Opening or just checking a library opened catalog.log and catalog.lock through whatever was at those names: through a planted link the journal cut the target to 0 bytes or appended to it, the library lock was taken on that file, and a dangling link created its target. FsStore::read also read catalog.snap or prefs.json through a link, a FIFO or a device. FsStore now opens a file in place only when it is a regular file (a symlink_metadata check, then on Unix a device and inode match right after the open), and a missing log is created with create_new, which never follows a link. catalog.lock is opened the same way, and a link or anything else that isn't a regular file there opens the library unlocked, with a warning. A link at a catalog name makes Journal::open fail with a message that names the file and says to remove it, which also covers the catalog part of #2122. The owner note, catalog.lock.owner, is left to #2596, which already writes it without following a link. Fixes #2552.

## Summary

This pull request brings three improvements to LightCraft across lens profile resolution, fitted camera tone curve evaluation, and filmstrip UI responsiveness.

Canon CR3 raw files embed radial vignette opcodes inside the file but omit rectilinear distortion tables, relying on external lens profile databases. title: Detail view: zoom past 100% shows the photo's pixels instead of a bilinear blur (#2643)
author: radialmonster
body:
Fixes #2643.

Photo textures were uploaded with `TextureOptions::LINEAR`, so at 200–800 % the GPU blended neighbouring pixels and the zoomed view looked softer than the file. Photo textures now use nearest-neighbour for magnification and keep linear for minification:

- Above 100 %, each pixel shows as a solid block, so focus, sharpening and noise can be judged from what the file actually holds.
- Thumbnails and Fit shrink the texture, so they keep the linear filter and look the same as before.

The change is one named constant (`PHOTO_TEXTURE` in `crates/ui-egui/src/render.rs`) used at the two texture uploads. The software painter already honours separate magnification and minification filters.

**Tested:** a test build on a 24 MP Nikon D5600 NEF at 800 %. Before, the lettering and rivet dots were smooth gradients. After, they show hard pixel blocks matching another raw editor at a similar zoom. Fit view looks unchanged. `cargo check -p lightcraft-ui-egui` is clean.

**For review:** at fractional zooms between 100 % and 200 % (or 100 % on a scaled display), nearest gives uneven pixel widths. If that looks worse than the slight blur, the filter could switch to nearest only from 200 % up. I kept it simple here.

title: Never crash: the work gate's byte count saturates instead of overflowing (#2576)
author: insideTheFlux
body:
Fixes #2576 (audit LC-27).

## Problem
`WorkGate::acquire` and `acquire_urgent` (`crates/engine/src/memory.rs`) added the requested bytes with plain `+`. Callers weigh work with saturating maths (`export.rs` batch weights, `denoise.rs` raw denoise), so `bytes` can be `usize::MAX`. A debug build then panicked with the gate's mutex held. A release build wrapped the count, let the job in and left the accounting wrong until it ended.

## Fix
- The held count is a private `u128`: exact for any number of `usize` permits, so releasing them in any order leaves the others counted, and a holder of `usize::MAX` makes the next one wait even on a gate whose limit is `usize::MAX`. `usage()` saturates it to `usize` when reporting, so the API is unchanged.
- `acquire`, `acquire_urgent` and `Permit::drop` use saturating `u128` maths, so nothing can overflow.
## Test
`media::tests::work_gate_counts_past_usize_max_instead_of_overflowing` (next to the existing `work_gate_waits_for_room`) covers three cases. A `usize::MAX` permit plus an urgent 101-byte permit, with the large one dropped first: 101 bytes stay counted and the next holder waits. The urgent one dropped first: the gate stays full. A gate whose limit is `usize::MAX`: a second holder waits. On main (plain `+`) it panicked with `attempt to add with overflow` at `memory.rs:143`; with this PR's first version (a saturating `usize` count) it failed the release-order case (count 0 instead of 101).

## Checks (Windows 11)
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-engine`: 1225 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `tests_import::recursive_discovery_includes_sony_sr2_and_srf_case_insensitively`, a Windows-only path-separator failure already on main and fixed in #2377 (9111a616).
- `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.

title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: limit tone-curve steps between pixel populations (#1904)
author: radialmonster
body:
Fixes #1904

## Cause

The NEF decode is not the problem: the D3400 raw data decodes bit-exact with Adobe's DNG of the same frame. The posterization and blotchy noise come from the per-file camera look fitted from the embedded JPEG (`camera_preview.rs`).

The frame is dark (ISO 1100) and mostly saturated blue with some red. The camera JPEG renders the reds about 1.55x brighter than blues of the same scene luminance. Quantile tone matching puts the whole blue population's scene range under the reds' JPEG range and joins them with a near-vertical step: a log-log slope (elasticity) of 12 to 28 between two knots at scene luminance about 0.051. Every pixel on that step gets its luminance noise multiplied, and it renders as contours and blotches.

## Fix

Fitted tone curves (quantile and conditional-median) are limited to a log-log slope of 4 between knots (`MAX_TONE_ELASTICITY`). On the user samples the median look's steepest segment is 2.1 and the 95th percentile 3.6, so ordinary camera curves are left alone.

- A steeper segment is spread over the smallest window of knots around it whose end-to-end slope is under the bound; the knots inside move onto the straight log-log line between the window's ends. Knot positions and monotonicity are kept.
- A window that reaches an end of the curve is pinned there, which can drag most of the curve onto one line. So it is weighed against leaving that end free: the knots past the step follow a slope of 2 (`TONE_REPAIR_ELASTICITY`, about the median camera curve) from the step's other knot. The one with the lower absolute error against the fit's pixel pairs is kept.
- `LOOK_VERSION` 12 -> 13, `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 69 -> 70.
- New test `tone_fit_does_not_step_between_two_pixel_populations`: a synthetic two-population scene (blue at 1.7x, red at 2.64x) whose raw quantile knots step at elasticity above 10; the fit must stay under the bound, keep the knot positions and stay monotone, and a smooth curve must come back unchanged.

title: raw: read Canon CR3/CR2 preview colour space from the maker note (#2654)
author: radialmonster
body:
Fixes #2654

This follows #854, which covered TIFF-based raws (EXIF R03 interop and the Nikon maker note). CR3 was the gap it left, and Adobe RGB CR2s turn out to be one too.

## Cause

The default camera look is fitted to the raw's embedded JPEG. `decode_raw_preview` decodes that JPEG in the colour space `lightcraft_raw::embedded_preview_color_space` reports, because Canon's embedded JPEGs carry no colour tag of their own. That function started with `Tiff::parse`, which fails on a CR3 (ISO BMFF), so every CR3 was decoded as sRGB. For a body set to Adobe RGB, the fit then matched a desaturated target, and renders came out flatter and less colourful than the camera JPEG.

CR2 parses as TIFF but hit the same gap. Canon writes EXIF ColorSpace 0xFFFF (Uncalibrated) for Adobe RGB, with InteropIndex "R98" in a CR2 and no interop IFD at all in a CR3, so the R03 check from #854 never matches.

Tag pairs over our test files (EXIF 0xA001, InteropIndex, Canon maker-note ColorSpace 0x00b4; unique files):
- CR3: (1, none, 1) x 187, (0xFFFF, none, 2) x 35, (0xFFFF, none, 0xFFFF) x 6
- CR2: (1, R98, 1) x 401, (1, R98, absent) x 34, (0xFFFF, R98, 2) x 15, (0xFFFF, R98, absent) x 1

## Fix

Read the Canon maker-note ColorSpace (0x00b4: 1 = sRGB, 2 = Adobe RGB):
- CR3: from the `CMT3` block. When that's absent, an EXIF ColorSpace of sRGB in `CMT2` still counts as sRGB.
- CR2 (Make "Canon"): from the EXIF maker note, via the same `makernote::parse_makernote` path as Nikon, checked before the EXIF fallback.

A value other than 1 or 2, or a missing tag, leaves the result as before. `LOOK_VERSION` (13) and `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` (70) are bumped so cached smart previews and thumbnails are rebuilt, as #778 did. Smart previews of preview-only raws now follow `LOOK_VERSION` as well, since their proxy is the embedded JPEG read in the declared colour space. Unit tests use a synthetic CR3 (CMT3 = 2 or 1, CMT2-only sRGB, 0xFFFF/absent gives None) and a synthetic CR2 (R98 with note 2 or 1, no not…

author: aiongg
body:

title: Colour-range mask: cap the number of samples from automation
author: Matoo125
body:
A colour-range mask compares every pixel against every sample, so render and export cost is pixels × samples. The interactive sampler stops at 5 (`engine/src/cmd/masks.rs`), but `mask.add` / `mask.update` (`colorRange`) passed their `samples` array straight through, so a few hundred samples on a large render turned into billions of operations and hung rendering and export. The project already caps similar lists (`MAX_STROKE_DABS`, `MAX_DETAIL`).

The samples list from automation is now capped at 64 (`MAX_COLOR_RANGE_SAMPLES`).

**Test:** `color_range_samples_are_capped` — a request with 1000 samples is cut to 64, a two-sample request is unchanged. It fails without the cap (1000 ≠ 64) and passes with it. `cargo test -p lightcraft-engine`: 1232 passed; fmt and clippy clean on the changed file.
