title: LR-PROF-CAMERACOLOR: align lens-corrected camera JPEG training pairs
author: r3d42-git
body:
On Canon PowerShot G7 X Mark II CR2s, 0.13.0 can fit a posterized starting look with large pink sky regions. The sensor image and camera JPEG have different lens geometry and framing, so same-position samples can represent different subjects. The fitted colour/tone model may still pass its existing error gates.

This change aligns calibration correspondences using the already resolved geometric profile and the existing bounded framing search. Output pixels still come from the RAW. Tone fitting, white balance, decoding and their acceptance thresholds are unchanged.

## Changes

- For eligible uncalibrated non-CR3 files without an opcode warp, propose the resolved profile's green-plane geometry in sensor/default-crop coordinates. Use it only if both training and held-out edge-direction scores reach 0.90 and improve by at least 0.04 over the original proxy, with at least 192 supported edges and 80% support on each split. Matching is independent of subsequent colour error.
- Use the same geometry for file-local fits, pooled camera calibration and the existing RAW-to-DNG/merge colour-tag hook. Preserve established CR3 and opcode routes. Keep masks and invalid borders aligned with the sensor samples.
- Support the necessary native lookup case: when both lens name and lens specification are absent, a camera's fixed mount can select exactly one profile with that exact mount. Lensfun reserves lowercase initial mount names for fixed-lens cameras. Duplicate profile matches are rejected; named/specification lookup and existing crop handling are unchanged. title: LR-EDIT-OPTICS-PROFILE: preserve unknown crop factors in lens profiles
author: r3d42-git
body:
Missing or malformed crop factors currently become `1.0`, so a lens database entry with unknown calibration scale can still produce a correction. An explicitly invalid calibration override also falls back to the parent lens's crop. Both cases silently apply a scale the entry did not supply.

Preserve unknown crops as `None`. A calibration inherits the parent crop only when its attribute is absent; a present but invalid value stays unknown, and `Profile::correction` declines to convert it. A camera with an unknown crop still supplies its mount, while lookup can use the existing EXIF 35 mm-equivalent fallback. Explicit `1.0`, valid inheritance, the accepted parser range and the existing crop-mode rounding policy are preserved.

`Camera.crop_factor` and `Profile.crop_factor` change from `f64` to `Option<f64>`; the workspace consumer is adapted. The crop commit changes four files: the parser/converter, its tests, the engine adapter with its regression test, and lens-profile documentation.

## Separate CI prerequisite

#2544 is still open. As in #2675, this branch carries its exact one-line `bitDepth` guard simplification as the first, separate commit (`3e6f49fb`), followed by the crop fix as the second commit (`2e46e9df`). It removes the existing Rust 1.95 `clippy::nonminimal_bool` failure without changing behavior, suppressing a lint or updating a dependency. The combined PR diff therefore contains five files, including that one export line.

The crop change can be reviewed independently in the second commit. Maintainers can merge #2544 first and then take the crop commit. #2544 is a CI prerequisite, not a functional dependency of lens correction. The colour changes from #2675 are not included or required.

title: LR-CROP-AUTO: Auto straighten turns by at most 10° on at least 3 lines, and says when it finds nothing
author: ingolfteetz
body:
Part of #2686.

Auto straighten (Auto in the crop panel, or a double-click with the Straighten tool) now turns a photo by at most 10° and only when at least 3 lines agree. When it finds nothing, the app says so.

**Why:** on real photos, today's rule often turned straight photos. The edges of planks, a branch or a bird's wing were taken for the horizon, sometimes for a turn of 20° or more. It also said nothing when it found no lines, so the button looked broken. Numbers are in #2686: unwanted turns of more than 1° dropped from 79 to 19 of 300 photos left as shot. On 45 hand-straightened photos not used for choosing the limits, the misses of more than 1° dropped from 8 to 4, and the mean error from 2.61° to 1.40°, with the same 11 leveled within 0.5°.

**What changes**
- `upright::level_degrees`, which only Auto straighten uses, answers only for at most `STRAIGHTEN_MAX_DEGREES` (10°) and on at least `STRAIGHTEN_MIN_LINES` (3) agreeing lines. Upright Level (`level_angle`) is unchanged, so existing edits render as before.
- `LightcraftApp::auto_straighten` runs the command from both entry points and shows "No horizon or vertical lines to level by" (German translation included) when nothing is found, or the error.
- LR-CROP-AUTO goes from ✅ to 🟡 with the measurements. It still leaves most tilted photos alone; a vanishing-point/horizon prototype is described in #2686 for later.

**Tests**
- `auto_straighten_needs_more_than_one_line` and `auto_straighten_leaves_steep_lines_alone` (pipeline) both fail with the old limits.
- `auto_straighten_says_when_it_finds_nothing` (UI): Auto on a flat photo shows the message and leaves the angle at 0.
- `level_degrees_sign_matches_crop_angle` still passes.

`cargo xtask ci` passes locally.

title: perf(pipeline): Highlights/Shadows median about 2× faster on the CPU, bit for bit the same
author: nicolasfalesy
body:
## What and why

`local::median_row` is the running median behind process V2's Highlights/Shadows base (`median_hv` → `tone_base`). On the CPU renderer it was one of the two biggest costs of a 24 MP export: `perf` put 18 % of the whole CPU export inside it (Sony A7 III raw, `render_bench ONLY=export`).

Per pixel it ran two binary searches over the sorted window with `f32::total_cmp`, then `Vec::remove` + `Vec::insert`. The searches' branches mispredicted on most steps (annotate: the hottest instructions were the search loads and their `ja`s, plus two `memmove` calls).

This PR keeps the same sorted-window algorithm and changes how one step is done:

- The window holds `i32` keys that order exactly like `f32::total_cmp` (`total_key` applies the transform `total_cmp` itself uses; `total_key_inv` undoes it). Equal keys are equal bits.
- Both ranks (of the leaving and the entering key) come from one branch-free counting pass over the window, which the compiler vectorizes.
- One `copy_within` moves the keys between the two ranks by one slot over the leaving key, and the entering key is written at its rank.

The window is the same multiset in the same order at every step, so the output is **bit for bit the same**. The GPU path has its own median (`gpu/src/render.rs`) and is untouched.

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: AHD blends its candidates where noise alone would pick one, no maze in noisy raws (#2094)
author: pick2510
body:
Part of #2094. Independent of #1463 / #1400; either can merge first.

## What was wrong

AHD picked the horizontal or the vertical candidate outright, by the larger 3×3 homogeneity sum. In a flat, noisy area noise alone decides which sum is larger, so neighbouring pixels flip between two directional interpolations and the grain becomes short horizontal and vertical strokes: a maze. Under strong white balance (tungsten light) it comes out orange and blue. Noise reduction smooths the grain around the strokes, so turning it up made the pattern stand out more, which is how it was first noticed ("denoise results in artifacts").

## Change

`crates/raw/src/demosaic/ahd.rs`: the two candidates are blended linearly while their homogeneity sums (each 0–36) are within `BLEND` = 12 of each other, half and half when equal; beyond that the more homogeneous one is taken alone, as before. 12 is the widest blend that keeps the PSNR of the outright pick on the edge test.

## Measured

| | outright pick (main) | blend 12 |
|---|---:|---:|
| PSNR, synthetic smooth scene | 73.0 dB | 73.7 dB |
| PSNR, synthetic edge scene | 37.7 dB | 37.9 dB |
| Anisotropy of flat synthetic noise (bilinear = 3.9e-5) | 4.3e-4 | 2.9e-4 |
| ILCE-7CM2 ARW, ISO 4000, tungsten: flat dark region, maze measure | 5.4e-5 | 3.5e-5 |

On that photo eyelashes and hair keep their detail at 1:1.

## Not fixed here

Most of the orange/blue colour in that pattern comes from demosaicing before white balance (#1328). In the same region, demosaicing the white-balanced mosaic cut chroma high-pass RMS from 0.0077 to 0.0034, and the two changes together to 0.0028. That is #1463's fix, still waiting on #1400.

## Tests

- New `flat_noise_does_not_turn_into_a_maze` (fails on main: AHD's anisotropy on flat noise is about 11× bilinear's, the bound is 9×, the blend gives about 7.5×).
- `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` 70.
- `cargo xtask ci` locally: fmt, clippy, heif, test, parity, layers and assets pass with `LIGHTCRAFT_GPU=0`. `wasm` coul…

title: LR-FILT-LABEL: the label chip and filter bar show what label and labels let through together, not their union
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
The label chip and the filter bar's label buttons now show what a filter with both `label` and `labels` actually lets through.

A filter can carry the single `label` (saved filters, smart albums, agents) and the filter bar's `labels` list at once, and `Filter::matches` ANDs them: `label: red` with `labels: [red, yellow]` shows only the red photos, and `label: red` with `labels: [yellow]` shows nothing. The chip and the bar, though, showed the union: "Label: Yellow or Red" with both buttons lit, so clicking a third label grew the filter to all three instead of adding one to what was shown. Lightroom Classic's Library Filter shows the photos that match all the criteria set, and its label buttons are lit for what is being filtered, so this keeps the filter as it is and makes the chip and the buttons say the same thing. `Filter::labels_shown` gives the labels both let through; when they exclude each other the chip names both ("Label: Red and Yellow or Green"), as nothing is lit in the bar, and a click there starts a fresh label list. The filter itself, `describe()` and the stored format are unchanged. Happy to switch to folding the single label into the list instead, if you'd rather the two never coexist.

title: fix: document the deliberate buffer leak during thread teardown (SonarCloud)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
Resolves the open SonarCloud reliability finding for LightCraft.

`std::mem::forget(b)` in `crates/gpu/src/ctx.rs` is deliberate: during thread teardown wgpu's thread-locals may already be gone, and dropping (or trimming the pool, which drops) can abort the process. The device owns the memory either way. Annotated with that reason.

Verified: `cargo check -p lightcraft-gpu`, `cargo fmt --all --check`.

title: LR-META-LOCATION: the command sweep no longer starts a GeoNames download
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem

A test run tried to reach download.geonames.org. `tests::command_sweep` executes every registered command with empty params. `metadata.downloadPlaceNames` is one of them, and with empty params it falls back to the real GeoNames address (`GEONAMES_BASE`) and to the real settings folder (`<settings>/geonames`). So running the engine tests started a real download thread, which opened a connection to the internet and created a staging folder in the user's settings.

## Change

- `command_sweep` skips `metadata.downloadPlaceNames`. The command has its own tests in `cmd/geocode.rs`, which pass a loopback `base` and a temporary `dataset`.
- The sweep then asserts that no place names download was started (a `#[cfg(test)]` helper `PlaceNames::download_started`). The assertion fails if the command is renamed, or if another command ever starts the download with empty params.

**Not in this PR:** any change to the command itself or to where it stores the data. The test-only change leaves the other sweep commands as they are (`metadata.placeNamesStatus` and `metadata.reverseGeocode` only read local files).

## How it was checked

- [x] `command_sweep` with only the new assertion fails on the old code ("the sweep started a place names download"), and passes with the skip.
- [x] `cargo xtask ci`: all 8 steps pass.
- [x] Looked for other tests that fetch with default params (face and denoise model downloads, SAM 3 mirrors, `lightcraft_fetch`): they need an id and an acknowledgement, or use loopback mirrors, or are `#[ignore]`.

None: test-only change, nothing on screen changes.

## Merging

Overlap: #2659 changes `crates/engine/src/cmd/geocode.rs` (where place names are downloaded), this PR adds one `#[cfg(test)]` method there; the hunks are small and apart, and neither needs the other.

- [x] No new UI strings

Reworked after #2729 (merged), which made missing translations a report, never a failure. title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: a JPEG cut short imports from the data present
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

Why one PR: one behaviour, a JPEG cut short imports from the data present, and no part can land, be tested and be reverted alone: the header change without the decode change would import files that then render as unreadable, and the catalog mark without the probe change records nothing. Of the 846 changed lines, about 440 are tests and docs; the code is about 400.

## Problem

A JPEG that stops before its end-of-image marker (an interrupted download or copy) is refused at import as "truncated: the image data doesn't end with an end-of-image marker", from `header()` in `crates/codecs/src/jpeg.rs` (added with the header-only probes of #367). The data that did arrive is a picture: a progressive JPEG has several complete scans, a baseline JPEG has its first rows. Other photo managers import such files and show what is there. Where the file was already in a library, the decoders that thumbnails use (jpeg-decoder) fail on it with "failed to fill whole buffer", so it shows as unreadable.

## Change

- `read_header` accepts a JPEG with no end-of-image marker when it has something to show, and says so in a new `Header::truncated`. Progressive: the first DC scan of a component is whole. Baseline: the scan header is there with data after it.
- Decode reads such a file with zune-jpeg only. Progressive: the data up to the cut, closed with an end-of-image marker, shows from the scans that arrived. Baseline: read as it is, the rows that arrived show and the rest is flat grey; if zune runs out of data between two restart markers it is retried with an end-of-image marker. Zero bytes at the end (space a download reserved) are not data. Scaled decodes are box-reduced on the way instead of building a full-size float image.
- Still refused, as before: no SOI or frame header, unsupported frame types, no scan data, a file that ends in an end-of-image marker but has a damaged segment length inside its data, every other format, and cut JPEGs of the kinds only the slower decoder…

title: M12-OPEN: AI masks on openly licensed models in pure Rust
author: OneSlips
body:
## The problem

AI masks are a large part of a wedding edit. A typical gallery has hundreds of frames where the
couple, the dress, the sky behind the ceremony or one person's skin needs its own adjustment, and
it has to be repeatable across a whole series. Today LightCraft's AI masks are either heuristics
(Subject, Sky, Background) or need SAM 3, whose weights are gated behind Meta's SAM License and a
Hugging Face account: LightCraft can't host or download them, so a photographer who installs the

work.

This PR gives LightCraft model-based AI masks that work out of the box on models whose weights are
openly licensed (MIT / Apache-2.0), not gated, downloaded on demand after the user agrees, and run

title: CI: one test binary per crate, line tables only, one WASM check
author: aiongg
body:
Makes `cargo xtask ci` faster and its target dir smaller, following the measurements in storytold/craft-common-actions#60. Unlike the other apps, LightCraft keeps `cargo test` as its test runner; nextest is available with `LIGHTCRAFT_NEXTEST=1` (see below).

## Measured

`cargo xtask ci` on a 16-core Linux box, through a two-slot build queue (8 jobs per build), with dependencies and workspace crates already built. All 8 steps passed.

| | |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask ci` | 8:17 wall clock; the test step 6:55 |
| Tests | 4653 passed, 0 failed (179 skipped their checks: corpus, GPU, models) |
| Integration-test binaries | 19, from 51 files |
| Test executables run by the gate | 59 (98 on main before this change) |
| Target dir after the run | 13 GB, after removing older copies of rebuilt test binaries (`CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, as in CI) |

There is no clean "before" run on the same footing; the executable count is from a full `cargo xtask ci` on main the day before.

## Changes

title: Never crash: NaN in tone curves and an i16::MIN UTC offset (#2579 items 3 and 4)
author: darthnut
body:
Two small fixes from #2579, one commit each, each with a test that panicked before the fix.

**Item 3: tone curves** (`crates/color/src/spline.rs`)
- `MonotoneCurve::eval(NaN)` got past both bound checks and the binary search indexed past the end (or underflowed, for a NaN with the sign bit set). NaN now comes back as NaN, as `Lut1::eval` already does.
- `to_lut`, `Lut1::identity` and `Lut1::from_fn` make at least two entries (n = 1 divided 0 by 0).
- `Lut1::eval` reads a hand-built table shorter than two entries as a constant or the identity instead of underflowing on `n - 2`.

**Item 4: UTC offsets** (`crates/meta/src/datetime.rs`)
- `DateTime` deserializes with public fields, so an offset of `i16::MIN` can skip `valid()`. `abs()` overflowed: a panic in debug, a negative minute count printed by `to_iso()` in release. `valid()` and `to_iso()` now use `unsigned_abs()`.

**Testing.** `cargo xtask ci` on Windows 11 x64: fmt, clippy, heif, parity, layers, assets and wasm pass, as do 4,425 workspace tests. Two tests fail on main and on this branch alike: `tests_import::recursive_discovery_includes_sony_sr2_and_srf_case_insensitively` and `headless::tests::folder_discovery_matches_engine_extensions`. These are the Windows path-separator failures of #2579 item 11, which #2662 / #2547 address.

title: Never crash: History is bounded on load and by every op that sets it (#2579 item 8)
author: darthnut
body:
Item 8 of #2579: `HISTORY_LIMIT` (200 steps per photo) was applied only by `Op::PushHistory`. A snapshot, an `Op::AddPhoto` (op log replay, undo of a removal) or an `Op::SetHistory` could carry any number of steps, and every one stayed in memory.

- `Photo::trim_history` (`crates/catalog/src/model.rs`) keeps the newest `HISTORY_LIMIT` steps and moves the History cursor with its step, or to the oldest step kept when its own is dropped.
- `Catalog::repair`, which runs on every snapshot load, applies it and reports each photo it trimmed in `LoadReport::repaired`.
- `AddPhoto` and `SetHistory` apply it too. `SetHistory`'s inverse also restores the cursor when trimming moved it, so undo gives back exactly what was there.

**Not changed:** saved versions (`Photo::versions`) are unbounded in the same way, but there is no limit for them yet, so choosing one is left to a maintainer.

**Tests** (each failed before the fix, keeping 1,000 and 205 steps):
- `tests_repair::history_beyond_the_limit_is_trimmed_on_load`: a snapshot with 1,000 steps loads with the newest 200, the cursor on the same step, and one repair reported.
- `tests_journal::add_photo_and_set_history_are_bounded_and_invertible`: both ops trim, and undoing `SetHistory` restores the snapshot byte for byte.

**CI** on Windows 11 x64: fmt, clippy, heif, parity, layers, assets and wasm pass, as do 4,512 workspace tests. title: LRC-LIB-LIBFOLDERS: a refused move to another folder says what is wrong in plain words; photo.checkMove and skip
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem

Dropping photos on a Folders row asks "Move N photos to …?", and only after the person clicks Move does the move look at the disk. A name already taken in the destination, or a file that is missing or offline, then refuses the whole batch, and the toast reads: ``invalid parameters for `photo.moveToFolder`: beach.png already in /…/Home: nothing was moved. Rename the photo first or choose another folder``. That names an internal command, shows a full path, and gives no way to move the photos that are fine. There is also no way for an agent to ask beforehand what would go wrong.

## Change

**The sort of the photos moves into its own module** (`crates/engine/src/move_check.rs`): which photos go, which are in the folder already, which have a name taken there (including a second photo of the same batch with the same name) and which have a file that is missing or offline. The result lists each skipped photo with its reason: `{moved, folder, skipped: [{id, name, kind: clash|missing|asked}]}`. title: Control port: close gracefully so the client reads its last reply (Windows reset)
author: insideTheFlux
body:
**TL;DR:** On Windows, a control-channel client that sent a bad line followed by more input could get "connection reset" (os error 10053/10054) instead of the error reply explaining what was wrong. The server now closes the connection gracefully, so the client always reads its last reply.

## Change

`apps/lightcraft/src/control_server.rs`:

- After rejecting a line, the server used to close the socket at once. Any line the client had sent after the bad one then reached a closed socket, which answers with a reset. On Windows, that reset discards replies the client hasn't read yet, including the rejection itself.
- `serve_stream` now runs `serve_lines`, then `close_gracefully`: shut down the write side (FIN), read and drop whatever is left (at most `MAX_LINE`, 4 MiB, 500 ms per read and `DRAIN_TIME`, 1 s, in all), then close. The total limit keeps a client that trickles bytes from holding a connection slot.
- `close_gracefully` is taken from #1970. Thanks @LochLogic for writing it; they are co-author on the commit. It's split out because #1970 bundles it with the per-run token work (12 files), and this part is a standalone bug fix. If #1970 lands first, this PR can be closed.

## Tests

- `tcp_connection_is_closed_after_junk` reads the reply and the rejection, then sends another line and reads to the end. Without the fix it fails on Windows with os error 10053; with it, it passes (5 of 5 runs).
- New `a_closing_connection_is_not_held_open_by_a_trickling_peer`: a client sends one byte every 100 ms while the server drains. Without the total limit the drain lasts 10 s; with it, about 1 s.

## Background

This is the fix from #2377 (cross-platform CI), whose Windows leg found the bug. #2667 replaced #2377's workflow with the shared Linux gate, so #2377 is closing. #2377's two Windows test-path fixes are left out here because #2547, #2662 and #2351 already make them (thanks @OneSlips, @czarist and @mweinbach).

title: fix(codecs): validate JPEG ICC APP2 chunk sequences
author: ronibalthazar
body:
## Summary

Fixes a JPEG colour-decoding bug: incomplete or inconsistent ICC APP2 chunks could be silently concatenated and treated as a valid profile. That could give a photo or an embedded raw preview the wrong colour interpretation. Valid reordered ICC chunk sequences continue to work.

## Root cause

Both `lightcraft_codecs::jpeg::parse_markers` and `lightcraft_meta::container::jpeg_segments` collected ICC chunks by sequence number, then sorted and concatenated them without verifying the declared chunk count, sequence uniqueness, complete coverage, or full APP2 payloads. In the decoder, malformed ICC data could also be treated as absent, allowing a raw-container colour hint to take precedence.

## Changes

- Validate sequence numbers, consistent totals, uniqueness, complete coverage, checked byte totals, and complete APP2 segments before assembling a profile.
- Retain chunks as borrowed slices and allocate the assembled profile only after validation; the maximum assembled size is bounded by the number and maximum payload size of APP2 chunks.
- Preserve an invalid-profile marker through JPEG decoding so malformed ICC declarations use the existing unsupported-profile sRGB fallback and cannot be overridden by a raw-container hint.
- Keep unrelated embedded metadata readable when ICC chunks are malformed.
- Document the behavior in the codec and metadata READMEs, the supported-formats parity row, the gaps revision history, and What’s New. Readiness counts are unchanged.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p lightcraft-meta --lib jpeg_icc --offline`: 3 passed.
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-codecs --lib jpeg_icc --offline`: 4 passed.
- `cargo xtask ci` on the final commit: all 8 gates passed (formatting, clippy, HEIF, workspace tests, parity, layering, assets, and WASM). CI reported 148 environment-dependent skips for unavailable corpus, model, and font data.
- `cargo xtask parity`: 577 rows and 1,444 references; all referenced IDs and paths exist.

title: LRC-LIB-CATALOG-LOCK: quitting on macOS removes the lock's owner note
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem

After quitting LightCraft on macOS, `catalog.lock.owner` stays in the library folder and names a process that no longer exists. The window's close button and Quit from the menu bar both end with `std::process::exit(0)` (#1331, #444), so no destructor runs and `LibraryLock`'s `Drop`, the only thing that removes the note, never does. `close_library` saves but keeps the lock. The OS frees the lock itself, so nothing is ever blocked. Only the note is left behind, and it is misleading. Seen on a real quit on 23 Oct. `catalog.lock` staying in the folder is by design and is unchanged.

## Change

- New `Session::release_library_lock()`: drops the open library's lock (and so removes the owner note) while the library stays open in the session. A no-op without a library or a lock.
- `on_exit` in `apps/lightcraft` calls it on macOS only, after the library is saved and background work has stopped, right before `process::exit(0)`. The menu-bar Quit goes through `on_exit` too, so both paths are covered. If the save failed, the app exits anyway, so releasing is still right there.
- Windows and Linux are unchanged: eframe drops the app after `on_exit`, so the lock is released then, after the session's last writes (face data is written in `Drop` under the lock). A first version released on every platform; review found that this let go of the lock before those writes, so it is macOS only.
- The `lock.rs` module doc says who removes the owner note. What's New entry added.

Not in this PR: library switching still reuses the lock when the same folder is reopened (untouched); no change to when the note is written.

## How it was checked

- [x] `cargo xtask ci`: all 8 steps pass.
- [x] New engine test `release_library_lock_removes_the_owner_note`: after `close_library` the note is still there and a second opener is refused; after the release the note is gone and another opener gets in; a second call is harmless.

title: Fix smart album gte/lte rules missing equal f-number and focal length
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/catalog/src/rules.rs:673 (num_op), reached via Rule::matches at :956-957` (no existing issue): Smart album rules on f-number and focal length miss photos equal to the rule's value (f32 against f64 comparison).

## Cause
Photo `aperture` and `focal_mm` are f32 and were widened with `as f64`. That gives values like 1.39999998…, which fall outside the 1e-9 tolerance that `num_op` uses for `gte` and `lte` against the rule's f64 value. A rule such as `aperture ≥ 1.4` therefore missed a photo shot at f/1.4.

## Fix
A new helper, `f32_as_decimal`, converts the f32 to the f64 nearest its shortest decimal form, so 1.4f32 becomes 1.4. The `aperture` and `focalLength` rule fields now use it. The new test checks that `gte` and `lte` match boundary values and that `gt` and `lt` still don't.

## Verified
- Regression test `rules::tests::f32_boundary_values_match_gte_lte`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-catalog --lib f32_boundary_values_match_gte_lte`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The tolerances in `num_op` are unchanged. The `iso` field, `is`/`isNot` and the other numeric fields are unchanged.

title: Brush dabs: build only as far as the caller will look (#1520)
author: saad-mughal435
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1520, the residual aggregate gap after #1892.

`MAX_STROKE_DABS` bounds one stroke at two million and is enforced during interpolation, so the per-stroke case is closed. What is left is the two callers that will not look at anywhere near that many and check the length *after* the vector exists. As the issue puts it, a postconstruction length check cannot serve as an allocation guard: it only discards what was already paid for.

- **`crates/gpu/src/render.rs`** rejects a brush mask past `MAX_DABS`, which is **4096 across the whole mask**, after `strokes.iter().map(brush_dabs).collect()`. Each stroke may construct two million dabs first, and the sum that rejects them is only reached once they all exist. That is the GPU path @aiongg noted on reopening.
- **`crates/pipeline/src/spots.rs`** skips an Auto Mask stroke past `MAX_DABS_CONSIDERED`, **200,000**, after `brush_dabs` has built the whole stroke.

`brush_dabs_within` takes the caller's own budget, and `push_dabs_within` charges against it instead of `MAX_STROKE_DABS`. Both callers now ask for **one more than they accept**, so a stroke past the threshold is still recognised as past it without the remainder being built:

| caller | accepts | built before | built now |
|---|---|---|---|
| GPU brush mask | 4,096 total | up to 2,000,000 **per stroke** | 4,097 total |
| Auto Mask spot window | 200,000 | up to 2,000,000 | 200,001 |

## Behaviour

Unchanged for anything either caller keeps.

A result shorter than its budget was never truncated, so it is the whole stroke. A truncated one only ever reaches a caller that was going to reject it, because both ask for one more than their threshold.

Worth stating plainly, since it surprised me while testing: **a truncated stroke is not a prefix.** Running out of room makes a segment lay its remaining dabs further apart rather than stop mid-segment, because `n.min(room)` then divides the lerp by the smaller `n`. That is how `push_dabs_counted` already…

title: LR-BEHAV-DRAGDROP: the message after a drop that moved, added or tagged photos has an Undo button
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem

A drop onto a Folders row, an album or a keyword is one undo step, but the only hint is a line of text that names Edit > Undo. After a drop onto the wrong row there is nothing to click: the person has to find the menu or remember the shortcut.

## Change

- The message after a drop that moved photos, added them to an album or gave them a keyword carries an Undo button for six seconds. So does the message after Move Selected Photos Here in a folder's menu, which moves the same way. One click runs `edit.undo` and the message becomes "Undo".

The button is withdrawn when the message is replaced or expires, when another step is committed, when the undo or redo stack has changed (Edit > Undo from the menu, another library opened), and while a dialog is open. Undo and then Redo from the menu brings it back, because the stacks are as the drop left them.
- The button is drawn in its own layer above the toast's dark plate, in the toast's own colors (the plate is dark in every theme). It is reachable with Tab and has a name for screen readers. Any other toast is painted as before and takes no clicks.

title: Never crash: Refuse an ORF whose 12-bit strip runs past the file (#2561)
author: endthestart
body:
An uncompressed 12-bit ORF with one strip only checked the strip's declared byte count. When the strip runs past the end of the file, the decoder still allocated the full sample buffer and unpacked rows from whatever bytes were there. A file of a few kilobytes could ask for up to 2 GiB at import when it has no CFAPattern, and a full decode came back with most of each row left black.

The branch now refuses the strip as corrupt when the bytes present are fewer than its rows need, the same way the 16-byte block branch next to it already does. I added a test that moves a valid strip so it starts 24 bytes before the end of the file and checks that decode and the header probe both return an error. It failed before the change.

This covers the ORF part of the issue. The ERF and MEF part is in #2155, and the ARW paths are still open. Let me know if you'd rather fix it another way. Thank you.

Part of #2561

title: Never crash: ARW and SRW strips shorter than declared are refused before allocating (#2561)
author: mercuryVM
body:
Part of #2561: the ARW and SRW paths. ERF/MEF are fixed in #2155 and ORF in #2738. With those two, this closes #2561.

### Problem

`chunk_bytes` clamps a strip to the end of the file, and the full decode of these layouts checked only the strip's *declared* `StripByteCounts` against the frame size:

- ARW, compression 32767, one byte per sample (`strip_len == samples`) and packed 12-bit (`is_packed12`).
- SRW, word (32769) and packed 12-bit (32770) strips (`coding`).

So a file of a few hundred bytes that declares a 3000 × 2000 frame (or up to 2³⁰ samples) passed every check. The decoder then allocated the whole frame (`vec![0u16; w * h]`, up to 2 GiB) to unpack the few bytes that were there, and returned a black image.

### Fix

Both decoders now compare the bytes the file actually holds with the declared strip before they allocate. A short strip is refused as `Corrupt`, the way the ORF 16-byte-block path (`src.len() as u64 != total`) and RAF (`len < required`) already do:

- `arw.rs`: the one-byte and packed-12 full-decode arms check the slice against `strip_len`.
- `srw.rs`: the full decode checks the slice against `strip`.

A whole file is unaffected: every real file's strip ends inside the file. MRW, named in the issue as "needs verification", already slices exactly the bytes it needs (`s.get(..need)`) before allocating, so it needs no change.

### Tests

- New test-only helper `vendor::declare_strip_len` rewrites a single-strip `StripByteCounts` entry. Each test builds a valid small file and then makes its 12-byte strip declare a 3000 × 2000 frame.
- `arw::a_strip_cut_short_is_refused_before_allocating` (one-byte and packed-12 strips) and `srw::a_strip_cut_short_is_refused_before_allocating` (word and packed-12 strips; `probe` still names the format): the full decode returns `Corrupt`.
- Run without the fix, both tests fail at their `Corrupt` assertions: the short strip is accepted and the full frame is allocated.

title: Tests: fix the Windows clippy failure in doc_path's GVfs check (unused variable since #2412)
author: insideTheFlux
body:
**TL;DR:** Since #2412, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (and so `cargo xtask ci`) fails on Windows with `error: unused variable: gvfs` in `crates/engine/src/doc_path.rs`. This PR moves that variable into the block that uses it. Test-only change; nothing in the app changes.

## Why it fails only on Windows

The test `relative_paths_are_taken_from_the_document_folder_and_other_computers_are_refused` ends with a check for a catalog on a GVfs network mount (the folder path GNOME uses for an SMB share on Linux):

```rust
let gvfs = Path::new("/run/user/1000/gvfs/smb-share:server=tokyo,share=photos/catalog.lrcat");
#[cfg(not(windows))]
assert_eq!(resolve("a.jpg", Some(gvfs)), Ok(gvfs.with_file_name("a.jpg")));
```

The assert is rightly skipped on Windows, where `:` can't be part of a folder name. The `let gvfs` line isn't skipped, though, so on Windows the variable is created and never used. Rust reports that as a warning, and clippy with `-D warnings`, the setting the project's checks use, turns every warning into an error.

## Who it affects

- **Windows contributors** running `cargo xtask ci` or clippy with `-D warnings`: the check fails on main before it reaches their own changes, so any real warning of theirs is hidden behind this one.
- **Not affected:** the app itself, plain `cargo build` / `cargo test` on Windows (a warning there, not an error), and the Linux gate from #2667, which is why it went unnoticed.

## Change

The `let` and the assert now sit in one `#[cfg(not(windows))]` block, so on Windows neither is compiled. On Linux and macOS the test runs exactly as before.

## Checks (Windows 11)

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (on main it fails with the error above).
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib doc_path`: passes.

Thanks @aiongg for #2412; this is a small Windows follow-up to its test.

title: LRC-LIB-LIBFOLDERS: moving a folder refuses a missing destination and says why in plain words
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem

Moving a folder on disk (`folder.move`, `folder.rename`) did things a person would not expect and said so badly:

- A destination folder that was not there was created (`create_dir_all`). Pick a folder on a disk that has since been unplugged, and LightCraft tried to make its path, or made a stray folder tree somewhere you did not mean.

title: Never crash: tiles far larger than the image are refused before decoding (#2554)
author: mercuryVM
body:
Fixes #2554

### Problem

`check_image` (`crates/raw/src/tiffraw.rs`) bounds the *image* (`w · h · cpp ≤ MAX_SAMPLES`), but every tile is decoded at its *nominal* size, and tile sizes come from the file independently of the image. `decode_chunk` only checks each tile against `MAX_SAMPLES` (2³⁰). Lossless-JPEG tiles may be coded only as tall as the part inside the image, then `v.resize(n, 0)` grows them to the nominal size. All decoded tiles are collected before the copy. So a 16 × 16 DNG whose one tile claims 16384 × 16384 is a few hundred bytes. It passes the header-only import, then the first full decode allocates 512 MiB for that tile, or N × 2 GiB with more tiles (and aborts on wasm32). `read_quad_tiles` and `read_ycbcr_tiles` in `vendor/arw.rs` start from the same `check_image`.

### Fix

`check_image` now also bounds the sum of the chunks' nominal samples to four times the image's samples, with a floor of one 2048 × 2048 tile (`TILE_SAMPLES_FLOOR`, 2²² samples, 8 MiB of `u16`) for tiny images. Past that it returns `RawError::Limit` before anything is decoded:

- A grid of tiles no larger than the image spans less than twice its width and its height, so a real tiled file stays under 4× (DNG writers use 256 or 512 px tiles).
- Strips are already clipped to the image height by `ImageInfo::chunks`, so they never come near the bound.
- The floor keeps a fixed-size tile on a small image working (a 256 × 256 tile on a 16 × 16 image is tested).

Because the bound is in `check_image`, it applies to the header-only probe (import), the full DNG decode, and both ARW tiled readers. This caps what a crafted file can make the decoder hold. Streaming each tile into the output instead of collecting them (the issue's third suggestion; item 2 of #2579) would lower the peak of *legitimate* tiled files. That is a separate change, not needed to close this hole, and left out of this PR.

### Tests

- `tiffraw::lossy_tests::tiles_far_larger_than_the_image_are_refused`: a 16 × 16 imag…

body:

title: Reject truncated times of day in normalize_iso instead of using midnight
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/catalog/src/stacks.rs:298 (iso_seconds), reached via normalize_iso at crates/catalog/src/dates.rs:61` (no existing issue): normalize_iso silently turns a time with a one-digit hour (or no minutes) into midnight.

## Cause
`iso_seconds` only read a time of day when the string was at least 16 characters long. Any shorter string was treated as a bare date and read as 00:00:00. `normalize_iso` only compares the 10-character date prefix, so inputs like `2026-04-01 9:30`, `2026-04-01T10` and `2026-04-01 10:5` were accepted and the typed time was silently dropped.

## Fix
In `iso_seconds`, a string longer than the 10-character date but shorter than 16 characters now returns `None`. Only a bare date gets midnight. Strings of 16 characters or more are parsed as before. The regression test covers the three truncated inputs and checks that `2026-04-01 09:30`, `2026-04-01t09:30` and a bare date still parse.

## Verified
- Regression test `dates::tests::normalize_iso_rejects_a_truncated_time`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-catalog --lib normalize_iso_rejects_a_truncated_time`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The parsing of full-length strings is unchanged, including the accepted separator characters and lowercase `t`. I did not change the callers of `normalize_iso`.

title: Reject fractional and out-of-range ratings in photo.rate
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/library.rs:736` (no existing issue): photo.rate accepts fractional and out-of-range ratings by truncating them.

## Cause
photo.rate read `rating` as f64 and cast it with `as i64`, which truncates toward zero, before the 0..=5 range check. A value like 5.9 was stored as 5 and -0.9 as 0, where the command should have returned an error.

## Fix
photo.rate now reads `rating` with `index_req`, which rejects non-integral and negative numbers, and then checks that the result is at most 5. Fractional or out-of-range values now return a BadParams error. Whole numbers, including 5.0, are still accepted.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::rating_rejects_fractional_values`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib rating_rejects_fractional_values`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I did not change `index_req` or `f64_req`. A missing `rating` key now reports 'rating must be a whole number 0..5' instead of 'missing number `rating`'.

title: LR-VIEW-PHOTOGRID: an op that fails leaves no touched photos behind in the catalog
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem

The catalog remembers which photos its latest ops touched, so the grid and the tallies can follow a small edit without rereading every photo (`touched_since`, `aspects_since`). `Catalog::apply` notes a touch before it checks that the photo exists, and it returns an error without taking the note back. A batch that fails on its second op is rolled back, but the notes made by its first op and by the rollback stay. So a failed op or a rolled-back batch is remembered as having changed photos it never changed, including ids that do not exist, and a failed album or stack op makes every earlier revision "unknown", so views read the whole library again for nothing. CodeRabbit found it on #2464 (outside the diff there), which reads these records.

## Change

- `Catalog::apply` drops, on any error, the notes made for the revision the op would have made (nothing earlier carries that revision), and puts back the "broad change" mark. It covers every op, a direct failure and a batch rollback alike, with no copy of the history: the notes are at the end of the list and are popped until the revision differs.
- A batch whose rollback itself fails (an inverse the catalog refuses, so the catalog really did change) is the one case that keeps its notes: it makes a revision (so caches keyed by it rebuild) and marks everything before it as unknown, as an op of wider reach does.
- Any other error leaves the revision as it was.
- Tests: `an_op_that_fails_leaves_no_touched_photos_behind` (missing photo for each kind of op, a failed album op, two failing batches, then a good op still reported), `a_batch_that_cannot_be_rolled_back_whole_makes_earlier_changes_unknown`, and the older touched-photos test now expects the exact lists where it allowed "more is said".
- Touch records are in memory only (`#[serde(skip)]`, never in the journal or snapshot), so no catalog format changes.

Not in this PR: any change to what a successful op records, or to the 8,192-note cap.

author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem

`library.source` clears the filter's library folder when a library folder becomes the source ("one folder at a time"), but it does not clear the filter's album when an album does. While an album is shown, `LibrarySource::to_filter` (`view.rs`) makes the shown album replace the filter's, so the grid is right. The filter bar has no album chip, though, so the old album stays in the filter where nothing shows it, and it narrows the next source (All Photos, Picks) with no chip to explain the smaller grid. It would also be laid over a smart album's rules by "save the view as a smart album". Steps: `library.filter {album: X}`, `library.source {kind: "album", id: A}`, `library.source {kind: "all"}`: the grid still shows only X's photos.

## Change

title: LR-VIEW-PHOTOGRID: a thumbnail that can't be read is tried again only when its photo changes (#2682)
author: insideTheFlux
body:
Part of #2682 (split from #2678): the "negative cache" ask. The other half, not sending videos to the image decoders, is #2765.

## Problem
The renderer remembers a failed render (`Renderer::failed` in `crates/ui-egui/src/render.rs`) only until the catalog revision moves, and any op moves it. At launch, face recognition and metadata reads write results photo by photo, so every write sent each undecodable file back to the decoder. #2682 measured it: six files, 37 attempts each in 154 s of idle, 222 of 230 log lines.

## Fix
- `Renderer::follow_catalog` replaces the line in `poll` that copied the revision. When the revision moves, it asks the catalog which photos the ops since the last poll touched (`Catalog::touched_since`). A failure whose photo isn't among them stays failed.
- A failure whose photo did change (Locate Missing File, Reload, an edit) is retried as before, and so is every failure when the catalog can't say which photos changed (`None`: an album or stack op, or history it no longer keeps).
- A failure whose file is missing (a drive unplugged) is not parked: it is retried at every library change, as on main, so the photo comes back once the drive does. `follow_catalog` asks the availability cache (`session.media.availability`, non-blocking in the app) about each failure it would otherwise park.
- The failure record keeps its shape and the meaning of each field. Six open PRs read or write it (#1065, #1390, #1486, #1962, #2237, #2531).

Trade-off: a file that is there but stops failing without any library change (the decoder stops refusing it) is retried when its photo is touched, the display changes, the preview cache is cleared, or at the next launch. Before, any unrelated change happened to retry it.

## Test
`render::thumbnail_tests::a_failed_thumbnail_is_retried_only_when_its_photo_changes`, beside the existing retry test, with a stub for the availability check. Five rating changes to another photo retry nothing; a change to the photo itself retries i…

A drag started with the right mouse button over a photo in the grid starts a photo drag. On a photo that isn't selected it also replaces the selection with that photo first. title: security: bound codec allocation to what a hostile file declares
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
Attacker-supplied codec headers can make a small file buy an allocation far past the documented pixel budget, before any check runs:

- **GIF (#65):** the canvas is size-checked, but `image`'s decoder allocates its first frame buffer at the frame's own declared size — a ~20-byte file could describe a 65535×65535 first frame inside a 2×2 canvas. The first image descriptor is now read from the block headers and refused on the same `max_pixels` gate before any decode.
- **PNG (#82):** `get_text()` inflates compressed iTXt with no bound of its own; XMP now goes through png's bounded `decompress_text_with_limit` (4 MiB cap) and oversized documents are dropped, not expanded.
- **JPEG (#95/#106):** both allocating decoders were handed hostile frame headers unchecked — zune-jpeg decoded before any allocation gate, and jpeg-decoder's full-size decode was bounded by a marker path it doesn't re-parse itself. Each now checks its own freshly-parsed header against the same budget first. An APP1 flood (extended-XMP reassembly is quadratic in fragment count) is now capped at 128 markers.

Regression tests for every gate included; whole codecs test suite green locally.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * JPEG decoding now rejects files with more than 128 APP1 segments and checks frame dimensions against decode size limits before allocation.
  * GIF decoding checks the first image frame’s dimensions before decoding, helping prevent oversized frames from being processed.
  * PNG XMP extraction omits compressed text that exceeds the 4 MiB limit or cannot be read. Smaller compressed XMP remains available, and image decoding can continue when oversized XMP is omitted.

title: Fix relative-date view and source-count cache expiry
author: ronibalthazar
body:
## Summary
Relative-date filters and smart albums could leave the current photo view and source counts stale when the session clock advanced without a catalog edit. This change expires those cached results on the next session-clock minute.

## Root cause
The engine keyed `Session::visible` and `Session::source_total` caches on catalog/query state only. Although rule evaluation uses the session clock, no clock stamp participated in cache freshness. Clock expiry therefore did not trigger recomputation unless another operation changed the catalog or explicitly refreshed the view.

## Changes
- Store a minute stamp with time-dependent visible and source-count caches, using one captured clock value for both expiry and rule evaluation.
- Detect relative-date dependencies in direct filters and smart albums referenced by a query, without rescanning albums on unchanged frames.
- Keep clock expiry separate from held-view identity so held photos remain until refresh while newly matching photos can enter.
- Add fixed-clock regressions for direct and nested smart albums, source totals before/after visible refresh, absolute and same-minute cache reuse, held views, and unchanged revision/undo history.
- Update the smart-album parity notes, gap revision history, and What's New.

## Testing
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib relative_clock` — 5 passed.
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib tests_view_follow` — 8 passed.

title: Reject signed numeric character references in XML entity decoding
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/meta/src/xmp.rs:184 (entity); the same pattern is in crates/lensdb/src/xml.rs:45 and crates/engine/src/preset_luminar.rs:90` (no existing issue): XMP reader accepts signed numeric character references such as &#+65; and &#x+41;.

## Cause
The entity decoders parse numeric character references with `u32::from_str_radix(h, 16)` and `str::parse::<u32>()`. Both accept a leading `+`, so malformed references such as `&#+65;` and `&#x+41;` decode to 'A'. XML only allows digits in a character reference.

## Fix
Before parsing, each decoder now checks that the digits are all ASCII digits, or all ASCII hex digits for `&#x`. A reference that fails the check is rejected, as any other invalid entity already was. The fix is in `entity` in `crates/meta/src/xmp.rs` and `crates/lensdb/src/xml.rs`, and in `unescape` in `crates/engine/src/preset_luminar.rs`. Each of the three has a regression test.

## Verified
- Regression tests `xmp::tests::entity_rejects_signed_numeric_references`, `xml::tests::entity_rejects_signed_numeric_references`, `preset_luminar::tests::unescape_rejects_signed_numeric_references`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-meta entity_rejects_signed_numeric_references && cargo test -p lightcraft-lensdb entity_rejects_signed_numeric_references && cargo test -p lightcraft-engine unescape_rejects_signed_numeric_references`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Other number parsing in the repository, including `parse_rgb`, is unchanged. The existing accepted entity forms are unchanged: the named entities, plain decimal references, hex references, and the XML `Char` validation in the meta crate.

title: LR-EDIT-OPTICS-PROFILE: Fujifilm X-S20 embedded lens corrections and spectral matrices
author: samuelili
body:
Adds embedded RAF lens corrections (`0xf00b` distortion, `0xf010` vignetting) and spectral color profiles for the **Fujifilm X-S20** (along with sensor mappings for the X-S10 and X-M5).

### Why the X-S20 needed a special case
The X-S20 pairs the older 26.1 MP X-Trans CMOS 4 sensor (`6240 × 4160`, half-diagonal `3749` px) with the newer X-Processor 5. Because of the processor, the camera's firmware writes a lens correction scale factor of `scale × 9 = 4643`—which is actually the half-diagonal for the 40 MP X-Trans 5 HR sensor—even though the 9 correction knots (`√(k/8)`) are still indexed across the 26.1 MP active area.

Previously, `scale_matches` rejected the X-S20's tables because `4643` didn't match the frame's actual `3749` px half-diagonal. 

### What Changed
- **RAF Lens Corrections (`raf_lens.rs`)**: Updated `scale_matches` to accept `scale × n ≈ 4643` on the X-S20 when the active frame's half-diagonal matches the full 26.1 MP sensor (`3749` px within `SCALE_TOLERANCE`). In-camera crop modes are still left uncorrected as expected.
- **Spectral Color Matrices (`spectral.rs`)**: 
  - Mapped the `X-S20` (and updated `X-S10`) to `X-T4` in `SAME_SENSOR`, as they share the same stabilized 26.1 MP X-Trans 4 assembly. This gives the X-S20 proper Standard Illuminant A / D65 matrices and Kelvin WB scaling.
  - Added `X-M5` mapped to `X-T3`.
- **Cache & Tests**: 
  - Bumped `RENDER_CACHE_VERSION` from 69 → 70 (`media.rs`).
  - Broadened the corpus test glob in `corpus.rs` to `raf-fuji*` so it picks up `xtask`'s `raf-fujifilm-*.raf` naming convention.
  - Updated parity and lens correction docs.

### Verification
Tested against the CC0 X-S20 sample from `raw.pixls.us` (#6666, `raf-fujifilm-x-s20.raf`):

title: security/raw: bound hostile-memory paths in the raw decoders
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
SonarCloud findings on the raw crate, each fixed with a regression test that failed before it:

- **Sparse strips walker** (dc3bd92a family, d58355f0): pending-pointer dedup and work budgets instead of queueing every declared SubIFD pointer.
- **Truncated MEF / lossy-JPEG strips** (77be2526, b843baeb): the decoders now require enough actual strip bytes / check JPEG output dimensions before allocating and unpacking.

title: LR-LIB-VIRTUALCOPY: prevent numbering overflow in copy batches
author: ronibalthazar
body:
## Summary

Fix virtual-copy numbering at the `u32` limit. Exhausted default numbering now returns an actionable `BadParams` error before changing the catalog, while explicitly named copies remain available.

## Root cause

`photo.virtualCopy` calculated `1 + max(Copy N)` inside the per-photo creation helper before checking whether the caller supplied a custom name. At `Copy 4294967295`, that addition overflowed and became an unexpected command failure. Since the command created and committed each copy as it iterated, a later exhausted target could also leave earlier copies from the same request behind.

## Changes

- Resolve all requested copy names before allocating IDs or mutating the catalog.
- Bypass numeric suffix scanning for explicit nonblank names.
- Use checked per-master reservations for default names, including multiple requested photos sharing a master.
- Add regressions for explicit naming at exhaustion, actionable exhaustion errors, atomic batch rejection, same-master reservations, and creation/undo of `Copy 4294967295`.
- Update the virtual-copy parity notes, gaps history, and What's New entry.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib virtual_copy` — 7 passed.
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib virtual_copies` — 3 passed.
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib tests_organize` — 18 passed.
- `cargo xtask ci` — passed all 8 stages (fmt, clippy, HEIF, tests, parity, layers, assets, wasm); 148 corpus/model/font-dependent tests were skipped because their optional data was unavailable.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

## Manual validation

Ran the supported headless demo CLI workflow. Explicit names, including `Proof copy`, succeeded with an exhausted numeric sibling; default naming returned the expected `BadParams`; a mixed batch was rejected without adding copies; and normal copy creation followed by undo restored the original copy count. The script's process exit was nonzero because it intentionally exercised two expected `BadParams`…

title: LR-IMP-FORMATS: decode GoPro GPR (VC-5)
author: 06needhamt
body:
GPR is a DNG (compression 9) whose raw image is one VC-5 coded tile. crates/raw/src/vc5.rs ports the decoder of GoPro's GPR SDK (Apache-2.0 or MIT; credited in NOTICE): segment parser, codebook 17 run-length highpass bands, three-level inverse 2/6 wavelet over the four channels (GS, RG, BG, GD) and the log-curve repack into an RGGB 14-bit or GBRG 12-bit mosaic. Bands and channels decode in parallel. Malformed streams (truncated, duplicate codeblocks, wrong channel count, size mismatch) are errors, never panics.

- dng.rs: decode compression 9 instead of refusing it; other CFA layouts stay Unsupported with a reason.
- import: .gpr is a raw extension (engine EXTENSIONS, xtask assets).
- tests: synthetic VC-5 streams (testdata feature) for unit, DNG and engine import tests; gpr_corpus.rs checks eight CC0 bodies from raw.pixls.us (HERO5-11, FUSION; pinned in RAW_SAMPLES) by size, layout, white level, green-pair correlation and pinned hashes.

title: Forget Local records directly in drive and share roots
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/catalog/src/local.rs:62 (folder_of), used by forget_local_plan at :192 and :204` (no existing issue): Local browse records directly in a drive or share root are never forgotten.

## Cause
`folder_of` split `folder_key(path)` at the last '/', so a photo directly in `C:\` or `//srv/share/` got the folder `c:` or `//srv/share`. `Op::SetBrowsed` stores root folders as `c:/` and `//srv/share/`, so the `browsed` lookups in `forget_local_plan` never matched. Those folders looked never browsed, so their records counted as recent and were never evicted.

## Fix
`folder_of` now passes the parent directory back through `folder_key` with a trailing '/', so drive and share roots get the same key form (`c:/`, `//srv/share/`) that `SetBrowsed` stores. Other folders keep their usual key. The regression test `tests_local::drive_and_share_root_records_are_forgotten` covers a drive root and a UNC share root. Run it with `cargo test -p lightcraft-catalog drive_and_share`. The drive-root case failed before this change.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests_local::drive_and_share_root_records_are_forgotten`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p lightcraft-catalog drive_and_share`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`forget_local_plan` and `folder_key` are unchanged.

title: LR-BEHAV-AUTOSAVE: a change that could only be partly taken back is saved and can be undone
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem

When a change made of several steps fails part-way, `Catalog::apply` takes back what it had done, and it ignored the result of each step it took back (`let _ = self.apply_inner(inv)`). If one of those inverses failed too (putting a stack back needs a photo that only comes back later in the same rollback), the catalog stayed changed while `apply` returned a plain error. `Session::commit` then skipped the journal record and the undo step. The open library had the change; a restart replayed the old state and brought the change back out of existence, and Undo could not finish the job. CodeRabbit raised this as an outside-diff finding on #2761.

## Change

- `Catalog::apply` keeps the inverses that could not be applied (`Changes::leftover`, nested batches included) and returns them in a new `CatalogError::PartlyApplied { cause, remaining }`. `remaining` is what is left of the rollback: applied in order, it takes the catalog back to where it was before the batch. The error text says the change was only partly taken back. A failure that changed nothing is still a plain error.
- `Catalog::apply` makes a revision for such a batch, so what is derived from the revision (the grid's list, the tallies, the caches) is rebuilt, and marks everything before it as unknown.
- `Session::commit` journals the batch as it was asked for. Replaying it against the same catalog fails at the same point and leaves the same changes, so a restart finds exactly what the session had and the journal format is unchanged. The undo step is `remaining`, so Undo finishes the rollback. The error still goes to the caller (UI, MCP, CLI).
- `Session::apply_system` journals such a batch too.
- An undo or redo step that fails part-way is journaled as well. Its `remaining` becomes the step on the other stack (Redo after a failed Undo), so the stack does not stay stuck on a step that cannot run again from where the catalog now is. Sidecars the failed step still had to repair are handed on…

title: LR-LIB-SMARTALBUM: the catalog refuses an edit that makes a smart album include itself
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem

A smart album can test other albums ("album is Travel"), so the albums form a graph, and an album that tests itself, directly or through other smart albums, would include itself. Today `main` keeps that out only in the callers: `album.setRules` and `album.createSmart` check the rules they are given. The catalog accepts anything. An edit that comes another way is not checked: an op committed on its own by code that did not run those checks, a batch of edits that are each fine when checked against the library as it is but close a loop together, or a new album that takes the id a saved rule already names (an album that was deleted). A library that gets a loop that way shows an album whose photos depend on which album is looked at first.

## Change

The loop rule moves to the one place every new edit passes: `crates/catalog/src/lib.rs` and `Session::commit` in `crates/engine/src/lib.rs`.

- **`Catalog::apply_new`** is `Catalog::apply` for a new edit. Before it applies anything, it works out what the edit would do to which album tests which, and refuses the edit if a smart album would be newly on a loop. The refused edit never touched the library, so there is nothing to take back, no undo step and no journal line. The error names the album, for example `smart album “Travel” (album 7) would include itself: its rules lead back to it through the albums they test`.
- **`AlbumGraph`** holds, for every album, the albums its rules test (smart albums only; a plain album leads nowhere). `on_a_loop` finds the smart albums that lead back to themselves in one walk with its own stack (Tarjan's algorithm), so a ring of thousands of albums cannot overflow the stack. **`foresee`** applies an add, a removal, a change of rules, or a batch of them, to the graph, in order.
- **`Session::commit` uses `apply_new`**, so the rule holds whichever command, importer, task, MCP call or control request makes the edit, alone or in a batch. Undo, redo, replaying a saved log an…

title: Add an Android app shell
author: tzhazuma
body:
This adds `apps/lightcraft-android`: a Gradle project that hosts the existing egui UI inside an `android-activity` window. The engine, the UI, the theme and the command table are unchanged — the shell only supplies what the desktop shell gets from the OS.

## What the shell does

- **Entry point and storage** — builds as `libmain.so`, loaded with `System.loadLibrary`. `$HOME` is set to `AndroidApp::internal_data_path()` before the app starts, so LightCraft's *own* code points the library at `<files>/Pictures/LightCraft Library` and its preferences at `<files>/.config/lightcraft` — no code in the desktop crate had to learn about Android.
- **File pickers** — `ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT` through the Activity; the picked photo is copied into `<filesDir>/import/` and imported with the app's own `library.import` command. Exports write to a scratch path and are published to the `ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT` destination afterwards.
- **Phone layout** — `phone_layout()` opens on the photo grid with the left and right panels closed and the filmstrip kept; `TouchShell` raises hit targets to 40 pt after LightCraft installs its theme, and its `Tokens` toolbar/filmstrip heights grow with that.
- **Command palette** — long-press the top 8% for 500 ms. The buttons send LightCraft's own command ids (`file.addPhotos`, `dialog.export`, `view.photoGrid`, …), so this is a finger-sized menu bar, not a second UI.
- **Fonts** — the `/system/fonts` CJK face is appended to every family, including the theme's named `semibold` family, after the theme's fonts are live (earlier, egui panics).
- **GPU** — the develop pipeline's secondary `wgpu` device is off by default; the window itself is still drawn by eframe/wgpu. The setting turns it back on.

title: fix(ui): wrap the Edit header buttons instead of letting Reset cover HDR
author: Enthendor
body:
## Edit panel: Reset no longer covers HDR in longer languages

Noticed while reviewing the German catalog (#2800). In the Edit header, Reset was laid out right-to-left in whatever width Auto, B&W and HDR left. With a longer label it drew on top of HDR. In German at the default panel width only "HD" was visible.

The new test measured how widespread this was:
- At the default width (222 pt inside the 270 pt panel), Reset covered HDR in **11 of the 18 languages**.
- At some width between the narrowest panel and 400 pt, it happened in **16 of 18**; only the two Chinese catalogs were never affected.
- In Polish at the narrowest panel, HDR itself also ran past the edge.

### Change
- `header_buttons` (in `panels/edit.rs`) plans the row before drawing it. A button that doesn't fit starts the next row, and Reset stays right-aligned on whichever row it lands.
- When everything fits, the layout is unchanged (English from the default width up).
- `widgets::text_button_size` gives a `text_button`'s width ahead of drawing. `text_button` uses the same formula, so the plan and the drawn row always agree.

### Tests
- New `edit_header_buttons_do_not_overlap_in_any_language`, checked for every `Locale::ALL` at widths 200, 222, 260 and 400 pt:
  - no two buttons intersect
  - none runs past the edge
  - Reset is right-aligned
  - German wraps at 222 pt
  - English keeps one row from 222 pt up
- `cargo clippy -p lightcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -D warnings` clean.
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-ui-egui`: 1389 passed. The 6 `tests_model_setup` failures also occur without this change: my local build "cannot run denoise models".
- Headless snapshots (`lightcraft-cli snapshot --demo`, de/en/it) checked by eye:
  - German and Italian: Reset sits on a second row, right-aligned.
  - English: unchanged.

title: Enable Filters: a folder moved while filters are off is followed by the filter put aside, and Cmd+L still brings it back (follow-up to #2709)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Follow-up to #2709, from a point raised in its review: a folder moved on disk while the filter names it, with Enable Filters (Cmd+L) off or on.

Three ways it went wrong:

- `library.filter {folder}` set, Cmd+L off, the folder moved (`folder.move` / `folder.rename`), Cmd+L on: the filter came back with the old path and showed nothing.
- The same with filters on: `filter.folder` stayed on the old path while the photos were relinked to the new one, so the grid emptied.
- Browsing a folder in Local with a filter set (say 4 stars), Cmd+L off, the browsed folder moved, Cmd+L on: `follow_folder` had written the new path into the live filter while it was off, so Cmd+L put *that* aside instead of bringing the stars back. Filtering stayed off and the stars were gone.

What changes, in `follow_folder` only: both the live filter and the one put aside follow a moved `folder` the way they already follow `libraryFolder`, and while filters are off the live filter is left empty instead of getting the browsed path. Lightroom Classic's Enable Filters turns the last-used filters back on as they were.

Tests are in a new `tests_shelved_folder.rs`, to stay out of the way of the other Enable Filters PRs.

## Validation

- `cargo test --workspace --lib -- tests_shelved_folder`: all three tests fail on main, pass here (also alone with `--test-threads=1`); dropping any one of the three lines of the fix fails its own test
- `cargo test --workspace --lib -- tests_folders tests_enable_filters move rename browse`: green
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean

(macOS, Apple silicon)

title: LR-BEHAV-BG-TASKS: a preview build asked for while another runs can wait in line for it (engine)
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem

Only one preview build runs at a time, and a second one asked for meanwhile (Build Previews, or Build / Discard Smart Previews in the background) is refused with "a preview build is already running". An agent on the control channel or MCP that wants to build previews of several shoots has to poll, retry and race other callers. The same refusal rule is what #1943 and #1955 want for imports and Synchronize Folder: jobs that must not run side by side need a line to wait in, not an error.

## Change

The queue core of #1933, rebuilt on `main`'s own activity registry so it can land on its own. Engine only: the File ▸ Previews menu items do not ask to queue yet, so nothing changes on screen.

- Jobs that must not run side by side share a `Lane` (`activity::Lane`; for now the preview lane: `previews` and `smartPreviews`). `Activity::enqueue` puts a request in line behind the others of its lane; it is refused for a kind with no lane and when 100 tasks (`MAX_WAITING`) already wait.
- `library.buildPreviews` and `library.smartPreviews {background: true}` take `queue: true`. While a preview build runs (or others already wait) the call answers `{queued: id, place}` instead of being refused. It keeps what it was asked with the photos written out, so it builds the photos chosen when it was asked, not those chosen when its turn comes. `queue` together with `wait` while one runs is refused: a call cannot both wait in line and return when the build is done.
- `Session::start_waiting` starts the first waiting task whose lane is free, under the id it had in line, by running the command it was asked with (not journaled a second time). It runs after every `execute` and from the app's frame loop, and does not re-enter itself. A start that fails is logged and the next in line goes on.
- `activity.list` lists the waiting tasks after the running ones, and `TaskInfo` gains `waiting`, `place` (1 = next in its lane, 0 when running) and `lane`. `activity.cancel {id}` ta…

title: LR-BEHAV-DRAGDROP: a right-click while photos are carried opens no context menu
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem

While photos are carried from the grid (the primary button held), a right-click on a sidebar row (an album, a folder or a keyword) opens that row's context menu. A menu is not what the person is doing with the pointer in the middle of a drag.

Found by a headless test on `main`: carry a photo over each of the three row kinds, press and release the secondary button there, and the row's menu is open afterwards. The report said the photos stay carried; on `main` that part does not hold. The same release also counts as the drop (the album gains the photo, a folder row asks to move it), and that is the separate change in #2766, not this one.

## Change

- `widgets::context_menu`, the one function every sidebar row menu (and the grid cell's and the Keyword List's) opens through, returns without opening anything when the right-click arrives while photos are carried.
- "Carried" is read from a flag set once at the start of each frame: the photos are in `dragging_photos` and the primary button is down. A drag left over without its button (full screen skips the code that ends it) does not hold menus back.
- Tests in `tests_carried_right_click.rs`: a right-click while carrying opens no menu on an album row, a folder row and a keyword row; without a drag the same right-click still opens each row's menu; a leftover drag without its button does not hold the menu back.
- What's New and the parity row.

**Not in this PR**: what the right button's release does to the drag (it ends it and drops, fixed by #2766); the Esc contract of #2204; the right-click menu of a text field (it does not go through `widgets::context_menu`); dragged albums, sections and keywords.

title: LR-CROP-AUTO: Auto straighten reads the vertical vanishing point and the horizon
author: ingolfteetz
body:
Part of #2686 (numbers and method in the issue comment).

Auto straighten now takes the camera's roll from three cues, in this order, in the new `crates/pipeline/src/straighten.rs`:

1. **Plumb lines**: the roll from the vertical vanishing point (at least 8 inliers, 1.5 half-long-edges of line, spread over 0.6, the point well outside the frame). Converging verticals of a building shot upward no longer turn the photo by their lean.
2. **The horizon**: the straight full-width line with brighter rows on one side, scored by its 30% quantile column so that waves, clouds and ridges don't make one; a coarse search (±10°, 0.25°) refined to 0.02°.
3. **Long lines**: the existing consensus (at least 3 agreeing). It also vetoes a horizon it disagrees with by more than 1°.

The limit drops from 10° to 5° (`straighten::MAX_DEGREES`). Upright Level and its `level_angle` are unchanged. `upright::analysis_plane` is factored out of `analyze_source` so that the horizon reads the same image the segments come from.

**Measured** on 113 photos I straightened by hand in Lightroom Classic:

| | comes out straighter | comes out more tilted | mean error |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 29 | 10 | 1.01° |
| this PR | **50** | 10 | **0.82°** |

Of 300 photos left as shot, 11 instead of 8 are turned by more than 3°.

**Tests**
- `auto_straighten_finds_a_sea_horizon_among_ripples` and `auto_straighten_takes_the_roll_from_converging_verticals` both fail with the long-line rule alone.
- `auto_straighten_ignores_a_single_short_line` replaces "needs more than one line": a straight edge across the whole width is a horizon now, a short single line still isn't.
- `auto_straighten_leaves_steep_lines_alone` now checks the 5° limit.
- `level_degrees_sign_matches_crop_angle` moves from 6° to 4° to stay under that limit.

LR-CROP-AUTO stays 🟡 with the new numbers.

title: LR-META-INFO: the Info panel can show metadata for the selected photos
author: dotCooCoo
body:
With several photos selected, the Info panel showed the active photo's values only, with no sign of which fields the other selected photos hold differently (gap 30 in `docs/gaps.md`). By default, Target Photo is selected as the option to view metadata." title: PERF-CATALOG: equal develop settings are held once in memory
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem

A photo holds its develop settings behind an `Arc`, and so do its history steps, versions and import look. Nothing on `main` makes equal settings one value, so every photo read from a library, or imported, holds a copy of its own. Most photos of a library were never edited and hold the defaults, so a large library pays for the same settings value once per photo: on a test library of 100,000 photos a photo takes 4.4 kB, and about 1.6 kB of that is its settings.

## Change

Rebuilt on `main`'s own types from the memory part of #823, which is stacked on the catalog format work (#800, #814) and reads through that stored form. This PR has none of it, and keeps #823's names (`shared::settings`, `shared::default_settings`, the per-thread `Seen` list of recent values).

- New `crates/catalog/src/shared.rs`. Every settings value that enters a catalog is replaced by the value already held when an equal one is: the held default, the current photo's settings, or one of the last four values seen on the thread.
- Read from a saved library: `deserialize_with` on `Photo.develop`, `Version.settings`, `HistoryStep.settings` and `Photo.import_look`. Given by a change: `Catalog::apply` for `AddPhoto`, `SetDevelop`, `PushHistory`, `SetHistory` and `SetVersions`. `Photo::new` starts from the held default.
- **Equal means the same down to the saved JSON.** `==` takes -0.0 for 0.0, which the saved form, a photo's fingerprint and the preview-cache key tell apart, so settings holding a negative zero are never shared and never what others share. The check walks the value as `Serialize` does, without writing any text (writing every float out roughly doubled the cost of opening in a first version).
- Sharing can't carry one photo's edit to another: settings behind an `Arc` are replaced, never changed in place (`Arc::make_mut` copies a shared value).
- What a thread remembers is a handful of `Weak` pointers: it keeps no settings alive.
- The files and the catalog format …

title: Tests: the launch-list read-only test compares a held lock file without reading it (Windows)
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## Problem

On Windows, `tests_launch_library::listing_the_libraries_leaves_every_folder_byte_identical` fails on `main` every time, so `cargo xtask ci` stops at its test step for every Windows contributor:

```
panicked at crates\ui-egui\src\tests_launch_library.rs:143:60:
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: Os { code: 33, kind: Uncategorized, message: "The process cannot access the file because another process has locked a portion of the file." }
```

The test's `snapshot` reads every file in its folder, including `Held/catalog.lock`, which the test holds with `LibraryLock::acquire`. On Windows, `File::try_lock` is `LockFileEx`, and the [LockFileEx documentation](https://web.archive.org/web/20261002054757/https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/FileAPI/nf-fileapi-lockfileex) says a second handle of the locking process cannot access the locked region until it is unlocked. On Linux and macOS the lock is `flock`, which is advisory, so the read works there. The test came in with #2701.

The app itself does not read a held lock file: `unavailable` in `panels/library_problem.rs` lists the folder and opens the snapshot or the log, `resolve_dir` in `crates/engine/src/library.rs` compares the file name only, and the lock code reads only `catalog.lock.owner`.

## Change

- `snapshot` records each file's length next to its contents and modification time.
- A new `contents` helper reads a file. When the read of a `catalog.lock` fails with os error 33 (`ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION`) on Windows, it returns `None`, and that file is compared by its length and modification time. Any other read error still fails the test.
- Every other file is still compared byte for byte, and on Linux and macOS the held lock file is too.

**Not in this PR:** changes outside the test.
