title: LRC-LIB-SMARTCOLL: a smart album on a loop of albums holds no photos, and says which album it loops through
author: nledford
body:
Off `main`.

## Problem

A smart album can test other albums ("album is Travel"), so albums can form a ring: A's rules test B and B's rules test A, or an album tests itself. The commands refuse to make such a loop, but a library can already hold one: saved by an older version, edited by hand, or made when an album that a rule still names was deleted and its id taken again.

What an album on a loop shows is an accident. `smart_album_has` stops the recursion with a runtime guard that cuts the loop wherever the question happened to enter it, so the album shows a subset of photos that depends on which album is asked about. The sidebar marks it with a warning sign, but the empty grid never says why, because it is not empty.

## Change

A smart album on a loop holds nothing, whoever asks. The rule, stated once:

- **An album on a loop** (a ring of smart albums that test one another, or one that tests itself) holds no photos: `album_photos`, `album_count` and `album_contains` agree, so the grid, the sidebar count, the tallies and an Album rule of another smart album all see it empty.
- **An album off every loop** is worked out as before.
- **An album that only tests a looping album** is not on the loop. It keeps working and sees the looping album as the empty album it is, so "is in" that album matches nothing and "isn't in" it matches every photo that is not deleted.
- **Mending the loop** (changing the rules of an album on it, or removing one) gives the albums their photos back. Nothing is stored, and opening a library that holds a loop works as before.

How:

- `AlbumGraph` and `on_a_loop` find the albums on a loop in one walk over the albums (Tarjan's, with its own stack, so a ring of thousands of albums cannot overflow the call stack). The two are the same text as in the open PR that refuses new loops.
- The set of looping albums is memoized in the catalog's derived lookups (`Indexes`, next to the stack and album indexes) and forgotten when an album is added or removed…

title: LR-META-LOCATION: reject malformed typed GPS coordinates
author: ronibalthazar
body:
## Summary
Fixes a bug in typed GPS metadata editing: malformed coordinate text could be silently reinterpreted as a different location. For example, exponent-like or arbitrary surrounding text was discarded and its remaining numbers were treated as degrees/minutes.

## Root cause
`crates/engine/src/cmd/library.rs::parse_gps` split input on every character except digits and decimal points, then interpreted the remaining values as degrees, minutes, and seconds without requiring the entire coordinate expression to be consumed. It also did not validate minutes and seconds independently or match hemisphere markers to the coordinate axis.

## Changes
- Replace permissive character splitting with a bounded parser for complete decimal and DMS coordinate pairs.
- Validate finite values, coordinate ranges, DMS component ranges, axis-appropriate hemispheres, signs, and marker uniqueness; retain supported prefix/suffix markers, case handling, pair separators, and Unicode-minus normalization.
- Reject unknown text and exponent notation. Invalid GPS returns the existing `BadParams` before `photo.setMeta` changes any field.
- Add parser regressions and a batch metadata/history regression, while retaining GPS-to-XMP persistence coverage.
- Update `docs/gaps.md`, `docs/parity-checklist.md`, and `docs/whats-new.md`. Feature readiness and gap counts are unchanged.

## Testing
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib gps_tests` — 8 passed.
- `cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib gps_typed_in_is_saved_to_xmp` — 1 passed.
- `cargo xtask ci` — all 8 stages passed: fmt, clippy, HEIF, tests, parity, layers, assets, and WASM.
- CI reported 148 skips for unavailable external corpora, model files, and some optional fonts; no applicable GPS check was skipped.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

title: LR-VID-PLAY: MP4/MOV video import and cataloguing with duration and container badges
author: d-rouge
body:
# LR-VID-PLAY: MP4/MOV video import and cataloguing with duration and container badges

Part of M14 (Video support)

## Problem

  Lightroom catalogs regularly contain mixed libraries of photographs and video clips captured by cameras or smartphones.
  Previously in LightCraft:
    - `.mp4`, `.mov`, and `.m4v` files were ignored by folder discovery and the import review (`MediaKind::Video` existed in the catalog schema but was unused).
    - There was no video container sniffer or metadata parser to extract duration or dimensions.
    - If a video entry was placed in the catalog, the engine would attempt to spawn image decode/render jobs, failing and tagging the file as damaged or broken.

## Change

Implements pure-Rust video container probing, import, and clean UI presentation:

1.  **Pure-Rust ISO-BMFF / QuickTime metadata parser (`crates/meta/src/video.rs`)**:
 - Parses `ftyp`, `moov`, `mvhd`, `tkhd`, `mdhd`, `mvex`, `mehd` boxes safely without external libraries.
 - Extracts duration in seconds (supporting both 32-bit and 64-bit integer timescales, plus fragmented movie headers), display dimensions (handling 90°/180°/270° matrix transformations), creation datetime, and camera metadata.
 - Strictly bounded and hardened: hostile or truncated inputs return graceful fallbacks and never panic.

2.  **Engine ingestion & job management (`crates/engine`)**:
  - `import.rs`: adds `.mp4`, `.mov`, `.m4v` to import discovery; populates `ProbeInfo` and `ImportCandidate` with video duration and dimensions.
 - Full support for Add in place, Copy, and Move import modes (including date-based subfolder routing `Originals/YYYY/YYYY-MM-DD/` from creation time).
 - Duplicate detection by path and probe hash works identically for video clips.
 - Smart Collections / filtering properly evaluate `kind: video` and `duration` criteria.
 - `media.rs`: suppresses pipeline render, thumbnail, and quick-view jobs for `MediaKind::Video`. Unplayable clips do not
  consume render worker resource…
